### Finding 129 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, moderate - a real, numbered BOQ line item whose description happens to start with the word "Total" was silently dropped from the parsed schedule entirely, mistaken for a running subtotal row)

**Area:** discovery (`engine/discovery/boq_extraction.py` - deterministic BOQ/priced-schedule line-item
parsing off a buyer's own .xlsx/.xlsm workbook).

**Scenario:** `_SKIP_ROW_RE` exists to stop a workbook's own running subtotal/grand-total/carried-forward
rows (real rows in the sheet, never real priced line items - e.g. `["Sub Total", None, None, None,
302760]`) from being counted as items. Its `total`/`sub total`/`grand total` branches were a bare PREFIX
match (`^(sub[\s-]?)?total\b`, no end anchor) against the row's cleaned description. A genuine, numbered
line item whose description happens to start with the word "Total" - entirely ordinary civil-engineering
BOQ phrasing, e.g. `"Total length of guardrail to be supplied and installed"` (unit `m`, qty `850`, rate
`320`, amount `272000`) or `"Total area of paving to be removed and relaid"` - matched the same prefix
and was silently skipped in `extract_items_from_grid()`, with no trace in the parsed `items` list or the
workbook's own `note` - the module's own stated "we stop, we never guess" discipline guards against
*fabricating* an item, but this bug went the other way and *dropped* a real, correctly-priced one,
understating the scope a human reviewer or a downstream financial summary would see.

```python
>>> import boq_extraction as boq
>>> bool(boq._SKIP_ROW_RE.match("Total length of guardrail to be supplied and installed"))
True   # wrongly treated as a subtotal row and dropped
```

**Fix:** tightened only the `total`/`sub total`/`grand total` branches of `_SKIP_ROW_RE` to require the
REST of the cleaned description (after the matched keyword) to be nothing but trailing punctuation or a
currency marker (`:`, `-`, `(R)`) and then end-of-string - matching how a real subtotal row's description
cell actually looks (just the bare label, e.g. `"Total"`, `"Sub Total"`, `"Total (R)"`). The other skip
phrases (`vat`, `page N`, `carried forward`/`brought down`, `c/f`/`b/f`, `notes`) were deliberately left as
prefix matches, unchanged - none of them is a plausible first words of a real line-item description, so
there is no equivalent false-positive risk there to fix.

**Verified red-then-green.** Added `test_real_item_description_starting_with_the_word_total_is_not_dropped_
as_a_subtotal_row()` to `engine/discovery/test_boq_extraction.py` - a sheet with two real "Total ..."
line items plus a genuine bare `"Sub Total"` row, asserting both real items are kept AND the bare
subtotal row is still correctly excluded. Revert-and-confirm-red on `boq_extraction.py` alone: the new
test failed exactly as predicted (`got []` - both real items dropped), the bare-"Sub Total"-still-excluded
assertion still passed; restored, `0 failure(s)` across the full file (14 tests). `py_compile` clean on
both touched files. Regression: re-ran `test_list_tenders.py` (discovery rotation's other recent touch
point) and imported `transnet_etenders.py` cleanly - both unaffected, confirming no stray import/syntax
issue from this change.

**Regression:** `engine/discovery/boq_extraction.py` (`_SKIP_ROW_RE`, ~10 lines including comment);
`engine/discovery/test_boq_extraction.py` (one new test function, wired into `main()`). No change to the
`vat`/`page`/`carried forward`/`brought down`/`notes` skip branches, the numeric-quantity-ratio check, or
any other guard in the module.

### Finding 130 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, moderate - a malformed pack.yaml made `fill_financial.py` raise a raw `KeyError` instead of the `ValueError` its own caller specifically catches, crashing the WHOLE SANRAL pack build for one bad field in one sheet)

**Area:** SANRAL pack (`engine/fill_financial.py` - mechanical-field filler for the Financial Submission
workbook; had zero mentions in this file and no dedicated test at all before this pass).

**Scenario:** `main()` already raises a clean `ValueError` for one data-shaped refusal ("Position '...'
has no row on this Financial workbook's TENDERER INPUT DATA sheet") - and `pack/assemble_pack.py`'s own
caller (line ~318) specifically catches `ValueError` around `fill_financial.main()` and degrades
gracefully (`financial_out, financial_note = None, f"fill_financial.py refused: {e}"`, pack build
continues with the Technical workbook, Forms B1-B7, envelope covers all still produced). But three OTHER
equally-real malformed-pack shapes went through plain dict/key lookups with no guard at all, so they
raised a raw `KeyError` instead:
  - `pack["company"]["name"]` when the pack has no `company.name`;
  - `pack["people"][kp["person"]]` when a `key_persons` entry references a person key absent from the
    pack's own `people` map (a stale/inconsistent pack - the key_persons list and people map falling out
    of sync, e.g. a person removed or renamed upstream without updating both);
  - `person["name"]` when a `people` entry exists but has no `name` field.

A raw `KeyError` is NOT a `ValueError`, so `assemble_pack.py`'s existing catch never fires - it propagates
straight out of `main()` and crashes the entire SANRAL pack assembly (not just the Financial workbook)
for what should have been one gracefully-degraded sheet, exactly the "one contained module's own data
problem takes down the whole pack build" shape already fixed twice this session (Finding 125:
`make_envelope_covers.py`; Finding 128's sweep: the job-queue bridges).

**Fix:** wrapped the `company.name` lookup in its own `try/except KeyError` raising a clear `ValueError`
naming the gap; replaced the two unguarded `people`-map lookups with `.get()` + an explicit `None`/falsy
check, each raising a `ValueError` that names the dangling person key or missing field. All three now
match the module's own existing "data problem, not a worker crash" contract that `assemble_pack.py`
already relies on - no change needed in `assemble_pack.py` itself, since its existing `except ValueError`
now correctly catches all four refusal shapes instead of just one.

**Verified red-then-green.** New dedicated test file `engine/test_fill_financial.py` (none existed
before this pass) against the real shipped template
(`templates/samples/financial/R.334-030-2025.1F_Financial_Submission_ran.xlsm`, not a hand-built
fixture) - one happy-path test plus three adversarial-pack tests, each asserting a `ValueError` (naming
the bad field) is raised, not a raw `KeyError`. Revert-and-confirm-red on `fill_financial.py` alone: all
three adversarial tests failed exactly as predicted (`raised a raw KeyError instead of ValueError:
KeyError('ghost')` / `KeyError('name')` / `KeyError('name')`), the happy-path test still passed; restored,
`0 failure(s)` across all four tests. `py_compile` clean on both touched files. Regression:
`test_form_field_audit.py` (exercises `fill_financial.row_for_position()` against all 6 real sample
contracts) and `pack/test_assemble_pack.py` both re-ran clean, unaffected.

**Regression:** `engine/fill_financial.py` (`main()`, ~15 lines including comments); new file
`engine/test_fill_financial.py` (4 tests). No change to `row_for_position()`, the SANRAL-confirmed row
mapping, or `assemble_pack.py`'s own existing `except ValueError` handling.

### Finding 131 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, moderate - found in TWO files - a smart quote/en-dash in a copy-pasted company or signatory name rendered as a silent "?" on a real printed MBD/SBD form and on every SANRAL pack's own page-number stamp, with the self-verification check fooled into reporting it as correctly placed)

**Area:** non-SANRAL pack (`engine/general/fill_flat_pdf.py`'s `_pdf_str()`/`verify_placements()`) and,
found in the same sweep, SANRAL pack (`engine/pack/pdf_merge.py`'s `_pdf_text()` - explicitly named by
`fill_flat_pdf.py`'s own docstring as "the same technique" this module borrowed its overlay-text
approach from).

**Scenario:** both files draw text onto a PDF page with a hand-built `/Type1 /BaseFont /Helvetica`
overlay font whose `/Encoding` is declared `/WinAnsiEncoding` - i.e. cp1252. But the helper that escapes
the text for the `Tj` operator (`_pdf_str()` in `fill_flat_pdf.py`, `_pdf_text()` in `pdf_merge.py`) encoded
with Python's `"latin-1"` codec instead - a DIFFERENT single-byte encoding that disagrees with cp1252 in
the 0x80-0x9F byte range, where WinAnsi/cp1252 places the right/left single and double smart quotes
(`'`/`'`/`"`/`"`), en/em dashes, bullets and the trademark sign. None of those characters is encodable in
latin-1 at all (its range is only U+0000-U+00FF; a smart quote is U+2019, far outside it), so
`.encode("latin-1", "replace")` silently replaced every one of them with a literal `"?"` - and this is
NOT an exotic input: it is exactly what Microsoft Word's own autocorrect puts into a copy-pasted company
or signatory name the moment someone types a plain apostrophe or hyphen ("O'Brien's Construction" typed
in Word becomes `O'Brien's Construction`, a company name South African tender-prep staff paste into the
Tender Workspace from a Word document routinely).

Confirmed live:
```python
>>> "O’Brien’s Construction – Civils".encode("latin-1", "replace")
b'O?Brien?s Construction ? Civils'
```

Worse, `fill_flat_pdf.py`'s own `verify_placements()` - the "nothing is assumed to have worked" read-back
check this module's whole docstring is built around, and the exact mechanism the 2026-10-29 whitespace-
only finding already caught being fooled once - re-derived its comparison string by applying the SAME
lossy `.encode("latin-1", "replace")` to `pl.value` before comparing. So the degraded `"?"` on both sides
of the comparison matched each other, and the field was reported `"placed"` (verified, correctly done)
even though the real printed MBD 1 / Form of Offer / CEQ showed `"O?Brien?s Construction"` instead of
the company's real legal name - silently wrong data on a real buyer-facing submission, with the report
actively vouching for it.

`pdf_merge.py`'s `_pdf_text()` has the identical shape in its page-number stamp (`_stamp()`), used on
every page of every SANRAL and general pack this engine builds. Its current caller only ever passes a
plain contract number (`stamp_label`, e.g. `"R.334-030-2025.1F"`), so it isn't yet reachable through
today's one call site - but the helper itself is general-purpose, carries the exact same docstring-cited
"same technique" relationship to `fill_flat_pdf.py`, and the same fix costs nothing extra once the shape
is already understood, so it was fixed in the same pass rather than left for a future caller to
rediscover.

**Fix:** both helpers now encode with `"cp1252"` first (what the declared `/WinAnsiEncoding` font
encoding actually means) and then decode those bytes with `"latin-1"` - a byte-value-preserving
round-trip, so the later plain `.encode("latin-1")` deeper in each module still succeeds trivially and
reproduces the exact correct cp1252 bytes. `fill_flat_pdf.py`'s `verify_placements()` was also fixed to
compare against the TRUE `pl.value` directly, not a re-degraded copy of it - so a character genuinely
outside cp1252's own repertoire (true non-Western script, an emoji) now correctly FAILS verification
(`"written but did not read back from the PDF - check by eye"`) instead of silently "passing" because
both sides of the comparison lost the same character the same way.

**Verified red-then-green, both files, independently.** `engine/general/test_fill_flat_pdf.py`: new
smart-quote/en-dash case added to the existing real-synthetic-MBD1 harness, placing `"O'Brien-Smith"`
as the signatory's contact-person value and reading the REAL output PDF back with `pdfplumber` to assert
the genuine `'`/`-` characters are present and no `"?"` leaked in. `engine/pack/test_pdf_merge.py`: new
`test_stamp_renders_a_smart_quote_en_dash_as_the_real_glyph_not_a_question_mark()`, calling `_stamp()`
directly on a real blank page and reading the written PDF back with `pdfplumber`. Reverted each file
individually: both failed exactly as predicted (`'O?Brien?Smith Civils'` / the flat-PDF equivalent with
`"?"` in place of both real characters); restored: `0 failure(s)` on both test files. `py_compile` clean
on all four touched files. Regression: `test_form_field_audit.py` (fill_sbd_docx/fill_flat_pdf's
Klipcorp-divergent audit) and `pack/test_assemble_pack.py` both re-ran clean.

**Regression:** `engine/general/fill_flat_pdf.py` (`_pdf_str()`, `verify_placements()`, ~20 lines
including comments); `engine/pack/pdf_merge.py` (`_pdf_text()`, ~10 lines including comments);
`engine/general/test_fill_flat_pdf.py` (4 new checks on the existing harness); `engine/pack/
test_pdf_merge.py` (1 new test function, wired into `main()`). No change to either module's own
text-measurement (`text_width()`/`_fit()`), placement-geometry, or verification-box logic - only the
final character encoding and the verify-step's own comparison string.

### Finding 132 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, severe - a real, already-built, already-tested compliance check (a document that is fine today but will have lapsed by a tender's own closing date) never actually reached a real company's inbox, because `daily_digest.py`'s live mode - the automated pipeline that actually sends the digest email - never called it)

**Area:** compliance/reminders (`engine/notify/daily_digest.py` / `engine/notify/send_digest_emails.py`,
found while confirming `engine/compliance/watch_deadlines.py`/`registration_reminders.py` were already
exhausted for this rotation).

**Scenario:** `watch_deadlines.find_documents_lapsing_before_closing()` is a real, carefully-built
function (added 2026-10-17, hardened again 2026-10-24 for a SAST closing-time edge case) that catches
exactly the gap a plain 60-day expiry window can't see: a document that is still "fine" by the normal
measure today, but will already have expired by the closing date of a tender the company is actively
preparing (a `tender_packs` row exists for it). It is fully tested
(`engine/compliance/test_watch_deadlines_urgency.py`) and already wired into `watch_deadlines.py`'s own
`--out` JSON report. But `daily_digest.py` - the script whose live mode actually builds the automated
digest email every opted-in company receives via `send_digest_emails.py` - built its `document_expiry`
section from `find_due_documents()` + `find_due_person_credentials()` + the two registration-catalog
functions (`registration_reminders.find_due_registrations()`/`find_due_property_documents()`), and
never called `find_documents_lapsing_before_closing()` at all. Confirmed by grep before this fix: zero
references to it anywhere under `engine/notify/`.

End to end: a company could have, say, a SARS Tax Compliance Status PIN expiring in 90 days - genuinely
outside the normal 60-day "renew soon" window, so `find_due_documents()` has nothing to report - while
preparing a tender closing in 100 days. The one automated channel built specifically to catch this exact
risk (a document that will be expired on submission day, even though it looks perfectly fine today)
computes the right answer every time `watch_deadlines.py` runs, but that answer never reaches the
company's actual inbox - only a separate, non-automated channel (an external scheduled session reading
`watch_deadlines.py --out report.json` directly, per that script's own docstring) would ever see it. A
company relying on the real digest email alone would have no warning at all until the document was
already inside the normal 60-day window - by which point, on this scenario, the tender would already be
closed.

**Fix:** extracted the inline `document_expiry` build in `daily_digest.py`'s live mode into a new,
directly-testable `document_expiry_signals(url, key, seen, today, lead_days)` function, and added the
missing `+ watch_deadlines.find_documents_lapsing_before_closing(...)` call to it (same pattern every

### Finding 133 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, severe - a transient failure recording ONE recipient's pack-ready email permanently lost the email for every OTHER recipient too, on a one-shot notification that never gets a second chance)

**Area:** notify (`engine/notify/send_pack_ready_email.py` - the Bid Pack Compilation Complete email,
sent right after a `generate_pack` job goes `ready`).

**Scenario:** this file's own history already fixed this exact bug CLASS twice - `claim_notification()`
(a one-time-only token; this job id never runs again) used to be called too early, so a failure in the
recipients lookup/render/tender-select (2026-10-30) or a missing API key (2026-10-28) would burn the
claim with nothing ever sent. Both fixes moved the claim to immediately before the first real send. But
the per-recipient loop AFTER that claim has its own, un-isolated version of the identical risk:

```python
for to in recipients:
    result = _send_via_resend(to, email["subject"], email["html"], email["text"])
    client.rpc("record_notification_sent", {...})   # a real network RPC call, no guard
```

`_send_via_resend()` already never raises (its own blanket except converts every failure to a
`{"status": "failed", ...}` dict) - but `record_notification_sent()`'s own RPC call can genuinely fail
transiently (a network blip, a Supabase hiccup), and when it does for the FIRST recipient, the exception
propagates out of the loop into the function's OUTER `except Exception`, which returns - the loop never
reaches the SECOND (or any later) recipient at all. Since the claim is already consumed and this job id
never runs again, every recipient after the one whose audit-write happened to fail would PERMANENTLY
never receive the pack-ready email, with no retry possible.

Confirmed live: a fake client with two opted-in recipients, where `record_notification_sent` raises only
for the first recipient's call - the real Resend send was attempted for recipient 1 only; recipient 2
got nothing at all, silently, with just one generic `"pack_ready email failed for job ..."` alert giving
no hint that a second person was also owed an email and never got one.

**Fix:** wrapped only the `record_notification_sent()` call (not `_send_via_resend()`, which can't raise)
in its own `try/except` inside the loop, recording a per-recipient `system_alerts` warning that
explicitly says the send itself already happened and only the audit-log write may be missing, then
continuing to the next recipient - same per-item isolation pattern as every "claim call sits outside its
own try block" fix this session (Findings 123/126/128), applied here to an audit-write failure rather
than a claim failure, inside a loop that this file's own commit history already protected the OUTSIDE
of twice.

**Verified red-then-green.** New test
`test_one_recipients_record_notification_sent_failure_does_not_lose_the_rest()` in
`engine/notify/test_send_pack_ready_email.py` - two opted-in recipients, `record_notification_sent`
monkeypatched to raise only for the first; asserts BOTH recipients get a real Resend send attempt and
both get a `record_notification_sent` call attempted (the second succeeding). Reverted the production
file alone: failed exactly as predicted (`sent_to == ['a@example.com']`, recipient b lost); restored:
`0 failure(s)` across all 7 tests in the file. `py_compile` clean on both touched files. Regression:
`process_general_jobs.py`'s own test suite (the real caller) re-ran clean.

**Regression:** `engine/notify/send_pack_ready_email.py` (one `try/except` added inside the per-recipient
loop, ~20 lines including comments); `engine/notify/test_send_pack_ready_email.py` (1 new test function,
wired into `main()`). No change to `claim_notification()`'s own timing, the missing-API-key check, or
`_send_via_resend()`'s own failure handling.

### Finding 134 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, severe - the "claim call sits outside its own try block, no per-item isolation in the polling loop" bug class, Finding 128's own "deliberate sweep", missed `process_cv_jobs.py` - the one real CV-document-GENERATION bridge - at the time)

**Area:** worker/job-queue (`engine/cv/process_cv_jobs.py` - CV document generation, distinct from
`extract_cv_fields.py`'s own CV-field-EXTRACTION bridge, which Finding 126 already fixed for this exact
shape).

**Scenario:** Finding 128 (2026-11-04) explicitly declared this bug class "exhausted" after sweeping
every remaining `process_*_jobs.py` bridge: `process_pack_jobs.py`, `process_general_jobs.py`,
`process_narrative_jobs.py`, `process_onboarding_jobs.py`. `process_cv_jobs.py` - a fifth, distinct
bridge in the same family (`generated_cvs` jobs, polled by `poll_once()`, each one claimed by
`claim_job()` before `process_job()`'s own try block) - was never included in that sweep's file list,
and turned out to have the identical shape: `claim_job()` sits BEFORE `process_job()`'s own `try:`, and
`poll_once()`'s own `for job in jobs: if process_job(...): handled += 1` has no try/except around the
call either. `process_job()` itself never re-raises (its blanket `except Exception` always marks the
job failed and returns `True`) - so the only way a job here could still raise is `claim_job()`'s own
`supabase_request()` call (a network blip, a 500). Before this fix, that propagated straight out of
`poll_once()`'s loop, aborting the whole pass: a second, genuinely pending CV generation job was never
even attempted that cycle, not just the one whose claim failed.

Confirmed live: two queued `generated_cvs` jobs, `claim_job()` made to raise for the first -
`poll_once()` crashed with an uncaught `RuntimeError` before ever reaching the second job's own claim
attempt.

**Fix:** wrapped the per-item `process_job(...)` call in `poll_once()`'s own loop in `try/except`,
alerting under the bridge's existing `system_alerts` source (`"cv"`) and continuing to the next job -
identical pattern to Findings 123/126/128.

**Verified red-then-green.** New test
`test_poll_once_does_not_abort_the_whole_pass_when_one_jobs_claim_fails()` in
`engine/cv/test_process_cv_jobs.py`, monkeypatching the real `supabase_request`/`fetch_job_context` to
make the first of two queued jobs' claim raise while the second succeeds - confirms the second job is
still attempted (and its own, separate in-`process_job()` failure is handled normally) and the claim
failure gets its own alert. Revert-and-confirm-red on the production file alone: reproduced the exact
predicted uncaught `RuntimeError` at the claim call site; restored, `0 failure(s)` across the whole
file. `py_compile` clean on both touched files. Full regression sweep across every bridge touched this
session (`run_bridges.py`/`test_poll_loop.py`, `extract_cv_fields.py`/`test_extract_cv_fields.py`, and
all four of Finding 128's own fixes) - all clean, this bridge is now the last one of six, genuinely
exhausted.

**Regression:** `engine/cv/process_cv_jobs.py` (`poll_once()`, ~15 lines including comment);
`engine/cv/test_process_cv_jobs.py` (1 new test function). No change to `process_job()`'s own exception
handling, `claim_job()`'s own call shape, or `fail_stale_jobs()`.

### Finding 135 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, severe - Eskom's own REFERENCE field truncates at 20 characters, cutting a glued notice word mid-word on a real, live bulletin entry; the old word list never matched the surviving fragment, so `refers_to_reference` for over a quarter of all real notice entries checked could never match any real tender, silently orphaning the notice)

**Area:** discovery (`engine/discovery/eskom_bulletin.py` - Eskom's own Tender Bulletin reader, zero
mentions in this file and zero dedicated test coverage before this pass beyond the shared
`test_gov_sources.py` fixture).

**Scenario:** `base_reference()` recovers the real tender a notice entry (cancellation, award, regret,
validity extension, bidders list, ...) refers to, by stripping Eskom's own glued notice word off its
`REFERENCE` field (e.g. `"E3484CXMWPList of bidders"` -> `"E3484CXMWP"`). `tender_changes.py` then uses
that recovered reference to attach the notice, as a change event, onto the REAL tender a customer is
already seeing - the whole point of reading this notice at all.

Fetched the real, live bulletin (322 entries, 2026-11-05) to check this against actual production data,
not a constructed scenario. Confirmed: Eskom's `REFERENCE` field truncates at exactly 20 characters - so
when a notice word glued onto a long enough base reference would push the combined string past that
limit, the notice word itself gets CUT MID-WORD:

```
'E2116DXFSOURValidit'    - "Validity" missing its own final letter
'E2292GXMPKRINOTIFICA'   - "Notification" cut to 8 letters ("NOTIFICA") - a word this list never had at all
'NAMEOFE2818GXMPARNR'    - the list only had plural "names", not singular "name"
'BIDDERSNAME1404GXPOU'   - "bidders" alone stripped, leaving "NAME" glued to the real reference behind it
```

None of these matched any word already in `REF_NOTICE_WORDS`, so `base_reference()` fell through to
returning the WHOLE original string unchanged - still carrying the notice word - which then matches no
real tender's own clean reference. Scanning all 139 real notice entries in the live fetch: **38 of them**
(over a quarter) came back with a `refers_to_reference` that could never match anything, silently
orphaning the notice - the cancellation/award/validity-extension event gets computed but never reaches
the tender it was actually about, exactly the "silently wrong data" risk this whole module exists to
avoid.

**Fix:** added `"validit"` (after the existing full `"validity"` - Python's `re` module tries
alternatives left to right and stops at the FIRST match, not the longest, so order matters: the longer
word must be tried first or the shorter one wins and leaves a trailing character glued to what
follows), `"notifica"` (new - `"notification"` was never in the list), and `"nameof"`/`"name"` (the list
only had plural `"names"`; `"nameof"` must precede the shorter `"name"` for the same left-to-right
reason). Confirmed by re-fetching the live bulletin after the fix: 38 of the 41 originally-broken cases
now resolve correctly. The remaining 3 (`REGRETLETTERA`, `CANCELLATIONTLETTER`, `CancellationLetter`)
have ZERO digits in their own `REFERENCE` field at all - the real tender reference exists only inside
`HEADER_DESC` text (e.g. `"CANCELLATION-E2126DXKZN-The establishment..."`) - genuinely unfixable from
`base_reference(ref)` alone, since it only ever receives the reference string, never the header. Left
as a known, smaller, separate gap (would need `HEADER_DESC` parsing, a bigger scope change) rather than
widening this fix to chase it.

**Verified red-then-green.** Four new rows added to `test_gov_sources.py`'s own `ESKOM_NOTICES` fixture
(already used by `test_eskom()`), using the exact real `REFERENCE`/`HEADER_DESC` pairs confirmed from
the live bulletin - asserting both the correct `classify()` kind and the correct recovered
`base_reference()`. Revert-and-confirm-red on the production file alone: all four new checks failed
exactly as predicted (`refers to E2116DXFSOUR`, `refers to E2292GXMPKRI`, `refers to E2818GXMPARNR`,
`refers to 1404GXPOU`); restored: `ALL PASSED`. `py_compile` clean on both touched files. Regression:
`test_tender_updates.py` and `test_download_discovered_documents.py` both re-ran clean.

**Regression:** `engine/discovery/eskom_bulletin.py` (`REF_NOTICE_WORDS`, 4 words added/reordered, ~20
lines including comments); `engine/discovery/test_gov_sources.py` (4 new fixture rows in
`ESKOM_NOTICES`). No change to `classify()`'s own pattern matching, `normalize()`, or any other
notice-word list's ordering.

### Finding 136 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, severe - `company_documents.write_docx()` was the ONE docx writer in this engine that never got the control-character guard every sibling writer needed; a stray control character in a tender's own buyer-published/OCR'd description crashed the WHOLE SANRAL pack build, not just the authority letter)

**Area:** SANRAL pack (`engine/company_documents.py` - the per-company letter-of-authority-to-sign
mechanism, called from `assemble_pack.py`'s SANRAL pack build).

**Scenario:** this exact bug class - a stray control character (`\x00-\x08`, `\x0B`, `\x0C`, `\x0E-\x1F`)
in a tender's own buyer-published/OCR'd text crashing python-docx/lxml with a raw `ValueError: All
strings must be XML compatible...` - has now been found and fixed FIVE times this session across every
other docx-writing function in this engine: `generate_cv.py` (original), `make_envelope_covers.py`
(Finding 125), `pdf_merge.py`'s contents-page builder and `build_general_pack.py`'s completion guide
(commit `b099ce5`), and `sanral_fill.py`'s `Workbook.set_value()` (commit `59c20a7`). `company_documents.
write_docx()` - the authority-to-sign letter's own docx writer - was the one writer this sweep never
reached: it writes `text` straight into python-docx paragraph runs (`p.add_run(line)`,
`p.add_run(block[2:].strip())`) with zero sanitisation.

`text` can genuinely carry a control character: `authority_facts()` sets `"tender_description":
tender.get("description")` - a buyer-published, sometimes OCR'd field - and a company whose own
guideline marks `{{tender_description}}` has that raw text substituted straight in via `fill_fields()`.
`assemble_pack.py`'s own call to `fill_authority_letter.produce_letter()` (line ~364) has NO try/except
around it - unlike several of the OTHER steps in the same pipeline, which already learned this lesson
(Finding 125's own fix was specifically about `make_envelope_covers.py` having no try/except either) -
so a crash here takes down the entire SANRAL pack build, not just the one letter.

Confirmed live: `company_documents.write_docx("...\x0b...", out)` raised
`ValueError: All strings must be XML compatible...` exactly as every prior instance of this bug class did.

**Fix:** imported `generate_cv._safe_text()` (the same `_XML_INVALID_RE` sanitiser every sibling fix
this session already reuses rather than re-implementing) and applied it to `text` at the top of
`write_docx()`, before any paragraph is built from it - one line, matching the minimal-footprint pattern
every prior fix in this class used.

**Verified red-then-green.** New case "6c" in `engine/test_company_documents.py`'s own `run()` - a
company whose guideline marks `{{tender_description}}`, fed a tender description with an embedded
control character (matching the real `assemble_pack.py` call shape exactly, through
`fill_authority_letter.produce_letter()`, not a direct call to `write_docx()`) - asserts no crash, the
letter still generates, and the real text on either side of the control character survives with just
the control character itself removed. Reverted the production file alone: failed exactly as predicted
(the control-character crash); restored: `0 failure(s)` across the whole file. `py_compile` clean on
both touched files. Regression: `pack/test_assemble_pack.py`, `cv/test_extract_cv_fields.py` (confirms
the new `cv/` sys.path insert doesn't collide with CV's own module resolution) and `test_fill_financial.py`
all re-ran clean.

**Regression:** `engine/company_documents.py` (one `sys.path`/import line, one `_safe_text()` call in
`write_docx()`, ~15 lines including comment); `engine/test_company_documents.py` (1 new case, "6c").
No change to `fill_fields()`, `guard_only_company_wording()`, `render_guideline()`'s own AI-placement
logic, or any other document type's handling.

### Finding 138 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, moderate - `years_experience_at()`'s own malformed-date guard only caught an unparsable STRING; a non-string `initial_graduated` value raised an uncaught `TypeError` from the exact same call site, the identical gap `watch_deadlines.days_until()` was fixed for)

**Area:** CV (`engine/pack_generator/suggest_pack.py`'s `years_experience_at()` - called by both
`generate_cv.py`'s CV builders and `score_candidate()`'s SANRAL key-person suggestion scoring).

**Scenario:** this function's own docstring already describes being fixed once for "a malformed
`initial_graduated`" crashing "suggestion-building for the WHOLE company, not just that one person" -
but its `try: grad = datetime.date.fromisoformat(grad) except ValueError:` only catches an unparsable
STRING. `watch_deadlines.days_until()` (QA pass, 2026-10-23) was fixed for the exact same underlying
risk - a value that isn't a string at all (a number, bool, or a list/dict, the kind of thing a hand-
edited profile JSON with no schema behind it can genuinely hold, e.g. `suggest_pack.suggest()`'s own
`--profile` file or `daily_digest.py --mode local`'s) - and that fix's own docstring explicitly
documents WHY a bare `except ValueError` isn't enough: a non-string value raises `TypeError` from
`fromisoformat()`, not `ValueError`. `years_experience_at()` was never given the same guard.

Confirmed live: `years_experience_at({"qualifications": {"initial_graduated": 20261231}}, closing_date)`
(and the same for `True`, a list, and a dict) raises `TypeError: fromisoformat: argument must be str`,
uncaught.

**Fix:** added the identical `isinstance(grad, str)` check `days_until()` already uses, before the
`fromisoformat()` call - returning `None` (the function's own existing "treat as unknown" contract,
already handled by both real callers) with the same kind of actionable warning the existing
`ValueError` path already prints.

**Verified red-then-green.** New test
`test_years_experience_at_survives_a_malformed_non_string_initial_graduated()` in
`engine/pack_generator/test_suggest_pack.py` - a bare int, a stray boolean, a list, and a dict, each
asserting `None` with no crash; plus unaffected-case checks (a falsy `False`, a genuinely malformed
string, a real valid date). Revert-and-confirm-red on the production file alone: all four new bad-input
checks failed exactly as predicted (`raised TypeError: fromisoformat: argument must be str`); restored:
`0 failure(s)` across the whole file. `py_compile` clean on both touched files. Regression:
`pack/test_process_pack_jobs.py` (the real `score_candidate()` caller's own test suite) and
`cv/test_generate_cv.py` both re-ran clean.

**Regression:** `engine/pack_generator/suggest_pack.py` (`years_experience_at()`, ~10 lines including
comments); `engine/pack_generator/test_suggest_pack.py` (1 new test function, wired into `main()`). No
change to `score_candidate()`'s own scoring logic, `rank_candidates()`'s tie-break, or the existing
`ValueError` path.

### Finding 139 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, moderate - the proactive "lapses before closing" check Finding 132 added for company-wide VAULT DOCUMENTS never existed for a key PERSON's own professional registration, a gap Finding 132 itself explicitly flagged but deliberately did not fix)

**Area:** Compliance / reminders (`engine/compliance/watch_deadlines.py`, wired into
`engine/notify/daily_digest.py`'s live digest).

**Scenario:** Finding 132 fixed the live digest to call
`find_documents_lapsing_before_closing()` - a document that is fine TODAY, outside the normal
60-day reminder window, but will genuinely have lapsed by the closing date of a tender the company
has a pack for. That finding's own writeup explicitly noted the identical gap existed for a key
PERSON's own professional registration (`ecsa_expiry`/`sacpcmp_expiry`/`sacnasp_expiry`/
`sagc_expiry`, `TRACKED_PERSON_EXPIRY_FIELDS`) - a person whose ECSA registration, say, is valid for
another 90 days (well outside the 60-day window `find_due_person_credentials()` already covers) but
will have lapsed before the SPECIFIC tender they are confirmed onto closes in 100 days, was never
proactively flagged anywhere; only reactively, if someone happened to open that tender's own
compliance report page (`app/lib/tenderCompliance.ts`). Finding 132 left this gap open for Sarel's
own call on priority rather than fixing it inline.

**Fix:** new function `find_person_credentials_lapsing_before_closing(url, key, seen, today,
lead_days)` in `watch_deadlines.py`, mirroring `find_documents_lapsing_before_closing()`'s exact SAST
closing-day math and "already inside the normal window" / "already expired" guards (so this never
duplicates what `find_due_person_credentials()` already reports), scoped per PERSON and per
ASSIGNMENT rather than company-wide. Joins `tender_pack_assignments` on `confirmed_person_id` -
deliberately the human-set, hard-gated assignment field, never the merely AI-`suggested_person_id` -
through `tender_packs` to the real `tenders` row (for `closing_date`/`status`/`contract_no`) and
`people` (for the tracked expiry columns). Wired into `daily_digest.py`'s
`document_expiry_signals()` as an 8th OR-term.

**Verified with a real adversarial scenario**: new test
`find_person_credentials_lapsing_before_closing_scopes_to_the_real_assignment()` in
`test_watch_deadlines_urgency.py` constructs two people sharing an IDENTICAL expiring ECSA
credential - one (`p-assigned`) referenced by a real `tender_pack_assignments` row confirming them
onto a specific open tender, one (`p-unassigned`) referenced by no assignment at all - and confirms
only the confirmed person is reported, naming the real tender they're confirmed onto (not any other
open tender the company happens to have a pack for), with seen-store de-dup proven across a second
same-day run.

**Caught and fixed my own bug in the new test before it reached production code**: my first draft's
final assertion passed the raw result dict as the `check(cond, msg)` helper's `msg` argument -
`check(item["field"] == "ecsa_expiry" and ..., item)` - but that helper unconditionally does
`"  PASS " + msg`/`"  FAIL " + msg`, so a non-string `msg` crashes with `TypeError: can only
concatenate str (not "dict") to str` regardless of `cond`'s truth value, independent of whether the
production code itself was correct. Confirmed via an actual run: the first three checks of the new
test printed PASS correctly (proving the production function itself was already working: exactly 1
item returned, for the right person, naming the right tender) before this line crashed the whole
script before the file's own pre-existing multi-pass scenario ever ran. Fixed by formatting it as
`f"{item}"`, matching every other `check()` call in this file.

**Verified red-then-green, precisely.** `git diff` of the two production files
(`watch_deadlines.py`, `daily_digest.py`) saved to a patch, reverted with `git apply -R`, re-ran
`test_watch_deadlines_urgency.py` - failed exactly as predicted, `AttributeError: module
'watch_deadlines' has no attribute 'find_person_credentials_lapsing_before_closing'`; reapplied the
patch, re-ran - `0 failure(s)`, including the file's own pre-existing multi-pass `main()` scenario
(document/task reminders, escalation-on-expiry, SAST closing-day math) running clean end to end.
`py_compile` clean on all three touched files. Regression: `engine/notify/test_digest_live.py` and
`engine/notify/test_send_digest_emails.py` (both exercise `document_expiry_signals()`'s own call
site directly) - both `0 failure(s)`, no change in behaviour for any existing scenario.

**Regression:** `engine/compliance/watch_deadlines.py` (1 new function, ~100 lines including
docstring/comments, inserted between `find_documents_lapsing_before_closing()` and
`find_due_tasks()`); `engine/notify/daily_digest.py` (`document_expiry_signals()`, 1 new OR-term plus
explanatory comment); `engine/compliance/test_watch_deadlines_urgency.py` (1 new test function, wired
into `main()`). No change to `find_documents_lapsing_before_closing()`, `find_due_person_credentials()`,
or any other existing reminder path.

### Finding 140 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, moderate - a "lapses before closing" digest line silently duplicated the tender's closing date and never showed the document/credential's own actual expiry date, the one fact a reader needs to know when to renew by)

**Area:** Notify (`engine/notify/send_digest_emails.py`'s `render_text()` - the actual customer-facing
email body, not `daily_digest.py`'s assembly step).

**Scenario:** found while adversarially testing Finding 139's new `person_credential_before_closing`
item shape against the real email renderer, not just the JSON `daily_digest.py` builds. A
`lapses_before_closing` item (both `find_documents_lapsing_before_closing()`'s own
`document_before_closing` items, and Finding 139's new `person_credential_before_closing` items)
carries BOTH `expiry_date` (the document/credential's own real lapse date - the one thing the reader
actually needs, to know when to renew by) AND `closing_date` (the tender's) on the SAME item -
confirmed by reading both functions' own `due.append({...})` dict literals directly. `_item_date()`'s
own documented priority order checks `"closing_date"` BEFORE `"expiry_date"` - correct for
`new_tenders`/`submission_due` items, which never set `expiry_date` at all, but this is the one
`document_expiry` shape where both keys coexist on the same item. The trailing `(date)` `render_text()`
always appended after its own custom "will have lapsed before X closes (closing_date)" sentence
therefore silently resolved to `closing_date` again - duplicating the exact date already shown - while
the document/credential's own real `expiry_date` never appeared in the sent email anywhere at all.

Confirmed live by calling `render_text()` directly with a real item shape (not assumed from reading the
code): `SARS Tax Compliance Status PIN - will have lapsed before R.396-010-2025/1F closes (2027-01-05)
(2027-01-05)` - the same date twice, and the item's real `expiry_date` (`2027-01-15`) nowhere in the
email. Identical for the new person-credential shape. This predates Finding 139 entirely (Finding 132,
2026-11-05, introduced the first instance of this item shape) - Finding 139 only inherited the same
bug by correctly mirroring that shape, and widened its real-world reach (both document AND person
items now hit it on every send that includes one).

**Fix:** when `status == "lapses_before_closing"`, the sentence now names both dates explicitly -
`"{label} (expires {expiry_date}) - will have lapsed before {tender_label} closes ({closing_date})"`
- and the generic trailing `_item_date(item)` call is skipped for this branch entirely (both dates are
already shown inline, so appending a third copy would either re-duplicate `closing_date` or, if
`_item_date()`'s order were naively flipped instead, misapply `expiry_date`'s meaning to every OTHER
section that relies on the existing priority order for its own, non-overlapping date key).

**Verified red-then-green.** New test
`test_render_text_does_not_duplicate_the_closing_date_or_drop_the_real_expiry_date()` in
`test_send_digest_emails.py`, covering both the original `document_before_closing` shape and Finding
139's `person_credential_before_closing` shape (plus confirming the person-name prefix and the
tender's own closing date each still appear exactly once). Reverted `send_digest_emails.py` via `git
apply -R`, re-ran - both new checks failed exactly as predicted, printing the real duplicated-date
body; reapplied, re-ran - `0 failure(s)`. `py_compile` clean on both touched files. Regression:
`test_digest_live.py`, `test_send_pack_ready_email.py`, `test_digest_opt_in.py` - all `0 failure(s)`,
no behavioural change to any other section's rendering.

**Regression:** `engine/notify/send_digest_emails.py` (`render_text()`, one `if`/`else` branch
restructured, ~20 lines including comments); `engine/notify/test_send_digest_emails.py` (1 new test
function, wired into `main()`). No change to `_item_date()` itself, `send_one()`, or any other
section's rendering logic.

### Finding 141 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, low real-world severity since unreached in production - `poll_loop.poll_forever()`'s own `max_runtime` parameter always read the REAL wall clock even when `sleep` was faked, so pairing it with this module's own documented test-injection pattern busy-spins at full CPU for `max_runtime`'s own real duration instead of behaving deterministically)

**Area:** Worker / job-queue (`engine/worker/poll_loop.py` - the one polling loop shared by every
async bridge: `process_cv_jobs.py`, `process_general_jobs.py`, `extract_cv_fields.py`,
`process_onboarding_jobs.py`, `process_narrative_jobs.py`, `process_pack_jobs.py`, and
`run_bridges.py` itself).

**Scenario:** `max_cycles`/`max_runtime` bound the loop, per this module's own docstring, "(tests, and
any host that wants a run to end on its own)". `max_cycles` is exercised by every existing test and by
`run_bridges.py`'s own `--max-cycles` flag. `max_runtime` had ZERO test coverage anywhere in the repo
and ZERO real callers (confirmed by grepping every bridge and `run_bridges.py` for `max_runtime`) -
unreached in production, but a real, documented, public parameter of a shared module, not dead code by
accident.

Writing this parameter's first-ever test, by following the module's own explicitly documented
convention for every OTHER test in this file ("`sleep` is injectable so tests can prove the loop
really sleeps between polls without waiting in real time") immediately produced a real bug:
`started = time.monotonic()` and the `max_runtime` check's own `time.monotonic() - started + interval
> max_runtime` both called the REAL wall clock directly, with no injection point - unlike `sleep`,
which is fully injectable. Pairing a no-op/instant fake `sleep` (exactly what every other test in this
file does to stay fast and deterministic) with `max_runtime` therefore busy-spins the loop at full CPU
for `max_runtime`'s own REAL wall-clock duration, since the only thing that could ever make the check
trip is actual time passing. Confirmed directly: `interval=0.05, max_runtime=0.3` with a no-op sleep
produced **403,277 wasted cycles over ~0.25 real seconds** instead of the ~6 logical cycles a
deterministic test expects - not a crash or a hang, but a real CPU-burning footgun for the exact
testing pattern this module tells its own users to rely on.

**Fix:** added an injectable `now` parameter (default `time.monotonic`, same shape as the existing
`sleep` injection), and replaced both `time.monotonic()` call sites (`started = ...` and the
`max_runtime` check itself) with it. Zero behaviour change for every real caller (none pass `now`,
so `time.monotonic` is used exactly as before) - purely additive test-support, mirroring the module's
own existing `sleep` pattern.

**Verified red-then-green.** New test
`test_max_runtime_uses_an_injectable_clock_not_the_real_one()` in `test_poll_loop.py`, using a fake
`now`/`sleep` pair that advances a shared logical clock (`fake_sleep` adds to `clock["t"]`, `fake_now`
reads it) - asserts the loop stops after exactly 4 cycles (0, 30, 60, 90 -> would be 120 > 100),
instantly, with zero real waiting. Reverted `poll_loop.py` via `git apply -R`, re-ran - the test itself
can no longer even call the old signature (`TypeError: poll_forever() got an unexpected keyword
argument 'now'`), confirming red without needing to re-trigger the actual busy-spin; reapplied -
`0 failure(s)` across the WHOLE `test_poll_loop.py` suite (including `run_bridges.py`'s own SIGTERM/
timeout/Popen-failure tests, unaffected by this change). `py_compile` clean on both touched files.
Regression: all 5 bridges' own test suites (`process_cv_jobs.py`, `process_general_jobs.py`,
`extract_cv_fields.py`'s sibling, `process_onboarding_jobs.py`, `process_narrative_jobs.py`,
`process_pack_jobs.py`) - all `0 failure(s)`, confirming the new `now` parameter's default behaviour
is identical to the old hardcoded call for every real caller.

**Regression:** `engine/worker/poll_loop.py` (`poll_forever()`, 1 new parameter, 2 call sites changed
from `time.monotonic()` to `now()`, ~15 lines including comments); `engine/worker/test_poll_loop.py`
(1 new test function, wired into `main()`). No change to `sleep`'s own injection, signal handling,
`max_cycles`, or any real bridge's call site (none pass `now`).

### Finding 142 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, low real-world severity since the one real write path already guards it client-side - `sanral_b7.py`'s own `_num()` never got the NaN/Infinity guard `fill_financial_hours.py`'s identical pattern was fixed for on 2026-10-28, so a NaN percentage sailed past `check_plan()`'s own validation and `fill_b7()` would have written it into the real SANRAL Form B7 workbook as a literal `<v>nan</v>` numeric cell)

**Area:** SANRAL pack (`engine/sanral_b7.py` - Form B7, "Subcontracting to Targeted Enterprises").

**Scenario:** `fill_financial_hours.py`'s own `fill()` was fixed on 2026-10-28 for a specific, already-
documented risk: a capture value of `.nan`/`.inf` (valid YAML 1.1 float literals PyYAML's own
`safe_load` parses without complaint) sails past a naive `hours < 0` guard (NaN compares `False` to
every comparison) and gets written into a real SANRAL workbook as a literal `<v>nan</v>`/`<v>inf</v>`
numeric cell - not valid per that cell's own XML Schema type, a real corruption risk. `sanral_b7.py`'s
own `_num()` helper, used by `check_plan()` to validate every Targeted Enterprise's
`pct_of_contract`/`pct_excl_provisional`/`black_ownership_pct`, has the IDENTICAL shape (`float(v)` with
only a bare `try/except (TypeError, ValueError)`, no `math.isfinite()` check) and was never swept for
this fix.

Confirmed directly: `_num(float("nan"))` returns `nan` (not `None`), and `check_plan()`'s own
`v is None or v < 0 or v > 100 or (key != "black_ownership_pct" and v == 0)` guard is entirely false for
NaN (every comparison with NaN is `False`) - so a NaN percentage produces **no error at all**, and
`fill_b7()` goes on to call `frac(te["pct_of_contract"])` (`round(nan / 100.0, 6)` = `nan`) and write it
via `wb.set_value()`, which (being a `float`) takes the numeric-cell branch and writes `repr(nan)` =
`"nan"` as a literal `<v>nan</v>`. Infinity, by contrast, IS already caught here (`inf > 100` is `True`
in IEEE754), so this is specifically a NaN-shaped gap, not the full class.

**Reachability, checked directly, not assumed:** the one real write path for a Targeted Enterprise's
percentages is `app/app/tenders/[id]/b7-actions.ts`'s Server Action, which always calls
`sanralB7.ts`'s `parsePlan(raw)` - "Parse a plan out of untrusted JSON (the Workspace form)" - before
`checkPlan()`/the `upsert()`. `parsePlan()`'s own `num()` helper explicitly does
`Number.isFinite(n) ? n : null`, so NaN/Infinity can never reach the database via genuine product use.
This gap is defense-in-depth, not a currently reachable production path - the same conclusion reached
for `fill_financial_hours.py`'s own capture table while investigating this area (no app write path
exists for THAT table at all, confirmed by grep; not written up as a finding since it needs a direct
DB bypass to trigger, same bar used throughout this QA pass's history for "theoretically constructible
but not evidenced" leads).

**Fixed anyway, by the same precedent `years_experience_at()` used in Finding 138** (fixed by analogy
to an accepted, already-reviewed sibling fix, even where the specific gap's own production reachability
was narrow): added the identical `math.isfinite()` check to `_num()`, so a NaN/Infinity value now
returns `None` - the same "missing value" path `check_plan()` already turns into an error for every
other reason (empty, non-numeric, out of range).

**Verified red-then-green.** New checks in `test_sanral_b7.py`: NaN for each of the three percentage
fields, plus `inf`/`-inf` for two of them (confirming infinity was already caught, to pin that fact
down rather than assume it) - both `check_plan()` (must list the field as an error) and `fill_b7()`
(must raise `ValueError`, never reach `wb.set_value()`) checked for each. Reverted `sanral_b7.py` via
`git apply -R`, re-ran - exactly the 6 NaN-specific checks failed as predicted (the 2 infinity checks
still passed, confirming they were never part of the gap); reapplied - `ALL PASSED`. `py_compile`
clean on both touched files. Regression: `test_fill_b7_legacy_precedence.py` and
`engine/pack/test_assemble_pack.py` - both `0 failure(s)`.

**Regression:** `engine/sanral_b7.py` (`_num()`, `math` import added, ~15 lines including comments);
`engine/test_sanral_b7.py` (5 new checks appended to the existing `check_plan()`/`fill_b7()` validation
section). No change to `read_setup()`, `applicability()`, or any passing-case write in `fill_b7()`.

### Finding 143 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, moderate - `assess_tender.CIDB_RE`'s own `"GRADING?"` could only ever match "GRADIN"/"GRADING", never the equally common "CIDB Grade X" phrasing real South African buyers use interchangeably - a tender naming its requirement this way read as having no CIDB requirement at all, in both discovery scoring and the non-SANRAL pack's own submission plan)

**Area:** Non-SANRAL pack (`engine/general/requirements.py`'s CIDB detection), sharing
`assess_tender.CIDB_RE` with discovery scoring (`assess_tender.extract_signals()`).

**Scenario:** `CIDB_RE = re.compile(r"CIDB\s*(?:CONTRACTOR\s*)?GRADING?\s*(?:OF\s*)?(?:AT\s*LEAST\s*)?"
r"([0-9]+\s*[A-Z]{1,3})", re.IGNORECASE)`. The `?` on `GRADING?` only makes the trailing `"G"`
optional, giving `"GRADIN"` or `"GRADING"` - it structurally can never match `"GRADE"` (diverges at the
5th character: `"GRADE"` vs `"GRADI"`). Confirmed directly: `CIDB_RE.search("CIDB Grade 6CE")`,
`CIDB_RE.search("CIDB grade of 7GB")` and `CIDB_RE.search("CIDB Contractor Grade 9CE")` all return
`None`, while the equivalent `"...Grading..."` phrasing matches correctly. "CIDB Grade X" is standard,
common South African procurement wording (confirmed via web search of real South African tender-advice
and procurement-guide sources, which use "CIDB Grade" at least as often as "CIDB Grading") - not a
narrow or contrived phrasing.

**Impact, both real consumers of this shared regex**: in discovery (`assess_tender.extract_signals()`),
a tender phrased this way read as having no `cidb_grading` signal at all - the same kind of lost
compliance signal Finding 135 (Eskom's truncated `REFERENCE` field) found for reference matching.
In the non-SANRAL pack (`requirements.py:1378`, this rotation's own area), `manifest["cidb"]` was
never set, so `submission_plan.py`'s dedicated, correctly-cautious "CIDB grading N required - confirm
this meets or exceeds" step never appeared, and the generic "CIDB registration / grading" returnable
(matched on the bare `\bCIDB\b` keyword) was the ONLY signal shown - silently losing the specific
grading number and the comparison prompt that step exists to give.

**Fix:** `GRADING?` replaced with an explicit `(?:GRADING|GRADE)` alternation (longest first, so
`"GRADING"` is matched whole rather than relying on backtracking after a partial `"GRADE"` match
fails against the digits that follow). Verified directly against 8 real-shaped phrasings (both
`"Grading"`/`"Grade"`, with/without `"Contractor"`, with/without `"of"`/`"at least"`) - zero regression
on any previously-matching case, all 4 new `"Grade"` cases now match.

**Verified red-then-green.** New test `check_cidb_grade_phrasing_is_detected_not_just_grading()` in
`engine/general/test_requirements.py`, running the real `extract_requirements()` pipeline against 4
fixture texts (2 "Grading", 2 "Grade", with/without "Contractor"). Reverted `assess_tender.py` via
`git apply -R`, re-ran - the 2 "Grade" cases failed exactly as predicted (`manifest['cidb']` never
set), the 2 "Grading" cases stayed green; reapplied - `0 failure(s)`. `py_compile` clean. Regression:
every other direct/indirect consumer of `assess_tender.py` or `CIDB_RE` -
`engine/discovery/test_taxonomy.py`, `test_discovery_fanout.py`, `test_discovery_downgrades.py`,
`test_boq_extraction.py`, `test_document_reader_fallback.py`, `engine/general/test_submission_plan.py`,
`test_build_general_pack.py`, `engine/intake/test_classify_tender.py` - all `0 failure(s)`.

**Regression:** `engine/discovery/assess_tender.py` (`CIDB_RE`, 1 regex changed, ~10 lines including
comments); `engine/general/test_requirements.py` (1 new test function, wired into `main()`). No change
to any other regex in this file, `extract_signals()`'s own dispatch, or `requirements.py`'s own CIDB
handling logic beyond what the corrected regex now feeds it.

### Finding 144 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, moderate - `document-scan/page.tsx`'s own `company_principals`/`people`/`companies` reads were never captured, so a failed read is indistinguishable from the genuine "nothing on file yet" case, and for `companies` specifically silently drops the real CIDB-contractor-name-mismatch check with no sign it was ever meant to run)

**Area:** Onboarding bulk document scan (`app/app/company/document-scan/page.tsx`), feeding
`review.tsx`'s `DocumentReviewCard`.

**Scenario:** traced from the standing "49-hit `const { data"` read-grep" thread's own remaining
untraced `.tsx` hits (System-Status.md, 2026-11-06 entry, line ~156: `document-scan/page.tsx:96`
listed but never traced to its real consequence). The page's one `Promise.all` fetches `pending`,
`principals`, `people`, `queuedCount`, `company` and `failed` - only `pending` and `failed` captured
`error`; `principals`, `people` and `company` did not, read straight into `principals ?? []`/
`people ?? []`/`company?.legal_name ?? null` with no distinction from a genuine empty/missing row.
Traced both consumers in `review.tsx`, not stopped at "returns `[]`, looks safe": (1) for an
`id_document`/`cv` row, `principals.length === 0`/`people.length === 0` renders "Nobody is on your
directors/shareholders register yet - add them first" / "Nobody is on your People page yet - add them
first" (lines 252-256/270-272) - on a transient read failure this tells a company that already has
directors/people on file that it doesn't, and (since both `<select>`s are `required`) leaves the
reviewer with no way to pick the right one until they refresh. (2) `companyLegalName` feeds
`cidbMismatch` (`cidbNameMismatchWarning()`, review.tsx:168-174) - the real CIDB-contractor-name-vs-
registered-name compliance-mismatch warning this same findings log already documented once
(commit `2d4c124`). A failed `companies` read makes `company` `null`, so `companyLegalName` is `null`,
so `cidbMismatch` is always `null` for that render - the mismatch check silently never runs, with
nothing on the page to say so; a reviewer could confirm a CIDB document with a real name mismatch
undetected, for no reason other than a transient read failure on an unrelated table.

**Fix:** same established convention as `people/bulk-cv/page.tsx`'s identical-shaped fix
(`bc1e7b5`, 2026-11-06): captured `error` on all three reads, logged each via `console.error`, and
added a banner ("Couldn't load your directors/people or company record just now - the review cards
below may wrongly say nobody is on file yet, or miss a name-mismatch check. Try refreshing before
confirming anything.") shown whenever any of the three failed and there is at least one document
actually waiting for review. No change to the non-error path, to `review.tsx` itself, or to any
Server Action - the underlying data flow into `DocumentReviewCard` is unchanged; only the
previously-silent failure is now visible.

**Verification run myself, real exit codes - no red/green test, honest limitation.** This is a
React Server Component page with no extracted testable logic and no existing test file (consistent
with the same honest-limitation precedent this doc's companion `System-Status.md` has already used
for `submission-pack.tsx`/`general-workspace.tsx`/`ImpersonationBanner.tsx`): correctness rests on
`npm run typecheck` (0 errors), `npx eslint .` (0 errors, same 3 pre-existing warnings), `npx next
build` (compiled successfully, same route table), and a plain reading of the diff and its two traced
consumers - not an actual red/green cycle. `npx vitest run` (458/458, 58/58 files - unchanged, no
test file touched) and the per-file `*.test.ts` loop (27 files, 0 failures - unchanged) both confirm
no regression anywhere else.

**Regression:** `app/app/company/document-scan/page.tsx` only (~27 lines added: 3 more
destructured `error` fields, 3 `console.error` calls, 1 derived `reviewDataError` boolean, 1 new
conditional banner). No change to `review.tsx`, `actions.ts`, or any other file in this directory.

### Finding 145 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, moderate - `send-discovered-tenders.ts`'s own fixed 2-day `created_at` lookback window, already flagged as a real residual gap by the 2026-11-07d fix, permanently and silently lost whichever opportunities aged out of it before a zero-recipient company ever got a recipient)

**Area:** Notify (`app/scripts/send-discovered-tenders.ts`'s candidate query, `app/lib/discoveredTendersDigest.ts`).

**Scenario:** this file's own header comment, written by the 2026-11-07d fix that closed the
zero-recipients-batched-send bug for this and `send-compliance-digest.ts`, explicitly named the
residual it deliberately left open: "the read below is bounded to the last 2 days (`sinceIso`) on
the assumption every row gets claimed-or-skipped daily. A company with zero recipients for MORE
than 2 consecutive days will still lose whichever of its opportunities aged out of that window in
the meantime... Widening the window, or querying for genuinely-unclaimed rows directly instead of
a fixed lookback, would close that residual edge; left for a future pass." Picked up directly, per
the standing review's own priority list naming this item as concrete and fixable, not a Sarel
policy call.

Re-derived the actual gap from the code, not trusted from the comment alone: `main()`'s candidate
query was `.gte("created_at", sinceIso).in("verdict", [...])` with `sinceIso = now - 2 days` - a
row outside that window is never even fetched, regardless of whether it was ever claimed. Once a
row ages out, nothing in this script (or anywhere else - grepped `engine/`, `app/scripts/` for any
other reader of `discovered_opportunities` by id) ever revisits it. Confirmed `discovered_opportunities`
itself has no bound on age the way the query's own window implied: `verdict` is written once at
discovery/re-score time and is never swept back to `closed` as a tender's own deadline later passes
(read every writer of that column - `seed_supabase_opportunities.py`, `tender_changes.py`, the
`discovery_downgrades.py` re-assessment path - none of them re-visit an existing row's verdict
purely because its closing date arrived), and `app/app/discovery/page.tsx`'s own module comment
independently confirms the same growth characteristic drove an earlier, separate pagination fix
there (PR #111/Sarel, 2026-10-23: "discovered_opportunities accumulates one row per OCDS release
ever scored against this company, forever").

**Fix:** replaced the `created_at` window with a `closing_date`-bounded one - the thing that
actually decides whether a "newly discovered tender" email is still worth sending at all. A tender
that has already closed is never worth this email, no matter when it was discovered or how long a
company went without a recipient, so bounding on `closing_date is null OR closing_date >= now`
closes the gap outright instead of just widening it, while staying naturally bounded: unlike
`discovered_opportunities`' own ever-growing full history, the set of currently-open tenders any
company has ever been matched against does not grow without bound (an old row's `closing_date` is a
fixed fact in the past, so it drops out of this filter on its own once that date arrives, regardless
of its stale `verdict`). Extracted as a pure, testable `openDiscoveredOpportunityWindow(now)` in
`discoveredTendersDigest.ts` rather than inlined, so the exact filter shape has its own unit tests
independent of a live Supabase connection (same convention this file's other pure helpers already
use). Also added a loud `console.error` if the existing `MAX_CANDIDATE_ROWS` (20,000) ceiling is
ever actually hit post-fix - removing the 2-day bound changes what that ceiling is a ceiling ON (a
running "every still-open candidate" total instead of "one day's worth"), and a silently-truncated
success is exactly this review's own dominant tracked bug-class shape; this is a precaution against
introducing a new instance of it, not a confirmed-live problem (not measured against real
production volume at the new scope - flagged honestly, not assumed safe).

**Verified red-then-green.** New tests in `discoveredTendersDigest.spec.ts` (4 tests) pin the exact
filter shape: the 3 verdicts unchanged, the `.or()` string built correctly from a frozen clock, the
cutoff moving with the clock, and the no-argument default using the real current time. `git stash
push -- app/lib/discoveredTendersDigest.ts` (keeping the new tests and `send-discovered-tenders.ts`'s
own changes in place) and re-ran: all 4 new tests failed with `TypeError: ... is not a function`
(the function didn't exist pre-fix) - confirmed these tests actually exercise the new code, not a
tautology. `git stash pop` restored the fix; `npx vitest run lib/discoveredTendersDigest.spec.ts` -
12/12 passed again. Full regression: `npx vitest run` from `app/` - 462/462 passed, 58/58 files (up
from 458/58: +4 new tests, no file added). The per-file `*.test.ts` loop (no `--test` flag) - 27
files, 0 failures, unchanged (neither touched file is a `*.test.ts`). `npm run typecheck` - 0
errors. `npx eslint .` on all touched files - 0 errors, same 3 pre-existing warnings. `npx next
build` - compiled successfully, same route table. Ran `send-discovered-tenders.ts` directly with no
env vars set - identical pre-fix "must both be set" exit-1 message, confirming the CLI-arg/env guard
above the changed query is unaffected.

**Not independently verified against live production data** (no live Supabase credentials in this
environment) - whether removing the 2-day bound causes the real `discovered_opportunities` table's
closing_date>=now row count to approach `MAX_CANDIDATE_ROWS` is reasoned from its growth
characteristics (above), not measured against a real production count; the new `console.error` is
the safety net if that reasoning turns out wrong, not a guarantee it won't happen.

**Regression:** `app/lib/discoveredTendersDigest.ts` (1 new exported const, 1 new exported pure
function, ~35 lines including comments); `app/lib/discoveredTendersDigest.spec.ts` (4 new tests);
`app/scripts/send-discovered-tenders.ts` (query construction swapped to use the new helper, 1 new
truncation-warning check, header/`MAX_CANDIDATE_ROWS` comments updated - no change to
`processDiscoveredTenderCompany()`, the claim/send/log logic, or any other function). No change to
`send-compliance-digest.ts` (that file never had this residual - its own candidates are re-derived
from live expiry dates every run, not a creation-date window, per the 2026-11-07d entry) or any
