### Finding 189 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, moderate - `lephalale.py`'s own `normalize()` never took the batch listing's own "Date uploaded" value as a parameter at all, so every Lephalale release's `published_date` was always `None`, unlike every sibling direct-site reader with an equivalent field)

**Area:** `engine/discovery/lephalale.py` `normalize()`/`fetch_releases()`. Test coverage added in `engine/discovery/test_lephalale.py`.

**How this was found.** Finding 188's own "also checked and ruled out" list named this exact lead as not yet exhaustively checked: `engine/discovery/gov_sources.py`'s 11-source family (`etenders_portal`, `sanral`, `eskom_bulletin`, `transnet_etenders`, `capetown_procurement`, `sars_procurement`, `cidb_tenders`, `dbsa_procurement`, `vaal_central_water`, `lephalale`, `kouga`), each with its own `fetch_releases()`/`sanral_releases()` reader, compared field-by-field against `source_http.release()`'s full parameter list (`ocid`, `contract_number`, `title`, `description`, `buyer`, `procurement_category`, `closing_date`, `opening_date`, `documents`, `awards`, `contracts`, `has_award_data`, `source`, `source_id`, `source_url`, `status`, `province`, `tender_type`, `briefing`, `published_date`, `modified_date`). This pass read every one of the 11 readers' own `normalize()`/equivalent in full (not just grepped for the call) and checked each field each one omits against whether the underlying site genuinely has no equivalent data (the overwhelming majority of omissions - no province on a single-municipality site, no briefing data in a feed that never carries one, etc - all checked this way and ruled out as real, not dropped) versus a field the reader's own parsing demonstrably already has in hand and just never wires through.

**The sibling family, this field specifically.** Every direct-site reader whose own listing page states a publish/upload date passes it through as `published_date`: `etenders_portal.py` (`date_Published`), `cidb_tenders.py` (`tender_advert_date_time`), `dbsa_procurement.py` (`published`), `eskom_bulletin.py` (`PUBLISHEDDATE`), `transnet_etenders.py` (`publishedDate`), `capetown_procurement.py` (`posted`), `sars_procurement.py` (`entry["published"]`), `kouga.py` (`start`, the card's own "Start Date:"), `vaal_central_water.py` (`uploaded`, the row's own "Date uploaded" column). `randwater.py` and `sanral` (`gov_sources.sanral_releases()`) are the only two genuine negatives - neither site's own listing or detail page states a publish/upload date anywhere (confirmed by re-reading `list_tenders.py`'s and `detail.py`'s own field sets: SANRAL's detail page does carry a "Create Date" stat, read into `d.get("create_date")`, but `create_date` genuinely isn't the tender's publish date - it's the document record's own create timestamp, unlike `last_updated`, which `sanral_releases()` already correctly uses for `modified_date` - so leaving `published_date` unset there is a defensible, if underdocumented, choice, not this finding). `lephalale.py` is the one reader whose own listing page states this field - under the exact same column name and semantics as `vaal_central_water.py`'s own "Date uploaded" (confirmed from `test_lephalale.py`'s own `FIXTURE_LISTING`: `<th>Date uploaded</th>`, real values like `2026-10-05`) - and whose own `parse_listing()`/`fetch_releases()` already read it correctly into a loop variable (`uploaded`), but whose `normalize()` function signature (`internal_ref, tnumber, desc, closing_dt, batch_url, batch_label`) had no parameter to receive it at all. `fetch_releases()`'s own `for url, label, uploaded, closing in rows:` loop bound a real value every single call and then never used it - the value was read off the live page and thrown away before it ever reached `source_http.release()`.

**Root cause, traced, not guessed.** `parse_listing()`'s own docstring already correctly describes its return shape as `[(url, label, uploaded_date, closing_date)]` - the field was never missing from the reader's own parsing, only from the one function boundary between `fetch_releases()`'s loop and `normalize()`'s call. No comment anywhere explained the omission; nothing downstream of `normalize()` needed `uploaded` for any other purpose, so there was no competing user of the variable masking the gap.

**Real downstream consequence, confirmed by reading the actual consumers, not assumed.** `published_date` has two real, live consumers in `tender_changes.py`, both silently losing effect for Lephalale specifically: (1) `diff_listing()`'s first-sighting branch flags a late-added addendum-type document when `up - pub >= LATE_DOC_GRACE` (comparing a document's own `date_modified` against the release's `published_date`) - with `published_date` always `None` for Lephalale, `pub` is always falsy and this check can never fire for a Lephalale release, regardless of how late a real addendum was actually added to its own batch PDF. (2) `relistings()` - built specifically for "a buyer that lists the SAME bid number again as a new listing with a different closing date," the exact pattern Lephalale's own `_disambiguate_reused_refs()` docstring says is a real, demonstrated mechanism on this buyer's site ("SA municipalities routinely re-advertise within weeks of a failed closing") - sorts same-bid-number releases by `(x.get("published_date") or "", x.get("ocid") or "")` to decide which listing is newer, then reports the change "on the OLDER listing, pointing to the newer one." With every Lephalale `published_date` equal to `None`, this sort degrades entirely to comparing `ocid` strings (`"lephalale:8/2/<ref>"` or its disambiguated `:<slug>` suffix) - alphabetical, unrelated to real recency - so if Lephalale's own re-advertisement pattern and `relistings()`'s detection window were ever both live in the same run (not yet observed, but the mechanism `_disambiguate_reused_refs()` itself is already built to guard a narrower version of), the "use the newer listing" guidance could point at the wrong one.

**Fix.** Smallest correct change: `normalize()` gained one new parameter, `uploaded=None` (default, so the pre-existing 6-positional-argument call site in `test_lephalale.py` keeps working unchanged), and now passes `published_date=sh.iso_sast(uploaded)` through to `source_http.release()` - the identical convention every sibling reader with an equivalent field already uses. `fetch_releases()`'s own call site now passes its own already-bound `uploaded` loop variable through as the 7th argument. No change to `parse_listing()`, `parse_batch()`, `_disambiguate_reused_refs()`, or any other function - the value was already being read correctly; only the one missing hop was added.

**Verified red-then-green.** Added two checks to `test_lephalale.py`'s existing "normalize() -> the shared release shape" section: `published_date` is `None` when `normalize()` is called without the new argument (confirming the default stays backward-compatible), and a second `normalize()` call passing the real fixture's own `uploaded` value (`rows[0][2]`, `"2026-10-05"`, the September batch's real "Date uploaded" value) produces `published_date == "2026-10-05T00:00:00+02:00"`. **Red:** reverted `lephalale.py` to its parent commit's content (`git show HEAD:engine/discovery/lephalale.py`) with the new test left unchanged - real exit code `1`, failing exactly as predicted: `TypeError: normalize() takes 6 positional arguments but 7 were given` (the old signature has no 7th parameter to receive the new test's real "Date uploaded" value). **Green:** restored the fix - real exit code `0`, all 41 checks in the file pass, "ALL PASSED".

**Full verification suite.** `python3 engine/discovery/test_lephalale.py` - exit `0`, 41/41. `python3 engine/discovery/test_gov_sources.py` - exit `0`, "ALL PASSED" (no regression in `gov_sources.merge()`/`_fold()`/the re-listing test already in that file). `python3 engine/discovery/test_tender_changes.py` - exit `0`, "0 failure(s)" (no regression in either of `published_date`'s two real consumers, `diff_listing()`/`relistings()`). Full `engine/` Python sweep, every `test_*.py` found by `find engine -name "test_*.py"` (86 files, unchanged count) run with plain `python3 <file>`, real exit codes captured directly - **86/86, 0 failures**. Python-only, single-file production change (plus its own test file) - no TypeScript/schema/call-site elsewhere touched, so `npm run typecheck`/`npx eslint .`/`npx vitest run`/`npx next build` were not re-run (same scope discipline as Finding 188).

**Also checked and ruled out, field-by-field, across the remaining 10 sources (completing the lead Finding 188 named as not yet exhaustive):** `randwater.py` (no publish-date field exists on the live page at all - ref/closing/title only, confirmed from `BID_BLOCK`'s own 3 capture groups and the module's own docstring describing the page's structure); `sanral`/`gov_sources.sanral_releases()` (SANRAL's list endpoint has no publish-date column - confirmed from `list_tenders._parse_row()`'s own 6-cell unpack; its detail page's "Create Date" stat is read into `d.get("create_date")` but is a document-record timestamp, not the tender's own publish date, unlike "Last Updated"/`modified_date`, which is already correctly wired - a defensible omission, not a dropped field); `etenders_portal.py`/`eskom_bulletin.py`/`transnet_etenders.py`/`capetown_procurement.py`/`cidb_tenders.py`/`dbsa_procurement.py`/`sars_procurement.py`/`kouga.py`/`vaal_central_water.py` all correctly pass their own equivalent field through already - no divergence found in any of them. `briefing` was checked the same way across all 11: only `etenders_portal.py` and `transnet_etenders.py`'s own sites actually publish briefing-session data at all (confirmed from each reader's own field set); every other reader's absence of a `briefing=` argument is a real "this site has none," not a drop. `modified_date` was checked the same way: only `etenders_portal.py` (from each document's own `dateModified`), `eskom_bulletin.py` (`DATEMODIFIED`) and `sanral` (the detail page's "Last Updated") have an underlying field to draw from, and all three correctly use it; no other reader's site publishes a last-modified timestamp at all. This closes out the `gov_sources.py` 11-source lead for this field set - no further divergence found after Finding 189's own fix.

**Why this looked backwards at first, and why it isn't.** `app/app/tenders/[id]/general-pack-review-logic.ts`'s own header comment states, as design rationale for why its general-tender Pack Review screen is simpler than SANRAL's: "general tenders have no provenance/assumed-default machinery - field_provenance is SANRAL-only." **Fix.** Smallest correct change, mirroring `process_general_jobs.py`'s own write exactly: (1) added an `upsert(self, table, rows, on_conflict)` method to `process_pack_jobs.py`'s `SupabaseRest` class - identical REST shape (`POST .../rest/v1/<table>?on_conflict=...` with `Prefer: return=representation,resolution=merge-duplicates`) to `process_general_jobs.py`'s own `Supabase.upsert()`, the same kind of one-method gap Finding "the pack-ready-email fix" (2026-11-06) already found and fixed for `.rpc()` on this identical class; (2) in `process_job()`, right after the upload loop (so `outputs["field_provenance"]`, the local JSON path `assemble_pack.py` already produces on every successful build, is still intact), load that file, de-duplicate by `field_key` keeping the last entry (the identical "last write wins" rule `process_general_jobs.py`'s own write already applies, needed because the DB's `unique(tender_pack_id, field_key)` constraint rejects a batch upsert with a repeated key), and `client.upsert("field_provenance", [...], "tender_pack_id,field_key")` using `job["tender_pack_id"]` - already re-derived and company/tender-matched by `gather()` earlier in the same function (which raises `ValueError` and aborts before this point otherwise), the same trust boundary this function already relies on for `job["company_id"]`/`job["tender_id"]` in its own `except` block. Guarded with `if prov_path and os.path.exists(prov_path)` / `if seen:` so a pack whose outputs dict has no `field_provenance` key (defensive - in practice `run_forms_pipeline.main()` always produces one on a successful build) is a no-op, not a crash. No schema/migration/RPC change - reuses the existing `field_provenance` table and its existing unique constraint exactly as `process_general_jobs.py` already does.

### Finding 191 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, moderate - `app/app/my-cv/actions.ts`'s `applyMyCvExtraction()` never called `queueStandardCvs()` at all, unlike its true sibling `app/app/people/actions.ts`'s `applyCvExtraction()`, so a CV extraction confirmed exclusively through the My CV self-service page never got a single standard CV queued, with no way to retry once confirmed)

**Area:** `app/app/my-cv/actions.ts` `applyMyCvExtraction()`. Test coverage added in `app/app/my-cv/actions.spec.ts`.

**How this was found.** This pass's task was to extend the sibling-comparison method into genuinely unswept TypeScript Server Action territory, per the standing brief's own named candidate "`app/app/people/` and `app/app/my-cv/` beyond the `applyCvExtraction()`/`applyMyCvExtraction()` races already fixed." Both functions' own TOCTOU/race fix (moving the read-gate-write sequence into one locked RPC, `apply_cv_extraction_checked`/`apply_my_cv_extraction_checked`, 0123, standing review 2026-11-06/07) was already done and explicitly out of scope to re-litigate - but reading the two functions side by side for what each one does AFTER its own rpc call succeeds (not just how it gets there) turned up a second, independent, unrelated divergence: `applyCvExtraction()` calls `queueStandardCvs(supabase, companyId, personId!, user?.id ?? null)` right after its rpc succeeds; `applyMyCvExtraction()`, doing the exact same "confirm this CV extraction" job for the exact same `cv_extraction_results`/`people` tables, does not call it, or anything like it, at all.

**The sibling family.** Two "confirm/apply an AI-extracted CV" Server Actions exist in this codebase, both landing fields ticked on a review card onto the same `people` row and marking the same `cv_extraction_results` row applied: `app/app/people/actions.ts`'s `applyCvExtraction()` (the full People page, any owner/admin/member) and `app/app/my-cv/actions.ts`'s `applyMyCvExtraction()` (the My CV self-service page, 0065's `employee` role - the ONE page an `employee` can use for this at all). `applyMyCvExtraction()`'s own header comment is explicit about exactly one intentional difference from its sibling ("no project-adding step... kept deliberately small for this page") - it says nothing about the standard-CV queue, which is the signature of an oversight under this method, not a documented scope cut.

**Root cause, traced, not guessed.** `queueStandardCvs()` (then a private, unexported function inside `people/actions.ts`) was written and wired into exactly one call site - `applyCvExtraction()` - when My CV's own `applyMyCvExtraction()` either didn't yet exist or wasn't updated when the two confirm screens converged on the same shape. `uploadCv()`'s own header comment in `people/actions.ts` already documents the general design intent correctly ("The standard... CV formats are queued for pre-generation... at that confirm step, not here: until the fields are confirmed the record they'd be built from is still empty or out of date") - but that documented intent was only ever implemented for the People-page confirm step, never the My-CV one.

**Real downstream consequence, confirmed by reading the actual consumers, not assumed.** `queueStandardCvs()` is the ONLY writer, anywhere in this codebase, of a `generated_cvs` row with `tender_id` null (confirmed: `grep -rn "tender_id.*null\|is(\"tender_id\"" app/app` finds no second writer; `createPersonWithCv()`/`bulkUploadCvs()` only ever create `cv_uploads` rows, never `generated_cvs`). Both `apply_cv_extraction_checked()` and `apply_my_cv_extraction_checked()` (0123) require the extraction's own `review_status` to still be `'pending_review'` before they'll touch it - once either confirm action has run, the row moves to `'applied'` and neither function (nor anyone re-trying the other one) can ever act on that same extraction again. So for every CV confirmed exclusively through My CV: (1) the My CV page's own "My generated CVs (read-only)" card (`app/app/my-cv/page.tsx`) showed "None generated yet." permanently, with no way for the employee or an admin to ever change that for this extraction; (2) the identical card on the full People page (`app/app/people/[id]/page.tsx`, `is("tender_id", null)`) showed the same permanent empty state; (3) `engine/general/process_general_jobs.py`'s own per-role CV lookup (`gather()`'s `cvs` loop, `client.select("generated_cvs", {"person_id": ..., "company_id": ..., "status": "ready"}, order="requested_at.desc")` - no `tender_id` filter at all, so it takes whichever `ready` row is newest, standard or tender-specific) is a real, live fallback CV source for a general-tender pack: a person tagged for a role with no tender-specific CV ever requested and no as-is upload would show `"no CV uploaded or generated for this person"` for that role, even though their CV fields were, in fact, fully confirmed - the exact same silent-gap shape as every other "a real downstream consumer would notice" finding in this file.

**Fix.** Smallest correct change: extracted `queueStandardCvs()` (previously private to `people/actions.ts`) into a new shared module, `app/lib/standardCvQueue.ts`, with its own doc comment explaining why it is now shared and what this finding was. `people/actions.ts` now imports it (its own `STANDARD_CV_FORMATS`/`STANDARD_CV_DETAILS` constants and the function body were removed, call site at `applyCvExtraction()` unchanged). `my-cv/actions.ts` now imports it too and calls it from `applyMyCvExtraction()` right after its own rpc succeeds, exactly where `applyCvExtraction()` calls it - `requireOwnPerson()` already returns `userId`/`companyId` alongside `personId`, so no new lookup was needed. A failed queue attempt now fails the request (`"Fields saved, but your standard CVs could not be queued - try again. If it keeps happening, let us know."`) the same way `applyCvExtraction()`'s own `queueError` branch already does, rather than silently reporting success.

**Verified red-then-green.** Added two tests to `my-cv/actions.spec.ts`: one asserting the rpc-success path inserts exactly 4 `generated_cvs` rows (`sanral_keyperson`/`world_bank` x `summary`/`detailed`, each carrying the right `company_id`/`person_id`/`status: "requested"`/`requested_by`); one asserting that a failed `queueStandardCvs()` pending-check read fails the whole request rather than redirecting with `saved=extracted`. **Red:** reverted `my-cv/actions.ts`/`people/actions.ts`/the new `app/lib/standardCvQueue.ts` via `git stash push -u` (new tests left in place, parent commit `2ccb681`) - real exit code showed 2 failures, exactly as predicted: `expected [] to have a length of 1 but got +0` (no insert happened at all) and `expected '/my-cv?saved=extracted' not to contain 'saved=extracted'` (the pending-check failure was never reached because the call that would hit it doesn't exist yet); all 6 other tests in the file still passed unchanged. **Green:** `git stash pop` to restore the fix, re-ran - all 8 tests in the file pass.

**Full verification suite.** `npx vitest run app/my-cv/actions.spec.ts app/people/actions.spec.ts` - exit `0`, 20/20. Full `npx vitest run` - exit `0`, **506/506 passed, 66 files** (504 standing baseline + this pass's 2 new tests). `npm run typecheck` - exit `0`. `npx eslint .` - exit `0`, same 3 pre-existing warnings, unchanged. The node `*.test.ts` loop (plain `node <file>`, no flags) - **28/28, 0 failures**, unchanged. `npx next build`, run in a disposable `git worktree` with `app/node_modules` bind-mounted (not symlinked) in - clean, no errors, same route list as every prior clean build in this environment (no live-Supabase-only `/login` prerender failure this time, unlike several earlier entries in this file - this build genuinely produced zero errors). Full `engine/` Python sweep re-run as a no-op regression check even though no Python changed - `find engine -name "test_*.py" | wc -l` = `86`, looped with plain `python3 <file>` - **86/86, 0 failures**, unchanged. Worktree removed and its bind mount unmounted after the build; no scratch Postgres database was needed for this fix (no race/lock reproduction involved).

All 10 PRs remain open and unmerged - re-confirmed via `mcp__github__list_pull_requests` before this pass's own push: `#164`/`#165`/`#176`/`#177`/`#178`/`#179`/`#180`/`#181`/`#182`/`#183`, none touched, amended, or merged this pass or by anyone else. Pushed directly to `main` (small, safe - a shared-helper extraction plus one new call site in a Server Action file, no RLS/money-path/hard-stop-gate touched, no schema/migration/RPC change, no worker-image surface touched), per the binding guardrails' own "small, safe fix -> push directly" rule.

### Finding 192 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, moderate - a sweep across all 6 `process_*_jobs.py` worker bridges found 10 more `system_alerts.record()` calls whose `context` never carried `company_id`, the same bug class as Findings 186/188, plus a separate, more significant gap in `narrative/process_narrative_jobs.py`'s own `fail_stale_jobs()`, which never alerted on a real staleness reclaim at all, unlike its `pack`/`general` siblings)

**Area:** `engine/cv/process_cv_jobs.py`, `engine/cv/extract_cv_fields.py`, `engine/pack/process_pack_jobs.py`, `engine/general/process_general_jobs.py`, `engine/onboarding/process_onboarding_jobs.py`, `engine/narrative/process_narrative_jobs.py`. Test coverage added/extended in each file's own sibling `test_*.py`.

**How this was found.** Findings 186 and 188 each independently caught ONE instance of the same bug class (`system_alerts.record()`'s own `context` dict missing `company_id`, so the admin System Alerts page's tenant badge, `platform_admin_companies()` resolving `context.company_id`, renders with no tenant for that row) in two unrelated files, found by two different sessions on two different passes. Two independent hits on the identical shape is the standing signal to stop treating it as isolated and sweep the whole sibling family instead of waiting for a third session to re-find it a third time - this pass's rotation landed on worker/job-queue, so it did exactly that: read every `system_alerts.record(` call site in all 6 `process_*_jobs.py` bridges side by side and checked whether a `company_id`-bearing row was already in scope at that call site (it always is: `client.select()`'s `RestClient.select()` always appends `select=*`, so any row already fetched carries its own `company_id` for free - no new query needed anywhere this fix applies).

**What was actually missing, file by file.**
- `cv/process_cv_jobs.py`: the malformed-`claimed_at` alert in `fail_stale_jobs()`, and the nested "could not mark a failed CV job as failed" alert in `process_job()`'s second-level `except`.
- `cv/extract_cv_fields.py`: the nested "could not {what}" alert inside the shared `_safe_update(write, upload, what)` helper.
- `onboarding/process_onboarding_jobs.py`: the identical `_safe_update()` nested alert (this file's sibling helper, same shape, same gap - distinct from Finding 188's own `fail_stale_uploads()` fix in this same file, a different function).
- `pack/process_pack_jobs.py`: the nested "could not mark a failed pack job as failed" alert in `process_job()`; `sync_tender_requirements()`'s "could not read SETUP sheet" alert; `sync_b7_setup()`'s "could not read Form B7 category" alert.
- `general/process_general_jobs.py`: `_within()`'s malformed-`completion_date` alert; the nested "could not mark a failed general job as failed" alert in `process_job()`.
- `narrative/process_narrative_jobs.py`: the malformed-`started_at` alert in `fail_stale_jobs()` - plus the separate, larger gap below.

**The separate, more significant gap: `narrative/process_narrative_jobs.py`'s `fail_stale_jobs()` never alerted on a real staleness reclaim at all.** Comparing it structurally against its `pack`/`general` siblings (not just checking for the company_id sub-pattern) showed `pack`/`general`'s own `fail_stale_jobs()` both raise an `"error"`-severity alert the moment a row is genuinely marked `failed` for staleness (a worker died mid-job - operationally the more urgent of the two cases, since it means a worker process is crashing, not just that one row had a bad timestamp). `narrative`'s own version only ever alerted on the malformed-timestamp row; the real stuck-job branch printed to stdout and silently reclaimed the row with no alert, no admin visibility, nothing - confirmed via `grep -n "system_alerts" engine/narrative/process_narrative_jobs.py` before the fix, which found zero hits inside `fail_stale_jobs()` itself. Added the matching `"error"`-severity alert, same shape as the pack/general siblings, carrying `job_id`/`company_id`/`started_at`.

**Fix.** All 10 call sites: added `"company_id": <row>.get("company_id")` to the existing `context` dict, using whichever row/dict was already in scope at that call site (`job`, `upload`, `item`, `d`/`tid`-resolved row) - no new query added anywhere. `narrative/process_narrative_jobs.py`'s `fail_stale_jobs()`: added the new real-staleness `"error"` alert block, matching `pack`/`general`'s own sibling pattern exactly.

**Deliberately left out of scope.** Two OCR-crash alerts in `extract_cv_fields.py` (lines ~192/224) only have a bare file path in scope at that point, not a company-linked row - fixing those would need a bigger refactor (threading the upload row further down the call chain) and was left alone rather than forcing an unsafe fix (e.g. a spurious extra query, or fabricating a value).

**Verified red-then-green.** Extended/added tests in all 6 sibling `test_*.py` files asserting the relevant alert's `context["company_id"]` matches the fixture row's own value, plus (for `narrative`) that the stale-reclaim path now fires an `"error"` alert where it previously fired none. One test-fixture bug surfaced and was fixed along the way: `pack/test_process_pack_jobs.py`'s shared `FakeClient` has no real per-table separation (one flat `self.rows` list, `select()` matches by field-value equality regardless of the `table` string) - adding list-value ("IN"-filter) support for `sync_b7_setup()`'s own lookup caused a spurious fixture collision with `sync_tender_requirements()`'s own "have I already written this?" check; fixed by overriding `select()` in that test's own local `FakeClient` subclass to special-case the colliding table, not by redesigning the shared fixture for every other test. **Red:** saved a single diff of all 6 production files, `git apply -R`, re-ran all 6 test files - all 6 failed exactly as predicted (the new/extended assertions on `company_id`/alert-count failed; `narrative`'s own test crashed with `IndexError` reaching for the now-absent second alert). **Green:** `git apply` to reapply, re-ran all 6 - `0 failure(s)` / `ALL PASSED` across all 6. `python3 -m py_compile` clean on all 6 production files and their test files. Broader regression check: `engine/worker/test_poll_loop.py` and `engine/alerts/test_system_alerts.py` (the two suites most likely to indirectly exercise these bridges) both still pass unchanged.

**Backlog status.** No new backlog items opened by this fix. `git fetch origin main` immediately before writing this entry and again immediately before pushing showed no sibling commits landed in between.

To verify independently: `grep -n "company_id" engine/cv/process_cv_jobs.py engine/cv/extract_cv_fields.py engine/pack/process_pack_jobs.py engine/general/process_general_jobs.py engine/onboarding/process_onboarding_jobs.py engine/narrative/process_narrative_jobs.py` and confirm each of the 10 call sites listed above now includes it; confirm `narrative/process_narrative_jobs.py`'s `fail_stale_jobs()` now has a `system_alerts.record(..., "error", ...)` call on its genuinely-stale branch, not just its malformed-timestamp branch. Run each of the 6 test files directly with plain `python3 <file>` from its own directory and confirm `0 failure(s)` / `ALL PASSED`.


### Finding 193 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, low/moderate - `app/app/admin/customers/page.tsx`'s per-company `platform_admin_company_members()` RPC never captured its own error, unlike its sibling `platform_admin_companies()` read in the exact same function, so a transient per-company RPC failure rendered identically to a genuine zero-member company directly underneath that same row's own non-zero member count)

**Area:** `app/app/admin/customers/page.tsx`, `app/app/admin/customers/CustomerRow.tsx`. New shared helper `app/lib/customerRowData.ts`, with its own test file `app/lib/customerRowData.spec.ts`.

**How this was found.** The standing brief named `app/app/admin/`'s "other pages beyond System Alerts, with their own field-resolution pattern" as a candidate family genuinely not yet swept for this review's own dominant bug class (a discarded Supabase/RPC read's error treated as false-safe) - checked first against this doc's own history: `app/app/admin/**/page.tsx` had only been swept once before, and only for a *different* bug class (TOCTOU/lost-update write races, `System-Status.md` 2026-11-07xiii's own entry, which explicitly characterised every admin page including `customers` as "read-only display data... no write path" and stopped there, never applying the discarded-read-error lens to any of them). `CustomerRow.tsx`/`admin/customers/page.tsx` had only ever been mentioned in passing (performance/N+1 note, 2025-10-25; company_members-grep exclusion notes) - never read end to end for this specific angle. Read `AdminCustomersPage()` in full: it fires three separate Supabase reads - one top-level `platform_admin_companies()` RPC (`error` captured and `console.error()`d immediately, line 63 pre-fix) and then, inside a `Promise.all(rows.map(...))`, one `platform_admin_company_members()` RPC and one `platform_admin_company_readiness_data()` RPC PER COMPANY ROW - neither of which had its own `error` ever read at all. Three siblings performing the same kind of "trust this RPC, use its `data`" job inside the one function; one correctly checks `error`, two silently don't, with no comment anywhere explaining the omission - exactly the sibling-divergence shape this method looks for, just inside a single function rather than across files.

**Real downstream consequence, confirmed by reading the actual consumer, not assumed.** `memberLists[i].data ?? []` was the only use of the per-company members RPC's result - a failed RPC call (network blip, a transient Postgres error, a timeout) produces the exact same `[]` a real zero-member company would, with **no distinguishing signal anywhere**. `CustomerRow.tsx` then rendered that `[]` as `customer.members.length === 0 && "No members."` in the expanded detail panel, and `primaryContact` (`members.find(m => m.role === "owner")?.email ?? members[0]?.email ?? null`) fell to `null`, rendered as `"no members"`. Critically, this is **not** an isolated false-empty-state the way most of this review's prior findings are: the SAME row's own header line, two lines above, shows `customer.member_count` - a real, non-zero count sourced from the entirely separate, successfully-read `platform_admin_companies()` RPC (`CompanyOverviewRow.member_count`, a plain column on that row, never derived from the per-company members list at all). So a platform admin expanding a company whose per-company members RPC happened to fail would see, in the same expanded row, "3 members" in the header and "No members." immediately below it for the identical company - a direct, visible self-contradiction, not just a quiet wrong number. (`platform_admin_company_readiness_data()`'s own discarded error was checked for the same shape and found materially less severe: `CustomerRow.tsx`'s own pre-existing doc comment on `readinessPercent` already documents its `null` case as ambiguous - "readiness couldn't be computed (no readiness data row, e.g. a company somehow missing)" - so a failed read rendering the same as "no row yet" is already the file's own stated, accepted behaviour, not an undocumented silent divergence the way the members RPC's total silence was.)

**Fix.** Smallest correct change that also makes the logic genuinely testable (this page had no test coverage at all before this fix, consistent with every other admin `page.tsx` in this codebase - server components doing live Supabase calls aren't unit-tested directly here; the established split for exactly this situation is `fetchSavingsCounterSummary()`/`computeBidReadiness()`, a DB-touching fetcher in the page plus a pure, unit-tested builder in `app/lib/`). Extracted the per-row derivation (previously 20 lines inline in `page.tsx`'s own `rows.map()`) into `buildCustomerRow()` in a new `app/lib/customerRowData.ts`: both RPC results' `error` are now captured and `console.error()`d (matching the already-correct `platform_admin_companies()` convention), and a new `membersError: boolean` field on `Customer` lets `CustomerRow.tsx` distinguish a real empty list from an unknown one - "Couldn't load members - try refreshing. If it keeps happening, let us know." (the same wording convention used by every other "couldn't load" banner in this codebase, e.g. `admin/customers/page.tsx`'s own existing top-level error banner) in place of "No members.", and `"couldn't load"` in place of `"no members"` for the primary-contact line. `readinessRows[i]`'s error is now logged too (cheap, consistent, no reason not to) but deliberately does not change the UI, per the reasoning above - no behavioural change to the already-accepted ambiguous-null case.

**Verified red-then-green.** `app/lib/customerRowData.spec.ts` (6 tests): a real successful members read passes through untouched; a genuine empty list is NOT reported as `membersError`; a failed members RPC sets `membersError: true`, empties `members` safely, nulls `primaryContact`, leaves the sibling `member_count` field untouched, and is logged via `console.error("platform_admin_company_members rpc failed", ...)`; a failed readiness RPC is logged but renders the pre-existing null case, and doesn't affect `membersError`; the no-owner-role primary-contact fallback; `trialDaysRemaining` only computed when `subscription_status === "trialing"`. **Red:** `git stash push -u` on the 3 fix files (`CustomerRow.tsx`, `page.tsx`, the new `customerRowData.ts`) with the new spec file left in place - real exit `1`, failing exactly as predicted (`Cannot find module './customerRowData'` - the fix genuinely does not exist pre-fix, since this is a brand-new file with no pre-fix equivalent to diff against). **Green:** `git stash pop` to restore - real exit `0`, 6/6 new tests pass.

**Full verification suite.** `npm run typecheck` - exit `0`. `npx eslint .` - exit `0`, same 3 pre-existing warnings, unchanged. `npx vitest run` - exit `0`, **512/512 passed, 67 files** (506/506 + 66 files standing baseline after Finding 191, + this pass's 6 new tests + 1 new file). The node `*.test.ts` loop (plain `node <file>`, no flags) - **28/28, 0 failures**, unchanged (no `.test.ts` file touched). `npx next build`, run directly in the primary checkout (its own `app/node_modules` is already a real directory, not a symlink, so the usual worktree/bind-mount step - needed only to dodge a *fresh worktree's* symlinked `node_modules` under Turbopack - does not apply here; no worktree was created, so none needed cleaning up) - clean, `/admin/customers` compiles, same Partial Prerender route table as every prior clean build. Full `engine/` Python sweep re-run as a no-op regression check even though no Python changed - `find engine -name "test_*.py" | wc -l` = `86`, looped with plain `python3 <file>` - **86/86, 0 failures**, unchanged. No scratch Postgres database was needed (no race/lock reproduction - this is a missing error-capture bug, verified with plain Vitest unit tests against a hand-built fixture, no live Supabase/Postgres access required).

**Backlog status.** Finding 168, the `start_payfast_checkout()` revenue-integrity gap, and Finding 190's own pre-existing-SANRAL-pack `field_provenance` backfill all remain exactly as left, untouched, per the standing guardrails. **Real consequence, not just a missing log line.** Because `AdminLayout` already confirmed the signed-in user is a platform admin moments earlier in the same request, a FAILURE of `taxonomy/page.tsx`'s own, separate, redundant call to the identical RPC is not really "this user might not be an admin" - it is near-certainly a second, independent, transient failure of the same RPC (an intermittent Supabase blip), hitting a user who is, in fact, a platform admin. ### Finding 200 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, moderate - `award_outcomes.py`'s `parse_rand()` silently flipped a text-typed negative rand amount positive ("-45000.00" -> 45000.0) and returned `None` entirely for the same amount in standard accounting parentheses notation ("(R 45 000.00)"), affecting any text-typed BOQ omission/credit line item read through `boq_extraction.py`'s own rate/amount columns, or any award-value correction recorded as text)

**Area:** `engine/discovery/award_outcomes.py` `parse_rand()`, consumed by `engine/discovery/boq_extraction.py`'s `extract_items_from_grid()` (quantity/rate/amount columns) and by `award_outcomes.py`'s own award/estimate-amount parsing. Test coverage extended in `test_award_outcomes.py` (4 new cases) and `test_boq_extraction.py` (1 new end-to-end test).

**How this was found.** This pass's rotation landed on discovery. Per the standing brief, constructed real adversarial/boundary input against `parse_rand()` - the shared rand-amount parser `boq_extraction.py`'s own docstring explicitly calls out as reused "rather than a second hand-rolled parser" - specifically a negative amount, since every example in the function's own docstring ("Seen on 2026-10-17: ...") is positive and no existing test exercised a negative one. `python3 -c "import award_outcomes as ao; print(ao.parse_rand('-45000.00'))"` returned `45000.0`, not `-45000.0` - confirmed the sign was silently dropped, not just a formatting quirk.

**Root cause, traced, not guessed.** `parse_rand()`'s own pipeline is: strip any `(...)` group unconditionally (built only for a trailing annotation like `"(Including VAT.)"`), then strip every character that isn't a digit/comma/period via `re.sub(r"[^0-9,.]", "", s)`. A literal `"-"` is not in that allowed set, so it is discarded with no record kept - the function has no concept of "negative" at all. The same blanket `(...)`-stripping also means standard accounting negative notation - the whole value wrapped in parens, e.g. `"(R 45 000.00)"` - loses every digit along with the parens and returns `None` (no digits remain after stripping), rather than being read as a negative amount.

**Why this matters, and where it's actually reachable.** Confirmed via `sanral_fill.Workbook._decode_cell_value()`: a genuine Excel numeric cell is NOT at risk - its raw `<v>` XML value already carries the correct sign (negative-currency parentheses display is purely a styles.xml format, never the stored value), and `parse_rand()`'s own `isinstance(raw, (int, float))` branch passes a numeric cell straight through with `float(raw)`. The bug only bites a **text-typed** cell or an HTML table value - exactly the shape `parse_rand()`'s own docstring says these numbers are seen in live (`"R551 189,00"`, `"678228,5"`, etc. are all text, pulled from award-notice HTML or a buyer's own text-formatted spreadsheet cell). `boq_extraction.py`'s rate/amount columns are the most realistic place this surfaces: a real BOQ's "Omit" or credit line (a provisional-sum adjustment being deducted, a common and legitimate BOQ row shape) or a buyer's own retention/discount line can carry a negative rand value, and if that buyer's template has the cell formatted/typed as text rather than a native Excel number, the value silently becomes `None` (dropped - the item would then be rejected entirely by `extract_items_from_grid()`'s own "no number anywhere" skip, since parse_rand returning None for the only priced field leaves nothing) or, worse, a wrong POSITIVE figure that looks like a normal priced line with no error anywhere downstream.

**Fix.** `parse_rand()`: before the existing character-stripping, detect two negative shapes - (1) the whole trimmed string wrapped in parens with nothing but a currency marker/digits/separators inside (`^\(\s*R?\s*[\d,.\s]+\)$`) - negative, parens removed, falls through the rest of the pipeline normally; distinct from a trailing annotation like `"(Including VAT.)"`, which has no digits of its own and is unaffected, still stripped as before; (2) a literal `-` appearing anywhere before the first digit (`^[^0-9]*-`), covering `"-45000.00"`, `"-R 45 000.00"`, `"R-45000.00"`. The parsed magnitude is then negated at the very end, right before return (`-value if negative and value else value`, the `and value` guard avoiding a cosmetic `-0.0` for a genuinely-zero amount). Deliberately NOT changed: a dash that appears AFTER the first digit (e.g. the already-existing, unrelated `"45-50"` input, which was never a real rand-amount shape this parser receives and is unaffected either way, confirmed unchanged pre/post-fix).

**Verified red-then-green.** Added 4 new cases to `test_award_outcomes.py`'s existing `cases` dict (`"-45000.00"` -> `-45000.0`, `"-R 45 000.00"` -> `-45000.0`, `"(R 45 000.00)"` -> `-45000.0`, `"(1 234,50)"` -> `-1234.50`) and one new end-to-end test in `test_boq_extraction.py`, `test_negative_omission_credit_line_keeps_its_sign()`, building a real minimal in-memory `.xlsx` with a text-typed ("inlineStr") BOQ "Omit" line (`amount_zar` cell `"(R 45 000.00)"`) and a text-typed rate+amount row (`"-45,00"`/`"-5 400,00"`), asserting both the omission line is kept (not dropped as "no number anywhere") and all three negative values keep their sign through the real `sanral_fill.Workbook` -> `boq_extraction.extract_items_from_grid()` -> `award_outcomes.parse_rand()` path, no mocking. **Red:** saved the production diff, `git apply -R`, re-ran both test files - exactly the 4 predicted failures in `test_award_outcomes.py` (`got 45000.0`/`got 45000.0`/`got None`/`got None`) and 3 in `test_boq_extraction.py` (amount `None` instead of `-45000.0`; rate/amount `45.0`/`5400.0` instead of negative). **Green:** `git apply` to reapply, re-ran both - `ALL PASSED` / `0 failure(s)`. Also manually verified no regression on realistic non-negative inputs and on the pre-existing, unrelated `"45-50"` edge case (identical result pre/post-fix - `4550.0`, never a real input shape, not claimed to be handled). `python3 -m py_compile` clean on both production and test files. Broader regression sweep: `test_boq_extraction.py`, `test_tender_enrichment.py` (also calls `parse_rand()`), and `test_store_award_outcomes.py` all still pass unchanged.

**Backlog status.** No new backlog items opened by this fix. `git fetch origin main` immediately before writing this entry and again immediately before pushing showed no sibling commits landed in between.

To verify independently: `python3 -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'engine/discovery'); import award_outcomes as ao; print(ao.parse_rand('-45000.00'), ao.parse_rand('(R 45 000.00)'))"` and confirm it prints `-45000.0 -45000.0`, not `45000.0 None`. Run `python3 engine/discovery/test_award_outcomes.py` and `python3 engine/discovery/test_boq_extraction.py` from their own directory and confirm `ALL PASSED` / `0 failure(s)`.

### Finding 202 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, moderate - SANRAL Form B7's `check_plan()` (`engine/sanral_b7.py`) and its Tender Workspace twin `checkPlan()` (`app/lib/sanralB7.ts`) bounded each Targeted Enterprise's own subcontracting percentage to 0-100% individually, but never checked the SUM across TEs - two individually-valid percentages (60% and 55%) totalled 115% of the contract price with no error or warning anywhere)

**Area:** `engine/sanral_b7.py` `check_plan()`, `app/lib/sanralB7.ts` `checkPlan()` (the Tender Workspace's own pre-pack-request copy of the identical rule - the module's own header comment says to "keep the two in step"). Test coverage extended in `engine/test_sanral_b7.py` (2 new cases) and a new, narrowly-scoped `app/lib/sanralB7.spec.ts` (no spec file existed for this module before this pass, confirmed by grep - scoped to just this new check, not a retroactive full-coverage rewrite).

**How this was found.** This pass's rotation landed on SANRAL pack. Constructed real adversarial/boundary input against `sanral_b7.py`'s own Targeted Enterprise percentage validation - a plan with two TEs, each individually well within the existing 0-100% per-field bound (60% and 55% of the contract price excluding provisional sums), run through the real `check_plan()`: `errors == []`, `warnings` contained nothing about the total at all - only an unrelated "local share" warning computed off the already-impossible 115% total.

**Root cause, traced, not guessed.** `check_plan()`'s per-TE loop validates `pct_of_contract`/`pct_excl_provisional`/`black_ownership_pct` are each individually 0-100 (`_num(te.get(key))` bound-checked), and separately warns when the TEs' combined `pct_excl_provisional` total falls BELOW SANRAL's 30% policy minimum (line ~210, pre-existing) - but nothing anywhere checks the sum for exceeding 100%, a factually impossible allocation (more of the contract subcontracted to Targeted Enterprises than the whole contract is worth) most realistically caused by a data-entry mistake (a typo, or forgetting to subtract an already-allocated TE's share before adding a new one), not a real plan. `app/lib/sanralB7.ts`'s `checkPlan()` - the exact TypeScript mirror the Tender Workspace form calls before a pack is even requested, confirmed via its own header comment ("Mirror of engine/sanral_b7.py... Keep the two in step") - has the structurally identical gap, so this was never a one-sided sibling divergence: both the engine's pack-build-time check and the Workspace's own earlier, user-facing check were silent on this, confirmed by reading both side by side.

**Fix.** Both functions: after the existing below-30%-minimum warning, added a parallel warning (not an error - matching the existing below-minimum check's own severity, since SANRAL's own form has no hard block either) when the TEs' total `pct_excl_provisional` exceeds 100%: "Targeted Enterprises total {total}% of the contract price (excl. provisional sums) - more than the whole contract has been allocated; check for a data-entry error." Kept as a warning rather than an error deliberately, the same reasoning the existing below-minimum check already uses - the company may still have a real, if unusual, reason for the figures as entered, and an error would block pack generation outright rather than surface the figure for a human to check.

**Verified red-then-green.** `engine/test_sanral_b7.py`: added a case with two TEs totalling 115% (asserts the new warning fires, no error) and a case at exactly 100% (asserts it does NOT fire - no false positive at the boundary). **Red:** saved the diff, `git apply -R`, re-ran - the 115% case failed exactly as predicted (no over-allocation warning present); **Green:** `git apply` to reapply, re-ran - `ALL PASSED`. `app/lib/sanralB7.spec.ts` (new file): 3 tests - the same 115%/100%-boundary pair, plus one confirming the pre-existing below-30%-minimum warning is unaffected by the new check. **Red:** reverted both production files via the same diff, re-ran `npx vitest run lib/sanralB7.spec.ts` - 1 of 3 failed exactly as predicted (`expected false, got true` on the over-allocation assertion); **Green:** reapplied, re-ran - `3 passed`. `python3 -m py_compile` clean on both Python files. `npx eslint lib/sanralB7.ts lib/sanralB7.spec.ts` clean. Broader regression: full `npx vitest run` - 68/71 files, 501/506 tests pass; the 5 failures (`lib/properties.spec.ts`, `lib/payfast.spec.ts`, `app/company/properties/actions.spec.ts`) are a pre-existing, unrelated environment gap (`date-fns` not installed in `node_modules` in this container - confirmed via `ls node_modules/date-fns` failing and the error naming that import directly), not caused by or related to this fix. `npx tsc --noEmit` shows the same pre-existing `date-fns`/`react-day-picker` module-resolution errors in unrelated files, none in `sanralB7.ts`/`sanralB7.spec.ts`.

**Backlog status.** No new backlog items opened by this fix. `git fetch origin main` immediately before writing this entry and again immediately before pushing showed no sibling commits landed in between. Note on numbering: the sibling "standing solution-architect review" track's own Finding 201 (`fix/retry-onboarding-upload-rls-rpc`, PR #184) is unmerged - `main`'s own `QA-Edge-Case-Findings.md` still topped out at Finding 200 at the time this entry was written, but 201 was already claimed by that open PR, so this entry is numbered 202, not 201, to avoid a future collision once #184 merges.

To verify independently: run a plan with two Targeted Enterprises whose `pct_excl_provisional` total over 100% through `engine/sanral_b7.check_plan()` and confirm the returned warnings include "more than the whole contract has been allocated"; confirm the identical input through `app/lib/sanralB7.ts`'s `checkPlan()` gives the same warning text. Run `python3 engine/test_sanral_b7.py` (`ALL PASSED`) and `cd app && npx vitest run lib/sanralB7.spec.ts` (3 passed) from their own directories.

### Finding 203 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, severe - the SANRAL Pack Review screen's `signatureStatus()` (`app/app/tenders/[id]/pack-review-logic.ts`) showed the algorithm's SUGGESTED DEFAULT signatory's name whenever ANY signatory had been explicitly chosen, never the actually-chosen person's name, unless the two happened to coincide - confirmed live via the real caller, `pack-review-data.ts`)

**Area:** `app/app/tenders/[id]/pack-review-logic.ts` `signatureStatus()`, `app/app/tenders/[id]/pack-review-data.ts` (its one real caller). Test coverage extended in `app/app/tenders/[id]/pack-review-logic.test.ts` (2 new cases, 3 existing call sites updated for the new parameter).

**How this was found.** This pass's rotation landed on non-SANRAL pack; `engine/general/submission_plan.py`'s own `compile_plan()` was checked first and confirmed to be intentionally CLI-only reference tooling, not the production path (per its own TypeScript port's header comment, `submission-plan-logic.ts`: "the plan can't be computed by calling that Python module live from the app... per the architecture resolved with Sarel 2026-10-21"). Redirected to the real production classifiers and picked the least-referenced one, `general-pack-review-logic.ts` - reading it side by side with its SANRAL sibling `pack-review-logic.ts` (the file it explicitly says it "reuses... vocabulary and generic classifiers" from) surfaced the actual finding on the SANRAL side, not the general side.

**Root cause, traced, not guessed.** `signatureStatus()` took `{chosenId, fallback}` - no information about who `chosenId` actually resolves to, only `fallback` (whichever signatory `pickDefaultSignatory()` suggests as the pre-selected default). `pickDefaultSignatory()` (`signatory-logic.ts`) is, by its own docstring, "the default to pre-select when NOBODY has chosen a signatory for this tender yet" - it has no parameter for and no knowledge of `chosenId` whatsoever; it always returns its own scope-matched suggestion regardless of any real choice. Confirmed via the one real caller, `pack-review-data.ts`: `fallback = pickDefaultSignatory({signers, scopes, tender})` is computed completely independently of `chosenId`, then both are passed into `signatureStatus({chosenId, fallback})`. When `chosenId` was truthy, the OLD code unconditionally returned `value: \`${fallback.name} - ${fallback.signatory_capacity}\`` - the suggested default's name, not the real choice's. Any company with more than one person holding a signatory capacity, where the explicitly-chosen signatory differs from the algorithm's own top-scoring suggestion (a routine, likely scenario - e.g. a CEO explicitly chosen for one tender while a regional director scores higher on the generic region/industry/discipline match), had the Pack Review screen's "Who signs this bid" line show the WRONG PERSON'S NAME on a live compliance checklist, while the real, correctly-stored `tender_answers.signatory_person_id` value was unaffected (the bug is display-only, confirmed by reading `requestSubmissionPack()`'s own validation and the pack bridge's own read path, neither of which goes through `signatureStatus()`).

**Why the existing test never caught it.** `pack-review-logic.test.ts`'s own "an explicit choice is confirmed" test called `signatureStatus({chosenId: "person-1", fallback: {name: "Jane Soap", ...}})` and asserted `value === "Jane Soap - Director"` - but the fixture never gave the chosen person their OWN name, so a wrong-person bug and a right-person result were indistinguishable in that one test. The exact same shape as this file's own header comment about `general-pack-review-logic.ts`'s sibling `signatureAnswerStatus()`, which was written correctly from the start (threading the real `chosenPerson` through via `people.find()`) and already has its own "can no longer be found" branch - `pack-review-logic.ts`'s SANRAL version never got either.

**Fix.** `signatureStatus()` now takes `chosenPerson: {name, signatory_capacity} | null` alongside `chosenId`/`fallback`. When `chosenId` is set: uses `chosenPerson`'s own name/capacity if resolved, or returns a new "missing"/"The chosen signatory can no longer be found - choose again" state (mirroring `signatureAnswerStatus()`'s identical branch) if not. The `needs_input`-with-fallback-suggestion branch is unchanged, reached only when nobody has chosen at all. `pack-review-data.ts`: resolves `chosenPerson = chosenId ? signerList.find(p => p.id === chosenId) ?? null : null` - the same `signerList` already fetched to compute `fallback`, no new query.

**Verified red-then-green.** Rewrote the misleading "an explicit choice is confirmed" test to use the SAME name for chosen and fallback explicitly (so it still tests the coincidence case honestly) and added two new tests: an explicit choice DIFFERENT from the fallback (asserts the chosen person's own name appears, not the fallback's), and a `chosenId` that no longer resolves (asserts the new "can no longer be found" state, not a stale fallback name). Updated the 2 scenario tests' own call sites for the new parameter. **Red:** saved the diff (both production files), `git apply -R`, re-ran `node --experimental-strip-types app/app/tenders/[id]/pack-review-logic.test.ts` directly (node's own `--test` CLI flag doesn't glob-match this bracketed directory path; running the file directly works since it self-registers via `node:test`) - exactly 2 of 22 failed, precisely the two new adversarial cases. **Green:** `git apply` to reapply, re-ran - 22/22 pass. `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npx eslint` both clean on all 3 touched files.
