Proper collision check, real merge-base diff per PR: fetched all 28 open PR heads read-only (`git fetch origin pull/<n>/head:pr-<n>-tmp` for `#164`/`#165`/`#176`-`#201`, never checked out as a working branch), then `git diff $(git merge-base main pr-<n>-tmp) pr-<n>-tmp -- engine/discovery/store_award_outcomes.py engine/discovery/test_store_award_outcomes.py` for all 28 - **zero PRs touch either file.** All 28 temp refs deleted immediately after (confirmed 0 remain, `git branch --list "pr-*-tmp"` empty). Re-`git fetch origin main` immediately before pushing - still clean at `c4d8928`, no sibling-track activity landed during this pass. Pushed directly to `main`: a pure-Python, already-unit-tested merge function, no RLS, no money path, no hard-stop gate, no worker-image change, no schema/migration - same classification this track has used throughout for engine-side logic fixes.

### Finding 247 (CONFIRMED AND FIXED ON `main` - low/moderate, cross-source data-attribution class - the SAME bug shape Finding 246 fixed for `winner_amount_zar`, recurring in the two sibling fields `merge()` left untouched: `winner_points`/`winner_bbbee_points`)

**Area:** `engine/discovery/store_award_outcomes.py`'s `merge()`, the `winner_points`/`winner_bbbee_points` fields - this pass's own task brief's concrete starting point ("does `merge()` have any OTHER pair of related fields with this same shape") named these two explicitly as the ones Finding 246's own fix didn't touch, and they turned out to be real, not a false lead.

**The concrete reason: `winner_name` is picked one way, `winner_points`/`winner_bbbee_points` another, with no check they describe the same part.** Finding 246 fixed `winner_amount_zar`'s fallback to only accept an amount from a part naming the SAME winner (or no winner at all). `winner_points`/`winner_bbbee_points` were left going through the plain `first()` helper - the first (`SOURCE_PRIORITY` order: `sanral_awarded` > `sanral_closed` > `etenders_portal`) part that HAS the field at all, with no check that part is `winner_part` (the part `winner_name` actually came from) or even names the same company. `part_from_sanral()` sets `winner`, `winner_points` (`rec["full_points"]`) and `winner_bbbee_points` (`rec["bbbee_points"]`) from the SAME `rec` - one SANRAL detail page's own label rows (`SANRAL_FIELDS`, `award_outcomes.parse_sanral_result_page()`), parsed independently of each other. A detail page can genuinely have `awarded_to` filled in with `full_points`/`bbbee_points` blank (not every SANRAL award-notice page template carries that row) - a normal, already-anticipated gap, the same way a SANRAL award page can lack a parseable `approved_contract_amount` (Finding 246's own `with_contract_amount` evidence). `part_from_portal()` never sets `winner_points`/`winner_bbbee_points` at all, so only SANRAL parts (`sanral_awarded`, `sanral_closed` - two genuinely different detail-page scrapes for the SAME tender, e.g. before/after an appeal or re-award, Finding 246's own named scenario) can ever supply them.

**Confirmed real, not hypothetical.** Built the real repro directly through `part_from_sanral()` (no mocking, same builder production code calls) - the higher-priority `sanral_awarded` part names a real winner with no points row on its page; a lower-priority `sanral_closed` part for the SAME tender, naming a genuinely DIFFERENT company, carries real points:
```python
awarded_rec = {"source": "sanral_awarded", "reference": "N.003-004-2026/1", "title": "Test tender 3",
               "awarded_to": "Acme Construction (Pty) Ltd", "full_points": None, "bbbee_points": None}
closed_rec = {"source": "sanral_closed", "reference": "N.003-004-2026/1", "title": "Test tender 3",
              "awarded_to": "Beta Builders CC", "full_points": "87.4000", "bbbee_points": "10.0000"}
row = sao.merge("sanral:N.003-004-2026/1", [sao.part_from_sanral(awarded_rec), sao.part_from_sanral(closed_rec)])
```
**RED, confirmed real:**
```
winner_name: "Acme Construction (Pty) Ltd"
winner_points: "87.4000"          # Beta Builders' own score, from an entirely different winner
winner_bbbee_points: "10.0000"    # likewise
```
with no note at all - unlike the amount case pre-fix, `first()` doesn't even leave a trace that a different source's value was used.

**Why this matters downstream, not just internally.** `app/app/tenders/[id]/market-context.tsx` renders `outcome.winner_points` directly beside the winner's own name on a bidder-facing tender page ("`{outcome.winner_points} points`") - a misattributed score would show a specific company's name next to a specific points figure it never earned. `winner_bbbee_points` feeds migration `0062`'s `market_trend_by_tags` RPC (`bbbee_rows` CTE: `group by winner_bbbee_points`) - a market-intelligence BBBEE-level distribution read by `app/lib/marketTrendLogic.ts` - so a misattributed BBBEE level skews that aggregate, not just one row's own display.

**Fix.** Added `winner_field(field, label)`, the same guard Finding 246 gave `winner_amount_zar`, applied to both `winner_points` and `winner_bbbee_points`: a value is only accepted from a part whose own `winner` (if present) name-matches (`norm_name()`) the chosen `winner`, or from a part naming no winner at all. When nothing clears that bar, the field stays `None` and a new note names the excluded source and the OTHER winner its score actually belongs to - same "say why, don't go quiet" convention. The legitimate case (same real winner, spelled differently per SANRAL page, points on only one of them) still fills in, since it only ever needed the name-normalized match it already has.

**Verified red-then-green.** Two permanent regression tests added to `engine/discovery/test_store_award_outcomes.py`, registered in its own `main()`: `test_points_fallback_never_crosses_to_a_different_winners_source()` (the repro above) and its mirror, `test_points_fallback_still_works_for_the_same_winner_spelled_differently()` (SANRAL `"Build Co (Pty) Ltd"` / `"BUILD CO LTD"` - same company, one page's points must still fill in). `git stash push -- engine/discovery/store_award_outcomes.py` (keeping both new tests), `python3 test_store_award_outcomes.py` → `2 FAILED` (`winner_points`/`winner_bbbee_points` carrying Beta Builders' own figures instead of `None`; the mismatch-note check) - exactly the first test, the mirror test already passes pre-fix (confirming it isn't vacuous). `git stash pop`, same command → `0 failure(s)`, all 10 tests (the 8 Finding-246-era tests plus these 2). Full existing suite re-run clean - no regression to `find_winner()`'s own tests, the batch-upsert key-shape test, the zero-amount test, or the `winner_amount_zar` fallback tests. `engine/discovery/test_award_prices.py` re-run clean, `0 failure(s)`. `python3 -m py_compile store_award_outcomes.py test_store_award_outcomes.py` clean.

### Finding 248 (CONFIRMED AND FIXED ON `main` - moderate, real-browser-reproduced UI bug - `DownloadAllButton` (`app/app/tenders/[id]/download-all-button.tsx`), the "one-click Download submission pack" control, silently delivered only the LAST of N files to the user whenever a job has more than one output file - the common case for every real SANRAL pack, not an edge case)

**Area:** `app/app/tenders/[id]/download-all-button.tsx`, rendered by `submission-pack.tsx` (line ~352) for every `ready` SANRAL pack job, with `urls = [storage_path_pdf, ...Object.values(output_files)]` mapped through signed URLs - i.e. the main merged PDF plus every other output file (at minimum the filled Financial `.xlsm` workbook; `submission-pack.tsx`'s own tooltip text: "The filled .xlsm workbooks come with them"). This file had never been mentioned anywhere in `System-Status.md` or this doc before (confirmed by basename search across both files) - a genuinely never-swept pure-client component, distinct from the `*-actions.ts`/`*-logic.ts` files this track's many `tenders/[id]` sweeps have already exhausted.

**The bug.** The button's `onClick` looped over every URL synchronously, creating an `<a>`, appending it, calling `.click()`, and removing it, for each file in the same tick:
```tsx
for (const url of urls) {
  const a = document.createElement("a");
  a.href = url;
  a.rel = "noopener";
  document.body.appendChild(a);
  a.click();
  a.remove();
}
```
`rel = "noopener"` with no `target` set at all is itself a tell - that attribute only does anything paired with `target="_blank"`, which this code never sets, suggesting an attribute got dropped at some point. Calling `.click()` on several plain, same-tab anchors back to back, with no `download` attribute and no `target`, triggers several competing top-level navigations in the same task; each new one supersedes the previous before its own download can register. The network layer still sees every request (confirmed below), but the browser only ever completes ONE download - the last URL in the array - silently. For any pack with 2+ output files (every real SANRAL pack), "Download submission pack (N files)" button delivers 1 file, not N, with no error, no partial-success message, nothing - contradicting its own label and its own doc comment ("fires all of them from one click instead of making someone click each link in turn").

**Reproduced live in a real browser (Playwright/Chromium, not jsdom - jsdom implements no real navigation, so it could never have caught this), against a real two-origin HTTP topology matching production** (this app's own origin vs. a Supabase Storage signed-URL origin are different origins in real deployment): one plain Python HTTP server on port 8920 serving a page that runs the exact onClick body above against 3 URLs on a SEPARATE server on port 8913/8911/8912 (tried with no `Content-Disposition` header at all - matching this codebase's real `createSignedUrl(p, 600)` calls, which never pass `{download: ...}` - and separately with `Content-Disposition: attachment` set, and with the `download` attribute added, same-origin and cross-origin, to isolate the real cause). Result, every cross-origin variant: all 3 `file1.pdf`/`file2.pdf`/`file3.pdf` requests genuinely hit the server (confirmed via Playwright's own `request` log), but exactly **1** Playwright `download` event fired, always the LAST URL in the array (`file3.pdf`) - regardless of `Content-Disposition` or the `download` attribute, both of which only help in the same-origin case. Staggering the three clicks with a `setTimeout(..., i * 300)` instead of a tight synchronous loop - with no other change, no `download` attribute, no `Content-Disposition` - reproducibly fixed it: all 3 `download` events fired, every run. This matches a well-known real-world browser limitation (programmatically clicking several same-tab anchors in one tick collapses to the last one) rather than anything specific to this app's markup.

**Fix.** Replaced the synchronous loop with `urls.forEach((url, i) => setTimeout(() => { ... }, i * 250))` - each file's anchor click now runs on its own task, 250ms apart, clearing the collapsing-navigation window the repro above measured, while staying well under a second so N files still feels like one click. Kept `a.download = ""` as a free, no-downside addition (forces a same-origin link in this family to download rather than navigate, should one ever exist; confirmed in the repro it does nothing extra for the real cross-origin case, but costs nothing either).

**Verified red-then-green, myself, with real output.** `git stash` on the one touched file, reran the exact onClick body in the Playwright harness against a genuinely cross-origin 3-file case (app page on port 8920, files on port 8913, no `Content-Disposition`) - **RED**, exactly as described: `Total "download" events fired: 1` (`file3.pdf` only), all 3 requests seen on the file server. `git stash pop`, same harness with the fix's staggered-click shape - **GREEN**: `Total "download" events fired: 3` (`file1.pdf`, `file2.pdf`, `file3.pdf`, in order). No existing automated test covers this component (confirmed: no `.spec.tsx`/React-component-testing infrastructure exists anywhere in this repo - every `app/`-side test is a pure-logic `.spec.ts`/`.test.ts`, and jsdom couldn't observe this bug class even if one existed) - the Playwright browser harness above is the real, reproducible verification for this fix, same standing this track already gives a real scratch-Postgres run for a DB-layer finding. `npx tsc --noEmit` clean. `npx eslint "app/tenders/[id]/download-all-button.tsx"` clean (0 errors). Full `npx vitest run` from `app/`: **72/72 files, 576/576 tests** - unaffected, confirming no regression (this fix touches no other file, and no existing test exercises this component at all, so an unchanged count here is the expected, correct result, not a gap).

**Backlog status.** `git fetch origin main` at the start of this pass, and again immediately before pushing, both found local already matching `origin/main` exactly - `a86f99f` (the task brief's own stated HEAD) - no sibling-track commit landed in between. Proper collision check, read-only, per the standing guardrail: read every one of the 28 open PRs' own changed-files list via `mcp__github__pull_request_read` (`get_files`) and confirmed **zero touch `download-all-button.tsx` or `submission-pack.tsx`'s `DownloadAllButton` render site** - `#178`/`#180` both touch `submission-pack.tsx`, but only its `disabledReason`/`fixCount` gate near the top of the file (lines ~166-185), nowhere near the `DownloadAllButton` call (line ~352) this fix doesn't touch at all. No fetched PR branch was checked out or left as a local ref. Pushed directly to `main`: a pure client-side UI timing fix in one presentational component, no RLS, no money path, no hard-stop gate, no worker-image change, no schema/migration - small and safe per the standing guardrail's own definition.

To verify independently: read `app/app/tenders/[id]/download-all-button.tsx` and confirm the `onClick` now wraps each file's anchor-click in `setTimeout(..., i * 250)` rather than a tight `for` loop. In a real browser (not jsdom), build a page on one origin whose button fires the pre-fix onClick body against ≥2 signed URLs on a different origin with no `Content-Disposition` header, and confirm only the last file's download actually completes even though every file's own HTTP request lands; confirm the post-fix (staggered) version delivers every file. `cd app && npx vitest run` → `576/576`; `npx tsc --noEmit` → clean; `npx eslint "app/tenders/[id]/download-all-button.tsx"` → clean. `mcp__github__pull_request_read` (`get_files`) on any of the 28 open PRs shows none touching this file.

### Finding 249 (CONFIRMED AND FIXED ON `main` - low/moderate, UI content-correctness class, the same "these surfaces can't quietly disagree" shape as Findings 240-243 (`lib/readiness.ts`) - `app/app/company/page.tsx`'s own `VaultProgressSummary` document count used a path-only "on file" rule for all 7 `VAULT_DOCUMENTS` kinds, silently disagreeing with `ComplianceDocumentsSection.tsx`'s/`ReadOnlyView.tsx`'s own already-correct, broader rule rendered directly below it on the exact same page)

**Area:** `app/app/company/page.tsx` (`documentsOnFile`, feeding `VaultProgressSummary`'s "N of 7 on file" card); new centralised function `app/lib/vaultDocuments.ts`'s `vaultDocumentOnFile()`. Test coverage added in `app/lib/vaultDocuments.test.ts`.

**How this was found.** Fresh-angle sweep per this pass's own task brief, deliberately away from `tenders/[id]` (already exhaustively covered by the three preceding negative passes). Rather than re-sweep `app/app/pipeline/`, billing, or `engine/`'s larger-surface candidates - all of which cross-checking against this file's and `QA-Edge-Case-Findings.md`'s own mention counts showed were already heavily covered - ranked every `.ts`/`.tsx` file under `app/app/` by how many times its own filename appears anywhere in either standing doc, surfacing a cluster of `app/app/company/_components/*.tsx` presentational components with literally zero prior mentions (`BankDetailsSection.tsx`, `BeeCidbSection.tsx`, `CompanyIdentitySection.tsx`, `ComplianceDocumentsView.tsx`, `DocumentRow.tsx`, `LettersSection.tsx`, `SavingsBaselineSection.tsx`, `SizeOfficesSection.tsx`, `VaultProgressSummary.tsx`, `ui.tsx`, `types.ts` - never once named by this track before). Read `VaultProgressSummary.tsx` (a pure presentational component, its own header comment naming `page.tsx` as the source of its `documentsOnFile`/`documentsTotal` props) then traced that count back to its real computation in `page.tsx`.

**Root cause, traced, not guessed.** `page.tsx`'s own comment claimed parity ("the same 7 `VAULT_DOCUMENTS` columns `ComplianceDocumentsSection` already renders one row per"), but its actual formula was `(Object.keys(VAULT_DOCUMENTS) as VaultDocumentKind[]).filter((k) => !!row[VAULT_DOCUMENTS[k].column]).length` - a **path-only** check for all 7 kinds. `ComplianceDocumentsSection.tsx`'s own per-row `status` (and `ReadOnlyView.tsx`'s own separate "not on file" rollup, which independently duplicates the identical rule a THIRD time) instead already use a broader "document uploaded OR the matching text/level/date field was typed in directly" rule for 5 of the 7 kinds: `cidb` (path OR `cidb_grading` OR `cidb_expiry`), `sars_tcs_pin` (`sarsTcsPinOnFile()` - Finding 240's own centralised function), `pi_insurance` (path OR `pi_insurance_policy_number`), `bank_letter` (path OR `bank_confirmation_letter_date`), `bee_proof` (path OR `bee_level`) - each field independently typeable through `EditForm.tsx`'s own plain text/date/number inputs, with no document upload required. `page.tsx`'s own `documentsOnFile` never read any of those 5 extra fields.

**Reproduced RED, real code, not reasoned about.** A Node script (`node --experimental-strip-types`) importing the real, unmodified `lib/vaultDocuments.ts` and running `page.tsx`'s own pre-fix formula, verbatim, against a company row with 5 of 7 kinds genuinely captured by typing in (not uploading) `cidb_grading`, `sars_tcs_pin`, `pi_insurance_policy_number`, `bank_confirmation_letter_date` and `bee_level` - a completely normal, common real state (per `sarsTcsPinOnFile()`'s own comment: "the PIN is usually typed in, not uploaded"):
```
documentsTotal: 7
page.tsx's own current (pre-fix) documentsOnFile: 0 -> would render: '7 still missing - add them'
ComplianceDocumentsSection's/ReadOnlyView's own per-kind 'on file' rule says: 5 of 7 are genuinely on file
MISMATCH: true (expected true - this is the bug)
```
Concretely: a company with 5 of 7 compliance facts genuinely on file would see `VaultProgressSummary` say "0 of 7 on file - 7 still missing, add them" directly above `ComplianceDocumentsSection` correctly showing 5 of those same 7 rows as valid/on file, on the exact same page.

**Fix.** Added `vaultDocumentOnFile(kind, company)` to `lib/vaultDocuments.ts`, centralising the same per-kind "on file" rule `ComplianceDocumentsSection.tsx`/`ReadOnlyView.tsx` already compute inline (duplicated identically in both) - including delegating `sars_tcs_pin` to the existing `sarsTcsPinOnFile()` rather than re-deriving it a third way, and matching both files' own treatment of `iso_9001` (on file only when `certified === true` AND a document is uploaded; `certified === false`/`null` both read as "not on file", the same tone both existing renderers already give them). `page.tsx`'s `documentsOnFile` now calls this shared function instead of its own path-only check. Deliberately left `ComplianceDocumentsSection.tsx`/`ReadOnlyView.tsx` untouched (both already correct) - the minimal, lowest-risk fix is to make the one wrong site agree with the two already-right ones, not to refactor files that aren't broken.

### Finding 250 (CONFIRMED AND FIXED ON `main` - moderate, `db-max-rows` class (the same PostgREST-1000-row-cap bug `lib/marketPricing.ts`/PR #111, `lib/discoveryPagination.ts` and `lib/personCredentials.ts` were each already fixed for) - `app/app/company/page.tsx`'s own `cv_uploads` read, feeding BOTH the `BidReadinessCard` score shown on this exact page AND the new `VaultProgressSummary` "people/CVs" card right below it, was a plain, unpaginated `.select("person_id")` - the identical table this exact cap was already fixed for, in `lib/companyReadinessData.ts`, for the dashboard/discovery surfaces, but never in this one)

**Area:** `app/app/company/page.tsx` (the `cv_uploads` read feeding `peopleWithCvIds`, used by both `computeBidReadiness()`'s `peopleWithCvCount` and `VaultProgressSummary`'s `peopleWithCv`/`peopleMissingCv` props).

**How this was found.** Continuing directly from Finding 249's own fresh-angle sweep of `VaultProgressSummary.tsx`'s own data source in `page.tsx` - rather than re-sweep the already-exhausted `app/app/company/_components/*.tsx` cluster a second time (read in full this pass: `BankDetailsSection.tsx`, `BeeCidbSection.tsx`, `CompanyIdentitySection.tsx`, `ComplianceDocumentsView.tsx`, `DocumentRow.tsx`, `LettersSection.tsx`, `SavingsBaselineSection.tsx`, `SizeOfficesSection.tsx`, `ui.tsx`, `types.ts`, `shared.tsx`, `VaultDocumentUploader.tsx`, `DirectVaultDocumentUploader.tsx` - all genuinely clean, no logic bugs, each view/action pair already using the shared `vaultDocumentOnFile()`/`filenameFromPath()` rule consistently), did a fresh mention-count ranking across a wider slice of `app/app/` (counting each `.ts`/`.tsx` filename's own occurrences in both standing docs) rather than taking the task brief's own named cluster on faith - turned up `app/tools/cidb-grade/CidbGradeClient.tsx` and `app/tools/b6-estimator/B6EstimatorClient.tsx` as genuinely low-mention, substantial-surface candidates; both turned out to already correctly reuse the real, shared, already-tested `lib/cidbGrading.ts`/`lib/sanralScoring.ts` functions the real tender-compliance flow also uses (confirmed by reading `app/tenders/[id]/compliance-data.ts`'s own call site of `estimateSanralConventional()` side by side with the estimator's own call - same function, consistent argument shapes, no divergence) - a clean negative, not pursued further. **Root cause, traced, not guessed.** `page.tsx`'s own `cv_uploads` read was a plain `supabase.from("cv_uploads").select("person_id")` - no `.range()`, no `fetchAllRows()`. This is the exact same table `lib/companyReadinessData.ts`'s own `fetchCompanyReadiness()` (used by `dashboard/page.tsx` and `discovery/page.tsx`) already had to fix for this exact reason - that file's own comment explains why, in detail: `cv_uploads`' own migration (`0008`) makes "re-uploading a newer CV... a new row (history kept), not an overwrite" with no retention, so "one company's own upload history grows forever" and "a long-lived company could pass 1000 rows and silently undercount distinct people-with-a-CV" against PostgREST's own documented, confirmed-live 1000-row response cap (`lib/supabasePaging.ts`'s own `POSTGREST_PAGE_SIZE` comment, confirmed live 2026-10-23 during the Market Intelligence QA pass, and independently re-fixed for this exact same reason in `lib/marketPricing.ts` (PR #111), `lib/discoveryPagination.ts` and `lib/personCredentials.ts`). `page.tsx`'s own module comment even explicitly claimed parity with `companyReadinessData.ts` ("Scoring itself lives in lib/readiness.ts (pure, unit-tested) so this page, the dashboard and the onboarding end screen can never quietly disagree - see lib/companyReadinessData.ts") - but `page.tsx` only ever reused the PURE scoring function (`computeBidReadiness()`), never the paginated FETCHER (`fetchCompanyReadiness()`) that comment points at; it ran its own separate, unpaginated query instead. So once a single company's `cv_uploads` history passes 1000 rows (a realistic state for a long-lived company, per `companyReadinessData.ts`'s own comment, not a contrived edge case), `/company`'s own `BidReadinessCard` could show a genuinely LOWER readiness score than the identical company's own dashboard/discovery readiness chip for the exact same underlying fact, and `VaultProgressSummary`'s "People/CVs" card could list real people as "missing a CV" who, per `/people/<id>`'s own page, genuinely already have one on file - the same "two surfaces computing the same fact two different ways" bug class as Findings 240-243/249, just reached through a pagination gap rather than a field-rule gap.

**Reproduced RED, real code, not reasoned about.** A scratch script (`node --experimental-strip-types`) importing the REAL, unmodified `fetchAllRows` from `lib/supabasePaging.ts` and a mock PostgREST-shaped server stub that caps every response at 1000 rows - the same `serverThatCapsAt()` shape `lib/supabasePaging.spec.ts`'s own existing regression test already uses for this exact documented cap - against 1056 simulated `cv_uploads` rows (1050 re-uploads by 3 "chatty" people, plus one row each for 6 other, genuinely distinct people whose single uploads land after row 1000 in insertion order, the realistic shape `companyReadinessData.ts`'s own comment describes), running `page.tsx`'s own pre-fix logic (`new Set(cvRows.map(r => r.person_id))`, fed by a single, unpaginated page(0, 99999) call) side by side with the fix (`fetchAllRows`):
```
Total cv_uploads rows simulated: 1056 - real distinct people with a CV: 9
OLD page.tsx logic (unpaginated select): {"peopleWithCvCount":3,"peopleMissingCv":["Person 4","Person 5","Person 6","Person 7","Person 8","Person 9"]}
NEW page.tsx logic (fetchAllRows, matches companyReadinessData.ts): {"peopleWithCvCount":9,"peopleMissingCv":[]}
RED (bug reproduced on old logic): true
GREEN (fix gives the real count): true
```
Concretely: 6 real people with a genuine CV on file would be shown on `VaultProgressSummary` as "missing a CV - add one", and the company's own bid-readiness score on `/company` would read `peopleWithCvCount: 3` instead of the real `9`, while the identical company's own dashboard/discovery readiness chip (via the already-paginated `fetchCompanyReadiness()`) would correctly show `9`.

**Fix.** `page.tsx`'s own `cv_uploads` query now goes through `fetchAllRows()` (imported from `@/lib/supabasePaging`, the same shared helper `lib/companyReadinessData.ts`/`lib/marketPricing.ts`/`lib/discoveryPagination.ts`/`lib/personCredentials.ts` already use for this exact table/this exact reason), with the same `20_000`-row cap `companyReadinessData.ts` itself uses. `peopleWithCvIds` is now built from `cvUploads.rows` instead of a plain `cvRows ?? []`. The misleading module comment claiming parity with `companyReadinessData.ts` while not actually calling its fetcher was corrected in place to describe what the code now actually does, rather than left to mislead the next reader the way it misled this one. Deliberately minimal - no refactor of `fetchCompanyReadiness()` itself, and no change to `peopleRows`/`experienceCount`'s own queries (both already `count: "exact", head: true` or a small, bounded `people` select, neither at risk of this cap).

### Finding 251 (CONFIRMED AND FIXED ON `main` - moderate, `db-max-rows` class (the same PostgREST-1000-row-cap bug Finding 250 and its own five named predecessors - `lib/marketPricing.ts` PR #111, `lib/discoveryPagination.ts`, `lib/companyReadinessData.ts`, `lib/personCredentials.ts`, `scripts/send-*.ts` - were each already fixed for) in a code path the prior sweeps' own grep method never covered: `.rpc(` calls, not `.from().select()` calls) - `app/app/admin/discovered-opportunities/page.tsx`'s `platform_admin_discovered_opportunities()` and `app/app/admin/tenders/page.tsx`'s `platform_admin_tender_catalog()` were each a single, unranged `supabase.rpc(...)` call reading an entire cross-tenant table with no filter and no internal `LIMIT`)

**Area:** `app/app/admin/discovered-opportunities/page.tsx` (its `platform_admin_discovered_opportunities()` RPC, migration `0072`) and `app/app/admin/tenders/page.tsx` (its `platform_admin_tender_catalog()` RPC, migration `0103`).

**Origin of this finding.** This pass's own task was explicitly the db-max-rows lead Finding 250's own write-up surfaced: "are there any OTHER `.from(...).select(...)` calls anywhere in `app/` that read a table which can realistically exceed 1000 rows, with no `fetchAllRows()`/explicit pagination?" The 2026-11-06 systematic sweep of this exact bug class (`System-Status.md`'s own "did the SYSTEMATIC version of the unranged-`.select()`-hits-1000-row-cap sweep" entry) documented its own mechanical method in full: `grep -n "\.select(" app/lib/*.ts` and every `app/**/actions.ts` file, plus a targeted `.from("tenders")`/`.from("tender_requirements")` grep once the shared tables emerged as the real risk factor. That method's own grep pattern structurally never matches a bare `.rpc(fn)` call (there is no `.select(` token anywhere near it) and was never pointed at `page.tsx` files in general (only `lib/*.ts` and `actions.ts`) - which is exactly why Finding 250 itself (a `page.tsx` file) slipped through that same sweep, and why the entire class of RPC-backed reads has never once been checked for this cap, anywhere in this codebase's history, before this pass.

**Confirming the premise this finding depends on - does PostgREST's db-max-rows cap actually apply to `.rpc(` calls, not just `.from().select()` reads - rather than assuming it.** This project has no live Supabase/PostgREST credentials reachable from this sandbox, so the original 2026-10-23 live confirmation method (hit the real API with `.limit(5000)` and read `Content-Range`) could not be repeated here. Two independent, verifiable checks were used instead, both done for real, not reasoned about from memory:
1. **Client library:** `node_modules/@supabase/postgrest-js/src/PostgrestClient.ts`'s `rpc()` method returns a `PostgrestFilterBuilder` - the exact same builder type `.from().select()` returns, with `.range()` available on it unconditionally (confirmed by reading `PostgrestTransformBuilder.ts`'s `range()` implementation: it just sets `offset`/`limit` URL search params on `this.url`, with no branch excluding an RPC-issued request). Several existing call sites in this codebase already chain `.rpc(...).range(...)` in the same file (e.g. `app/discovery/page.tsx`, `lib/marketPricing.ts`), confirming this compiles and is an established pattern here, even though no existing call actually ranges an RPC's own result (every existing `.range()` in those files is on a sibling `.from()` call).
2. **Server behavior:** downloaded PostgREST's own real source (`git clone --depth 1 --branch v12.2.3 https://github.com/PostgREST/postgrest.git` to a scratch directory, read-only, deleted after use - not executed; running the compiled `postgrest` binary itself to stand up a live local server was attempted first and was denied by this session's own sandbox classifier as "[Code from External]" when trying to run the downloaded binary - a genuine sandbox denial, not worked around, so a true live-server test could not be completed in this pass). Read `src/PostgREST/Plan.hs` directly: `dbActionPlan` routes `ActRoutine identifier invMethod -> DbCall <$> callReadPlan identifier conf sCache apiReq invMethod` (an RPC call) exactly the same way it routes `ActRelationRead`/`ActRelationMut` (a table/view read) through `wrappedReadPlan`/`mutateReadPlan` - and `callReadPlan` itself calls `rPlan <- readPlan relIdentifier conf sCache apiRequest`, the IDENTICAL `readPlan` function `wrappedReadPlan`/`mutateReadPlan` call for ordinary table/view reads. `readPlan`'s own body (line 329-335) is where `configDbMaxRows` is applied via `treeRestrictRange configDbMaxRows (iAction apiRequest)`. Since RPC calls and table reads share this exact code path with no branch distinguishing them, `db-max-rows` applies identically to both - a conclusion read from PostgREST's own planner source, not inferred.

Given both checks hold (the server-side planner genuinely treats a `SETOF`/`TABLE`-returning function call as a read like any other, and the client genuinely supports `.range()` on an RPC result the same way), this finding is treated as confirmed, with this limitation stated plainly: the live-server step of the standard verification method (hit the real API, read `Content-Range`) could not be completed in this sandbox, unlike the original 2026-10-23 confirmation for `.select()` reads. A future pass with real Supabase/staging credentials, or one not blocked from running a downloaded PostgREST binary, can close this gap directly - noted in `System-Status.md` as an open item for that check specifically, separate from the RPC-pagination fix itself, which does not depend on it (see "why fixing this is safe either way" below).

**Why fixing this is safe even if the live-server step were somehow wrong.** `fetchAllRows()`'s own loop (`lib/supabasePaging.ts`) stops paging as soon as a page comes back shorter than the requested range (`if (!data || data.length < to - offset + 1) break;`). If PostgREST's RPC path turned out NOT to honor `.range()` at all and always returned the full result regardless of the requested window, the very first page would already contain every row, come back shorter than the requested `POSTGREST_PAGE_SIZE` window (since the real row count is far below 1000 for any admin page actually used today), and the loop would stop after exactly one call - identical behavior to the unfixed code, with no risk of looping or duplicating rows. The fix cannot make either page worse than it already was; it can only make it correct once the real row count passes 1000.

**The two real candidates, and why they are the two highest-risk query shapes in this codebase per its own established precedent.** Per Finding 250's own "the rare one that reads an unbounded-growth table either with no filter or with a filter that doesn't bound growth (company-wide or system-wide reads of an append-only, no-retention table are the highest-risk shape)" framing:
1. **`platform_admin_discovered_opportunities()`** (migration `0072`) - `select ... from discovered_opportunities o join companies c ... where is_platform_admin() order by o.first_seen desc`, no `LIMIT`. Migration `0004`'s own comment on this table: "One row per (company, OCDS release) the discovery watch has ever scored and reported" - no retention mentioned anywhere, and `lib/discoveryPagination.ts`'s own header comment independently confirms "a per-company table that accumulates one row for every OCDS release ever scored against that company, forever - no retention/archival exists." This admin RPC reads it for EVERY company at once (`app/app/admin/discovered-opportunities/page.tsx`'s own page copy: "Every tender/RFQ/RFP/EOI Discovery has scored, for every company - not scoped to one tenant") - the sum across every company's own unbounded history, the single highest-risk shape named in this codebase's own precedent.
2. **`platform_admin_tender_catalog()`** (migration `0103`) - `select ... from tenders t where is_platform_admin() order by t.closing_date asc nulls last, t.created_at desc`, no `LIMIT`. `tenders` is this codebase's own independently-named highest-risk table for this exact cap: migration `0001`'s own header comment calls it "SHARED/PUBLIC...Shared across every company - not tenant-scoped", and the 2026-11-06 systematic sweep's own write-up records live tests of individual discovery scrapers each returning 268 (`capetown_procurement.py`) and 292 (`kouga.py`) rows from a SINGLE buyer alone, fed daily by "a dozen+ discovery scrapers." Five other reads of this exact table (`lib/personCredentials.ts`, three `scripts/send-*.ts` cron senders) were already independently fixed for this cap in that same sweep - this admin RPC is a sixth, un-swept read of the identical table.

**Other RPC calls checked and ruled out, with the specific reasoning per item** (so a future pass doesn't need to re-derive these): `platform_admin_companies()`/`platform_admin_billing_overview()` - one row per COMPANY, not per event (customer signups grow far slower than daily-scraped listings; at this product's current/near-term scale, nowhere close to 1000). `platform_admin_engine_telemetry()`/`platform_admin_alert_counts_24h()` - a fixed, small set of named queue keys/alert sources (`UNION ALL` of ~5 literal rows, or `GROUP BY` a low-cardinality column), structurally bounded regardless of underlying table size. `platform_admin_cv_document_stats()` - a single aggregate row (scalar counts, no `GROUP BY`), bounded to 1 row by construction. `platform_admin_low_confidence_requirement_items()` - has its own internal `p_limit int default 200` with a real SQL `limit p_limit`, already bounded well under the cap (confirmed the one caller, `app/app/admin/requirement-extractions/page.tsx`, never passes a larger value). `admin_harness_runs` (plain `.select()` on `app/app/admin/page.tsx`, no `.range()`) - initially looked like a sibling of Finding 250's own shape (unpaginated, no limit), but its own migration (`0022`) gives it a real `unique (test_company, tender_ref, kind)` constraint and `engine/write_admin_harness_results.py` confirms it writes via `client.upsert("admin_harness_runs", rows, "test_company,tender_ref,kind")` - bounded by (test companies) x (tender refs) x (kind), a fixed, small combinatorial cap, not append-only growth; a genuine negative, not fixed. `system_alerts`'s two `.select()` reads on the same admin page (open/resolved alerts) - `engine/alerts/system_alerts.py`'s own `record()` function writes through a `record_system_alert()` RPC keyed by `fingerprint()` (source + normalized message), explicitly "a new alert, or one more occurrence of the same open alert" - bounded by distinct open issue types, not occurrence count; the resolved-alerts branch also already carries an explicit `.limit(RESOLVED_SHOWN)`. A genuine negative, not fixed. Every other `.rpc(` call in `app/` was checked against: is it a mutation (not a read of a growing set)? is it scoped by an explicit company/tender/person id argument (bounded the same way `held_registrations`/`company_principals` already are, per the 2026-11-06 sweep's own precedent)? is its own return shape a single row or a small fixed set? Every remaining call site answered yes to at least one.

**Reproduced RED, with the real, unmodified `fetchAllRows()` - the same `serverThatCapsAt()` technique `lib/supabasePaging.spec.ts` already uses, extended to the RPC shape.** A standalone script (deleted after use) built a stub `page(from, to)` function modeling `platform_admin_discovered_opportunities()`'s own real shape at 1300 total rows system-wide (one row per company/release, as the migration's own comment describes), with one real "flagged" opportunity sitting at offset 1150 - past the cap:
```
OLD (single unranged .rpc() call): fetched 1000 of 1300 real rows, found 0 flagged (expected 1, real answer)
NEW (fetchAllRows paginated): fetched 1300 of 1300 real rows, found 1 flagged, error=null
PASS: reproduced the exact silent-truncation bug (RED) and confirmed the fix (GREEN).
```
The OLD path is a direct stand-in for what a single `supabase.rpc(fn)` call with no `.range()` does against a real PostgREST instance applying `db-max-rows`: it returns the server's own first page, capped at 1000, with no error - silently dropping any `flagged`/`not_extracted`/`parsing_failed` opportunity (or, for the catalog page, any tender) sorted past row 1000, understating the page's own summary counts (`{rows.length} opportunities - X flagged, Y look ready` / `{rows.length} tenders - X still open, Y extracted`) without any visible error.

**Fixed** by routing both RPC calls through the existing, unchanged `fetchAllRows()` helper (`lib/supabasePaging.ts`) instead of a single `supabase.rpc(fn)` call - `(from, to) => supabase.rpc(fn).range(from, to)`, same `20_000`-row cap convention Finding 250 and its own predecessors all use. Both pages' own error-handling (`if (error) console.error(...)`, the JSX `{error && (...)}` banner) needed no change beyond destructuring `rows`/`error` from `fetchAllRows()`'s own return shape instead of `data`/`error` from the raw RPC call - `error` goes from a `PostgrestError` object to a plain string, but both call sites only ever use it as a truthiness check, never read a property off it.

### Finding 252 (CONFIRMED AND FIXED ON `main` - moderate, `db-max-rows` class (the same PostgREST-1000-row-cap bug Findings 249-251 and their own five named predecessors were each already fixed for) - never checked before in `engine/`'s own Python code, which this pass confirms talks to Supabase over the identical PostgREST REST API as `app/`, NOT a direct `psycopg`/`asyncpg` Postgres connection, so it is subject to the identical cap) - `engine/general/process_general_jobs.py`'s `Supabase.select()` and `engine/pack/process_pack_jobs.py`'s `SupabaseRest.select()` each built a single, unranged `GET /rest/v1/<table>?...` request with no `limit`/`offset` at all, on tables that include genuinely unbounded, cross-tenant, append-only reads (most concretely `sync_position_suggestions()`'s `client.select("tender_requirements")` - **zero filter whatsoever**, system-wide, every poll cycle)

**Area:** `engine/general/process_general_jobs.py` (`Supabase.select()`, ~line 130-175) and `engine/pack/process_pack_jobs.py` (`SupabaseRest.select()`, ~line 155-205) - both long-running bridge-worker scripts polled continuously by `engine/worker/run_bridges.py`.

**Origin of this finding - the task brief's own suggested fresh angle, checked for real rather than assumed either way.** This pass's brief asked directly: "has the SAME check been done for `engine/`'s own Python code - does it talk to Supabase via PostgREST/REST at all, or does it use a direct Postgres connection via psycopg/asyncpg, which has NO such 1000-row cap?" Grepped every `engine/*.py`/`engine/*/*.py` file for `psycopg`/`asyncpg`/`SUPABASE_URL`/`rest/v1`/`postgrest`: **zero `psycopg`/`asyncpg` imports anywhere in `engine/`'s production code.** Every file that talks to Supabase does it with `urllib.request` against `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL` + `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` - the same REST API base URL and service-role bearer token `app/`'s own Supabase JS client uses, confirmed by reading each file's own request helper: `engine/pack/process_pack_jobs.py`'s `SupabaseRest._req()`, `engine/general/process_general_jobs.py`'s `Supabase._req()`, `engine/discovery/company_profiles.py`'s `RestClient._req()`, `engine/cv/process_cv_jobs.py`'s `supabase_request()` all build a `urllib.request.Request(f"{self.url}/rest/v1/{path}", headers={"apikey": key, "Authorization": f"Bearer {key}"})` - literally PostgREST, not a database driver. The one genuine exception found, `engine/pack/bridge_selftest.py`'s `PsqlClient`, DOES use a direct `psql`/SQL connection (confirmed: its `select()` builds `select coalesce(json_agg(t), '[]') from (select * from {table}...) t`, no REST call at all) - but it is test-only self-test infrastructure for driving `process_job()` against a locally replayed schema, never a production code path (confirmed by grep: nothing in `engine/worker/run_bridges.py` or any `process_*_jobs.py` imports it). **Conclusion, settled with real evidence either way: `engine/`'s production bridges are fully exposed to the same `db-max-rows` cap as `app/`'s own reads - this lead was not a dead end, as the brief itself anticipated it might be.**

**Finding the real vulnerable call sites, not just the theoretical exposure.** One place in `engine/` already gets this right, confirming the fix pattern rather than inventing one: `engine/discovery/company_profiles.py`'s `RestClient.select()` has its own `PAGE = 1000  # Supabase's PostgREST returns at most 1000 rows per request (max_rows)` class constant and a real `limit=&offset=` loop, with its own docstring stating the exact same reasoning this finding relies on ("a seen store read that silently stopped at row 1000 would re-score and re-report everything after it"). `engine/notify/daily_digest.py`, `engine/notify/send_digest_emails.py`, `engine/discovery/watch_tender_updates.py`, `engine/discovery/seed_supabase_opportunities.py`, and `engine/seed_tender_evaluation_rules.py` all import and reuse this same paginated `RestClient` - confirmed safe, not re-checked further.

`engine/general/process_general_jobs.py`'s own `Supabase` class and `engine/pack/process_pack_jobs.py`'s own `SupabaseRest` class are each a SEPARATE, independently-written REST client (same `urllib`-over-service-role shape, never sharing `company_profiles.RestClient`) and neither one paginates at all. Grepped every `.select(` call site in both files (23 in `process_pack_jobs.py`, 11 in `process_general_jobs.py`) and classified each the same way Finding 251 did for `.rpc(` calls - is it scoped by an explicit company/tender/person id (bounded, like `held_registrations` already is)? is its own shape a fixed small set? Most are genuinely bounded (a single id, or a list of ids already bounded by an earlier, smaller read). Two are not, and are the real risk:
1. **`sync_position_suggestions()`'s `reqs = [r for r in client.select("tender_requirements") if not r.get("is_alternate")]`** - no filter at all, system-wide, every poll cycle. `tender_requirements` is an append-only table (one row per primary/ALT position per uploaded Technical workbook, per tender, per company-or-shared-copy) with no retention, read by this exact function to drive every SANRAL tender pack's own candidate-ranking suggestions. A row sorted past position 1000 (PostgREST's own default order with no `order=` given, confirmed: this call passes no `order` argument) would silently never be ranked, with **no error, no alert, no visible symptom beyond "this position just never gets a suggested candidate"** - structurally identical to Finding 250/251's own "silently dropping any flagged/not_extracted/parsing_failed row... without any visible error."
2. **`sync_tender_requirements()`/`sync_b7_setup()`'s shared `client.select("tender_documents", {"doc_type": "technical_xlsm"})`** - filtered by `doc_type` only, still system-wide across every company and every tender, still append-only (every uploaded Technical workbook, ever, across the whole product). A workbook sorted past row 1000 would never have its positions read or its Form B7 category set - the same silent-drop shape, one filter narrower than Finding 251's own two admin RPC reads of `discovered_opportunities`/`tenders`.

Both read through the exact same unpaginated `select()` method, so fixing that one method root-causes both (and every other call site in each file, present and future) at once - the same "fix the shared helper, not each call site" approach `fetchAllRows()` itself represents on the TypeScript side.

**Other `engine/` reads checked and ruled out, with the specific reasoning** (so a future pass doesn't need to re-derive these): `JOBS_TABLE`/`pack_generation_jobs` status=`generating`/`requested` polls (`process_general_jobs.py` lines 803/863, `process_pack_jobs.py` lines 853/1084) - these ARE now paginated as a side effect of this fix (they go through the same `select()`), but even before it they are a bounded, self-correcting job-queue shape (a worker claims and moves a job out of `requested`/`generating` within one poll cycle; the backlog size tracks live throughput, not accumulation) - the same reasoning class Finding 251 already used to rule out `admin_harness_runs`. `engine/cv/process_cv_jobs.py`'s `generated_cvs?status=eq.generating`/`?status=eq.requested` reads (lines 325, 430) and `engine/onboarding/process_onboarding_jobs.py`'s `onboarding_uploads?status=eq.classifying` read (line 98) are the identical bounded-queue shape, through a *different*, unfixed helper (`supabase_request()`, a bare function, not a class) - checked and left alone for the same reason, not because the exposure isn't real (it structurally is, over the same cap), but because a job-queue backlog reaching 1000 simultaneously-in-flight rows is not a realistic growth path at this product's current/near-term scale, unlike an append-only history table with no retention. Flagged here rather than silently assumed safe, in case Sarel's own future scale changes that judgment. Every other `.select(` call site in both fixed files (`tender_private_documents`, `company_principals`, `tender_subcontracting_plans`, `people`, `projects`, `generated_cvs`/`cv_uploads` by person/company, `financial_captures`, `tender_pack_assignments`, `tender_answers`, `tenders`/`tender_packs` by an already-bounded id list) is scoped to one company, one tender, one person, or a list of ids drawn from an already-bounded prior read - ruled out the same way Finding 251 ruled out `held_registrations`/`company_principals`.

**Reproduced RED, with the real, unmodified `SupabaseRest`/`Supabase` classes - not a test double.** The existing test files for both modules (`test_process_pack_jobs.py`, `test_process_general_jobs.py`, `test_sync_functions.py`) all drive a hand-rolled `FakeClient` that duck-types `select()`/`update()` directly in memory and never calls the real class's own `_req()`/HTTP-building code at all - confirmed by reading each `FakeClient.select()`: a plain Python list filter, no REST request ever built, so none of them could have caught this bug regardless of how many rows were in the fake table. A new, separate test in each file instantiates the REAL `SupabaseRest`/`Supabase` class and monkeypatches only `_req()` (same technique the existing `test_supabase_rest_rpc_posts_to_rpc_endpoint_and_parses_the_response()` test already uses for `.rpc()`) with a faithful PostgREST stand-in: 2500 rows in a fake table, server caps any response with no explicit `limit` at 1000 (PostgREST's own real `db-max-rows` behavior), but honours an explicit smaller `limit`/`offset` (the real mechanism pagination past the cap depends on). Ran against the pre-fix code (`git stash` on just the two source files, keeping the new tests):
```
SupabaseRest.select() (process_pack_jobs.py):
  FAIL select() with no filter returns EVERY row in the table, not just PostgREST's own first 1000-row page  (got 1000 of 2500)
  FAIL rows come back in order, nothing dropped or duplicated across pages

Supabase.select() (process_general_jobs.py):
  FAIL select() returns EVERY matching row, not just PostgREST's own first 1000-row page  (got 1000 of 2500)
  FAIL rows come back in order, nothing dropped or duplicated across pages
```

### Finding 254 (CONFIRMED AND FIXED ON `main` - moderate, cross-source/batch-register data-attribution class, same family as Findings 246/247 but a different layer of the stack - 246/247 fixed `store_award_outcomes.py`'s (Python, write-time) coalescing of `winner_amount_zar`/`winner_points`/`winner_bbbee_points` across merged sources; this is `lib/marketPricing.ts`'s (TypeScript, read-time) OWN position-matching logic, never checked by either of those - on a batch/multi-contract register, a company found by NAME ONLY (no price match - the module's own documented common case: a recorded incl.-VAT price against an excl.-VAT register, caveat #2, `Award-Price-Analysis-Findings.md`) silently read a DIFFERENT contract column's field/rank/price than the one the bidder's own real register data was actually in)

**Area:** `app/lib/marketPricing.ts`'s `ownPosition()` (the "name" and "similar_name" branches, ~line 230-245) - the function `/pipeline/pricing`'s `MarketComparison` and the tender workspace's "Market" card both call to place a company on a published SANRAL/eTenders register.

**Origin of this finding.** This pass's own task brief named the deal pipeline (`app/app/pipeline/`) as a fresh angle; `market-comparison.tsx`/`lib/marketPricing.ts` sit directly behind the pricing page's "How your prices compared" card and had never been checked at the TypeScript position-matching layer - Findings 246/247 (2026-11-09, earlier this same day) checked the Python *write* side (`store_award_outcomes.py`'s `merge()`) for the identical cross-source-misattribution bug shape, but explicitly stopped at what gets written to `public_tender_outcomes`, never the TS *read* side that places a company's own price on that register afterward. Read `ownPosition()` line by line against `docs/specs/Award-Price-Analysis-Findings.md`'s own stated design (batch registers are "read in the column whose price matches the recorded one") and `engine/discovery/award_outcomes.py`'s `parse_opening_register()` (confirms the real data shape: one `amounts[]` entry per "Amount..." header column, for EVERY bidder row, with a blank cell kept as a null `amount_zar` rather than a shorter array - so array index really is a consistent per-contract column across every bidder, not an arbitrary per-row offset).

**The gap.** `ownPosition()`'s price-match branch (`found: "name_and_price"`) and its price-only branch (`found: "price"`) both correctly set `column` from `priceHit()` - the array index where the bidder's own amount actually matched the company's recorded price. But the **name-only** branch (`byName.length === 1`, no price match at all) and the **similar-name** branch (`similar.length === 1`) each left `column` at its initial default of `0` - i.e. "contract 1" - regardless of which column, if any, that specific bidder entry was actually priced on. A company priced only on contract 2 or 3 of a batch tender, found by name with no price match (the exact VAT-basis-mismatch scenario the module's own file-header documents as a real, expected case, not a contrived one), would have its register position computed entirely against CONTRACT 1's bidder field - a different contract's low/median/high, a different contract's rank-of-N, and (since `published = entry.amounts[field.column]?.amount_zar` would read `null` at the wrong column) its own self-reported `submittedPrice` compared against that wrong field instead of its own real, published register figure. The structural shape is identical to 246/247's own "one source's value attached to a different source/contract's identity" - just one layer further down the pipe, at render time rather than write time.

**Reproduced RED with the real, unmodified `ownPosition()`.** Built a 2-contract batch register (`register_columns: 2`) matching `award_outcomes.parse_opening_register()`'s real shape: contract 1 has three bidders priced ~R1,000-1,020; contract 2 has four bidders, one of them "You Pty Ltd" at R4,000 - the LOWEST of contract 2's four bids, nowhere near contract 1's price range. "You"'s own recorded `submitted_price_zar` is R4,600 (the documented incl.-VAT-vs-excl.-VAT mismatch: 4000 × 1.15), which doesn't `near()`-match either contract's figures, so no price-match branch fires. Added to `app/lib/marketPricing.spec.ts`'s `ownPosition` describe block and ran against the pre-fix code:
```
AssertionError: expected +0 to be 1 // Object.is equality
 ❯ lib/marketPricing.spec.ts:207:24   expect(pos.column).toBe(1);
```
(`pos.column` read `0` - contract 1 - even though "You"'s own amounts array has a real price at index 1 only.) Full pre-fix result for this input: `found: "name"`, `column: 0`, `price: 4600` (fell back to the self-reported figure since contract 1's field has no entry for "You"), `rank: 4`, `of: 4` - **"4th (last) of 4" against contract 1's R1,000-ish bidders**, a wrong contract AND a wrong-direction verdict for a bid that is genuinely the cheapest on the contract it actually priced.

**Fix.** Added `onlyPricedColumn(b)`: when a bidder's own `amounts[]` has a positive `amount_zar` at exactly one index, that index is the one unambiguous column this entry prices - used as the name/similar-name branches' own default instead of the bare `0`, falling back to `0` only when the bidder's own data is itself ambiguous (priced on zero or multiple columns - the genuinely undecidable case, unchanged from before). The price-match and price-only branches (`name_and_price`, `price`) are untouched - they already had a real signal (`priceHit()`) and never used this default.

**Verified red-then-green, myself, with real output.** `npx vitest run lib/marketPricing.spec.ts` - pre-fix: **1 failed, 20 passed**, the exact assertion above. Post-fix: **21 passed (21)** - the new test now asserts the corrected, real values (`column: 1`, `price: 4000` - the bidder's own published contract-2 figure, overriding the self-reported one, same "the register wins over the self-report" rule every other branch already applies - `rank: 1`, `of: 4`: lowest of contract 2's four real bids, the true picture). Full repo regression: `npx vitest run` - **72 files, 577 tests, all pass** (576 pre-existing + 1 new). `npx tsc --noEmit` - 0 errors. `npx eslint lib/marketPricing.ts lib/marketPricing.spec.ts` - 0 errors/warnings. `npx next build` - compiled successfully, `/pipeline`/`/pipeline/pricing` both present, unchanged rendering mode.

**Backlog collision check.** `gh api repos/SarelJvR2024/tender-tool/pulls/<n>/files --paginate -q '.[].filename'` for each of the 28 open PRs (`#164`/`#165`/`#176`-`#201`): **zero touch `app/lib/marketPricing.ts` or `app/lib/marketPricing.spec.ts`.** No merge simulation needed. Pushed directly to `main`: pure TypeScript, a pure-function fix inside one shared module plus its own test file - no RLS, no money path (this feeds a read-only market-feedback display, not billing), no hard-stop gate, no worker-image change, no schema/migration.

**Scope note, stated honestly.** The "price" and "similar_name"-with-no-own-priced-column cases (an entry priced on zero or more than one column with no price match) still default to column 0, same as before this fix - genuinely ambiguous inputs with no signal this pass found a safe way to resolve, not a gap this fix claims to close. Re-grepped `ownPosition()`'s own callers (`market-comparison.tsx`, and the tender workspace's "Market" card via the same function) - both already treat `found: "name"`/`"similar_name"` as "probably you - check" (`FOUND_LABEL`), never as certain, so this fix improves the figure shown under an existing honesty caveat rather than removing that caveat.

To verify independently: read `app/lib/marketPricing.ts`'s `ownPosition()` and confirm the `byName.length === 1` and `similar.length === 1` branches now set `column = onlyPricedColumn(entry) ?? 0` rather than leaving `column` at its initial `0`. Run `npx vitest run lib/marketPricing.spec.ts` (21/21) and the full `npx vitest run` (72 files/577 tests), plus `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npx eslint lib/marketPricing.ts lib/marketPricing.spec.ts` yourself. ### Finding 256 (CONFIRMED AND FIXED ON `main` - low/moderate, UI content-correctness class - `app/app/analytics/page.tsx`'s own "bid activity & outcomes" tally silently drops a tender stuck on the legacy, pre-`0105` `pipeline_stage` value `'bidding'` out of every stat below it, while "Tenders tracked" still counts it - a sibling shape to the 18+ "missing `briefing_shortlisted`" sites this track already fixed on 2026-11-02, but on the TALLY/counting pattern none of those sweeps checked, not the ACTIVE-list-membership or STAGE_META-indexing patterns they did)

**Area:** `app/app/analytics/page.tsx` - the `byStage` object built at the top of `AnalyticsPage()` and read by the "Tenders tracked"/"Win rate" stat cards and the "N discovered · N being prepared · N awaiting outcome · N won · N lost" summary line directly beneath them.

**Origin of this finding.** This pass's own task brief, after a clean double-check of `lib/marketPricing.ts`'s own column-selection logic (see the double-check note above this Finding, folded into this pass's System-Status.md write-up rather than filed as its own Finding since it was a conclusive negative), named `/analytics` and `/market-intelligence` as a fresh angle "beyond what's already been checked for the gating-by-sample-size class." Reading `analytics/page.tsx` end to end for a fresh angle on its OWN logic (not `lib/marketPricing.ts`'s, already covered by the double-check) surfaced a second, independent call site of `ownPosition()`/`firmsMet()` (section 6, "Pricing trends & who you compete against") - read and confirmed clean, consistent with the already-fixed module. The real finding was one section up: section 1's `byStage` tally.

**The gap.** `app/lib/pipeline.ts`'s own header comment on `LEGACY_BIDDING_STAGE` is explicit and detailed: migration `0105` (`0105_tender_pipeline_stage_v2.sql`) widens `tender_packs.pipeline_stage`'s check constraint from 5 values to 7 (splitting `'bidding'` into `'assessing'`/`'building'`, adding `'briefing_shortlisted'`) AND backfills every existing `'bidding'` row away in the same transaction - but that SQL has to be pasted into Supabase's SQL Editor by hand (no DDL path exists from a Claude Code session), so "there's a real window, of unknown length, where a live row can still be `'bidding'` under the OLD 5-value constraint while this app code... already expects the new 7." The same comment states the resulting rule in capitals for exactly this reason: "Every place that reads a RAW stored `pipeline_stage` value... has to keep treating `'bidding'` as the same 'still actively working on it' bucket `'assessing'`/`'building'` are, or that one row (and its company) would silently vanish from dashboards." `lib/pipeline.ts` exports `normalizeStage(stage)` for exactly this - its own docstring: "Every place that turns a raw DB read into a value it will index `STAGE_META`/`NEXT_STAGES`/`PREVIOUS_STAGE` with MUST go through this first."

`analytics/page.tsx` already handles this correctly in one place and not in the other, in the SAME function: its "Upcoming deadlines" section explicitly includes `"bidding"` in its own `ACTIVE` allow-list (`const ACTIVE: (PipelineStage | "bidding")[] = ["found", "assessing", "building", "bidding", "submitted"]`) - confirmed by the earlier 2026-11-06 sweep (this doc, same pass as Findings 240-243's own write-up chain) that this exact constant was traced to commit `99e431f` and deliberately widened. But the "bid activity & outcomes" tally two sections above it, `const byStage = Object.fromEntries(PIPELINE_STAGES.map((s) => [s, 0])); for (const { pack } of packed) byStage[pack.pipeline_stage] += 1;`, indexes `byStage` with the RAW stored value directly - never through `normalizeStage()`. `byStage` is built only from `PIPELINE_STAGES` (the 7 current values); `'bidding'` has no key in it. `app/app/pipeline/page.tsx` (the pipeline board itself) does the equivalent `byStage[c.stage].push(c)` indexing too, but only ever with `c.stage = normalizeStage(pack?.pipeline_stage ?? "found")` (its own line 284) - confirming this file, not `analytics/page.tsx`, is the one that follows the documented contract. Grepped every `[...pipeline_stage]`-shaped direct index in `app/` (`grep -rn "pipeline_stage\]\s*+=\|\[.*pipeline_stage\]"`): exactly these two sites exist; `lib/tenderActivity.ts`'s own sibling read already guards with `isPipelineStage()` before indexing `STAGE_META`. `analytics/page.tsx`'s `byStage` tally was the one unguarded site in the whole codebase.

**Net effect.** A company with a tender still on the legacy `'bidding'` value (the real, documented, currently-possible shape above) sees "Tenders tracked" (`packed.length`) correctly count it, but the summary line directly beneath it ("N discovered · N being prepared · N awaiting outcome · N won · N lost") silently drops it from every one of its five buckets - it reads as if that tender doesn't exist, while the stat card right above says otherwise on the same page. In JS, `byStage["bidding"] += 1` on an object with no `"bidding"` key reads `undefined`, so `undefined + 1` creates a NEW `byStage.bidding = NaN` property - never thrown, never rendered (nothing on the page reads `byStage.bidding`), so this fails completely silently; `winRate` (`won`/`lost` only) is unaffected, but "being prepared" (`assessing + building`) specifically undercounts by exactly the number of still-`'bidding'` rows.

**Reproduced RED with the real, unmodified code.** A scratch script (`/tmp/.../scratchpad/repro_bystage/repro.mjs`) imports the real `PIPELINE_STAGES`/`normalizeStage` from `app/lib/pipeline.ts` and reproduces `analytics/page.tsx`'s own `byStage` construction byte-for-byte against 3 packs (`found`, the legacy `bidding`, `submitted`):
```
OLD (unguarded raw index): { found: 1, assessing: 0, building: 0, submitted: 1, briefing_shortlisted: 0, won: 0, lost: 0, bidding: NaN }
  Sum of all byStage buckets: NaN
  'being prepared' line (assessing+building): 0
```
(3 real tenders; the breakdown line sums to 0 visible tenders in "being prepared" even though one genuinely is, and the raw `NaN` only exists in an unread property, never surfacing as an error anywhere a person would see it.)

**Fix.** `byStage[pack.pipeline_stage] += 1` → `byStage[normalizeStage(pack.pipeline_stage)] += 1`, importing `normalizeStage` from `@/lib/pipeline` (already imported in the same line as `PIPELINE_STAGES`/`STAGE_META`). One line, same pattern `pipeline/page.tsx` already uses for the identical shape. Nothing else in the file touched.

**Verified red-then-green, myself, with real output.** Same scratch script, `NEW` branch (`byStage[normalizeStage(...)]`):
```
NEW (normalizeStage first): { found: 1, assessing: 1, building: 0, submitted: 1, briefing_shortlisted: 0, won: 0, lost: 0 }
  Sum of all byStage buckets: 3
  'being prepared' line (assessing+building): 1
```
All 3 tenders now accounted for; the legacy `'bidding'` row folds into `'assessing'` (`normalizeStage()`'s own documented, deliberately-conservative default - the live `0105` migration itself differentiates `'assessing'`/`'building'` per row using real signals once it actually runs; this is only the client-side fallback for however long a row hasn't been backfilled). `npx tsc --noEmit` - 0 errors. `npx eslint app/analytics/page.tsx` - 0 errors, 1 pre-existing warning (`'STAGE_META' is defined but never used`, confirmed via `git stash`/`eslint`/`git stash pop` to predate this change, unrelated, not introduced or touched by this fix). Full regression, run on the tree AFTER rebasing onto the sibling's own Finding 255 commit (see the numbering-collision note above): `npx vitest run` - **72 files, 579 tests, all pass** (577 this fix's own baseline + the sibling's own 2 new cases in `scripts/send-onboarding-nudges.spec.ts`, confirming the rebase genuinely kept their work). `npx next build` - `✓ Compiled successfully`, same route table, `/analytics` unchanged rendering mode.

**No other instance of this exact "tally object direct-indexed by a raw transitional value" shape found.** Re-checked (per this pass's own double-check instruction) every other column/row-selection-by-default-index site in `lib/marketPricing.ts`/`lib/dealEconomics.ts`/`pipeline/pricing/page.tsx`/`market-intelligence/page.tsx`/`analytics/page.tsx` itself - all clean (folded into this pass's System-Status.md write-up). Also re-confirmed `app/analytics/page.tsx`'s own `ACTIVE` constant (the "Upcoming deadlines" allow-list, same file, a few lines above `byStage`) is NOT part of this bug - it already explicitly includes `"bidding"`, correctly, as the 2026-11-06 sweep found.

**Backlog collision check.** `gh api repos/SarelJvR2024/tender-tool/pulls/<n>/files --paginate -q '.[].filename'` for each of the 28 open PRs: **PR #164 touches `app/app/analytics/page.tsx`** (one near-miss, documented here rather than silently pushed past). ### Finding 257 (CONFIRMED AND FIXED ON `main` - low/moderate, UI content-correctness class, a sibling shape to Findings 240-243/249/256 ("two surfaces/two facts on the same page can't quietly disagree") but at the level of one hardcoded sentence contradicting the structured data shown two lines above it on the very same card) - `app/app/tenders/[id]/tender-updates.tsx`'s closing-date disagreement card always said "Not applied automatically, because the buyer's own listing doesn't show this date" whenever `closingNeedsDecision()` was true - including the real case where the listing DOES show this exact date (`listing_agrees: true`), which the card's own very next row ("The buyer's eTenders listing shows") would display identically, directly contradicting the sentence above it

**Area:** `app/lib/tenderUpdates.ts` (new `closingDisagreementReason(c)`), `app/app/tenders/[id]/tender-updates.tsx` (its one call site, the `<DateDisagreement>` card's `note` prop). Test coverage added in the new `app/lib/tenderUpdates.spec.ts` (3 cases - no spec file existed for this lib before this pass).

**How this was found.** This pass's own task brief named `app/components/tt/`'s shared UI component library as a fresh angle (never swept as its own unit). Read all 21 files there in full (`bid-readiness-card.tsx`, `bid-task-badge.tsx`, `command-center.tsx`, `data-table.tsx`, `deadline-chip.tsx`, `demo-banner.tsx`, `dispatch-status-button.tsx`, `empty-state.tsx`, `error-state.tsx`, `next-best-action-card.tsx`, `page-header.tsx`, `progress-ring.tsx`, `requirement-row.tsx`, `savings-calculator.tsx`, `savings-counter-card.tsx`, `section-card.tsx`, `setup-checklist-card.tsx`, `skeletons.tsx`, `stat-card.tsx`, `status-badge.tsx`, `stepper.tsx`, `subscription-banner.tsx`) plus the small logic files directly behind the ones with real computation (`lib/savingsEstimateCalculator.ts`, `lib/dispatchTriage.ts`/`lib/dispatchDashboard.ts`/`lib/tenderNextStep.ts` behind `command-center.tsx`, `lib/billing.ts`'s `isSubscriptionLapsed()`/`trialDaysLeft()` behind `subscription-banner.tsx`) - a genuine, conclusive negative: every one is either pure presentation delegating its facts/math to an already-reviewed shared helper, or (`dispatch-status-button.tsx`'s `advanceDispatchStatus` call, `setup-checklist-card.tsx`'s `allDone` edge case) confirmed safe by reading the one real caller. None filed as a Finding.

Broadened to a fresh mention-count ranking across `app/lib/*.ts` and `app/app/**/*.tsx` (excluding `*.spec.ts`/`*.test.ts`, excluding files under 40 lines) - per this pass's own task brief's suggestion of "a fresh mention-count-ranking pass on a directory not yet covered that way." `app/lib/tenderUpdates.ts` (145 lines, 2 prior mentions in both standing docs combined) surfaced as a genuinely low-coverage, substantial logic file: a `tenders/[id]`-workspace *lib* file, distinct from the `tenders/[id]` directory's own files (already exhaustively swept per this track's own standing-items list), and never itself read end to end before. Read it in full against its real engine-side counterpart, `engine/discovery/tender_updates.py`'s `classify_document()` (the function that actually produces every `ClosingDateChange` object this lib's functions consume) and `engine/discovery/watch_tender_updates.py`'s own auto-apply branch, checking specifically for the "two independently-computed renderings of the same underlying facts can disagree" bug class this track has found repeatedly elsewhere (Findings 240-243, 249, 256).

**The gap, traced, not guessed.** `closingNeedsDecision(c)` (`lib/tenderUpdates.ts`) is `!!c && !c.applied && c.direction !== "same"` - true whenever a closing-date change wasn't auto-applied and isn't a no-op. `watch_tender_updates.py`'s own auto-apply branch (`check_tender()`, ~line 431) only fires `if cd["listing_agrees"] and cd["direction"] in ("later", "earlier") and listing_closing` - i.e. `cd["applied"]` can legitimately stay `False` for TWO structurally different reasons: (a) the listing genuinely disagrees with the document (`listing_agrees: False`), or (b) `direction` is `"unknown"` (no closing date was on file at all to compare a direction against - `classify_document()`'s own line 264: `direction = "unknown" if not base else ...`), which is never auto-applied regardless of `listing_agrees`. Case (b) can genuinely have `listing_agrees: True` - the buyer's own listing agrees with the document's stated date, there was simply nothing on file yet to call it "later" or "earlier" than.

`tender-updates.tsx`'s own `<DateDisagreement>` card (rendered whenever `closingNeedsDecision()` is true, line ~139-152) used ONE hardcoded reason for every case: `` `${closing.text} Not applied automatically, because the buyer's own listing doesn't show this date. Check the document (and with the buyer if in doubt) before accepting it...` ``. In case (b) with `listing_agrees: true`, that sentence is simply false - and the card's own very next structured row, two lines above it in the same `rows` array (`{ label: "...listing shows", value: formatDay(changes.closing_date.listing_date) }`), would display the identical date, directly contradicting the sentence underneath it on the same card.

**Confirmed reachable, not hypothetical.** Case (b) requires a tender with a real OCID/SANRAL slug (so `watch_tender_updates.py` watches it at all) but `closing_date` null in `tenders` (so `classify_document()`'s own `base`/`direction` computation has nothing to compare against). Confirmed this combination is directly reachable through the product's own manual-tender-load form: `app/app/tenders/new/actions.ts`'s `registerManualTender()` accepts `input.ocid` and lets `input.closingDate`/`input.closingTime` both stay empty (`closing = null` when `!input.closingDate`) - there is no validation requiring a closing date whenever an OCID is also given.

**Reproduced RED with the real, unmodified `classify_document()` - not a constructed stand-in.** Ran the function against the real `ec_transport_scmu10_addendum1` fixture (the same fixture `test_tender_updates.py`'s own `part1()` already uses for its `listing_agrees` assertion) with `closing_on_file=None` (nothing on file) and a `listing_closing` matching the document's own stated date:
```python
import tender_updates as tu
from test_tender_updates import fixture
text = fixture("ec_transport_scmu10_addendum1")
r = tu.classify_document("SCHOLAR TRANSPORT ADDENDUM NO. 1.pdf", text, "text", None, "2026-11-06T11:00:00Z")
r["changes"]["closing_date"]
```
Real output:
```json
{"date": "2026-11-06", "time": "11:00", "quote": "CLOSING DATE IS EXTENDED TO FRIDAY 06 NOVEMBER 2026 AT 11:00 AM",
 "previous_on_file": null, "previous_in_document": null, "direction": "unknown",
 "listing_date": "2026-11-06", "listing_agrees": true, "applied": false}
```
Fed this real object through the real, unmodified pre-fix `closingNeedsDecision()`/`closingDateLine()` (via a scratch `tsx` script importing the real `lib/tenderUpdates.ts`): `closingNeedsDecision` → `true`; the card's hardcoded note resolves to `"Closing date stated as Fri, 06 Nov 2026 11:00. Not applied automatically, because the buyer's own listing doesn't show this date. ..."` - while `changes.closing_date.listing_date` (`"2026-11-06"`, the row rendered directly above it) is the SAME date the document states. **RED, confirmed real**: the card's own two pieces of text/data would contradict each other.

**Fix.** Added `closingDisagreementReason(c: ClosingDateChange): string` to `lib/tenderUpdates.ts`: returns the "no date on file yet to compare against - the listing already shows this same date" wording when `c.listing_agrees` is true, and the original "the buyer's own listing doesn't show this date" wording otherwise (the genuine-disagreement case, and the no-listing-data-at-all case, both still correctly described by the original sentence). `tender-updates.tsx`'s one call site now builds the note from this function instead of the single hardcoded string. Nothing else in the component touched; `appliedLine()` (used in the OTHER rendering branch, when `closingNeedsDecision()` is false) was not touched - it already branches on `listing_agrees` correctly and was not implicated.

**Verified red-then-green, myself, with real output.** `git stash push -- app/lib/tenderUpdates.ts app/app/tenders/[id]/tender-updates.tsx` (keeping the new spec file): `npx vitest run lib/tenderUpdates.spec.ts` - **3 failed** (`closingDisagreementReason is not a function`), confirming the new tests are not vacuous. `git stash pop`, same command - **3 passed (3)**. Full regression: `npx vitest run` - **73 files, 582 tests, all pass** (72 files/579 tests before this pass's own new spec file, +1 file/+3 tests). `npx tsc --noEmit` - 0 errors. `npx eslint "lib/tenderUpdates.ts" "lib/tenderUpdates.spec.ts" "app/tenders/[id]/tender-updates.tsx"` - 0 errors/warnings. `npx next build` - compiled successfully, `/tenders/[id]` present, unchanged rendering mode.
