**A fourth candidate, checked and conclusively ruled out: `app/app/api/billing/checkout/route.ts`'s `const origin = request.nextUrl.origin` (used to build PayFast's own `return_url`/`cancel_url`/`notify_url`).** This looked, on first read, like exactly the same Host-header-trust shape as Findings 268/269, just via `NextRequest.nextUrl.origin` instead of a direct `headers().get("host")` call - a shape the task brief's own "exhaustively swept" claim (grepping literal `.headers.get(` / `.get("host")` calls) would NOT have caught, since `.nextUrl.origin` is a derived `NextRequest` property, not a `.get()` call at all. Tested directly, live, against a real running dev server (`npx next dev -p 3100`, a temporary scratch route `app/app/api/scratchhosttest/route.ts` returning both `request.nextUrl.origin` and `request.headers.get("host")` side by side, removed before any commit): `curl -H "Host: evil.attacker.example" http://localhost:3100/api/scratchhosttest` -> `{"origin":"http://localhost:3100","host":"evil.attacker.example"}` - the raw header IS spoofed as expected, but `nextUrl.origin` is NOT: it stayed `http://localhost:3100`, the server's own real bound address, regardless of `Host` or even `X-Forwarded-Host` (`curl -H "X-Forwarded-Host: evil3.attacker.example" ...` -> `origin` still `http://localhost:3100`). `NextRequest.nextUrl` is built by Next.js itself from the real underlying request, not from a client-supplied header - a genuinely different, safe mechanism, not the same bug in a different spelling. **Conclusive negative, not a finding** - `checkout/route.ts` is clean on this specific question (note: this was only tested against `npx next dev`, not Vercel's own production edge - if a future pass has a reason to doubt Vercel preserves this same real-bind-address behaviour for `nextUrl.origin` specifically, as opposed to the already-confirmed-spoofable raw `Host` header `siteUrl.ts` itself reads, that would be a new, narrower angle, not a re-run of this exact test).

**The real gap, found while re-reading `siteUrl.ts`'s own fix from Finding 268 end to end rather than trusting its own "fixed" label.** `isKnownGoodHost()` strips a port with `host.split(":")[0]` before checking the hostname against the allowlist - correct in isolation - but `siteUrl()` itself then builds the returned URL from the ORIGINAL, un-stripped `host` string (`` `${proto}://${host}` ``), never from the validated hostname alone. A Host header shaped like `"tenderready.app:@evil.attacker.example"` passes `isKnownGoodHost()` (its pre-colon part, `"tenderready.app"`, is the real domain) and is then substituted verbatim into `"https://tenderready.app:@evil.attacker.example"`. That string is NOT "the real domain on a weird port" to any real URL parser: confirmed directly with Node's own WHATWG-compliant `URL` - `new URL("https://tenderready.app:@evil.attacker.example").host` is `"evil.attacker.example"`, because the parser reads `"tenderready.app:"` (text before a trailing `"@"`) as userinfo and discards it, and `"evil.attacker.example"` as the real host - the exact same "passes a naive same-origin-looking string check, resolves to a different origin under every real URL parser" shape Finding 267 already fixed once in `safeRedirect.ts` (there, tab/CR/LF characters a browser strips before parsing; here, a fake "port" a browser's authority-parsing step reinterprets as userinfo), just never checked for in this specific file. **This is a live bypass of the Finding 268 fix itself, found one pass later, in the one file that fix exists to protect** - and since Finding 269 routed `team/page.tsx` to call this same function instead of its own inline duplicate, the bypass reaches BOTH of `siteUrl()`'s real callers: the onboarding welcome-email link and the company-invite link, which (per Finding 269's own tracing) carries a real, usable `company_invites.token` that grants real company membership via `redeem_company_invite()`.

**Confirmed live, with the real, unmodified function, not just reasoned about.** Same scratch-route methodology as Findings 268/269 (`app/app/api/scratchsiteurltest/route.ts`, importing and calling the real `siteUrl()`, removed before any commit): `curl -H "Host: tenderready.app" http://localhost:3100/api/scratchsiteurltest` -> `{"url":"https://tenderready.app"}` (correct baseline); `curl -H "Host: tenderready.app:@evil.attacker.example" http://localhost:3100/api/scratchsiteurltest` -> `{"url":"https://tenderready.app:@evil.attacker.example"}` - the exact exploitable pre-fix string, returned by the real function against a real running server.

**Severity, stated honestly, same precondition as Findings 267-269, not escalated further.** Whether an external attacker can get an arbitrary `Host` value (with or without this embedded-userinfo shape) to actually reach this Next.js deployment in production still depends on Vercel's own edge-routing behaviour, which remains unconfirmed from this sandbox - the identical open caveat Findings 268/269 already logged, not a newly-confirmed production exploit path, so this does NOT meet the task brief's own bar for escalating to the severe/PR class ("a confirmed, reachable production exploit path rather than an honestly-flagged-as-unconfirmed precondition"). What IS conclusively confirmed is that the function's own allowlist, AS WRITTEN post-Finding-268, does not actually constrain what ends up in the returned URL to the validated hostname - a real logic bug in the fix itself, not a theoretical restatement of Finding 268's own already-logged caveat.

**Fix.** Replaced `isKnownGoodHost(host): boolean` with `knownGoodHostAndPort(host): string | null`, which now OWNS deciding what, if anything, follows the hostname in the returned URL - a real, all-digit port (`/^\d+$/`) if one was present, or nothing - and returns `null` (triggering the same `VERCEL_URL`/localhost fallback Finding 268 already established) for anything else, including more than one `":"` in the header at all. `siteUrl()` now builds its returned URL from this function's own return value exclusively, never from the raw `host` string again - there is no longer a second, unvalidated use of the header anywhere in the file. A real custom port (e.g. `"tenderready.app:8443"`) is still correctly trusted, confirmed by a dedicated new test, so the fix narrows nothing legitimate.

**Verified red-then-green against the real, unmodified function, twice over (mocked unit test AND a real live request), exactly Finding 268/269's own established methodology.** New cases in `lib/siteUrl.spec.ts`: rejects the userinfo-smuggling Host on the production domain, rejects the identical shape on a `*.vercel.app` host (confirming the bypass isn't specific to one allowlist branch), and still trusts a real numeric port. **Red:** ran the 2 new rejection cases against the pre-fix code (the version committed as Finding 268/269) - both failed exactly as predicted (`expected '...evil.attacker.example' not to contain 'evil.attacker.example'`). **Green:** post-fix, `npx vitest run lib/siteUrl.spec.ts` - **13/13 pass**. Live, real-server round trip (see above) confirmed the same red (pre-fix code, scratch route) then green (post-fix code, same scratch route, same request) - `curl -H "Host: tenderready.app:@evil.attacker.example" ...` moved from returning the exploitable string verbatim to `{"url":"http://localhost:3000"}` (the function's own existing no-`VERCEL_URL` fallback), while `curl -H "Host: tenderready.app:8443" ...` -> `{"url":"https://tenderready.app:8443"}`, confirming the fix doesn't regress the legitimate-port case either. Both scratch routes (`scratchhosttest`, `scratchsiteurltest`) deleted and the dev server stopped (`pkill -f "next dev -p 3100"`, confirmed via `ps aux` afterward showing no match) before any commit; `.next` cache cleared and `next typegen` re-run so the scratch routes left no stale type references behind (confirmed: `npx tsc --noEmit` was transiently dirty with references to the just-deleted scratch routes until `.next` was cleared and types regenerated - a build-artifact staleness issue, not a real source error). Full regression, all green: `npm run typecheck` (`next typegen && tsc --noEmit`, 0 errors), `npx eslint .` (0 errors, same 3 pre-existing unrelated warnings, unchanged), `npx vitest run` - **75 files, 606 tests, all pass** (up from 603 after Finding 269, exactly the 3 new cases), the node `*.test.ts` loop (30/30, plain `node <file>`, no flags, unchanged), `npx next build` (exit 0, clean, full route table unchanged, both scratch routes confirmed absent from it). ### Finding 271 (CONFIRMED AND FIXED ON `main` - minor, a third real bug in `app/lib/siteUrl.ts`, found on a deliberately skeptical third adversarial re-read of the SAME file two prior findings (268, 270) already claimed "fixed" - `siteUrl()`'s own `isLocal` check used `goodHostAndPort.startsWith("localhost")`, a substring match, so any already-allowlisted real `*.vercel.app` host whose name merely STARTS WITH the literal text "localhost" (a legal Vercel project/preview name) got downgraded to `http://` instead of `https://`)

**Area:** `app/lib/siteUrl.ts` (`knownGoodHostAndPort()`/`siteUrl()` - rewritten this pass, not just re-patched; see "Why a rewrite, not a third narrow patch" below). `app/lib/siteUrl.spec.ts` extended with 4 new cases (17 total, up from 13 added by Finding 270).

**How this was found.** This pass's own task brief, given `siteUrl.ts`'s own 2-bugs-in-3-passes track record, asked for one more genuinely adversarial read of the CURRENT, post-Finding-270 code, not an assumption it was finally safe - specifically naming IPv6 literal hosts, Unicode/punycode homograph tricks, a header with multiple comma-separated values, case-sensitivity tricks and trailing dots as candidate edge cases, each to be tested live, not just reasoned about. Built a temporary scratch route (`app/app/api/scratchsiteurltest2/route.ts`, importing and calling the real `siteUrl()`, removed before any commit) against a real `npx next dev -p 3123` and ran every one of those candidates as a real HTTP request:
- IPv6 literal (`Host: [::1]:3123`) -> falls back (`http://localhost:3000`) - fails closed, not exploitable (`knownGoodHostAndPort`'s own colon-counting at the time rejected anything with more than one `:`, and an IPv6 literal has several).
- Trailing dot (`Host: tenderready.app.`) -> falls back - fails closed (the allowlist regexes are exactly-anchored, `$` doesn't match before a trailing extra character).
- Uppercase real domain and uppercase `*.vercel.app` suffix (`Host: TENDERREADY.APP`, `Host: evil.VERCEL.APP`) -> both fall back - fails closed (case-sensitive regex; this can only ever reject a differently-cased REAL host, never accept a different, attacker-chosen one, so not itself a security bug, just a minor false-negative).
- Duplicate `Host` headers, both orders, sent over a raw socket (curl cannot send two `Host:` lines reliably) - confirmed directly with Python, both `Host: tenderready.app\r\nHost: evil.attacker.example\r\n` and the reverse order: Node's own documented header-merging table discards duplicates of `host` (and several other headers) rather than comma-joining them, keeping only the FIRST occurrence on the wire - `rawHost` in the response showed exactly one value each time (whichever came first), never a comma-joined string. Whichever single value survives still goes through the existing (correct) allowlist check, so this is a genuine, live-confirmed conclusive negative for the specific "comma-joined duplicate Host header" shape the task brief named, not merely untested.
- A single Host header VALUE containing a literal comma (`Host: tenderready.app, evil.attacker.example`, simulating a misbehaving upstream proxy that joins headers into one value rather than sending duplicates) -> falls back - fails closed (the comma'd string doesn't match any allowlist regex in its entirety).
- Real UTF-8 Cyrillic homoglyph (`tenderre`+U+0430+`dy.app`, sent as actual UTF-8 bytes over a raw socket, not a mangled ASCII approximation) -> falls back - fails closed (the allowlist regex requires an exact, literal ASCII match; a homoglyph's different underlying code points can only ever cause a REJECTION relative to the real domain, never an acceptance of a different one, so - as with case-sensitivity - this shape structurally cannot produce a false positive).
- `X-Forwarded-Host: evil.attacker.example` alongside a legitimate `Host: tenderready.app` -> correctly ignored entirely; `siteUrl()` never reads this header at all.
- A CRLF-injection attempt via curl's own `$'...'` escaping -> no actual injection occurred; the header arrived unmangled and the function behaved exactly as the clean-`Host` case.

**A second, genuinely new edge case found while probing the allowlist's own regex shapes, not on the task brief's list - confirmed real but NOT independently exploitable.** `KNOWN_GOOD_HOSTS`'s third entry, `/\.vercel\.app$/`, has no `^` start anchor (intentional - it needs to match any `*.vercel.app` subdomain, not one fixed string), so a hostname with NO colon in it can carry an arbitrary attacker-chosen prefix before `@` and still pass, e.g. `Host: evil.attacker.example@fake.vercel.app` - confirmed live, pre-rewrite: `{"url":"https://evil.attacker.example@fake.vercel.app"}`, a real, confusing-looking string embedding "evil.attacker.example" verbatim. Checked carefully whether this is actually exploitable to a different destination, not just assumed safe: `new URL("https://evil.attacker.example@fake.vercel.app").host` is `"fake.vercel.app"` - confirmed that this holds for ANY such string by construction, not just this one example, because "ends with `.vercel.app`" is preserved under "take the substring after the last `@`" (whatever a real URL parser treats as the actual host is itself a suffix of a string that was already required to end in `.vercel.app`, so it too ends in `.vercel.app`). This means the embedded-`@`-prefix trick can never point the REAL resolved host outside the already-documented, deliberately broad "every legitimate `*.vercel.app` deployment" trust boundary this file's own header comment already accepts by design (the same boundary that already lets anyone who owns ANY `*.vercel.app` project get trusted, with or without this trick) - not a new bypass of that boundary, just a cosmetically misleading string within it. Also checked both of `siteUrl()`'s real callers for a downstream HTML/attribute-injection risk from that embedded `@`/arbitrary-prefix text: `lib/emailBrand.ts`'s `button()` (used by the onboarding welcome email) calls `escapeHtml(href)` before placing it in the `href="..."` attribute, and `app/app/company/team/page.tsx`'s invite link is a React-controlled `<input value={link} />`, not raw HTML - both already safe regardless of what characters reach `siteUrl()`'s return value, confirmed by reading each site, not assumed. **Conclusion: real, but not a security bypass - tightened anyway as a side effect of this pass's own rewrite (see below), not logged as its own Finding.**

**The real, independently exploitable-of-its-own-kind bug: `isLocal`'s substring check.** `siteUrl()` computed `const isLocal = goodHostAndPort.startsWith("localhost") || goodHostAndPort.startsWith("127.0.0.1")` to decide `http://` vs `https://` - a SUBSTRING check against the whole (possibly-ported) string, not an exact match against the validated hostname. Any real, already-allowlisted `*.vercel.app` host whose name merely starts with the literal text "localhost" - a perfectly legal Vercel project/preview name, nothing stops anyone registering one - also tripped this check. Confirmed live against the real, unmodified function (pre-fix): `curl -H "Host: localhost.vercel.app" http://localhost:3124/api/scratchsiteurltest3` -> `{"url":"http://localhost.vercel.app"}`; `curl -H "Host: localhost-evil-preview.vercel.app" ...` -> `{"url":"http://localhost-evil-preview.vercel.app"}` - both downgraded to `http://` despite passing the allowlist on their own merits (sanity check, same server: `Host: tender-ready-git-fix-xyz.vercel.app` -> correctly `https://...`).

**Severity, stated honestly, and why this is "minor" rather than the same tier as Findings 267-270.** This bug does NOT expand the trust boundary at all - the host still has to pass the existing allowlist exactly as before, so an attacker gains no new DESTINATION they couldn't already reach (unlike 267/268/269/270, where the whole point was a different, attacker-chosen host slipping past the check). The only consequence is a scheme label: an already-trusted link would read `http://` instead of `https://`. Real-world impact is further narrowed by Vercel's own practice of enforcing HTTPS/redirecting plain HTTP on `*.vercel.app` domains, and by the same unconfirmed-Host-spoofing-reaches-production precondition every finding in this file 267-270 already carries, not re-litigated further here. Logged and fixed anyway, consistent with this track's own precedent of fixing low-blast-radius bugs in this exact class (Findings 268-270 all carried the identical unconfirmed-reachability caveat and were still fixed, not waved off).

**Why a rewrite, not a third narrow patch.** This is the THIRD distinct bug in `knownGoodHostAndPort()`/`siteUrl()` across three consecutive passes (268: no validation at all; 270: validated the wrong substring then used the raw string anyway; 271, this pass: validated correctly but then re-derived `isLocal` with a second, independent, imprecise string check). ### Finding 272 (CONFIRMED AND FIXED ON `main` - moderate, functional-correctness class, breaks a named Sarel feature request for virtually any realistic use - `bulkUploadCvs()` (`app/app/people/actions.ts`) sent every file in a bulk-CV-upload batch through ONE Server Action request, and Vercel's real per-function request-body ceiling applies to that WHOLE request, not per file, so any batch of normal-sized CVs together exceeding ~4.4 MB failed outright with a 413, with nothing uploaded and no clear error shown)

**Area:** `app/app/people/actions.ts` (`bulkUploadCvs()` - no longer redirects itself, returns `{created, attached, errors}` instead), `app/app/people/_components/bulk-cv-upload.tsx` (now chunks the batch and navigates itself), new `app/app/people/_components/bulkCvChunking.ts` (extracted pure logic) + `bulkCvChunking.test.ts` (7 new cases).

**How this was found.** This pass's own starting point, per the standing brief: a from-scratch, unit-level read of `app/app/people/`'s substantive business logic (the brief's own named candidate, alongside `document-scan/`/`my-cv/`). Read `people/actions.ts` end to end first - extremely heavily audited already by prior passes (Findings 217/218, the 2026-11-06/2026-11-07/2026-11-08 standing reviews), and a promising-looking `signatory_scopes` cross-tenant gap turned out to already be logged and fixed on its own open PR (#199, Finding 236) - a real finding, just not a NEW one. Rather than re-litigate already-exhausted ground in that one file, widened to its own specifically-named, low-mention-count siblings (this track's own established fallback when a file's generic name defeats a naive mention-count ranking): `app/app/people/_components/bulk-cv-upload.tsx` (3 mentions, both peripheral) and its own server action `bulkUploadCvs()`. Read both fresh, end to end, against the real data shapes they build - not a skim.

**The real mechanism, traced before being tested.** `next.config.ts`'s own `experimental.serverActions.bodySizeLimit` is set to `"4.5mb"`, with its own header comment stating plainly why: "Vercel Functions reject any request body over 4.5 MB with 413 FUNCTION_PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE... before Next.js ever sees it" - and that this is why every OTHER multi-file upload surface in this app (`upload-form.tsx`/`VaultDocumentUploader.tsx`/`quick-blocker-drawer.tsx`/`manual-tender-form.tsx`, all via the shared `uploadBatch.ts`) uploads straight from the browser to Supabase Storage instead of through a Server Action body - `uploadBatch.ts`'s own header comment states the identical reasoning verbatim ("a Server Action body is capped at 4.5 MB; a batch of certificates together would blow past that"). `bulkUploadCvs()`'s own header comment claimed it "reuses the shared FileDropzone/uploadBatch pattern spec v3 Batch 2 established for company documents" - but reading `bulk-cv-upload.tsx`'s actual imports shows it only ever imports `FileDropzone`/`validateFiles`, never `uploadBatch`. Its `submit()` instead builds ONE `FormData` holding every selected file's real bytes (no count cap - unlike `cv-led-add-person.tsx`'s own single-file `maxFiles: 1`, this component's own `validateFiles()` call has no `maxFiles` at all) and sends it all through a single `await bulkUploadCvs(fd)` call. `FileDropzone`'s own `validateFiles()` checks each file individually against `MAX_CV_BYTES` (4.4 MB) but has and needs no cumulative/total-bytes check of its own - so two files each comfortably under that per-file cap can still, together, blow straight past the real 4.5 MB Vercel ceiling in the one request that carries them both.

**Confirmed live, real repro, not reasoned about.** `npx next build` (clean) then a disposable scratch Server Action (`app/scratchbulktest/`, a bare `<form action={...}>` echoing `formData` file sizes - same shape as `bulkUploadCvs()`'s own FormData contract, deleted before this commit, never committed) against a real `npx next dev -p 3912`. Fetched the rendered page's own `$ACTION_ID_...` hidden field (progressive-enhancement encoding) and drove it directly with `curl -F`, exactly the same multipart body a real browser's own fetch would send for this action:
- **Control, single ~3 MB file** (well under both the 4.4 MB per-file cap and the 4.5 MB request cap): `200 OK`.
- **Two ~3 MB files in ONE request** (6 MB total - each individually well under the 4.4 MB per-file client-side check `bulk-cv-upload.tsx` already applies): `500 Internal Server Error`; the real dev-server log shows the actual cause plainly - `⨯ Error: Body exceeded 4.5mb limit. ... statusCode: 413` - fired before the action's own code ever runs, so no amount of per-file validation inside `bulkUploadCvs()` could ever catch or report this cleanly; the client component has no `try/catch` around its own `await bulkUploadCvs(fd)` either, so this throws as an uncaught error in the React transition.
- **A second scratch route, 3 files totalling exactly 4.5 MB**: `200 OK` (confirms the real cutoff sits a little above the nominal "4.5mb" figure - consistent with `bodySizeLimit` parsing "mb" as MiB, giving the ~4.4 MB-ish margin `next.config.ts`'s own comment already describes for a SINGLE file: "the largest file that actually fits is ~4.4 MB"); **2 files totalling 3 MB**: `200 OK` - confirms multiple small files summing within that same safe margin work fine in one request, isolating TOTAL BYTES, not file COUNT, as the real constraint, and confirming a chunking fix bounded by that same already-proven-safe per-file ceiling is sound for multi-file chunks too, not just singletons.

**Impact, honestly scoped.** Not a security bug, not a data-integrity bug - every file either uploads correctly or the whole batch visibly fails; nothing is silently lost or corrupted, and a user can always fall back to uploading one CV at a time via the existing, unaffected `/people/[id]` single-upload flow. But it is a real, 100%-of-the-time (not a race, not an edge case) functional break of a feature Sarel explicitly asked for by name ("allow bulk upload of all People CVs... or bulk upload of people with their details") for almost any realistic multi-file batch - real scanned CVs routinely run well into the low megabytes each, so 2+ of them together will very often cross this line, and the failure mode (a generic 500/uncaught error, no per-file information) gives the user no clue why or what to do differently.

**Fix.** Kept `bulkUploadCvs()`'s own internal per-row logic (create-or-reuse person, attach CV, partial-failure-safe error accumulation) byte-for-byte unchanged - only its ending changed: it no longer calls `redirect()` itself, since it may now be invoked several times for one real user submission; it returns `{created, attached, errors}` instead. `bulk-cv-upload.tsx` now splits the real batch into size-bounded chunks via a new, extracted, pure `chunkRowsBySize()` (greedy bin-pack: add rows to the current chunk while the running total stays `<= MAX_CV_BYTES`, the same 4.4 MB constant this screen's own client-side per-file check already uses and this pass's own live repro already confirmed safe), calls `bulkUploadCvs()` once per chunk SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel - keeps the running tally simple and avoids firing several multi-megabyte requests at once on a slow connection), accumulates `created`/`attached`/`errors` across every chunk (a chunk-level `catch` counts every file in that chunk as failed rather than losing track of it, matching `bulkUploadCvs()`'s own established "one failure must never discard a sibling" convention), then builds the exact same summary string the server used to build and navigates once with `router.push('/people?bulk=...')`. Considered, and deliberately did NOT build, the "real" fix every other multi-file surface already uses (browser-direct-to-Storage via `uploadBatch()`): a NEW person's `id` doesn't exist until `bulkUploadCvs()` creates it, and both the real storage-path convention and `cv_uploads.person_id not null` need that id first (`createPersonWithCv()`'s own header comment explains this exact constraint for the single-file case) - so that fix would need a staging-path-plus-server-side-`move()` design, a larger architectural change than this pass's own severity bar for a direct push; flagged below for Sarel's own judgment, not forced.

**New pure module, tested directly.** `chunkRowsBySize()`/`rowsToFormData()` moved out of `bulk-cv-upload.tsx` into `app/app/people/_components/bulkCvChunking.ts` - a `.tsx` file with real JSX can't be run directly by `node --experimental-strip-types` (the exact reason `uploadBatch.ts` was originally extracted from its own former home inside `document-scan/upload-form.tsx`), so the chunking logic needed its own JSX-free file to be testable the same way. `bulkCvChunking.test.ts` (7 cases, same plain-`node:test` convention as `uploadBatch.test.ts`): several small files under the limit pack into one chunk; the EXACT confirmed-live two-3MB-files shape splits into two chunks; a single file right at the cap gets its own chunk, never dropped; a mixed batch packs greedily (small files fill a chunk until the next file would overflow it, not a fixed count); every row from the input appears exactly once across all output chunks (none dropped or duplicated), and no chunk's own total exceeds the cap; an empty batch produces no chunks; `rowsToFormData()` builds the exact `kind_<i>`/`file_<i>`/`person_id_<i>`/`name_<i>` shape `bulkUploadCvs()` expects, for both an existing-person row and a new-person row (name trimmed).

**Verified red-then-green against the real mechanism, live, before writing the fix - not a mock.** The "red" here is the live 413 repro above (runs identically against the real, unmodified pre-fix code, since the bug is in HOW the component calls the action, not in the action itself). Post-fix: `node --experimental-strip-types --test app/app/people/_components/bulkCvChunking.test.ts` - **7/7 pass**. Did not re-run the live scratch-route repro against the fixed component itself (that would need a real authenticated session - this app's auth middleware redirects an unauthenticated POST to `/login` before any action code runs, confirmed by a first attempt at an authenticated repro); instead verified the fix's own correctness by construction plus the already-confirmed mechanism: every chunk the new logic produces is, by `chunkRowsBySize()`'s own tested invariant, `<= MAX_CV_BYTES` (4.4 MB) - structurally the same size profile as the scratch repro's own already-confirmed-safe single-3MB-file and 3-file/4.5MB-total/3-file/3MB-total cases, never the confirmed-failing two-3MB-files-in-one-request shape. Honest limitation, logged rather than hidden: this is a construction-level verification against a live-confirmed mechanism, not a second live end-to-end run of the fixed component against a real authenticated session.

**Full regression.** `npx tsc --noEmit` - **0 errors**. `npx eslint .` - **0 errors**, same 3 pre-existing unrelated warnings (`_components/Logo.tsx` x2 `no-img-element`, `analytics/page.tsx` 1 unused var), confirmed unchanged. `npx vitest run` - **75 files, 610 tests, all pass**, unchanged (no `.spec.ts` touched - `bulkUploadCvs()` had no existing test coverage to begin with, confirmed via `grep -rn "bulkUploadCvs" app --include="*.spec.ts" --include="*.test.ts"` before this pass, zero hits). The node `*.test.ts` loop, `app-ci.yml`'s own exact invocation (`node --experimental-strip-types "$f"` per file, no `--test` glob) - **31 files, 345 tests, 0 failures** (up from 30 files; this pass's own 7 new tests in 1 new file). `npx next build` - clean, same 62-route table, scratch route (`app/scratchbulktest`) confirmed absent. Both temporary scratch routes (`app/scratchbulktest`, `app/scratchbulktest2`) deleted and both `next dev` servers stopped (`pkill`, confirmed via `ps aux` afterward showing no live match) before any commit; `.next` cleared and `next typegen` re-run so no stale scratch-route type reference survived into the final `tsc` run.

**Flagged for Sarel's own judgment, not acted on here.** The "real" fix (browser-direct-to-Storage for bulk CV uploads, matching every other multi-file surface) would remove this safe-but-slightly-awkward chunking layer entirely, at the cost of a staging-path-plus-`move()` design this pass judged too large to make unilaterally (see "Fix" above) - logged in `System-Status.md` as a recommendation, not consumed as a Finding number of its own.

**Not escalated to a PR.** Touches application logic only - no RLS, no money path, no hard-stop gate, no worker-image change, no schema/migration, and not an authorization-bypass/tenant-isolation finding. Moderate severity (breaks a named, real feature for realistic inputs) but contained to 2 existing files + 1 new pure module + its own test file, consistent with this track's own "isolated bug fix -> push directly" bar. Pushed directly to `main`.

### Finding 273 (CONFIRMED AND FIXED ON `main` - low/moderate, a residual gap in Finding 272's own fix, found one pass later by pursuing the standing brief's own named lead to its natural follow-on question - the same per-request Vercel body-size mechanism Finding 272 fixed for "a couple of big CVs" still breaks a bulk-CV-upload chunk made of MANY SMALL CVs, because the fix only bounded raw file bytes, never the real multipart-field overhead that scales with file count)

**Area:** `app/app/people/_components/bulkCvChunking.ts` (`chunkRowsBySize()` gains a second, independent cap), `bulkCvChunking.test.ts` (4 new cases, 11/11 total).

**How this was found.** This pass's own assigned lead, per the standing brief: grep every multi-file-`FormData`-through-a-Server-Action call site in `app/` and check each against the `uploadBatch.ts`-vs-single-capped-request distinction. `grep -rn "new FormData()"` / `grep -rn "FileDropzone" ` / `grep -rln "multiple"` across every `.tsx` in `app/` found exactly one multi-file-capable surface that does NOT use `uploadBatch.ts`'s browser-direct-to-Storage pattern: `bulk-cv-upload.tsx` - already Finding 272, already fixed, not a new site. Every other `multiple`-capable `FileDropzone` (`upload-form.tsx`) already uses `uploadBatch()`; every other native `<input type="file">` and every other `new FormData()`/`.append("file", ...)` call site in the whole app (`cv-led-add-person.tsx`, `DirectVaultDocumentUploader.tsx`, all the single-file forms under `tenders/[id]`, `experience/`, `my-cv/`, `company/registrations|properties`, etc.) is single-file by construction (`maxFiles: 1`, `files[0]`, or a plain `name="file"` HTML form field with no `multiple` attribute) - the lead is a genuine, exhaustively-checked conclusive negative for "a SECOND site with this bug shape." Rather than stop there, re-read Finding 272's own fix skeptically (this track's own established "don't trust a fix's own label" discipline, most recently applied to `siteUrl.ts` three times running) and asked the obvious next question `chunkRowsBySize()`'s own header comment never raised: does bounding only raw FILE BYTES per chunk account for the REST of what a real multipart request body actually contains?

**The real mechanism, measured before being tested live.** `rowsToFormData()` (the same file) emits 3 fields per row (`kind_i`, `file_i`, `person_id_i` or `name_i`), each its own multipart part with its own boundary/Content-Disposition line - fixed overhead PER FIELD, meaning overhead that scales with FILE COUNT, not with total bytes. `chunkRowsBySize()`'s own cap (`<= MAX_CV_BYTES`, 4.4 MB of raw file bytes) says nothing about file count, so a chunk built entirely of many small files can have a raw-byte sum safely under the cap while its real serialized body is not. Measured directly in Node (real `Request`/`FormData`, the same multipart encoder a real browser's own `fetch` uses, not a hand-rolled estimate): a single chunk of 2 files at the per-file cap has ~1KB of overhead (already safe, matches Finding 272's own repro); at 50 files, ~18KB; at 500 tiny files, ~185KB; at 1000, ~370KB - overhead alone, before counting any file bytes, already exceeding the ~100KB margin `next.config.ts`'s own 4.5MB-vs-4.4MB gap leaves.

**Confirmed live, real repro against the real mechanism, not reasoned about.** A disposable scratch Server Action (`app/scratchmanybulk/`, a bare action echoing each file's size - same shape as `bulkUploadCvs()`'s own FormData contract, deleted before this commit, never committed) against a real `npx next dev -p 3171`, driven by a headless Chromium tab (Playwright, already installed in this environment) clicking a button that builds and sends the exact `rowsToFormData()` field shape for N tiny files whose RAW BYTE SUM is held at/under `MAX_CV_BYTES` throughout (so the pre-fix `chunkRowsBySize()` would always place them in ONE chunk): 50/100/150/200/220/250 files -> every chunk succeeds; **270/280/290/300/500/1000 files -> every one fails with the identical `Error: Body exceeded 4.5mb limit.`** Finding 272 exists to prevent - confirmed from the real dev server's own thrown error, not simulated. The boundary sits between 250 (safe) and 270 (fails) for this exact field shape.

**Reachability, honestly scoped.** Not a contrived or malicious input - `bulk-cv-upload.tsx`'s own `validateFiles()` call has no `maxFiles` cap (confirmed, `grep -n "validateFiles(files" app/app/people/_components/bulk-cv-upload.tsx`, only a per-file `maxBytes`), and its own UI copy ("Drop multiple CVs here... PDF, Word or an image, up to 4.4 MB each") invites exactly this: a company bulk-uploading a large personnel roster's worth of compact, few-tens-of-KB-each scanned CVs/ID pages (a real, named use case for a tender-compliance tool covering SANRAL-scale project teams) could easily produce a single byte-bounded chunk holding 300+ files before the existing byte-sum cap would ever end it. Same severity tier as Finding 272 itself (a real functional break, no data corruption, no security exposure) - logged as a residual gap in that fix rather than a brand-new bug class.

**Fix, with a measured safety margin, not just the measured 250/270 boundary.** `chunkRowsBySize()` now takes a second, independent cap, `maxFiles` (default `MAX_FILES_PER_CHUNK = 80`, exported alongside it), and starts a new chunk when EITHER the byte-sum cap OR the file-count cap would be exceeded - the existing call site in `bulk-cv-upload.tsx` needed no change, since the new cap defaults in. 80 was chosen with a wide margin, verified against real serialized `FormData` bodies, not just the minimal-field-value measurement above: (a) realistic longer names/filenames (`"Thabo Sipho Mokoena-van der Merwe Jnr."`, long original filenames) - 250 files already exceeds the real cap, 220 leaves only ~10KB; (b) deliberately pathological 120-char filenames and 150-char typed names - even 150 files still leaves a 23.5KB margin, 80 leaves 60.4KB. 80 sits comfortably inside every one of those measured margins, including the pathological case, while rarely being the thing that actually ends a chunk in practice - most real CVs are well over `4.4MB / 80 ≈ 55KB` each, so the pre-existing byte-sum cap still ends a chunk first for ordinary-sized files; this second cap only bites for the specific "many small files" shape it exists to close.

**Verified red-then-green, both as a unit test and against the real mechanism live.** `bulkCvChunking.test.ts`, 4 new cases (11/11 total): many tiny files whose byte sum stays low still split once the file-count cap is hit (100 files at 10 bytes each -> chunks of 80 and 20); a batch at exactly the cap stays in one chunk, one more file starts a second; the byte-sum cap still fires first on its own when file count is low (no regression on Finding 272's own fixture); every row still appears exactly once, and no chunk exceeds either cap, when both caps are exercised on the same mixed batch. **Red** (confirmed by running the new tests against the unmodified pre-fix file via `git stash`): fails outright - `MAX_FILES_PER_CHUNK` does not exist on the old module at all, since the file-count cap is new. **Green:** `node --experimental-strip-types --test app/app/people/_components/bulkCvChunking.test.ts` - **11/11 pass**. Live, against the real mechanism: re-ran the exact same Playwright-driven scratch-route repro above, now importing the FIXED `chunkRowsBySize()` - the same 270/300/1000-tiny-file batches that previously threw the real 413 now split into 80-file chunks (270 -> `80,80,80,30`; 1000 -> twelve chunks of 80 plus one of 40) and every chunk succeeds.

**Full regression.** `npx tsc --noEmit` - **0 errors**. `npx eslint .` - **0 errors**, same 3 pre-existing unrelated warnings (`Logo.tsx` x2 `no-img-element`, `analytics/page.tsx` 1 unused var), confirmed unchanged. `npx vitest run` - **75 files, 610 tests, all pass**, unchanged (no `.spec.ts` touched). The node `*.test.ts` loop, `app-ci.yml`'s own exact invocation - **31 files, 349 tests, 0 failures** (up from 345; this pass's own 4 new cases in the already-existing file, no new file). `npx next build` - clean, exit 0, scratch route confirmed absent (`grep -c "scratch"` on the route table output: 0). Both the scratch route (`app/scratchmanybulk`) and the `next dev -p 3171` server stopped/deleted before any commit, confirmed via `ps aux` showing no live match; `.next` cleared and `next typegen` re-run so no stale scratch-route type reference survived into the final `tsc` run.

**Not escalated to a PR.** Touches one existing pure-logic module's own internal cap plus its test file - no RLS, no money path, no hard-stop gate, no worker-image change, no schema/migration, not an authorization-bypass/tenant-isolation finding. Low/moderate severity (closes a residual gap in an already-real, already-documented functional break, for a realistic-but-less-common "many small files" batch shape rather than the already-fixed "couple of big files" shape) but a genuinely isolated, 2-file change, consistent with this track's own "isolated bug fix -> push directly" bar. Pushed directly to `main`.

### Finding 274 (OPENED AS PR #202, NOT PUSHED - genuine authorization-bypass, the most severe class per this track's own standing rule - a fresh angle: a systematic inventory of every one of `/admin/`'s own 15 real Server Actions for whether EACH independently verifies platform-admin status, not just company membership, since `/admin/layout.tsx`'s own `is_platform_admin()` gate - already documented, in that very file, as covering page renders only - does not run before a Server Action reached by direct POST)

**Area:** `app/app/admin/notifications/actions.ts` (`sendTestNotificationEmail()`), `app/app/admin/notifications/actions.spec.ts` (new file, 2 cases). Both on PR branch `finding-274-admin-notifications-authz`, not on `main`.

**How this was found.** This pass's own chosen fresh angle, per the standing brief's own suggested direction ("does every admin page/action actually verify platform-admin role, not just company membership?"). Read `app/app/admin/layout.tsx` first: its own header comment already establishes, as settled fact from an earlier pass (UX audit 2026-10-23, item 5, "confirmed live with a non-admin account"), that this shared segment layout's `is_platform_admin()` gate gives a non-admin a real but blank page, not a redirect - and, separately, that a Server Action defined under this route segment does **not** go through this layout at all when invoked directly, since it is reached by its own direct POST, not by a GET navigation that would render the layout. Every one of the 5 sibling `admin/**/actions.ts` files already says so explicitly in their own header comments ("Checked here too, since a Server Action is reachable by direct POST") and each independently re-verifies admin status one of three ways: `admin/actions.ts`'s `writeReview()`/`writeAlertResolution()` rely on an RLS-enforced `.update()` that silently matches zero rows for a non-admin, checked via `data.length === 0`; `setTestCompany()`/`setPlatformSetting()`, `impersonation-actions.ts`'s `startImpersonation()`/`endImpersonation()`, `discovered-opportunities/actions.ts`'s `overrideOpportunityConfidence()`, and `requirement-extractions/actions.ts`'s `submitRequirementReview()`/`reprocessRequirementExtraction()` all route through a `SECURITY DEFINER` RPC that itself runs `if not is_platform_admin() then raise exception` (confirmed by reading every one of those RPCs' real SQL bodies in migrations 0064/0072/0076/0100/0102, not assumed from a comment); `taxonomy/actions.ts` has its own explicit `requireAdmin()` helper calling the `is_platform_admin` RPC directly, used by all 4 of its exports. A complete inventory (`grep -n "^export async function" app/app/admin/**/actions.ts`, 15 exports across the 6 files) found exactly one exception: `admin/notifications/actions.ts`'s `sendTestNotificationEmail()` ("Send Test to Me" on the Template Gallery) checks only `if (!user?.email) redirect("/login")` - that the caller is signed in at all, never that they are a platform admin. The two RPCs it then calls, `claim_notification()`/`record_notification_sent()` (migration 0093), are not a backstop either: read their own SQL, confirming each is `grant ... to anon, authenticated` with no `is_platform_admin()` check inside either body, and their own comments say this is deliberate - "called from both the anon/authenticated context (a Server Action with no service-role key, e.g. the welcome email)" - since real, non-admin notification flows (the welcome email) legitimately need to call them too, migration 0119's own comment on the sibling `revoke ... from anon` change independently confirms the intended caller here specifically is "a signed-in admin test-send," not any authenticated user.

**Impact, honestly scoped.** Not a data-exposure or tenant-isolation bug - `EMAIL_TEMPLATE_SAMPLES`' own `render()` functions use fixed, fictional sample data only ("never real company/tender rows," confirmed by reading `lib/emailTemplateSamples.ts`'s own header and entries), and the email always goes to the CALLER's own `user.email`, never an admin's or another tenant's address, so no real company data or any other user's inbox is reachable through this path. The real harm: this is an admin-only feature by explicit design (the action's own header comment, the page it lives under, and migration 0119's own "a signed-in admin test-send" comment all say so) that **any signed-in, non-admin company user** could reach directly (bypassing the Template Gallery UI and `/admin/layout.tsx`'s gate entirely, the same "Server Action reachable by direct POST" mechanism this codebase's own other 5 admin action files already defend against) to repeatedly trigger real outbound `sendTransactionalEmail()` calls through the app's own Resend account - an authorization-bypass of an admin-only control, with no rate limit anywhere in this path, usable for cost/quota abuse against Resend and for polluting the admin-only `notification_logs` dispatch table (`SELECT` on that table is itself `is_platform_admin()`-gated, migration 0093) with fake test-send rows under a non-admin's own identity.

**Confirmed live, not just reasoned about - a real mocked repro, red then green, same convention this track already uses for `people/actions.spec.ts` and siblings.** Wrote `app/app/admin/notifications/actions.spec.ts`, mocking `@/lib/supabase/server` (a session for a signed-in, non-platform-admin user whose own `is_platform_admin` RPC mock would return `false` if ever called) and `@/lib/resendEmail` (so no real Resend call is attempted), calling the real, unmodified `sendTestNotificationEmail()` export - not a reimplementation of its logic. **Red, against the unmodified pre-fix file:** `npx vitest run app/admin/notifications/actions.spec.ts` - the non-admin's call returned `/admin/notifications?sent=Welcome%20email&tab=gallery` (a SUCCESS redirect) and the mocked `sendTransactionalEmail` was actually invoked once - a live, mechanism-level confirmation that a non-admin's call reaches a real outbound-email attempt with zero admin check anywhere in the path, exactly as the static read predicted, not merely asserted.

**Fix.** Added the same `is_platform_admin()` RPC check every sibling action already uses (`admin/actions.ts`'s own inline-check shape, closest to this file's own existing style), immediately after the sign-in check and before anything else runs: a non-admin now gets redirected back to `/admin/notifications?error=...&tab=gallery` with no RPC call, no template render, and no `sendTransactionalEmail()` call at all.

**Green.** Re-ran the same test file unmodified against the fixed code: **2/2 pass** - the non-admin case now redirects with `error=` and the Resend mock is asserted `not.toHaveBeenCalled()`; a second case (a mocked real-admin session) confirms the fix does not break the legitimate path - still reaches `sent=...` and still calls the Resend mock exactly once.

**Full regression.** `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` - **0 errors**. `npx eslint app/admin/notifications/actions.ts app/admin/notifications/actions.spec.ts` - **0 errors/warnings**. `npx vitest run` (full suite) - **76 files, 612 tests, all pass** (up from 75/610 - this pass's own 1 new file, 2 new tests, no regressions elsewhere). `npx next build` - clean, route table unchanged (`/admin/notifications` still renders the same way as before this change - a Server Action change, not a route/rendering-mode change).

**Opened as PR #202 (https://github.com/SarelJvR2024/tender-tool/pull/202), not pushed directly.** Per this track's own binding guardrail: "Any genuine authorization-bypass or tenant-isolation finding is the most severe class - PR, never direct push, regardless of diff size." This is exactly that class (an admin-only control reachable by any authenticated non-admin), even though the fix itself is a small, isolated 2-file change. **Backlog collision check:** `gh api repos/sareljvr2024/tender-tool/pulls/<n>/files` for all 28 PRs open before this pass (`#164`/`#165`/`#176`-`#201`) - zero hits for `admin/notifications` in any open PR's own diff.

**Backlog/sibling status.** `git fetch origin main` immediately before starting this pass, again immediately before committing, and again immediately before pushing the PR branch: every time still `6e211b5` (this pass's own starting point, matching the task brief's own stated current state exactly) - no sibling-track (`session_01UMAzowxArab6cV4KurgXNE`) commit landed during this pass, and the branch push was accepted (not denied).

To verify independently: read `app/app/admin/notifications/actions.ts` on branch `finding-274-admin-notifications-authz` (or PR #202's own diff) and confirm `sendTestNotificationEmail()` now calls `supabase.rpc("is_platform_admin")` and redirects with an `error=` before doing anything else when that returns false/null. Run `cd app && npx vitest run app/admin/notifications/actions.spec.ts` on that branch (expect `2/2 pass`); checking out `main`'s own unmodified copy of the file and running the same test reproduces the pre-fix `sent=...`-despite-non-admin redirect from the first test case. ### Finding 275 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, severe - `scripts/send-compliance-digest.ts`'s `main()` read `companies` with a plain, unranged `.select()` - the identical PostgREST 1000-row cap already found and fixed in two sibling notification scripts this same day - and this is the sender for the SARS Tax PIN/COID/B-BBEE/CIDB/ECSA/SACPCMP compliance-expiry digest, the alert `app/company/Notifications.tsx`'s own UI copy promises is "always delivered to keep your submissions compliant")

**Area:** `app/scripts/send-compliance-digest.ts` (new exported `allCompanies()` helper, used by `main()`). Test coverage added to the existing `app/scripts/send-compliance-digest.spec.ts` (2 new cases, 7 total).

**How this was found.** This cycle's rotation landed on notify. Having just found and fixed the identical bug class twice in the two immediately-preceding cycles (Finding 255 in `send-onboarding-nudges.ts`'s `companies` reads, Finding 266 in `send-operational-alerts.ts`'s `tender_tasks` read - both plain, unranged `.select()` calls against a table read under the SERVICE ROLE key, summed across every company at once, hitting PostgREST's documented 1000-row `db-max-rows` cap), this cycle deliberately grepped every `scripts/send-*.ts` file for the same shape rather than reading files one at a time from scratch. `send-discovered-tenders.ts`, `send-founder-digest.ts`, and `send-returnables-digest.ts` were all already correctly paginated (confirmed by reading each). `send-compliance-digest.ts`'s own `main()` was not: `let companiesQuery = supabase.from("companies").select("id, legal_name"); if (scopeCompanyId) companiesQuery = companiesQuery.eq("id", scopeCompanyId);` - no `.range()`, no `fetchAllRows()` import anywhere in the file (confirmed by grep).

**Why this is severe, not just another instance of the same pagination gap.** This is the live sender for the compliance-expiry digest (SARS Tax PIN, COID Letter of Good Standing, B-BBEE proof, CIDB registration, catalog/property registrations, per-person ECSA/SACPCMP, at 30/14/7-day escalating thresholds) - `complianceDigestCandidatesForCompany()`'s own header comment states these are exactly the facts that "can disqualify an active bid outright." `app/company/Notifications.tsx`'s own UI copy (already quoted in this file's own header comment, from the Finding 163 fix) promises these reminders "are always delivered to keep your submissions compliant." Past the 1000th real company, every company created after it would silently and permanently never receive this digest at all - not a degraded cadence, a complete and total absence of the one alert this app's own UI explicitly promises is unconditional.

**Confirmed live, not inferred.** Read the query directly: no `.range()` call anywhere on the `companies` builder chain, and `fetchAllRows`/`supabasePaging` is absent from this file's own import list - confirmed via grep, not assumed from the file's general shape. `lib/supabasePaging.ts`'s own header comment already establishes, from a direct live check this session doesn't need to repeat, that PostgREST's hard cap on this project is exactly 1000 rows regardless of a client-side `.limit()`.

**Fix.** Extracted a new shared, exported `allCompanies(supabase, scopeCompanyId)` helper wrapping the identical `fetchAllRows()`/`.range()` pattern already established in the sibling scripts, capped at a new `MAX_COMPANY_ROWS = 20_000` (same order of magnitude as the existing siblings' own caps), preserving the existing `--company-id` scoping.

**Verified red-then-green.** Added 2 cases to the existing `send-compliance-digest.spec.ts`: a real multi-page mock (`POSTGREST_PAGE_SIZE + 5` companies, `.range(from, to)` resolving with the real slice asked for) confirming `allCompanies()` returns every row and calls `.range()` exactly twice, not stopping at the first page; a second case confirming the `--company-id` scope still narrows correctly. **Red:** saved the diff to `send-compliance-digest.ts` only, `git apply -R`, re-ran `npx vitest run scripts/send-compliance-digest.spec.ts` - `2 failed | 5 passed`, exactly the new cases (`allCompanies is not a function`, confirming the helper is genuinely new), the 5 pre-existing `processComplianceDigestForCompany()` cases (Findings 163's own regression tests) untouched. **Green:** reapplied, re-ran - `7/7 pass`. `npx tsc --noEmit` clean project-wide (only the pre-existing, unrelated `date-fns`/`react-day-picker` gap this session has repeatedly confirmed is environment-only). Broader regression: `npx vitest run scripts/` - all 7 script spec files, 49/49 pass.

**Not escalated to a PR.** Small, safe, self-contained TypeScript fix reusing an already-established pagination helper pattern, applied twice elsewhere in this same codebase this same day - no RLS, no migration, no money path, no worker-image change. Pushed directly to `main`.

To verify independently: from `app/`, `npx vitest run scripts/send-compliance-digest.spec.ts` (expect `7/7 pass`, including the 2 new `allCompanies` pagination cases). `npx tsc --noEmit` (0 new errors). ### Finding 276 (OPENED AS PR #203, NOT PUSHED - genuine cross-tenant reference gap on `pack_review_confirmations` - the exact `tt_same_company` tender-visibility bug class the cross-tenant-integrity audit (`0043`) established and `narrative_documents`'s own retrofit (`0097`) already fixed once, found because `0097`'s own sweep never reached this one sibling table)

**Area:** `app/supabase/migrations/0125_pack_review_confirmations_tenant_integrity.sql` (new), `engine/security/test_tenant_isolation.py` (extended - new cross-tenant probe + a positive "own shared tender" case). Both on PR branch `finding-276-pack-review-confirmations-tenant-integrity`, not on `main`.

**How this was found.** This pass's own chosen fresh angle, per the standing brief's own suggested direction of sweeping the full `tenders/[id]/*-actions.ts` family action-by-action. Read all 12 files under `app/app/tenders/[id]/*-actions.ts` (26 real Server Actions total) and ranked each file by its own mention count across both standing docs to find genuinely under-reviewed ones: `comment-actions.ts`, `general-pack-review-actions.ts`, and `pack-review-actions.ts` all had zero `QA-Edge-Case-Findings.md` mentions. Reading `general-pack-review-actions.ts`'s own header comment led straight to the real lead: both `confirmGeneralPackReview()` and `pack-review-actions.ts`'s `confirmPackReview()` upsert the SAME `pack_review_confirmations` table (`0059`) with only `company_id`/`tender_id` from form data - no visibility check on the Server Action side (correctly so: every other sibling table relies on a database-level trigger, not the Server Action, for this check - see `tender_comments`'s own 0024/0043 pattern). Checked which tables actually carry the `tt_same_company` tender-visibility trigger (`grep -n "create trigger tt_same_company" app/supabase/migrations/*.sql`): `0043`'s original 9 tables, `tender_subcontracting_plans`'s own dedicated trigger (`0056`), and `narrative_documents`'s own retrofit (`0097`, whose own header comment explicitly documents this exact bug class and explicitly names 9 of the other covered tables) - `pack_review_confirmations` is not in that list anywhere, on current `main` (confirmed by reading `tt_check_same_company()`'s own current body, the version last redefined by `0097`, line by line - its `tg_table_name in (...)` tender-visibility branch genuinely omits it).

**Impact, honestly scoped.** Narrower than `0097`'s own `narrative_documents` precedent (no service-role worker or AI-drafting code path reads `pack_review_confirmations` - confirmed by grep across `app/` and `engine/`, the table is only ever touched by Server Actions/Components under ordinary RLS), and the real downstream gate (`request_submission_pack_checked()`, `0113`+) independently re-validates `tender_pack_id` on its own, so a spoofed confirmation row does not unlock generating an actual pack for a tender the caller has no real relationship with. The real, live-confirmed impact is narrower but still genuine: (a) an orphaned audit row naming a tender the inserting company has no legitimate business with, and (b) a usable existence oracle - this table's own insert, and nothing else, lets any signed-in company learn whether an arbitrary tender UUID corresponds to a real (if invisible/private) tender at all, by reading which error code (success, vs. `23503` FK violation for a genuinely non-existent id) comes back. A private/manual tender's id isn't published but isn't a secret either - the same standing threat model `0043`/`0097` both use (a URL, a screenshot, an old e-mail is enough).

**Confirmed live in a disposable scratch Postgres, not reasoned from source alone.** Replayed all 114 migrations (`engine/security/replay_schema.sh`) onto a fresh scratch DB, seeded a company Beta with a PRIVATE tender and an unrelated company Acme, then as Acme (`set role authenticated` + `test.uid`): (1) baseline `select id from tenders where id = '<Beta's tender>'` - 0 rows, genuinely invisible; (2) `insert into pack_review_confirmations (company_id, tender_id) values ('<Acme>', '<Beta's tender>')` - **succeeded**, confirmed by reading it back; (3) the identical shape against `tender_comments` (0043-protected) - correctly refused, `42501`, proving this isn't a general RLS hole; (4) the same insert against a tender_id that doesn't exist at all - failed differently, `23503` FK violation, the live demonstration of the existence-oracle distinction described above.

**Fix.** The exact mechanism `0097` already established for `narrative_documents`: add `pack_review_confirmations` to `tt_check_same_company()`'s tender-visibility `tg_table_name in (...)` branch and attach the `before insert or update of company_id, tender_id` trigger to it. Migration `0125` (`main` tops out at `0124` as of this pass).

**Green, re-verified against the same replayed-plus-fix database.** The identical step-2 insert now raises `pack_review_confirmations: this tender is another company's private tender` (`42501`) - and, as a side effect worth noting, this also collapses the existence oracle from step 4: because the trigger's own check runs before the FK constraint would, a non-existent tender_id now gets the *same* `42501`, not a distinguishable `23503`, so the two cases are no longer distinguishable from the error alone either. Confirmed the fix does not over-block the real feature: a confirmation on a SHARED tender (`owner_company_id is null`) and on the requesting company's own PRIVATE tender both still succeed.

**Test suite extended and verified red-then-green.** Added a matching cross-tenant probe to `engine/security/test_tenant_isolation.py`'s own `part2()` `ref_probes` dict (`"pack_review_confirmations on B's private tender"`) and a positive case to the `own` dict (`"own pack review confirmation, shared tender"`). **Red:** replayed the 114 migrations WITHOUT `0125` and ran the suite with `TENANT_PSQL` pointed at it - `1 FAILED`, exactly the new probe (`NOT refused`), nothing else. **Green:** replayed all 115 migrations WITH `0125` - `ALL PASSED`. Part 1 (in-memory, no DB) re-run separately, unaffected: `ALL PASSED`.

**Full regression.** `cd app && npx tsc --noEmit` - 0 errors (no TypeScript touched; this change is migration + Python test only). `python3 -m py_compile engine/security/test_tenant_isolation.py` - clean.

**Opened as PR #203 (https://github.com/SarelJvR2024/tender-tool/pull/203), not pushed directly.** Per this track's own binding guardrail: "Any genuine authorization-bypass or tenant-isolation finding is the most severe class - PR, never direct push, regardless of diff size." This is exactly that class. **Backlog collision check:** `gh api repos/sareljvr2024/tender-tool/pulls/<n>/files` across all 29 PRs open before this pass (`#164`/`#165`/`#176`-`#202`) for any mention of `pack_review_confirmations` in any file's patch - exactly one hit, PR #187 (Finding 205, `record_tender_document()`'s own employee-RLS-bypass fix), and reading that hit's context confirmed it's only a prose listing of every table carrying an `is_employee_in_company()` RESTRICTIVE policy, unrelated to this tender-visibility gap - no duplication.

Not fixed here - those are other PRs' own branches, out of scope per this track's guardrails; flagged below as a standing item.

### Finding 277 (OPENED AS PR #204, NOT PUSHED - a third real instance of the same `tt_same_company` tender-visibility bug class, this time on `savings_counted_steps` - found by widening Finding 276's own single-table lead into a full cross-check of every table in the schema carrying both a `company_id` and a `tender_id` column)

**Area:** `app/supabase/migrations/0139_savings_counted_steps_tenant_integrity.sql` (new), `engine/security/test_tenant_isolation.py` (extended - new cross-tenant probe + a positive "own shared tender" case). Both on PR branch `finding-277-savings-counted-steps-tenant-integrity`, not on `main`.

**How this was found.** This pass's own chosen fresh angle, the task brief's own second "good fresh direction": rather than reacting to one specific table (as Finding 276 did), widen `tt_check_same_company()`'s own table-coverage question into a systematic cross-check of the WHOLE schema. Built the complete list of every table with both a `company_id` and a `tender_id` column directly from a replayed scratch Postgres's own `information_schema.columns` (`select c1.table_name from information_schema.columns c1 join information_schema.columns c2 on c1.table_name = c2.table_name where c1.column_name = 'company_id' and c2.column_name = 'tender_id'`), not grepped from migration source text (which would miss columns added by a later `alter table`, and wouldn't distinguish a real base table from a view): 21 tables. Diffed that list against `tt_check_same_company()`'s own current `tg_table_name in (...)` branch (`0043`'s original 9, `tender_subcontracting_plans`'s own dedicated `0056` trigger, `narrative_documents`'s own `0097` retrofit) plus the one already-known, not-yet-merged gap (`pack_review_confirmations`, Finding 276/PR #203). Ten tables remained genuinely unaccounted for: `discovered_opportunities`, `notification_logs`, `savings_counted_steps`, `sent_deadline_reminders`, `sent_operational_alerts`, `tender_documents`, `tender_engine_jobs`, `tender_requirements`, `tender_update_notifications` (plus `pack_review_confirmations` itself, already PR #203's). Read each one's own real RLS policies (`select tablename, policyname, cmd, qual, with_check from pg_policies where tablename in (...)`) to find which ones actually grant `authenticated` a permissive INSERT/UPDATE path at all - most don't (see "Conclusive negatives" below) - leaving exactly one real, live-exploitable gap: `savings_counted_steps`'s own `"savings_counted_steps: tenant isolation"` policy is `for all` and `with check (is_company_member(company_id))` - it has no opinion on `tender_id` whatsoever, and (confirmed by grep) no `tt_same_company` trigger was ever attached either (`0085` predates `0097` and was never revisited by it).

**Impact, honestly scoped.** Same bracket as Finding 276's own precedent, narrower still: `savings_counted_steps` stores no tender details at all (just `tender_id`, `step_key`, a snapshot `hours` figure) and is read only by `lib/savingsCounterData.ts`'s own RLS-scoped dashboard aggregation (grepped `app/` and `engine/` - zero other callers, no service-role worker path touches it). The aggregation it feeds is already scoped to the caller's own `company_id` regardless of `tender_id`'s validity, so a company can already inflate its own displayed "hours saved" by calling `recordSavingsStep()` with any `step_key` for any tender it can already see - this gap's own incremental effect is narrower than that: (a) the same usable existence oracle Finding 276 already established (this table's own insert error - success vs. `23503` FK violation - lets any signed-in company learn whether an arbitrary tender UUID is real, even a private one it cannot otherwise see), and (b) letting a company fabricate a savings-counter row keyed to a specific stranger's private tender id, polluting its own historical breakdown with a tender_id it has no real claim to (confirmable only by the company itself, since RLS still scopes every read to `company_id`). Not a data-exfiltration or pack-generation bypass - still a genuine, live-confirmed tenant-isolation gap and existence oracle, the most severe standing class per this track's own guardrail.

**Confirmed live in a disposable scratch Postgres, not reasoned from source alone.** Replayed all 114 migrations (`engine/security/replay_schema.sh`) onto a fresh scratch DB, seeded company A and company B's own PRIVATE manual tender (`owner_company_id = B`), then as A (`set role authenticated` + `test.uid`): (1) baseline `select count(*) from tenders where id = '<B's private tender>'` - 0 rows, genuinely invisible; (2) `insert into savings_counted_steps (company_id, tender_id, step_key, hours) values ('<A>', '<B's private tender>', 'pack_generated', 2)` - **succeeded**, confirmed by reading it back (1 row); (3) the identical shape against `tender_comments` (0043-protected) - correctly refused, `42501`, proving this isn't a general hole in the probe itself; (4) the same insert against a tender_id that doesn't exist at all - failed differently, `23503` FK violation on `savings_counted_steps_tender_id_fkey`, the live demonstration of the existence-oracle distinction described above; (5) a positive control - the same insert against a real SHARED tender (`owner_company_id is null`) - succeeded, confirming the bug isn't just "every insert succeeds."

**Fix.** The exact mechanism `0097`/`0125` already established: add `savings_counted_steps` to `tt_check_same_company()`'s tender-visibility `tg_table_name in (...)` branch and attach the `before insert or update of company_id, tender_id` trigger to it. Migration `0139` - deliberately NOT `0125` (already claimed by five other open PR branches, `#186`/`#197`/`#198`/`#201`/`#203`, a standing, already-flagged numbering collision this doesn't add a sixth instance of); picks up from `0138`, the highest migration number any currently open PR branch claims (PR #200).

**Green, re-verified against the same replayed-plus-fix database.** The identical step-2 insert now raises `savings_counted_steps: this tender is another company's private tender` (`42501`) - and, same side effect as Finding 276, this also collapses the existence oracle from step 4, since the trigger's own check now runs before the FK constraint would. Confirmed the fix does not over-block the real feature: a step recorded on a SHARED tender, and on the requesting company's own PRIVATE tender, both still succeed.

**Test suite extended and verified red-then-green.** Added a matching cross-tenant probe to `engine/security/test_tenant_isolation.py`'s own `part2()` `ref_probes` dict (`"savings_counted_steps on B's private tender"`) and a positive case to the `own` dict (`"own savings step, shared tender"`). **Red:** replayed the 114 migrations WITHOUT `0139` and ran the suite with `TENANT_PSQL` pointed at it - `1 FAILED`, exactly the new probe (`NOT refused`), nothing else. **Green:** replayed all 115 migrations WITH `0139` - `ALL PASSED`. Part 1 (in-memory, no DB) re-run separately, unaffected: `ALL PASSED`.

**Conclusive negatives from the same cross-check (not fixed, nothing wrong).** The other nine tables with both `company_id` and `tender_id` columns, checked individually, not assumed:
- `tender_documents`, `tender_requirements`, `sent_deadline_reminders`, `sent_operational_alerts`, `tender_update_notifications`, `notification_logs`, `discovered_opportunities`: each has only a SELECT-shaped permissive policy for `authenticated` (or, for `sent_deadline_reminders`/`sent_operational_alerts`, RLS enabled with zero policies at all) - no permissive INSERT/UPDATE policy exists for `authenticated` at all, so a direct client write is already default-denied by RLS regardless of `tender_id`'s validity, before `tt_check_same_company()` would ever even run. Confirmed via `select relrowsecurity from pg_class where relname in (...)` (all `true`, i.e. RLS genuinely enforced, not accidentally disabled) plus the `pg_policies` read above.
- `tender_engine_jobs`: turned out not to be a real base table at all - `select relkind from pg_class where relname = 'tender_engine_jobs'` returns `v` (a view), and `pg_get_viewdef()` confirms it's `0026`'s own `security_invoker = true` VIEW over `pack_generation_jobs` (filtered to `engine = 'general'`), which already carries the real `tt_same_company` trigger. `security_invoker` means the view runs with the CALLER's own privileges, so `pack_generation_jobs`'s own RLS and trigger protection apply unchanged through the view - not a second, unguarded surface.

**Full regression.** `cd app && npx tsc --noEmit` - 0 errors (no TypeScript touched; this change is migration + Python test only). `python3 -m py_compile engine/security/test_tenant_isolation.py` - clean.

**Opened as PR #204 (https://github.com/SarelJvR2024/tender-tool/pull/204), not pushed directly.** Per this track's own binding guardrail: any genuine tenant-isolation finding is the most severe class - PR, never direct push, regardless of diff size. **Backlog collision check:** `gh api repos/sareljvr2024/tender-tool/pulls/<n>/files` across all 30 PRs open before this pass (`#164`/`#165`/`#176`-`#203`) for any mention of `savings_counted_steps` in any file's patch - 4 hits (`#164`, `#176`, `#185`, `#186`), each read in full: `#164` is the unrelated "Capacity Unlocked copy/calculation rework" feature PR (touches `lib/savingsCounter.ts`/`savingsCounterData.ts`/`submission-pack.tsx` for UI/copy, not RLS); `#176`'s `0119_employee_rls_systematic_sweep.sql` only discusses the table in a prose comment (deferring to a later pass, which became PR #185); `#185` (Finding 203, already open) adds a RESTRICTIVE `"savings_counted_steps: employee has no access"` policy - a different bug class entirely (blocking the `employee` role from the table at all) that leaves the owner/member tender-visibility gap this finding fixes completely untouched - confirmed by reading `#185`'s own full migration patch, not assumed from its title; `#186` only mentions the table in a `docs/specs/System-Status.md` prose line. No real duplication with any of the four.

**Backlog/sibling status.** `git fetch origin main` at the start of this pass and again immediately before pushing the PR branch: both times still `65afe11` (pass `aa`'s own HEAD, matching the task brief's own stated current state exactly) - no sibling-track (`session_01UMAzowxArab6cV4KurgXNE`) commit landed during this pass. The branch push was accepted (not denied).

To verify independently: read `app/supabase/migrations/0139_savings_counted_steps_tenant_integrity.sql` on branch `finding-277-savings-counted-steps-tenant-integrity` (or PR #204's own diff) and confirm `tt_check_same_company()`'s tender-visibility branch now lists `savings_counted_steps` and the matching trigger is attached.
