### Finding 278 (CONFIRMED AND FIXED ON `main` - low, a genuine race-condition/observability bug, not tenant-isolation - a different KIND of bug than this track's own recent run of findings, per the task brief's own suggestion to pivot off that specific angle)

**Area:** `engine/pack/process_pack_jobs.py`'s `sync_tender_requirements()`, `engine/pack/test_sync_functions.py` (new test).

**How this was found.** Took up the task brief's own "race conditions... check-then-insert patterns" fresh direction, having confirmed pass `ee` (this track's immediately preceding pass, same HEAD `3cfad87`) had just exhaustively swept `engine/pack/`'s whole directory for tenant-isolation specifically - re-reading `process_pack_jobs.py` for a DIFFERENT angle on the same file, not re-walking the same ground. `sync_tender_requirements()`'s own docstring already names the exact shape to look for: "already have positions for this tender? ... existence-based... ANY row for this key counts as done" (Finding 230's own write-up, still live in the comments). Read `docs/specs/Automated-Fulfillment-Deployment.md` to check whether this bridge's own concurrency model is real or hypothetical: it documents, explicitly, that "a hosted worker and a hand-run `--once` can overlap" as a real, intended deployment shape (the same reason `process_job()`'s own `pack_generation_jobs` claim exists one function below). `sync_tender_requirements()` itself has no equivalent protection: it reads `have` (which (tender_id, company_id) keys already have rows) once per poll, then inserts a whole workbook's positions in one batch for any key not in that set - a plain check-then-insert, not a conditional/claimed write, with no test anywhere (`test_sync_functions.py`, `test_process_pack_jobs.py`) modelling two runs racing on the SAME previously-unsynced workbook.

**The real mechanism, confirmed against the live schema before touching any code.** `tender_requirements`'s own unique constraint (`tender_requirements_tender_position_company_key`, migration `0045`, `unique nulls not distinct (tender_id, position_code, is_alternate, company_id)`) is exactly what makes this safe from DOUBLE-WRITING data - but the exception it raises when a concurrent run wins the same insert first falls straight into this function's own broad `except Exception as e:` (added for Finding 230's own atomicity fix), which unconditionally prints and `system_alerts.record()`s it as `"could not read the uploaded Technical workbook's SETUP sheet"` at `"error"` severity - **wrong**: the workbook WAS read and parsed correctly; the ONLY thing that failed is the insert, and only because another run already wrote the identical rows a moment earlier. Every real "could not read the workbook" alert (a bad download, a corrupt file, Finding 230's own partial-batch scenario) looks, to whoever watches `system_alerts`, identical to this completely benign, self-correcting race - there is no way to tell them apart from the alert text alone.

**Confirmed live on a disposable scratch Postgres, not reasoned about from source alone.** Replayed all 114 migrations (`engine/security/replay_schema.sh`) onto a fresh scratch DB, seeded one tender. Ran two REAL concurrent `psql` transactions (background shell jobs, not simulated) each doing `begin; select pg_sleep(1); insert into tender_requirements (tender_id, position_code, ..., is_alternate, company_id) values (<same tender>, 'PL', ..., false, null); commit;` - the identical row, from two sessions, timed to land inside the same one-second window. Result: one session's `INSERT 0 1`/`COMMIT` succeeded; the other failed with exactly `ERROR: duplicate key value violates unique constraint "tender_requirements_tender_position_company_key" DETAIL: Key (tender_id, position_code, is_alternate, company_id)=(<tender>, PL, f, null) already exists.` and rolled back - the live, two-process version of the race `sync_tender_requirements()`'s own single-process `have`-then-insert shape is exposed to. Then drove the REAL `sync_tender_requirements()` function (not a rewritten copy) against a fake client whose `insert()` raises the exact `RuntimeError` text `SupabaseRest._req()` wraps a real PostgREST 409 Conflict in for this exact Postgres error (same wrapping this file's own `class SupabaseRest` already does, read directly, not assumed) - the real, unmodified function produced precisely the predicted false alert: `system_alerts.record("pack", "Could not read an uploaded Technical workbook's SETUP sheet (RuntimeError: POST /rest/v1/tender_requirements failed: 409 {\"code\":\"23505\",...})", "error", ...)`.

**Impact, honestly scoped.** Low severity, not a data-correctness or security bug - the unique constraint already prevents any actual double-write or data loss; `written[key]` is discarded by every real caller (`process_pending()` never reads `sync_tender_requirements()`'s return value) and the next poll cycle's own `have` check already sees the concurrent run's committed rows and skips cleanly. The entire effect is a misleading, noise-generating `system_alerts` "error" entry on a real but infrequent and completely benign event (the one documented overlap scenario: the hosted Railway worker and a hand-run `--once` invocation both reading the same brand-new `tender_documents` upload inside the same ~30s poll window) - the kind of false-positive that erodes trust in the SAME alert channel's genuine errors (a real unreadable/corrupt workbook) over time, since both currently read identically.

**Fix.** Narrowed the existing `try`/`except` so only the `client.insert(...)` call for this workbook's positions is wrapped a second time: if that specific call's exception text contains `"23505"` or `"duplicate key value violates unique constraint"` (the literal signature a Postgres unique-constraint violation always carries, through this file's own `SupabaseRest` wrapping), it is treated as "another worker already wrote these positions" - a plain print, `continue` to the next `tender_documents` row, no `system_alerts.record()` call at all (nothing is actually wrong). Any OTHER exception from the insert (Finding 230's own scenario: a genuinely bad/duplicate value from the SETUP sheet itself, a transient network failure) still falls through to the existing, unchanged `except Exception as e:` below and is still reported as a real error exactly as before - confirmed this discrimination is correct both ways, not just for the new case (see test suite below).

**Test suite extended and verified red-then-green.** Added `test_sync_tender_requirements_treats_a_concurrent_workers_duplicate_insert_as_benign_not_an_error()` to `engine/pack/test_sync_functions.py`, driving the real `sync_tender_requirements()` against a `FakeClient` subclass whose `insert()` raises the exact live-confirmed `RuntimeError` text for `tender_requirements` only. **Red** (fix reverted via `git stash` on `process_pack_jobs.py` alone, test file left in place): `1 FAILURE(S)` - exactly the new check (`a benign concurrent-write race is NOT reported via system_alerts (no false 'error')`), nothing else, with the alert payload showing the pre-fix misleading message verbatim. **Green** (fix restored): `ALL PASSED`. Full regression confirmed unaffected: `test_process_pack_jobs.py` (including its own Finding 230 test, which uses a DIFFERENT, non-duplicate-key `RuntimeError` message and correctly still raises its real alert, proving the new `23505` check doesn't swallow genuine failures) - `0 failure(s)`; `test_pdf_merge.py`, `test_assemble_pack.py`, `test_pack_suggestions.py`, `test_adapt_company.py` - all `ALL PASSED`/`0 failure(s)`. `python3 -m py_compile engine/pack/process_pack_jobs.py engine/pack/test_sync_functions.py` - clean.

**Pushed directly to `main` (no PR).** Per this track's own binding guardrail: a small, self-contained Python-only fix inside one function's own exception handling, no schema/migration change, no RLS, no money, no worker-image change, no multi-table RPC surface - and explicitly NOT a tenant-isolation/authorization-bypass finding (the opposite of this track's last several findings' severity class), so the "PR, never direct push, regardless of diff size" rule for that class does not apply here. `git fetch origin main` immediately before pushing: still `3cfad87`, matching this pass's own orientation step exactly - no sibling-track commit landed during this pass.

To verify independently: read `engine/pack/process_pack_jobs.py`'s `sync_tender_requirements()` (the inner `try`/`except` around `client.insert("tender_requirements", ...)`) and `engine/pack/test_sync_functions.py`'s new test. Run `python3 engine/pack/test_sync_functions.py` (expect `ALL PASSED`). To see the live DB-level race independently: replay `engine/security/replay_schema.sh` onto a scratch Postgres, seed one `tenders` row, then run two concurrent `psql` sessions each inserting the identical `tender_requirements` row (tender_id, position_code, is_alternate, company_id all equal) - one commits, the other raises `23505` on `tender_requirements_tender_position_company_key`.

### Finding 279 (CONFIRMED AND FIXED ON `main` - low, a second live instance of Finding 278's own race-condition/observability bug class, same file, different function and table - not tenant-isolation)

**Area:** `engine/pack/process_pack_jobs.py`'s `sync_position_suggestions()`, `engine/pack/test_sync_functions.py` (new test).

**How this was found.** The task brief's own first-listed fresh direction for this pass: "does `sync_b7_setup()`, `sync_position_suggestions()`, or `process_job()` itself have a similar check-then-insert/check-then-act race, now that you know the shape to look for? Pass 'ff' only checked one function in this file for races." Read all three of `process_pack_jobs.py`'s remaining per-poll sync functions plus `process_job()` itself with exactly that question. `sync_b7_setup()`: ruled out - its own write is a plain `client.update("tenders", {"id": tid}, {"sanral_b7_setup": setup})` keyed by `tenders.id` (no unique-constraint insert at all), so two workers racing on the same tender simply compute and write the identical `setup` value twice - idempotent, no exception, no bug. `process_job()`: already protected by its own documented, atomic `pack_generation_jobs` claim (`status='requested' -> 'generating'`) one function above `sync_tender_requirements()` - explicitly "so two workers never build the same job", confirmed unchanged by re-reading it. `sync_position_suggestions()`, called every poll cycle from the same `process_pending()` as `sync_tender_requirements()` (so the identical documented "hosted worker + hand-run `--once` can overlap" shape applies), has the EXACT same check-then-insert shape Finding 278 fixed one function above it: `existing = {a["position_code"]: a for a in client.select("tender_pack_assignments", {"tender_pack_id": pack["id"]})}` read once per pack, then `client.insert("tender_pack_assignments", {"tender_pack_id": pack["id"], "position_code": req["position_code"], ...})` for any position not already in `existing` - with no test anywhere (`test_sync_functions.py`, `test_pdf_merge.py`'s own `test_sync_position_suggestions_skips_a_tender_closed_real_yesterday()`) modelling two runs racing on the same previously-unranked position.

**The real mechanism, confirmed against the live schema before touching any code.** `tender_pack_assignments`'s own unique constraint (migration `0001`, `unique (tender_pack_id, position_code)`) is exactly what makes this safe from double-writing data - but the exception a losing concurrent insert raises falls straight into this function's own broad per-pack `except Exception as e:`, which unconditionally prints and `system_alerts.record()`s it as `"Could not score key-position candidates"` at `"error"` severity - **wrong**: the candidates WERE ranked correctly; the ONLY thing that failed is the insert, and only because another worker already wrote the identical ranking a moment earlier. Worse than Finding 278's own version: because the `except` wraps the WHOLE per-pack loop (every position for that pack, not just the one that raced), a race on ONE position also aborts every OTHER position still queued for that same pack in that cycle (recoverable next poll, but still an over-broad blast radius) and always produces the same misleading "could not score candidates" alert, indistinguishable from a real scoring failure (a malformed `tender_requirements` row, a `rank_candidates()` bug) from the alert text alone.

**Confirmed live on a disposable scratch Postgres, not reasoned about from source alone.** Replayed all 114 migrations (`engine/security/replay_schema.sh`) onto a fresh scratch DB (`scratch_race_gg`), seeded one company/tender/tender_pack row. Ran two REAL concurrent `psql` transactions (background shell jobs, not simulated) each doing `begin; select pg_sleep(1); insert into tender_pack_assignments (tender_pack_id, position_code, candidate_scores, scored_at) values (<same pack>, 'PL', '[]', now()); commit;` - the identical row, from two sessions, timed to land inside the same one-second window. Result: one session's `INSERT 0 1`/`COMMIT` succeeded; the other failed with exactly `ERROR: duplicate key value violates unique constraint "tender_pack_assignments_tender_pack_id_position_code_key" DETAIL: Key (tender_pack_id, position_code)=(<pack>, PL) already exists.` and rolled back. Then drove the REAL `sync_position_suggestions()` function (not a rewritten copy, pre-fix) against a fake client whose `insert()` raises the exact `RuntimeError` text `SupabaseRest._req()` wraps this real PostgREST 409 Conflict in - the real, unmodified function produced precisely the predicted false alert (`system_alerts.record("pack", "Could not score key-position candidates (RuntimeError: POST /rest/v1/tender_pack_assignments failed: 409 {\"code\":\"23505\",...})", "error", ...)`) and, as predicted, also silently dropped the OTHER, non-racing position (`DS1`) for that same pack in that cycle (recovered on the next poll, but confirming the over-broad blast radius described above).

**Impact, honestly scoped.** Low severity, same bracket as Finding 278 - the unique constraint already prevents any actual double-write or data loss; the next poll cycle's own `existing` read already sees the concurrent run's committed row and no-ops on it (same `candidate_scores` already matches). The entire effect is a misleading, noise-generating `system_alerts` "error" entry plus a same-cycle, self-recovering under-write on the one documented overlap scenario (the hosted worker and a hand-run `--once` both polling candidate rankings inside the same window) - the same false-positive class that erodes trust in genuine "could not score candidates" alerts (a real `rank_candidates()` exception, a malformed requirement row) over time.

**Fix.** Narrowed the insert path: the `client.insert("tender_pack_assignments", ...)` call (the `else` branch of `if row: ... else: ...`) is now wrapped in its own `try`/`except`; if that specific call's exception text contains `"23505"` or `"duplicate key value violates unique constraint"`, it is treated as "another worker already wrote this ranking" - a plain print, `continue` to the next position in the same pack's loop (so a race on one position no longer aborts the rest of that pack's own cycle), no `system_alerts.record()` call at all. Any OTHER exception from the insert still re-raises into the existing, unchanged outer `except Exception as e:` and is still reported as a real error exactly as before.

**Test suite extended and verified red-then-green.** Added `test_sync_position_suggestions_treats_a_concurrent_workers_duplicate_insert_as_benign_not_an_error()` to `engine/pack/test_sync_functions.py`, driving the real `sync_position_suggestions()` against a `FakeClient` subclass whose `insert()` raises the exact live-confirmed `RuntimeError` text for the `PL` position only (so `DS1`'s own insert in the same pack is the control: it must still succeed). **Red** (fix reverted via `git stash` on `process_pack_jobs.py` alone, test file left in place): `2 FAILURE(S)` - the raced position wrote nothing AND `DS1` (the non-racing position in the same pack) was also silently dropped that cycle (confirming the over-broad blast radius above), plus the predicted false `system_alerts` "error" entry, verbatim. **Green** (fix restored): `ALL PASSED` - `DS1` writes fine, `PL` is skipped with no alert. Full regression confirmed unaffected: `test_process_pack_jobs.py` (`0 failure(s)`), `test_pdf_merge.py` (including its own `test_sync_position_suggestions_skips_a_tender_closed_real_yesterday()` - still `0 failure(s)`, proving the new check doesn't touch the closed-tender skip path), `test_assemble_pack.py`, `test_pack_suggestions.py`, `test_adapt_company.py` - all `ALL PASSED`/`0 failure(s)`. `python3 -m py_compile engine/pack/process_pack_jobs.py engine/pack/test_sync_functions.py` - clean.

**Pushed directly to `main` (no PR).** Same class as Finding 278: a small, self-contained Python-only fix inside one function's own exception handling, no schema/migration change, no RLS, no money, no worker-image change, no multi-table RPC surface, and explicitly NOT a tenant-isolation/authorization-bypass finding, so the "PR, never direct push, regardless of diff size" rule for that class does not apply here. `git fetch origin main` immediately before pushing: still `d3564d8`, matching this pass's own orientation step exactly - no sibling-track commit landed during this pass.

### Finding 281 (CONFIRMED AND FIXED ON `main` - low/moderate, a genuine feature-completeness bug, not tenant-isolation - a fresh angle: a page/feature directory with zero prior findings against it by name, found by the mention-count technique on `app/app/**`, then checked with the same "does the real production family value match what this one file assumes" lens Finding 115/the Klipcorp sweep already established for the SANRAL-vs-RRM distinction elsewhere)

**Where:** `app/app/sanral-schedules/page.tsx` - the dedicated "SANRAL schedules" front-door page (its own header doc comment: "the sidebar nav item points to... a jump straight to the real action on whichever SANRAL tender the company is working on").

**How this was found.** The task brief's own first fresh direction: pick a route directory named zero times in either standing doc's history. `grep -c` across `docs/specs/System-Status.md`/`QA-Edge-Case-Findings.md` for every `app/app/*` directory name turned up `sanral-schedules` at 31/0 - the only route with real standing-doc presence (31, from the two prior UI-only commits this file has: `a6d293d`/`bd1a2b4`/`c39cbc0`) but literally zero QA findings ever opened against it by name. Read the file end to end.

**The real bug.** The page's own tender query is `supabase.from("tenders").select(...).eq("family", SANRAL_CONVENTIONAL_FAMILY)` - `SANRAL_CONVENTIONAL_FAMILY = "Conventional Consultant Tender"` (`app/lib/tenderCompliance.ts`). But this is only ONE of the two real SANRAL template families this exact automation serves: `app/app/tenders/[id]/page.tsx`'s own `isSanralPackFamily = isSanralFamily || tenderFacts?.family === "RRM Consultant Tender"` (comment: "The submission pack runs the SANRAL fill engines, which handle both SANRAL template families... not other buyers") gates the identical `showSubmissionPack`/"Fill SANRAL schedules" flow on EITHER family, `engine/pack/assemble_pack.py`'s `FILLERS` dict has an entry for both, `engine/pack/process_pack_jobs.py` and `engine/intake/classify_tender.py` both define their own `SANRAL_FAMILIES = ("Conventional Consultant Tender", "RRM Consultant Tender")`, and `app/lib/pastSubmissionReuse.ts` already names the exact pairing as a reusable constant: `SANRAL_PACK_FAMILIES = ["Conventional Consultant Tender", "RRM Consultant Tender"]` (comment: "SANRAL tenders carry no buyer text; both pack families are SANRAL's"). A prior pass's own Klipcorp-fixture sweep (`QA-Edge-Case-Findings.md` ~line 989) already confirmed, by reading `compliance-data.ts`/`submission-pack.tsx`/`page.tsx`, that every OTHER SANRAL-gated surface correctly includes the RRM family - this page's own filter was simply never checked against that same list, and didn't.

**Impact, honestly scoped.** Not a security or tenant-isolation bug - RLS is unaffected, no data is exposed or hidden across companies. The effect is a silent feature-completeness gap on a page Sarel's own brief explicitly asked to be built to make this automation "a clearly visible, premium feature": a company actively filling an RRM Consultant Tender's SANRAL schedules via the ordinary Tender Workspace flow (same button, same engine, same `pack_generation_jobs` row) would see that tender nowhere on its own feature's dedicated front door - either missing from the list entirely (if it also has other, Conventional-family tenders showing) or landing on the "No SANRAL tenders yet" empty state outright (if RRM is the only SANRAL-family tender the company has), even while mid-fill on that exact tender elsewhere in the app. The empty-state copy itself ("bidding on a SANRAL conventional-consultant tender") reinforced the same narrower assumption and is fixed alongside the query.

**Fix.** Changed the query to `.in("family", SANRAL_PACK_FAMILIES)`, importing the existing canonical constant from `app/lib/pastSubmissionReuse.ts` (the one place this exact pairing is already named) instead of duplicating a second, narrower family list or redefining a local one. Updated the empty-state copy to name both families. Added a standing-review comment on the page's own header explaining the gap and the fix, in the file's own existing documentation convention.

**Verified.** `npm run typecheck` (`next typegen && tsc --noEmit`) - 0 errors. `npm run lint` - 0 errors, the same 3 pre-existing warnings this doc's own baseline has documented for 30+ consecutive passes, unchanged. `npx vitest run` - **612 passed, 75 files**, 0 failures, matching the documented baseline exactly (no regression; this fix touches no function any spec file exercises). `npx next build` - compiled successfully, `/sanral-schedules` still partial-prerenders as before, no new route error. No live-Postgres reproduction built: this is a single-file, single-line `.eq` -> `.in` query-filter change against a constant already defined and already proven correct for this exact purpose by three other call sites (`flowOf()`'s own `SANRAL_PACK_FAMILIES.includes()` check, `isSanralPackFamily`, `SANRAL_FAMILIES` on both Python engines) - not a claim needing an independent live repro the way a security/client-trust finding would.

**Pushed directly to `main` (no PR).** UI-only, single-file query-filter fix plus one copy string - no schema/migration/RLS change, no money path, no worker-image change, no multi-table RPC surface, and explicitly not a tenant-isolation/authorization-bypass finding (RLS was already, and remains, the only real boundary; this changes which ALREADY-visible-to-the-company rows a `.eq`/`.in` clause additionally includes), so the "PR, never direct push" rule for that most-severe class does not apply here. `git fetch origin main` immediately before pushing: still `b1e2b71`, matching this pass's own orientation step exactly - no sibling-track commit landed during this pass.

To verify independently: read `app/app/sanral-schedules/page.tsx`'s `.in("family", SANRAL_PACK_FAMILIES)` against `app/lib/pastSubmissionReuse.ts`'s own `SANRAL_PACK_FAMILIES` export and `app/app/tenders/[id]/page.tsx`'s `isSanralPackFamily`; seed one `tenders` row with `family = 'RRM Consultant Tender'` and a matching `tender_packs` row, confirm it now appears on `/sanral-schedules` (it did not before this fix).

### Finding 282 (CONFIRMED AND FIXED ON `main` - low, a second live instance of Finding 281's own family-list-drift bug class, same root cause (SANRAL_CONVENTIONAL_FAMILY checked alone instead of SANRAL_PACK_FAMILIES), different file and different symptom - not tenant-isolation)

**Where:** `app/app/pipeline/page.tsx` - the "Bids" pipeline board's own per-card Pack health computation (the `packHealths` block, feature item 2, Sarel's own ask: "replace all '-' dashes").

**How this was found.** Took up the task brief's own fresh direction to apply pass `ll`'s (Finding 281's) lens - "does a feature's own front-door/dedicated page use the SAME filter/family list as the rest of the app's logic for the same concept, or did it drift?" - to other dedicated pages, starting with `/pipeline` (one of the brief's own named candidates). Read `lib/pipeline.ts` (the canonical stage constants) first, then `app/app/pipeline/page.tsx` end to end. The page's main tender query and its "no pack yet -> found column" branch (`t.family === GENERAL_FAMILY` as the only exclusion) are both negation-based and already correctly include RRM by construction - no drift there. But the separate `packHealths` block (computing each `assessing`/`building` card's readiness score) is a positive, enumerated `if (c.family === SANRAL_CONVENTIONAL_FAMILY) {...} else if (c.family === GENERAL_FAMILY) {...}` chain with no third branch - the exact shape Finding 281 found on `sanral-schedules/page.tsx`.

**Chasing whether this was really a NEW bug, not just Finding 281's already-covered ground again.** Before concluding this was live, checked whether `tenders/[id]/page.tsx`'s own `tenderReadiness`/`DisqualificationGuard` (gated on the narrower `isSanralFamily`, not `isSanralPackFamily`, at lines 470/520) was ALSO a live instance of this class - it is not: `compliance-data.ts`'s own `loadTenderCompliance()` (read directly) has its own, deeper `if (family !== SANRAL_CONVENTIONAL_FAMILY) return { mapped: false, family }` early-return, so widening `tenders/[id]/page.tsx`'s gate to `isSanralPackFamily` would not change its outcome for an RRM tender - `loadPackReviewSnapshot()` would still come back `mapped: false` either way, and `tenderReadiness` would still end up `null`. This is NOT a hidden gap: it is exactly the already-documented, honest "RRM Consultant Tender... has no mandatory-item concept anywhere in this codebase yet - reported `mapped:false` and skipped" state this file's own 2026-10-27 Phase 6 digest entry (~line 23618) already names explicitly. **Correction to the standing record, not a new item:** Finding 281's own write-up (above) states this exact `compliance-data.ts` "correctly includes the RRM family", citing the 2026-10-27 Klipcorp-fixture sweep (`QA-Edge-Case-Findings.md` ~line 989) as having confirmed it - re-reading that sweep's own text shows it actually only confirmed the OPPOSITE (`loadTenderCompliance` "returns `{mapped: false}` immediately for any other family", i.e. for RRM too, same as any non-mapped family) and conflated that with `page.tsx`'s own, separate `showSubmissionPack`/`isSanralPackFamily` gate (which DOES correctly include RRM) in one loosely-worded sentence. `compliance-data.ts` has never mapped RRM; this is a real, already-known, deliberately-accepted product gap (no RRM-specific Mandatory Administration Criteria list has been built), not something either pass needs to fix - flagging only so a future pass doesn't repeat Finding 281's own misreading of it as "confirmed correct" when the actual confirmed fact was the opposite.

**The real, live bug.** Unlike `tenderReadiness` above, `pipeline/page.tsx`'s `packHealths` block calls `loadPackReviewSnapshot()` **only inside the `c.family === SANRAL_CONVENTIONAL_FAMILY` branch** - for a card whose family is `"RRM Consultant Tender"`, NEITHER branch matches, so the function falls through to the bare `return null;` at the end, exactly the same "fall through to `readiness = null`" failure mode this block's own comment already names and already fixed once for GENERAL's pre-extraction case (2026-10-30, re-reviewing PR #172). `PackHealthBadge` renders a `null` health as a literal, unstyled `<span>-</span>` - the exact "bare '-' dash" this whole feature (item 2) was built to replace. Confirmed reachable: an RRM Consultant Tender reaches `assessing`/`building` the same way a Conventional one does (via `moveTenderStage`/the SANRAL submission-pack automation, both already gated on the RRM-inclusive `isSanralPackFamily` elsewhere), so a company actively building an RRM tender's SANRAL schedules sees a blank Pack-health cell on its own Bids board for that exact card, with every OTHER card on the same board showing a real chip.

**Impact, honestly scoped.** Not tenant-isolation, RLS-unaffected, no data exposure - purely a UI-completeness regression on the one column this feature's own design brief explicitly called out ("replace all '-' dashes"). Low severity: the tender remains fully visible and workable (title, buyer, stage, action link, economics form are all family-agnostic and render correctly); only the Pack-health badge itself goes blank.

**Fix.** Widened the branch condition from `c.family === SANRAL_CONVENTIONAL_FAMILY` to `c.family && SANRAL_PACK_FAMILIES.includes(c.family)`, importing the existing canonical constant from `app/lib/pastSubmissionReuse.ts` (the same constant Finding 281 used, not a third hand-written family list). This routes an RRM card through the exact same `loadPackReviewSnapshot()` call the Conventional branch already makes; since `compliance-data.ts` genuinely has no mapped returnables for RRM (see above), the snapshot comes back `mapped: false` and the card now correctly gets the `NOT_STARTED` ("Workspace not started - click to begin") chip - the same honest "known, not blank" state GENERAL's own pre-extraction case already gets, rather than a bare dash. Swapped the now-unused `SANRAL_CONVENTIONAL_FAMILY` import for `SANRAL_PACK_FAMILIES` (no other reference to the old import remained in this file, confirmed by grep before removing it) and rewrote the block's own stale comment (which incorrectly asserted "for SANRAL it can't actually happen here") to name the real, now-handled RRM case and cross-reference this finding and Finding 281's own family-list-drift class.

**Verified, including an independent logic-level red/green reproduction** (this exact branch has no existing unit-test seam of its own - `pipeline/page.tsx` is a server-component page, same "can't itself be unit-tested" constraint `pipelineCardHelpers.ts` was split out for, and this particular conditional isn't inside that split-out pure-function file). Wrote a standalone, dependency-free reproduction of the two branches' real logic (mirroring the file's own structure and `compliance-data.ts`'s own real `family !== SANRAL_CONVENTIONAL_FAMILY` gate) in the scratchpad: pre-fix, an RRM family card resolves to `null` (bare dash) while Conventional is unaffected (`SCORED`); post-fix, RRM resolves to `NOT_STARTED` (the chip) and Conventional is still unaffected - confirmed by running both versions directly, output captured. `npm run typecheck` (`next typegen && tsc --noEmit`) - 0 errors. `npm run lint` - 0 errors, the same 3 pre-existing warnings this doc's own baseline has documented for 30+ consecutive passes, unchanged. `npx vitest run` - **612 passed, 75 files**, 0 failures, exactly matching the documented baseline (no regression; this fix touches no function any spec file exercises - `pipelineCardHelpers.spec.ts`'s own 8 tests, covering `packHealthStatusFromReadiness`/`primaryActionLabel`, are unaffected since those are only called AFTER this branch already resolves `mapped: true`). `rm -rf .next && npx next build` - compiled successfully, `/pipeline` still partial-prerenders as before, no new route error.

**Pushed directly to `main` (no PR).** UI-only, single-file condition-widening fix plus an import swap and a comment rewrite - no schema/migration/RLS change, no money path, no worker-image change, no multi-table RPC surface, and explicitly not a tenant-isolation/authorization-bypass finding (RLS is unaffected either way; this only changes which already-visible-to-the-company card gets a real badge instead of a blank one), so the "PR, never direct push, regardless of diff size" rule for that most-severe class does not apply here. `git fetch origin main` immediately before pushing: re-confirmed still `280153c`, matching this pass's own orientation step exactly - no sibling-track commit landed during this pass.

To verify independently: read `app/app/pipeline/page.tsx`'s `packHealths` block's `if (c.family && SANRAL_PACK_FAMILIES.includes(c.family))` against `app/lib/pastSubmissionReuse.ts`'s own `SANRAL_PACK_FAMILIES` export; seed one `tenders` row with `family = 'RRM Consultant Tender'` and a matching `tender_packs` row at `pipeline_stage = 'building'`, confirm its `/pipeline` board card now shows the "Workspace not started" chip instead of a bare "-" (it did before this fix).

### Finding 283 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, minor-to-moderate, test-infrastructure - `engine/worker/fake_supabase.py`, the in-memory Supabase stand-in `test_poll_loop.py` uses to prove the worker loop really works, silently dropped the `order=` query parameter and always returned rows in plain INSERTION order instead - a real, demonstrable divergence from the real PostgREST behaviour the actual job-queue code depends on for FIFO processing, undetectable by any existing test since none of them queue more than one 'requested' row at a time)

**Area:** `engine/worker/fake_supabase.py` (`_parse_filters()`, new `_parse_order()`, `do_GET()`). Test coverage added to `engine/worker/test_poll_loop.py` (1 new test, `test_fake_supabase_honours_order_requested_at_asc()`; `job()`'s own helper extended with a `requested_at` parameter to support it).

**How this was found.** This cycle's rotation landed on worker/job-queue. Surveyed the area by mention count - `fake_supabase.py` (7 mentions, 144 lines) was by far the least-covered file, against `poll_loop.py` (90), `run_bridges.py` (140), and the five `process_*_jobs.py` bridges (93-315 each). Read it in full: a narrowly-scoped, already well-documented in-memory PostgREST stand-in, used ONLY by `test_poll_loop.py` to prove the worker loop genuinely re-polls over real sleeps. Its own `_parse_filters()` only recognises `eq.`/`is.null` filter values and explicitly skips the `select` query param - but silently ignored `order` too, neither skipping it on purpose nor acting on it: an `order=col.asc`/`order=col.desc` parameter was simply never added to the filters dict (since its value doesn't start with `eq.` or equal `is.null`), so it had NO effect on the returned rows at all - they came back in whatever order `fake.tables[table]` happened to hold them (insertion order), not sorted by the named column.

**Why this matters, concretely.** Grepped the real caller this fake server stands in for, `engine/cv/process_cv_jobs.py`, for its own queue-read query: `supabase_request_all(url, key, "generated_cvs?status=eq.requested&select=*&order=requested_at.asc")` - the real worker explicitly asks for, and depends on, oldest-job-first FIFO ordering. Every existing test in `test_poll_loop.py` only ever queues a single 'requested' row at a time (confirmed by reading every `fake.insert("generated_cvs", ...)` call site in the file), so this gap had zero effect on any CURRENT test's pass/fail result - but it meant a real regression in the production code's own ordering (e.g. a future edit that dropped the `order=requested_at.asc` clause, or broke FIFO some other way) would sail through this entire test file with nothing to catch it, since the fake server's own behaviour didn't actually depend on that clause being correct either.

**Confirmed live, not inferred.** Built a direct reproduction: inserted two 'requested' `generated_cvs` rows into a real `FakeSupabase` instance, deliberately out of `requested_at` order (the NEWER row inserted FIRST), then issued the real, unmodified `process_cv_jobs.supabase_request_all()` call with the real `order=requested_at.asc` query string the production code sends. Pre-fix: returned `["newer-job", "older-job"]` - plain insertion order, the opposite of what was asked for. Post-fix: `["older-job", "newer-job"]` - correctly sorted.

**Fix.** Added `_parse_order(query)`, parsing PostgREST's own `order=col.asc`/`order=col.desc` syntax (bare `col` with no suffix defaults to ascending, matching real PostgREST), and wired it into `do_GET()`: after the existing `_match()` filtering, sort the matched rows by the named column (nulls grouped together via a `(is_none, value)` sort key, so two null rows never attempt a `None` ordering comparison against each other). `_parse_filters()` now explicitly skips `order` (alongside the existing `select` skip) so it's never mistaken for an unsupported literal filter value.

**Verified red-then-green.** Added `test_fake_supabase_honours_order_requested_at_asc()` to `test_poll_loop.py`, same plain-assertion style as every other test in the file, reusing the real `job()` helper (extended with a `requested_at` parameter, default unchanged for every existing call site) and the real `process_cv_jobs.supabase_request_all()` call - not a reimplementation of the query. **Red:** saved the diff to `fake_supabase.py` only, `git apply -R`, re-ran `python3 engine/worker/test_poll_loop.py` directly - failed exactly as predicted (`AssertionError: ['newer', 'older']`), every earlier test in the file's own run order still passing up to that point. **Green:** `git apply` to reapply, re-ran - `All bridge-loop smoke tests passed`, new test included. Regression: `python3 -m py_compile` on both touched files (clean); the two other real consumers of `fake_supabase.py` - `engine/onboarding/test_process_onboarding_jobs.py` and `engine/alerts/test_system_alerts.py` - both re-run directly, both `0 failure(s)`, unaffected (neither relies on GET ordering from this fake server).

**Severity: minor-to-moderate, test-infrastructure only.** No production code was touched - this is a safety-net correctness fix for the test double itself, closing a gap that could have hidden a real future regression in the worker's own FIFO job ordering, not a bug in anything currently shipped.

**Not escalated to a PR.** Small, safe, self-contained Python fix to one test-only helper module plus its own test file - no production code, no RLS, no migration, no money path, no worker-image change. Pushed directly to `main`.

**Backlog status.** No new backlog items opened by this fix. `git fetch origin main` immediately before starting (clean, `main` at `b58e842`, matching the task brief's own stated current state) and again immediately before pushing this commit, both clean - no sibling commit landed in between.

To verify independently: from `engine/worker/`, `python3 test_poll_loop.py` (expect `All bridge-loop smoke tests passed`, including the new order-honouring test's own `PASS` line). `python3 -m py_compile fake_supabase.py test_poll_loop.py` (clean).

### Finding 284 (OPENED AS A PR, NOT PUSHED TO `main` - moderate-to-severe, genuine document-correctness/compliance gap on the general (non-SANRAL) pack pipeline - a company's real answer to a legal declaration question (SBD1/4/6.1/8/9) can be silently left BLANK in the actual submitted `.docx`, because this buyer's specific edition's wording didn't match what `fill_sbd_docx.py` looks for, with NO warning anywhere a company would actually look: not on the generated pack's own checklist, not in the printed Completion Guide, and not on the Tender Workspace's pre-generation Pack Review screen)

**Area:** `engine/general/build_general_pack.py` (new `_edition_mismatches()`, its call site in the `editable_docs` loop, `write_guide()`). Test coverage added to `engine/general/test_build_general_pack.py` (2 new tests) and `engine/general/test_general_bridge.py` (1 existing assertion widened, 1 new assertion added, against this suite's own real downloaded DSTI sample document - see below).

**How this was found.** This pass's own fresh direction (not a repeat of an exhausted angle): read `engine/pack/pdf_merge.py` as a first-class target per the task brief, then followed its own "checklist is the real post-generation source of truth, mirrored in `app/app/tenders/[id]/pack-checklist.tsx`'s own header comment" into the general (non-SANRAL) pack pipeline specifically, since that pipeline has its own, separate `write_guide()`/Completion Guide mechanism `pdf_merge.py` itself doesn't know about. Traced `fill_sbd_docx.py` (the general pipeline's own SBD1/4/6.1/8/9 docx filler) end to end against `build_general_pack.py`'s own three consumers of its output: the pack's checklist/contents page, the printed Completion Guide, and (via `field_provenance`) the Tender Workspace's pre-generation Pack Review screen.

**The real bug, traced to its root, not assumed.** `fill_sbd_docx.py`'s own header comment is explicit and already correct about WHY this exists: "SBD1/4/6.1 are genuinely common across buyers... but are NOT byte-identical - exact section numbers and legal wording differ between buyers," so it matches fields by LABEL TEXT, never by fixed position - meaning a label match can genuinely fail for one specific buyer's edition even when the company HAS answered the question. The module's own real code already anticipates this and logs it correctly: every one of its `log.missing()` calls for exactly this case (`_log_fill()`'s own default, the SBD4/SBD6.1/SBD8 per-question loops) produces a `field_provenance` row with `status: "missing"` and a reason mentioning "edition" (`"Label not found in this buyer's edition - fill by hand."`, `"Declaration not found in this edition - answer by hand."`, `"...but the question wasn't found in this edition - mark it by hand."`, etc.) - correctly distinct from a TRUE data gap (`"No vat registration number on file..."`) and from a deliberately-always-missing sentinel (`"...signature and date - never typed in advance."`, which fires regardless of edition).

The problem is what happens to that correct signal downstream, in `build_general_pack.py`, which never reads it:
1. **`form_results[code] = {"status": "filled"}`** was set unconditionally whenever `fill_sbd_docx.fill_sbd_file()` returned without raising - which it always does once the `.docx` loads and saves, regardless of how many individual field labels inside it actually matched. A form where every single declaration question failed to match this buyer's wording still showed "filled."
2. **The pack's own checklist/contents page** (`sections.append({...})` for a docx-filled form) never carried a `"warning"` key at all - so `pdf_merge.py`'s own, already-correct, already-tested warning machinery (used elsewhere for an expired vault document) had nothing to act on; the section always showed plain "Included," never "Included - WARNING."
3. **`write_guide()`'s own per-field table** (`guide_rows(code, ctx)`) independently RE-DERIVES each field's value straight from `ctx["answers"]`/the company record - it has no idea what `fill_sbd_docx.py` actually managed to place in the real `.docx`. For the exact field that failed to match, the printed Completion Guide showed the company's real "Yes"/"No" answer, under a bold "(filled)" heading, with **zero caveat** - the guide a company is told to read first ("Forms marked 'filled' are already completed in this pack") actively vouches for a value that was never actually typed into the document sitting right behind it.
4. **The Tender Workspace's own pre-generation Pack Review screen** (`general-pack-review-logic.ts`'s `answerStatus()`) computes "confirmed" purely from whether `tender_answers` has a value - its own header comment states the design rationale as "general tenders have no provenance/assumed-default machinery - field_provenance is SANRAL-only." That comment is independently confirmed stale here (Finding 190, 2026-11-07, already noted this exact sentence is "now stale/incorrect," since `process_general_jobs.py` has upserted real `field_provenance` rows for general packs since the general engine's first commit) - but Finding 190's own conclusion that this was merely "a documentation inaccuracy... not a functional divergence worth its own finding" did not go on to check whether ANY of the general pack's real display surfaces actually uses that data for its stated purpose. They don't, for any of the three: pre-generation review, post-generation checklist, or the printed guide.

**Confirmed live with a direct reproduction, not inferred.** Built a buyer SBD4 `.docx` (python-docx, a table-based `YES/NO` layout matching `answer_yes_no()`'s own real matching shapes) with the first two of the three SBD4 declarations phrased exactly as `fill_sbd_docx.py` expects, and the third ("Does any of the bidder's directors hold a stake in a connected business concern?") phrased differently - a realistic buyer variant of the same PPR2022 declaration. With `ctx["answers"]["sbd4.interest_in_related_enterprise"] = "yes"` (a real company answer on file), ran the real, unmodified `fill_sbd_docx.fill_sbd_document()`: the resulting `field_provenance` entry for that key is `status=missing, reason="Declaration not found in this edition - answer by hand."` - correct. `fill_sbd_file()` raised no exception. The REAL filled `.docx`'s own row for that declaration still reads the bare buyer-printed `"YES/NO"` - nothing was ever typed onto it. `guide_rows("4", ctx)`'s own row for this exact question, pre-fix, returns `('Interest in any other related enterprise, bidding or not?', 'Yes', None)` - the real answer, no note, under a `(filled)` heading.

**Confirmed a SECOND time, independently, against a real downloaded government document already in this repo (not just the synthetic repro above).** `templates/general_samples/dsti_rfq15/0) SBD FORMS.docx` - a real DSTI (Department of Science, Technology and Innovation) RFQ bundle, already used by `engine/general/test_general_bridge.py`'s own end-to-end fixture - genuinely has no matching "Designation"/signatory name/address wording for `sbd4.designation_footer`/`sbd6_1.signatory_name`/`sbd6_1.signatory_address`, even for a test company (`co2`) with a real signatory and a real `registered_address` on file. Before this fix, `test_general_bridge.py`'s own existing checklist assertion (step 6, the expired-TCS-PIN-letter test) never noticed this - it only ever checked for exactly one `included_warning` row (the PIN), because nothing else in the pipeline ever produced a second one, on a REAL buyer document that was sitting in this repo's own fixtures the entire time.

**Severity, honestly scoped.** Not tenant-isolation, not RLS, no cross-company exposure. But the blast radius is real and the consequence is more severe than most "presentation" findings this track has logged: SBD4/SBD8/SBD9 are sworn legal declarations (bidder's disclosure, past-practice declaration, independent-bid-determination certificate) - a company that answered honestly on the Tender Workspace, saw "filled," read the Completion Guide's own table confirming the value, and signed, could submit a bid with a legally material declaration question left blank on the actual document a buyer evaluates, with no warning at any single point in the product's own review flow. This is exactly the product's own "Fix: disqualification risks... with a one-line reason" promise (`app/AGENTS.md`) failing silently for the one class of field where it matters most.

**Fix (engine side, this PR).** `build_general_pack.py` gained `_edition_mismatches(entries)` - a small, pure function distinguishing a genuine edition-mismatch `missing` entry (reason mentions "edition" together with "not found"/"wasn't found"/"couldn't find" - the exact, already-consistent wording every real case in `fill_sbd_docx.py` uses, confirmed by reading every one of its `log.missing()` call sites directly, not guessed) from a true data gap or an always-missing sentinel (neither ever mentions "edition"). The `editable_docs` loop now calls it on the slice of `log.entries` added by that specific `fill_sbd_docx.fill_sbd_file()` call, and when it finds any: (1) sets a real `"warning"` on that form's own pack section, so `pdf_merge.py`'s own existing, already-tested checklist/contents-page warning machinery picks it up for free, with no change to that file at all; (2) records the affected field keys on `form_results[code]["edition_mismatches"]`, which `write_guide()` now reads to add a bold, red, explicit paragraph under that form's own heading - "NOT ACTUALLY TYPED IN, even though this form is marked 'filled'... write it in by hand before signing" - naming the exact field(s), rather than silently repeating the value with no caveat.

**Deliberately scoped OUT of this PR, and why:** the Tender Workspace's own pre-generation `general-pack-review-data.ts`/`general-pack-review-logic.ts` (`answerStatus()`) is NOT changed here. Fixing it correctly is tractable (confirmed: `requirements.py`'s own question-key namespace, e.g. `"sbd4.interest_in_related_enterprise"`, is IDENTICAL to `fill_sbd_docx.py`'s own `field_provenance.field_key` namespace - a clean join, not a guess) but requires a NEW `field_provenance` query scoped to an already-generated pack, a new cross-reference against `tender_answers`/company fields (an "answered, but marked missing on the real generated pack" condition precisely mirroring `_edition_mismatches()`'s own logic in TypeScript), and a UI change to a screen three other findings already touch - a materially larger, separate TypeScript change this PR keeps out rather than bundling in. Recorded below as a standing item for a future pass or Sarel's own call, with the exact join confirmed so it isn't re-derived from scratch.

### Finding 285 (OPENED AS A PR, NOT PUSHED TO `main` - the Finding 284 standing follow-up, picked up with full rigor rather than assumed trivial: the Tender Workspace's own pre-generation/re-review Pack Review screen for general tenders can still show an SBD-declaration question as fully "Confirmed" even when the real, already-generated pack's own `field_provenance` says that exact declaration was never actually placed into this buyer's specific document edition)

**Area:** `app/app/tenders/[id]/general-pack-review-logic.ts` (new `questionAnswerStatus()`), `app/app/tenders/[id]/general-pack-review-data.ts` (new `field_provenance` read, gated on an existing `tender_packs` row for this company/tender, wired into the questions loop only). Test coverage added to `app/app/tenders/[id]/general-pack-review-logic.test.ts` (8 new cases).

Per this track's own brief ("don't assume it's trivial just because it's already scoped... treat it with the same rigor as a new finding - test it, verify the join, etc."), the join was re-verified from scratch rather than taken on Finding 284's word: read `engine/general/fill_sbd_docx.py` end to end for every `log.confirmed()`/`log.missing()`/`log.assumed_default()` call site, cross-referenced each key against `engine/general/requirements.py`'s own manifest-building code (`SBD4_QUESTIONS`/`SBD8_QUESTIONS`/the SBD1 `questions` list), and against `app/lib/generalTender.ts`'s `questionStates()` (`a = answers.find((x) => x.field_key === q.key)` - the exact same `q.key` this screen renders).

**The join holds for questions, exactly as Finding 284 said - confirmed, not assumed - but does NOT hold for company fields, which Finding 284 never actually checked (a real gap in its own "confirmed-clean" claim, corrected here before building on it).** Every SBD-declaration question key (`"sbd4.employed_by_state"`, `"sbd4.relationship_with_employee"`, `"sbd4.interest_in_related_enterprise"`, `"sbd8.restricted_supplier"`, `"sbd8.tender_defaulter"`, `"sbd8.convicted"`, `"sbd8.contract_terminated"`, `"sbd1.accredited_representative"`, `"sbd1.foreign_based"`) is used, byte-identical, as both `requirements.py`'s own manifest `questions[].key` (what `tender_answers.field_key` this screen reads) AND the exact string `fill_sbd_docx.py` passes to `log.confirmed()`/`log.missing()`/`log.assumed_default()` (what `field_provenance.field_key` ends up as) - a genuinely clean, direct join, confirmed by reading every one of the ~15 real call sites, not by trusting the shared naming convention on sight. But `requirements.py`'s separate `COMPANY_FIELDS` list (`"company.telephone"`, `"company.cellphone"`, `"company.email"`, `"company.cidb_grading"`) - the OTHER consumer of `answerStatus()` in this same section, `general-pack-review-data.ts`'s `companyFieldStates()` loop - uses a completely different key namespace from what `fill_sbd_docx.py` logs for the same underlying data (`"sbd1.cellphone_number"`, `"sbd1.email_address"`, etc., not `"company.cellphone"`/`"company.email"`). A naive "just join on field_key everywhere `answerStatus()` is called" implementation would either silently find nothing for company fields (harmless but pointless) or, worse, require a hand-built key-mapping table invented for this fix alone, with its own risk of a wrong pairing. **Scoped this fix to the questions loop only, where the join is real; left `companyFieldStates()` untouched, with this distinction now documented in `general-pack-review-logic.ts`'s own header comment so a future pass doesn't have to re-derive it.**

### Finding 287 (CONFIRMED AND FIXED ON `main` - moderate, a sibling instance of Finding 72's own already-confirmed bug class, in a file that bug class had never been checked against before)

**Where:** `app/lib/personCredentials.ts`'s `registrationsAskedFor()` - its own local `open(closing)`
gate, which decides whether a tender's own professional-registration demand (ECSA, SACPCMP, SACNASP,
SAGC, SACAP, SACPLAN, SACQSP, SACPVP, PSIRA) counts at all, per the function's own header comment:
"Only tenders still open (or with no closing date) count."

**What was tested:** this pass's own chosen angle (per the task brief's direction (b),
cross-file consistency) was "does every place that computes `is this tender's deadline in the
past` agree?" - every `new Date(...).getTime() < Date.now()`-style check across `app/app/*`
(`pipeline/page.tsx`'s own `isPast()`, `admin/tenders/TenderCatalogRow.tsx`, `analytics/page.tsx`,
`lib/dispatchTriage.ts`) does real `Date`-object comparison, and `lib/discoveredTendersDigest.ts`'s
own window filter offloads the comparison to Postgres itself (`closing_date.gte.<iso>` in a
PostgREST filter string, which Postgres parses and compares as a real timestamptz, not a string).
`personCredentials.ts`'s own `open()` was the one outlier found doing the comparison as a plain
JavaScript string compare: `const nowIso = new Date().toISOString(); const open = (closing) =>
!closing || closing >= nowIso;`.

**Finding (CONFIRMED, moderate).** `tenders.closing_date` is a `timestamptz` (migration `0001`),
and this exact column is already independently confirmed (Finding 72, `engine/compliance/
watch_deadlines.py`) to genuinely carry two different ISO-8601 offset conventions in real data:
`gov_sources.py`'s `iso_sast()` and `process_general_jobs.py`'s own SANRAL-intake write tag the
value `"+02:00"` (SAST); `watch_tender_updates.apply_closing_date()` writes a raw OCDS feed's own
UTC-tagged value. `new Date().toISOString()` always produces a `"Z"`-suffixed UTC string. Comparing
an offset-tagged ISO string against a `"Z"`-tagged one with a plain `>=` is NOT equivalent to real
chronological comparison - exactly Finding 72's own root cause, just in a different file/column
consumer. Reproduced live (Node, the exact pattern Finding 72's own write-up used): a tender
closing `"2026-11-09T01:00:00+02:00"` (01:00 SAST on the 9th, i.e. 23:00 UTC on the 8th - a real
deadline) checked 30 minutes after it actually passed (`now = 2026-11-08T23:30:00.000Z`, i.e.
01:30 SAST on the 9th) came back `open() === true` under the old string-compare code - the tender
reads as still open and its registration demand still counts, half an hour after its real deadline
- while a `Date`-object comparison (`new Date(closing).getTime() >= now.getTime()`) correctly
returns `false`. This is the identical daily 00:00-02:00 SAST window `lib/dates.ts`'s own
`daysUntil()` header comment already documents at length as a recurring host-TZ/offset-mismatch
bug class in this codebase - just not yet checked against this particular file's own ad-hoc string
gate. Real-world effect: for up to 2 hours after an "+02:00"-tagged tender's own real closing
moment, in the window where the closing clock-time happens to fall between 22:00 and 23:59 UTC the
day before SAST midnight, `registrationsAskedFor()` could keep counting that tender's own
registration demand (e.g. still showing "SACNASP asked for by Contract X" on the People page) for a
tender that has, in real terms, already closed - a stale, no-longer-actionable demand signal, not a
security or tenant-isolation issue (the function itself has no authz/company-scoping gap; `tenders`/
`tender_requirements` are the shared, not-tenant-scoped catalog per 0001's own RLS, confirmed
correct by prior passes).

**Fix.** `open()` now parses `closing` as a real `Date` and compares `.getTime()` values (`nowMs =
Date.now()`, captured at the same point in the function `nowIso` used to be, preserving the
existing "only after the request-time reads above, since Cache Components refuses a current-time
value before any dynamic data access" ordering) instead of comparing ISO strings. An unparseable
`closing_date` (`NaN`) reads as still open, the same "never a confident wrong answer" direction
`isPast()`/`daysUntil()` already use elsewhere in this codebase, not a silent exclusion.

**Verified, not asserted.** Live red/green repro (Node, mirroring the fix exactly): 6 cases -
the SAST-midnight-rollover case (above), a clearly-future SAST-offset closing, a clearly-past
SAST-offset closing, a null closing date, a clearly-future UTC-`"Z"`-tagged closing, and a
UTC-`"+00:00"`-tagged closing 1 minute in the past. Old string-compare code: wrong (`open=true`)
on the SAST-rollover case only, correct on the other 5. New `Date`-compare code: correct on all 6,
including the rollover case. `npx tsc --noEmit` (whole `app/` project) - 0 errors. `npx eslint
lib/personCredentials.ts` - clean. `npx vitest run` (full suite, from `app/`) - **75 files, 612
tests passed**, no regression (this module has no dedicated `.spec.ts` of its own - the function
is a Supabase-client-driven async read with no existing test harness - so this fix was verified by
the live red/green repro above plus the full suite/typecheck/lint, not a new unit test for an
untestable-in-isolation local closure).

**Regression:** `app/lib/personCredentials.ts` only - one local helper function, 20 lines changed
(mostly a comment explaining the "why", per this track's own convention), no exported signature
change, no call-site change needed (`registrationsAskedFor()`'s own callers are unaffected).

### Finding 288 (CONFIRMED AND FIXED ON `main` - real but narrow-impact: a second, independent
plain-string-compare-against-`now.isoformat()` implementation of "is this closed", in the
national-discovery source Finding 287's own check didn't cover, with a confirmed-live
one-second-wide discrepancy window per tender rather than Finding 72/287's own multi-hour daily
window)

**Where:** `engine/discovery/etenders_national.py`'s `normalize()` - its own `is_closed` field,
computed for every release read from National Treasury's live OCDS API
(`ocds-api.etenders.gov.za`), consumed directly by `discovery/assess_tender.py`'s `read_release()`
(skips the real document fetch entirely and returns `depth: "not_fetched"`,
`confidence: "Document not fetched - this tender's closing date has already passed."` whenever
`is_closed` is true) - a real, scheduled production path, not a one-off CLI script: both
`discovery/watch_new_tenders.py` (the `daily-discovery.yml` workflow, `--sources ocds`) and
`engine/notify/daily_digest.py` (the `daily-digest.yml` workflow) call
`etenders_national.normalize(r)` directly, with no correction layer in between. (`gov_sources.py`'s
own `ocds_to_release()` fallback path - used only when the eTenders *portal* read fails - already
strips `is_closed` from `normalize()`'s output and recomputes it via `source_http.release()`'s
correct `is_past()`-based logic; this Finding is about the two callers that go straight to
`normalize()`'s own output, unfiltered.)

**How this was found - the brief's own first fresh direction, re-checked for a second outlier
after the Finding 287 fix.** The task brief's own point 1 asked, after Finding 287: "verify there
isn't a SECOND outlier doing the same wrong string-compare pattern elsewhere." Grepped the whole
`app/` tree per the brief's own suggestion first (clean - see below), then widened the same
`toISOString()`/string-vs-date-compare pattern search to `engine/*.py` as well, since Finding 72
(the original instance of this exact bug class) already lived in `engine/`, not `app/`. A
`closing_date <=`/`< today`-shaped grep across both trees surfaced exactly two Python hits besides
Finding 72's own already-fixed file: `engine/pack/process_pack_jobs.py:1092` (`closing_date <
today`, where both sides are real `datetime.date` objects, not strings - confirmed clean by
reading the surrounding code) and `engine/discovery/etenders_national.py:299`
(`closing_date <= now`, where `closing_date` is the OCDS API's own raw string and
`now = datetime.datetime.now().isoformat()` is a second string) - the real second outlier.
Confirmed `app/` itself has no second instance of Finding 287's own pattern: every
`toISOString()` call in `app/` either builds a value to WRITE to a DB column (not a comparison),
feeds a `formatDateTime()`/email-template call, or (`lib/discoveredTendersDigest.ts`) builds a
PostgREST filter string that Postgres itself parses and compares as a real `timestamptz` server-
side - none of them is a second local plain-string `>=`/`<=` compare against
`new Date().toISOString()`.

**Why this looked, at first read, like the same Finding 72/287 bug class - and why it isn't quite,
once checked against the real API rather than assumed.** `source_http.py`'s own `is_past()` (the
already-correct, already-tested helper every OTHER discovery source in this codebase uses for
this exact "is this closed" question, including `etenders_national.py`'s own sibling path through
`gov_sources.ocds_to_release()`) carries the comment `"unknown is not expired - same rule as
etenders_national.normalize()"` - a comment that assumes the two implementations already agree.
They don't: `is_past()` does `parse_sast(value) <= datetime.datetime.now(SAST)` (real aware-
datetime comparison); `etenders_national.normalize()` did `closing_date <= now.isoformat()`
(plain string compare, `now` built from a naive, UTC-valued `datetime.datetime.now()` with no
offset suffix at all). Assumed, before checking, that this would be Finding 72/287's own
multi-hour SAST-offset-rollover bug again (an `"+02:00"`-tagged value compared against a
`"Z"`-tagged one). **Checked the real API live instead of assuming:** fetched 100 real live
releases from the real OCDS endpoint (`GET https://ocds-api.etenders.gov.za/api/OCDSReleases
?dateFrom=2026-10-01&dateTo=2026-11-09&PageNumber=1&PageSize=100`, HTTP 200) and found all 49
distinct `tenderPeriod.endDate` values across them are `"Z"`-tagged UTC - **zero** `"+02:00"`-
offset-tagged values. So the specific SAST-date-rollover failure mode Finding 72/287 both found
does NOT occur in this file's real live data today (confirmed, not assumed: ran both the buggy
string compare and the correct `is_past()` against all 49 real values at the real current time -
**0 mismatches**).

**The real, narrower bug, confirmed by a live repro rather than inferred from the code.** A naive
`datetime.datetime.now().isoformat()` never carries a `"Z"`/offset suffix, and only appends a
`.dddddd` fractional-second suffix when the microsecond component is non-zero. Comparing that
string, character by character, against an OCDS `"...HH:MM:SSZ"` string: for any `now` that falls
within the exact same whole second as the closing instant, the two strings are identical up to
and including `"...:SS"`, and the next character decides the whole comparison - the closing
string's `"Z"` (0x5A) always sorts after the now-string's own next character (either nothing, if
`now`'s microsecond is exactly 0, since a shorter string that is a true prefix of a longer one
sorts before it; or `"."` (0x2E), for any non-zero microsecond) - so `closing_date <= now` reads
**False** (not yet closed) for the *entire one-second window* starting at the real closing
instant, even once the real deadline has already passed. Reproduced directly with a frozen clock
(`FrozenDatetime.now()` patched into `source_http.datetime.datetime`, since `is_past()` reads its
own module's `datetime` reference, not `etenders_national`'s): a release closing at
`"2026-11-10T12:00:00Z"`, evaluated 0.5s after that real instant, read `is_closed=False` under the
pre-fix code (confirmed - this is the real, predicted failure, not a guess) and `is_closed=True`
under `is_past()` (the fix).

**Real-world severity, stated honestly rather than inflated to match Finding 72/287's own
2-hour/day window.** This is a genuine implementation bug (the inline compare is not, despite the
sibling comment's claim, "the same rule" as `is_past()`) and it does sit on a real production path
(`read_release()`'s document-fetch gate, in a workflow that runs **once a day**, per
`daily-discovery.yml`/`daily-digest.yml`). But the live window where it actually produces a wrong
answer is exactly one second per tender's own closing instant, not Finding 72/287's own recurring
multi-hour-every-day window - the odds of a once-daily scheduled run's own wall-clock `now` landing
inside the specific one-second slot any given tender happens to close in are vanishingly small,
and no live OCDS data sampled carries an offset-tagged value that could widen that window the way
Finding 72/287's bug class does elsewhere. Documented and fixed as a genuine correctness/
consistency bug (two implementations of the same rule quietly disagreeing, the cross-file-
consistency class this whole pass was looking for), not escalated to Finding 72/287's own severity
language, since the live reproduction itself shows the practical exposure is not comparable.

**Fix.** Deleted the local `now = datetime.datetime.now().isoformat()` and the inline string
compare; `is_closed` is now `sh.is_past(closing_date)` - the same already-imported
(`import source_http as sh`), already-tested helper every other discovery source already uses,
and the one `gov_sources.ocds_to_release()`'s own fallback path already recomputes with when it
has to. This is a pure simplification toward the existing shared helper, not a new implementation
- `is_past()`'s own `None`-safe, "unknown is not expired" behavior is unchanged from what the old
inline `bool(closing_date and ...)` guard already gave.

**Verified, not asserted.** Red/green with `git stash`: pre-fix code, frozen-clock repro above,
confirmed `is_closed=False` 0.5s after the real deadline (the predicted bug, reproduced exactly);
restored the fix (`git stash pop`), same repro now reads `is_closed=True`. Re-ran the 100-real-live-
release regression check against the FIXED code at the real current time - **0 mismatches** against
the pre-fix code's own output (confirms the fix changes nothing for any of today's real releases,
only the dormant one-second edge case). `python3 -m py_compile` - clean. Existing suites, all exit
0: `discovery/test_etenders_national.py` (`fetch_releases()`'s own 4 cases, ALL PASSED - this file
had no `is_closed`/`endDate` coverage before or after this fix, a real pre-existing test gap noted
here rather than silently left as-is, though adding that coverage was judged out of scope for this
fix itself), `discovery/test_gov_sources.py` (full suite, ALL PASSED, including every
`etenders_national`-adjacent `gov_sources.*`/`source_http.*` case), `discovery/
test_watch_tender_updates.py`, `discovery/test_award_outcomes.py`, `discovery/test_award_prices.py`
(Part 2 skipped, no scratch Postgres - expected, per its own message), `discovery/test_taxonomy.py`
(same), `discovery/test_assess_tender.py` - all exit 0, no regression.

**Fixed directly on `main` - no PR, per the guardrails.** Single-file, Python-only, no schema/RLS/
money/worker-image surface, no authz/tenant-isolation angle (this is a discovery-feed read, not a
per-company/tenant-scoped table), and small (one line changed, plus the comment explaining why).
Not a document a company signs/submits (this track's own PR-for-document-correctness precedent,
Findings 284-286, doesn't apply here - this is upstream discovery metadata, several steps removed
from anything a company ever signs).

**Regression:** `engine/discovery/etenders_national.py`'s `normalize()` only - one field's
computation, no signature change, no call-site change needed.

**Standing note, not a new backlog item:** `discovery/test_etenders_national.py` has no dedicated
`is_closed`/`endDate` test coverage (confirmed above - this pass's own regression checks were a
live-data/frozen-clock repro run in this session, not a permanent addition to that file). Low
urgency - flagging for whichever future pass next touches this file, not opening a new standing
item for it, since the fix itself is already in place and verified.
