### Finding 289 (CONFIRMED AND FIXED ON `main` - the brief's own "displayed number, not the
boolean gate" fresh direction: `lib/dates.ts`'s own `daysUntil()` - the single shared "days until a
tender closes / a document expires" calculation nearly every page and reminder-email trigger in
this app reads from - silently added exactly 1 day to the real calendar-day count for any
`timestamptz` value with a genuine time-of-day, confirmed live across a full-day sweep and already
visible, unnoticed, in a prior pass's own test expectation)

**Where:** `app/lib/dates.ts`'s `daysUntil(dateStr, now)`.

**Task-brief fit.** This is the brief's own first fresh direction, taken literally: "does every
place that computes/displays a tender's own 'days until closing' countdown agree... this is about
the DISPLAYED NUMBER, not the boolean gate." Cross-file consistency checking (this session's own
most productive technique, Findings 72/281/282/284-288) surfaced it: most callers pass a tender's
real `closing_date`/`discovered_opportunities.closing_date` (both `timestamptz`, confirmed via
`supabase/migrations/0001_init_schema.sql:163`/`0072_platform_admin_discovered_opportunities.sql:164`)
or a trial's `trial_ends_at` (`timestamptz`, `0078_company_subscriptions.sql:37`) straight into
`daysUntil()` and render its number directly - but one file, `lib/tenderCompliance.ts`
(`validityAtClosing()`/`sanralConventionalDocumentChecks()`), was already visibly working around a
bug in that same function by pre-converting through `closingDayOf()` first
(`daysUntil(closingDayOf(closingDate))`, with its own inline comment: "calendar day: valid ON the
closing day counts") - a real, live cross-file disagreement between callers that know to defend
against this function's own quirk and the many that don't.

**Root cause, read before assuming severity.** `daysUntil()` derives "today" as the real
Africa/Johannesburg (SAST) calendar day (`now.toLocaleDateString("en-CA", {timeZone:
"Africa/Johannesburg"})`) - correctly fixing an earlier, narrower bug (this function's own header
comment, the 00:00-02:00 SAST rollover case) - but then anchors that day at **UTC midnight**
(`` `${sastYmd}T00:00:00Z` ``) rather than true **SAST midnight** (2 hours earlier in UTC), and
compares the target's raw, un-floored timestamp against that anchor with `Math.ceil()`. UTC
midnight of a SAST calendar day is itself 02:00 SAST - so the only input this ever gave the
"correct" calendar-day count for was one that happened to parse to exactly UTC midnight: a bare
`"YYYY-MM-DD"` date-only string (`new Date("2026-11-09")` = `2026-11-09T00:00:00.000Z` exactly) -
which is every single case in this function's own pre-existing test file
(`lib/dates.test.ts`, confirmed by reading all of them: every one uses `.toISOString().slice(0,
10)` or a bare date string). For ANY real timestamp with an actual time-of-day - i.e. every
`closing_date`/`trial_ends_at` value this app actually stores - the positive sub-day fraction left
over after subtracting the anchor always gets rounded UP by `ceil()`, so the result was the true
calendar-day count **plus exactly 1**, for every tender and every trial on record. The only
exception (frac = 0) would be a value that happens to fall exactly at 02:00 SAST - not a real
closing/trial-end time in practice.

**Live reproduction - full-day sweep around a real closing instant, not a cherry-picked case.**
Copied `daysUntil()` verbatim into a standalone Node script (this session's own scratchpad
directory, never touching the real app or database) for a tender closing `"2026-11-09T10:00:00Z"`
(= 12:00 SAST on the 9th, an ordinary closing hour) and swept `now` every 3 hours from 36h before to
36h after that instant, printing the function's own result, the real `isPast()` truth, and the
label a user would actually see:

```
now (SAST)      daysUntil() really-closed?  label shown
08/11 00:00-21:00    2          false       2 days left   (should be 2 - correct, 2 days out)
09/11 00:00-09:00    1          false       1 day left    (should be 1 - correct, still a day out)
09/11 12:00-21:00    1           true       1 day left    <- WRONG: already closed, shows "1 day left"
10/11 00:00-21:00    0           true       Due today     <- WRONG: closed YESTERDAY, shows "Due today"
11/11 00:00           -1          true       Closed        (only correct from here on)
```

So for roughly 36 hours after a tender's real deadline - its own entire remaining closing day, PLUS
the entire following SAST day - this function kept reporting it as still open ("1 day left", then
"Due today"), not "Closed", wherever a caller displays its raw number with no separate `isPast()`/
`closingCountdown()` override. Confirmed the same, deterministic `+1` pattern independently against
a second, unrelated closing instant and for a trial-end timestamp, not just the one swept case.

**This had already visibly surfaced once, unnoticed as a bug.** `lib/dispatchTriage.test.ts`'s own
2026-10-28 fix ("the 7-day boundary agrees with lib/dates.ts's own daysUntil() - no second,
disagreeing day count") recorded, in its own comment, that `daysUntil()` read "8 days left" for a
tender genuinely 7 SAST calendar days out (`2026-10-28T15:00+02:00` -> `2026-11-04T09:00+02:00`) -
and then made `dispatchTriage.ts`'s own inline day-count match THAT number rather than questioning
whether it was right, baking the same `+1` into `classifyDispatchBucket()`'s 7-day urgency boundary
and into that test's own asserted expected value (`8`). That test's own number was never actually
correct; it was simply two different pieces of code agreeing on the same wrong one.

**Confirmed blast radius - checked column types directly, not assumed.** Grepped every
`add column .../create table` line in `supabase/migrations/*.sql` for every field this function (or
a sibling that reuses it) is ever called on:
- **Affected (`timestamptz`, a real time-of-day in practice):** `tenders.closing_date`,
  `discovered_opportunities.closing_date`, `company_subscriptions.trial_ends_at`.
- **NOT affected (plain `date`, PostgREST always returns a bare `"YYYY-MM-DD"`):** every
  company-vault expiry column (`coid_letter_of_good_standing_expiry`, `cidb_expiry`,
  `sars_tcs_pin_expiry`, `pi_insurance_expiry`, `iso_9001_expiry`,
  `bank_confirmation_letter_valid_until`, `bee_proof_expiry`), `people.ecsa_expiry`/
  `sacpcmp_expiry`, `held_registrations.expiry_date`, `tenders.briefing_date`,
  `tender_tasks.due_date` - so the Company Vault's own document-expiry overview
  (`lib/documentExpiry.ts`/`lib/notifications.ts`/`lib/readiness.ts`, all sourced from these
  columns) was never actually affected, despite calling the same function.
- **Real, affected consumers of the two `timestamptz` columns, confirmed by reading each one:**
  tender-closing displays with no separate `isPast()`/`closingCountdown()` override
  (`app/sanral-schedules/page.tsx`, `app/dashboard/page.tsx`'s "New opportunities for you",
  `app/analytics/page.tsx`'s "Upcoming deadlines", `lib/tenderTimeline.ts` ->
  `submission-plan-view.tsx`'s `DeadlineChip`); `lib/dispatchTriage.ts`'s
  `classifyDispatchBucket()`/`deriveDecisionNeeded()` 7-day triage/escalation boundary;
  `lib/deadlineReminders.ts`'s own exact-day tender-deadline reminder email trigger; and
  `lib/trialLifecycle.ts`'s `trialDay7Candidates()` (the `trial_day_7_milestone` nudge email) -
  all five reminder-threshold families (`deadlineReminders.ts`, `briefingReminders.ts`,
  `clarificationWindowReminders.ts`, `complianceDigestCandidates.ts`, `trialLifecycle.ts`) compare
  this function's real output against an exact day count, so the `+1` silently shifted every one of
  them a real calendar day later than its own stated threshold - though only
  `deadlineReminders.ts`/`trialLifecycle.ts` are actually fed a `timestamptz` column; the other
  three (briefing/clarification/compliance-digest) run on `date`-only columns and were unaffected in
  practice despite sharing the same exact-match code shape.
  `app/app/pipeline/page.tsx`/`TenderCard` were NOT among the broken displays - both already guard
  every closing display with an explicit `isPast()` check before ever showing `daysUntil()`'s own
  number, and already render the actual countdown text from `closingCountdown()` (time-aware), only
  ever feeding `daysUntil()`'s result into `closingColorClass()`'s colour banding - confirmed by
  reading both files; this is exactly why this bug stayed invisible on the one screen (Pipeline)
  that would otherwise have shown it most often.

**Fix.** `daysUntil()` now converts the target to its own SAST calendar day first (reusing
`closingDayOf()`'s already-tested timestamp -> `"YYYY-MM-DD"` conversion, a function declaration so
already available despite being defined later in the same file) and diffs that against today's
already-correct SAST calendar day, as two whole-day instants - a pure calendar-day count no longer
dependent on either side's time-of-day at all. `closingDayOf()`'s own header comment, which
documented the original fraction-rounding quirk as the reason `tenderCompliance.ts` has to call it
ahead of `daysUntil()`, was updated to note this is now harmless/idempotent rather than load-bearing
(double-applying `closingDayOf()` on an already-date-only string is a no-op).

**Verified before pushing - red then green, not asserted from reading alone.** Added 4 new
regression cases to `lib/dates.test.ts` (today/earlier-today/yesterday/exactly-7-days, all against
a REAL timestamp with a non-midnight time-of-day - the one input shape none of this function's
existing tests exercised) and corrected `lib/dispatchTriage.test.ts`'s own baked-in `8` ->
`7`/`"radar"` -> `"in_progress"` (with a comment explaining why, not silently). `git stash push --
lib/dates.ts` to isolate the pre-fix implementation with the new tests still in place: **5 failures**,
exactly the predicted ones (`1 !== 0`, `1 !== 0`, `-0 !== -1`, `8 !== 7`, `8 !== 7`) -
`node --experimental-strip-types --test lib/dates.test.ts lib/dispatchTriage.test.ts`, 40 pass / 5
fail. `git stash pop` to restore the fix: same command, **45/45 pass**. Full suite after restoring:
`npx vitest run` - **75 files, 612 tests, all passed**; every `*.test.ts` file in the repo run the
same way CI does (`find . -name "*.test.ts" -not -path "*/node_modules/*"` then
`node --experimental-strip-types` each one) - all exit 0; `npx tsc --noEmit` (whole `app/` project) -
0 errors; `npx eslint lib/dates.ts lib/dates.test.ts lib/dispatchTriage.test.ts` - clean. Re-ran the
original full-day sweep against the fixed code: the pattern now reads "1 day left" through the
whole prior day, "Due today" for the entire real closing day (matching this function's own
documented, pre-existing, date-only "today regardless of current time" semantics - unchanged, not
loosened), and correctly "Closed"/"-1" from the very next SAST day onward, instead of staying wrong
for 36 hours.

**Fixed directly on `main` - no PR.** Single-file production change (`lib/dates.ts`), plus the two
test files that needed their own expectations corrected to match the now-correct behaviour. No
RLS, no payment/money-transaction surface (trial-day-7 is a retention nudge email, not a billing
charge - PayFast checkout itself, the real payment path, is untouched), no schema, no worker-image
change, no authz/tenant-isolation angle - this is a pure date-math correctness fix inside a single
already-heavily-tested helper, every one of whose callers needed no change of their own to pick up
the fix. **Flagging explicitly, not asking permission:** because this shifts the real calendar day
on which `deadlineReminders.ts`'s tender-deadline-reminder emails and `trialLifecycle.ts`'s trial-
day-7 email actually fire (one real day earlier than before, i.e. now firing on the day their own
threshold constants actually name), Sarel may want to sanity-check the next few days' worth of
sent reminder logs against this change rather than be surprised by the shift.

**Regression:** `app/lib/dates.ts` (`daysUntil()`'s own body and header comment, plus
`closingDayOf()`'s header comment) and two test files (`lib/dates.test.ts`,
`lib/dispatchTriage.test.ts`) - no exported signature change on `daysUntil()` itself, no call-site
change needed anywhere in either `app/` or the many files that import it.

**What WAS found, on the Python side.** `engine/compliance/watch_deadlines.py`'s own `days_until()`

NOT affected: it already truncates (and only ever receives) plain `date`-typed values (document/
registration/task expiry columns, confirmed the same way Finding 289 confirmed the TS side's
`date`-only columns), with no midnight-anchor arithmetic in its own body at all (a plain
`(d - today).days` on two already-date-only values). But `engine/notify/daily_digest.py`'s
`submission_due_signals()` - which reports a release as "closing soon" when its real
`closing_date` (a genuine `timestamptz`, not a `date`) falls inside the digest's lead-time window -
derived that release's own calendar day with `datetime.date.fromisoformat(closing[:10])`: a naive
truncation of the raw closing_date STRING that silently assumed its first 10 characters already
named the true SAST calendar day. `tenders.closing_date`/`discovered_opportunities.closing_date`
come back from PostgREST in UTC - every closing_date fixture in this repo uses this shape (e.g.
`test_discovery_fanout.py`'s `"2099-01-01T11:00:00Z"`) - so for any closing time whose UTC
time-of-day falls in `22:00-23:59:59` (SAST `00:00-01:59` the FOLLOWING day), the naive slice read
the wrong, EARLIER UTC calendar day instead of the true, later SAST one. This is not a rare corner
case: `app/lib/dates.ts`'s own `formatClosingDateTime()` docstring already documents that a source
giving no real closing time at all has its value defaulted to SAST midnight by `parse_sast()` as a
generic "unknown" marker - stored as exactly `"...T22:00:00Z"`, squarely inside the broken window -
so this hit every tender with an unspecified closing time, not just a theoretical edge case. The
shared, already-correct conversion already exists elsewhere in this same engine
(`discovery/tender_updates.to_date()`, docstring: "in SAST (UTC+2) like app/lib/dates.ts
closingDayOf()", already used by `watch_tender_updates.active_pursuits()`) - `daily_digest.py`
simply never called it for this one calculation.

**Confirmed live**, not just by reasoning: a closing_date of `"2026-11-20T23:30:00+00:00"` (01:30
SAST on 2026-11-21) with "today" fixed at 2026-11-19 SAST read `days_left=1` via the naive slice
(`to_date()` -> SAST day 2026-11-20) instead of the correct `2` (`to_date()` -> true SAST day
2026-11-21) - run directly against the real, unmodified `submission_due_signals()` function, no
reasoning-only claim.

**Fix.** Replaced the naive `closing[:10]` slice with a call to the shared
`tender_updates.to_date()` (imported as `_closing_to_sast_date` to avoid shadowing this file's own
`tender_updates` local variable/parameter name, used in several of its functions) - same shared
helper already proven correct and already used elsewhere in this engine for exactly this
conversion, rather than a second, independent (and wrong) one here. `to_date()` already returns
`None` for an unparseable value with no exception raised, so the existing "malformed -> skip, not
crash" behaviour (and its own test coverage) is unchanged.

**Verified before pushing - red then green.** Added a new regression case to
`notify/test_digest_live.py` (`test_submission_due_signals_uses_sast_calendar_day_not_a_naive_utc_slice`)
using a closing_date constructed to land exactly in the broken UTC-day window relative to the real
"today" the test runs on (23:00 UTC, 2 days out in UTC terms = true SAST day 3 days out), asserting
`days_left == 3`. `git stash push -- engine/notify/daily_digest.py` to isolate the pre-fix
implementation with the new test still in place: **1 failure**, the exact predicted one
(`days_left` read `2`, not `3`), every other check in the file (36 checks) still passing. `git
stash pop` to restore the fix: same command, **0 failures** (full file, including the new test).
Full suite after restoring: `python3 notify/test_digest_live.py` - 0 failures;
`python3 discovery/test_tender_updates.py` - ALL PASSED (the shared `to_date()` this fix now
depends on); `python3 compliance/test_watch_deadlines_urgency.py` - 0 failures;
`python3 discovery/test_gov_sources.py` - ALL PASSED; `python3 discovery/test_watch_tender_updates.py`
- ALL PASSED (the other real caller of `watch_tender_updates`, imported by `daily_digest.py`).
`python3 -m py_compile` on both changed files - clean. `ruff check` on both changed files - 19
findings, confirmed against the pre-fix baseline (18) that the one new line is the SAME
already-present, already-accepted `# noqa: E402` style this file already uses on every other
sys.path-dependent import (`RUF100`/"unused noqa, E402 not enabled" - a pre-existing, accepted
convention in this file, not a new issue class); no `BLE001`/`SIM115` or other real finding added.

**Fixed directly on `main` - no PR.** Two-file change (`engine/notify/daily_digest.py` plus its own
test file) - no RLS, no payment/money-transaction surface (this reorders which releases appear in
an informational "closing soon" digest section; PayFast/billing is untouched), no schema, no
worker-image change, no authz/tenant-isolation angle, no document a company signs/submits. Same

**Regression:** `engine/notify/daily_digest.py` (`submission_due_signals()`'s own closing-day
derivation, now via `tender_updates.to_date()`) and its own test file
(`engine/notify/test_digest_live.py`) - no exported signature change, no other call site affected

### Finding 291 (CONFIRMED AND FIXED ON `main` - a second, independent recurrence of the SAME
`engine/` naive-UTC-slice mistake Finding 290 just fixed, found by checking every other `[:10]`
truncation of a real closing-date STRING across `engine/` rather than assuming Finding 290 was the
only one: `general/process_general_jobs.py`'s own `_within()` - whether a company's Experience
Library evidence counts as "recent enough" for a tender's `window_years` eligibility rule)

**Why checked.** Finding 290's root cause (`datetime.date.fromisoformat(closing[:10])` on a real,
UTC-formatted `timestamptz` string) is a specific, nameable anti-pattern, not a one-off typo -
worth checking for elsewhere before concluding the engine-side sweep was complete. `_within()`
already had HALF of this exact bug fixed once before, in a DIFFERENT branch of the same function:
its own "no closing date -> fall back to today" path was fixed under the heading "Finding 9c"
(2026-10-21, this file's own comment, still present), with a dedicated test
(`test_within_missing_closing_date_uses_real_sast_today_not_naive_utc`) - but that fix only touched
the fallback (`closing` is falsy) side of `ref = datetime.date.fromisoformat(str(closing or
today_sast)[:10])`. The OTHER side of that same ternary - when a real `closing` (the tender's own
`closing_date`, a genuine `timestamptz`) IS given - still sliced it naively, carrying the identical
mistake Finding 9c had already named and fixed one branch over.

**Confirmed live.** `closing_date = "2026-10-20T22:30:00+00:00"` (00:30 SAST on 2026-10-21) with a
5-year `window_years` rule: the true SAST ref day is 2026-10-21, so the real cutoff is 2021-10-21 -
an Experience Library row dated `2021-10-20` (genuinely ONE DAY before that cutoff, outside the
window) should read `False` ("not within"). Pre-fix, `_within()` read `True`: the naive slice read
`ref` as `2026-10-20` (the UTC day), moving the cutoff one day early to `2021-10-20` - exactly on
the test item's own date - so the stale row was wrongly treated as recent-enough evidence for the
tender's eligibility rule. Run directly against the real, unmodified `_within()` function.

**Impact, honestly scoped.** Narrower than Finding 289/290: it only matters when (a) the pursued
tender's own `closing_date` lands in the same `22:00-23:59` UTC window as Finding 290 (the same
SAST-midnight-defaulted closing times are the most common real-world trigger), AND (b) a company's
own Experience Library has a row dated at or within one day of the `window_years` cutoff - a
day-level coincidence on top of a year-level window. Not reproduced against any real production
row; this is a genuine, confirmed-live mechanism, not a theoretical one, but with a narrower
real-world hit rate than Findings 289/290.

**Fix.** Same shape as Finding 9c's own prior fix to the sibling branch: convert the real `closing`
value via its own timezone info (`datetime.fromisoformat(...).astimezone(SAST).date()`, the SAST
constant already defined locally in this file - kept a local conversion rather than importing
`discovery.tender_updates.to_date()`, per this file's own explicit "local constant, not a
cross-directory import" convention stated in its header comment just above `SAST`'s own
definition) instead of a string slice. The existing "malformed closing -> fall back to today, no
crash, no alert" behaviour is unchanged (a `ValueError` from the conversion now falls back to
`today_sast` exactly as before, just via `pass` instead of a second `except` block).

**Verified before pushing - red then green.** Added
`test_within_real_closing_date_uses_its_own_sast_day_not_a_naive_utc_slice` to
`general/test_process_general_jobs.py`, directly alongside the existing Finding-9c sibling test,
covering: the stale item one day before the real cutoff (must now be excluded), a fresh item
exactly on the real cutoff (must stay included - confirms no over-correction), and a malformed
closing_date (must still fall back to today, not crash). `git stash push --
engine/general/process_general_jobs.py` to isolate the pre-fix implementation with the new test
still in place: **1 failure**, the exact predicted one, every other check in the file (28 checks)
still passing. `git stash pop` to restore the fix: same command, **0 failures**. Full suite after
restoring: `python3 general/test_process_general_jobs.py` - 0 failures; `python3
general/test_general_bridge.py` - ALL PASSED; `python3 general/test_build_general_pack.py` - 0
failures. `python3 -m py_compile` - clean. `ruff check` - 13 findings, identical count and content
to the pre-fix baseline (confirmed by diffing both outputs) - no new issue introduced.

**Fixed directly on `main` - no PR.** Two-file change (`engine/general/process_general_jobs.py`
plus its own test file) - no RLS, no payment/money-transaction surface, no schema, no worker-image
change, no authz/tenant-isolation angle. This DOES affect which Experience Library evidence a
generated pack treats as valid, which is adjacent to "a document a company submits" - but the
change only ever makes the eligibility check MORE conservative (narrower, more correct), never
includes evidence the pre-fix code would have excluded, and the pre-existing sibling fix (Finding
9c) to the other branch of this exact same function was itself pushed directly to `main` with no
PR - same precedent, same risk class, applied consistently.

**Regression:** `engine/general/process_general_jobs.py` (`_within()`'s own real-closing-date
conversion) and its own test file (`engine/general/test_process_general_jobs.py`) - no exported

### Finding 292 (CONFIRMED AND FIXED ON `main` - a third, independent instance of the same
naive-UTC-anchor-day bug class, found by a dedicated engine/-wide sweep for `[:10]` slices AND
unwrapped `datetime.now()`/`date.today()` calls after pass `ccc`'s Finding 290/291 fix: this time
not a `[:10]` string slice at all, but the bare-`date.today()` half of the same bug class, in
`discovery/gov_sources.py`'s own `read_source("etenders_ocds")`)

**Why checked.** The task brief's own fresh direction: verify the ENTIRE `engine/` tree (not just
the files pass `ccc` already checked) for this exact anti-pattern, checking both `[:10]`/
`fromisoformat()` truncations AND bare `datetime.now()`/`date.today()` calls not wrapped in a
SAST-aware conversion. Ran `grep -rn "\[:10\]" engine --include="*.py"` and `grep -rn
"datetime\.now(\|date\.today(" engine --include="*.py"` across every `engine/*/*.py` file (both
commands and full output in `System-Status.md`'s own pass entry below), then checked every hit
individually against whether it actually needs SAST-awareness, per the brief's own explicit
"don't over-flag a legitimate log timestamp" instruction.

**What the sweep found.** Every `[:10]` slice already on `main` is either already fixed (Findings
290/291's own sites), a non-date use (a hash-suffix truncation in `dbsa_procurement.py`/
`vaal_central_water.py`, a `[:10]`-items-list limiter in `send_digest_emails.py`), or a slice on a
value that is genuinely already a plain `YYYY-MM-DD` string with no time-of-day component to lose
(e.g. `intake/classify_tender.py`'s workbook-vs-DB closing-date comparison). Of the bare
`datetime.now()`/`date.today()` hits, most are genuinely harmless: report `"generated_at"`/
`"generated"`/`"confirmed_date"` metadata stamps in CLI/admin-only tooling
(`pack_generator/suggest_pack.py`, `fingerprint.py`, `discovery/award_outcomes.py`,
`etenders_national.py`'s own `main()` `--out` report, `pack/harness_pack.py` - a synthetic-company
test harness), a PDF `/CreationDate` metadata field (`pack/pdf_merge.py`), and
`narrative/process_narrative_jobs.py`'s `years_experience = (date.today() - graduated).days //
365` - a years-level floor division where a one-day anchor error can never flip the result (the
exact opposite of a day-count display, where one day IS the whole unit). None of these need the
treatment.

**One real instance found: `discovery/gov_sources.py:219`, `read_source("etenders_ocds")`.** This
function builds its own OCDS API fetch window (`date_from`/`date_to`, a 14-day lookback ending
"today") from a bare `today = datetime.date.today()` - even though this exact same "what calendar
day is it for this OCDS fetch" computation is done CORRECTLY, SAST-aware, by both of this
function's own real callers for the IDENTICAL purpose: `watch_new_tenders.py`'s own `today =
datetime.datetime.now(sh.SAST).date()` a few lines before it calls into
`gov_sources.releases_for_watch()`/`fetch_all()` (which includes `etenders_ocds` unconditionally -
`fetch_all()`'s own `by_source["etenders_ocds"] = read_source("etenders_ocds", ...)` line), and
`daily_digest.py`'s own `datetime.datetime.now(watch_deadlines.SAST).date()` for the same purpose
one layer up. `gov_sources.py` already imports `source_http as sh` at module scope (used
throughout the rest of the file) - this was the one spot that didn't use it.

**Confirmed live**, not reasoning-only, against the real, unmodified function (full script and
output also saved at the time in the session's own scratchpad, not committed): monkeypatched
`etenders_national.fetch_releases` to capture its arguments and froze the simulated instant at
2026-11-09 22:30 UTC (00:30 SAST on 2026-11-10, squarely inside the `00:00-01:59 SAST` danger
window this whole bug class lives in). `read_source("etenders_ocds")` built `date_to="2026-11-09"`
- the stale, UTC-anchored day - when the real SAST "today" was already `2026-11-10`. Every OCDS
release genuinely published so far "today" (true SAST) would be silently excluded from this
source's own fetch for that run.

**Impact, honestly scoped.** This is the mildest of the four engine-side instances found this
session (72/290/291/292): (a) `watch_new_tenders.py`'s own scheduled cron run (`daily-discovery.yml`,
02:45 UTC = 04:45 SAST) never actually lands inside the 00:00-01:59 SAST danger window, so the
ONE scheduled production run per day is unaffected in practice today; (b) even a run that DOES
land in the window only loses that one day's worth of `etenders_ocds` releases for that single
run - the next run's own 14-day lookback (now computed from the correct, later "today") re-covers
the missed day in full, so this is a transient, self-healing miss, never a permanent loss, and
`discovery_seen_releases`'s own per-company dedup means nothing is double-reported either. The
real, live risk is a manual `workflow_dispatch` run (or any ad hoc invocation of
`watch_new_tenders.py`/`gov_sources.fetch_all()`) triggered inside that narrow UTC window, and the
fact that this function silently disagreed with its own two callers about what "today" means for
the exact same purpose, in the exact same run, is a real inconsistency worth fixing on its own
merits even before counting the narrow production exposure.

**Fix.** Changed `today = datetime.date.today()` to `today = datetime.datetime.now(sh.SAST).date()`,
matching every sibling caller's own pattern exactly, reusing the module's already-imported `sh`
(no new import needed).

**Verified before pushing - red then green.** Added
`test_etenders_ocds_fetch_window_uses_sast_calendar_day_not_naive_utc_today` to
`discovery/test_gov_sources.py` (a `FixedDateTime` freeze at the same 22:30 UTC / 00:30 SAST
instant, a monkeypatched `etenders_national.fetch_releases` to capture the real `date_from`/
`date_to` args `read_source()` passes). `git stash push -- engine/discovery/gov_sources.py` to
isolate the pre-fix implementation with the new test still in place: **2 failures**, the exact
predicted ones (`date_to`/`date_from` both one day stale), every other check in the file (139
total checks) still passing. `git stash pop` to restore the fix: **0 failures, ALL PASSED**. Full
related suite after restoring: `python3 discovery/test_gov_sources.py` - ALL PASSED; `python3
discovery/test_etenders_national.py` - ALL PASSED; `python3 discovery/test_watch_tender_updates.py`
- ALL PASSED; `python3 discovery/test_tender_updates.py` - ALL PASSED (Part 3 skipped, no scratch
Postgres, as documented).

**Fixed directly on `main` - no PR.** Single-file code change (`discovery/gov_sources.py`) plus
its own test file - no RLS, no payment/money-transaction surface, no schema, no worker-image
change, no authz/tenant-isolation angle. This affects which releases a single discovery source
contributes to one run's own fetch, self-healing on the next run - same risk class as Findings
290/291, same precedent for a direct push.

**Regression:** `engine/discovery/gov_sources.py` (`read_source("etenders_ocds")`'s own fetch-
window anchor) and its own test file (`engine/discovery/test_gov_sources.py`) - no exported
signature change, no other call site affected (`fetch_all()`/`releases_for_watch()` just receive
the now-correct window transparently).

### Finding 293 (CONFIRMED on `main` - a real, live-reproduced cross-file "expiring soon" threshold
disagreement between the Company vault's Document expiry overview (`lib/documentExpiry.ts`) and
both the topbar notification bell (`lib/notifications.ts`) and the vault's own Compliance documents
section (`ComplianceDocumentsSection.tsx`), directly contradicting two explicit "can never disagree"
comments already written into the first file's own code - FIXED the false comments, deliberately
NOT the underlying 30-vs-60-day threshold choice itself, which is a Sarel judgment call, same
precedent as standing items 18/24)

**Why checked.** Task brief's own suggested fresh direction: "does every place that determines a
document's 'expiring soon' threshold ... use the SAME number, or has one place drifted ... without
anyone noticing?" Grepped every `RENEW_SOON`/`WINDOW_DAYS`/`THRESHOLD_DAYS`/`windowDays` constant
across `app/lib`, `app/app`, `app/components`, `app/scripts` and read each one's real usage rather
than trusting the constant name alone.

**What's actually there (3 independent "is this document due for renewal" surfaces over the same
`COMPANY_EXPIRY_FIELDS` list):**
- **The bell** (`lib/notifications.ts`'s `getNotifications()`): `DOCUMENT_WINDOW_DAYS = 60` as the
  default, but reads each `COMPANY_EXPIRY_FIELDS` entry's own `windowDays` first
  (`withinWindow(left, windowDays ?? DOCUMENT_WINDOW_DAYS)`) - the one entry with an override,
  `bank_confirmation_letter_valid_until` (`windowDays: 30`, since that letter is only valid 3
  months), gets 30; the other 6 company fields, every `held_registrations` row and every person's
  ECSA/SACPCMP get 60. This per-field override was itself added 2026-10-29 (per this file's own
  comment) specifically to fix an earlier version of this exact bug class for the bank letter.
- **The vault's own Compliance documents section** (`ComplianceDocumentsSection.tsx`): calls
  `documentStatus(hasFile, expiry, renewSoonWithinDays = 60)` (`lib/dates.ts`) per document,
  explicitly passing `BANK_LETTER_RENEW_SOON_DAYS` (= 30, `lib/vaultDocuments.ts`) only for the
  bank letter row and leaving every other row at the function's own 60-day default - same 60/30
  split as the bell, confirmed by reading every one of its 7 entries directly, not inferred.
- **The Document expiry overview** (`lib/documentExpiry.ts`'s `loadDocumentExpiryOverview()` /
  `statusFor()`, rendered by `DocumentExpiryOverview.tsx` on the company page): applies a single,
  flat `EXPIRING_SOON_WINDOW_DAYS = 30` to literally every row - company fields, held
  registrations, and people - never reading `windowDays` at all. Its own header comment (and
  `DocumentExpiryOverview.tsx`'s own, separately) explicitly claims this "can never disagree with
  what the bell already says about the same document - just shows more of it."

**That claim is false, and was false from this file's own first commit.** `git log --follow -p --
app/lib/documentExpiry.ts` shows the "can never disagree ... just shows more of it" sentence and
`const EXPIRING_SOON_WINDOW_DAYS = 30` were both introduced in the SAME original commit
(`7e8e8c8`, 2026-10-21, PR #42) - and at that point the bell itself was still a flat 60 for every
field (the `windowDays` per-field override didn't exist until 2026-10-29), so even on day one a
document 31-60 days from expiry was already classified "valid" by this file while the bell (flat
60 at the time) was already nagging about it. The claim was never once true.

**Live-reproduced, not reasoning-only.** Wrote a standalone vitest spec importing the real,
unmodified `statusFor()` from `documentExpiry.ts` and the real `COMPANY_EXPIRY_FIELDS` list, and
swept every entry's `daysLeft` from 31 to 60 (the exact band where the bell's 60-day default and
this file's flat 30-day window must disagree for any field without its own `windowDays` override):

```
field: 'coid_letter_of_good_standing_expiry', daysLeft: 45, bellFlags: true, overviewStatus: 'valid'
total disagreements: 180   // 6 non-overridden fields x 30 days each (31..60) = 180 of 210 checked
```

Confirmed concretely: a COID Letter of Good Standing 45 days from expiry shows a green "Valid" chip
on the Document expiry overview, and is excluded from its own "N documents need attention before
your next bid" banner count - while the topbar bell is, at the exact same instant, already showing
an amber "renew soon" notification for that identical document. The one field where the two
genuinely agree is the bank confirmation letter (`windowDays`/`BANK_LETTER_RENEW_SOON_DAYS` both
30, which happens to equal this file's own flat 30 too) - the coincidence that likely let the false
"can never disagree" claim go unnoticed for this long, since the field it was presumably written
and tested against is the one field where it happens to hold.

**Severity, honestly scoped - this is a documentation-correctness finding, not forcing a behavior
change.** `EXPIRING_SOON_WINDOW_DAYS`'s own adjacent comment (unchanged by this fix) states the 30-
day flat window is deliberate: "'Expires in 30 days' per Sarel's own spec - a tighter window than
the notification bell's 60-day 'renew soon' glance, since this list is meant to answer 'what needs
attention before my next bid', not 'what's worth a heads-up eventually'." That is a real, stated
product decision, not an accident - so the actual question of whether the overview's threshold
should ever match the bell's per-field `windowDays` exactly is Sarel's own call (same precedent as
standing items 18 and 24, both left open for exactly this reason). What this Finding fixes is the
file's OWN separate, factually incorrect claim that the two already agree - a false invariant that
could mislead a future pass (or Sarel himself, reading the code) into trusting a guarantee that was
never real.

**Fixed directly on `main` - no PR.** Comment-only change in two files
(`lib/documentExpiry.ts`'s header + its `EXPIRING_SOON_WINDOW_DAYS` comment, and
`DocumentExpiryOverview.tsx`'s header) replacing the false "can never disagree" claim with an
accurate description of the real, deliberate-but-undocumented 30-vs-60/per-field split, plus a new
regression test (`lib/documentExpiry.spec.ts`) that locks in and documents the real relationship so
a future pass sees it as a verified, intentional fact rather than rediscovering it from scratch -
zero behavior change, no RLS/money/schema/worker-image surface, no authz/tenant-isolation angle.

**Verified.** `npx vitest run lib/documentExpiry.spec.ts` - 16/16 passed (1 new test added,
asserting the real disagreement for daysLeft 31/45/60 against `statusFor()` and the bell's own 60-
day default, explicitly framed as "deliberate, not a regression" so an intentional future change
doesn't look like silent test rot). Full suite after: `npx vitest run` - **75 files, 613 tests, all
passed**. `npx tsc --noEmit` - 0 errors. `npx eslint` on all 3 changed files - clean.

**Open standing item added** (see `System-Status.md`'s consolidated list, item 25): whether the
Document expiry overview's flat 30-day classification window should ever be made per-field
(matching the bell/vault-page's `windowDays`/`BANK_LETTER_RENEW_SOON_DAYS` exactly for every
field, not just the bank letter) is Sarel's own call - not changed here.

**Regression:** `app/lib/documentExpiry.ts`, `app/app/company/DocumentExpiryOverview.tsx`
(comments only, no logic change), `app/lib/documentExpiry.spec.ts` (one new test) - no exported
signature change, no other call site affected.

### Finding 295 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, minor-to-moderate - `engine/discovery/download_documents.py`'s `download_one()` built its own failure `error` field with `result.get("html", "no link returned")` - a default that only fires when the "html" key is ABSENT, never when it's present with a null value - and `main()`'s own status-line formatting hit the identical trap a second time, so a server response shaped `{"success": false, "html": null}` crashes the WHOLE batch run with a bare `TypeError`, outside any per-slug error handling, losing every other queued tender's download attempt)

**Area:** `engine/discovery/download_documents.py` (new `download_error_message()`, extracted from `download_one()`). New test file `engine/discovery/test_download_documents.py` (7 checks) - this script had no test coverage at all before this (confirmed via `find`).

**How this was found.** This cycle's rotation landed on discovery - a large area (34 non-test `.py` files). Mention-count survey put `download_documents.py` (6 mentions, 211 lines) far below every other candidate (the next-lowest was `run_discovery.py` at 12). Read it in full: a Playwright browser-automation script for SANRAL's own gated document-download form, whose own extensive header comment already documents, from real production attempts, that reCAPTCHA v3 reliably rejects every submission - this script is confirmed non-functional against the live site today and kept only "in case SANRAL's defenses or terms change," reached via an explicit opt-in flag (`run_discovery.py`'s default behaviour is to print links for a human instead). Precisely because this is the one path that always ends in `{"success": false, ...}` on every real invocation right now, its own failure-handling code is the part of this file that actually executes every single time it's run live - so it was read adversarially rather than skipped as "dead/experimental and therefore lower value."

**Confirmed live, not inferred.** `download_one()`'s failure branch: `return {"slug": slug, "success": False, "error": result.get("html", "no link returned")}`. `.get(key, default)` only substitutes `default` when `key` is ABSENT from the dict - a response shaped `{"success": false, "html": null}` (plausible: a server-side validation failure with no HTML message body to return, as distinct from the reCAPTCHA failure's own documented non-null message) has the key PRESENT with value `None`, so `result.get("html", "no link returned")` returns `None`, not the fallback string. `main()`'s own per-slug status-line formatting then does the IDENTICAL thing a second time: `r.get("error", "")[:200]` - same trap, `r["error"]` is present with value `None`, so this also evaluates to `None`, and `None[:200]` raises a bare `TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not subscriptable`. Reproduced directly in a plain Python REPL with exactly this dict shape: confirmed the crash happens AFTER `download_one()` already returned normally (no exception there to be caught by `main()`'s own per-slug `try/except`), so it aborts the `for slug in args.slugs:` loop outright - every tender queued after the one with this response shape is never attempted, not just the one that triggered it.

**Fix.** Extracted the error-message derivation into a new, pure, exported `download_error_message(result)` function, using `result.get("html") or "no link returned"` - `or` falls through on BOTH "key absent" and "key present but falsy" (`None`, empty string), closing the gap at its actual source rather than patching the downstream slice. `download_one()` now calls this helper instead of repeating the narrower `.get(key, default)` pattern inline.

**Verified red-then-green.** Added `test_download_documents.py` (new file, same plain-`check()`-list convention as `test_award_outcomes.py`): a real non-null `html` message passes through verbatim; `html: null`, a missing `html` key, and an empty-string `html` value all fall back to the same safe string; a final loop over all three "bad" shapes confirms the result is always a real string (never `None`), directly guarding against the exact slice that crashed `main()`. This file imports `download_documents`, which imports `playwright.sync_api` at module scope - not installed in this sandbox by default (confirmed: absent from `requirements.txt`, absent from `.github/workflows/bridge-worker-ci.yml`'s Python dependency setup, and this script itself was never wired into that CI file's own explicit test allowlist) - installed locally (`pip3 install playwright`, Python package only, no browser binaries needed since no browser is launched) purely to run this verification; the test file itself is NOT added to CI, matching this script's own existing, already-accepted "never run in automation" status rather than expanding CI's dependency surface as an unrelated change. **Red:** saved the diff to `download_documents.py` only, `git apply -R`, re-ran `python3 test_download_documents.py` - `AttributeError: module 'download_documents' has no attribute 'download_error_message'`, confirming the function is genuinely new. **Green:** `git apply` to reapply, re-ran - `ALL PASSED`, 7/7. `python3 -m py_compile` clean on both files. Confirmed the one real caller, `run_discovery.py`'s `from download_documents import sync_playwright, download_one`, still imports cleanly (unaffected - no existing export was renamed or removed).

**Not escalated to a PR.** Small, safe, self-contained Python fix (one function extracted, one call site updated, no RLS/schema/money/worker-image surface - this script isn't even part of the deployed worker image's own CI-tested surface). Pushed directly to `main`.

**Backlog status.** No new backlog items opened by this fix. `git fetch origin main` immediately before starting (clean, `main` at `b9126b6`/Finding 294, matching the task brief's own stated current state) and again immediately before pushing this commit, both clean - no sibling commit landed in between.

To verify independently: `pip3 install playwright` (package only), then from `engine/discovery/`, `python3 test_download_documents.py` (expect `ALL PASSED`, 7/7). `python3 -m py_compile download_documents.py` (clean).

### Finding 296 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, minor - currently dormant, not live-reachable - `lib/dispatchTriage.ts`'s own `CLOSED_STAGES` list was missing `briefing_shortlisted`, the same "already closed out, stop nagging/triaging it" stage-exclusion class Finding 258 already fixed once for `lib/briefingReminders.ts`, and which 7+ OTHER sibling lists across this codebase already apply correctly)

**Area:** `app/lib/dispatchTriage.ts` (`CLOSED_STAGES`, `classifyDispatchBucket()`'s own doc comment). `app/lib/dispatchTriage.test.ts` (one existing test widened).

**How this was found.** This pass applied Finding 294's own lens literally, per the task brief's suggested fresh direction: "wherever a canonical enumerable list exists, check every place that's supposed to iterate 'all N items of that kind' and verify it actually uses the canonical list rather than a hand-copied subset." `lib/pipeline.ts`'s `PIPELINE_STAGES` (7 stages, migration 0105) is exactly such a canonical list. Grepped every hand-rolled "pipeline stage subset" literal across `app/lib/` and `app/app/` (searching for `"won".*"lost"` arrays specifically, since every "already closed/done" list in this codebase ends in those two) and found the closed-stage-exclusion concept re-implemented independently at least 9 times: `lib/returnablesDigestCandidates.ts`'s `RETURNABLES_EXCLUDED_STAGES`, `lib/briefingReminders.ts`'s `BRIEFING_REMINDER_EXCLUDED_STAGES`, `lib/printCutoffReminders.ts`'s own identically-named `CLOSED_STAGES`, `lib/opportunityInsights.ts`'s `DONE_STAGES`, `lib/pastSubmissionReuse.ts`'s `DONE_STAGES`, `lib/deadlineReminders.ts`'s `DEADLINE_REMINDER_EXCLUDED_STAGES`, two inline array literals in `app/tenders/[id]/page.tsx`, and one in `app/tenders/[id]/market-context.tsx` - all 8 read `["submitted", "briefing_shortlisted", "won", "lost"]`, verified by reading each one directly rather than trusting the grep alone. The ONE outlier: `lib/dispatchTriage.ts`'s own `CLOSED_STAGES`, which read `["submitted", "won", "lost"]` - missing `briefing_shortlisted` - the same bug class Finding 258 (2026-11-0x) already found and fixed once for `lib/briefingReminders.ts`, independently recurring in a 9th file this time, not caught by that earlier pass because `dispatchTriage.ts` wasn't part of its scope.

**Confirmed live against the real, unmodified function before writing anything.** Wrote a standalone script importing the real `classifyDispatchBucket()` directly (no reimplementation) and called it with a tender closed 10 days ago, pack `dispatch_status: "submitted_and_receipted"`, across all four "should be excluded" stages:
```
submitted            -> null
briefing_shortlisted -> in_progress   <- WRONG: should be null, like its 3 siblings
won                   -> null
lost                  -> null
```
`lib/dispatchTriage.test.ts`'s own existing regression test for this exact guarantee ("classifyDispatchBucket: null once the tender is submitted, won or lost - not triaged at all") only ever looped over `["submitted", "won", "lost"]` - the identical gap baked into the test too, so it never caught this.

**Scoped severity honestly: NOT currently live-reachable.** Traced every caller of `classifyDispatchBucket()` (there is exactly one: `lib/dispatchDashboard.ts`'s `loadDispatchCards()`) and every caller of THAT (exactly one: `app/dashboard/page.tsx`). `dashboard/page.tsx` builds its `activeBids` array by filtering `myRows` to `(IN_PROGRESS_STAGES as readonly string[]).includes(stageOf(t))` BEFORE ever calling `loadDispatchCards()` - and `IN_PROGRESS_STAGES` (`lib/pipeline.ts`) is `["found", "assessing", "building", LEGACY_BIDDING_STAGE]`, which can never contain `"briefing_shortlisted"`. So a `briefing_shortlisted` `pipelineStage` can never actually reach `classifyDispatchBucket()` through the one real, live code path today - the live-repro bug above is real but currently dormant, the same "latent, not live" category this track has already used for `LEGACY_BIDDING_STAGE`'s own post-migration-0105 unreachability. What makes this worth fixing rather than filing as a pure negative: the module's own header comment explicitly states this logic is "reusable from both the dashboard (a whole company's active bids) and the tender workspace (one tender's own header badge)" - a stated intent to be called from a second context this pre-filter doesn't cover - and `CLOSED_STAGES`'s own adjacent doc comment claimed "call sites filter those out before this runs" as if it were a property of every caller, which is true today only by coincidence of the one caller that exists, not a guarantee the function itself provides.

**Fixed directly on `main` - no PR** (one array literal, one doc comment, in a single pure-logic file with no RLS/money/schema/worker-image surface and no authz/tenant-isolation angle; the one real call path is provably unaffected since `briefing_shortlisted` can't reach it there anyway). `CLOSED_STAGES` is now `["submitted", "briefing_shortlisted", "won", "lost"]`, matching all 8 sibling lists exactly. Rewrote `classifyDispatchBucket()`'s own doc comment to state the real relationship (the one live caller already filters this out too, but `CLOSED_STAGES` is the function's own independent guarantee, not a claim about every possible caller).

**Verified red-then-green.** Widened `dispatchTriage.test.ts`'s existing stage-exclusion test to loop over `["submitted", "briefing_shortlisted", "won", "lost"]` instead of the 3 it checked before. `git stash push -- app/lib/dispatchTriage.ts` (isolating the pre-fix implementation with the widened test in place), `node --experimental-strip-types --test lib/dispatchTriage.test.ts`: **28 tests, 1 fail** - exactly the new `briefing_shortlisted` case, the other 27 (including the 3 pre-existing stage checks) still green. `git stash pop` to restore (no `rm`/overwrite): same command, **28/28 pass**. Full regression after restoring: `node --experimental-strip-types --test lib/dispatchTriage.test.ts lib/dates.test.ts` - 17+28, all passed; `npx vitest run` - **75 files, 616 tests, all passed**; `npx tsc --noEmit` - 0 errors; `npx eslint lib/dispatchTriage.ts lib/dispatchTriage.test.ts` - clean.

**Backlog status.** No new standing item opened - this was a mechanical fix with a trivial, already-verified change, not a judgment call. `git fetch origin main` before starting this check (HEAD `b9126b6`, matching the task brief) found a sibling-track commit had landed in the interim (`f0fa09a`, Finding 295, `engine/discovery/download_documents.py` - zero file overlap with this fix); fast-forwarded (`git merge --ff-only`) rather than rebasing since no local commit existed yet, re-verified the real last Finding number (295, so this is 296) and the open-PR count (still 35, `#164`/`#165`/`#176`-`#208`) before writing this fix, then `git fetch origin main` again immediately before pushing - still at `f0fa09a`, no second collision.

**Regression:** `app/lib/dispatchTriage.ts` (one array literal widened, one doc comment corrected - no exported signature change, no other call site affected), `app/lib/dispatchTriage.test.ts` (one existing test's loop widened by one stage).

### Finding 297 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, minor-to-moderate, live-reachable - `app/lib/sanralMatrices.ts`'s own position-held matrices (`TECH_POSITION_ROWS`, `MAN_POSITION_ROWS`) have no row for `"PL(T)"` even though it's one of SANRAL's 23 published key-person codes, offered to real users as a "position held" suggestion - so a person recorded as having held PL(T) on a past project silently scored a confident 0, byte-for-byte identical to picking "Undefined" ("none of the above"), on both the SANRAL functionality-score estimate and the tender-workspace compliance report)

**Area:** `app/lib/sanralScoring.ts` (`lookup()`, new `heldCodeIsKnownButUntabulated()` helper, `estimatePosition()`'s two position-held note blocks). `app/lib/sanralScoring.test.ts` (2 new tests).

**How this was found.** Took up pass `hhh`'s own left lead directly: a first-class read of `app/lib/sanralMatrices.ts`'s `SANRAL_POSITION_CODES`/`TECH_POSITION_ROWS`/`MAN_POSITION_ROWS`/`DS_SPECIALISMS` constants, cross-checked against the Python engine's own SANRAL position-matching logic for the canonical-list-drift pattern. The Python side came back clean on that specific angle: `engine/sanral_fill.py` only maps codes to toll-form labels for FORM-FILLING (`"PL(T)" <-> "PL(Toll)"`) and has no scoring-matrix equivalent at all to drift against - `sanralMatrices.ts`'s position-held matrices are the sole implementation, so there is no second, Python-side copy to disagree with them. Widened the lens to an internal-consistency check of the TS file's own four related lists instead: counted `SANRAL_POSITION_CODES` precisely (`node -e` parse) - 24 entries, confirmed as exactly the 23 real codes `docs/specs/Tender-Evaluation-Engine-Audit.md` already states Book 1 defines (line 227: "SANRAL Book 1 defines 23 key-person codes") plus `"Undefined"`, so that list itself is accurate (its own header comment's "22 codes + Undefined" is an off-by-one typo, not touched - cosmetic, no functional effect). Comparing `TECH_POSITION_COLUMNS` (23 entries: the 23 real codes minus `PL(T)`, plus a literal `"UNDEFINED"` column) and the row-key sets of `TECH_POSITION_ROWS`/`MAN_POSITION_ROWS` (22 keys each, both missing exactly `PL(T)`) against that same 23-code list found the one real gap: `PL(T)` has a real, non-zero column in `MAN_POSITION_COLUMNS`/`MAN_POSITION_ROWS` (every other row's `PL(T)` column has a plausible nonzero value, e.g. `PL: [... 2.5, 2.5, 2.5]` for its `PL(T)`/`CE(T)`/`CM(T)` columns) but NO row of its own in either matrix - unlike its four toll siblings `DS(T)`/`CE(T)`/`CM(T)`/`ETS(T)`, which all have both a row and a column.

**Confirmed live, not inferred - traced to a real, reachable UI path first.** `SANRAL_POSITION_CODES`'s own header comment states it is read as "Suggestions for Form B1's 'POSITION HELD (coded)' on the People page" - confirmed directly: `app/app/people/[id]/page.tsx` line 996 renders `<datalist id="sanral-position-codes">{SANRAL_POSITION_CODES.map(...)}</datalist>` on exactly the "Position code" field of "+ Add a project to this person's history" (line 994-996), which writes straight into `SanralProject.position_code` - the same field `sanralScoring.ts`'s `lookup()` reads as `held`. `"PL(T)"` ("Project Leader (Toll)") is one of the 24 options in that list, offered to any real user adding a past toll-road project. So a company whose key person's CV includes "Project Leader (Toll)" on a past SANRAL toll project, typed or picked verbatim from this exact suggestion list, is live-reachable today, not a hypothetical.

Reproduced directly with the real, unmodified `estimatePosition()` (standalone script, no reimplementation) - a person tendered for `CE(T)` with one project, closing 2027-01-01, held position varied:
```
held=PL(T)      technical={"min":5,"max":10}   <- identical to Undefined
held=DS(T)      technical={"min":7.5,"max":12.5}  (real tabulated toll sibling)
held=CE(T)      technical={"min":10,"max":15}     (real tabulated toll sibling, own diagonal)
held=Undefined  technical={"min":5,"max":10}   <- SANRAL's own genuine "none of the above"
```
`PL(T)` and `Undefined` produced byte-for-byte identical `technical` ranges and notes before this fix - `lookup()`'s own existing comment ("unknown held code = SANRAL's own 'Undefined' row (0)") was applied to `PL(T)` even though `PL(T)` is not SANRAL's "none of the above" answer, it's a real, named, defined code this file's own transcription simply never gave a row.

**Scoped severity honestly - live-reachable, user-facing, but an estimate, not a submitted form.** `sanralScoring.ts`'s `estimateSanralConventional()`/`estimatePosition()` feed `app/tenders/[id]/compliance-data.ts` + `compliance-report.tsx` (the real tender-workspace compliance report shown to a company) and the standalone `/tools/b6-estimator` page - both are explicitly-labelled, informational functionality-SCORE ESTIMATES (the file's own header: "Every unknown is a range, never a guessed point value"), not the actual SBD/Form B1 submission content itself (that's `engine/sanral_fill.py`, unaffected - it never scores anything, only fills the toll-label text). So this doesn't corrupt a document a company signs or submits; it silently understates a company's own estimated competitiveness whenever this specific, real code is on file, which could affect a bid/no-bid judgment call made off that number.

**Fix.** `lookup()` now distinguishes "held code genuinely blank/unrecognised" (kept at a confident 0, matching SANRAL's real "Undefined" answer) from "held code is one of SANRAL's own 23 published codes but has no transcribed row in THIS matrix" (new `heldCodeIsKnownButUntabulated()` helper, checked against `SANRAL_POSITION_CODES`) - the latter now returns `null`, which both call sites (`posPts`/`manPos`) already fall back to a `0-5` range for, the exact same mechanism already used when the TENDERED position isn't in a matrix's columns. Added a matching explanatory note (mirroring the existing "Position code X isn't in SANRAL's position matrix" note for the tendered-position case) for both the technical and managerial branches, naming the specific untabulated held code(s) so a user sees "shown as a range" rather than a confident, silently-wrong number. No matrix data was invented - Book 1 itself is not available in this sandbox to transcribe the real `PL(T)` row from, so the fix makes the honest uncertainty visible instead of guessing numbers.

**Verified red-then-green.** Added 2 new tests to `sanralScoring.test.ts`: one confirming `PL(T)` now widens to `{min:5,max:15}` (vs. `Undefined`'s unchanged `{min:5,max:10}`) with the new note, and that the real tabulated `DS(T)` sibling is untouched; one confirming the identical gap in the managerial branch (`MAN_POSITION_ROWS`) also widens `management` into a real range with its own note. `git stash push -- app/lib/sanralScoring.ts` (isolating the pre-fix implementation with both new tests in place), `node --experimental-strip-types --test lib/sanralScoring.test.ts`: **6 tests, 2 fail** - exactly the 2 new cases, the 4 pre-existing tests still green. `git stash pop` to restore: same command, **6/6 pass**. Full regression after restoring: `npx tsc --noEmit` - 0 errors; `npx eslint lib/sanralScoring.ts lib/sanralScoring.test.ts` - clean; `npx vitest run` - 71/75 files, 605/616 tests pass (the same 4 files / 11 tests fail identically on unmodified `main` too, confirmed by re-running after `git stash` with no code changes - a pre-existing, environment-clock artifact: this sandbox's wall clock is currently 00:xx SAST, inside the exact "naive UTC vs. true SAST calendar day" window Findings 72/287-292 already describe, and `complianceDigestCandidates.spec.ts`/`readiness.spec.ts`/`tenderTimeline.spec.ts`/`send-operational-alerts.spec.ts` each construct a bare `new Date()` for a "tomorrow/today/yesterday" boundary case rather than freezing a clock, so they flake in this same ~2-hour window regardless of any code change - unrelated to this fix, not touched this pass); the `node --experimental-strip-types --test` loop over every `*.test.ts` file shows the same pre-existing, same-root-cause flake in `lib/dates.test.ts`'s own 3 bare-`new Date()` cases, also reproduced identically on unmodified `main`. Every suite touching `sanralScoring.ts`/`sanralMatrices.ts` specifically (`sanralScoring.test.ts`) is 6/6 green.

### Finding 298 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, test-only, minor - the 00:00-02:00 SAST test flake pass `iii` surfaced but deliberately left untouched (`complianceDigestCandidates.spec.ts`, `readiness.spec.ts`, `tenderTimeline.spec.ts`, `send-operational-alerts.spec.ts`, plus 3 original cases in `lib/dates.test.ts`) - now fixed, test-only, no production code behaviour changed)

**Area:** `app/lib/complianceDigestCandidates.spec.ts`, `app/lib/readiness.spec.ts`, `app/lib/tenderTimeline.spec.ts`, `app/scripts/send-operational-alerts.spec.ts`, `app/lib/dates.test.ts` - test files only. No production `.ts` file touched.

**How this was found.** Not a fresh discovery this pass - the task brief handed this pass pass `iii`'s own side-discovery (made while verifying Finding 297's regression suite) as its first priority: `npx vitest run`'s 4 failing spec files, plus `dates.test.ts`'s 3 flaky `node --test` cases, all fail specifically during the real 00:00-02:00 SAST window, confirmed by pass `iii` via `git stash` showing the identical failures on unmodified `main` with zero code changes. Re-verified pass `iii`'s own claim directly rather than citing it blindly: `git fetch origin main` confirmed `main` still at `502ac14` (pass `iii`'s own commit, matching the task brief exactly), `TZ=Africa/Johannesburg date` confirmed the sandbox's real wall clock was genuinely inside the window (`Tue Nov 10 00:16:38 SAST 2026`) before touching anything, and `npx vitest run` plus `node --experimental-strip-types --test lib/dates.test.ts` on the untouched tree reproduced the exact same 11 vitest failures (4 files) and 3 `dates.test.ts` failures pass `iii` documented, with the same assertion values (e.g. `expected 9 to be 10`, `expected -4 to be -3`, `expected 'past' to be 'urgent'`).

**Root cause, read directly from each file, not assumed.** All 5 files share one shape: a `daysFromNow()`/`daysFromToday()` test helper built a "N days from today" fixture off the real ambient host clock (`new Date()`, then `.setDate()`/`.setHours(0,0,0,0)`, then `.toISOString().slice(0, 10)` or the full ISO string) - a UTC calendar day, since no `TZ` env var is set on this sandbox or any CI runner this project uses. The function actually under test (`complianceDigestCandidatesForCompany()`, `computeBidReadiness()`, `tenderTimeline()`, `runBriefingReminders()`/`runClarificationWindow()`, all via `lib/dates.ts`'s `daysUntil()`) computes "today" as the real SAST calendar day instead - correct, by design, since Finding 289 already fixed `daysUntil()` itself to do exactly this. `daysUntil()` already accepts an injectable `now: Date = new Date()` parameter (confirmed by reading its signature directly, `app/lib/dates.ts` line 103) - none of these 5 call sites passed one, so it silently defaulted to the SAME ambient clock a second time. For the ~2 hours before UTC midnight every day (00:00-02:00 SAST), SAST's calendar day is one ahead of UTC's, so the fixture's "N days from today" and the function's own internal "today" disagree by exactly one day - not a rare edge case, the same every-single-day window Findings 72/287-292 already describe at length, just hitting the TEST layer instead of production code this time. `dates.test.ts`'s own 3 original (pre-Finding-289) cases carry the identical shape one level down: they build `tomorrow`/`today`/`yesterday` off ambient `new Date()` and call `daysUntil()` with no `now` argument either - the 4 newer (Finding 289) cases in the same file already pass a frozen `now` explicitly and were never affected.

**Fix - no production code touched, per each function's own existing convention.** For the 4 vitest spec files: froze the clock to one explicit, unambiguous instant, `2026-06-15T10:00:00.000Z` (mid-day in both UTC and SAST, nowhere near either timezone's own midnight, so UTC-today and SAST-today are provably the same calendar day, removing the ambiguity outright rather than just hiding it at this one moment), using `vi.useFakeTimers()`/`vi.setSystemTime()` - the exact convention `lib/payfast.spec.ts`'s own `nextPeriodEnd` suite already established in this codebase, checked first via `grep -rn "useFakeTimers" app/` before choosing it, rather than inventing a different pattern. Each helper now builds its fixture off that frozen constant (via UTC-safe `setUTCDate`/`setUTCHours` methods, not local-time ones) instead of `new Date()`, and each file's own `beforeEach`/`afterEach` freezes the SAME instant for the actual function-under-test call, so the fixture and the function's own ambient `new Date()` read the identical "now." Scoped deliberately in `send-operational-alerts.spec.ts`: only `describe("runBriefingReminders", ...)` and `describe("runClarificationWindow", ...)` got the fake-timer hooks - `describe("runPrintCutoff", ...)`'s own `pack` fixture deliberately anchors to the real ambient clock (`Date.now() + 40h`) for an unrelated hours-based cutoff calculation and was read closely first to confirm applying this globally would have silently broken it (freezing time to June 2026 while that fixture's `closing_date` stays computed from the real November 2026 run time would desync them by months) - left untouched. For `lib/dates.test.ts`'s plain `node --test` file (no `vi`/vitest available there, confirmed by checking its own imports - `node:test`/`node:assert` only): passed the identical frozen instant directly as `daysUntil()`'s own `now` parameter, the exact same pattern the file's own 4 newer (Finding 289) tests already use two tests below these three, rather than introducing a different technique for the same file.

**Verified red-then-green, run myself, at the live wall-clock instant, not simulated.** `git stash push` on the 5 touched test files (isolating the pre-fix versions from the real repo history, not hand-reconstructed) and re-ran at `Tue Nov 10 00:22:10 SAST 2026` (confirmed still inside the window via `TZ=Africa/Johannesburg date` immediately before running): **red** - `node --experimental-strip-types --test lib/dates.test.ts` gave `17 tests, 3 fail` (the identical 3), `npx vitest run` on the 4 spec files gave `4 failed files, 11 failed | 25 passed` (the identical 11). `git stash pop` to restore (never a plain `rm`/overwrite): **green** - `dates.test.ts` `17/17 pass`; the 4 spec files `4 passed (4), 36/36 tests pass` - all at `Tue Nov 10 00:22:21 SAST 2026`, still genuinely inside the 00:00-02:00 SAST window, not outside it. Full regression after restoring: `npx vitest run` from `app/` - **75/75 files, 616/616 tests pass** (unchanged file/test count from pass `iii`'s own last-known-good baseline, since this pass added no new test cases, only fixed existing ones). The separate per-file `node --experimental-strip-types --test` loop over every `*.test.ts` file in the repo (30 files) - **0 failures**. `npx tsc --noEmit` - 0 errors. `npx eslint` on all 5 touched files - 0 errors.

**Fixed directly on `main` - no PR.** Test-only change (5 test files, no production `.ts` file touched, no exported function signature changed anywhere) - squarely the task brief's own "small, safe → push directly" category, no RLS/money/schema/worker-image surface, no authz/tenant-isolation angle.

**Backlog status.** No new standing item opened - this closes out a known, already-documented (pass `iii`) gap rather than opening a new judgment call. `git fetch origin main` immediately before starting (clean, `main` at `502ac14`/Finding 297/pass `iii`, matching the task brief's own stated current state exactly) and again immediately before pushing this commit (still `502ac14`, no sibling-track commit landed in between - a plain fast-forward push, `502ac14..1e58ddd`).

**Regression:** `app/lib/complianceDigestCandidates.spec.ts`, `app/lib/readiness.spec.ts`, `app/lib/tenderTimeline.spec.ts`, `app/scripts/send-operational-alerts.spec.ts` (clock-freezing added to 2 of its 3 `describe` blocks only), `app/lib/dates.test.ts` (3 existing cases given an explicit frozen `now`, no new cases added, no existing case's intent changed).

To verify independently: from `app/`, at ANY time of day (the whole point of this fix), run `npx vitest run lib/complianceDigestCandidates.spec.ts lib/readiness.spec.ts lib/tenderTimeline.spec.ts scripts/send-operational-alerts.spec.ts` (expect 4 files / 36 tests pass) and `TZ=UTC node --experimental-strip-types --test lib/dates.test.ts` (expect 17/17 pass). ### Finding 299 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, minor-to-moderate, live-reachable - `lib/principals.ts`'s `idWarnings()` already cross-checked a typed gender/sa_citizen against what the person's SA ID number itself encodes, but never date_of_birth, even though it already calls `parseSaId()` and that function already computes `birth` for exactly this purpose)

**Area:** `app/lib/principals.ts` (`idWarnings()`), `app/lib/principals.spec.ts`.

**How this was found.** Following up the task brief's own suggested fresh angle ("SA ID number checksum/date-of-birth extraction consistency across `app/` and `engine/`"). First checked the Luhn-checksum/embedded-date-plausibility logic itself cross-file (`isValidSaId()` in `app/lib/principals.ts` vs. `_plausible_sa_id()`/`_luhn_ok()` in `engine/cv/extract_cv_fields.py`) - both implement byte-for-byte the identical algorithm (same digit-doubling-from-the-right Luhn variant, same both-century max-day date check, same citizenship-digit check), already deliberately synchronized by a prior pass's own 2026-11-08 fix comments in both files; a genuine conclusive negative, nothing to fix there. The Python side has no date-of-birth EXTRACTION logic at all (it only finds-and-redacts the ID number, confirmed by grepping `engine/cv/extract_cv_fields.py`/`engine/onboarding/classify_documents.py` for `birth`/`dob` - no hits beyond the comments already read) - `parseSaId()` (TS-only) is the sole place in the codebase that derives a birth date from an ID number, so there is nothing on the Python side to drift against either. Rather than stop at two conclusive negatives, read `parseSaId()`'s own callers to see whether its `birth` output was used consistently, and found `idWarnings()` - the function whose own docstring is literally "Mismatches between what the person typed and what their ID number encodes" - calling `parseSaId()` already, using its `gender`/`citizen` fields for exactly that cross-check, but never touching the `birth` field it also returns.

**Confirmed live-reachable, not just theoretical.** `date_of_birth` is a free-typed form field (`app/app/company/principals/actions.ts`'s `savePrincipal()`, `natural ? str(formData, "date_of_birth") : null` - entirely independent of `id_number`, no cross-validation anywhere in the save path). Traced where the stored value is actually used: `app/app/company/principals/page.tsx`'s `PrincipalCard()` computes `ageOn(p.date_of_birth ?? parsed.birth)` - the typed field wins whenever present, the ID-derived one is only a fallback - and that age drives the card's own "Youth" (18-35) B-BBEE tag. Traced further to confirm this isn't just a display nicety: migration `0050_principals_registrations_properties.sql`'s own `company_ownership_breakdown` view (lines 255-256) computes `youth_pct`/`black_youth_pct` as `sum(pct) filter (where ... age_years between 18 and 35)` - a real, server-side B-BBEE ownership-demographics percentage, not merely this card's own chip. So a typo, a paste from the wrong record, or simply never having been corrected after a real ID document review would silently feed a wrong age into a real scoring percentage, with `idWarnings()` - the one place already designed to catch exactly this class of mistake for gender and citizenship - saying nothing about it.

**Fix - a direct string comparison, not a "now"-dependent calculation (deliberately checked against this session's own recurring bug class).** Added one check to `idWarnings()`: when both `p.date_of_birth` and `parseSaId(p.id_number).birth` are present and differ, push `"Date of birth recorded as <X>, but the ID number encodes <Y>."`, mirroring the existing gender/sa_citizen warnings' own wording and style exactly. Both sides are plain `"YYYY-MM-DD"` calendar-day strings with no time-of-day component at all - `parseSaId()`'s own `birthDate.toISOString().slice(0, 10)` (built from `Date.UTC()`, so host-TZ-independent) compared against a Postgres `date` column's own round-tripped string - so this is a one-time, fixed-point string equality check, not a repeat of the naive-UTC-"now" anchor class this session already found and fixed many times over (Findings 72/287-292/298); confirmed there is no `now`/ambient-clock read anywhere in the new code. Widened `idWarnings()`'s own parameter type from `Pick<PrincipalRow, "id_number" | "gender" | "sa_citizen">` to add `"date_of_birth"` - its one real caller (`page.tsx`'s `PrincipalCard()`) already passes a full `PrincipalRow`, so this is a strictly additive, non-breaking type change (confirmed via `tsc --noEmit`).

**Verified red-then-green.** `idWarnings()` had NO existing test coverage at all (confirmed by grepping `principals.spec.ts` for `idWarnings` before starting - zero hits beyond an unrelated comment) - added 5 new tests covering the new date_of_birth check plus, for the first time, the pre-existing gender/sa_citizen checks and the invalid-id_number/no-crash path. `git stash push -- app/lib/principals.ts` (isolating only the production file, keeping the new tests) and re-ran: **red** - `npx vitest run lib/principals.spec.ts` gave `17 passed | 1 failed` (exactly the one new date_of_birth-mismatch test, `expected [] to include 'Date of birth recorded as 1990-01-05...'`). `git stash pop` to restore (never a plain `rm`/overwrite): **green** - `18/18` pass. Full regression: `npx vitest run` from `app/` - **75/75 files, 621/621 tests pass** (up from 616 - the 5 new cases, no existing case changed). `npx tsc --noEmit` - 0 errors. `npx eslint lib/principals.ts lib/principals.spec.ts` - 0 errors.

**Fixed directly on `main` - no PR.** Pure-logic TypeScript, no RLS/schema/worker-image surface, no authz/tenant-isolation angle. Does not touch document generation or the actual B-BBEE percentage calculation itself (that's computed server-side by migration 0050's own SQL view, entirely unaffected by this change) - this only adds a warning surfaced on the Company vault's People & principals page, the exact same tier as the pre-existing gender/sa_citizen warnings already living in this same function, which this pass takes as this track's own established precedent for the direct-push category rather than a new judgment call.

**Backlog status.** No new standing item opened - straightforward additive warning, not a judgment call (nothing here asks Sarel to choose between two defensible designs the way, e.g., items 18/24/25 on the standing list do). `git fetch origin main` immediately before starting (clean, `main` at `652b3c9`/Finding 298, matching the task brief's own stated current state exactly) and again immediately before pushing this commit (still `652b3c9`, no sibling-track commit landed in between - a plain fast-forward push, `652b3c9..46b7645`).

**Regression:** `app/lib/principals.ts` (`idWarnings()`'s parameter type widened, one new check added - `isValidSaId()`/`parseSaId()`/every other export unchanged), `app/lib/principals.spec.ts` (5 new tests, 0 existing tests changed).

To verify independently: from `app/`, `npx vitest run lib/principals.spec.ts` (expect 18/18 pass, including the 5 new `idWarnings` cases). Confirm `app/lib/principals.ts`'s `idWarnings()` signature now includes `"date_of_birth"` in its `Pick<PrincipalRow, ...>` parameter and pushes a `"Date of birth recorded as..."` message when it disagrees with `parseSaId()`'s own `birth` output.
