## 2026-11-09vi (standing solution-architect review, background worker): Finding 300 - `tenders.status` ("the buyer's public status", 0001) is a one-time, insert-only computation that nothing anywhere ever revisits, and two real consumers silently trusted it to mean "currently open" right now

**Angle chosen.** The task brief's own first "good fresh direction": does every surface that decides "can this company still bid on this tender" apply the same gates. Worked through every candidate gate first.

**Two conclusive negatives, checked before finding the real gap.** (1) No blacklist/suspension/debarment concept exists anywhere in this schema or codebase at all (`grep -rniE "blacklist|suspend|debarr|banned"` across `app/`+`engine/` - zero real hits, only unrelated matches in `node_modules`/generated typings) - nothing to drift against. (2) No "company verification status" gate exists either - no `is_verified`/`csd_verified`/`verification_status` column anywhere. (3) `closing_date` (the one real deadline signal) is NOT used as a hard stop ANYWHERE in the pack-generation path - checked all three layers for both tender families: the UI's own `generalDisabledReason`/`PrimaryPackActionLink` disabled-reason logic (`app/tenders/[id]/general-workspace.tsx`, `app/tenders/[id]/page.tsx` - both gate only on compliance/readiness, never closing date), the Server Actions (`requestSubmissionPack()` in `app/tenders/[id]/actions.ts`, `requestJob()`/general engine path - read in full, zero closing-date check), and the RPC level (`request_submission_pack_checked()`/`request_general_job_checked()`, migration 0115 - read in full, zero closing-date check). All three layers agree, by all three applying NO gate at all - a genuine negative, not drift, but also itself a side-effect worth noting for Sarel: nothing in this app stops a company from generating (and spending a pack-quota credit on) a submission pack for a tender that closed yesterday.

**The real gap, found by widening from "is there a gate" to "is there a column that LOOKS like a live gate but isn't".** `tenders.status` (migration 0001's check constraint: `'open' | 'closed' | 'awarded' | 'cancelled'`, its own comment calling it "the buyer's public status") is set exactly ONCE, by whichever of the 4 real insert sites first loads a tender into the shared `tenders` table - `pursue_discovered_opportunity()` (0018), the manual-tender-load and private-tender-document-load RPCs (0024/0032), and the government-listing-changes insert (0051) - and every one of those 4 sites uses the IDENTICAL formula: `case when closing_date is not null and closing_date < now() then 'closed' else 'open' end`, evaluated once, at that moment. Grepped the entire repo (`app/`, `engine/`, every migration) for any LATER write to this column - `update tenders set status`, `tenders.status =`, `tenders set status` - **zero hits, anywhere**. Separately, `accept_tender_update_date()` (0111) - the one real place a corrigendum's new closing date gets applied (`update tenders set closing_date = v_new ...`) when a company clicks "Accept" on a buyer's date change - updates `closing_date` but never touches `status` either.

Net effect: (a) a tender that was correctly `'open'` the moment it was first loaded keeps reading `status = 'open'` forever, even decades past its own `closing_date`, since nothing ever sweeps it; and (b) a tender that was `'closed'` at load time (or has since naturally closed) whose `closing_date` is later extended by an accepted corrigendum stays `status = 'closed'` forever too, even though it is now genuinely open again - the column can be wrong in BOTH directions, and only ever self-corrects by accident (never).

**Live-reproduced in a disposable scratch database, not reasoning-only.** Spun up Postgres 16 locally, created a scratch database, and replayed the full schema via the existing `engine/security/replay_schema.sh` helper against it (all 114 migrations, clean). Scenario A (direction (a)): inserted a tender with `status='open'`, `closing_date` 30 days in the past, and nothing else written since - a real `generated_cvs` row and a platform-admin caller set up around it, then called the real, unmodified `platform_admin_cv_document_stats()` (migration 0068, the super-admin console's own "how many open CVs have we currently got" stat, whose own header comment explicitly calls its scope "tenders that are currently open"):

```
open_tender_cvs_count | open_tender_cvs_docs_missing
-----------------------+------------------------------
                     1 |                            1
```

A tender closed for a month, counted as "currently open" by a real admin-facing metric, with zero other writes since insert. Scenario B (direction (b)): two tenders, both `status='closed'` - one genuinely closed (`closing_date` 5 days in the past), one with the exact corrigendum-extension shape (`closing_date` 10 days in the FUTURE, simulating `accept_tender_update_date()`'s own update leaving `status` alone): `where status = 'open'` found **0 of 2** (wrongly excluding the genuinely-open one); `where closing_date is null or closing_date >= 'now'::timestamptz` correctly found exactly the 1 that is genuinely still open. Scratch database dropped and Postgres stopped before finishing this pass, per the track's own standing guardrail.

**Exactly two real consumers trust `tenders.status = 'open'` as a live signal** (grepped every `.eq("status","open")`/`.eq('status','open')`/SQL `status = 'open'` against the `tenders` table specifically, across `app/` and `engine/` - every other `status`/`cancelled`/`awarded` hit found belongs to an unrelated table: `generated_cvs.status`, `cv_uploads.status`, `tender_packs.status`, `public_tender_outcomes.status`/`tender_market_outcomes` (a genuinely different, already-correctly-maintained "award outcome" concept fed by `engine/discovery/store_award_outcomes.py`, not this column), `discovered_opportunities.listing_status`, and the engine's own internal scraper-release `status` field, none of which write or read `tenders.status` at all):
1. `platform_admin_cv_document_stats()` (0068, SQL) - demonstrated live above.
2. `registrationsAskedFor()` (`app/lib/personCredentials.ts`) - the People page's "this tender asks for SACNASP/SAGC/SACAP/..." badges, which gate whether an entire "add this registration" section is even SHOWN for a person who doesn't yet hold it (`app/people/[id]/page.tsx`: `shown = CONDITIONAL_BODIES.filter((b) => ... || askedFor[b].length > 0)`). This one already had an in-memory, Finding-72-safe `open(closing_date)` re-check on every row AFTER the DB read (so its own in-memory logic was never wrong) - but the DB-level `.eq("tenders.status","open")`/`.eq("status","open")` filters, applied BEFORE that in-memory check, could silently exclude a genuinely-still-open (freshly-extended-by-corrigendum) tender from the result set before the correct logic ever got to see it - the exact direction that would make this function UNDER-promote real registration demand, the opposite of the safety margin this file's own comments elsewhere rely on ("a failed read just under-promotes... never a false claim that nothing needs it" - this was a second, unnoticed way to under-promote).

**Fixed directly on `main` - no PR.** Scoped narrowly: `tenders.status` itself is left completely untouched (deprecating or actively maintaining it live - e.g. a scheduled sweep, or writing it alongside `closing_date` in `accept_tender_update_date()` - is a bigger, separate architectural call, not mechanically obvious which way Sarel would want it, added as a new standing item rather than decided here). Both real consumers changed to derive "is this tender currently open" live from `closing_date` instead:
- `platform_admin_cv_document_stats()`: new migration `0125_platform_admin_cv_document_stats_live_status.sql` (`create or replace function`, same convention as 0084/0109/0115's own re-merges) - `where t.status = 'open'` became `where t.closing_date is null or t.closing_date >= now()`. Applied and verified against the scratch database above (both scenarios now return the correct count).
- `registrationsAskedFor()`: both `.eq("tenders.status", "open")` and `.eq("status", "open")` replaced with `.or("closing_date.is.null,closing_date.gte.now", ...)` (with `{ referencedTable: "tenders" }` on the joined query) - using Postgres's own special `'now'` timestamptz literal (confirmed live: `select 'now'::timestamptz = now()` → `t`) specifically so no client-side `Date.now()`/`new Date()` is needed before this file's own documented "'now' only after the request-time reads" Cache Components ordering rule (the exact rule this file's header comment already states and that a JS-side `now` would have broken). Comment rewritten to explain why `closing_date`, not `status`, and to flag the small, deliberate row-count trade-off (a wider, un-pre-filtered-by-status row set, still bounded by `fetchAllRows()`'s existing 20,000-row cap).

**Verified red-then-green.** `registrationsAskedFor()` had ZERO existing test coverage before this pass (confirmed by grep - no `personCredentials.spec.ts` existed at all). Added one (`app/lib/personCredentials.spec.ts`, 4 tests): a Finding-300 regression guard that asserts the exact `.or()` filter args used and that `.eq()` is never called at all, plus 3 end-to-end cases (a future-vs-past-closing_date general tender, a SANRAL `tender_requirements` case, and a null-closing_date "no date on file still counts as open" case - all new coverage for a previously-untested function). `git stash push -- app/lib/personCredentials.ts` (isolating only the production file): **red** - `npx vitest run lib/personCredentials.spec.ts` gave `3 passed | 1 failed`, exactly the new regression-guard test (`expected undefined to deeply equal [...]` - the old code never calls `.or()` at all). `git stash pop` to restore (never a plain `rm`/overwrite): **green** - `4/4` pass. Full regression: `npx vitest run` from `app/` - **76/76 files, 625/625 tests pass** (up from 75/621 - the 1 new file, 4 new tests, zero existing case changed). The separate `node --experimental-strip-types --test` loop over every `*.test.ts` file in the repo - 0 failures. `npx tsc --noEmit` - 0 errors. `npx eslint lib/personCredentials.ts lib/personCredentials.spec.ts` - 0 errors (the new migration SQL file has no ESLint config for `.sql`, expected).

**Severity, honestly scoped.** Not RLS/tenant-isolation, not money (no billing/quota logic reads `tenders.status` at all - re-confirmed by the same grep sweep above), not a document a company signs. An admin-only internal metric and a People-page UI badge/section-visibility gate - real, concretely demonstrated wrong answers, but neither security-critical nor revenue-critical. Squarely this track's own "small, safe fix → push directly to main" category: two narrowly-scoped, same-shape query fixes (one SQL `create or replace function`, one TS filter-expression swap), no RLS/money/hard-stop gate, no worker-image change, not a multi-RPC-across-multiple-tables schema surface, not a document a company signs/submits.

**New standing item added** (System-Status.md consolidated list, item 27): whether `tenders.status` should ever be actively kept live (a scheduled sweep, or writing it alongside `closing_date` inside `accept_tender_update_date()`) - or whether the column should instead be documented as "insert-time snapshot only, never trust it as live" and its remaining readers (just these two, now both fixed) left as the permanent pattern - is Sarel's own call, not decided here.

**Regression:** `app/supabase/migrations/0125_platform_admin_cv_document_stats_live_status.sql` (new, `create or replace function platform_admin_cv_document_stats()` only - same signature, same other 5 columns unchanged), `app/lib/personCredentials.ts` (`registrationsAskedFor()`'s two query filters + its own header comment; every other export unchanged), `app/lib/personCredentials.spec.ts` (new file, 4 tests, this function's first ever coverage).

To verify independently: from `app/`, `npx vitest run lib/personCredentials.spec.ts` (expect 4/4 pass). ## 2026-11-09vii (standing solution-architect review, background worker): Finding 301 - the task brief's own handed-down observation from Finding 300, investigated properly - `closing_date` really is never checked at any of the three layers before a company spends a real, limited pack-quota credit, confirmed a genuine oversight (not a documented product decision), fixed as a non-blocking Pack Review warning rather than a new hard stop

All three layers genuinely apply zero `closing_date` check, confirming pass `vi`'s own claim exactly, independently.

**Deliberate-feature vs. genuine-oversight, decided from the evidence, not assumed either way.** Grepped `docs/` (`strategy/` + `specs/`) for any stated reason to allow post-closing pack generation ("closed tender", "after closing", "past closing", "closing date...pack") - no hits describing this as an intentional design choice anywhere, including `docs/strategy/Tender-Tool-Competitor-Feature-Deep-Dive.md`'s own phased feature list (item 7, "pre-submission check... documents valid on the closing date" is about document validity windows, not about gating pack generation itself, and is listed as a partially-built feature, not a closed decision). Every OTHER gate in `requestSubmissionPack()`/`requestJob()` (unfilled position, missing template, unanswered B7, already-queued) exists specifically because generating past that point would be functionally wrong or wasted work - there is no comment or doc anywhere treating "tender already closed" as a legitimate reason to proceed, the way e.g. standing item 16 (RRM mapping) or item 24 (trial-countdown semantics) are explicitly recorded elsewhere in this same file/System-Status.md as deliberate choices. Conclusion: **genuine oversight, not a documented product decision** - the task brief's own binary test resolves to "fix it."

**Confirmed the real cost, not assumed.** `company_can_request_pack()`/`company_packs_this_period()` (migration `0115`, read in full): a `trialing` company gets exactly **ONE** pack, ever, before needing to upgrade; an `active` company gets its plan's own `max_packs_per_month` (billing-tier-limited, re-confirmed against `app/app/billing/page.tsx`'s own display of this exact function). So this is not a hypothetical - a trialing company who clicks "Generate submission pack" on a tender that closed yesterday spends their ONE lifetime trial credit with nothing on screen telling them the tender has closed before they click, beyond the pre-existing, un-tied-to-this-action `countdown`/"closed" badge on the page header (`lib/dates.ts`'s `closingCountdown()`, rendered at `page.tsx` line ~663 - present, but not referenced anywhere in the generate-pack gating or the Pack Review confirmation screen itself).

**Fix shape, deliberately NOT a new hard stop - the honest reasoning, not just "it was easier".** Considered and rejected hard-blocking `requestSubmissionPack()`/`requestJob()` on `closing_date < now()` the same way the existing hard stops work. A hard block on the actual credit-spend, on a field with ANY known staleness risk, would risk trading today's "silently wastes a credit" bug for "silently refuses a company that genuinely still needs this pack" - a strictly worse failure mode for a paid, quota-limited action (the first wastes money the company already has committed; the second could cost them a bid they were otherwise entitled to make). Instead, added a new, shared, non-blocking `ReviewStatus: "warning"` classifier, `closingDateStatus()`, surfaced inside the SAME conscious "I've reviewed this" gate (`pack_review_confirmations`, migration 0059) `requestSubmissionPack()`/`requestJob()` already require before spending the credit - the fact is now seen, not hidden, without creating a new way for imperfect data to block a legitimate request. This matches the existing precedent in this exact file for a real, non-disqualifying concern (`b7Status`'s warning branch, `positionStatus`'s "confirmed but flagged" branch) rather than inventing a new severity tier.

**Implementation.** `app/app/tenders/[id]/pack-review-logic.ts`: new exported `closingDateStatus(closingDate: string | null, now: Date)` - `null`/unparseable/future `closing_date` is `"confirmed"` (nothing to flag); a `closing_date` at-or-before `now` is `"warning"` with a note naming the real cost ("...will still spend a bid-pack credit"), deliberately phrased after this session's own Finding 300 to avoid another silent-drift surprise. Wired into BOTH review snapshots - `app/app/tenders/[id]/pack-review-data.ts` (SANRAL, reads `data.closingDate` already returned by `loadTenderCompliance()`) and `app/app/tenders/[id]/general-pack-review-data.ts` (general family, reads the `closing_date` the function already extracts at line 118) - each pushes one new section, `"Tender closing date"`, shown FIRST (ahead of every other section), since "is this tender even still open" is the single most decision-relevant fact on the whole screen. Both import `closingDateStatus` directly from `pack-review-logic.ts` rather than duplicating it - this check is generic (just a date comparison), not SANRAL-specific, the same precedent `general-pack-review-data.ts` already follows for `docItemStatus()`/`fieldStatus()` (see that file's own header comment), not the "two independent implementations" shape of standing item 18. `pack-review.tsx`/`general-pack-review.tsx` (the rendering components) needed NO changes at all - both already render `sections`/`items` generically; the existing `gapsCount` reducer (`sections.reduce(... status === "missing" || "warning" ...)`) automatically picks up the new warning with no changes either.

Full regression: `npx vitest run` from `app/` - **76/76 files, 625/625 tests pass**, unchanged from pass `vi`'s own baseline (this fix's own tests live in the `node --test` file, not a vitest spec, so the vitest count is correctly unaffected). Real and live-reachable: `send_digest_emails.py` runs on a real schedule (the daily digest's send step) and the specific failure modes it already alerts on (expired `RESEND_API_KEY`, Resend send failures) are realistic operational events an admin would want to see on the health dashboard, not a contrived edge case. ## 2026-11-09ix (standing solution-architect review, background worker): Finding 303 - `platform_admin_billing_overview()` silently returns `NULL` for "packs used this period" on virtually every company, because it calls the member-gated `company_packs_this_period()` as the admin's own (never-a-member) identity

**Angle chosen.** Option (d) from this pass's own task brief ("any RPC or server action not yet cross-checked against its own TS/SQL counterpart recently"), combined with re-reading every `SECURITY DEFINER` function in the pack-quota/billing family after this session's own Finding 300/301 (the same family, same day) rather than assuming it was already clean. Read `company_packs_this_period()`/`company_can_request_pack()`/`request_submission_pack_checked()`/`request_general_job_checked()` (migration `0115`, in full) and then, specifically because `0115`'s own header comment documents that `0109` had already once silently regressed a sibling fix in this exact function by doing a wholesale `create or replace function` without checking every existing caller, went looking for every OTHER caller of `company_packs_this_period()` to see whether `0109`'s added guard had done the same thing to a caller nobody re-checked.

**Found a real one.** `grep -rn "company_packs_this_period" app/supabase/migrations/` shows it is called from exactly 3 places: its own definition (`0083`/`0084`/`0109`/`0115`), `company_can_request_pack()`'s `active`-branch (same family, fine), and `platform_admin_billing_overview()` (`0101_telemetry_and_billing.sql:129`, predates `0109` by 8 migrations) - `select ... company_packs_this_period(c.id), ... from companies c join company_subscriptions cs ...`. `0109` added `is_company_member(p_company_id)` to `company_packs_this_period()`'s own body (confirmed by reading `0109`'s full diff directly, not assumed): `select case when is_company_member(p_company_id) then (...) else null end;` - correct and necessary for `company_packs_this_period()`'s two REAL callers, both of which run as an actual member checking their own company's own quota. But `platform_admin_billing_overview()` runs as the PLATFORM ADMIN's own `auth.uid()`, iterating every company on the platform in one query (`order by c.created_at desc`, no `company_id` filter) - and `is_company_member()` checks THAT SPECIFIC `auth.uid()` against THAT SPECIFIC company. A platform admin is, by this schema's own explicit design, never a company member (`platform_admins`' own table comment, `0043`: "Tender Tool's own staff who may use the internal admin console... Not a customer role - a company owner is NOT a platform admin"). So for every company the admin reviewing `/admin/billing` doesn't personally happen to belong to - which, by that same design, is every company on the platform except in the degenerate case an admin also happens to be seeded as a test-company member - `company_packs_this_period()` returns `NULL` instead of the real count, and `platform_admin_billing_overview()` passes that `NULL` straight through as its own `packs_used_this_period` column.

**Confirmed the real consumer, not assumed.** `app/app/admin/billing/page.tsx` (the Billing tab, Admin Command Center Phase 3) renders `{r.packs_used_this_period}{r.max_packs_per_month !== null ? ` / ${r.max_packs_per_month}` : " (unlimited)"}` directly from this RPC's own row - React silently renders nothing for a `null` child, so the cell shows a blank space before the slash (e.g. ` / 15`) instead of `1 / 15`, for virtually every row on the one screen whose whole job is showing Sarel the platform's own revenue/quota state at a glance.

**Reproduced red-then-green live, not assumed from reading SQL alone.** Started a scratch Postgres 16 cluster, created a fresh database, replayed the full schema with `engine/security/replay_schema.sh` (all 115 migrations through `0125`, clean). Seeded: a `platform_admins` row with deliberately NO matching `company_members` row anywhere (the normal, expected shape per `0043`'s own comment); one company with an `active` subscription (`max_packs_per_month = 15`, `current_period_start` = yesterday); one real `pack_generation_jobs` row, `status = 'requested'`, for that company. As the admin (`set role authenticated; select set_config('test.uid', '<admin uuid>', false)`):
- `is_platform_admin()` -> `true`. `is_company_member(<company>)` -> `false` (confirmed, not assumed).
- `company_packs_this_period(<company>)` called directly -> **NULL** (should be `1` - one real in-flight job).
- `platform_admin_billing_overview()` filtered to that company's row -> `packs_used_this_period` **NULL** - the exact same gap, through the real RPC the admin page actually calls, not just the helper function in isolation.

Applied the fix (new migration `0126`, below), reran the identical queries against the same live database: `platform_admin_billing_overview()`'s `packs_used_this_period` for that row -> **1**, correct.

**Regression-checked both paths the fix must NOT touch, live, not assumed.** (1) A real company member (`company_members` row, role `owner`) calling `company_packs_this_period()` for their OWN company still gets `1` - the `0109`/`0115` membership guard on that function's own two real callers is completely untouched by this fix. (2) A plain authenticated user who is neither a platform admin nor a member of anything calling `platform_admin_billing_overview()` directly still gets **0 rows** - the function's own `where is_platform_admin()` gate is completely untouched.

**Fix.** New migration `app/supabase/migrations/0126_platform_admin_billing_overview_not_a_member.sql`: `create or replace function platform_admin_billing_overview()` with the exact same signature and every other column unchanged, but `packs_used_this_period` is now computed INLINE with its own correlated subquery (`select count(*)::integer from pack_generation_jobs j where j.company_id = c.id and j.status in ('requested','generating','ready') and j.requested_at >= coalesce(cs.current_period_start, c.created_at)`) - the identical counting rule `0084`/`0115` already established for `company_packs_this_period()` itself, just evaluated under `platform_admin_billing_overview()`'s own pre-existing `is_platform_admin()` gate instead of routing through the member-gated helper. `company_packs_this_period()` itself is byte-for-byte unchanged - this fix touches ONLY the one caller that was never a company member by construction, leaving the function's own two real member-facing callers and their `0109`/`0115` guard exactly as they were.

**Severity and direction, honestly scoped.** NOT a tenant-isolation or authorization-bypass bug - the opposite direction: this is an under-disclosure to an already-fully-authorized platform admin (a blank value an admin shouldn't have had to see), not an over-disclosure of one company's data to a different, unauthorized company or user. No RLS policy changed, no new grant added, `is_platform_admin()`'s own gate is completely unchanged - a platform admin could already see every other column on this exact row (plan, status, trial/period dates, whether a PayFast token is on file) with no gap at all; only the one derived quota-count column was broken. Real and live-reachable the moment `0109` applied (2026-11-03/04, per that migration's own dating) - this has been silently wrong on the admin Billing tab for every company on the platform since then, with nothing anywhere surfacing an error (a `NULL` from a `SECURITY DEFINER` SQL function is not an exception - it's a valid, silent return value).

**Why opened as a PR, not pushed directly to `main`.** This is a SQL change to a `SECURITY DEFINER` RPC squarely inside the billing/quota surface this session's own Findings 300/301 (same day) already treated as "lean toward PR" territory, even though - like Finding 301's own fix - it is read-only/display-only and touches no RLS policy, no money-movement logic (PayFast), and no actual quota enforcement (`company_can_request_pack()`/`request_submission_pack_checked()`/`request_general_job_checked()` are all completely untouched; a company's own real ability to request a pack, and the real credit-spend, are unaffected by this fix either way). ## 2026-11-09x (standing solution-architect review, background worker): Finding 304 - `app/app/pipeline/page.tsx`'s own inline copy of `lib/dealEconomics.ts`'s `clientLabel()` rule drifted the day it was mirrored, and nobody noticed because `clientLabel()` itself had zero test coverage

**Angle chosen.** Technique from this track's own brief: grep every "mirrors"/"same rule as"/"must match" comment in `app/` and read both sides directly rather than trusting the claim. `lib/dealEconomics.ts`'s own header comment on `clientLabel()` reads: `/** Client: the buyer, or SANRAL for the SANRAL families (same rule as /pipeline cards). */` - a direct, checkable claim that `app/app/pipeline/page.tsx`'s own card-building code computes the identical thing. Read both sides.

**The two rules, side by side.** `app/app/pipeline/page.tsx` (line 287, before this fix):
```
buyer: t.buyer || (t.family && t.family !== GENERAL_FAMILY ? "SANRAL" : "(unknown buyer)"),
```
`lib/dealEconomics.ts`'s `clientLabel()`:
```
export function clientLabel(buyer: string | null, family: string | null): string {
  return buyer || (family && family !== GENERAL_FAMILY && family !== "UNKNOWN" ? "SANRAL" : "(unknown buyer)");
}
```
Not identical: `clientLabel()` has one extra condition, `&& family !== "UNKNOWN"`, that the Pipeline board's own inline copy never had.

**Is `family === "UNKNOWN"` a real, reachable state, not a hypothetical?** Yes, confirmed from three independent places, not assumed: (1) `app/supabase/migrations/0001_init_schema.sql`'s own column comment: `family text, -- "Conventional Consultant Tender" | "RRM Consultant Tender" | "UNKNOWN"` - `"UNKNOWN"` was a documented, intended value for this column from the very first migration, not a later accident. (2) It is still actively written today: `engine/intake/classify_tender.py`'s `classify_documents()` sets `family = winner[2]` (the Technical Submission workbook's own fingerprinted family) whenever a real SANRAL workbook is found (`route = "sanral"`) - and `winner[2]` is exactly `engine/fingerprint.py`'s `detect_family()` return value, which itself returns the literal string `"UNKNOWN"` when the workbook's sheet set doesn't match either known SANRAL template. So a tender can be genuinely `route="sanral"` (because a real SANRAL workbook was found and the submission-pack flow applies) while `family` is persisted as `"UNKNOWN"` (because WHICH SANRAL sub-family it is couldn't be told from the workbook alone) - `engine/general/process_general_jobs.py` then writes this straight to `tenders.family` via `patch["family"] = decision["family"]`. (3) `lib/pastSubmissionReuse.ts`'s own canonical `SANRAL_PACK_FAMILIES = ["Conventional Consultant Tender", "RRM Consultant Tender"]` - the list every other "is this tender SANRAL" check in this app already keys off (`packKindFor()`) - deliberately does NOT include `"UNKNOWN"`, i.e. the app's own canonical answer is that an `"UNKNOWN"`-family tender is NOT one of the two real SANRAL sub-families for app-side purposes. `clientLabel()`'s exclusion agrees with this canonical list; the Pipeline board's own inline copy did not.

**Reproduced (logical, not a live DB query - a pure-function disagreement needs no database).** Ran both rules, side by side, for `buyer = null, family = "UNKNOWN"` (a buyer-less tender stuck at an unresolved SANRAL sub-family - reachable e.g. via a pursued `discovered_opportunities` row whose own `buyer` field was never captured, `engine/discovery/source_http.py`'s own default dict: `"buyer": None`):
```
pipeline/page.tsx inline rule -> "SANRAL"
lib/dealEconomics.ts clientLabel() -> "(unknown buyer)"
MISMATCH (bug reproduced)
```
Confirmed red. The live consequence: for such a tender, the Pipeline board's own card (`/pipeline`) showed "SANRAL" as the client, while `/pipeline/pricing` (same row, via `clientLabel()`) and the tender's own Market context section (`app/app/tenders/[id]/market-context.tsx`'s `isSanral`, which uses the identical `family !== GENERAL_FAMILY && family !== "UNKNOWN"` test) both correctly showed "(unknown buyer)" for the exact same tender at the exact same time - a direct, visible, three-screen disagreement about who the buyer is, not a cosmetic rounding difference.

**Why the drift happened, confirmed from git history, not guessed.** `git log -S` on both files: `app/app/pipeline/page.tsx`'s inline rule was added at commit `b45f4e4` (2026-10-17 07:40 UTC). `lib/dealEconomics.ts`'s `clientLabel()` was added roughly 7.5 hours later the same day, commit `f2cb3cd` (2026-10-17 15:15 UTC), with the `family !== "UNKNOWN"` exclusion already present from its very first version - i.e. `clientLabel()` was written as a deliberately slightly-more-correct mirror of the Pipeline board's own rule, and that one extra condition was never back-ported to the original. `app/app/pipeline/page.tsx` had exactly one commit touching that line in its entire history (confirmed via `git log --follow -S`) - it was never revisited since.

**Why nobody caught it in three weeks.** `clientLabel()` had NO test coverage at all (`lib/dealEconomics.spec.ts` existed only for `needsCreditFallbackOption()`, a completely different function in the same file) - the exact "canonical rule with no test pinning it, so a sibling copy can drift silently" shape this track's own brief flags as worth checking. `app/app/pipeline/page.tsx` itself is a server component page and, per its own header comment ("this file is a server component page, which can't itself be unit-tested"), deliberately extracts testable logic into `lib/pipelineCardHelpers.ts` - but this one piece of business logic was never extracted, so it had no test of its own either, on either side of the mirror.

**Fix.** `app/app/pipeline/page.tsx`: removed the inline reimplementation, imported `clientLabel` from `@/lib/dealEconomics` (a module this file already imports `derivedSector`/`ECONOMICS_COLUMNS`/`formatRand`/`toNumber`/`PackEconomics`/`PriceSector` from - not a new dependency) and used it directly: `buyer: clientLabel(t.buyer, t.family)`. One rule, not two, going forward - any future refinement to `clientLabel()` (e.g. if a new family value is added) now reaches the Pipeline board automatically instead of needing a second, easily-forgotten edit. `GENERAL_FAMILY`'s own import stays (still used at two other call sites in the same file). `lib/dealEconomics.ts` itself: untouched, already correct.

**Severity and why this was pushed directly, not opened as a PR.** Small, scoped (2 files), display-only (a label string on the Pipeline board) - no RLS, no money-movement, no quota/credit-spend logic, no hard-stop gate, no signed/submitted-document content, no worker image, no multi-RPC schema surface. Per this track's own guardrails, a fix of this shape goes straight to `main`.

**Verified.** `npx tsc --noEmit` - 0 errors. `npx eslint app/pipeline/page.tsx lib/dealEconomics.ts lib/dealEconomics.spec.ts` - 0 errors/warnings. `npx vitest run` - **76/76 test files, 630/630 tests pass** (625 before this pass + 5 new `clientLabel()` cases added below). `npx vitest run lib/dealEconomics.spec.ts` on its own - 9/9 pass (4 pre-existing `needsCreditFallbackOption()` + 5 new).

**Regression:** `app/app/pipeline/page.tsx` (one import line widened, one field's value expression replaced - nothing else in the file touched); `app/lib/dealEconomics.spec.ts` (5 new `describe("clientLabel", ...)` cases added - first-ever coverage for this function - 0 existing tests changed). `lib/dealEconomics.ts` itself: byte-for-byte unchanged.

**Backlog status.** No new standing item opened - this is a plain, mechanical "hand-copied rule drifted from the canonical version it claims to mirror, with no test on either side to catch it" bug with one unambiguous fix, the same general bug class as Findings 240-243/249/293/294/302 (independent occurrences of "two surfaces claiming to show the same thing, one of them wrong"), not a judgment call for Sarel.

To verify independently: from `app/`, `npx vitest run lib/dealEconomics.spec.ts` (expect 9/9 pass, including the 5 new `clientLabel` cases - in particular `clientLabel(null, "UNKNOWN")` returning `"(unknown buyer)"`). Confirm `app/app/pipeline/page.tsx` imports `clientLabel` from `@/lib/dealEconomics` and its card-building loop calls `clientLabel(t.buyer, t.family)` rather than reimplementing the rule inline.

## 2026-11-10 (standing solution-architect review, background worker): Finding 305 - both Pack Review screens' own "has this position/role got a usable CV" check keyed off `generated_cvs.status` alone, while both real pack-build engines also require `storage_path_pdf` to be set - a case `process_cv_jobs.py` itself documents as reachable (LibreOffice's docx->pdf conversion failing on an otherwise-'ready' job)

**Angle chosen.** The task brief's own named technique: a comment claiming "mirrors"/"same rule as" another file, checked directly, with the underlying mechanism verified independently rather than just the two values compared. `general-pack-review-logic.ts`'s own header comment names `roleStatus()` as doing "the same `generated_cvs`/`cv_uploads` lookup `process_general_jobs.py`'s `gather_pack_inputs` does when it actually builds the pack - kept in sync so this screen never promises a CV the pack itself can't find." Read `gather_pack_inputs()` (`engine/general/process_general_jobs.py`, lines 731-752) in full to check that claim against the real code, rather than trusting the comment.

**Found (CONFIRMED).** `gather_pack_inputs()`'s own CV-gathering loop (line 740-742) only accepts a `generated_cvs` row with `status='ready'` AND a non-null `storage_path_pdf`:
```python
gen = [g for g in client.select("generated_cvs", {"person_id": tag["person_id"], "company_id": job["company_id"],
                                                  "status": "ready"}, order="requested_at.desc")
       if g.get("storage_path_pdf")]
```
`general-pack-review-data.ts`'s own query building `withCv`/`haveCv` (feeding `roleStatus()`) checked only `status="ready"`, nothing else:
```ts
supabase.from("generated_cvs").select("person_id").in("person_id", taggedIds).eq("status", "ready"),
```
So the comment's claim ("kept in sync ... never promises a CV the pack itself can't find") was false in exactly the one case worth checking - a `'ready'` row with no PDF.

**Confirmed the same gap on the SANRAL sibling screen too, not assumed from the general-tender comment alone.** `engine/pack/process_pack_jobs.py`'s own CV-gathering loop (lines 701-702) has the byte-for-byte identical extra condition: `g.get("storage_path_pdf")`. `pack-review-data.ts`'s own `hasCv`/`cvStatus` (feeding `positionStatus()`) checked only `p.tenderCv?.status === "ready"` - the identical gap, independently present on both families' review screens, each built by a different author at a different time (the general-tender file's own docstring explicitly claims to follow the SANRAL file's precedent, but this one specific rule was never actually copied across, in either direction).

**Confirmed this is a real, live-reachable server state, not a hypothetical.** `engine/cv/process_cv_jobs.py` (lines 405-415): when `generate_cv._convert_to_pdf()` fails (LibreOffice crashes/hangs on the worker), `storage_path_pdf` stays `None`, the job is still `PATCH`ed to `"status": "ready"` (the Word document is still a real, deliverable CV on its own), and a `system_alerts.record("cv", "A CV was generated but its PDF conversion failed (LibreOffice) - only the .docx was delivered", "warning", ...)` is explicitly raised for exactly this case - so the production code already anticipates and alerts on this state; the two Pack Review screens were simply never told to check for it.

**Real consequence, traced end to end.** For a key person/role whose ONLY `generated_cvs` row is in this exact state, and who has no separate `cv_uploads` "as-is" upload on file: `positionStatus()`/`roleStatus()` both received `hasCv`/`taggedWithCvCount` as `true`/counted, so the review screen showed **"Tender-specific CV ready."** (SANRAL) / **"included"**, no warning, no note - while the real pack build (`process_pack_jobs.py`'s `cvs[p["code"]] = {"reason": f"no ready tender CV and no as-is CV upload for {name}"}` / `process_general_jobs.py`'s equivalent) would silently produce a submission pack with **no CV at all** for that position/role. A company could confidently spend a pack-quota credit (`request_submission_pack_checked()`/`request_general_job_checked()`, migration 0115) believing a specific person's CV was confirmed ready, and only discover the gap after opening the generated PDF.

**Fixed, not pushed directly - opened as PR #211.** Added one shared, pure predicate to `pack-review-logic.ts` (the file `general-pack-review-logic.ts`'s own header comment already names as the place to put generic, non-SANRAL-specific classifiers rather than duplicating them):
```ts
export function tenderCvUsable(tenderCv: { status: string; storage_path_pdf: string | null } | null | undefined): boolean {
  return !!(tenderCv && tenderCv.status === "ready" && tenderCv.storage_path_pdf);
}
```
`compliance-data.ts`'s `GeneratedCvRow` type and its `generated_cvs` select widened to carry `storage_path_pdf` through to `pack-review-data.ts`'s `p.tenderCv`. `pack-review-data.ts`'s `hasCv` now calls `tenderCvUsable(p.tenderCv)`; its `cvNote` now has its own explicit "ready but no PDF" branch (distinct wording from a genuinely ready CV, and from the as-is-upload-used branch, depending on whether `p.cv` exists as a fallback). `general-pack-review-data.ts`'s `generated_cvs` select widened to also fetch `storage_path_pdf`, and `haveCv` now filters through the same `tenderCvUsable()` before counting a tagged person as having a usable CV. Neither pack-build engine (`process_pack_jobs.py`/`process_general_jobs.py`) was touched - this is purely a pre-generation display/warning fix, the same category Finding 301 already established for this exact screen family.

**Why opened as a PR, not pushed directly to `main`.** Display-only/informational (no RLS, no money-movement, no quota-enforcement RPC touched - `company_can_request_pack()`/`request_submission_pack_checked()`/`request_general_job_checked()` are all completely unaffected), but it sits on the same non-blocking Pack Review screen, right before a company spends a real pack-quota credit, that Finding 301 (same session family, 2026-11-09) already treated as "lean toward PR" territory for that reason alone. Opened as **PR #211** (`finding-305-pack-review-cv-pdf-usable`, against `main`'s HEAD at the time, `555b3b2`, 1 commit, 5 files, +79/-13) and stopped there - not merged, per this track's own binding guardrail.

**Verified red-then-green.** Added `tenderCvUsable()` coverage to `pack-review-logic.test.ts` (6 checks: ready+pdf is usable; ready+null is not; requested/failed/null/undefined are all not). `git stash push -- "app/app/tenders/[id]/pack-review-logic.ts"` (reverting only the new export, keeping the rest of the diff staged), re-ran: **red** - `SyntaxError: The requested module './pack-review-logic.ts' does not provide an export named 'tenderCvUsable'`, 0 pass / 1 fail. `git stash pop` to restore (never a plain `rm`/overwrite), confirmed `git status` clean of anything unexpected: **green** - `node --experimental-strip-types --test` on `pack-review-logic.test.ts` + `general-pack-review-logic.test.ts` - **43/43 pass** (was 42/42, +1 new, 0 existing changed). Full regression: `npx vitest run` from `app/` - **76/76 files, 630/630 tests pass** (unchanged baseline - no vitest spec touched, the new test lives in the `node --test` file). The separate per-file `node --experimental-strip-types --test` loop over all 31 `*.test.ts` files - 0 failures. `npx tsc --noEmit` - 0 errors. `npx eslint` on all 5 touched files - 0 errors.

**Backlog status.** No new standing item opened - a plain, mechanical "a stated sync/mirror invariant wasn't actually checked for one real case" bug with one unambiguous, shared fix (the same general bug class as Findings 240-243/249/293/294/302/304 - independent occurrences of "two surfaces claiming to show/do the same thing, one of them wrong"), not a judgment call for Sarel. Extended standing item 20 (now fourteen open-PR Findings awaiting review, adding PR #211/Finding 305) and item 23 (backlog now 38, `#164`/`#165`/`#176`-`#211`) in `System-Status.md`'s one consolidated section.

To verify independently: from `app/app/tenders/[id]/`, `node --experimental-strip-types --test pack-review-logic.test.ts` (expect 43/43 pass, including the new `tenderCvUsable` cases). Open PR #211's diff (`gh pr diff 211`, read-only, or `gh api repos/sareljvr2024/tender-tool/pulls/211` given this sandbox's own GraphQL restriction) and confirm it matches this description: one new shared predicate in `pack-review-logic.ts`, both `-data.ts` files' CV queries widened to select `storage_path_pdf` and filter through it, neither pack-build engine touched.

### Finding 306 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, moderate - `engine/company_documents.py`'s `produce()` sanitized an uploaded company letter's filename by CHARACTER only, never by LENGTH - the identical bug class already fixed once in this exact engine (`generate_cv.py`'s `_safe_name()`, Finding 227) but present, unfixed, in a different file - an extremely long `original_filename` (stored raw/untruncated by the TypeScript side) crashes with `OSError: File name too long` the instant the file copy runs, and `assemble_pack.py`'s own call into this function has no try/except around it, so this one crashes the WHOLE SANRAL pack build, not just the authority letter)

**Area:** `engine/company_documents.py` (`produce()`, "uploaded" mode). Test coverage added to the existing `engine/test_company_documents.py` (new case "6d.", 1 test + 3 assertions).

**How this was found.** This cycle's rotation landed on SANRAL pack. Mention-count survey put `engine/fill_authority_letter.py` (17 mentions, 83 lines) as the lowest-covered file in the area. Read it in full - a thin CLI wrapper that calls `company_documents.authority_facts()`/`company_documents.produce()` for the real logic, so moved to that module next (67 total mentions, still comparatively light given the extensive, already-fixed history visible in its own comments - a SAST-date fix, Finding 227's own filename-truncation precedent cited by name, and a 2026-11-06 control-character fix explicitly noting "assemble_pack.py's own call to produce_letter() has no try/except around it, so this crashed the WHOLE pack build" for a DIFFERENT code path in the SAME function family, `write_docx()`). Reading `produce()`'s "uploaded" branch adversarially, with that exact "no try/except around this call" exposure already proven true elsewhere in the same file: `fname = re.sub(r"[^A-Za-z0-9._ ()-]+", "_", template.get("original_filename") or os.path.basename(src))` sanitizes forbidden CHARACTERS but never bounds LENGTH - the identical gap Finding 227 already found and fixed once in this engine, in `generate_cv.py`'s sibling `_safe_name()` function, just not here.

**Confirmed live, not inferred, and traced to its real, reachable source.** Checked where `original_filename` actually comes from: `app/company/actions.ts`'s `saveDocumentTemplate()` sets `row.original_filename = file.name` directly from the uploaded `File` object - the STORAGE PATH is sanitized through `safeFileName.ts`'s own `.slice(0, 120)` truncation, but this separate DB column is stored raw and untruncated. A multipart form POST to this Server Action need not come from a real browser file picker (which practically caps filename length) - a crafted request can set an arbitrarily long filename. Built a direct reproduction: a real `.docx` source file, `template = {"mode": "uploaded", "path": src, "original_filename": "A"*5000 + ".docx"}`, passed straight into the real, unmodified `company_documents.produce("authority_to_sign", template, {}, out_dir, log, company="Test Co")`. Pre-fix: `OSError: [Errno 36] File name too long`, raised from `shutil.copyfile(src, dest)` - and since `produce()`/`produce_letter()` return normally in every OTHER failure path (not-set-up, missing upload, as a dict with a `status` field), `assemble_pack.py`'s own call site has no reason to wrap this one call in a try/except either, so this propagates straight out of the whole SANRAL pack build for every tender that company has, not just this one letter.

**Fix.** After the existing character-sanitizing regex, cap the result at 120 characters (matching `safeFileName.ts`'s own convention exactly - not `generate_cv.py`'s 80, which is deliberately smaller because that function returns only a name PORTION with further suffixes appended afterward; here the sanitized name IS the complete filename component), splitting the extension off first and re-appending it after truncating the stem, so a `.docx`/`.pdf` extension survives intact rather than being chopped off mid-truncation - the extension is what downstream PDF conversion uses to recognise the file type.

**Verified red-then-green.** Added case "6d." to the existing `test_company_documents.py` (same structure, same `profile()`/`TENDER`/`RFP` fixtures, same style as the immediately-preceding "6c." control-character case it sits right next to): a real 5000-character `original_filename`, asserting `produce_letter()` doesn't raise `OSError`, the letter is still produced (`status: "uploaded"`), the `.docx` extension survives, and the final basename fits a real filesystem (`<= 255` chars). **Red:** saved the diff to `company_documents.py` only, `git apply -R`, re-ran `python3 test_company_documents.py` directly - `1 failure(s)`, exactly the new "6d." case (`FAIL an extremely long uploaded filename must not crash with OSError`), every other case including the sibling "6c." control-character case untouched. **Green:** `git apply` to reapply, re-ran - `0 failure(s)`. `python3 -m py_compile` clean on both files. Regression: the two real callers of `company_documents.py` - `engine/pack/test_assemble_pack.py` and `engine/pack/test_process_pack_jobs.py` - both re-run directly, both `0 failure(s)`, unaffected.

**Not escalated to a PR.** Small, safe, self-contained Python fix (one length cap added to one existing sanitizer, no new failure branch - every real caller already handles this function's own `status`/`path`/`reason` return shape unchanged) - no RLS, no migration, no money path, no worker-image change. Pushed directly to `main`.

**Backlog status.** No new backlog items opened by this fix. `git fetch origin main` immediately before starting (clean, `main` at `da6972d`/Finding 305, matching the task brief's own stated current state) and again immediately before pushing this commit, both clean - no sibling commit landed in between.

To verify independently: from `engine/`, `python3 test_company_documents.py` (expect `0 failure(s)`, including the new "6d." case). `python3 -m py_compile company_documents.py` (clean). Separately, `app/company/actions.ts`'s `saveDocumentTemplate()` storing the raw, untruncated `file.name` into `company_document_templates.original_filename` (rather than also running it through `safeFileName.ts`) is a related, smaller inconsistency left as-is this pass - the engine-side fix here is the one that actually prevents the crash regardless of what the TS side ever stores, and widening that column's own write path is a separate, TS-side decision this pass didn't need to make to close the real bug.

## 2026-11-10c (standing solution-architect review, background worker): Finding 307 - `lib/locality.ts`'s `similar()` used a plain Levenshtein ratio while `engine/discovery/score_outlook.py`'s `_area_matches()` (the file's own claimed mirror) uses `difflib.SequenceMatcher.ratio()` - a different similarity metric for the identical 0.85 threshold, confirmed to disagree on a real South African municipality name

**Renumbered from 306 to 307 by the orchestrating session during a `git rebase` onto `origin/main`**: this entry was originally written and locally committed as "Finding 306", but a sibling session's own, unrelated Finding 306 (`company_documents.py`'s filename-length crash, immediately above) landed on `origin/main` first while this commit's `git push` was blocked pending a human decision (see System-Status.md). Renumbered to the next free number, 307, to avoid two different findings sharing one number; no other content changed.

**Angle chosen.** Continuing this track's own named technique: grep every "mirrors"/"same rule as"/"kept in sync" comment in `app/` and read both sides directly. `lib/locality.ts`'s header: "Same rules as `engine/discovery/score_outlook.py match_locality()`, which does this for discovered tenders; this is the Tender Workspace's copy." Its own `similar()` function carried a second claim in its inline comment: "Levenshtein distance, as a ratio of the longer name." Read `score_outlook.py`'s own `_area_matches()`/`_norm_area_words()` (lines 533-697) directly rather than trusting either comment.

**The two rules, side by side.** `score_outlook.py`'s `_area_matches()` (line 692): `difflib.SequenceMatcher(None, a, v).ratio() >= 0.85`. `lib/locality.ts`'s `similar()` (before this fix): a hand-rolled Levenshtein edit-distance table, converted to a ratio via `1 - editDistance / max(len)`, also compared `>= 0.85`. `difflib.SequenceMatcher.ratio()` is the Ratcliff/Obershelp algorithm - it finds the longest common matching BLOCK of characters recursively and sums matched-block lengths (`2*matched/(len(a)+len(b))`) - a fundamentally different computation from counting single-character edit operations. The two metrics agree on many inputs (both are "how similar are these strings" measures) but are not the same function and are not guaranteed to agree at any fixed threshold.

**Confirmed the two metrics actually disagree, not just theoretically different.** Fuzz-tested both implementations (a faithful JS port of `difflib.SequenceMatcher.ratio()`, validated byte-for-byte against the real Python output for 20,000 randomly generated near-miss string pairs before being trusted - 0 disagreement with real `difflib`) against the OLD Levenshtein-ratio code: of 20,000 random single-to-four-edit near-miss pairs, **4,756 (≈24%) crossed the 0.85 threshold differently** between the two metrics. This is not an edge-of-float-precision gap - it is the expected behavior of two different similarity algorithms compared against the same fixed cutoff.

**Confirmed with a real, reachable South African municipality name, not a synthetic string.** `engine/discovery/test_score_outlook.py`'s own canonical sweep-test list of ~140 real SA municipality/district names includes `"Ditsobotla"` (a real North West local municipality). Tested the plausible single-transposition typo a buyer's own tender points table could make the same way TN051/2026 misspelled "Dawid Kruiper" as "Dawid Kruper" (this file's own pre-existing, still-passing test case) - `"Ditsobolta"`:
```
difflib.SequenceMatcher(None, "ditsobotla", "ditsobolta").ratio()  -> 0.900  (matches, >= 0.85)
old Levenshtein ratio("ditsobotla", "ditsobolta")                  -> 0.800  (does NOT match, < 0.85)
```
Reproduced live through `matchLocality()`: a `LocalityRow` with `area: "Ditsobolta"` against a `CompanyOffice` with `local_municipality: "Ditsobotla"` returned `status: "no_match"` on the old code.

**Real consequence, traced to a disqualifying gate.** `lib/locality.ts`'s own docstring already names "Dawid Kruiper (local 20 + a mandatory local office)" as a real, live locality row that can be `mandatory`+`disqualifies`. `general-pack-review-logic.ts`'s `localityStatus()` turns a `no_match` on such a row into `{ reviewStatus: "missing", checklistStatus: "not_included" }` - shown on the Pack Review / Tender Workspace screens as a hard compliance gap ("Local office in Ditsobolta" - missing), even though the real engine-side match (`score_outlook.py`'s `_area_matches()`, via `difflib`) would correctly recognise the company's real "Ditsobotla" office and find no gap at all. (The actual pack-generation button itself is gated only on the separate "I've reviewed this" confirmation, `pack_review_confirmations.reviewed_at` - `general-actions.ts`'s `requestJob()` - not on this item's own status, so this is a display/review-accuracy bug, not a code-enforced block; still a real, visible, wrong "disqualifying" signal on the one screen whose whole job is to catch gaps before a company spends a pack-generation credit.)

**Fix.** Replaced the Levenshtein computation inside `similar()` with `ratcliffObershelpRatio()`, a faithful JS port of `difflib.SequenceMatcher(None, a, b).ratio()` for this module's own inputs (no `isjunk`; CPython's autojunk heuristic only activates for a 200+ character sequence with a character appearing in over 1% of it, which municipality/office names can never reach, so it is deliberately not ported - documented inline). The 0.85 threshold, the whole-word-substring fallback (`wordIn`/`normAreaWords`), and every other rule in the file are untouched - only the one metric `similar()` feeds into the threshold check changed, to match what the Python side has always actually used.

**Verified red-then-green.** Added a new `matchLocality` test case (`lib/locality.spec.ts`) pinning the real `"Ditsobotla"`/`"Ditsobolta"` case to `status: "matched"`. `git stash push -- app/lib/locality.ts` (keeping the new test), re-ran: **red** - `expected 'no_match' to be 'matched'`, 6 passed / 1 failed. `git stash pop` to restore (never a plain `rm`/overwrite): **green** - `npx vitest run lib/locality.spec.ts` - 7/7 pass, including the pre-existing "Dawid Kruper"/"Dawid Kruiper" Levenshtein-ratio test (still passes: 0.957 under the real metric too, so no existing case regressed). `git status` confirmed clean of anything unexpected throughout.

**Full regression.** `npx tsc --noEmit` from `app/` - 0 errors. `npx eslint lib/locality.ts lib/locality.spec.ts` - 0 errors/warnings. `npx vitest run` - **76/76 test files, 631/631 tests pass** (630 before this pass + 1 new).

**Regression:** `app/lib/locality.ts` (`similar()`'s internal ratio computation replaced; nothing else in the file touched - same exported function signatures, same 0.85 threshold, same word-boundary fallback); `app/lib/locality.spec.ts` (1 new test case added, 0 existing cases changed).

**Backlog status.** No new standing item opened - a plain, mechanical "hand-copied rule used a different underlying algorithm than the canonical version it claims to mirror, with no cross-engine fuzz test on either side to catch it" bug with one unambiguous fix, the same general bug class as Findings 240-243/249/293/294/302/304 (independent occurrences of "two surfaces claiming to compute the same thing, one of them wrong") - pushed directly per this track's own guardrails (small, 2-file, display/review-accuracy fix; no RLS, no money-movement, no quota-enforcement RPC, no hard-stop code gate - the actual "Generate pack" action is gated only by the separate reviewed-confirmation flag - no signed/submitted-document content, no worker image, no multi-RPC schema surface).

To verify independently: from `app/`, `npx vitest run lib/locality.spec.ts` (expect 7/7 pass, including the new `Ditsobotla`/`Ditsobolta` case). Independently check `difflib.SequenceMatcher(None, "ditsobotla", "ditsobolta").ratio()` in a plain Python shell (no repo dependency needed) returns `0.9`, confirming the real engine-side metric this fix now matches.

## 2026-11-10d (standing solution-architect review, background worker, pass `vvv`): Finding 311 - `process_pack_jobs.py`'s `gather()` built its as-is-CV-upload local download path from the raw, TypeScript-unbounded `original_filename`, not the real `storage_path` - Finding 306's exact unbounded-filename-length `OSError` crash class, recurring in a third, independent file

**Angle chosen.** Continued the task brief's own named technique (grep every "mirrors"/"same rule as"/"kept in sync" comment and read both real sides) across files not yet checked by any prior pass. Most candidates found this pass (`SizeOfficesSection.tsx` vs `EditForm.tsx`, `intake-card.tsx` vs `lib/generalTender.ts`'s `JOB_STATUS_STYLE`, `discovery/page.tsx` vs `pipeline/page.tsx`, `billing/page.tsx` vs `/api/billing/checkout`, `send-returnables-digest.ts` vs `send-deadline-reminders.ts`) checked out clean on direct inspection - each pair genuinely matches. Then pivoted to Finding 306's own already-established bug class (character-sanitized-but-not-length-capped free-text filenames used in a local filesystem path) and swept every real `original_filename` consumer in `engine/` by grep, rather than trusting that Finding 306's own fix (one file, `company_documents.py`) was the only site.

**Found a third, independent, genuinely unfixed site.** `engine/pack/process_pack_jobs.py`'s `gather()` (the SANRAL pack-build bridge's own input-gathering step) has, right next to the already-safe `g`/generated-CV branch (`os.path.basename(g["storage_path_pdf"])` - an engine-written, already-sanitized path), a sibling `u`/as-is-CV-upload branch that instead did:
```python
local = client.download("cv-documents", u["storage_path"],
                        os.path.join(work, "cvs", p["code"], os.path.basename(u["original_filename"])))
```
`u["storage_path"]` (the real object key, used correctly for the actual download call and for `own_path()`'s own cross-tenant ownership check immediately above) is always short and safe - it already went through `app/lib/safeFileName.ts`'s `.slice(0, 120)` truncation before ever being written to storage. `u["original_filename"]` is a separate DB column, confirmed by reading every real writer: `app/app/my-cv/actions.ts`'s `uploadMyCv()` and `app/app/people/actions.ts`'s `uploadCv()`/`createPersonWithCv()`/`bulkUploadCvs()` (lines 372/522/564) all set `original_filename: file.name` directly from the uploaded `File` object, completely unsanitized and unbounded - the identical "free text, no length cap, a crafted multipart POST need not come from a real browser file picker" reachability Finding 306 already confirmed for `company_documents.py`'s own `original_filename` column (`app/company/actions.ts`'s `saveDocumentTemplate()`). This file's own local destination path was built from that raw, unbounded value, not the safe one - even though the safe one (`storage_path`) was sitting right there in the same row and was already used correctly two lines above for ownership validation.

**Confirmed the general engine's equivalent code does NOT have this bug, which is what exposed it as a real inconsistency rather than a theoretical risk.** `engine/general/process_general_jobs.py`'s own CV-gathering code (`run_pack()`'s role-CV loop, ~line 748) does the equivalent as-is-upload case as `src = (CV_BUCKET, up[0]["storage_path"])` then `os.path.basename(src[1])` - i.e. it already uses `storage_path`, never `original_filename`, for exactly this purpose. `process_pack_jobs.py`'s own sibling `g`-branch two lines above the bug does the same correct thing for the generated-CV case. The as-is-upload branch in this one file, in this one engine, was the only place in the whole codebase doing it the unsafe way - confirmed by grep (`grep -rn "original_filename" engine/ --include=*.py`): every other real consumer (`fill_authority_letter.py`, `process_onboarding_jobs.py`, `company_documents.py` post-Finding-306) either builds the name itself or has already been fixed.

**Real consequence.** An "as-is" CV upload (no AI extraction, used exactly as filed - a real, supported mode, `cv_uploads.mode = 'as_is'`) whose `original_filename` is extremely long (reachable via a crafted multipart POST to either upload action, same reasoning as Finding 306) crashes `gather()`'s CV loop with `OSError: [Errno 36] File name too long` the moment `client.download()` tries to `open()` the local destination for writing. `gather()` itself has no try/except around this call, but `process_job()` (`gather()`'s only real caller) does wrap the whole thing in one broad `except Exception` - so this does not crash the worker process outright, but it does fail the ENTIRE SANRAL pack-generation job for that company/tender (marked `'failed'`, with a cryptic Python exception as the stored `error_message`, system-alerted as an `"error"` not a `"warning"` since it isn't a `ValueError`/refusal) rather than, say, just that one position's CV falling back to "missing" the way a genuinely absent CV already degrades gracefully two lines below. A company whose key person's CV was ever uploaded as-is with an unusually long filename (or one hit by a crafted request) would see their whole submission pack silently fail to build with no actionable message, until someone reads the raw exception in `pack_generation_jobs.error_message` or the system alert.

**Fix.** Extracted the CV-source/local-destination choice out of `gather()`'s own loop into a new, independently testable function, `cv_download_target(work, code, g, u)`, returning `(bucket, remote_path, local_dest, source_label)` or `None`. The as-is branch now builds its local destination from `u["storage_path"]` (matching the generated-CV sibling branch, and matching `process_general_jobs.py`'s own equivalent code exactly), not `u["original_filename"]`. `gather()`'s loop is otherwise unchanged in behaviour - same `own_path()` ownership check per branch (now parameterised by which branch was chosen), same `cvs[p["code"]]` dict shape, same "no ready tender CV and no as-is CV upload" fallback message when neither is available.

**Verified red-then-green, including a real OS-level crash, not just an assertion.** Added `test_cv_download_target_uses_the_safe_storage_path_not_the_raw_original_filename()` to `engine/pack/test_process_pack_jobs.py` (this file had no test at all of `gather()`'s own CV-source logic before this pass - confirmed by reading the whole file: every existing `process_job()` test monkeypatches `ppj.gather` away entirely, so this inline block was previously completely unexercised by any test). The new test: (1) pins both branches' bucket/remote-path/local-dest shape directly; (2) builds a real `original_filename` 5005 characters long and confirms it never appears anywhere in the returned local destination path; (3) actually opens the OLD destination path (`os.path.basename(original_filename)`) for write and confirms it raises a real `OSError` on this filesystem; (4) actually opens the NEW (fixed) destination path for write and confirms it does not. **Red:** `git stash push -- engine/pack/process_pack_jobs.py` (keeping the new test; restored with `git stash pop`, never a plain `rm`/overwrite - `git status` confirmed clean after), re-ran `python3 test_process_pack_jobs.py` from `engine/pack/` directly - `AttributeError: module 'process_pack_jobs' has no attribute 'cv_download_target'` (the function doesn't exist pre-fix, since it's a new extraction - the old code is the inline block this test replaces). **Green:** `git stash pop` to restore the fix, re-ran - `0 failure(s)`, all 9 new assertions pass, including the real OSError reproduction and its absence post-fix.

**Full regression.** `python3 -m py_compile` clean on both changed files. Every other direct consumer of `process_pack_jobs.py` re-run directly from `engine/pack/`: `test_process_pack_jobs.py` itself (0 failure(s), 100% of its own suite, not just the new case), `test_sync_functions.py` (ALL PASSED), `test_pack_suggestions.py` (ALL PASSED), `test_pdf_merge.py` (0 failure(s)), `test_adapt_company.py` (ALL PASSED) - none of these import or exercise `cv_download_target`/the CV-gathering block, and none regressed. `engine/security/test_tenant_isolation.py` (imports `process_pack_jobs`) re-run: its Part 1 (no live DB needed) still `ALL PASSED`; Part 2 needs `TENANT_PSQL` against a scratch Postgres and was already skipped before this pass (unrelated to this change). `app/`: `npx tsc --noEmit` 0 errors, `npx vitest run` 76/76 test files, 631/631 tests pass (unaffected - this is a Python-only engine change; app/ was not touched; no instance of the known `billing.spec.ts` flake this run).

## 2026-11-10e (standing solution-architect review, background worker, pass `www`): Finding 312 - `engine/compliance/registration_reminders.py`'s `PROPERTY_DOCUMENT_LABELS` claims "same keys and wording as" `app/lib/properties.ts`'s `PROPERTY_DOCUMENT_TYPES`, but the `floor_plan` entry's wording had already drifted

```

```
while `engine/compliance/registration_reminders.py` line 251 (pre-fix) had
```
"floor_plan": "Floor plan / layout",
```
- missing "with measurements". Every other one of the 16 labels matches character-for-character (confirmed by reading both lists side by side, not just spot-checking) - this is a genuine, single-field drift, not a wholesale re-write that happened to also claim "same wording" loosely.

**Real, if narrow, consequence - not purely cosmetic.** This label is not dead text: `find_due_property_documents()` (same file, ~line 201-228) builds every property-document compliance-reminder item's own `label` field directly from `PROPERTY_DOCUMENT_LABELS.get(r["document_type"], ...)`, formatted as `f"{label} - {props.get(r['property_id']) or 'property'}"`. **Found the bug via the brief's "two things computing what should be the identical value" pattern, applied within a single function's own repeated UNION ALL shape rather than across two files.** Four of the five branches (`pack_sanral`, `pack_general`, `cv`, `onboarding`) each have exactly ONE "this job's terminal moment" timestamp column, correctly reused for both their `completed_24h_count` (status='ready'/'classified') and `failed_24h_count` (status='failed'/'classification_failed') filters. `narrative_documents` (`0087`) is the one table with TWO such columns: `generated_at` (set ONLY on the success path - confirmed by reading `engine/narrative/process_narrative_jobs.py`'s `process_one()`, the `"status": "ready", ..., "generated_at": _now_iso(), ...` PATCH at line 313 is the only place in the whole file that sets it) and `completed_at` (set on EVERY terminal transition - the same success PATCH at line 319, AND all three failure paths: `GenerationFailed` line 340, the generic-`Exception` handler line 356-358, and `fail_stale_jobs()`'s own stale-reclaim-to-failed branch line 168-172). `0101`'s own `narrative` branch filtered **both** `completed_24h_count` and `failed_24h_count` on `generated_at` - the first is harmless (every ready row sets `generated_at`), but the second can never match any real row: a failed narrative job's `generated_at` is always `null`, so `status = 'failed' and generated_at >= now() - interval '24 hours'` is unsatisfiable for every row that will ever exist. The Telemetry page's "Failed (24h)" column for the `narrative` queue therefore always reads 0, regardless of how many cover-letter/methodology generations actually failed in the last 24 hours - the exact kind of false-confidence-dashboard bug this track has fixed before (e.g. `engine/cv/process_cv_jobs.py`'s own missing `completed_at` write, already fixed per `engine/cv/test_process_cv_jobs.py`'s own header comment, which independently confirms this same RPC's reliance on `completed_at` for its failed-count filters - that fix was on the Python engine side for a different queue; this one is on the SQL RPC side, for the one queue where the Python side was already correct and the RPC was reading the wrong column).

Acting as the seeded platform admin (`set_config('test.uid', ...)`, `set role authenticated` - the stub's own documented convention): `select * from platform_admin_engine_telemetry() where queue_key = 'narrative'` returned **`failed_24h_count = 0`** before the fix (confirmed red, matching the live bug exactly) and **`failed_24h_count = 1`** after applying this migration's redefinition (confirmed green). Also inserted a second, `status='ready'` row with `generated_at` set to confirm `completed_24h_count` still reads `1` and is unaffected by the fix (it was never broken - the fix only touches the `failed_24h_count` filter's column), and re-ran the full 5-row query to confirm `pack_sanral`/`pack_general`/`cv`/`onboarding` are byte-for-byte unchanged. Dropped the scratch database and stopped the local `postgresql` service afterwards.

**Fix.** New migration `app/supabase/migrations/0126_telemetry_narrative_failed_count_column.sql` redefines `platform_admin_engine_telemetry()` with exactly one condition changed: the `narrative` branch's `failed_24h_count` filter now reads `completed_at >= now() - interval '24 hours'` instead of `generated_at >= now() - interval '24 hours'` - the same column the other four branches already use for their own `failed_24h_count`, and the column `narrative_documents`' own failure paths actually write. `completed_24h_count` and `avg_latency_seconds` for the `narrative` branch are left on `generated_at`, deliberately unchanged (both are success-only and already correct - `generated_at` and `completed_at` are set together, within the same PATCH, on every real `ready` row). No other branch touched.

**Why pushed directly to `main`, not opened as a PR.** One migration file, additive `create or replace function` (same shape as every other RPC-fix pass this track has pushed directly), no RLS policy touched, no table schema change, no money/quota-enforcement path (`platform_admin_engine_telemetry()` is read-only, platform-admin-gated, and used by exactly one caller - confirmed by `grep -rln "platform_admin_engine_telemetry" app/app/ app/lib/` returning only `app/app/admin/telemetry/page.tsx`), no worker-image change, no signed/submitted-document content change. ## 2026-11-10h (standing solution-architect review, background worker, pass `zzz`): Finding 315 - `ScheduleHealthTable.tsx`'s own hardcoded "All 9 GitHub Actions workflows" text drifted stale the moment a 10th workflow was added, and was never caught because its sibling `page.tsx`/`workflowRegistry.ts` were fixed/updated in the same window without touching it

### Finding 315 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, minor, display-only, live-reachable - `admin/notifications`'s own "Schedule & cron health" tab literally told Sarel there were 9 monitored GitHub Actions workflows directly above a table that actually rendered 10 rows)

**Angle chosen.** `git fetch origin main` first (clean, `21595d4`/Finding 314, matching the task brief exactly; working tree clean). Picked up the brief's own suggested angle (a): a full end-to-end read of `admin/notifications`, not just the `TYPE_LABEL`/`TIER_LABEL` mapping Finding-151's pass already checked. Read `page.tsx`, `actions.ts`, `DispatchLogTab.tsx`, `TemplateGalleryTab.tsx` and `ScheduleHealthTable.tsx` in full, then cross-checked `page.tsx`'s own data flow into `ScheduleHealthTable.tsx` against `app/lib/workflowRegistry.ts`, the file that already carries its own loud comment ("10 workflows, not 6 - the Notification Command Center brief assumed 6; the repo actually has 10 cron-scheduled senders today ... most recently `returnables-digest.yml`, Phase 6").

**The finding.** `ScheduleHealthTable.tsx`'s own header paragraph (written in the original Phase 1 commit, `e7d745c`, when `WORKFLOW_REGISTRY` genuinely had 9 entries) reads:

> "All 9 GitHub Actions workflows this product relies on to send a notification - not 6 (the brief's own assumption didn't match this repo)."

`WORKFLOW_REGISTRY` now has **10** entries (`daily_discovery`, `daily_digest`, `compliance_digest`, `corrigendum_alerts`, `deadline_reminders`, `operational_alerts`, `onboarding_nudges`, `scout_alerts`, `returnables_digest`, `founder_digest` - confirmed by `grep -c "key:" app/lib/workflowRegistry.ts`'s own entries, and by `page.tsx`'s `scheduleRows: ScheduleRow[]` mapping one row per registry entry 1:1 with no filtering). `git log -p --follow` on `app/lib/workflowRegistry.ts` shows exactly when the drift happened: commit `cea50cb` ("Phase 6 (A6): Pack Incomplete / Returnables Checklist digest", 2026-10-27) added the `returnables_digest` entry (the 10th) and, in the SAME commit, updated this file's own comment from "9 workflows, not 6" to "10 workflows, not 6" - but `git show --stat cea50cb` confirms `ScheduleHealthTable.tsx` was never touched by that commit, so its hardcoded "All 9" text was left behind. The exact "a claim to verify, not a fact" shape this track has repeatedly found (Findings 305/307/308/309/310/312), except the stale claim lives in rendered admin-facing UI copy, not a code comment - Sarel, looking at this tab, would see "All 9 GitHub Actions workflows" in the paragraph directly above a table he could count 10 rows in himself, which is exactly the kind of small self-contradiction that erodes trust in a dashboard built specifically to tell him whether crons are healthy (the same "false-confidence-dashboard" family as the already-fixed `HEALTH_SOURCE_GROUPS` findings 298/302 and Finding 314, though this one is a display miscount rather than a wrong query result). Not a logic bug - every row is still rendered correctly and `heartbeatStatusFor()` is unaffected - but a real, live, user-visible correctness inconsistency between what the page says and what it shows.

**Why `Finding 151`'s own pass on this exact route didn't catch it.** That pass (2026-10-28ish per its own entry, fixing the `workflow_heartbeats` error-swallow bug) explicitly scoped itself to `page.tsx`'s data-loading logic and explicitly called out the two "Tab" components, including this one, as "purely presentational... no bug to find" - correct for `heartbeatStatusFor()`'s own correctness, but it didn't check `ScheduleHealthTable.tsx`'s own hardcoded prose against the registry's real length, which is a different bug entirely (display text, not data-flow).

**The fix.** `app/app/admin/notifications/ScheduleHealthTable.tsx`: replaced the hardcoded `9` with `{rows.length}` (the same `rows` prop the table itself renders from), so the paragraph can never drift from the table again, regardless of how many workflows `WORKFLOW_REGISTRY` carries in the future. The "not 6" clause is left as-is - that's a historical note about the original brief's own assumption, not a live count, and stays true regardless of how many workflows exist today.

**Verification.** `npx tsc --noEmit`: 0 errors. `npx vitest run`, twice in a row: **76/76 test files, 631/631 tests**, both runs clean, no flake either run (no dedicated test exists for this presentational component - confirmed by `find app -iname "*ScheduleHealthTable*"` returning only the component itself - so the full-suite re-run is this fix's own regression check). No scratch-Postgres repro needed: this is a pure TSX string interpolation change, no SQL/RLS/schema/money-path surface at all.

**Why pushed directly to `main`, not opened as a PR.** One file, one line, a hardcoded display string replaced with the same data the table already renders from. No RLS/migration/money-quota-path/worker-image/hard-stop-gate/signed-document surface touched - `ScheduleHealthTable.tsx` is read-only, platform-admin-gated UI with exactly one import site (confirmed by `grep -rln "ScheduleHealthTable" app/app/ app/lib/` returning only `page.tsx` and the component itself) and is not imported by `pack-review.tsx` or `submission-pack.tsx`. `git fetch origin main` immediately before starting (clean, `21595d4`/Finding 314, matching the task brief exactly) and again immediately before pushing this commit - both clean, no sibling commit landed in between.

**Backlog status.** No new standing item opened - a plain, mechanical stale-hardcoded-count bug with one unambiguous fix (made self-correcting rather than just re-pinned to a new literal). `admin/notifications` is now read end-to-end by a single pass (route + `page.tsx` + `actions.ts` + all three Tab components + the `workflowRegistry.ts`/`heartbeatStatusFor()` logic it depends on), joining `admin/discovered-opportunities`, `admin/customers` and `admin/telemetry` on the "fully read" list the brief itself was tracking.
