## 2026-11-10i (standing solution-architect review, background worker, pass `aaaa`): Finding 316 - `admin/billing`'s "Period end / trial end" column went blank for exactly the row Sarel most needs a date on - a trial that lapsed with no payment ever on file

### Finding 316 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, minor, display-only, live-reachable - `app/app/admin/billing/page.tsx`'s own "Period end / trial end" column picked the wrong source column once a trial lapsed, hiding the one date that explained why)

**Angle chosen.** `git fetch origin main` first (clean, `000e543`/Finding 315, matching the task brief exactly; working tree clean). Confirmed the real next Finding number by grep (`grep -n "^## Finding\|### Finding" docs/specs/QA-Edge-Case-Findings.md` - last entry is 315) and the real open-PR count (`gh api repos/sareljvr2024/tender-tool/pulls --paginate -q '.[].number'` - exactly 39, `#164`/`#165`/`#176`-`#212`, matching the brief exactly). Picked up the brief's own suggested angle (b): a full end-to-end read of `app/app/admin/billing/page.tsx` beyond what Finding 303/PR #210 already touched (that finding is about `platform_admin_billing_overview()`'s SQL silently returning `NULL` quota for `packs_used_this_period` - a different column, a different bug, still unmerged on PR #210 and not re-litigated here).

**The bug.** `page.tsx` computes two different notions of a subscription row's status: the RAW stored DB column (`r.status`, one of `trialing`/`active`/`past_due`/`cancelled`, written once at signup and never rewritten by any clock-driven job - `lib/billing.ts`'s own header comment: "nothing in this app runs a clock-driven job to rewrite it") and the EFFECTIVE status (`r.effectiveStatus`, via `effectiveSubscriptionStatus()`, which correctly flips a trial whose `trial_ends_at` has passed to `past_due` for display purposes - confirmed by `billing.spec.ts`'s own test, `"a trial past trial_ends_at reads as past_due, even though the stored status is still 'trialing'"`). The status chip and the five stat cards at the top of the page correctly use `effectiveStatus` throughout - that part was fine. But the table's own "Period end / trial end" column picked its date source off `effectiveStatus` too:

```tsx
{r.effectiveStatus === "trialing" ? formatDate(r.trial_ends_at) ?? "-" : formatDate(r.current_period_end) ?? "-"}
```

The moment a trial lapses, `effectiveStatus` flips from `"trialing"` to `"past_due"` - and this ternary then switches from showing `trial_ends_at` to showing `current_period_end`. For a company that signed up, took the standard 14-day trial, and never paid, `current_period_end` is `NULL` forever: migration `0078`'s own `insert into company_subscriptions (...)` on company creation only ever sets `trial_ends_at` (`values (new.id, 'sanral_pro', 'monthly', 'trialing', now() + interval '14 days')`), and `current_period_end` is only ever written later, by `start_payfast_checkout()`'s/the ITN route's own `UPDATE ... current_period_end = coalesce(p_period_end, current_period_end)` path (`0078`/`0081`/`0082`/`0083`/`0110`/`0112`) - i.e. only once a real payment has actually gone through. So the exact row Sarel most needs a date on - "Past due", chased-worthy, a trial that lapsed with nobody ever paying - showed `"-"` in the one column meant to tell him when. The `trial_ends_at` value was already selected into the row and sitting right there (`r.trial_ends_at`), just never shown once `effectiveStatus` stopped being `"trialing"`.

**Red-then-green repro.** A standalone Node script reimplementing `effectiveSubscriptionStatus()` verbatim and the page's own ternary, both the old and new form, over a seeded row (`status: "trialing"`, `trial_ends_at` 40 days in the past, `current_period_end: null`):

```
effectiveStatus: past_due
OLD cell (keyed off effectiveStatus): -
NEW cell (keyed off raw status):      2026-10-01
```

confirming the exact failure mode and the fix.

**Fix.** Changed the column's own condition from `r.effectiveStatus === "trialing"` to `r.status === "trialing"` (the raw, never-rewritten stored column) in `app/app/admin/billing/page.tsx`. This correctly separates "which kind of date does this row even have" (a question about the row's real history - was it ever only a trial, with no period-end ever recorded? - which the raw `status` answers) from "is this subscription currently in good standing" (the chip/stat-card question, which `effectiveStatus` still correctly answers, untouched). A genuinely active, paid, later-lapsed subscription (raw `status = 'past_due'`, real `current_period_end` from its last successful payment) is unaffected by this change - it already fell into the `current_period_end` branch either way, since its raw status was never `'trialing'`.

**Scope check.** One file, one ternary condition, display-only (admin, platform-admin-gated, read-only page - `export const instant = false` is its only data dependency, same RPC call as before, untouched). No RLS/migration/money-quota-path/worker-image/hard-stop-gate/signed-document surface touched - nothing was written, no SQL changed. `app/app/admin/billing/page.tsx` has no importers at all (confirmed by `grep -rl "admin/billing/page" app --include=*.tsx --include=*.ts`, matching only the Next.js-generated `.next/types/validator.ts`) and is not imported by `pack-review.tsx`/`submission-pack.tsx`.

**Verification.** `npx tsc --noEmit`: 0 errors. `npx vitest run`, twice in a row: **76/76 test files, 631/631 tests**, both clean, no flake either run (no dedicated test exists for this page - it is an async Server Component with no unit-testable export - the full-suite re-run plus the standalone repro script above is this fix's own regression check).

**Why pushed directly to `main`, not opened as a PR.** Single-file, single-condition, display-only TSX change on a read-only admin page with zero importers. No RLS/migration/money-quota-path/worker-image/hard-stop-gate/signed-document-content surface - `company_packs_this_period()`, `effectiveSubscriptionStatus()`, `platform_admin_billing_overview()` and every other function this page calls are completely untouched; only which already-fetched column a `<td>` renders changed. Not imported by `pack-review.tsx`/`submission-pack.tsx` (confirmed above). `git fetch origin main` immediately before starting (clean, `000e543`/Finding 315, matching the task brief exactly) and again immediately before pushing this commit - both clean, no sibling commit landed in between.

**Backlog status.** No new standing item opened - a plain, mechanical display-logic fix (wrong status variable backing a ternary) with one unambiguous correction, not a judgment call for Sarel. `admin/billing` is now read end-to-end by a single pass, beyond the slice Finding 303/PR #210 already covers.

## 2026-11-10j (standing solution-architect review, background worker, pass `bbbb`): Finding 317 - `admin/customers`' own status chip coloured a lapsed trial as an ordinary in-progress trial, directly contradicting the "trial expired" text sitting right next to it in the same chip

### Finding 317 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, minor, display-only, live-reachable - `CustomerRow.tsx`'s status chip tone was keyed off the same raw, never-rewritten column Finding 316 already established as unsafe to trust for display, on a different page)

**Baseline re-verified live first.** `git fetch origin main`: `c3cb17a`/Finding 316, matching the task brief exactly; working tree clean. Open-PR count re-confirmed via `gh api repos/SarelJvR2024/tender-tool/pulls?state=open --paginate -q '.[].number'`: exactly 39, `#164`/`#165`/`#176`-`#212`, matching the brief exactly. Next Finding number confirmed by grep (`grep -n "^## " docs/specs/QA-Edge-Case-Findings.md` - last entry is 316) - 317 is free.

**Angle chosen.** The task brief's own suggested angle (a): Finding 316's specific shape - a raw `status` column vs. a derived/effective status, used inconsistently within the SAME component for different fields - checked elsewhere. `admin/billing` itself is the only page that computes an `effectiveStatus` variable by name (confirmed by `grep -rln "effectiveStatus\|effective_status" app/app app/lib`), but `lib/billing.ts`'s own `effectiveSubscriptionStatus()`/`isSubscriptionLapsed()` are the real underlying mechanism, not that one local variable name - so the real angle is every other caller of a company's subscription status, not just literal `effectiveStatus` hits. `grep -rln "company_subscriptions\|fetchCompanySubscription\|CompanySubscriptionRow"` found `app/app/_components/AppShell.tsx` (→ `components/tt/subscription-banner.tsx`), `app/app/billing/page.tsx` (the company-facing twin of `admin/billing`), and `app/lib/trialLifecycle.ts`. Read all three end to end: `billing/page.tsx` and `subscription-banner.tsx` both consistently key every branch off the one correctly-computed `effectiveSubscriptionStatus()`/`isSubscriptionLapsed()` result (the banner's own `everTrialed = subscription.status === "trialing"` is a deliberate, correct use of the RAW column - "was this company ever on a trial at all," a question the effective status can't answer once it's flipped to `past_due` - not a bug); `trialLifecycle.ts`'s three candidate-selection functions correctly select on the raw DB column too, since they run as a batch job reading the table directly, not rendering a lapsed-trial-aware UI. All three genuinely clean.

**Widened the search to every OTHER consumer of a company's subscription status, not just ones calling `effectiveSubscriptionStatus()` by name**, since the bug class is "a raw status column rendered as if it reflects the lapsed-trial rule" - and `admin/customers` (`app/lib/customerRowData.ts` / `app/app/admin/customers/CustomerRow.tsx`) reads `subscription_status` straight from `platform_admin_companies()` (migration `0064`/`0098`) without ever calling `effectiveSubscriptionStatus()` at all, despite `admin/customers` being explicitly flagged by multiple prior passes as "already heavily hardened" and "confirmed clean" - for different bug classes (`membersError`/`readinessError` discarded-read-error handling, the trial-countdown-value-vs-admin-days-left disagreement already tracked as standing item 24). Confirmed via `grep -n "create or replace function platform_admin_companies"` + reading migration `0098` line 59 (`cs.plan_tier, cs.status, cs.trial_ends_at`) that `subscription_status` really is `company_subscriptions.status` verbatim - the exact same raw, "never rewritten by a clock-driven job" column `lib/billing.ts`'s own header comment documents for Finding 316's root cause.

**The bug.** `CustomerRow.tsx`'s status chip:
```tsx
const statusTone = customer.subscription_status ? SUBSCRIPTION_STATUS_TONE[customer.subscription_status] : undefined;
...
{statusTone && (
  <span className={...STATUS_CHIP_CLASS[statusTone]}>
    {planLabel ?? "no plan"}
    {customer.subscription_status === "trialing" && customer.trialDaysRemaining !== null
      ? ` - trial ${customer.trialDaysRemaining >= 0 ? `${customer.trialDaysRemaining}d left` : "expired"}`
      : ""}
  </span>
)}
```
`SUBSCRIPTION_STATUS_TONE` maps `trialing` to `"warning"` (yellow) and `past_due`/`cancelled` to `"destructive"` (red) - the identical tone table `admin/billing/page.tsx` uses for its own chip, now correctly keyed off `effectiveStatus` there since Finding 316. Here it was keyed off the raw `subscription_status` instead. For a company that took the standard 14-day trial and never paid, `subscription_status` stays `'trialing'` forever (the same fact Finding 316 already established, now confirmed a second time for this table's own column) - so its chip rendered `"Professional - trial expired"` inside a yellow, in-progress-trial-coloured pill, not the red "needs chasing" pill a platform admin scanning this list for exactly that purpose would expect. The chip's own text (correctly computed from `trialDaysRemaining`, which is already allowed to go negative - see its own pre-existing doc comment) and its own colour visibly disagreed for the exact row most needing attention, the same "two adjacent facts about the same row contradict each other" shape already named in this doc's own `admin/customers` Finding 288/membersError write-up, just with a different mechanism (a missing derived-status call, not a discarded RPC error).

**Red-then-green repro.** Added 3 new tests to `app/lib/customerRowData.spec.ts` (`effectiveSubscriptionStatus flips to past_due for a lapsed trial...`, the matching-cases test, and the no-subscription-row null case). **Red:** `git stash push -- app/app/admin/customers/CustomerRow.tsx app/lib/billing.ts app/lib/customerRowData.ts` (fix files only, new spec left in place) → `npx vitest run lib/customerRowData.spec.ts`: real exit `1`, **3 failed, 6 passed (9)** - every new assertion failed with `expected undefined to be '...'` (the field genuinely doesn't exist pre-fix), every pre-existing test untouched and still green. **Green:** `git stash pop` to restore the fix → re-ran: real exit `0`, **9/9 passed**. `git status` confirmed clean before and after.

## 2026-11-10k (standing solution-architect review, background worker, pass `cccc`): Finding 318 - the admin "Quality Scout" review queue never actually removed an item once an admin reviewed it, so every reviewed item kept reappearing on every page load, forever

### Finding 318 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, moderate, live-reachable via a real scratch-Postgres repro - `platform_admin_low_confidence_requirement_items()` (0076/0100) never joined against `requirement_extraction_reviews` at all, directly contradicting its own migration's stated purpose for `item_key`)

**Baseline re-verified live first.** `git fetch origin main`: HEAD still `b086c1d` / Finding 317, matching the task brief exactly; `git status` clean. Next Finding number confirmed by grep (`grep -oE "Finding [0-9]+" docs/specs/QA-Edge-Case-Findings.md | sort -t' ' -k2 -n -u | tail`: highest is 317) - 318 is free, no sibling collision. The subscription-status raw-vs-derived pairing (Findings 316/317) is explicitly exhausted per the brief, so this pass's own angle was the brief's suggestion (a) generalised - "other raw-vs-derived pairs beyond subscription status" - but widened further while reading `admin/requirement-extractions` (19 mentions across both standing docs, the admin route this task brief's own mention-count heuristic flagged as lighter-covered than `admin/notifications`/`admin/billing`/`admin/customers`, all now read end-to-end by prior passes).

**Angle and read.** Read `app/app/admin/requirement-extractions/page.tsx`, `RequirementItemRow.tsx`, `RequirementItemTable.tsx`, `actions.ts` end to end, then the SQL they depend on: migration `0076_requirement_extraction_reviews.sql` (original) and `0100_quality_scout_triage.sql` (the version actually live - it `drop function if exists ... create or replace`s the same name with 2 extra OUT columns). `0076`'s own header comment states `item_key`'s whole reason for existing: "a manifest item has no natural primary key of its own... item_key is a deterministic hash of (tender_id, item_type, document, quote)... the UI building the review queue needs to recognise 'this is the same item I already reviewed' across re-extractions without a round trip, and a content hash gives it that for free." That is a specific, checkable claim about what the queue function does with `requirement_extraction_reviews` - so read `platform_admin_low_confidence_requirement_items()`'s actual SQL body (both the `0076` and the live `0100` version) rather than trusting the comment: neither version references `requirement_extraction_reviews` anywhere. The function's `items` CTE filters purely on `(elem.item ->> 'confidence')::int < p_threshold` against the live `tenders.document_requirements`/`tender_packs.document_requirements` JSONB - nothing excludes, flags, or even surfaces an item that already has a verdict recorded against it. Confirmed by grep (`grep -rn "requirement_extraction_reviews" app/`) that the table is written to by exactly one place (`submit_requirement_extraction_review()`) and read from nowhere in the TS app at all - not even to show an "already reviewed" badge - despite the explicit read policy ("platform admins can select") existing for exactly that purpose.

**Traced whether anything ELSE removes a reviewed item from the queue instead**, since a missing join in the queue function alone wouldn't matter if the item's confidence score itself moves back above threshold on review. Read `engine/general/requirements.py`'s `_apply_past_corrections()`/`_item_identity()` (the only other consumer of `requirement_extraction_reviews`, via `process_general_jobs.py` passing in "up to 5 recent rows... globally" as `past_corrections`) line by line: a `"false_positive"` or `"corrected"` match only ever **lowers** a *similar future* item's confidence (`-25`/`-12`, on a DIFFERENT item, matched by a stable identity field like a form code - never the quote, "that's tender-specific free text and would never recur," per its own comment) - a `"correct"` verdict does nothing at all, to any item. So there is no path, in either the SQL or the Python, by which marking an item "correct" ever raises its confidence or otherwise removes it from this exact filter - and for the shared manifest (`company_id` null), there is no reprocess path at all either (`0100`'s own header: "it is only ever rebuilt as a side effect of some company's own real job"), so a shared-manifest item's `document_requirements` entry, and therefore its confidence, can never change by any means this app provides. The one-line "Reviewed" confirmation row `RequirementItemRow.tsx` shows after a successful save (`reviewedAs` state) is plain React state with no persistence - a page reload (or simply opening the page again tomorrow) loses it entirely, and the same item comes back indistinguishable from one nobody has ever looked at.

**Red-then-green repro on a real scratch Postgres (per the task brief's own recommended method for a SQL-level claim), not just reasoned about.** `sudo -u postgres pg_ctlcluster 16 main start`; `createdb finding318_test`; `bash engine/security/replay_schema.sh -d finding318_test` (116 migrations, clean). Seeded one real `tenders` row with a `document_requirements` manifest containing one `forms` item at confidence 25 (below the default threshold 60), one `platform_admins` row, impersonated via `select set_config('test.uid', '<uuid>', false)` (the stub's own documented `auth.uid()` mechanism, not `request.jwt.claims`). **Red:** called `platform_admin_low_confidence_requirement_items(60::smallint, 200)` - the item appears, as expected. Called the real `submit_requirement_extraction_review(...)` with `verdict := 'correct'` and the exact same `item_key` hash the function itself computes (verified by using the identical `md5(tender_id || '|' || item_type || '|' || document || '|' || quote)` expression `0076`'s own header documents). Called the queue function again with no other change: **the same item came back, completely unchanged** - confirming the bug live, not from reading alone. Wrote the fix (below), re-ran `replay_schema.sh` against a fresh `finding318_full` db to confirm all 117 migrations (116 + the new one) still replay clean end to end, then re-applied just the new migration to `finding318_test` and re-ran the exact same two queries. **Green:** the already-reviewed item no longer appears; a second, never-reviewed low-confidence item seeded on the same tender afterward (confidence 10, different document/quote) still appears correctly, proving the fix excludes only the specific reviewed item, not the whole tender or the whole queue. `sudo -u postgres dropdb` both scratch databases and `pg_ctlcluster 16 main stop` afterward, per the task brief's own guardrail.

**Fix.** New migration `app/supabase/migrations/0127_requirement_review_queue_excludes_reviewed.sql`: `drop function if exists .../create or replace` (same Postgres OUT-parameter-change constraint `0100`'s own header already documented and worked around, though this fix doesn't actually change the OUT columns - kept the `drop` for safety and consistency with the two prior versions of this same function) `platform_admin_low_confidence_requirement_items()`, computing `item_key` once inside the `items` CTE (instead of only in the final `select`, so it can also be used to filter) and adding `and not exists (select 1 from requirement_extraction_reviews r where r.tender_id = i.tender_id and r.item_key = i.item_key)` to the final `where` clause. Any verdict (`correct`/`corrected`/`false_positive`) now removes an item from the active queue - matching the function's own stated job ("every item... an admin can mark... correct/corrected/false positive," a worklist to clear, not a permanent list) and the `item_key` column's own documented reason for existing. A genuine future re-extraction that changes the item's `document`/`quote` text produces a different `item_key` (the same hash the UI's own `item_key`/`md5()` formula in `RequirementItemRow.tsx`'s `submit()` call relies on) and is correctly still treated as unreviewed - this does not suppress a real new finding, only an exact repeat of one already triaged. No TS/JS file needed changing: the function's OUT columns are unchanged, and the one real caller (`app/app/admin/requirement-extractions/page.tsx`) already just renders whatever rows come back.

**Why this is a real, previously-undocumented bug, not the `0100`-documented "no reprocess for shared items" gap re-litigated.** That standing gap (System-Status.md, Phase 2 entry) is about there being no WAY to get a shared-manifest item's underlying confidence to improve - a legitimate, disclosed architecture limit. This finding is different and strictly worse: even where a real, working path to change an item's confidence or disposition DOES exist (any company-scoped item, reprocessable; any item at all, reviewable), reviewing it has **zero effect on whether it is shown again** - the queue was built as, and is still described in its own schema comments as, a worklist of outstanding items, but nothing in it ever shrinks. Every page load re-surfaces the FULL historical set of every low-confidence item ever extracted, with no way for an admin to tell a freshly-found item from one they verdict-ed weeks ago, undermining the entire "feeds back into future extractions" review workflow Sarel asked for.

**Scope check.** One file, pure SQL, additive-only (a `WHERE ... NOT EXISTS` added to an existing read-only query - no column added, no OUT-shape change, no RLS policy touched, no existing row's data rewritten). Not a billing/quota RPC, not a hard-stop gate, not a money path, not a worker-image change, not a signed/submitted-document correctness change. `platform_admin_low_confidence_requirement_items()` has exactly one real caller anywhere in the app (`app/app/admin/requirement-extractions/page.tsx`, confirmed by `grep -rn "platform_admin_low_confidence_requirement_items" app/app app/lib`), which is not imported by, and does not import, `pack-review.tsx` or `submission-pack.tsx` (confirmed by grep). Admin-console-only, read-only display surface - genuinely small and safe per the task brief's own direct-to-`main` criteria.

**Verification.** `npx tsc --noEmit`: 0 errors (no TS file touched by this fix at all). `npx vitest run`, twice in a row: **76/76 test files, 634/634 tests**, both clean, no flake either run (unchanged from the task brief's own stated baseline - no existing test exercises this SQL function, consistent with every other platform-admin RPC in this codebase, which this doc has repeatedly confirmed have no RSC/SQL test harness in this environment). Full replay of all 117 migrations (`bash engine/security/replay_schema.sh -d finding318_full`) confirmed clean end to end, not just the one new file in isolation. `git fetch origin main` re-run immediately before pushing this commit - still clean at `b086c1d`, no sibling commit landed in between. `git status` clean before and after; both scratch databases dropped and the local `postgresql` service stopped.

**Why pushed directly to `main`, not opened as a PR.** One additive SQL migration to one non-billing, non-quota, read-only admin RPC with a single caller, no RLS/schema-shape/money-path/worker-image/signed-document surface, not imported by the pack-quota-credit screens. Matches this track's own established precedent for Findings 300/303/314 (additive SQL fixes to read-only admin RPCs, pushed directly) rather than Findings 301/305/310 (opened as PRs specifically because those sit on or feed the pack-quota-credit screen itself, which this does not).

**Backlog status.** No new standing item opened - this is a complete, mechanical fix with one unambiguous correction (exclude what's already been triaged), not a product judgment call. Recommend a future pass spot-check whether `RequirementItemRow.tsx`'s own `reprocess` button, once a shared-manifest reprocess path is ever built (the standing, disclosed gap above), should also re-validate that a reused `item_key` from a genuinely-changed re-extraction is treated as unreviewed by this fix - traced already (a changed `document`/`quote` text changes the hash), so no action needed now, just worth re-confirming whenever that gap is closed.

## 2026-11-10l (standing solution-architect review, background worker, pass `dddd`): Finding 319 - an expired, never-accepted company invite permanently occupied a seat in the plan's own seat-cap count

### Finding 319 (CONFIRMED, FIXED on PR #213 (unmerged) - `create_company_invite_checked()` (0113) counted a dead invite link exactly like a real, still-acceptable one, forever)

**Baseline re-verified live first.** `git fetch origin main`: HEAD `42f691d`/Finding 318, matching the task brief exactly; `git status` clean. Next Finding number confirmed by grep (`grep -n "^## Finding\|^### Finding" docs/specs/QA-Edge-Case-Findings.md` - last entry 318) - 319 free, no sibling collision. Open-PR count re-confirmed via `gh api repos/sareljvr2024/tender-tool/pulls --paginate -q '.[].number'`: exactly 39, `#164`/`#165`/`#176`-`#212`, matching the brief exactly.

**Angle chosen.** The brief's own suggested angle (b): a company-facing route lighter-covered than the admin routes already read end-to-end, picked by the brief's own mention-count heuristic across both standing docs. `company/bank-accounts` (37 mentions, lowest of the untouched company-facing routes - `people/bulk-cv` at 16 is explicitly already exhausted) read end to end first (`page.tsx`, `actions.ts`, `bank_account_summaries()` RPC, 0050) - genuinely clean; already hardened against the Finding-177 principal-fallback class and its own RLS-race-vs-zero-rows class (the same `.select("id").maybeSingle()` pattern `app/company/actions.ts`'s `uploadVaultDocument()` established), with nothing new to find. Moved to `company/team` (40 mentions) next, read end to end (`page.tsx`, `actions.ts`).

**What was found.** `team/page.tsx`'s own "Pending invites" list query (`supabase.from("company_invites").select(...).eq("company_id", companyId).is("accepted_at", null)...`) never checks `expires_at` - an invite nobody ever accepted within its 14-day window (`company_invites.expires_at` default `now() + interval '14 days'`, `0077_company_invites_and_employee_role.sql` line 57) sits there labelled "Pending invites" indefinitely, indistinguishable from a real, still-acceptable one, with its copy-able link shown exactly the same way - even though `/invite/<token>` itself (`invite_preview()`, same migration) would tell anyone who actually clicked it "Invite expired."

**Widened past display to the functional consequence**, since this doc's own standing heuristic treats a "claim to verify, not a fact" pattern as worth tracing to its real effect, not just its UI symptom: `create_company_invite_checked()` (0113, the SECURITY DEFINER RPC this Server Action calls, also callable directly via `supabase.rpc()` by any signed-in company admin) computes its own seat-cap count with the IDENTICAL gap - `select count(*) into v_pending_count from company_invites where company_id = p_company_id and accepted_at is null` - no `expires_at` check there either. A dead invite link doesn't just look pending in the UI; it permanently counts as an occupied seat against `company_subscriptions.max_users` (0083), forever, unless an admin happens to notice the stale dates and manually revokes it.

**Reproduced live in a disposable scratch Postgres** (`scratch_find319_invite_seatcap`, `engine/security/replay_schema.sh` through 0127, dropped after). Seeded one real company, one real owner (`company_members`), `company_subscriptions.max_users = 2`. As that owner (`set_config('test.uid', ...)`, `set role authenticated`, never `service_role`), called `create_company_invite_checked()` once (1 member + 1 invite = 2, at cap, correctly not yet over) then manually back-dated that invite's `expires_at` to yesterday (standing in for 14 real days passing with nobody clicking it - `accepted_at` still null, exactly what a real dead link looks like). **Red:** a second, brand-new invite call for the SAME company was refused: `ERROR: Your plan allows 2 people - upgrade on the Billing page to add more.` - with only 1 of 2 seats genuinely occupied (the owner; the dead invite can never be accepted again). Applied the fix migration (below) to the SAME database (no reseed) and re-ran the identical call. **Green:** it succeeded. Then, as a regression check, seeded a THIRD invite attempt against a now genuinely-live (non-expired) second invite at the same cap: correctly refused, confirming the fix excludes only dead invites, not pending ones generally. Dropped the scratch database and stopped the `postgresql` service afterward.

**Fix (PR #213, `finding-319-invite-seat-cap-excludes-expired`, not merged).** New migration `app/supabase/migrations/0128_invite_seat_cap_excludes_expired.sql`: `create_company_invite_checked()`'s `v_pending_count` now reads `where company_id = p_company_id and accepted_at is null and expires_at >= now()` - the same two-part "could this invite still actually be accepted" test `invite_preview()` already uses for the link page itself, rather than re-deriving it a third time. `app/app/company/team/page.tsx`'s "Pending invites" query gets the matching `.gt("expires_at", new Date().toISOString())` filter, so a dead link stops being listed as if it were live. Added `engine/security/test_tenant_isolation.py`'s `part2_invite_seat_cap_excludes_expired()` (`[20]`), covering both the fix and the non-regression case (a genuinely live pending invite still correctly blocks a new one at the cap) - run against the full suite on schemas with and without `0128` applied, red (`FAIL ... ERROR: Your plan allows 2 people...`) then green (`ALL PASSED`).

**Why opened as PR #213, not pushed directly to `main`.** `create_company_invite_checked()` is a SECURITY DEFINER billing/quota RPC (the company seat-cap gate, `company_subscriptions.max_users`) - explicitly one of this track's own PR-only categories, regardless of the fix's own direction (this one only loosens an over-counting bug, touches no RLS policy, no payment/money path, and no pack-quota-credit screen - `pack-review.tsx`/`submission-pack.tsx` import neither `team/page.tsx` nor anything that calls this RPC, confirmed by grep). The accompanying `team/page.tsx` display fix rides along in the same PR rather than splitting into a separate direct-to-`main` commit, since both halves are the same root cause and the whole change is small (3 files, one of them test-only).

**Verification.** Red-then-green confirmed twice: once at the raw-SQL level directly against the scratch database, and again by running the FULL `engine/security/test_tenant_isolation.py` suite (not just the new check) against a schema replayed through 0127 only (red: `1 FAILED`, exactly the new `[20]` check, with the real over-counting error as its message) and again through 0128 (green: `ALL PASSED`, all 20 sections including the pre-existing `[19]` Team/billing RPC cross-tenant checks). `npx tsc --noEmit`: 0 errors. `npx vitest run`: **76/76 test files, 634/634 tests**, unchanged from the task brief's own stated baseline (this fix touches no file any existing vitest spec covers). Both scratch databases (`scratch_find319_invite_seatcap`, `scratch_find319_run2`/`scratch_find319_red`, the latter two used for the full-suite red/green run) dropped and the `postgresql` service stopped. `git fetch origin main` immediately before starting (clean, `42f691d`/Finding 318, matching the task brief exactly) and again immediately before pushing this docs-only commit directly to `main` (also clean, no sibling commit landed in between) - the PR branch itself (`finding-319-invite-seat-cap-excludes-expired`) was pushed separately and is not touched by this commit. `git status` clean throughout; no scratch git worktree needed (the PR branch is PR #213's own branch, already pushed, not a scratch artifact).

### Finding 320 (CONFIRMED, FIXED directly on `main` - `lib/principals.ts`'s `isBlack()` ignored citizenship, so a qualifying-race permanent resident was tagged "Black" on their own card while the real B-BBEE ownership percentage shown right above correctly excluded their shares)

**Baseline re-verified live first.** `git fetch origin main`: HEAD `d49f13f`/Finding 319, matching the task brief exactly; `git status` clean. Next Finding number confirmed by grep (`grep -oE "Finding [0-9]+" docs/specs/QA-Edge-Case-Findings.md | grep -oE "[0-9]+" | sort -n | tail -5` - last entries 318/318/318/319/319) - 320 free, no sibling collision. 40 open PRs unchanged, none touched.

**Angle chosen.** The brief's own suggested angle (b), re-applied to a company-facing route not yet confirmed read end-to-end by a single pass as a whole (`company/principals` - "Directors & shareholders", 0050) - prior passes had each fixed one specific site inside it (Finding 177's person-fallback gap, Finding 194's discarded-breakdown-read-error, Finding 217's `isValidSaId()` date/citizenship-digit gap, Finding 299's missing `date_of_birth` cross-check in `idWarnings()`) but none had read `page.tsx`+`actions.ts`+`lib/principals.ts` together against the SQL view they all exist to mirror (`company_ownership_breakdown`, migration 0050).

**What was found.** `lib/principals.ts`'s own module comment, directly above `RACES`, states the B-BBEE Act's definition in full: *"'Black people' in the B-BBEE Act = African, Coloured and Indian South Africans (and Chinese South Africans, per the 2008 High Court order)"* - citizenship is part of the Act's own definition, not an incidental detail. Migration 0050's `company_ownership_breakdown` view implements exactly that: `cp.race in ('african','coloured','indian','chinese_sa') and coalesce(cp.sa_citizen, true) as is_black`, feeding `black_pct`, `black_women_pct`, `black_youth_pct`, `black_disabled_pct` and the black component of `hdi_pct` - every "Black"-labelled percentage `/company/principals` shows. `lib/principals.ts`'s own `isBlack(race)` - the function `PrincipalCard()` (`page.tsx` line 175) calls to decide whether to show a "Black" chip on an individual director/shareholder's card - checked only `race`, never `sa_citizen`, despite the file's own comment two screens up stating citizenship is part of the definition it is implementing.

**Confirmed live-reachable, not cosmetic-only in the sense of "can't disagree with anything."** This is exactly the "page keys off the wrong of two closely-related variables" shape already found repeatedly on this page's siblings (Findings 316-319's own family, cited by the task brief), just for a boolean pair (race alone vs. race+citizenship) instead of a raw-vs-derived field. Concretely: a shareholder of a qualifying race recorded as `sa_citizen = false` (a real, supported value - the "SA citizen?" Yes/No field on this exact form, `page.tsx` line 325) is tagged "Black" on their own card, directly above the "Ownership, worked out from this list" summary Card which correctly excludes that same person's shares from `black_pct` (via the SQL view's `coalesce(sa_citizen, true)` check) - the one card contradicts the other for the exact same person on the exact same page load, and nothing anywhere says why. The aggregate `stated` vs. `derivedBlack` mismatch banner (`page.tsx` lines 125-130) is unaffected - both sides of that comparison already come from the SQL view/the Company profile field, neither calls `isBlack()`.

**Verified red-then-green.** `isBlack()` had NO existing test coverage at all (confirmed by grepping `principals.spec.ts` and the whole repo for `isBlack` before starting - zero hits beyond its own one-line definition and its one call site). Added 5 new cases to `lib/principals.spec.ts`: qualifying race with `sa_citizen` unset (true, matching the view's own `coalesce(..., true)`), qualifying race with `sa_citizen = true` (true), qualifying race with `sa_citizen = false` (false - the gap this finding fixes), non-qualifying race regardless of citizenship (false), no race at all (false). **Red:** ran `npx vitest run lib/principals.spec.ts` against the unfixed function (before editing `principals.ts`) - **22 passed, 1 failed**, exactly the new `sa_citizen = false` case (`expected true to be false`), all other new cases already passing since the fix only narrows the true case, never widens it. **Green:** edited `isBlack()` to take a second `saCitizen` parameter (`= null`, coalesced to `true` inside the function, same default as the SQL view) and updated its one call site (`page.tsx` line 175: `isBlack(p.race, p.sa_citizen)`) - re-ran, **23/23 pass**.

**Fix.** `lib/principals.ts`: `isBlack(race: string | null, saCitizen: boolean | null = null): boolean { return RACES.some((r) => r.value === race && r.black) && (saCitizen ?? true); }`. `app/company/principals/page.tsx`: the one call site now passes `p.sa_citizen`. ### Finding 321 (CONFIRMED, FIXED directly on `main` - `lib/principals.ts`'s `idWarnings()` only ever checked ONE of the two possible sa_citizen/ID disagreements, so a wrongly-recorded "permanent resident" on a real citizen went unflagged and silently under-counted that shareholder's B-BBEE Black ownership)

**Baseline re-verified live first.** `git fetch origin main`: HEAD `b9a966a`/Finding 320, matching the task brief exactly; `git status` clean. Next Finding number confirmed by grep (`grep -oE "Finding [0-9]+" docs/specs/QA-Edge-Case-Findings.md | grep -oE "[0-9]+" | sort -n | tail -5` - last entries 319/319/319/319/320) - 321 free, no sibling collision. 40 open PRs unchanged (`#164`/`#165`/`#176`-`#213`), none touched.

Finding 320 fixed `isBlack()`'s own missing citizenship check; this pass re-read `idWarnings()` - the function immediately above it, whose own docstring is "Mismatches between what the person typed and what their ID number encodes" - now that `sa_citizen`'s real downstream consequence (via `isBlack()`) was freshly confirmed.

**What was found.** `idWarnings()` checks three typed-vs-ID-encoded fields: `gender`, `sa_citizen`, and (since Finding 299) `date_of_birth`. The `gender` check (`p.gender !== parsed.gender`) and the `date_of_birth` check (`p.date_of_birth !== parsed.birth`) are both genuinely symmetric - any disagreement, in either direction, is flagged. The `sa_citizen` check is NOT: it only ever fires for `p.sa_citizen === true && parsed.citizen === false` ("recorded as a citizen, but the ID says permanent resident"). The opposite disagreement - `p.sa_citizen === false` recorded, while the ID's own citizenship digit (position 11, `0` = citizen) actually says the person IS a citizen - has never been checked, since this line was first written (`git log -p --follow` on `app/lib/principals.ts`: unchanged since the original 2026-10-?? commit `b0f7ad2`, through Findings 217/299/320, none of which touched it).

**Confirmed live-reachable, not cosmetic.** `sa_citizen` is a free-typed Yes/No form field (`company/principals/actions.ts`'s `savePrincipal()`), independent of `id_number`, with no cross-validation against the ID anywhere in the save path - the exact same "typo, wrong-record paste, or value never corrected after a real ID review" reachability Finding 299's own write-up established for `date_of_birth`. Traced the real consequence, not just the missing symmetry: `isBlack(race, saCitizen)` (fixed by Finding 320, same file, same day) takes `sa_citizen` at face value - `(saCitizen ?? true)` - and migration 0050's `company_ownership_breakdown` view does the byte-for-byte identical `coalesce(cp.sa_citizen, true)`. So a qualifying-race shareholder wrongly recorded as `sa_citizen = false`, whose real SA ID actually encodes citizenship, is silently excluded from their own "Black" chip AND from every Black-labelled percentage the view derives (`black_pct`, `black_women_pct`, `black_youth_pct`, `black_disabled_pct`, the Black component of `hdi_pct`) - a real B-BBEE ownership-demographics UNDER-statement, with `idWarnings()` - the one function built specifically to catch exactly this class of typed-vs-ID-encoded mistake - saying nothing, even though it already computes `parsed.citizen` and already uses it for the opposite direction two lines below.

**Verified red-then-green.** Added 3 new cases to `lib/principals.spec.ts` (bringing total project-wide `idWarnings` coverage for this field to both directions plus the agree-in-either-direction negative case). **Red:** ran `npx vitest run lib/principals.spec.ts` against the unfixed function - **25 passed, 1 failed**, exactly the new "recorded permanent resident, ID says citizen" case (`expected [] to include 'Recorded as a permanent resident...'`); the other 2 new cases (the already-working direction, and the no-mismatch negative) already passed, confirming the fix only adds a check rather than changing existing behaviour. **Green:** added the mirror-image `if (p.sa_citizen === false && parsed.citizen === true) out.push("Recorded as a permanent resident, but the ID number encodes an SA citizen.");` right next to the existing check - re-ran, **26/26 pass**.

**Fix.** `lib/principals.ts`'s `idWarnings()`: one new symmetric `if`, same style/wording convention as its own existing sibling check. No parameter-type change (still `Pick<PrincipalRow, "id_number" | "gender" | "sa_citizen" | "date_of_birth">`), no call-site change needed (`page.tsx`'s one real caller already passes a full `PrincipalRow`). Pure TypeScript, a validation-warning string only (feeds the Principals page's own warning list under each card, nothing structural) - no RLS/schema/money-path/worker-image/signed-document-content surface, no SQL touched. Not imported by `pack-review.tsx`/`submission-pack.tsx` (confirmed by grep: `idWarnings` has exactly 3 importers total - its own production file, its own spec file, and `company/principals/page.tsx`).

**Full verification suite, all run myself, real exit codes.** `npx tsc --noEmit`: 0 errors. `npx eslint lib/principals.ts lib/principals.spec.ts app/company/principals/page.tsx`: 0 errors. `npx vitest run` twice from `app/`: **76/76 test files, 642/642 tests** both times (639 baseline + 3 new `idWarnings` cases), no flake. `git fetch origin main` immediately before starting (clean, `b9a966a`/Finding 320, matching the task brief) and again immediately before pushing this commit (also clean, no sibling commit landed in between). `git status` clean throughout - no scratch Postgres needed (pure TS logic, no SQL change), no worktree, no temp branch.

## 2026-11-10s (standing solution-architect review, background worker, pass `nnnn`): resolved pass `mmmm`'s own flagged-but-unconfirmed `diff_listing()` asymmetry with real evidence (deliberate/necessary, not a bug - documented, not fixed), then found Finding 328 in a different function in the same file

### Part 1 - the flagged lead (`diff_listing()` never reports a removed document): investigated and CONCLUDED DELIBERATE/NECESSARY, not a bug. No code changed for this part.

**What was flagged.** Pass `mmmm` noticed `diff_listing()` (`engine/discovery/tender_changes.py`) only ever computes `set(now["documents"]) - set(prev.get("documents") or [])` (added documents), never the reverse direction, and left it as "may well be a deliberate ... design choice, not yet confirmed either way."

**What was actually checked.** The whole file (559 lines), plus its three real per-tender document-list producers and its two real callers (`engine/discovery/watch_new_tenders.py`, `engine/notify/daily_digest.py`) - not just the one function in isolation.

**Why a `document_removed` event is not safe to add as a simple additive change.** A listing's `documents` list is not a reliable "present or genuinely absent" signal from one run to the next - it is a "best read this run, possibly degraded" signal, and three of this module's own real sources already document that degradation explicitly:
- `engine/discovery/gov_sources.py`'s `sanral_releases()` defaults every release's `documents` to `[]` (line 182), then only overwrites it with the real attached-file list inside `if with_details and ...: try: ... except Exception as e: log(f"  WARNING: SANRAL detail {slug} failed: {e}")` (lines 186-202) - no re-raise, no `system_alerts.record()`. SANRAL's own detail-page fetch sleeps 1 second between up to ~85 pages (`sanral_releases()`'s own docstring), a realistic timeout/rate-limit target. A transient failure there silently leaves that tender's `documents` at `[]` for the whole run, indistinguishable from "this tender genuinely has no documents."
- `engine/discovery/eskom_bulletin.py`'s `fetch_releases()` (line 189) and `engine/discovery/transnet_etenders.py`'s `fetch_releases()` (line 117) both wrap their own per-release document reads in an identical `try/except`, each with its own comment stating the intent plainly ("one entry's documents failing must not lose the listing").
- `gov_sources.py` also has a normal, scheduled, first-class operational mode (`--no-documents` / `with_documents=False`, threaded through `read_source()`/`fetch_all()`/`releases_for_watch()`, reachable live from `daily_digest.py`'s own `--no-fetch-documents` flag) that skips document reads entirely, for every source that has them, by design - not an error path at all.

**Confirmed the consequence directly, not just reasoned about it.** Built a standalone repro of what a naive `set(prev.get("documents")) - set(now["documents"])` removal check would do against this real failure/skip shape: every SANRAL tender whose detail-page read failed this run, or every tender read under `--no-documents`, would have its *entire* previous document list reported as "removed" in the same run - a false, run-wide alert storm, strictly worse in practice than the current one-directional gap.

**This matches the project's own already-stated philosophy for exactly this kind of absence, confirmed by grep, not invented for this write-up:** `engine/discovery/opportunity_requirements.py`'s own comment ("absence is the 'not_downloaded' state, never a fabricated row") and `tender_changes.py`'s own `detect()` except-block comment ("degraded, not wrong") already establish the house rule this falls under: never promote an unreliable per-run absence into a positive claim.

**Conclusion.** Not a bug, and not safely fixable as a one-file additive change. The real prerequisite, if Sarel ever wants a "document removed" signal, is making each of the three document-list producers distinguish "genuinely has no documents this run" from "the document read failed/was skipped this run" (e.g. a `documents_unknown: bool` field carried on the release) - an architectural change touching three scraper modules, not a `diff_listing()` tweak. Documented here so a future pass does not re-flag this as an unconfirmed lead; this is the second time this exact lead has now been looked at (`mmmm` flagged it, `nnnn` resolved it) and should be treated as closed.

### Finding 328 (CONFIRMED, FIXED directly on `main` - `engine/discovery/tender_changes.py`'s `readvertisements()` silently kept the WRONG, oldest-not-most-relevant cancelled tender as its match whenever two different cancellations shared the same buyer+title, because of a dict-overwrite-plus-input-order interaction nobody had actually traced through)

**Where found.** Reading the same file end-to-end while resolving Part 1 above (not the flagged lead itself - a different function, `readvertisements()`, a few lines above `diff_listing()`).

**What was found.** `readvertisements(new_rels, cancelled_rels)` built its lookup as `by_title = {_title_key(c): c for c in cancelled_rels if c.get("title")}` - a plain dict comprehension. `_title_key()` normalizes to `(buyer, title-with-readvertisement-wording-stripped)`. When two genuinely DIFFERENT cancelled tenders from the same buyer share that normalized key - a real, common pattern for SA government recurring-service procurement, where an identical generic title ("Appointment of a service provider for cleaning services") gets cancelled and re-run every renewal cycle, sometimes more than once - the dict comprehension keeps only the LAST one encountered in iteration order; every earlier match for that key is silently discarded, no error, no log. The specific wrong answer this produces is not arbitrary-but-harmless: `cancelled_rels` arrives "newest first" - `etenders_portal.py`'s own documented order (`read_source()`'s own docstring: "Raw portal rows for one tab, newest first (the portal's own order)"), the exact ordering `tender_changes.py` itself already relies on elsewhere. Iterating newest-to-oldest and keeping "last seen" means the dict always ends up holding the OLDEST matching cancellation, not the newest - backwards from what's actually useful: a tender reappearing today is far more likely to be a re-advertisement of the MOST RECENT cancellation under that title, not whichever one happened to be cancelled longest ago.

**Confirmed live-reachable with a standalone repro before touching any code.** Two cancelled releases, same buyer, same normalized title, 5 weeks apart (`2026-10-01`/`2026-11-05`), passed to `readvertisements()` in the real newest-first order exactly as `etenders_portal.py` produces it. A fresh listing with the same title matched the 5-week-OLDER cancellation every time, pre-fix - surfacing that older tender's wrong `contract_number` and cancellation `reason`/date in the `readvertised` event's own summary text, the exact sentence a human reading the daily digest (`daily_digest.py`'s `listing_change_signals()`) reads to judge whether a re-advertisement is worth re-tracking.

**Mandatory open-PR cross-check (per the task brief's own guardrail).** `gh api repos/sareljvr2024/tender-tool/pulls --paginate -q '.[] | {number, title, head: .head.ref}'`: all 40 open PR branch names/titles checked against `tender_changes`/`readvertise`/`title_key`/`by_title`/`discovery` - zero hits; nothing here duplicates or collides with an open PR.

**Fix.** `readvertisements()`: `by_title` is now built with `by_title.setdefault(_title_key(c), []).append(c)` (a list per key, not an overwritten single value), and the lookup becomes `candidates = [c for c in by_title.get(_title_key(r), ()) if c.get("ocid") != r.get("ocid")]` followed by `prior = max(candidates, key=lambda c: (c.get("cancellation") or {}).get("cancelled_at") or "") if candidates else None` - picks the most-recently-cancelled genuine candidate, preserving the pre-existing "never match a release to itself" guard. Additive, Python-only, no RLS/schema/money-path/worker-image surface, `readvertisements(new_rels, cancelled_rels)`'s own signature and every other caller unchanged.

**Regression test.** New `test_readvertisement_duplicate_title_picks_most_recent_cancellation()` in `engine/discovery/test_tender_changes.py`: builds the exact real input shape (`cancelled_rels` passed newest-first, matching the documented real order, not an order that happens to dodge the bug), asserts the match is the more recent cancellation (`NEW-002`, not `OLD-001`) and that the summary carries that cancellation's own reason text; a second assertion re-runs with only the single (previously-only-ever-tested) cancellation to confirm the ordinary one-match case is unaffected by the list-grouping change.

**Full verification suite, all run myself, real exit codes.** Standalone red/green repro against `tender_changes.readvertisements()` directly, before and after the fix: red matched `OLD-001` (wrong), green matches `NEW-002` (right). `python3 engine/discovery/test_tender_changes.py`: all checks pass, including the new one by name. `python3 engine/discovery/test_gov_sources.py` (covers `tender_changes.detect()`/`readvertisements()`/`relistings()` from the other, real-portal-fixture angle): `ALL PASSED`, no regression. Full `engine/` sweep, every `test_*.py` found by `find engine -name "test_*.py"` (87 files - one more than pass `mmmm`'s own count of 86; a sibling evidently added one since, not investigated further, out of this pass's own scope), each run individually with plain `python3 <file>`, real exit codes: **86/87 passed, 1 failed** - the 1 failure is `engine/discovery/test_download_documents.py`, which fails at import time with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'playwright'` (confirmed via `pip show playwright`: genuinely not installed in this sandbox), a pre-existing environment gap entirely unrelated to this change (that file imports `download_documents.py`, never touched here). Re-ran the sweep excluding only that one known-pre-existing-environment-gap file, TWICE as the task brief requires whenever any failure is seen: **86/86 passed** both times, no flake, 0 other failures. TypeScript/`npx vitest`/`npx tsc`/`npx eslint` not re-run - no TS, schema, or SQL file touched, same scope discipline this file's own prior entries already apply (e.g. Finding 188's/Finding 174's write-ups) for a pure-Python, single-engine-file change. `git fetch origin main` immediately before starting (clean, `d563c31`, matching the task brief) and again immediately before pushing this commit (also clean, still `d563c31`, no sibling commit landed in between). `git status` clean throughout - no scratch Postgres needed (no SQL change to verify), no worktree, no temp branch.

**Backlog status.** No new standing item opened for Finding 328 - a plain, mechanical dict-overwrite-on-key-collision fix with a concrete, demonstrated wrong-match consequence (not a judgment call for Sarel). The flagged `diff_listing()` lead (Part 1 above) is now resolved and should be treated as closed, not re-flagged as unconfirmed - `System-Status.md`'s own standing-items/pass-log entry for this pass records the same conclusion and the concrete architectural prerequisite (per-source `documents_unknown` flag) if Sarel ever wants to revisit it.

### Finding 329 (CONFIRMED, FIXED directly on `main` - `engine/discovery/tender_changes.py`'s `eskom_notices()` attached an Eskom notice to whichever duplicate-reference release happened to come first in `releases`' own order, not the live/current one, the exact same duplicate-key universe `relistings()` (a few functions up in this same file) already exists to handle)

**Where found.** Following up Finding 328's own fix in the same file (`readvertisements()`): the task brief's own "highly productive techniques" list flags exactly this shape - a plain dict/map lookup built from a list where duplicate keys are plausible and the input has a meaningful order - as worth re-sweeping across the rest of this file and its siblings. `eskom_notices()`, the next `idx = {...}`-building function after `readvertisements()`, was read end-to-end next.

**What was found.** `eskom_notices(notices, releases)` built its lookup as `idx = {}` / `idx.setdefault(sh.norm_ref(r.get("contract_number")), r)` for `r in releases` - first-wins on a normalized-contract-number key. But `releases` (the exact same list `relistings()`, defined earlier in this same module, groups by `(buyer, sh.norm_ref(contract_number))` precisely because the SAME buyer can legitimately list the SAME bid number TWICE as two different, genuinely live releases - different `ocid`, different `closing_date`, both still "Published" (`relistings()`'s own docstring: "Seen live 2026-10-17: Eastern Cape Transport's scholar-transport bids SCMU10-26/27-0017 A..F were listed on the portal with a 26 Oct closing date and again as 0017A..F closing 6 Nov; both stay 'Published'"). `eskom_notices()` reads that identical `releases` list and normalizes the identical `contract_number` field via the identical `sh.norm_ref()`, so it hits the exact same duplicate-key universe `relistings()` was written to handle - with zero handling of its own. The old `setdefault()` silently kept whichever duplicate happened to be first in `releases`' own order (an artifact of `gov_sources.merge()`'s base-source list order, not a deliberate "most relevant" choice, and not even consistently "oldest" or "newest" - it simply depends on which one the base source returned first), so an Eskom `award`/`bidders_list`/`regret`/`cancellation`/etc. notice could attach to a stale, superseded listing's `ocid` while the actual current relisting - tracked separately in `tenders`, exactly as `relistings()` itself assumes - silently never received it. `eskom_notices()` had no dedicated test file of its own at all (confirmed by grep: zero hits for `eskom_notices`/`eskom` in `test_tender_changes.py`), and `test_gov_sources.py`'s own single Eskom-notice fixture never has more than one release sharing a reference, so this gap was never exercised by either existing suite.

**Confirmed live-reachable with a standalone repro before touching any code.** Two releases, same normalized reference (`E1234GXMWP-2026`), different ocids, different published/closing dates (an older listing published Aug, superseded by a Dec relisting under a new ocid - the exact `relistings()` shape) - one real Eskom `award` notice referring to that reference. ### Finding 330 (CONFIRMED, FIXED directly on `main` - `engine/discovery/gov_sources.py`'s `merge()`/`_find()` folded a direct-source release's own data into whichever duplicate-reference base-list (portal/OCDS) release happened to come first, not the live one, on a same-reference relisting - the SAME duplicate-key universe `relistings()`/Findings 328/329 already exist to handle, one file over from where the last two passes fixed it)

That file's own module docstring names `gov_sources.py` as the upstream producer of the exact `releases` list every one of these functions reads, so `gov_sources.py` - its `merge()` function in particular, the thing that actually BUILDS that shared `releases` list out of the portal/OCDS base plus every direct-site source - was read next with the same lens.

**What was found.** `merge(by_source, portal_closed=None)` builds `idx` via `_index(merged)`, which already does the correct thing - `idx.setdefault(k, []).append(r)`, a LIST per ref key, not an overwritten single value - precisely because `_find()`'s own caller knows more than one base-list (portal/OCDS) release can share a ref key (this is the exact same `relistings()`-documented reality: "Seen live 2026-10-17... both stay 'Published'"). But `_find(idx, r, family)`, the one function that actually consumes `idx` to match a direct-site release `r` (SANRAL/SARS/DBSA/CIDB/Rand Water/Vaal Central Water/Lephalale/Kouga/etc.) against the portal/OCDS base, built its own `cands` list correctly (collecting every base-list release the direct-site release's ref keys point to, filtered for lot-conflicts, cross-source, and buyer-family), then just returned `cands[0]` - plain first-wins, with no rule at all for which of several real candidates is the live one. Unlike Findings 328/329's `idx.setdefault(key, single_value)` shape, the list-grouping here was already right; the bug is one call further downstream, in the consumer that then throws the extra candidates away by position instead of by relevance. When a buyer relists the same bid number as two separate, both-"Published" portal/OCDS releases (different ocid, different closing date - `relistings()`'s own documented shape) AND that buyer is also one of the configured direct sources (SANRAL, SARS, DBSA, CIDB, Rand Water, Vaal Central Water, Lephalale, Kouga all qualify - each is itself a buyer whose tenders also appear on the shared portal/OCDS feed), `_find()` folds the direct site's own richer data - its documents, and its own province/tender_type/description/scm_reference/published_date/opening_date/procurement_category whenever the portal's own value was null, plus the closing-date-disagreement check - into whichever of the two relisted releases happened to be listed FIRST in `by_source["etenders_portal"]` (or `"etenders_ocds"`)'s own iteration order, which is an accident of that source's own fetch/merge order, never a check of which listing is actually current. Picking the stale, superseded relisting means: the live listing a company is actually tracking silently never gets the direct site's own documents/fields at all (it looks like a bare portal row), while the dead listing - which nobody should still be acting on - gets enriched with them. The same `cands[0]` call also feeds the sibling `closed_idx` branch a few lines below (the "buyer's own site says open, portal moved it to Closed" fold), so both of `_find()`'s two call sites in `merge()` shared the one root cause.
