### Finding 340 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, pushed directly to `main`): `company_offices.office_kind` - built specifically so a buyer's "registered office only" locality rule (Overberg DM) could be distinguished from a genuine "any office counts" rule (Cape Winelands DM) - was never actually read by either locality-matching implementation, so a company's branch/head/site office silently satisfied a rule that requires its CIPC-registered address specifically

**Where:** `engine/discovery/score_outlook.py`'s `extract_locality()`/`match_locality()`/`_area_matches()` (the Discovery fit-scoring engine's own locality check, also the shared function the real general-pack intake pipeline calls via `engine/general/requirements.py:1448` to populate `tenders.evaluation_rules.locality`), and its TypeScript mirror `app/lib/locality.ts`'s `matchLocality()`/`areaMatches()` (the Tender Workspace's own copy, the real, live consumer of that stored JSON via `app/app/tenders/[id]/general-pack-review-data.ts`'s "Office location" item on the general-tender Pack Review screen).

**How this was found.** Angle (c)/(d): swept `app/lib/*.ts` files whose own header comment claims to "mirror" a Python counterpart but were not in the list of mirror-pairs an earlier pass (`QA-Edge-Case-Findings.md`, ~line 12398) had already checked against drift (`readiness.ts`/`registrations.ts`/`billing.ts`/`sanralB7.ts`/`onboardingScan.ts`/`general-workspace.tsx`/`resendEmail.ts`/`scoutAnomalyAlerts.ts` were all checked there; `locality.ts` was not). Reading `locality.ts` side by side with `score_outlook.py`'s `match_locality()` confirmed the two algorithms themselves are in sync (both were just independently re-verified and fixed for the Ratcliff-Obershelp/`difflib.SequenceMatcher` port, same pass, 2026-11-10) - but reading `app/supabase/migrations/0015_company_offices.sql`'s own header comment next (the schema both functions are built against) surfaced a documented REQUIREMENT neither implementation ever enforces: "the kind of office and the proof held matter (Overberg only accepts the CIPC registered office)" - and `docs/specs/Tender-Evaluation-Engine-Audit.md`'s own "Round 2" table independently corroborates this as a real, observed buyer rule from a real live tender: "Overberg DM | ... verified from the 'CIPC/CIPRO ... Address of registered office' | District, province; **registered office only** | 6" - immediately next to Cape Winelands DM's own, deliberately different, "District, province; **any office**" rule in the same table. `office_kind` (`'registered_office' | 'head_office' | 'branch' | 'site_office'`) is a real, populated column on `company_offices`, selected by both `COMPANY_OFFICE_COLUMNS` (TS) and every office dict built for `score_outlook.py` - but `grep -n "office_kind" engine/discovery/score_outlook.py app/lib/locality.ts` (before this fix) showed it was read into every office record and then never once consulted by either matching function. `proof_type`/`proof_date` are the same story (selected, shown in the company's own office-management UI, never read by any matching/expiry logic anywhere) but are left as a separate, undecided item below - this Finding fixes only the `office_kind` gap, which has a concrete, confirmed real-tender example; `proof_type`/`proof_date` have no equivalent documented enforcement requirement to point to.

**Live-reproduced directly against the real, unmodified functions (no live Supabase project needed - this is a pure function, exactly how `engine/discovery/test_score_outlook.py` already tests it).** Built a text sample using the Audit doc's own verbatim quote ("Within the boundaries of Overberg District Municipality 6 ... verified from the CIPC/CIPRO company registration documents - Address of registered office"), ran the real, unmodified `extract_locality()` over it (correctly produced the two real rows, 6 points for the district, 4 for the province), then ran the real, unmodified `match_locality()` against a company office shaped `{province: "Western Cape", district_municipality: "Overberg District", office_kind: "branch"}` - a mere branch office, not the company's registered one:

```
{"status": "matched", "points": 6.0, "office": {... "office_kind": "branch"}, "reason": "office in Overberg District matches 'Overberg District' - 6 point(s)."}
```

A company whose only presence in the Overberg district is a branch office (its real CIPC-registered address could be anywhere else in the country) was told it is "matched" and would be shown the full 6 locality points on its Tender Workspace - a claim that does not actually hold up against the buyer's own stated verification method, the same "the UI claims an eligibility the buyer's own rule doesn't actually grant" bug class as Finding 226 (SANRAL B7's own >100%-of-contract over-claiming) and the general-pack-review "qualifying items" over-count bug (same doc, ~line 12512), just in a subsystem (Discovery locality scoring) nobody had checked against this specific angle before.

**Fix.** `extract_locality()` now also scans a small window of text around each locality row (`REGISTERED_OFFICE_ONLY_RE`: `CIPC/CIPRO` together, or "address of [the/its] registered office"/"registered office address" - specific enough jargon that it is not expected to appear incidentally next to an unrelated locality clause) and sets `requires_registered_office: true` on a row when found nearby - heuristic, like every other regex in this module (recall, not precision, is the open risk: a tender phrasing the identical rule differently without hitting either phrase is not caught), but a strict improvement over never checking `office_kind` at all, and it makes no existing match stricter unless this specific language is genuinely present (confirmed: Cape Winelands' own "any office" wording, run through the identical extraction, sets the flag on neither of its rows). `match_locality()`/`_area_matches()` (Python) and `matchLocality()`/`areaMatches()` (TypeScript, mirrored) now both skip any office whose `office_kind` isn't literally `'registered_office'` when a row carries that flag - the row is otherwise matched exactly as before (same area/province comparison, same best-points selection), and a row with no flag (every row on `main` today, since nothing set it until this fix) is completely unaffected, confirmed by the full existing test suites passing unchanged on both sides.

**Verified red-then-green, myself, on both sides.**
- **Python RED:** `git stash push -- engine/discovery/score_outlook.py` (new test file kept), ran `python3 engine/discovery/test_score_outlook.py` - the new `requires_registered_office`-reading assertion raised a real, uncaught `KeyError: 'requires_registered_office'` (the field didn't exist pre-fix), exactly as predicted. **GREEN:** `git stash pop`, re-ran - **0 failure(s)**, all 10 checks (5 pre-existing + 5 new: extraction flags Overberg-style wording, extraction does NOT flag Cape-Winelands-style wording, a flagged row rejects a non-registered office, a flagged row still matches the real registered office, an unflagged row is unaffected and still matches any office kind as before).
- **TypeScript RED:** `git stash push -- app/lib/locality.ts` (new spec assertions kept), `npx vitest run lib/locality.spec.ts` - **1 failed** (`expected 'matched' to be 'no_match'`), exactly the predicted test, the other 9 (6 pre-existing + 3 new) unaffected. **GREEN:** `git stash pop`, re-ran - **10/10 passed**.
- **Full regression, both sides.** Python: every one of the 88 files `find engine -maxdepth 2 -name "test_*.py"` finds, each run individually with plain `python3 <file>` (counted myself, not estimated) - **87/88 passed**, 1 failed: the same pre-existing, already-documented `engine/discovery/test_download_documents.py` (`ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'playwright'`), unrelated to this change, no new file added this pass (an existing test file was extended, not a new one created). `ruff check engine/discovery/score_outlook.py` - identical 1 pre-existing finding (an unrelated `f-string without any placeholders` at the file's own functionality-scoring code, confirmed present verbatim in `git show HEAD:engine/discovery/score_outlook.py` too) before and after, zero new. `python3 -m py_compile` on both changed Python files - clean. TypeScript: `npx vitest run` (full suite) - **661/661 passed, 79/79 files**. `npx tsc --noEmit` - clean. `npx eslint lib/locality.ts lib/locality.spec.ts` - clean. `npx next build` - completed cleanly, no new warnings.
- Also ran every direct importer of `score_outlook.py` individually to be sure (`engine/discovery/*` full sweep, `engine/general/*` full sweep, `engine/intake/test_classify_tender.py`) - all green, already included in the 87/88 count above.

**Where the fix's behavior actually reaches a real screen, and where it deliberately does not.** `app/lib/locality.ts`'s `matchLocality()` has exactly one real caller in `app/`: `general-pack-review-data.ts`'s locality item on the GENERAL (non-SANRAL) Pack Review screen (`general-pack-review.tsx`) - informational/confirm-or-change, not a hard gate. Traced the import graph by hand to confirm zero overlap with this track's own "anything bigger -> PR" guardrail list: `submission-pack.tsx` imports `compliance-data.ts` (SANRAL), which imports only `COMPANY_OFFICE_COLUMNS`/the `CompanyOffice` *type* from `locality.ts`, never `matchLocality`/`areaMatches` themselves; `pack-review.tsx` imports `pack-review-data.ts` (SANRAL), which does not import `locality.ts` at all (`grep -n "locality" app/app/tenders/[id]/pack-review-data.ts` - zero hits). Neither SANRAL screen, nor `packReadiness()`/`company_can_request_pack()` (the real pack-quota-credit gate), nor any SQL migration, is touched by or reachable through this change. `grep -rn "locality" app/supabase/migrations/*.sql` confirms no RPC reads it either - this is a pure display/compliance-estimate field on both the Discovery fit score and the general Pack Review screen, never a quota or submission gate.

**Mandatory open-PR cross-check.** `gh api repos/sareljvr2024/tender-tool/pulls --paginate -q '.[] | "\(.number)\t\(.head.ref)\t\(.title)"'`: all 45 open PRs (`#164`/`#165`/`#176`-`#213`/`#215`-`#219`) read by number/title/branch - zero mentions `locality`/`office`/`discovery`/`outlook`/`score_outlook` in either title or branch name (`grep -iE "locality|office|discovery|outlook|score_outlook"` over the full listing: no hits). Went further than title/branch matching alone per the task's own instruction: pulled the real changed-file list for all 45 PRs (`gh api repos/.../pulls/<n>/files -q '.[].filename'`, one call per PR) and grepped every one for `locality`/`score_outlook`/`company_offices`/`offices` - zero hits across all 45. Zero collision, confirmed by file list, not assumed from titles.

**Scope note - what this Finding does NOT fix, left open.** `company_offices.proof_type`/`proof_date` (the document type/date a company holds as proof of an office's address - municipal account, lease, bank letter, CIPC registration, etc.) are selected into `CompanyOffice` on both sides and shown in `OfficeLocations.tsx`'s own management UI, but are likewise never read by any matching or expiry-warning logic anywhere (confirmed by the same `grep` sweep that found the `office_kind` gap) - unlike `office_kind`, there is no equivalent documented real-tender example naming a SPECIFIC required proof type as a pass/fail condition (the Audit doc's own "proof buyers name" list reads as "pick one of these", not "this exact buyer requires exactly this one"), so this is left as an open, undecided item rather than a confirmed bug - noted in `System-Status.md` for a future pass or Sarel's own call, not acted on here. The extraction side's own recall limit (stated in the fix's own comment above) is also left as a known, accepted heuristic limitation, consistent with every other regex-based extraction in this module, not a new standing item.

To verify independently: `python3 -c "import score_outlook as so; loc = so.extract_locality(open('/path/to/overberg-style/text').read()); print(loc['rows'])"` from `engine/discovery/` and confirm `requires_registered_office: True` on both rows; then `so.match_locality(loc, [{'province': 'Western Cape', 'district_municipality': 'Overberg District', 'office_kind': 'branch'}])` and confirm `status: 'no_match'`, and the same call with `office_kind: 'registered_office'` confirming `status: 'matched'`. `python3 engine/discovery/test_score_outlook.py` (0 failures, 10 checks). `cd app && npx vitest run lib/locality.spec.ts` (10/10). `gh api repos/sareljvr2024/tender-tool/pulls/<n>/files -q '.[].filename'` for any of the 45 open PRs, confirm none mentions `locality.ts`/`score_outlook.py`/`company_offices`.

### Finding 341 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, minor-to-moderate, user-facing copy accuracy - `app/app/company/Notifications.tsx`'s own "Email notifications" toggle told a real customer, in product copy, exactly which alert categories bypass it ("addenda/corrigenda, returnable checklists, and closing deadline reminders... are always delivered") - an exhaustive-sounding list that omitted a 4th script, `send-compliance-digest.ts`, which joined the same bypass mechanism three weeks after this card's own copy was written, so a user reading this toggle would reasonably but wrongly conclude a lapsing SARS PIN/COID/B-BBEE/CIDB/ECSA/SACPCMP document still depended on it)

**Area:** `app/app/company/Notifications.tsx` (user-facing copy + its own header comment). No test file exists for this component (a server component rendering static JSX text, not pure logic) - verified by direct, exhaustive comparison against the real recipient-resolution call sites instead (see below).

**How this was found.** This cycle's rotation landed on notify. Surveyed the least-covered files first - `NotificationsBell.tsx` and `lib/notifications.ts` (both already thoroughly hardened by recent sibling-track fixes, Finding 294's SACNASP/SAGC addition and the 2026-11-06 error-swallowing fix; traced `getNotifications()`'s own unguarded `Promise.all` call site in `dashboard/page.tsx` and confirmed the enclosing `DashboardPage`'s own top-level `try/catch` - documented in that file's own comment - genuinely does catch a thrown read failure, not a stale claim). Moved to `Notifications.tsx` next: its own header comment makes a dated, falsifiable claim ("Those [3] now bypass this flag entirely... used by scripts/send-corrigendum-alerts.ts, send-returnables-digest.ts and send-deadline-reminders.ts") and its RENDERED copy makes the identical claim to a real user. Grepped every real caller of `lib/notificationRecipients.ts`'s `criticalBidRecipients()` (the actual bypass mechanism) directly rather than trusting either comment: five files reference the name, but one (`send-onboarding-nudges.ts`) only mentions it in a comment about a DIFFERENT function and never calls it - confirmed false positive by reading the call site. The four genuine callers are `send-corrigendum-alerts.ts`, `send-returnables-digest.ts`, `send-deadline-reminders.ts`, and `send-compliance-digest.ts` - the last one confirmed via its own header comment and import, switched to this unconditional resolver by Finding 163 (2026-11-07), a full week after this card's own 2026-10-30 copy was written and never revisited since.

**Why this is a real, user-facing accuracy problem, not a cosmetic nit.** The card's own copy uses an enumerate-and-conjoin phrasing ("X, Y, and Z... are always delivered") that reads as exhaustive, not illustrative - a signed-in user deciding whether the "Email notifications" toggle is safe to leave off would reasonably conclude, from this exact text, that nothing outside those three categories is guaranteed. The one category actually missing - the SARS Tax PIN/COID Letter of Good Standing/B-BBEE proof/CIDB registration/ECSA/SACPCMP compliance-expiry digest - is described by its own sibling module (`lib/complianceDigestCandidates.ts`'s header comment) as covering facts that "can disqualify an active bid outright." A user who correctly trusted this card's own words would have no reason to believe that digest was unconditional, when it has been for weeks.

**Fix.** Updated the card's own rendered copy to name all four categories, and updated the header comment above it to record when and why the compliance digest joined the list, so a future pass extending `criticalBidRecipients()`'s own caller list has a visible prompt to come back and update this copy again rather than silently drifting a second time.

**Verified by direct, exhaustive comparison, not a red/green test cycle** (no test harness in this codebase renders a static-JSX-text server component, and there is no logic here to exercise - the fix is to the TEXT itself). `grep -rln "criticalBidRecipients" scripts/` gives exactly 5 hits; each file's own call site was read directly to confirm which are genuine (4) vs. a stray comment mention (1, `send-onboarding-nudges.ts`). The new copy's own 4 named categories now map one-to-one onto those 4 real callers. `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npx eslint app/company/Notifications.tsx` both clean.

**Not escalated to a PR.** A text-only change to one server component's copy and its own header comment - no logic, no RLS, no migration, no money path, no worker-image change. Pushed directly to `main`.

**Backlog status.** No new backlog items opened by this fix. `git fetch origin main` immediately before starting (clean, `main` at `0b48fd2`/Finding 340, matching the task brief's own stated current state) and again immediately before pushing this commit, both clean - no sibling commit landed in between.

To verify independently: open `/company` while signed in and read the "Email notifications" card - it should now name addenda/corrigenda, returnable checklists, closing deadline reminders, AND compliance-expiry warnings as always-delivered. `grep -rln "criticalBidRecipients" app/scripts/` (from `app/`) should list exactly the 4 scripts now named in the copy, plus the one comment-only false-positive (`send-onboarding-nudges.ts`) that isn't.

### Finding 343 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, pushed directly to `main`): `match_locality()`/`matchLocality()` picks the single highest-scoring locality row ANY office satisfies with NO regard for `kind` (`specific_goals` vs `functionality`) - so a tender that states a locality rule TWICE for the same area, once as preference points and once as a separate functionality-scorecard criterion (uMlalazi LM, a real, live-fetched tender), could silently report the functionality criterion's own, unrelated points as if they were the specific-goals locality points, on both the Discovery page's score-outlook chips AND the general Pack Review screen's "Office location points" item

**Where:** `engine/discovery/score_outlook.py`'s `estimate_score_outlook()` - the one call site (`loc_all_match = match_locality(locality, offices)`) that fed `match_locality()` every row regardless of `kind`, whose result lands in the function's own returned `locality.match` field - and `app/app/tenders/[id]/general-pack-review-data.ts`'s "Office location" section, the TypeScript mirror of the same call shape, which fed `matchLocality()` (`app/lib/locality.ts`) every row from `tenders.evaluation_rules.locality.rows`/the manifest's own `locality.rows` the same unfiltered way.

**Angle taken.** This pass's own primary angle (the task brief's (a): "are there other places where the SANRAL and general pack paths... diverge in what they check", applied broadly rather than re-litigating CVs/vault-mismatch) led nowhere new after a careful read of `assemble_pack.py` vs `build_general_pack.py` and their own UI counterparts (both engines' `verify_pack()` gating, vault-document handling, and CIDB-vs-CIDB-PSP-report distinctions all checked out as deliberate, non-buggy differences in domain, not gaps - see the negative evidence below). Pivoted to angle (c) - re-reading `docs/specs/Tender-Evaluation-Engine-Audit.md`'s own "Round 2 (c)" locality table line by line against the actual extraction/matching code, since Finding 340 (this same pass family, same day) had just fixed ONE row from that exact table (Overberg DM's `requires_registered_office`) without checking whether any of the table's OTHER rows named a real, documented condition the code still didn't handle. uMlalazi LM's own row stood out: "Enterprise Located within uMlalazi Municipality 4 / within District Municipality 2 / within the Province 1"; **also** a functionality criterion: "Bidder operating within uMlalazi Municipality (Points = 10) ... King Cetshwayo District (5) ... Kwazulu Natal province (2)" - the SAME buyer naming the SAME area under TWO different mechanics with TWO different point values, a condition no prior pass's own locality work (Finding 340 included) had read with this specific "does the matcher conflate these" question in mind.

**Confirmed `extract_locality()` genuinely produces both rows, undeduped, for the same area - the precondition for the bug, not assumed.** `extract_locality()`'s own dedupe key is `(area, system, kind)` (score_outlook.py:695) - specifically keeps a `specific_goals` row and a `functionality` row for the same area as two separate entries, by design (confirmed by reading the function; this part is correct and deliberate). Ran the real, unmodified `extract_locality()` against a text sample built from uMlalazi's own verbatim quote shape:

```
rows = [
  {'area': 'uMlalazi', 'kind': 'specific_goals',  'points': 4.0,  ...},
  {'area': 'uMlalazi', 'kind': 'functionality',   'points': 10.0, ...},
]
```

Exactly as expected - both kinds present, same area, different points.

**Live-reproduced the conflation directly against the real, unmodified `match_locality()` - no live Supabase project needed, a pure function.** Fed it both rows above plus a company office in uMlalazi:

```python
so.match_locality({'rows': rows}, [{'province': 'KwaZulu-Natal', 'local_municipality': 'uMlalazi', ...}])
# -> {"status": "matched", "points": 10.0, "row": {..., "kind": "functionality"}, "reason": "office in uMlalazi matches 'uMlalazi' - 10 point(s)."}
```

`match_locality()`'s own selection rule (`row["points"] > best[0]["points"]`) has no idea `kind` exists - it always keeps whichever row scores higher, so the FUNCTIONALITY row (10) beat the SPECIFIC_GOALS row (4) purely on magnitude. This is not a hypothetical reading of the code: `_specific_goals()` (the function immediately above, in the same file) and the separate functionality-criterion summary line immediately below `estimate_score_outlook()`'s own buggy call both ALREADY filter `locality["rows"]` to the one `kind` each cares about before calling `match_locality()` - confirming the surrounding code fully understands the two kinds must never be mixed - but the THIRD call site, `loc_all_match = match_locality(locality, offices)`, was the one place nobody applied that same filter.

**Confirmed the real, reachable consumer, not assumed.** `estimate_score_outlook()`'s own return value stores this exact result as `locality.match` (score_outlook.py:924-925). Ran the FULL real pipeline end to end - `extract_locality()` -> `estimate_score_outlook()` - against the same uMlalazi-shaped text and a real company profile:

```python
result = so.estimate_score_outlook(text, "full", {"offices": [office]}, None)
result["locality"]["match"]  # -> {"status": "matched", "points": 10.0, "row": {..., "kind": "functionality"}, ...}
```

`app/lib/scoreOutlookChips.ts` (read in full) reads `outlook.locality?.match` directly for the Discovery page's own "How it's scored" chip row (`app/app/discovery/page.tsx`): `locMatch.status === "matched"` renders `Locality: matched (${locMatch.points}pt)` right next to the "Specific goals: ..." chip - so a real company viewing a discovered uMlalazi-shaped tender would have been told "Locality: matched (10pt)" when the real specific-goals locality points its own profile earns are 4, with the 10 actually belonging to an entirely separate functionality-scorecard criterion that has its own, unrelated pass/fail mechanics (doesn't even combine with specific goals in the tender's own price/preference math) - a real, visible over-claim on the one screen whose whole job is "how well suited... and how we'll score".

**Confirmed the identical gap, independently, on the TypeScript side - the same bug, not a copy-paste assumption.** `app/lib/locality.ts`'s own `matchLocality()` is a line-for-line port of `match_locality()` and has the exact same `row.points > best.row.points` selection with no `kind` check (confirmed by reading it fresh, not inferred from the Python side). Its one real caller in `app/`, `general-pack-review-data.ts`'s "Office location" section (the general, non-SANRAL Pack Review screen), built its own `locRows` from `tenders.evaluation_rules.locality.rows`/the manifest's own `locality.rows` - the SAME raw, undeduped-by-kind array `extract_locality()` produces - with no filter at all before handing it to `matchLocality()`. Live-reproduced directly against the real, unmodified function (`node --experimental-strip-types`):

```
matchLocality(rows, offices) // rows = the same uMlalazi-shaped [specific_goals 4, functionality 10]
// -> {"status": "matched", "points": 10, "row": {..., "kind": "functionality"}, ...}
```

Same defect, same real screen's own "Office location points" item would show "10 pts" instead of the real 4.

## 2026-11-10 (standing solution-architect review): one more pass of the naive-UTC-slice sweep (per this track's own task brief, after Findings 289-292/344/345) - Finding 346, a genuinely fresh 5th site, in the "Pack Incomplete / Returnables Checklist" digest's own window math, that none of those four passes' own scope ever covered

### Finding 346 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, pushed directly to `main`): `returnablesWindowCandidates()`'s own "is this tender inside the 3-5 business-day critical window" check compared a correctly SAST-derived `todayStr` against a naively UTC-sliced tender closing day - the exact naive-UTC-slice mistake Findings 289-292/344/345 already fixed elsewhere, missed here because an earlier (2026-11-06) pass fixed only the `todayStr` side of this same script and believed, per its own comment, that the whole bug class was closed for this digest

**Why this angle, one more time.** The task brief itself flagged this bug class as "found FOUR times already" (Findings 289-292 engine-side, then 3 TS display/RPC-argument sites, then Finding 344's 3-site TS sweep and Finding 345's 4th, `tender_tasks.due_date`-persisting site) and asked for exactly one more systematic pass before marking it exhausted. Re-ran the widened sweep across `app/app` and `app/lib` - `grep -rn "\.slice(0, *10)\|toISOString()\.split(\|substring(0, *10)\|substr(0, *10)"` - and read every hit's own context, not just the grep match, cross-referencing each against `app/supabase/migrations/` to confirm which column is genuinely `timestamptz` vs plain `date`.

**Area:** `app/lib/returnablesDigestCandidates.ts`'s `returnablesWindowCandidates()` (line 95 pre-fix) - the pure candidate-selection function behind `scripts/send-returnables-digest.ts`, Sarel's own Phase 6 "once a tracked tender enters the 3-5 BUSINESS day window before closing, and a mandatory returnable is missing, send one nudge" digest.

**What was tested, and why this site is genuinely new, not a re-tread of the already-fixed `todayStr` side of this exact script.** `returnablesWindowCandidates(tenderRows, todayStr, businessDaysBetweenFn)` computes `businessDaysBetweenFn(todayStr, tender.closing_date.slice(0, 10))` - a raw string slice of `tenders.closing_date` (confirmed `timestamptz`, migration 0001), not `closingDayOf()` (`lib/dates.ts`), the already-tested helper built specifically to convert a timestamptz into its real South African (SAST) calendar day. A 2026-11-06 pass (this same file's own comment at `send-returnables-digest.ts` lines 70-75) already found and fixed the IDENTICAL bug class on this exact script's `todayStr` side (`sastToday()` replacing a raw `new Date().toISOString().slice(0, 10)`) and believed, per that comment's own wording ("the same UTC-vs-SAST bug class fixed..."), that the bug class was closed for this digest - but that fix never touched `returnablesWindowCandidates()` itself, so the function's OTHER date argument, the tender's own real closing day, was left exactly as naive as before. Confirmed by reading the current file: no `closingDayOf` import anywhere in `returnablesDigestCandidates.ts` prior to this fix.

**Confirmed the real impact with arithmetic, not just "a slice looks naive."** For a closing instant whose UTC time-of-day is 22:00-23:59 (SAST 00:00-01:59 next day - the exact window Finding 345's own write-up names as "a SANRAL default-midnight closing time", a common real shape in this app's own tender data), the naive slice reads the UTC calendar day, one day EARLIER than the true SAST closing day. Since the script's cron runs daily and the window check only ever fires once per tender/company (the idempotency key has no date component - `send-returnables-digest.ts`'s own comment: "fires at most ONCE EVER"), the one-day undercount in `businessDaysLeft` shifts the whole 3-5 business-day window a day earlier than the real one: the digest can fire a full business day before a tender has genuinely entered the critical window (real days left = 6, computed as 5, which the `<= 5` check wrongly admits) - and, because the send is one-shot-ever, it then never fires again once that early, wrong send has already claimed the key, even once the tender genuinely enters the real 3-5 day window. For `businessDaysLeft` values genuinely inside the window (4 or 5 real days left, computed as 3 or 4), the shift is masked by the window's own width - the bug is real on every affected tender, but is most visibly wrong at the window's own edges.

**Confirmed live against the real, unmodified function**, not just read: `node --experimental-strip-types` one-liner calling `returnablesWindowCandidates()` directly with a synthetic tender closing at `"2026-11-13T23:00:00+00:00"` (real SAST closing day `2026-11-14`) and a capturing stub in place of `businessDaysBetweenFn` - pre-fix, the captured `endDateStr` argument is `"2026-11-13"` (one day early); post-fix, `"2026-11-14"` (the real SAST day). This is the exact string `businessDaysBetween()` (the real injected function in production, `lib/publicHolidays.ts`) would diff against `todayStr` to decide whether to send.

**Fix.** `app/lib/returnablesDigestCandidates.ts:95` - `businessDaysBetweenFn(todayStr, closingDayOf(tender.closing_date) ?? tender.closing_date.slice(0, 10))`, mirroring the exact `closingDayOf(x) ?? x.slice(0, 10)` fallback shape Finding 345's own fix used for an unparseable date. `closingDayOf()` itself is unchanged, and no other site in this file (`returnablesMissingMandatoryItems()` passes `tender.closing_date` straight through to `sanralConventionalDocumentChecks()`/`checkReturnable()`, which already do their own SAST-aware handling internally - confirmed by reading both, not assumed) needed the same fix.

**Verified red-then-green, myself, with real exit codes.** New test in the existing `app/lib/returnablesDigestCandidates.spec.ts` (table-keyed stub pattern already used by every other test in that file - a capturing `businessDaysBetweenFn` recording its own `endDateStr` argument). **RED:** `git show HEAD:app/lib/returnablesDigestCandidates.ts` restored over the fixed file (new test kept) - `npx vitest run "lib/returnablesDigestCandidates.spec.ts"` - exactly **1 failed**: `expected '2026-11-13' to be '2026-11-14'`, the precise pre-fix value the arithmetic above predicts; the other 6 pre-existing tests in the same file still passed (none of them exercise the actual string value, only mocked `businessDaysBetweenFn` return values, which is why this bug was never caught before). **GREEN:** restored the fixed file - **7/7 passed**.

**Full regression.** `npx vitest run` (from `app/`) - **79 files, 662 passed** (661 pre-existing on `main` + 1 new; Findings 344/345's own new spec files are not yet on `main`, still on their own unmerged PR branches, so this is the correct baseline for `main` today). `npx tsc --noEmit` - clean. `npx eslint lib/returnablesDigestCandidates.ts lib/returnablesDigestCandidates.spec.ts` - clean, 0 warnings. `npx next build` - completed cleanly, full route list unchanged.

**The rest of the widened sweep, for the record - so a future pass doesn't need to re-run it a 6th time.** Every other hit from the widened grep across `app/app`+`app/lib` was read and ruled on individually:

Not a bug.

## 2026-11-10 (standing solution-architect review): a fresh angle - the `--test-recipient` safety flag's own documented idempotency-key contract (`lib/senderCliArgs.ts`) is violated by exactly 2 of the 4 sender scripts that implement it

### Finding 347 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, pushed directly to `main`): `send-compliance-digest.ts` and `send-discovered-tenders.ts` both called `claim_notification()` - the RPC that actually inserts the ONE-SHOT-EVER `notification_claims` row - under the REAL idempotency key even when `--test-recipient` was passed, so a safe test send to a known test inbox permanently burned the real company's real one-time compliance-expiry/discovered-tender claim, with the real recipient never getting the real notification afterward - the exact outcome `lib/senderCliArgs.ts`'s own header comment says this flag exists to prevent

**Why this angle.** Per the task brief's "idempotency-key collisions" fresh-angle suggestion for the returnables-digest family, read every `*-digest.ts`/sender script under `app/scripts/` for a non-date-math bug class. `lib/senderCliArgs.ts` (the shared `--dry-run`/`--company-id`/`--test-recipient` flag parser, added 2026-10-27 per Sarel's own explicit requirement: "under no circumstances do we send unverified test runs to real companies") documents, in its own header comment on `testIdempotencyKey()`, an exact, load-bearing safety contract: "`--test-recipient` ... needs a DIFFERENT idempotency key than the real send would use ... using the real key here would permanently burn that one-time claim, and the real recipient would never get the real notification later." Four sender scripts import `testIdempotencyKey` (`send-compliance-digest.ts`, `send-corrigendum-alerts.ts`, `send-discovered-tenders.ts`) or implement the equivalent inline (`send-operational-alerts.ts`'s own `test-` prefix in its `claim()` helper) - checked all 4 against that one contract, not assumed from the import alone.

**The bug, read directly from each file's own code, not inferred.** `notification_claims` (migration `0093`) is a `primary key (idempotency_key)` table; `claim_notification(key, type)` does the real `insert ... exception when unique_violation then return false` - the row it inserts IS the permanent one-shot-ever dedupe gate (confirmed by reading `0093_notification_engine.sql` directly: `notification_claims` has no TTL/expiry column, nothing ever deletes a row). `record_notification_sent()` is a separate, purely informational `notification_logs` audit-trail insert with no gating role at all (the migration's own header: "Separate from the claim table because its job is different ... never the dedupe check itself").

- `send-compliance-digest.ts`'s `processComplianceDigestForCompany()` (pre-fix) computed `idempotencyKey = complianceDigestIdempotencyKey(company.id, candidate.itemKey, candidate.threshold)` and passed that REAL key straight to the `claim_notification` RPC call, with no `testRecipient` check anywhere near it - `testIdempotencyKey()` was only ever applied later, at the `record_notification_sent` call, for logging only.
- `send-discovered-tenders.ts`'s `processDiscoveredTenderCompany()` (pre-fix) had the identical shape: `claim_notification` was called with the bare `discoveredTenderIdempotencyKey(row.id)`, and the file's own adjacent comment at the `record_notification_sent` call site ("A test-recipient send uses a DIFFERENT key so it never burns the real one-time claim the real recipient still needs later") is literally true of that one log-only call but false of the whole run, because the claim itself - the thing that actually burns the key - had already happened under the real key, several lines earlier, in the same function.

**Confirmed the other 2 scripts already do this correctly**, so this is not a repo-wide pattern needing a 3rd/4th fix: `send-corrigendum-alerts.ts` computes `idempotencyKey = testRecipient ? testIdempotencyKey(realKey) : realKey` and passes that SAME variable to both the `claim_notification` call and the later `record_notification_sent` call. `send-operational-alerts.ts`'s own `claim()` helper computes `const key = opts.testRecipient ? \`test-${thresholdKey}\` : thresholdKey;` before its own insert, and reuses the identical `test-` prefix convention at every one of its 3 `logSend()` call sites (print-cutoff, briefing, clarification-window). Both were read end to end, not just grepped, to confirm the test-prefixed key is really what reaches the RPC call, not just a nearby variable.

**Concrete impact.** `--test-recipient` requires `--company-id` (`parseSenderCliArgs()`'s own refusal otherwise), so the blast radius of one test run is exactly the one real company named on the command line - but for that company, it is total and permanent: the exact compliance-expiry item/threshold (e.g. "SARS Tax PIN, 30 days left") or discovered-tender opportunity row tested against is claimed forever under its real key, so a real future run for that same company/item/threshold, or company/opportunity pair, will see `claim_notification` return `false` ("already sent") and silently skip it - with nothing in `notification_logs` showing a real send ever happened (only a `test-`-prefixed log row exists), so there is no record pointing at the real cause either. For `send-compliance-digest.ts` specifically, this is one of the "critical, bid-protecting" alert types (`app/company/Notifications.tsx`'s own promise: "closing deadline reminders ... are always delivered") - an operator running a routine test-recipient verification before trusting a new template change could silently and permanently cost a real customer their one SARS Tax PIN/COID/B-BBEE/CIDB/ECSA/SACPCMP expiry warning for that exact threshold.

**Fix.** Both files: moved the `testRecipient ? testIdempotencyKey(realKey) : realKey` computation to directly precede the `claim_notification` RPC call (previously it only existed at the `record_notification_sent` call), matching `send-corrigendum-alerts.ts`'s own already-correct pattern exactly.
- `app/scripts/send-compliance-digest.ts` (`processComplianceDigestForCompany()`, the claim loop): `realKey`/`idempotencyKey` now computed before `claim_notification`, reusing the existing `idempotencyKey` variable name the `claimError` log line already referenced.
- `app/scripts/send-discovered-tenders.ts` (`processDiscoveredTenderCompany()`, the claim loop): new `realKey`/`claimKey` locals, `claimKey` passed to `claim_notification` and used in the error log line (previously `discoveredTenderIdempotencyKey(row.id)` was recomputed inline in 3 separate places in that one loop body).
Neither file's later `record_notification_sent` call needed any change - both already recomputed the test-prefixed key correctly there; the bug was only ever in the earlier claim call.

**Verified red-then-green, myself, real exit codes, for both files.** New test in each file's existing `.spec.ts` (same sequential-RPC-mock pattern every other test in each file already uses - extended `send-discovered-tenders.spec.ts`'s own `mockSupabase()` to also capture each `rpc()` call's `params`, which it previously discarded, since no prior test needed to inspect them). Each new test calls the real exported function with `testRecipient` set to a non-empty test address and asserts the captured `claim_notification` call's own `p_idempotency_key` argument starts with `"test-"` and is not equal to the real key.
- **RED** (`npx vitest run "scripts/send-compliance-digest.spec.ts"` and `"scripts/send-discovered-tenders.spec.ts"` against the unfixed files): exactly 1 failure in each file - `expected false to be true` on `claimedKey.startsWith("test-")`, the real pre-fix value (the real key has no `test-` prefix) - 7/8 and 4/5 passed respectively, every pre-existing test in both files unaffected.
- **GREEN** (fixed files): `send-compliance-digest.spec.ts` 8/8, `send-discovered-tenders.spec.ts` 5/5.
- **Full regression** (`cd app && npx vitest run`): **79 files, 664/664 passed** (662 pre-existing on `main` + 2 new). `npx tsc --noEmit` clean. `npx eslint scripts/send-compliance-digest.ts scripts/send-compliance-digest.spec.ts scripts/send-discovered-tenders.ts scripts/send-discovered-tenders.spec.ts` clean, 0 warnings. `npx next build` completed cleanly, full route list unchanged.

**Why a direct push to `main`, not a PR.** `grep -rn "send-compliance-digest\|send-discovered-tenders\|senderCliArgs"` across `app/` (excluding the two touched `.spec.ts` files and their own doc-comments) confirms neither script is imported by any Next.js route or by `pack-review.tsx`/`submission-pack.tsx` - both are standalone cron scripts (`.github/workflows/`-triggered via `node --experimental-strip-types`), referenced elsewhere only in comments (`Notifications.tsx`'s UI-copy accuracy note, `send-operational-alerts.ts`'s own header, `lib/workflowRegistry.ts`'s `scriptPaths` metadata string, `lib/discoveredTendersDigest.ts`/`lib/complianceDigestCandidates.ts`'s own doc-comments) - none of which is a real import. Not RLS, not a money path, not a hard-stop/disqualification gate, no worker-container-image change, no migration/schema surface at all (pure TypeScript, no new SQL), and not a document a company signs or submits - this only changes which key a manual `--test-recipient` verification run claims under, never anything a real, non-test cron run does (a real run never passes `testRecipient`, so `idempotencyKey`/`claimKey` resolve to exactly the same real key as before the fix in every production path).

**Mandatory open-PR cross-check**, by the exact filenames touched (`app/scripts/send-compliance-digest.ts`, `app/scripts/send-compliance-digest.spec.ts`, `app/scripts/send-discovered-tenders.ts`, `app/scripts/send-discovered-tenders.spec.ts`), per Finding 343's own "filenames, not bug-topic keywords" lesson: `gh api repos/sareljvr2024/tender-tool/pulls/<n>/files -q '.[].filename'` for all **49** open PRs (`#164`/`#165`/`#176`-`#213`/`#215`-`#223`, re-confirmed via `gh api repos/sareljvr2024/tender-tool/pulls --paginate -q '.[].number' | wc -l` immediately before writing this fix, matching the task brief and Finding 346's own count exactly) - **zero hits** on any of the 4 touched filenames, in any of the 49 PRs' own changed-file lists.

**Backlog status.** No new standing item opened - a plain, mechanical "the safety flag's own documented key only reached the logging call, not the gating call" fix in 2 of 4 already-correctly-patterned sibling scripts, not a judgment call for Sarel. Does not touch any RLS/money-path/pack-quota-credit surface, standing items 28/29, or item 22's migration-collision tracking (no migration touched). Item 23's open-PR count is unchanged (nothing opened as a PR, no new migration number taken).

### Finding 348 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, pushed directly to `main`): `send-onboarding-nudges.ts`'s `companySubscriptions()` read `company_subscriptions` with a plain, unranged `.select()` - the identical PostgREST 1000-row-cap bug this same file was already fixed for on `companies`/`tender_packs` (Finding 255) - silently dropping all 3 trial-lifecycle nudges for any company past row 1000

**Why this angle.** The task brief's own fresh-angle suggestion to look at sender/digest scripts under `app/scripts/` beyond the 4 already checked for the idempotency-key pattern, for a DIFFERENT kind of bug - specifically naming "a batch-processing bug (partial failure handling, pagination)" as one example. `ls app/scripts/` lists 19 files; `send-onboarding-nudges.ts` (Tier 0 onboarding/trial-lifecycle nudges) stood out because its own header comments already document two PRIOR pagination fixes to itself (Finding 255, commit `3c99c78`/`4318dc3`: `allCompanies()`'s `companies` read and `allTenderPackCompanyIds()`'s `tender_packs` read both used to hit PostgREST's 1000-row cap, 20,000-row-capped `fetchAllRows()` pagers added for both) - a file that has twice needed this exact fix is a reasonable place to check whether a THIRD sibling read in the same file was missed.

**The bug, read directly from the code, not inferred.** `companySubscriptions()` (used by all three `runTrialDay7()`/`runTrialExpiring48h()`/`runTrialExpired()` callers) ran:
```ts
supabase.from("company_subscriptions").select("company_id, status, trial_ends_at, companies(legal_name)")
```
- a direct call with no `.range()` and no `fetchAllRows()` pager, the exact unpaginated shape Finding 255 already fixed twice in this same file for `companies`/`tender_packs`. `app/supabase/migrations/0078_company_subscriptions.sql`'s own schema confirms `company_subscriptions.company_id` is `unique` (`references companies(id) ... unique`) and the table's own comment states "One row per company ... there is never a company with no subscription row to read" - so `company_subscriptions` grows in exact 1:1 lockstep with `companies`, the identical table Finding 255 already named as liable to cross 1000 rows ("Past 1000 real (is_test_company = false) companies..."). `lib/supabasePaging.ts`'s own header comment documents PostgREST's hard cap as live-confirmed on this project (`content-range "0-999/39536"` on an unranged request past 1000 real rows) - a plain `.select()` past that cap silently returns only the first page, not an error.

**Concrete impact.** Once the platform has more than 1000 companies, every company whose `company_subscriptions` row sorts past row 1000 silently drops out of `companySubscriptions()`'s own result entirely - with no error, no retry, and nothing in the logs distinguishing "this company has no qualifying subscription today" from "this company's row was never read at all". That company then never receives any of the three Tier 0 trial-lifecycle emails this read feeds: `trial_day_7_milestone` (an exact-day match, `daysUntil(trial_ends_at) === 7` - not a retried window, so a company that misses it here never gets a second chance, the same one-shot shape Finding 255's own `lifecycleRecipients()` fix write-up already flags as the worst case for this file), `trial_expiring_48h`, and `trial_expired`. The bug is not reachable today (the demo/seed data is nowhere near 1000 companies), but it is the exact same growth-triggered, zero-warning failure mode Finding 255 already named and fixed twice over in this identical file - left open in a third, sibling read inside the very function (`companySubscriptions()`) that consumes the two already-fixed reads' own output.

**Fix.** `app/scripts/send-onboarding-nudges.ts`: `companySubscriptions()` now routes its `company_subscriptions` read through the same `fetchAllRows()` pager (`lib/supabasePaging.ts`, unchanged) every other read in this file already uses, capped at the same `MAX_COMPANY_ROWS` (20,000) constant `allCompanies()` uses (the exact 1:1-with-`companies` relationship justifies reusing that same cap rather than inventing a new one). Exported (it was previously a private, untested helper) so a direct regression test could exercise its own pagination behaviour the same way `allCompanies()`'s own test already does, rather than only indirectly through `runTrialDay7()`/etc.

**Verified red-then-green, myself, real exit codes.** New test in `send-onboarding-nudges.spec.ts` (`describe("companySubscriptions")`), same real-pagination mock-chain pattern `allCompanies()`'s own test already uses (`.range()` resolves the real page of 1005 synthetic rows asked for, not a single canned response) - built a second mock table for `tender_packs` (the file's other read inside the same `Promise.all`) alongside it so the test exercises the whole function, not a stub.
- **RED**: restored the real pre-fix function body (`git show HEAD:app/scripts/send-onboarding-nudges.ts`, with only the one-word `export` keyword added so the test could import it at all - no logic change) and ran `npx vitest run "scripts/send-onboarding-nudges.spec.ts"`: exactly 1 failure - `expected [] to have a length of 1005 but got +0` (the pre-fix code never calls `.range()` at all, so it reads nothing back from a mock that only serves data through `.range()` - the precise real-world defect: the function has no pagination path whatsoever) - all 7 pre-existing tests in the file unaffected.
- **GREEN**: restored the real fixed file: `npx vitest run "scripts/send-onboarding-nudges.spec.ts"` - 8/8 passed.
- **Full regression**: `npx vitest run` - **79 files, 665/665 passed** (664 pre-existing on `main` + 1 new). `npx tsc --noEmit` clean. `npx eslint scripts/send-onboarding-nudges.ts scripts/send-onboarding-nudges.spec.ts` clean, 0 warnings. `npx next build` completed cleanly, full route list unchanged (this file is a standalone cron script, not imported by any route).

**Why a direct push to `main`, not a PR.** `grep -rn "send-onboarding-nudges\|companySubscriptions"` across `app/` (excluding the touched `.ts`/`.spec.ts` files and doc-comments) confirms this script is not imported by any Next.js route, and neither `pack-review.tsx` nor `submission-pack.tsx` imports anything from it - it is a standalone cron script (`.github/workflows/onboarding-nudges.yml`), exactly like the 2 files Finding 347 fixed on the same basis. Not RLS, not a money path, not a hard-stop/disqualification gate, no worker-container-image change, no migration/schema surface (pure TypeScript, no new SQL, no new migration number), and not a document a company signs or submits - the fix only changes how many rows a background notification read can see, not what it does with them. A real, non-test cron run passes no mock, so `fetchAllRows()` behaves identically to a plain `.select()` for any company count genuinely under 1000 (today's real state) - the change only matters once the platform actually crosses that threshold.

**Mandatory open-PR cross-check**, by the exact filenames touched (`app/scripts/send-onboarding-nudges.ts`, `app/scripts/send-onboarding-nudges.spec.ts`): `gh api repos/sareljvr2024/tender-tool/pulls/<n>/files -q '.[].filename'` for all **49** open PRs (`#164`/`#165`/`#176`-`#213`/`#215`-`#223`, re-confirmed via `gh api repos/sareljvr2024/tender-tool/pulls --paginate -q '.[].number' | wc -l` immediately before writing this fix, matching the task brief exactly) - **zero hits** on either touched filename, in any of the 49 PRs' own changed-file lists.

**Backlog status.** No new standing item opened - the same tier as Finding 255 itself (a plain, mechanical "this read was never given the pagination fix its siblings in the same file already got" gap), not a judgment call for Sarel. Does not touch any RLS/money-path/pack-quota-credit surface or any standing item. No PR opened, no migration touched, item 23's open-PR count unchanged at 49.

### Finding 349 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, pushed directly to `main`): `send-founder-digest.ts`'s `countActiveSubscriptions()` read `company_subscriptions` with a plain, unranged `.select()` - the identical PostgREST 1000-row-cap bug this same file's own sibling, `countClosingWithin48h()`, was already paginated for, silently undercounting the "active paid subscriptions" number in Sarel's own 07:00 SAST founder daily digest past 1000 companies

**Why this angle.** This pass's primary angle, per the task brief: one more systematic sweep of the PostgREST 1000-row `db-max-rows` cap bug class (Findings 255, 266, 275, 348), explicitly looking for a sibling table read hiding in an already-mostly-fixed file - the exact shape that produced Finding 348 (a THIRD unpaginated read in `send-onboarding-nudges.ts`, after Finding 255 had already fixed two). `ls app/scripts/*.ts` (13 non-spec files) and `grep -n "\.select(" app/scripts/*.ts` against every one, checking each hit against the same two-part test a prior pagination-sweep pass (`System-Status.md`, "picked up the pagination-cap sweep's own unfinished thread") already established: (a) already paginated/count-only? (b) does the real, RLS-bypassed (service-role) scope realistically exceed 1000? `send-founder-digest.ts` stood out: that same prior sweep explicitly fixed its `countClosingWithin48h()` (a `tender_packs` read, summed across every company) but, reading the function immediately above it with fresh eyes, never checked `countActiveSubscriptions()` - a second, completely separate `.select()` against `company_subscriptions`, in the same file, never mentioned by name in either standing doc's pagination-sweep write-ups (confirmed by grep: `countActiveSubscriptions` appears only in Finding 160's own unrelated null-vs-0 write-up, which fixed this function's error handling without ever touching its row cap).

**The bug, read directly from the code, not inferred.** `countActiveSubscriptions()` ran:
```ts
supabase.from("company_subscriptions").select("company_id, status, companies(is_test_company)").eq("status", "active")
```
- a direct, awaited call with no `.range()` and no `fetchAllRows()` pager, under the SERVICE ROLE key, filtered only by `status = "active"` (no company scope at all) - summed across every company's own subscription row at once. `app/supabase/migrations/0078_company_subscriptions.sql` confirms `company_subscriptions.company_id` is `unique` ("One row per company ... there is never a company with no subscription row") - so this table grows in exact 1:1 lockstep with `companies`, the identical lockstep relationship Finding 348 already named and fixed for this exact table in `send-onboarding-nudges.ts`'s sibling function, `companySubscriptions()`. `lib/supabasePaging.ts`'s own header comment documents PostgREST's hard response cap as live-confirmed on this project - a plain `.select()` past 1000 matching rows silently returns only the first page, never an error.

**Concrete impact.** Once the platform has more than 1000 companies with an `active` subscription, every such company whose row sorts past row 1000 silently drops out of `countActiveSubscriptions()`'s own count - not a company-specific miss (no company is denied anything), but a wrong, understated BUSINESS NUMBER: the "active paid subscriptions" figure `founderDailyDigestEmail()` (`lib/emailTemplatesTier3.ts`) renders in Sarel's own 07:00 SAST inbox every morning would silently read lower than the real figure, with no error and nothing distinguishing it from a genuinely smaller active-subscription count. This is the exact same class of wrong founder-facing business number this file's own header comment already names for `countClosingWithin48h()` ("a wrong founder-facing business number, not a cosmetic gap") - just on the one sibling read that prior fix's own pass never reached. Not reachable today (nowhere near 1000 companies, let alone 1000 with an active subscription), the same growth-triggered, zero-warning failure mode as every other instance of this bug class.

**Fix.** `app/scripts/send-founder-digest.ts`: `countActiveSubscriptions()` now routes its `company_subscriptions` read through the same `fetchAllRows()` pager (`lib/supabasePaging.ts`) this file's own `countClosingWithin48h()` already uses, capped at a new `MAX_COMPANY_SUBSCRIPTION_ROWS = 20_000` constant (same order of magnitude as the file's existing `MAX_TENDER_PACK_ROWS`, same reasoning as Finding 348's own `MAX_COMPANY_ROWS` choice for the identical 1:1-with-`companies` relationship). The `is_test_company` filter stays in TypeScript afterward, unchanged from before - only the read itself is now paginated.

- **Full regression**: `npx vitest run` - **79 files, 666/666 passed** (665 pre-existing on `main` + 1 new). `npx tsc --noEmit` clean, 0 errors. `npx eslint scripts/send-founder-digest.ts scripts/send-founder-digest.spec.ts` clean, 0 warnings. `npx next build` completed cleanly, full route list unchanged (this file is a standalone cron script, not imported by any route, same as Finding 348).

Tracing every real consumer of `tender-readiness.ts`'s `computeTenderReadiness()` (the one function both tender families' Pack Review header score and "Generate submission pack" gating both read, per its own doc comment's explicit "can never disagree" promise) turned up two call sites in `app/app/tenders/[id]/page.tsx` - `PrimaryPackActionLink`'s `ready` prop and `WorkspaceStatusBadge`'s "Ready to submit" label - that were never updated when PR #40 ("Gate 'Generate submission pack' on open Fix items, both tender families") switched the real buttons from the then-only-available `thingsLeft` check to `fix.length > 0` specifically.

**The bug, read directly from the code and its own history, not inferred.** `page.tsx`'s own comment on `PrimaryPackActionLink` describes it explicitly as a pure navigational shortcut: "links to the real generate-pack control already further down this page (`SubmissionPack`/`GeneralTenderWorkspace`'s own pack section) instead of a second, new mutation path ... Disabled (with why) until there is a pack to generate from and nothing still blocking it" - i.e. it is documented to mirror the REAL control's own availability, not apply an independent, stricter rule. Before this fix it read:
```tsx
ready={!!tenderPack && !keyPositionsError && (!tenderReadiness || tenderReadiness.thingsLeft === 0) && openPositionsCount === 0}
```
`tenderReadiness` here is the exact same `computeTenderReadiness(snapshot.sections)` result `submission-pack.tsx`'s `fixCount`/`general-workspace.tsx`'s `generalFixCount` read (confirmed: both are computed from `loadPackReviewSnapshot()`/`loadGeneralPackReviewSnapshot()`, both React `cache()`'d, so it's the same request-scoped read, never a second one) - but `thingsLeft` (`totalCount - confirmedCount`) counts EVERY Provide item and every unconfirmed-but-non-disqualifying Verify item too, not just Fix items. `git show 6949cce --stat` (PR #40, "Gate 'Generate submission pack' on open Fix items, both tender families") touches only `app/AGENTS.md`, `general-workspace.tsx` and `submission-pack.tsx` - `page.tsx` is absent from that diff entirely, confirming this link's own `thingsLeft` gate (added earlier, PR #39, "Tender workspace header: show client, add unified readiness score" - `git log -S "thingsLeft === 0" -- app/app/tenders/[id]/page.tsx` shows no later touch) was simply never carried forward to the new, looser rule the two real buttons adopted.

**Concrete impact.** Any tender whose Pack Review snapshot has zero Fix items but at least one open Provide item or unconfirmed-but-non-disqualifying Verify item (a routine, common state - e.g. a signatory not yet chosen when a suggested default exists, a B-BBEE level on file but not yet re-confirmed) has its real "Generate submission pack" button already enabled (`fixCount === 0`), while this same page's own prominent, above-the-fold sticky-header CTA shows itself as a disabled `<span aria-disabled="true">` with the message "N readiness item(s) still need confirming first" - telling the user they cannot proceed yet, when they already can, by the app's own documented rule (`app/AGENTS.md`, "Submit button: disabled while any Fix item is open"). The companion `WorkspaceStatusBadge` ("Ready to submit" vs. "Assessing & building") has the identical `thingsLeft === 0` gate and shows the same false "still building" state in this exact scenario - left as a known, related, lower-severity sibling of this fix (a passive status chip, not a control that blocks an action) rather than changed here, since unlike `PrimaryPackActionLink` it carries no doc comment explicitly promising parity with the real button's own gate, and conflating the two risks second-guessing a genuinely separate "fully reviewed" product judgment Sarel never explicitly made either way for that badge.

**Fix.** `app/app/tenders/[id]/page.tsx`: `PrimaryPackActionLink`'s `ready` prop and its `disabledReason` fallback text now read `tenderReadiness.fix.length === 0`/`tenderReadiness.fix.length > 0` instead of `tenderReadiness.thingsLeft === 0`/`> 0`, matching `submission-pack.tsx`'s `fixCount`/`general-workspace.tsx`'s `generalFixCount` exactly - the disabled-reason text now says "N Fix item(s) still need fixing before the pack can be generated" rather than the generic, misleading "readiness items ... confirming first".

**Verified red-then-green, myself, real exit codes.** `page.tsx` is an async Server Component (reads `next/headers`/Supabase at module scope) and cannot be imported standalone into a plain Node test, so verification is two real, executable checks in `tender-readiness.test.ts` rather than a live `next dev` HTTP repro:

A pure-logic case building a `ReviewSection[]` with one Provide item and one unconfirmed-but-non-disqualifying Verify item (zero Fix items): confirms `computeTenderReadiness()` really does produce `fix.length === 0` alongside `thingsLeft === 2` for this realistic scenario, then checks the OLD gate formula (`thingsLeft === 0`) against the REAL button's own formula (`fix.length === 0`) and asserts they disagree, and that the NEW gate formula agrees.
2. A direct check against `page.tsx`'s own real source text (`readFileSync`) - asserts the `ready=` prop's expression matches `tenderReadiness.fix.length === 0` and no longer matches `tenderReadiness.thingsLeft === 0` - so this test fails for real against the actual pre-fix file, not just against a logical replica of it.

### Finding 352 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, pushed directly to `main`): `lib/dispatchTriage.ts`'s `operationalStatusMessage()` never checked `DISPATCHED_STATUSES` in its own physical-box branch, unlike `classifyDispatchBucket()`'s `notYetDispatched` guard and this SAME function's own digital-submission branch two lines below (which already has that exact check, and a dedicated test proving it) - a physical-box tender already `printed_and_bound`/`out_for_delivery`, still inside the 48h print-cutoff window on the raw date math, got told "CRITICAL: ... Confirm the pack is ready to print" (actively wrong - it's already printed) while `classifyDispatchBucket()` had already stopped calling that same tender "critical"

**Why this angle.** The task brief's own primary angle for this pass: the git-log-archaeology method that found Findings 350/351 (a rule changed/promised-mirrored in one place, verify every site that reads the same condition was actually kept in line), applied to a DIFFERENT gate than `thingsLeft`/`fix.length`. `grep -rn "can't disagree\|cannot disagree\|so this can't\|never disagree\|matches.*own gate\|mirrors" app/app app/lib app/components engine` turned up several candidates beyond the already-closed `page.tsx` ones; `lib/dispatchTriage.ts:208`'s own comment - "A tender shown in the dashboard's Critical lane had its own 'system speaks to you' status line say nothing about being critical. **Mirrored here so the two can't disagree.**" - names `classifyDispatchBucket()` as the "two" being mirrored, for the digital-submission branch specifically (2026-11-05 finding, already fixed and tested - see that branch's own test, "a digital submission already dispatched doesn't falsely claim CRITICAL"). Reading the WHOLE function with that promise in mind (not just the branch the comment sits in) turned up the physical-box branch immediately above it, which makes the identical "critical window" claim from the identical underlying date math but was never given the identical `DISPATCHED_STATUSES` guard - the exact "comment names the promise, only the branch it was written in keeps it" shape the brief's primary angle described.

**The bug, read directly from the code, not inferred.**
```ts
export function operationalStatusMessage(input: DispatchLogisticsInput, blockingSummary: string | null, now: Date = new Date()): string | null {
  const deadline = printSignDeadline(input);
  const hoursLeft = hoursUntilPrintSignDeadline(input, now);
  if (deadline && hoursLeft !== null) {               // <- no DISPATCHED_STATUSES check here
    if (hoursLeft <= 0) return "PRINT OVERDUE...";
    ...
    if (hoursLeft <= 48) {
      return blockingSummary ? `CRITICAL: ... ${blockingSummary}` : `CRITICAL: ... Confirm the pack is ready to print.`;
    }
  } else if (input.submissionType !== "physical_box" && input.closingDate && !DISPATCHED_STATUSES.includes(input.dispatchStatus)) { // <- the digital branch DOES check it
    ...
  }
```
`printSignDeadline()`/`hoursUntilPrintSignDeadline()` are pure date math over `closingDate`/`submissionType`/the two hour estimates - neither reads `dispatchStatus` at all, so `deadline && hoursLeft !== null` is true for a `physical_box` tender with a valid closing date regardless of whether it has already been printed, bound, or handed to a courier. `classifyDispatchBucket()` (the function this one's own sibling branch is explicitly written to match) requires `notYetDispatched` (`!DISPATCHED_STATUSES.includes(input.dispatchStatus)`) before it will ever return `"critical"` for the identical physical-box 48h-window condition - confirmed already tested (`dispatchTriage.test.ts`'s own "classifyDispatchBucket: not critical once printed and bound, even past the cutoff"). `operationalStatusMessage()`'s physical-box branch has no such guard, so it disagreed with `classifyDispatchBucket()` for exactly this one state.

**Concrete impact.** Once a physical-box tender's dispatch status reaches `printed_and_bound` or `out_for_delivery` while still inside the 48-hour print-cutoff window (a routine, common state - teams print well ahead of the deadline, then the pack sits bound on a desk or in transit for hours before the cutoff actually arrives), two real, user-facing surfaces both call `operationalStatusMessage()` with this exact input and both showed the wrong message:
- `app/app/tenders/[id]/page.tsx` (line ~514): the tender workspace's own "system speaks to you" operational-status line showed "CRITICAL: you have N hours until the print cutoff. Confirm the pack is ready to print." - telling the team to go confirm printing on a pack that is already printed and bound, instead of the function's own, already-written, correct fallback message for this exact status ("Printed and ready - confirm delivery before the cutoff.") three lines further down in the same function, which this bug made unreachable for a physical-box tender in this window.
- `app/components/tt/command-center.tsx`'s `CriticalDispatchBanner` (line 46): if this tender happened to be the single highest-urgency card shown (it wouldn't appear in the Critical lane's own card list, which is pre-filtered by `classifyDispatchBucket()`'s own, correct "critical" bucket - but `CriticalDispatchBanner` is only ever rendered from `cards` already filtered to bucket `"critical"` upstream, so this exact disagreement could not itself surface through THIS one specific call site under the current caller, only through `page.tsx`'s own, unconditional call).
This is the same class of bug as Findings 350/351 (a site that reads a condition promised to mirror another site, but was never actually kept in line with it when a guard was added elsewhere) - just a display-text correctness bug, not a navigation/action gate, and confined to the one workspace page call site for its real, reachable impact today.

**Fix.** `app/lib/dispatchTriage.ts`: `operationalStatusMessage()`'s physical-box branch condition is now `deadline && hoursLeft !== null && !DISPATCHED_STATUSES.includes(input.dispatchStatus)`, matching `classifyDispatchBucket()`'s `notYetDispatched` guard and this function's own digital-submission branch exactly. Once a physical-box tender is already `printed_and_bound`/`out_for_delivery`/`submitted_and_receipted`, this branch is skipped entirely and execution falls through to the function's own existing, already-correct fallbacks (`blockingSummary`, then the dedicated "Printed and ready - confirm delivery before the cutoff." message for the first two statuses, then `null`).

### Finding 353 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, pushed directly to `main`): `cover-page-preview.tsx`'s own header comment promises it "shows exactly what engine/make_envelope_covers.py prints" - but the real generator's `_addressee_block()` has printed the tender's own tender-box delivery address (when one was found at intake) since 2026-10-18, and this React preview never had a prop for it at all, so it silently showed the preview as if no delivery address was ever on file for EVERY SANRAL tender, including the ones the real generator already prints a different, tender-specific address for

**Why this angle.** The task brief's own primary angle, widened per its own instruction to check files beyond `app/app` `app/lib` `app/components` `engine` already swept by Findings 350-352. `grep -rniE "can't disagree|cannot disagree|so this can't|never disagree|matches.*own gate|mirrors|stays in sync|kept in sync|same rule|consistent with|same check|same gate|same condition"` across every `.ts`/`.tsx`/`.py`/`.sql` file in the repo (not just the 4 directories the prior 3 passes used), excluding `.test.`/`.spec.` files, turned up 157 hits across ~120 files; narrowing to files none of Findings 350-352 or the standing "already ruled out" list had touched turned up `cover-page-preview.tsx`'s own header comment (unchanged since this component's original 2026-10-?? commit, prompt 10 item 3): "Read-only: shows exactly what engine/make_envelope_covers.py prints on the Outer/Envelope covers today ... all already read elsewhere on this page (tenderFacts) or on the company record". Reading the WHOLE real generator (`engine/make_envelope_covers.py`) with that promise in mind - not just the fields the React component's own prop list already covers - turned up `_addressee_block()`'s own delivery-address lines, added in a dedicated, dated fix: "Until 2026-10-18 every cover carried SANRAL head office's ... address ... R.396's own Tender Notice says the tender box is at 20 Shoreward Drive, Bay West, Gqeberha. No address on file = no address printed ... never a guess." `CoverPagePreview`'s own prop list (`contractNo`, `nraReference`, `description`, `buyer`, `closingDate`, `company`) has no `deliveryAddress` prop at all - confirmed by reading the full, unmodified component before touching anything.

**The bug, read directly from the code, not inferred.** `engine/make_envelope_covers.py`'s `_addressee_block(d, delivery_address=None)`:
```python
lines = ["The South African National Roads Agency SOC Limited"] + [l for l in (delivery_address or []) if l]
```
- called by both `make_outer()` and `make_inner()`, fed `tender.get("delivery_address")` (`engine/pack/assemble_pack.py:409`) or, inside `process_pack_jobs.py`'s own `gather()`, `(tender_pack.get("intake") or {}).get("delivery_address") or (tender.get("intake") or {}).get("delivery_address")).get("lines")` - the tender's own tender-box address, read once at intake by `engine/intake/classify_tender.py`'s `find_delivery_address()` (SANRAL route only) and written into `intake_rec["delivery_address"]` by `engine/general/process_general_jobs.py` (committed into either `tenders.intake` or, for a shared tender this company has a private re-read of, `tender_packs.intake`). `app/lib/manualTender.ts`'s own `TenderIntake` type - the type `intake-card.tsx` already casts this exact column to - had no `delivery_address` field at all, confirmed by reading the whole type definition: every one of its other fields (`route`, `family`, `setup`, `fingerprint`, etc.) is present, this one silently never was, even though `process_general_jobs.py` has written it since the same 2026-10-18 commit that added the real engine's own printing of it. `CoverPagePreview`'s own `printLines` array and on-screen JSX both hard-coded the SANRAL addressee line with nothing after it - no read of `intake` anywhere on this page fed into it, confirmed by reading `page.tsx`'s own call site (`contractNo`/`nraReference`/`description`/`buyer`/`closingDate` only) and its `tenders`/`tender_packs` selects (neither selected the `intake` column at all before this fix).

**Concrete impact.** For any SANRAL-route tender where the extraction pipeline found a real tender-box delivery address in the tender's own documents (the routine, common case the 2026-10-18 engine fix itself was written for - a tender box anywhere other than SANRAL's own head office, which per that fix's own commit message is itself the common case, not the exception), the Cover Page Preview - the one screen whose entire stated purpose is to let the team "see exactly what will print ... read-only ... before building anything" - showed the SAME generic "The South African National Roads Agency SOC Limited" line with nothing after it, every time, regardless of what the real envelope covers would actually print underneath it. A team relying on this preview to sanity-check the delivery address before dispatch had no way to do so here at all - they would only discover the real, tender-specific address (or discover it was missing/ambiguous, both states `intake.notes` already records in free text) by opening the actual generated `.docx` after the pack is built, defeating the one thing this component exists to let them check early. Not a wrong document (the real generator, `make_envelope_covers.py`, was always correct and is untouched by this fix) - a silently incomplete, misleading PREVIEW of a correct document, the same "comment promises parity, only some sites were ever kept in sync" shape as Findings 350-352, just between a UI preview and the real generator it claims to mirror rather than between two UI call sites.

**Fix.**
- `app/lib/manualTender.ts`: `TenderIntake` gains the missing `delivery_address?: { lines: string[]; quote: string; ambiguous: boolean }` field the engine has written since 2026-10-18.
- `app/app/tenders/[id]/cover-page-lines.ts` (new): pure, exported `deliveryAddressLines()` (the same `[l for l in (delivery_address or []) if l]` blank-line filter as `_addressee_block()`) and `buildOuterEnvelopeLines()` (the full `printLines` array, now delivery-address-aware, output byte-identical to the old hard-coded array when no address is present - confirmed by test).
- `app/app/tenders/[id]/cover-page-preview.tsx`: new optional `deliveryAddress?: string[] | null` prop; `printLines` now built via `buildOuterEnvelopeLines()`; the on-screen dashed-border preview box now also renders the same address lines (`addressLines.map(...)`), right after the SANRAL line and before `CONTRACT`, matching `_addressee_block()`'s own line order exactly.
- `app/app/tenders/[id]/page.tsx`: both the `tenders` and `tender_packs` selects now include `intake`; a new `intake = tenderPack?.intake ?? tenderFacts?.intake ?? null` computation (the exact `tender_pack.intake`-over-`tender.intake` precedence `intake-card.tsx`'s own `ownPack?.intake ?? tender.intake` already established, matching `process_pack_jobs.py`'s own `gather()` read order) feeds `deliveryAddress={intake?.delivery_address?.lines ?? null}` into `CoverPagePreview`.
- `/demo` (`app/app/demo/page.tsx`) is unchanged - it never passes `deliveryAddress` at all, so the new prop is simply `undefined` there and the demo's own cover-page preview output is byte-identical to before this fix (confirmed by `buildOuterEnvelopeLines()`'s own no-address regression test and by `next build`'s unchanged `/demo` route).

**Verified red-then-green, myself, real exit codes.** New test file, `app/app/tenders/[id]/cover-page-lines.test.ts`, following `tender-readiness.test.ts`'s own established two-tier pattern exactly: pure-logic cases against the new `cover-page-lines.ts` functions, plus two source-text checks (`readFileSync`) confirming `cover-page-preview.tsx` and `page.tsx` actually wire the fix through, not just that the pure helper exists in isolation.
- **RED**: `git stash push -- "app/app/tenders/[id]/cover-page-preview.tsx" "app/app/tenders/[id]/page.tsx" "app/lib/manualTender.ts"` (reverting the three real pre-fix files, keeping the new `cover-page-lines.ts` and its test), then `node --experimental-strip-types "app/tenders/[id]/cover-page-lines.test.ts"`: **6 tests, 4 pass, 2 fail**, real exit code **1** - the 4 pure-logic tests pass regardless (they test the new, already-correct helper in isolation), but both source-text tests fail for real against the actual, unpatched `cover-page-preview.tsx`/`page.tsx` (no `deliveryAddress` prop, no `buildOuterEnvelopeLines()` call, no `intake` column in either select) - exactly the "some sites were never kept in sync" shape this bug has.
- **GREEN**: `git stash pop` (all three real files restored), re-ran the same command: **6/6 passed**, real exit code **0**.
- **Full regression**: every `*.test.ts` file run directly, the exact loop `.github/workflows/app-ci.yml` uses (`find . -name "*.test.ts" -not -path "*/node_modules/*"` then `node --experimental-strip-types` on each) - **32 files** (counted myself: 31 pre-existing + 1 new), **0 failures**. `npx vitest run` - **79 files, 666/666 passed**, unchanged (no `.spec.ts` file touched). `npx tsc --noEmit` - clean, exit 0. `npx eslint "app/tenders/[id]/cover-page-preview.tsx" "app/tenders/[id]/cover-page-lines.ts" "app/tenders/[id]/cover-page-lines.test.ts" "app/tenders/[id]/page.tsx" "lib/manualTender.ts"` - clean, 0 warnings. `npx next build` - completed cleanly, exit 0, full route list unchanged including `/tenders/[id]` and `/demo`.

**Why a direct push to `main`, not a PR.** Pure TypeScript/JSX plus one existing jsonb column added to two already-existing `.select()` calls (no new migration, no RLS policy touched, no new table/RPC) - not RLS, not a money path, not a hard-stop/disqualification gate (`CoverPagePreview` is read-only and gates nothing - confirmed by reading the whole component, same as Finding 352's own reasoning for `dispatchTriage.ts`). Not the production worker image. The real document-GENERATION code this preview claims to mirror (`engine/make_envelope_covers.py`, `engine/pack/assemble_pack.py`, `engine/pack/process_pack_jobs.py`) is completely untouched and was always correct - this fix only makes a read-only UI PREVIEW of that already-correct output accurately reflect it; it does not change what any company actually submits. `grep -rln 'tenders/\[id\]/page"\|cover-page-preview\|cover-page-lines'` across `app/` for `pack-review.tsx`/`submission-pack.tsx`'s own import blocks - confirmed neither imports from `page.tsx`, `cover-page-preview.tsx`, or `cover-page-lines.ts` (the same check Finding 350/351 already ran for `page.tsx` itself, re-run fresh here for the two new files too) - so the "touches a file those two import from" guardrail does not apply.
