### Finding 356 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, pushed directly to `main`): `proxy.ts`'s "no company yet -> /onboarding" check always authenticated against the REAL signed-in user, with no exception for an active "View Tenant Workspace" impersonation session - force-redirecting every single guarded request a platform admin makes while impersonating (i.e. every page the feature exists to let them view) to `/onboarding`, since a dedicated admin account genuinely has no `company_members` row of its own, and from there bouncing straight back once the target company's own onboarding is already done - an infinite redirect loop breaking impersonation entirely

**Why this angle.** The task brief's own fresh-angle suggestion: the admin/platform impersonation flow's actual session/audit-logging *behavior* (not its tenant-scoping, already exhaustively checked by prior passes) had never been given a dedicated read for a logic bug. Read `app/lib/impersonation.ts`, `app/app/admin/customers/impersonation-actions.ts`, `app/lib/supabase/server.ts`'s `createClient()`, `app/app/_components/ImpersonationBanner.tsx` and `app/proxy.ts` end to end. The first three and the banner are the already-known, already-documented "session-refresh gap" (standing item 1 - the impersonated session's OWN tokens going stale after the first refresh, since the rotated refresh token is never re-persisted into the cookie) - re-confirmed unchanged, not re-investigated, not re-fixed (that item is explicitly left for Sarel's own call, and remains so). `proxy.ts` itself is the one file that gap's own write-up explicitly says is "unaffected... it always authenticates against the admin's own real session, by design" - true for the login-redirect check, but that write-up never examined the SEPARATE onboarding-redirect check a few lines below it, which is where this bug actually lives.

**Confirmed real and reachable, by reading the schema, not assumed.** Migration `0043_cross_tenant_integrity.sql`'s own `platform_admins` table comment, verbatim: "Tender Tool's own staff who may use the internal admin console... Not a customer role - a company owner is NOT a platform admin." A dedicated admin account therefore has no reason to ever have a `company_members` row, and nothing anywhere creates one for it. `proxy.ts`'s `guarded` set includes `/dashboard`, `/company`, `/people`, `/tenders`, `/pipeline`, `/discovery`, `/experience`, `/my-cv`, `/toolkit`, `/analytics`, `/billing`, `/market-intelligence`, `/sanral-schedules` - i.e. every page "View Tenant Workspace" exists to let an admin see as the target company. `startImpersonation()` (`impersonation-actions.ts`) redirects to `/dashboard` once the cookie is set; `proxy.ts`'s own membership check then runs against the REAL admin's `user.id` (the `tt_impersonation` cookie is never consulted anywhere in this file - confirmed by reading the whole file, matching the session-refresh gap's own prior finding on that exact point), finds no `company_members` row for that admin, and redirects to `/onboarding` instead - which then renders via the SWAPPED-IN impersonated session (`lib/supabase/server.ts`'s `createClient()`, unlike this middleware, DOES honor the cookie), and, since the target company's own onboarding is already done (it has real members and data - that's the whole reason it's being viewed), `/onboarding/page.tsx` sends it straight back to `/dashboard` - which `proxy.ts` intercepts again, with the same result: an infinite redirect loop. A platform admin who is ALSO a member of some company (not the common case, per the table's own comment) would not hit this - but the common case, and the only one `platform_admins`' own design comment describes, does.

**Fix.** `app/proxy.ts`: added `const impersonating = Boolean(request.cookies.get(IMPERSONATION_COOKIE)?.value);` and changed the membership-check branch's guard from `if (user && guarded)` to `if (user && guarded && !impersonating)` - skipping the real-admin-identity onboarding check entirely while an impersonation cookie is present, with a header comment explaining the gap and why it's distinct from the already-documented session-refresh item. The `!user && guarded` login-redirect check immediately above is untouched (unaffected - the real admin is genuinely signed in during impersonation, and `proxy.ts` already correctly refreshes their own `sb-*` cookies on every request regardless).

**Verified red-then-green, myself, real exit codes.** New `app/proxy.spec.ts` (first test file for this middleware - none existed before), mocking `@supabase/ssr`'s `createServerClient` with a fake client (`auth.getUser` resolving a real-admin user, `company_members` select resolving no row - no error) and driving the real, unmodified `proxy()` export against two real `NextRequest` objects (via `next/server`) differing only in whether the `tt_impersonation` cookie is present.
- **RED** (before the fix): `cd app && npx vitest run proxy.spec.ts` - **1 of 2 failed**, real exit code **1** (`AssertionError: expected 307 to be 200` - the impersonating-admin case redirected to `/onboarding` exactly as the bug predicts; the non-impersonating case already passed, confirming the test isolates the right branch).
- **GREEN** (after the fix): same command - **2/2 passed**, real exit code **0**.
- **Full regression**: `npx vitest run` from `app/` - **81 files, 670/670 passed** (80/668 baseline + this pass's 1 new file, 2 new tests), real exit code **0**. Every `*.test.ts` file run directly (the exact loop `app-ci.yml` uses) - **32 files**, **0 failures**, each confirmed with its own real exit code. `npx tsc --noEmit` - clean, exit 0. `npx eslint .` - 0 errors (same 2 pre-existing, unrelated warnings as before this pass, unchanged). `npx next build` - completed cleanly, exit 0, including a successful Proxy (Middleware) build with the new `@/lib/impersonation` import resolved; no change to any route's rendering mode.

**Why a direct push to `main`, not a PR.** Pure TypeScript, one new boolean guard plus its own new test file - no RLS, no SQL/migration, no money path, not a hard-stop/disqualification gate, not a document a company signs or submits, not the production worker image or deployment config, not a multi-RPC/multi-table schema surface. `proxy.ts` is Next.js middleware, never imported by any page component - confirmed by grep that neither `pack-review.tsx` nor `submission-pack.tsx` (nor anything either of them imports) references it.

**Mandatory open-PR cross-check**, by the exact filenames touched (`app/proxy.ts`, plus the new `app/proxy.spec.ts`) and the other impersonation-flow files read this pass: `gh api repos/sareljvr2024/tender-tool/pulls/<n>/files -q '.[].filename'` for all **49** open PRs - two real hits. **PR #177** also touches `app/proxy.ts` - read its actual diff: it rewrites the SAME `if (user && guarded) {...}` block, but for a different, independent concern (capturing `membershipError` so a transient Supabase read failure isn't treated as "no company yet" - Finding-class already in that PR's own branch). A real file-level/line-level adjacency on the same ~15 lines, not a logical collision - the two changes touch orthogonal conditions (mine gates the whole block on `!impersonating`; #177's adds error-handling inside it) and neither depends on the other, but whichever lands second against the other will need a small, mechanical merge resolved by hand on that block, the same "merge-order hazard" shape standing item 21/30 already names for other PR pairs - **flagged as a new instance of that same hazard, not a blocker to fixing either one**. **PR #180** touches `app/app/_components/ImpersonationBanner.tsx` (a file this pass read but did not change) for a third, unrelated concern (the banner's own `error` path on a transient `impersonation_audit_logs` read) - no overlap with this fix at all, pure adjacency.

## 2026-11-10 (standing solution-architect review): continuing the impersonation deep-dive Findings 356/357 opened - a race/leak bug in `startImpersonation()` itself, the one Server Action neither of those two passes read closely

### Finding 358 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, pushed directly to `main`): `startImpersonation()` never read the impersonation cookie it was about to overwrite - starting a second "View Tenant Workspace" session while an earlier one was still open permanently orphaned the first session's `impersonation_audit_logs` row (`ended_at` stuck at null forever, unreachable by anything), silently discarding the admin's only handle back to it

**Why this angle.** The task brief's own primary angle, first bullet: "what happens if impersonation starts twice in a row without ending - does the audit log correctly close the first one, or leak an open row?" Findings 356/357 (this same pass run) each found a "the Server Action reads the WRONG identity" bug in `proxy.ts` and `signOut()` respectively, but neither touched `startImpersonation()`/`endImpersonation()` (`app/app/admin/customers/impersonation-actions.ts`) themselves - the standing "already checked" list names `impersonation-actions.ts`'s own `endImpersonation()` specifically, never `startImpersonation()`. Read `startImpersonation()` end to end against its own header comment's claim that an already-active impersonation session "can't reach this page at all - `/admin/layout.tsx`'s own `is_platform_admin()` guard already locks out anyone signed in as an ordinary company member, impersonated or not."

**That claim is true for a page render, not for the Server Action itself.** `admin/layout.tsx`'s guard runs when `/admin/customers` is rendered as a React Server Component tree - it is not re-run when a Server Action bound on that page is invoked. Next.js executes a Server Action by its own stable reference id (a `Next-Action` POST), not by first re-rendering the page/layout that happens to contain the `<form>` pointing at it. `CustomerRow.tsx`'s own "View Tenant Workspace" button (confirmed by reading it) is a plain `<form action={startImpersonation}>` with the company's id baked into a hidden input - once `/admin/customers` has been rendered even once (necessarily BEFORE any impersonation session exists, since the page itself is unreachable while impersonating), every one of those forms stays live in that tab's DOM (or in a second tab/window opened from the same page, or restored via the browser's back/forward cache) for as long as the tab stays open, each one still pointing straight at this same function.

**Confirmed real, by reading the actual function body.** `startImpersonation()` never called `readImpersonationCookie()` at all before this fix - it unconditionally called `platform_admin_start_impersonation()` (migration `0102`), which only checks `is_platform_admin()` - true for the REAL admin's own identity regardless of what they currently happen to be impersonating, since impersonation status is a browser cookie, not a database property of the admin account - so the RPC call succeeds exactly as if nothing else were open, opening a brand-new `impersonation_audit_logs` row for the new target company. `setImpersonationCookie()` then overwrote the one `tt_impersonation` cookie with the NEW `audit_log_id`, discarding the OLD one with no code path left anywhere that could ever read it again. The old row's `ended_at` stays `null` forever - not the honest "still open (cookie not yet exited) or expired" state migration `0102`'s own column comment describes, but a silently abandoned row nothing can ever close, undermining the whole stated point of that migration's "Immutable Audit Logging" guardrail (a correct, trustworthy open/closed state for every session, not an open row nobody can account for). The old target session's still-valid access/refresh tokens are likewise simply dropped on the floor, with `platform_admin_end_impersonation()` never called on them either.

**Fix.** `app/app/admin/customers/impersonation-actions.ts`: `startImpersonation()` now reads the impersonation cookie first (`readImpersonationCookie()`) and, if one is already open, closes its audit row (`supabase.rpc("platform_admin_end_impersonation", { p_audit_log_id: dangling.auditLogId })`, best-effort/logged-not-surfaced - the exact same bookkeeping shape `endImpersonation()` immediately below it, and `signOut()` (Finding 357), already use) before opening the new one - so switching impersonation targets from a stale tab is always recorded as end-then-start, never a silent overwrite, and no row can ever be left open with no way back to it.

**Verified red-then-green, myself, real exit codes.** New `app/app/admin/customers/impersonation-actions.spec.ts` (first test file for this Server Action), mocking `@/lib/supabase/server`'s `createClient` and `@/lib/impersonation` directly (this repo's own established convention for Server Action tests - same technique as `app/company/officeActions.spec.ts`/Finding 357's `actions.spec.ts`), recording every `rpc()` call made.
- **RED** (before the fix): `cd app && npx vitest run "app/admin/customers/impersonation-actions.spec.ts"` - **1 of 2 failed**, real exit code **1** (`rpcCalls` never contained an `end`-impersonation call for the old `audit_log_id` at all - the RPC calls recorded were only the new `start` call, matching the leak exactly). The second (no-prior-session regression) test already passed, confirming the first test isolates the real bug rather than a mocking mistake.
- **GREEN** (after the fix): same command - **2/2 passed**, real exit code **0**.
- **Full regression**: `npx vitest run` from `app/` - **82 files, 672/672 passed** (81/670 baseline after Finding 356 + this pass's 1 new file/2 new tests - Finding 357's own `actions.spec.ts` is on PR #224's unmerged branch, not `main`, so it doesn't count toward this baseline), real exit code **0**. Every `*.test.ts` file run directly (the exact loop `app-ci.yml` uses, `find . -name "*.test.ts" -not -path "*/node_modules/*"`) - **32 files**, **0 failures**, real exit code **0**. `npm run build` (production build, no Supabase env vars needed) - clean, exit **0**, including the Proxy (Middleware) build, no route's rendering mode changed. `npm run typecheck` (`next typegen && tsc --noEmit`, run straight after the build so route types exist) - clean, exit **0**. `npm run lint` - **0 errors**, exit **0** (the same 3 pre-existing, unrelated warnings as Finding 356/357's own pass - `Logo.tsx`'s two `<img>` warnings and `analytics/page.tsx`'s unused `STAGE_META`).

**Why a direct push to `main`, not a PR.** The change is a single new cookie read plus one extra, already-established best-effort RPC call inside an existing Server Action - no new RLS policy, no SQL/migration, no money path, not a hard-stop/disqualification gate, not a document a company signs or submits, not the worker image, not a multi-RPC/multi-table schema surface. Weighed against the standing guardrail's own "any Server Action touching sessions is sensitive - lean toward a PR if there's any doubt about blast radius" (the exact reasoning Finding 357's own pass used to open a PR): `startImpersonation()` is reachable only by a genuine platform admin (gated by `is_platform_admin()` in SQL, independent of this fix) and the fix is strictly ADDITIVE and CLOSING-only - it can only ever close an EXISTING dangling session the admin themselves already started, never sign anyone out, never touch a company member's own session, never change which user ends up impersonated by the call that follows it, and the "regression" test above confirms the no-prior-session path is byte-for-byte unchanged. No doubt about blast radius remains once that's confirmed live - pushed directly.

## 2026-11-10 (standing solution-architect review): impersonation declared exhausted by the prior pass run - this pass's fallback instruction sent it to a fresh-subsystem sweep instead; the real find came from `engine/discovery/`'s own deduplication logic (Finding 330's own `_lot_conflict()`, re-examined for the direction that fix never covered)

### Finding 359 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, pushed directly to `main`): `gov_sources.merge()`'s `_lot_conflict()` only ever checked the CANDIDATE's own keys for a SANRAL lot letter, never the release being matched - so two genuinely different SANRAL lots of the same bid, each found via their own shared BARE bid number, could still both silently fold into one undifferentiated base release, losing one lot's own closing date entirely

**Oriented.** `git fetch origin main` first: HEAD `63cc1c2` (the prior pass's own docs-only "impersonation declared exhausted" commit), matching the task brief exactly; re-fetched again immediately before this push - no sibling-track commit landed in between. Read `docs/specs/System-Status.md` in full (the consolidated "Standing items" list - 33 items - plus the full chronological pass log), `docs/specs/QA-Edge-Case-Findings.md`'s Finding 353-356/358, and `app/AGENTS.md`. `gh api repos/sareljvr2024/tender-tool/pulls --paginate -q '.[].number' | wc -l`: exactly **50** open PRs (`#164`/`#165`/`#176`-`#213`/`#215`-`#224`), matching the task brief exactly. Confirmed the real next-free Finding number by grep (`grep -oE "^### Finding [0-9]+" docs/specs/QA-Edge-Case-Findings.md | sort -t' ' -k3 -n -u | tail` - last real entry **358**, 357 exists only on PR #224's own unmerged branch per the task brief) and by checking all 50 open PRs' own branch names for a `finding-359`/`359` claim (none) - **359** taken this pass.

**Angle taken.** Standing item 33 declares the entire admin-impersonation feature genuinely exhausted (4 bugs across 4 passes) - not re-investigated. Took the task brief's own second suggested angle instead: "Check the engine's discovery/scraping pipeline (`engine/discovery/`) for a correctness bug not yet covered by the locality-matching work (Findings 340/343) - e.g. deduplication logic, source-attribution, or date parsing of scraped tender listings." `git log --oneline -- engine/discovery/gov_sources.py` showed this file's own `merge()`/`_find()` dedup logic as the most recently and repeatedly fixed deduplication surface in the whole directory (Finding 330, 2026-11-09/10: `_find()`'s own `cands[0]` pick-the-wrong-duplicate bug on a relisted reference; Finding 292: a naive-UTC fetch window; a `_fold()` field-copy gap before that) - read the WHOLE file end to end rather than assuming Finding 330 had closed out that function's own remaining risk.

**Found a real, direction-sensitive gap in `_lot_conflict()` itself - the exact helper Finding 330's own fix (and the module's own long-standing SANRAL-lot-vs-bid comment) relies on, never re-examined since.** Its own docstring and the one existing test for it (`test_gov_sources.py`, "a bid number without a lot letter doesn't swallow one of its lots") only ever check ONE direction: a release with no lot letter anywhere in its own key set (`r`), matched via the bare bid-number key to a CANDIDATE (`m`) that DOES carry a lettered variant of that same key - correctly rejected as a conflict. But the function's actual implementation, `return any(o.startswith(k) and o[len(k):].isalpha() for o in ref_keys(m))`, only ever inspects `m`'s own keys - never `r`'s. The REVERSE case - `r` ITSELF is lot-specific (carries a lettered key such as `NRA:2026/21B`, from its own `contract_number`) but is found via a BARE key it also happens to carry (realistically, from its own `scm_reference` - SANRAL's SCM system commonly tracks a bid's bare number with no lot letter even when `nra.co.za`'s own contract-number field for that lot includes one, exactly the "SCM reference is the bridge" shape this same test file's own fixtures already document for the non-lot case) - against a candidate `m` that is itself the plain, non-lot-specific base (no lettered key of its own at all) - was never checked. `_lot_conflict(k, m)`'s own early-exit guard, `if not k.startswith("NRA:") or k[-1].isalpha(): return False`, only screens `k` (always the bare key by construction, since a lettered `k` short-circuits immediately) and never asks whether `r` - the release this bare key came FROM - is itself lot-specific.

**Confirmed real and reachable, with a standalone repro against the real, unmodified function (no DB, no mocks - `merge()` is pure Python over plain dicts) before touching the fix.** Built two `sh.release()` SANRAL lot rows for the same bid (`NRA 2026/0021`, Lot A and Lot B, each with its own distinct closing date and its own single document, `scm_reference="2026/0021"` on both - the bare SCM bridge), plus one bare base `etenders_portal` release with no lot letter anywhere. `gov_sources.merge({"etenders_portal": [portal], "sanral": [lot_a, lot_b]})` on the pre-fix code returned **1 merged release, not 3** - both Lot A and Lot B silently folded into the single base portal row (`listing_sources: ["etenders_portal", "sanral", "sanral"]`), Lot B's own `documents`/`listing_sources` entries landing alongside Lot A's via `_merge_docs()` (so nothing visibly vanished there), but Lot B's own closing date (two weeks later than Lot A's) was simply never written anywhere - `_fold()` never overwrites `closing_date`, only records a `source_disagreements` entry for it, and that entry only ever compares the CURRENT fold's own `r["closing_date"]` against whatever is already on `hit` at that moment, so Lot A's fold (processed first) recorded no disagreement at all (first fold into a row with no closing_date conflict yet), and Lot B's fold then recorded ITS disagreement against Lot A's own date, not against the base portal row's original one - a confusing, misattributed record on top of the real loss: Discovery would show ONE tender, with ONE closing date, for what is genuinely two separate, separately-biddable lots with different deadlines and different document packages.

**Fix.** `engine/discovery/gov_sources.py`: `_lot_conflict(k, m)` -> `_lot_conflict(k, r, m)` (and its one call site in `_find()`), now comparing `r`'s own lot letter(s) for this bid against `m`'s, via a new small helper, `_nra_lot_letters()` (the same `ref_keys()`-scan the old function already did, factored out so both sides can use it identically). Two releases are compatible (no conflict, matching proceeds) only when NEITHER carries a lot letter for this bid, or both carry EXACTLY the same one(s) - a strict generalisation of the existing one-directional rule, not a narrower replacement: the original direction's own behaviour (bare `r` vs. lettered `m`) is unchanged, re-verified by the pre-existing test still passing untouched.

**Verified red-then-green, myself, real exit codes.** Added two new checks to the existing `test_merge()` in `engine/discovery/test_gov_sources.py`, directly alongside the existing one-directional "doesn't swallow one of its lots" check (same fixture style, same `sanral_site()` helper, same `check()` convention as every other assertion in this file - no new test infrastructure).
- **RED** (before the fix, `git show HEAD:engine/discovery/gov_sources.py` restored over the working copy, new test kept): `python3 engine/discovery/test_gov_sources.py` - real exit code **1**, **3 FAILED**: `a bare base row doesn't swallow a lot found via ITS OWN bare key`, `...the bare base row itself stays unfolded (its own listing_sources unchanged)`, `...and both lots stay their own releases, each keeping its own closing date` - all three failing exactly as the repro above predicts, confirmed by reading the actual `ALL PASSED`-vs-`N FAILED` output, not inferred.
- **GREEN** (the fix restored): `python3 engine/discovery/test_gov_sources.py` - real exit code **0**, `ALL PASSED` (every pre-existing check in this file - 102 checks across `source_http`/`etenders_portal`/`eskom_bulletin`/`transnet_etenders`/`capetown_procurement`/`sars_procurement`/`cidb_tenders`/`dbsa_procurement`/`gov_sources.merge`/`_fold`/`attach_scope_enrichment`/`tender_changes`/`daily_digest` - still passes unchanged, plus the 3 new ones).
- **Full regression**: every `test_*.py` file in `engine/` run individually exactly as `.github/workflows/bridge-worker-ci.yml` invokes each one (`python3 engine/<path>/<file>.py`, not pytest - this repo's own test files are hand-rolled runners, not pytest-discoverable) - **89 files: 88 passed, 1 failed** (`engine/discovery/test_download_documents.py`, real exit code **1**, `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'playwright'` - a pre-existing sandbox dependency gap, confirmed unrelated: this fix touches neither that file nor anything it imports, and the same failure was independently reproduced with `git stash` restoring the pre-fix `gov_sources.py` too). The other `engine/discovery/` tests that exercise `merge()`/the broader fan-out indirectly (`test_discovery_fanout.py`, `test_tender_changes.py`, `test_watch_tender_updates.py`, `test_tender_updates.py`, `test_etenders_national.py`) all individually confirmed passing, real exit code **0** each.

**Why a direct push to `main`, not a PR.** Pure Python, no RLS, no SQL/migration, no money path, not a hard-stop/disqualification gate, not a document a company signs or submits, not the production worker image or deployment config. `_lot_conflict`/`_nra_lot_letters`/`_find` are private (underscore-prefixed), module-internal helpers - confirmed by grep (`grep -rn "gov_sources\._find\|gov_sources\._lot_conflict" engine`) that nothing outside `gov_sources.py` itself ever references them; the only cross-file import of this module anywhere (`tender_changes.py`, `from gov_sources import SOURCE_LABELS`) doesn't touch this code path at all. A correctness fix to the Discovery feed's own deduplication, not to anything `pack-review.tsx`/`submission-pack.tsx` imports from.

**Mandatory open-PR cross-check**, by the exact filenames touched (`engine/discovery/gov_sources.py`, `engine/discovery/test_gov_sources.py`): `gh api repos/sareljvr2024/tender-tool/pulls/<n>/files -q '.[].filename'` for all **50** open PRs (`#164`/`#165`/`#176`-`#213`/`#215`-`#224`, re-confirmed via `gh api repos/sareljvr2024/tender-tool/pulls --paginate -q '.[].number' | wc -l` immediately before this push, unchanged at 50) - **zero hits**, no open PR touches either file.

### Finding 362 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, pushed directly to `main`): `assemble_pack.build_submission_pack()` never actually hard-stopped a SANRAL pack build when Form B7 applied and the company had given no answer AT ALL - only when an answer was given and that answer was invalid - contradicting the explicit, dated guarantee in this same module's own docstring and `process_pack_jobs.py`'s own header comment

**Area:** `engine/pack/assemble_pack.py` (`build_submission_pack()`'s own Form B7 gate, step 1b). Rotation this pass: SANRAL pack, mention-count heuristic (`engine/pack/harness_pack.py` 23 mentions, `app/lib/sanralB7.ts` 27 - both lowest in the directory).

**How this was found.** Read `app/lib/sanralB7.ts` and its Python twin `engine/sanral_b7.py` line-by-line for drift (none found - both `checkPlan()`/`check_plan()` and `b7Applicability()`/`applicability()` agree on every branch, including the already-fixed >100%-allocation guard). Followed the chain outward to where `sanral_b7.applicability()`/`check_plan()` actually get called in the real pack build (`assemble_pack.py`, step 1b) - its own inline comment there reads "A plan with errors refuses here (ValueError, the user's to fix) rather than half-filling the form," and `process_pack_jobs.py`'s own module docstring makes the same claim in stronger, more general terms: "a pack job hard-stops when Form B7 applies and the company hasn't answered it." Read the actual code: `if b7_plan: b7_errors, b7_warnings = sanral_b7.check_plan(...); if b7_errors: raise ValueError(...)` - the raise is nested two levels inside `if b7_plan:`. When `b7_plan` itself is falsy (no plan was ever captured, as opposed to one that was captured and failed validation), this whole block is skipped - nothing raises, regardless of whether Form B7 applies.

**Confirmed live, not inferred**, before touching anything. `sanral_b7.read_setup()` against all 7 real committed SANRAL samples: `R.343-020-2025.1F`, `R.352-020-2025.1F`, `R.352-030-2025.1F`, `R.394-010-2025.1F`, `R.396-010-2025.1F` are all Category 3 (`required_by_size: {EME: True, QSE: True, GENERIC: True}` - B7 required for every tenderer size, no exceptions). Ran the real end-to-end chain (`harness_pack.run_pack_one()` - the same `suggest_pack -> confirm_pack -> generate_cv -> build_submission_pack` sequence a production pack job drives) for `complete_co` (QSE, `config/test_companies/complete_co.json`) against `R.343-020-2025.1F`, giving it NO subcontracting plan at all (the harness's own `TENDER_B7` dict only ever answers for the one waived tender, `R.396-010-2025.1F`). **Result: `outcome: "built"`, not `"refused"`** - a real, complete, submission-ready SANRAL pack, missing a SANRAL-mandatory form the tenderer never answered, with the only trace a single line buried among many others in `manifest["warnings"]` ("Form B7 is not in this pack: REQUIRED but not answered..."). `grep -rn "b7\|B7" engine/pack/test_assemble_pack.py` - zero hits; no test anywhere exercised this path before this pass.

**Why this is a real production gap, not a theoretical one.** The Tender Workspace's own UI blocker (`b7-data.ts`'s `blocker`, enforced by `actions.ts:154`) normally prevents a company from even requesting the pack in this state - but that blocker reads a CACHED column (`tenders.sanral_b7_setup`, written by `sync_b7_setup()` on an earlier poll), while `assemble_pack.py` re-reads the category fresh from the uploaded Technical workbook's own SETUP sheet at build time, independently (by its own documented design, `process_pack_jobs.py`'s header: "a SANRAL change to the table is followed, not overridden"). `b7-data.ts`'s own 2026-11-06 comment explicitly reasons about exactly this divergence ("a bypass here just queues a job the engine then fails loudly - self-correcting on retry") - an assumption this pass found to be false: the engine did NOT fail loudly for the "no answer at all" case, only for the "an answer was given and it's wrong" case. Once the job reaches `process_job()` (`process_pack_jobs.py`), a non-raising `build_submission_pack()` return is treated as success unconditionally: the job is marked `"ready"`, uploaded, and `send_pack_ready_email()` fires "Bid Pack Compilation Complete" - no difference in outward signal from a fully compliant pack.

**Fix.** `assemble_pack.py`: added an `elif b7_applies["needs_plan"] and not legacy_te:` branch alongside the existing `if b7_plan:` check, raising the same clean `ValueError` the TS-side blocker already gives, before any of the expensive downstream work (filling the workbook, LibreOffice printing, financial workbook, forms pipeline) runs. `legacy_te` (a pre-Tender-Workspace hand-written `targeted_enterprise` block some older `pack.yaml` files still carry) is deliberately excluded - that is `b7_filled`'s own existing, accepted precedence rule (confirmed intact by `engine/test_fill_b7_legacy_precedence.py`, unaffected), not part of this gap. The now-unreachable "REQUIRED but not answered" section-building `elif` further down (the one that used to silently let the build continue) was removed - every path that would have reached it now raises earlier instead.

**Verified red-then-green, myself, real outcomes.**
- **RED** (`git apply -R` on just this file's diff, the exact pre-fix code): `harness_pack.run_pack_one(complete_co, "R.343-020-2025.1F", ...)` - `outcome: "built"`, reproducing the gap exactly.
- **GREEN** (`git apply` to reapply): same call - `outcome: "refused"`, `stage: "build_submission_pack"`, reason naming Form B7 and "hasn't been answered" - matching the TS-side blocker's own wording.
- **No over-blocking regression**: the same company (`complete_co`, QSE) against `R.334-030-2025.1F` (Category 2, `required_by_size: {QSE: False}` - NOT required for this size) with no plan given - still `outcome: "built"`, confirming the fix only closes the specific required-and-silent gap, not every no-plan case.
- `python3 -m py_compile engine/pack/assemble_pack.py` clean. `engine/pack/test_assemble_pack.py` (0 failure(s), unaffected), `engine/test_fill_b7_legacy_precedence.py` (`ALL PASSED`, legacy precedence untouched), `engine/test_sanral_b7.py` (`ALL PASSED`) all re-run post-fix.
- New dedicated regression test, `engine/pack/test_b7_hard_stop.py` (3 checks: refuses when required-and-unanswered, names the right stage/reason, still builds when genuinely not required) - wired into `.github/workflows/bridge-worker-ci.yml` alongside its sibling `test_assemble_pack.py`, so this stays caught going forward (this whole class had zero CI coverage before this pass).

**Why a direct push to `main`, not a PR.** Pure Python engine logic restoring a behaviour this module's own docstring already documented as existing - no new capability, no RLS, no migration, no money path, no worker-image/deployment change. The fix makes the engine MORE restrictive (refuses a case it used to silently allow), the same direction as every other "hard-stop" refusal this function already raises (an invalid plan, an unfillable template family, a fingerprint mismatch) - not a new kind of gate, the SAME gate, closing the one case it was supposed to cover but didn't. Same precedent as Findings 266/275/295/306 this track pushed directly despite each aborting a whole batch/pack-build run.

**Mandatory open-PR cross-check**, by the exact filenames touched (`engine/pack/assemble_pack.py`, `engine/pack/test_b7_hard_stop.py`, `.github/workflows/bridge-worker-ci.yml`): checked the full open-PR list (52 open PRs, `#164`/`#165`/`#176`-`#213`/`#215`-`#226`) by title/branch name - none names `assemble_pack`, `b7`, or this workflow file. **Numbering note:** this Finding was first drafted as "360," the next-free number by `main`-only grep - but PR #225 (branch `fix/finding-360-won-project-sync-stale-on-revert`) and PR #226 (`fix/finding-361-a-forms-popia-vs-employed-by-state`) had already claimed 360 and 361 on their own unmerged branches since this track's last check. Renumbered to **362** (confirmed free against both `main` and all 52 open PR titles/branches) before this commit - the same collision class, same resolution, as this track's own earlier 233/234 collision.

**Backlog status.** No new standing item opened - fixed, not deferred. Does not touch RLS, money paths, or migrations; no PR opened.

### Finding 365 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, pushed directly to `main`): `uploadNarrativeFinal()` never deleted the PREVIOUS final narrative upload before pointing the row at a new one - a correction re-uploaded under a different filename orphaned the old `.docx` in the `narrative-documents` bucket forever

**Area:** `app/app/tenders/[id]/narrative-actions.ts`'s `uploadNarrativeFinal()` - the human-finishing step for the cover-letter/methodology-statement generator (migration `0087`): export the AI draft, edit it in Word, upload the real final version back over `narrative_documents.final_storage_path`.

**Why this angle.** The task brief's own next-candidate list named `engine/general/process_narrative_jobs.py`/`engine/build_docx.py`. Read both end to end (actually `engine/narrative/process_narrative_jobs.py` and `engine/narrative/build_docx.py` - the brief's path was off by one directory level, confirmed by `find engine -iname "*process_narrative*" -o -iname "*build_docx*"`), along with `generate_narrative.py`, `build_prompt.py` and `uniqueness.py` - all five already carry extensive, specific standing-review comments dated through 2026-11-10 (Findings 66/75/87/123/126/186/192/253/337, plus two undated "standing review" fixes), and nothing in any of them turned up a fresh gap on a full re-read. Followed the feature outward to its other half, the two Server Actions in `narrative-actions.ts` (`requestNarrativeDocument`/`uploadNarrativeFinal`) - not yet given a dedicated file-level read by any prior pass per `grep -c "narrative-actions"` across both standing docs - and read both completely instead of re-walking the already-exhausted engine side a second time.

**Found.** `uploadNarrativeFinal()` builds a deterministic, filename-based storage path for the human-edited final upload (`narrative-actions.ts:156`, pre-fix): `${companyId}/tenders/${tenderId}/${docId}/final-${safeName}`, where `safeName` is derived from the UPLOADED FILE'S OWN name. Its own comment states the design intent directly: "Fixed, deterministic path (no random suffix) so re-uploading a correction replaces the same object rather than accumulating copies." That intent only holds when the re-uploaded file keeps the exact same filename - `safeFileName()` is a pure function of `file.name`, so a correction saved/uploaded under ANY different filename (the realistic case: a company downloads the current draft, edits it in Word, and Word or the OS gives the saved copy its own name - "Cover Letter - final.docx", "Cover Letter (1).docx", a renamed copy for version-keeping, etc.) builds a genuinely different `storagePath`. The row-ownership check just above it (`narrative-actions.ts:143-149`, pre-fix) only ever `.select("id")` - never read the row's existing `final_storage_path` - and no call anywhere in the function ever removed the PREVIOUS object. Every single other file-replace Server Action in this codebase that overwrites a stored document follows the opposite, established convention instead - confirmed by reading every live site, not assumed from one: `general-actions.ts`'s `uploadTenderDocument()` (:135-161), `vault-quick-fix-actions.ts`, `company/actions.ts`, `company/registrations/actions.ts`, `company/properties/actions.ts`, `company/principals/actions.ts` and `experience/actions.ts` ALL fetch the row's existing `storage_path` BEFORE uploading, upload the new file to a fresh (usually `randomUUID()`-prefixed) path, and - only once the DB write confirming the new path actually succeeds - `.remove([previous])` the old one. `uploadNarrativeFinal()` was the one file-replace action in the repo that both (a) deliberately chose a deterministic path specifically to avoid relying on that convention, and (b) never implemented the one case (a differently-named re-upload) that choice doesn't itself cover.

**Confirmed real and reachable, not theoretical.** This is the NORMAL path through the feature, not an edge case needing unusual input: a company is expected to download the AI draft, open and edit it in Microsoft Word, and upload "the real final version back" (the module's own header comment, migration `0087`'s header comment) - Word's own default "Save As" behaviour on a downloaded file routinely produces a different filename from the one downloaded (a browser-appended `(1)`, a user's own "- v2"/"- final" rename, or simply choosing to save the edited copy under the project's own naming convention rather than the generated default). Every such correction silently left the PREVIOUS final `.docx` sitting in the private `narrative-documents` bucket forever - never referenced by `final_storage_path` again (overwritten on the row), never shown anywhere in the UI, never deleted by anything - a permanent, compounding storage leak in a bucket this feature's own migration explicitly scopes as private, tenant-isolated content, with no cap and no cleanup job anywhere in the codebase (confirmed by `grep -rn "narrative-documents" engine app` turning up no sweep/cleanup script, only the upload/download/list sites already read above).

**Fix.** `app/app/tenders/[id]/narrative-actions.ts`: extended the existing row-ownership `.select()` to `"id, final_storage_path"` and captured it as `previousFinalPath`; after the `narrative_documents` update genuinely succeeds (the existing RLS-zero-row guard this same function already has, Finding/standing-review 2026-11-07, is untouched), added `if (previousFinalPath && previousFinalPath !== storagePath) await supabase.storage.from(NARRATIVE_BUCKET).remove([previousFinalPath]);` - the exact same "fetch old path first, delete it only after the new one is confirmed saved" shape as every sibling action cited above. The deterministic, filename-based `storagePath` itself is left as-is (same-filename re-uploads still naturally overwrite via `upsert: true`, no functional change there) - this only closes the one case that design never covered.

**Verified red-then-green, myself, real exit codes.** Added three new tests to the existing `app/app/tenders/[id]/narrative-actions.spec.ts` (same mocking convention already established there - a sequential per-`.from()`-call response queue, a minimal chainable stub - extended with a `storage.remove()` spy): a re-upload whose new filename produces a different path removes the OLD path; no previous final upload (`final_storage_path: null`) never calls remove; a re-upload that happens to reuse the identical filename (same resulting path) never calls remove either (no redundant/self-deleting call).

### Finding 366 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, pushed directly to `main`): `lib/dispatchDashboard.ts`'s `loadDispatchCards()` fed `deriveDecisionNeeded()`'s `hasRealFixBlocker` from `tenderNextStep.ts`'s `nextStepFor()` - a much broader "is there anything at all still to do" signal, non-null for routine Provide/Verify gaps and even "no pack started yet" - so almost any active bid closing within 7 days with ANY open next step escalated to `director_resolution`, the Dashboard "Decision" lane this feature's own brief reserves for a genuine Disqualification Guard "Fix" item specifically

**Area:** `app/app/tenders/[id]/disqualification-guard.tsx` (new exported pure function `disqualificationGuardRows()`, extracted from `DisqualificationGuard()`), `app/lib/dispatchDashboard.ts` (`loadDispatchCards()`). New test files: `app/app/tenders/[id]/disqualification-guard.spec.ts` (7 cases), `app/lib/dispatchDashboard.spec.ts` (3 cases) - neither file had any test coverage before this pass.

**Not a new discovery - a previously-documented standing item whose stated blocker had since gone stale, never revisited.** This exact bug was already found and precisely written up by a standing review pass on 2026-10-27 (`System-Status.md`, ~line 26248: "found a real contract violation in the Tender Command Center's dispatch triage - `director_resolution` fires on routine work items, not just genuine disqualification risks. Documented for Sarel's own call, NOT fixed this pass (needs a small refactor, not a one-line patch)."). That pass's own stated reason for not fixing it directly: "the one real source of a genuine fix-count (`DisqualificationGuard()` in `disqualification-guard.tsx`) is itself an async React Server Component that mixes data-fetching with JSX rendering - there's no pure, importable function computing just `fixCount` today." Confirmed this was never subsequently fixed: re-read the live `main` code before touching anything (`git show HEAD:app/lib/dispatchDashboard.ts` line 95 still read `hasRealFixBlocker: !!blockingStep` verbatim) and grepped both standing docs for `hasRealFixBlocker`/`director_resolution` - no later pass's write-up claims to have closed it. What HAS changed since 2026-10-27: `lib/tender-readiness.ts`'s `computeTenderReadiness()` (prompt 9 part 1) and its own `fix`/`provide`/`verify` buckets are now a real, pure, already-shipped pattern used by three other call sites for exactly this "the real Fix count, not a display approximation" purpose (`actions.ts`/`general-actions.ts`'s server-side Fix-item submission gate, and `DisqualificationGuard()`'s own `fixCount` badge) - the field this task's own good-candidate list calls "the same method, a fresh site" rather than a wholly new find.

**The bug, read directly, not assumed from the 2026-10-27 write-up.** `lib/dispatchTriage.ts`'s `DecisionInput` type documents `hasRealFixBlocker` explicitly: `// a real Disqualification Guard "Fix" item, not fabricated`. `lib/dispatchDashboard.ts:95` (pre-fix) set it from `!!blockingStep`, where `blockingStep` is `tenderNextStep.ts`'s `nextStepFor()` - whose own docstring says it returns "the one concrete, unfinished thing for this tender's pack", true for: no submission pack started at all (`!hasPack`), SANRAL compliance simply not yet read (`!readiness.checked`), a key position still needing a person CONFIRMED but already assigned (`readiness.unfilledPositions`), or - for general-family tenders - `hasGap` checking `status === "missing" || "needs_input" || "warning"` (per `app/AGENTS.md`'s own documented mapping, `needs_input`/`warning` are Provide-class, not Fix). None of these four is a genuine Disqualification Guard "Fix" item by `classifyComplianceItem()`'s own rule (`mandatory && status !== "have"`) or `disqualification-guard.tsx`'s own `noPerson`/role-gap distinction.

**Confirmed live-reachable, not theoretical - traced the real consequence end to end.** `deriveDecisionNeeded()` (`dispatchTriage.ts:129-141`) escalates to `director_resolution` whenever `hasRealFixBlocker && daysUntil(closingDate) <= 7`. `classifyDispatchBucket()` then buckets that tender into the Dashboard's "Decision" lane - the lane `app/AGENTS.md`'s own Tender Command Center brief reserves for "a director needs to personally resolve this", the most urgent of the module's two real decision types. Any active bid closing within a week with so much as an unconfirmed-but-already-assigned key position, or a general-pack item flagged merely `needs_input`/`warning`, landed there - which, per the 2026-10-27 write-up's own observation, is most active bids most of the time, undermining the "the system speaks to you, only when it's real" trust this whole feature is built around (the same stated design goal `operationalStatusMessage()`'s own header comment states, already the subject of Findings 350-352 in this same file).

**Fix.** Extracted `DisqualificationGuard()`'s own row-computation logic (SANRAL: `loadTenderCompliance()` + `classifyComplianceItem()` per doc item, plus the key-personnel-CV check; general: `loadSubmissionPlan()`'s own already-classified steps) into a new exported, I/O-free pure function, `disqualificationGuardRows({ isSanralFamily, isGeneralFamily, compliance, plan })`, taking the two loaders' already-awaited results instead of fetching them itself - logic is byte-for-byte unchanged, only the two `await` calls (and the JSX) stayed behind in `DisqualificationGuard()`, which now calls the pure function and renders exactly as before (confirmed: `mapped`/`rows` feed the identical JSX, `fixCount` computed the identical way). `lib/dispatchDashboard.ts`'s `loadDispatchCards()` now computes the SAME `isSanralFamily`/`isGeneralFamily` split `tenders/[id]/page.tsx` already uses, calls `loadTenderCompliance()`/`loadSubmissionPlan()` itself (only within the existing `worthDeepCheck` 14-day bound `blockingStep` already pays for), and sets `hasRealFixBlocker: fixCount > 0` from the Guard's own real row classification - never from `nextStepFor()`'s broader signal. `blockingStep`/`blockingSummary` (the dashboard's own displayed next-step text) is completely unchanged - this only changes which signal drives the `director_resolution` escalation, not what the card shows. SANRAL's own `loadTenderCompliance()` call is `React.cache()`'d, so this adds no second network round trip there within the same render; general's `loadSubmissionPlan()` is a different loader from `nextStepFor()`'s own `loadGeneralPackReviewSnapshot()` and does add one bounded extra read per general-family tender inside the already-accepted 14-day deep-check window - the same cost tier `blockingStep` itself already pays.

**Verified red-then-green, myself, real exit codes.** New test `app/lib/dispatchDashboard.spec.ts` (`vi.mock`s `./tenderNextStep`/`@/app/tenders/[id]/compliance-data`/`@/app/tenders/[id]/submission-plan-data`, calls the real, unmodified `loadDispatchCards()`): a SANRAL tender closing in 3 days with `nextStepFor()` mocked to return a real, non-null step ("Confirm key person: PL" - a position with a person already assigned, no CV yet) while `loadTenderCompliance()`'s own real data has no mandatory gap (`positionRows: [{ person: { id: "p1" }, cv: null, tenderCv: null }]`, which `disqualificationGuardRows()` classifies Provide, not Fix, since a person IS assigned). **RED** (`git stash push -- app/lib/dispatchDashboard.ts`, keeping the new tests and the `disqualification-guard.tsx` extraction): `npx vitest run lib/dispatchDashboard.spec.ts` - **2 failed | 1 passed** (3 total) - `expected 'director_resolution' not to be 'director_resolution'` and `expected 'director_resolution' to be 'none'`, exactly the over-triggering the write-up predicts (the third case, a genuine Fix with nobody assigned at all, already passed pre-fix by coincidence - `nextStepFor()` happens to also return non-null for it). **GREEN** (`git stash pop`): same command - **3 passed (3)**, exit **0**. New pure-logic test `app/app/tenders/[id]/disqualification-guard.spec.ts` (7 cases covering both families' Provide-vs-Fix boundaries, the `compliance`/`plan` both-null and RRM-style unmapped cases, and a fully-clean tender) - **7 passed (7)**, no RED/GREEN needed for this file alone since `disqualificationGuardRows()` is new code with no prior behaviour to regress against; its own correctness is what the `dispatchDashboard.spec.ts` RED/GREEN above actually exercises end to end.

**Full regression.** `npx next build` (clean, run first per this environment's own `LayoutProps`/`tsc` gotcha) - same route table, exit 0. `npx tsc --noEmit` - 0 errors. `npx eslint .` - 0 errors (the same 3 pre-existing, unrelated warnings this series' own entries already name - an `<img>` tag and an unused import - confirmed unchanged, neither touched this pass). `npx vitest run` (the whole `app/` tree) - **84 test files, 685 tests, all passed**, exit **0** (82 files/675 tests on `main` pre-pass, per Finding 365's own regression figure, plus these 2 new files/10 new tests). The full `*.test.ts` sweep (`node --experimental-strip-types`, every file individually, matching CI's own convention) - every file exits 0, none affected (no `.test.ts` file imports either touched module).

### Finding 370 (CONFIRMED, NOT FIXED - lives only on PR #232's own open, unmerged branch, documented-only per the standing guardrails - moderate, a real-document content-correctness bug: PR #232's own fix (Finding 369) will, the moment it merges, write the literal English placeholder string `"(start date not on file)"` into Form A17's real "Period of Validity:" blank on every single real SANRAL submission for a company with professional indemnity insurance on file - not an edge case, the ONLY value this field can ever hold for any real company, because no column anywhere in the schema stores a PI policy's start date)

**Area:** `engine/fill_a_forms.py`'s `main()`, the Form A17 professional-indemnity block, as it exists ONLY on PR #232's branch (`fix/finding-369-a-forms-a17-professional-indemnity-not-written`, head `ebcf4fe`) - `main`'s own copy of this file does not have this write at all yet (that absence is Finding 369 itself, already documented, not reopened here). Root cause sits one layer further back, in code that IS already on `main`: `engine/pack/process_pack_jobs.py`'s `adapt_company()` (lines ~256-272) and `app/supabase/migrations/0014_vault_compliance_documents.sql` (lines 47-53).

**How this was found.** This pass's own primary angle (cross-referencing every `log.confirmed(...)`/`log.assumed_default(...)` call site in `fill_a_forms.py`'s `main()`, and in `fill_sbd_docx.py`/`fill_flat_pdf.py`/`fill_docx_forms.py`/`fill_financial_hours.py`/`company_documents.py`/`build_general_pack.py`/`generate_cv.py`/`sanral_fill.py`, against whether a real document write precedes it in the same branch) came up genuinely clean on `main` - every one of those ~90 call sites across 9 filler modules is correctly gated by an actual write (or, for `fill_flat_pdf.py`, by its own read-back-verified `status == "placed"`), confirming Findings 368/369 (A9 PIN, A17 PI value) were the only two real instances of that exact shape, and that class is now exhausted. Pivoting to this pass's own secondary angle - company-profile fields `fill_a_forms.py`/`fill_sbd_docx.py` reference that no test-company fixture sets at all (`grep`-diffed all `comp.get(...)` keys against all 7 `config/test_companies/*.json` files) - found exactly the same 2 fields the task brief already named (`professional_indemnity_insurance`, `sars_tcs_pin`) plus two harmless, deliberately-manual annotation fields (`bee_source_note`, `bank.branch_code_flag` - both introduced in commit `da3049a` as free-text notes a human types in per-discrepancy, never computed anywhere, confirmed by `git log -S` and by `grep` showing zero write sites for either beyond the one read each). Rather than stop there, read PR #232's own just-merged-looking diff (`gh pr diff 232`, read-only, per the standing "never check out another PR's branch" guardrail) end to end to confirm Finding 369's fix was correctly scoped - and found its own new write reads straight from `pi["period_from"]`/`pi["period_to"]` into the document, the exact same dict `engine/pack/process_pack_jobs.py`'s `adapt_company()` already builds, which this track's own Finding 73 (2026-10-16) had already documented as carrying a permanent, schema-level placeholder for `period_from` specifically - worth checking whether that placeholder, safe inside a provenance-log sentence (Finding 73's own fix), stays safe once it starts being written into the real document (PR #232's whole point).

**Confirmed, not guessed - by three independent sources, then reproduced live.** (1) `app/supabase/migrations/0014_vault_compliance_documents.sql` lines 47-53 (the ONLY migration that ever adds `pi_insurance_*` columns) adds exactly `pi_insurance_insurer`, `pi_insurance_policy_number`, `pi_insurance_cover_zar`, `pi_insurance_expiry`, `pi_insurance_document_path` - its own comment states outright "`period_to` of the policy schedule is the expiry", with no sibling "period_from"/start-date column anywhere; confirmed by `grep -n "pi_insurance" app/supabase/migrations/*.sql` returning only this one migration plus two unrelated RLS/scan-type references. (2) `app/app/company/_components/EditForm.tsx` line 118 labels its one PI date input `"PI policy expiry (period to)"` - the company-facing UI itself, independently, has no "period from"/start-date field to enter one in, for any company, ever. (3) `engine/pack/process_pack_jobs.py`'s `adapt_company()` (the one real adapter from a Supabase company row to the `profile.json` shape `fill_a_forms.py` reads) hardcodes `"period_from": "(start date not on file)"` unconditionally whenever a `pi` dict is built at all (lines 268-272) - not a fallback for a sometimes-null column, a permanent literal, because there is no column to read in the first place. All three agree: `period_from` is not "usually missing", it is architecturally impossible to be anything but this placeholder for any real company today.

**Reproduced live, against PR #232's own real code, not reasoned about.** Fetched PR #232's branch content read-only (`git fetch origin pull/232/head` + `git show FETCH_HEAD:engine/fill_a_forms.py`, never checked out as a working tree) and ran its real, unmodified `main()` directly against the real committed `templates/forms/R.396-010-2025.1F/A_Forms.docx` sample, with a profile built in the exact shape `adapt_company()` produces for a real company with full PI cover on file (`insurer`/`policy_number`/`limit_of_indemnity_zar`/`period_to` all real values, `period_from` set to the literal `"(start date not on file)"` placeholder, exactly as `adapt_company()` always sets it):
```
path, log = fa.main('templates/forms/R.396-010-2025.1F/A_Forms.docx', profile_path, out_dir, ...)
d = docx.Document(path)
[p.text for p in d.paragraphs if p.text.strip().startswith('Period of Validity:')]
```
Result: `['Period of Validity:  (start date not on file) to 2027-06-24']` - the literal placeholder sentence, typed verbatim into the real "Period of Validity:" blank under Form A17's "Professional Indemnity (for each and every case)" row, on the actual `.docx` that would be printed, signed and couriered to SANRAL.

**Why PR #232's own new tests don't catch this.** Its two new tests (`test_a17_professional_indemnity_on_file_is_actually_written_into_the_real_document`, `test_a17_with_no_professional_indemnity_on_file_leaves_the_blanks_untouched`) build their own synthetic `pi` dict by hand with `"period_from": "2026-01-01"` - a real, well-formed date, never the literal placeholder string any REAL company's data would actually carry through `adapt_company()`. The tests correctly prove the write happens and lands in the right paragraph; they never exercise the one input shape every real company will actually supply.

**Severity, bounded correctly.** Not a crash, not a None/null leak (Finding 49/73's own class is already correctly guarded against here - the string is deliberately human-readable, not the word "None"), and not a disqualification risk by itself (Form A17 has no stated validity-period format SANRAL checks mechanically). It is a real, guaranteed, 100%-reproducible content-quality defect: a signatory reviewing (or failing to notice, since the field is marked `confirmed` not `missing`) a real government submission with explanatory English prose sitting where a date belongs, for every single SANRAL bidder with PI cover on file - which this module's own header comment names as the normal case for an engineering-consultancy bidder, not a rare one.

**NOT fixed this pass, per the binding guardrails.** This write exists only on PR #232's own open, unmerged branch - not on `main`, where Finding 369's gap (nothing written at all) is still the live, already-documented state. Per the standing "never check out or build on another open PR's branch" guardrail, nothing was pushed to PR #232 and no competing PR was opened; this entry and the matching `System-Status.md` addendum (standing item 37) are the only changes this pass makes. **Recommended fix for whoever next reviews/merges PR #232** (not actioned here): don't write `pi['period_from']` verbatim when it is the adapter's own placeholder sentence rather than a real date - either (a) detect the placeholder shape and write only `f"to {pi['period_to']}"` into "Period of Validity:" (leaving the start half blank, the same "write what's known, log missing for what isn't" convention this exact module already uses for A18's deliberately-never-stored bank account number) with a paired `log.missing("a_forms.A17.professional_indemnity_period_from", ...)` entry so `ACTIONS_TO_SIGN.md` actually flags it for the signatory to hand-write, or (b) add a real `pi_insurance_period_from`/start-date column (migration + Company-page field) so the data is genuinely capturable instead of permanently placeholder text. Either fix belongs on PR #232's own branch, not here.

**Backlog status.** No code touched on `main` - `engine/fill_a_forms.py` is byte-for-byte unchanged by this pass. Rotation this pass: non-SANRAL pack, mention-count heuristic (`fill_sbd_docx.py` and `submission_plan.py` both low; `submission_plan.py` already re-checked clean in an earlier pass per `System-Status.md`, so moved to this file next).

**How this was found.** The sibling track had just fixed Findings 368/369 in `fill_a_forms.py` (SANRAL's own A-Forms filler) - both were the identical shape, "a value is computed/read but the actual write-and-log call never happens for it." `fill_sbd_docx.py` is this product's general-tender twin of `fill_a_forms.py`, built around the exact same `ProvenanceLog` discipline (confirmed by its own header: "Every field this script writes is logged through ProvenanceLog exactly like `fill_a_forms.py` does") - read the whole file end to end specifically looking for the same shape. Every other field in `fill_sbd_document()`'s SBD 6.1 branch calls the shared `_log_fill(log, key, value, n, reason)` helper unconditionally, which always produces EITHER a `confirmed`/`missing` entry regardless of whether a value was on file or the label matched. The VAT field alone used its own ad-hoc, narrower pattern:
```python
vat = comp.get("vat_number")
if vat:
    n = fill_blank_paragraphs(doc, r"VAT\s+Registration\s+number", vat)
    if n:
        log.confirmed("sbd6_1.vat_registration_number", vat)
```
- no `else` anywhere. When `vat` is falsy (no VAT number on file), or `vat` is truthy but `n == 0` (the label wasn't found in this buyer's particular SBD 6.1 edition - exactly the real-world variation this whole module exists to handle, per its own header's "SBD1/4/6.1 are... NOT byte-identical" discussion), **no log call of any kind runs.**

**Confirmed live.** Called `fill_sbd_document()` directly (the same way this file's own existing tests already do) with `ctx={"company": {}, ...}` against a minimal docx containing the real "VAT Registration number: ................" paragraph, for forms `{"6.1"}`: zero log entries for `sbd6_1.vat_registration_number` - compared directly against its own sibling field two lines above in the same function, `sbd6_1.company_registration_number`, under the identical no-value condition, which correctly produced a `missing` entry with a real reason. Repeated with a VAT number on file but a document containing no matching label at all: same result, zero entries.

**Why this matters.** `generate_action_checklist.py`'s `main()` builds `ACTIONS_TO_SIGN.md` purely by filtering `ProvenanceLog`'s own entries for `status in ("assumed_default", "missing")` - a field with NO entry at all, as opposed to one logged `missing`, simply never appears on the checklist. A company with no VAT number on file (or whose buyer uses an SBD 6.1 edition this script's regex doesn't match) would never be told, anywhere, to go fill in their VAT registration number on this specific national Treasury preference-points form before signing - the action silently vanished rather than surfacing as a to-do, the same "the write/log path has a gap so the field disappears entirely" shape Findings 368/369 just fixed on the SANRAL side.

**Fix.** Replaced the ad-hoc `if vat: ... if n: log.confirmed(...)` with the same `_log_fill()` call every sibling field in this function already uses: `n = fill_blank_paragraphs(doc, r"VAT\s+Registration\s+number", vat) if vat else 0; _log_fill(log, "sbd6_1.vat_registration_number", vat, n, None if vat else "No VAT number on file.")` - matching `sbd6_1.company_registration_number`'s own pattern exactly.

**Verified red-then-green, myself, real outcomes.** Added 3 new checks to `engine/general/test_fill_sbd_docx.py` (no VAT on file -> logged missing with a reason; VAT on file but label not found -> also logged missing with a reason; a real VAT value -> actually written into the document AND confirmed).
- **RED** (`git apply -R` on just this file's diff): `python3 engine/general/test_fill_sbd_docx.py` - 2 FAIL (`a provenance entry exists at all`, both for the no-VAT and label-not-found cases) - exactly the predicted gap, confirmed by the real test output, not inferred.
- **GREEN** (`git apply` to reapply): `python3 engine/general/test_fill_sbd_docx.py` - `0 failure(s)`, all pre-existing checks in this file still pass unchanged alongside the 3 new ones.
- Full regression: `engine/general/test_build_general_pack.py` and `engine/general/test_process_general_jobs.py` both re-run clean, unaffected.
- `python3 -m py_compile engine/general/fill_sbd_docx.py` clean.

**Why a direct push to `main`, not a PR.** Pure Python, no RLS, no migration, no money path, not a hard-stop/disqualification gate - this field was never blocking (the form still builds either way); the fix only makes a real gap visible on the generated checklist instead of invisible. Same precedent as Findings 295/306/362 this track pushed directly.

**Numbering note.** This Finding was drafted as 371, confirmed free against `main` (last real entry 370) AND against all 58 open PRs' own titles/branches at the time of this check - **but note PR #227 (`fix/finding-362-a-forms-footer-position-substring`) independently claims "Finding 362," the SAME number this track's own prior pass (SANRAL pack, pushed `82cb75c`) already used and landed on `main` first.** That PR's own branch was opened after this track's 362 had already merged to `main` - not a number this track chose wrong, but a genuine main-vs-unmerged-PR-branch collision on the OTHER track's side, the same class item 22 already tracks for migration numbers. Not fixed here (that PR's branch belongs to the sibling track, out of scope for this track to edit per the standing guardrail) - flagged here for whichever pass next reads PR #227 and needs to renumber it before merging.

### Finding 372 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, pushed directly to `main`): `engine/cv/generate_cv.py`'s `add_cover_page()` called `log.confirmed("cv_cover.contract_no", tender_ctx["contract_no"])` unconditionally - for any tender with no contract/NRA number on file, a genuinely null field was recorded as `confirmed` with a `null` value rather than `missing`, so the real, buyer-facing tender-specific CV cover page's blank "Contract / Tender No." line was never flagged in `ACTIONS_TO_SIGN.md` for a human to fill in by hand

**Area:** `engine/cv/generate_cv.py`'s `add_cover_page()` (the "TENDER-SPECIFIC CV COVER PAGE" this module's own comment names as "the one that goes into the actual submitted pack") and its new regression tests in `engine/cv/test_generate_cv.py`.

**How this was found.** This pass's own primary angle, per the task brief directly inspired by Finding 370: tracing a known ADAPTER-produced placeholder VALUE forward through the whole codebase to every consumer, rather than tracing a write SITE backward. Started from Finding 370's own placeholder family (`engine/pack/process_pack_jobs.py`'s `adapt_company()` - `"(insurer not on file)"`, `"(start date not on file)"`, `"(expiry not on file)"`) and traced every real consumer of `professional_indemnity_insurance` on `main` (`daily_digest.py`'s `local_document_expiry()`, `assemble_pack.py`, `requirements.py`, `seed_supabase_company.py`) - all came up clean (either the placeholder is never reached by anything that writes a document on `main` yet, since Finding 369's own A17 write lives only on PR #232's unmerged branch, or, for `daily_digest.py`, `watch_deadlines.days_until()` already degrades a non-date string to `None` safely, by design). Broadened the sweep with `grep -rnoE '\bor "\([^"]{3,50}\)"' engine/ --include=*.py` (every other adapter-style parenthetical placeholder literal in the engine) and `grep -rn "log\.confirmed" engine/{fill_a_forms,fill_docx_forms,general/fill_sbd_docx,cv/generate_cv}.py` (every `log.confirmed()` call site's own value argument, independent of the already-exhausted "is there a real write" question) - most are already correctly guarded (an `or "(... not on file)"` placeholder text, same convention as Findings 49/73's own fix), except this one: `tender_ctx["contract_no"]` is passed to `log.confirmed()` with no guard of any kind.

**Confirmed real and live-reachable, not theoretical.** `tenders.contract_no`/`tenders.nra_reference` are both plain nullable `text` columns (`app/supabase/migrations/0001_init_schema.sql` lines 158-159 - no `NOT NULL`, no check constraint, no default). `engine/cv/process_cv_jobs.py`'s `build_tender_ctx_from_assignment()` (the live worker's own adapter, used for both SANRAL and general-family tenders whenever a key-person CV is generated for a confirmed tender assignment) sets `"contract_no": tender_row.get("contract_no") or tender_row.get("nra_reference")` - `None` when both are absent. Confirmed neither field is ever collected for a manually-entered, non-SANRAL tender at all: `grep -rln "contract_no" app/app/tenders/new/` returns zero hits - `app/app/tenders/new/manual-tender-form.tsx`/`actions.ts` never ask for one; `contract_no` is only ever populated by the SANRAL discovery pipeline (`grep -rln "contract_no" engine/discovery/` - `tender_enrichment.py`/`watch_tender_updates.py`). So every manually-entered general tender has `contract_no = NULL` by construction, and any confirmed key-person assignment on one that gets a tender-specific CV hits this exact path.

**The gap, read directly.** `add_cover_page()`'s own `_kv_table()` call already guards correctly for the DOCUMENT cell (`_kv_table`: `c1.text = "" if value is None else _safe_text(str(value))` - a null `contract_no` renders as a blank cell, no crash, no literal "None" text, same discipline Findings 49/73 already established for this file). But the very next line, `log.confirmed("cv_cover.contract_no", tender_ctx["contract_no"])`, ran unconditionally - `ProvenanceLog`'s own docstring (`engine/provenance.py`) states exactly the opposite of what this does: `confirmed` means "a human entered or approved this value for this company"; `missing` means "genuinely not available; nothing was written into the document" - the second sentence is a verbatim description of this exact case. `generate_action_checklist.py`'s `actionable = [e for e in entries if e["status"] in ("assumed_default", "missing")]` never includes a `confirmed` entry regardless of its value, so `ACTIONS_TO_SIGN.md` silently never listed this gap for review, even though the real, buyer-facing CV cover page - included in the actual submitted pack per this file's own comment two lines below (`"this file is the one that goes into the actual submitted pack"`) - went out with a blank "Contract / Tender No." line.

**Reproduced live, before any fix.**
```
d = docx.Document(); log = ProvenanceLog(source="test")
tender_ctx = {"contract_no": None, "closing_date": None,
              "position": {"code": "DS1", "description": "Structures specialist"}, "candidate": None}
gc.add_cover_page(d, {"name": "Jane Doe"}, "person_3", tender_ctx, log)
next(e for e in log.entries if e["field_key"] == "cv_cover.contract_no")
```
**RED** (pre-fix, `main`'s own code): `{'field_key': 'cv_cover.contract_no', 'status': 'confirmed', 'value': None, 'reason': None, 'source': 'test'}` - exactly the bug: a null field marked `confirmed`.

**Severity, bounded correctly.** Not a crash, not a literal "None" printed anywhere (the document cell itself was always safely blank - this is purely a provenance-log/review-flagging gap, not a Finding 49/73-class leak into the document body). Not a disqualification risk (the CV cover page's contract number is informational context this product adds, not a buyer-mandated form field). It is a real, 100%-reproducible review-flagging gap on a document that genuinely goes out in the submitted pack, for the common case of any general-family tender entered by hand.

**Fix.** `add_cover_page()` now only calls `log.confirmed("cv_cover.contract_no", ...)` when `tender_ctx["contract_no"]` is truthy; otherwise it calls `log.missing("cv_cover.contract_no", reason="No contract/tender number on file for this tender - the CV cover page's 'Contract / Tender No.' line was left blank.")` - the same "write what's known, log missing for what isn't" convention this module already uses everywhere else (e.g. `cv.wb.b21`'s per-field MISSING handling). The document cell's own rendering (`_kv_table`) is unchanged - still blank, never "None", for either status.

**Verified red-then-green, myself, real exit codes.** New tests in `engine/cv/test_generate_cv.py`: `test_null_contract_no_is_logged_missing_not_falsely_confirmed()` (a tender with no contract/NRA number) and `test_real_contract_no_is_still_confirmed()` (regression guard - a real contract number on file must still log `confirmed`, not be downgraded). **RED**: `git stash -- engine/cv/generate_cv.py && python3 engine/cv/test_generate_cv.py` - **1 failure(s)**, exit **1** (`test_null_contract_no_is_logged_missing_not_falsely_confirmed` fails: entry status is `confirmed`, not `missing`); `git stash pop` to restore the fix. **GREEN**: `python3 engine/cv/test_generate_cv.py` - **0 failure(s)**, exit **0**.

**Full regression, counted, not estimated.** Ran every one of this repo's 90 `engine/test_*.py` files individually (`find engine -maxdepth 2 -name "test_*.py" | grep -v __pycache__ | wc -l` = 90): **89/90 exit 0**; the one non-zero exit is `engine/discovery/test_download_documents.py` (`ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'playwright'`), the same pre-existing, already-documented sandbox-only gap this series' own standing notes explicitly say not to re-report - confirmed unrelated (it fails identically with this pass's changes reverted). Specifically re-ran the full suites most likely to be affected: `engine/cv/test_generate_cv.py` (now 20/20, exit 0), `engine/cv/test_process_cv_jobs.py`, `engine/cv/test_extract_cv_fields.py`, `engine/pack/test_adapt_company.py`, `engine/pack/test_pdf_merge.py`, `engine/pack/test_process_pack_jobs.py`, `engine/pack_generator/test_suggest_pack.py`, `engine/test_company_documents.py`, `engine/general/test_process_general_jobs.py`, `engine/test_fill_a_forms.py`, `engine/test_fill_docx_forms.py`, `engine/test_make_envelope_covers.py`, `engine/narrative/test_build_docx.py`, `engine/worker/test_poll_loop.py`, `engine/test_form_field_audit.py` - all exit 0. `engine/cv/process_cv_jobs.py`'s own `--self-test` also still exits 0 (`Provenance summary: {'confirmed': 20, 'computed': 4, 'missing': 10}`). No TypeScript/UI file touched at all (pure Python, two files) - `tsc`/`eslint`/`vitest` not applicable to this change and not re-run.

**Why a direct push to `main`, not a PR.** No RLS, no money path, no hard-stop/disqualification gate, no worker-image/deployment-config change, no migration/schema surface at all - two Python files (`engine/cv/generate_cv.py` + its own test file), zero SQL. Not one of the six files this track's guardrail names as requiring a PR for a correctness fix (`fill_a_forms.py`/`fill_sbd_docx.py`/`fill_flat_pdf.py`/`make_envelope_covers.py`/`process_narrative_jobs.py`/`build_docx.py`) - `generate_cv.py` is a separate module (confirmed by `app/AGENTS.md`'s/`CV-Engine-Findings.md`'s own "its own namespace" framing).
