### Finding 373 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, pushed directly to `main`): `engine/cv/generate_cv.py`'s "Position in team:"/"1. Proposed Position:" row - written into BOTH generated CV document formats - had either NO `field_provenance` entry at all (`build_sanral_keyperson()`) or a FABRICATED placeholder value wrongly marked `confirmed` (`build_world_bank()`), so a genuinely blank tender position description was completely invisible to a human either way

**Area:** `engine/cv/generate_cv.py`'s `build_sanral_keyperson()` (Form B1.1's own "Position in team:" row) and `build_world_bank()` (section 1, "Proposed Position:"), plus new regression tests in `engine/cv/test_generate_cv.py`.

**How this was found.** Per the task brief's own instruction to check ALL of `generate_cv.py` for the "confirmed vs written/logged" bug class (not just `add_cover_page()`, already closed by Finding 372), I enumerated every `log.confirmed(...)` call site in the file (`grep -n "log\.confirmed(" engine/cv/generate_cv.py` - 16 sites) and read each one's own call context. Most are already correctly guarded (`person.get("id_number")`/`if q.get(...)` checks, or genuinely non-nullable fields like `person["name"]`). Two, both built from the exact same line, `position_desc = (tender_ctx["position"]["description"] if tender_ctx else person.get("role", ""))` (appearing identically at lines 289 and 456), were not:
- `build_sanral_keyperson()` writes `("Position in team:", position_desc)` into its `_kv_table()` call (line 293) but, unlike `Name:` (`log.confirmed`) and `ID Number:` (`log.confirmed`/`log.missing`) two lines later in the exact same table, had **no provenance call for this field at all** - not `confirmed`, not `missing`, nothing.
- `build_world_bank()` instead called `log.confirmed("cv.wb.position", position_desc or "(standard CV - no tender position)")` **unconditionally** - a fabricated placeholder sentence substituted in and then marked `confirmed`, the exact same root shape Finding 372 just fixed for `cv_cover.contract_no` (an `or <fallback>` masking a genuinely missing value as "confirmed"), just with a literal explanatory sentence as the fallback instead of `None`.

**Confirmed real and live-reachable, not theoretical - `position_desc` really can be blank.** Two independent ways, read directly from the code, not assumed:
1. **Standalone CV, no tender context** (`tender_ctx` is `None` - `mode="standard"`, the path every company's general, non-tender-specific CV takes): `position_desc = person.get("role", "")` - `"role"` is a plain, optional `text` field on a key person; nothing requires it to be set, and this engine's own test fixtures routinely populate it precisely because so many other tests need a non-empty value, which had hidden how the ZERO-role case behaved in provenance until now.
2. **A real tender position with a genuinely blank stored description**: `tender_ctx["position"]["description"]` is set from `pack_suggestions.json`'s own `position` dict, built by `engine/pack_generator/suggest_pack.py`'s `read_required_positions()` - `"description": wb.cached("SETUP", f"{col}7")`, read straight from one cell of a SANRAL SETUP sheet with **no fallback, no `or` guard, nothing** (confirmed by reading `read_required_positions()` directly, lines 66-87 of `suggest_pack.py`) - only row 6 (`code`) is checked for emptiness before a position entry is even created (`if not code: continue`); row 7 (`description`) is read and stored as-is. A sparse/malformed SETUP sheet - the exact class of real-world shape this series has already found and fixed repeatedly elsewhere (e.g. the malformed-row/malformed-cell findings in `sanral_tenders.py`/`fill_financial.py`) - can genuinely have a real position CODE with a blank description cell.

**The gap, read directly.**
- `build_sanral_keyperson()`'s own "Position in team:" cell was, before this fix, the one field in that `_kv_table()` call with zero audit trail of any kind - whether the value shown was a real tender position, a person's generic role, or genuinely blank, nothing in `field_provenance` ever recorded it. `generate_action_checklist.py`'s `actionable = [e for e in entries if e["status"] in ("assumed_default", "missing")]` only ever reads `field_provenance` entries - a field with no entry at all is just as invisible to `ACTIONS_TO_SIGN.md` as one wrongly marked `confirmed` (the exact shape Findings 368/369/371/372 fixed), arguably worse: it leaves no trace in the provenance JSON either, for a reviewer checking that file directly.
- `build_world_bank()`'s `log.confirmed("cv.wb.position", position_desc or "(standard CV - no tender position)")` is actively misleading on top of hiding the gap: for case 2 above (a real tender_ctx with a blank SETUP-sheet description), the logged value falsely claims "no tender position" even though a real tender position code DOES exist for this document - the only thing missing is its description text. `ProvenanceLog`'s own docstring (`engine/provenance.py`) is explicit that `confirmed` means "a human entered or approved this value for this company" and `missing` means "genuinely not available; nothing was written into the document" - a fabricated explanatory sentence substituted in and marked `confirmed` satisfies neither definition.

**Reproduced live, before any fix.**
```python
tender_ctx = {"contract_no": "X", "closing_date": "2026-12-01",
              "position": {"code": "DS1", "description": ""},  # real position, blank SETUP-sheet description
              "candidate": {"specialism_warning": False, "rationale": "r", "score": 0.5}}
person = {"name": "Jane Doe", "id_number": "8001015009087", "role": "Engineer", "projects": []}
log = ProvenanceLog(source="test")
gc.build_sanral_keyperson({"company": {"legal_name": "Test Co"}}, person, "person_1", "full", tender_ctx, None, log)
[e for e in log.entries if e["field_key"] == "cv.b11.position"]
```
**RED** (pre-fix, `main`'s own code): `[]` - zero entries, the field is completely absent from provenance.
```python
log2 = ProvenanceLog(source="test")
gc.build_world_bank({"company": {"legal_name": "Test Co"}}, person, "person_1", "full", tender_ctx, None, log2)
next(e for e in log2.entries if e["field_key"] == "cv.wb.position")
```
**RED**: `{'field_key': 'cv.wb.position', 'status': 'confirmed', 'value': '(standard CV - no tender position)', 'reason': None, 'source': 'test'}` - `confirmed`, with a value that falsely denies a real tender position exists.

**Severity, bounded correctly.** Not a crash, not a literal "None" printed anywhere (the document cell itself was always blank in this case, same discipline Findings 49/73 established). Not a disqualification risk - "Position in team"/"Proposed Position" is informational context on a CV format this product builds, not a buyer-mandated pass/fail field. It is a real, 100%-reproducible review-flagging gap (and, for `build_world_bank()`, an actively misleading provenance entry) affecting the standard/standalone CV path (the common case for any key person not currently tied to a tender-specific CV) and any SANRAL tender whose SETUP sheet has a sparse position-description cell.

**Fix.** Both functions now share the same pattern already used elsewhere in this file (e.g. `cv.b11.id_number`): `if position_desc: log.confirmed(key, position_desc) else: log.missing(key, reason=...)`, with a reason that correctly distinguishes the two real causes - a blank SETUP-sheet description for a real tender position vs. no `role` on file for a standalone CV - rather than collapsing both into one fabricated sentence. The document cells themselves (`_kv_table()`'s existing `"" if value is None else ...` / the plain cell text) are unchanged - still blank, never "None", for either status; this is a provenance-logging fix only.

**Verified red-then-green, myself, real exit codes.** Five new tests added to `engine/cv/test_generate_cv.py`: `test_sanral_keyperson_position_in_team_is_logged_when_present`, `test_sanral_keyperson_position_in_team_blank_tender_description_logged_missing`, `test_world_bank_position_blank_tender_description_logged_missing_not_falsely_confirmed`, `test_world_bank_standalone_cv_no_role_logged_missing`, `test_world_bank_standalone_cv_with_role_still_confirmed` (regression guard). **RED**: `git stash push -- engine/cv/generate_cv.py && python3 engine/cv/test_generate_cv.py` (run from `engine/`) - **5 failure(s)**, exit **1**; `git stash pop` to restore the fix. **GREEN**: `python3 engine/cv/test_generate_cv.py` - **0 failure(s)**, exit **0**, all 49 checks across all 25 test functions in the file pass (14 pre-existing + the new 5, each with multiple `check()` assertions).

**Full regression, counted, not estimated.** Ran every one of this repo's 90 `engine/test_*.py` files individually (`find engine -name "test_*.py" | wc -l` = 90, run from `engine/`): **89/90 exit 0**. ### Finding 374 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, pushed directly to `main`): `engine/cv/generate_cv.py`'s own `_footer()` sanitizes a company's `legal_name` for control characters but never checks whether sanitizing left anything behind - the exact "empty-after-sanitize" crash shape Finding 367 found in `build_docx.py`'s subtitle, here instead in the one footer paragraph both real CV document formats share

**Area:** `engine/cv/generate_cv.py`'s `_footer(d, comp)` (shared by `build_sanral_keyperson()` and `build_world_bank()` - every CV this engine produces, in either format, ends by calling it), plus a new regression test in `engine/cv/test_generate_cv.py`.

**How this was found.** Per this pass's own third suggested angle ("trace a cross-cutting convention... across every site that should follow it, in a part of the codebase not yet checked this way"), I took the exact bug class the most recent negative-result pass's own hint named - `build_docx.py`'s subtitle, which Finding 367 (documented, but still unfixed on `main`, living only on PR #230's own unmerged branch - see standing item 35) found crashes with `IndexError` when a value that's non-empty BEFORE sanitizing becomes completely empty AFTER it, because `python-docx`'s own `add_paragraph("")` creates a paragraph with **zero runs**, and the very next line that reaches for `.runs[0]` to style it has nothing to reach for. I grepped every `.runs[0]` access across the whole engine (`grep -rn "\.runs\[0\]" --include=*.py .`, 40 hits across 9 files) and read each one's own paragraph-text argument, asking the same question Finding 367's own write-up asks: is this text a STATIC Python literal (can never sanitize to empty), or a DYNAMIC value with no guaranteed-non-empty literal padding around it (can)?

37 of the 40 are safe - either a hardcoded heading/label string (`_heading()`'s title arguments, table column headers, "STILL TO DO BY HAND", etc. - these can never be touched by `_safe_text()`'s control-character strip because they're never built from real/user data), or a dynamic value wrapped in enough literal surrounding text (a label, a colon-and-space, a joining " - ") that the final string can never fully vanish even if the dynamic part does (e.g. `engine/general/build_general_pack.py`'s own `f"{b['title']}: {b['reason']}"` - the literal `": "` alone survives). `engine/fill_a_forms.py`'s own helper, `set_paragraph_text()`, already guards this exact case explicitly (`if p.runs: ... else: p.add_run(text)`), so every one of its own call sites is already safe regardless of what the text sanitizes down to.

One site had neither protection: `generate_cv.py`'s own `_footer()`:
```python
d.add_paragraph()
p = d.add_paragraph(_safe_text(comp.get("legal_name", "")))
p.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER
p.runs[0].italic = True
```
`comp["legal_name"]` is wrapped in `_safe_text()` (added by an earlier fix, commit `13bdfc2`, for the *different*, already-closed bug of a raw `ValueError` on any control character) with **no literal text around it at all** - if sanitizing strips every character the value had, `add_paragraph("")` produces a paragraph with zero runs, and `p.runs[0].italic = True` on the very next line raises `IndexError`, failing the whole CV build. `legal_name` is `NOT NULL` in the schema (migration `0001_init_schema.sql`), but nothing enforces it being anything more than a single stray control byte - the identical realistic "OCR/paste corruption" source `_safe_text()`'s own docstring in this very file already names, and the identical scenario Finding 367 already accepted as sufficiently real for `contract_no` ("a tender `contract_no` that is nothing but a stray NUL byte").

**Reproduced live, before any fix** (`engine/cv/`, run with `python3 -I`):
```python
import docx
from generate_cv import _footer
d = docx.Document()
_footer(d, {"legal_name": "\x00"})
```
**RED:** `IndexError: list index out of range`.

**Confirmed reachable from both real document builders, not just the helper in isolation** - both `build_sanral_keyperson()` (line 458) and `build_world_bank()` (line 624) call `_footer(d, comp)` as their own last step, unconditionally, for every CV either format produces - a company whose `legal_name` happens to be corrupted down to nothing but control bytes can never get ANY CV generated for ANY key person, in either format, until this is fixed.

**Fix.** Same shape already recorded as the recommended fix for Finding 367's own `build_docx.py` case: only style the paragraph once sanitizing has actually left a real run behind.
```python
p = d.add_paragraph(_safe_text(comp.get("legal_name", "")))
p.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER
if p.runs:
    p.runs[0].italic = True
```
A `legal_name` that sanitizes to genuinely nothing now produces a blank, un-italicised footer line instead of crashing the build - the same "blank rather than guessed, and never a raw exception" discipline this file already applies everywhere else `_safe_text()` is used.

**Verified red-then-green, myself, real exit codes.** Added one new test, `test_company_legal_name_entirely_control_characters_does_not_crash_footer()`, to `engine/cv/test_generate_cv.py`, exercising BOTH `build_world_bank()` and `build_sanral_keyperson()` with `profile["company"]["legal_name"] = "\x00"` (nothing left after `_safe_text()`). **RED** (`git stash push -- engine/cv/generate_cv.py` to isolate the test from the fix, run from `engine/cv/`): `python3 test_generate_cv.py` - exit **1**, `2 failure(s)`:
```
  FAIL a legal_name that sanitizes to empty does not crash build_world_bank  (IndexError: list index out of range)
  FAIL a legal_name that sanitizes to empty does not crash build_sanral_keyperson  (IndexError: list index out of range)
```
`git stash pop` to restore the fix. **GREEN:** `python3 test_generate_cv.py` - exit **0**, `0 failure(s)`, **51/51** `check()` assertions pass across all **27** test functions in the file (the pre-existing 26 + this new one).

**Full regression, counted, not estimated.** Ran every one of this repo's 90 `engine/test_*.py` files individually (`find engine -name "test_*.py" | wc -l` = 90, run from `engine/`): **89/90 exit 0** on the first pass; the 90th, `engine/pack/test_b7_hard_stop.py`, hit this pass's own 60s-per-file timeout cap (exit `124`) and was re-run alone with a 180s cap - it passed in ~85s real time, a pre-existing slow-but-passing test (already flagged by this series' own standing notes), not a regression from this change. The one genuine non-zero exit, `engine/discovery/test_download_documents.py` (`ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'playwright'`), is the same pre-existing, already-documented sandbox-only gap this series' own standing notes say not to re-report. `python3 -m py_compile`/`ast.parse` clean on both touched files. `ruff check engine/cv/generate_cv.py engine/cv/test_generate_cv.py` - **16** findings before AND after this fix (confirmed via `git stash`/`git stash pop`), the exact same 16 rule violations at the exact same lines except one (`BLE001` on the pre-existing blind-`except Exception`), which shifted from line 722 to line 736 - precisely the 14 comment/code lines this fix inserted above it, not a new finding.

**Why pushed directly to `main`, not a PR.** No RLS, no money path, no hard-stop/disqualification gate, no worker-image/deployment-config change, no migration/schema surface - two Python files, zero SQL. `generate_cv.py` is explicitly NOT one of the six files this track's own guardrail names as requiring a PR for a correctness fix (`fill_a_forms.py`/`fill_sbd_docx.py`/`fill_flat_pdf.py`/`make_envelope_covers.py`/`process_narrative_jobs.py`/`build_docx.py`) - direct precedent already established three times in this exact file for this exact class of fix (the original `13bdfc2` sanitisation fix, the 2026-10-25 `cv.wb.education` fix, and Findings 372/373 immediately above, all pushed directly). Not auth-adjacent. Nothing in `pack-review.tsx`/`submission-pack.tsx`'s import graph touches Python at all. Looped `gh api repos/sareljvr2024/tender-tool/pulls/<n>/files -q '.[].filename'` over all 58 and grepped for `cv/generate_cv\.py|cv/test_generate_cv\.py` - **zero hits**, no open PR touches either file. `git fetch origin main` immediately before starting this pass, and again immediately before this push, both showed `main` unchanged at `98d9299` (Finding 373's own pass's commit) - no sibling-track commit landed in either gap.

### Finding 376 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, pushed directly to `main`): `fill_tender.py`'s and `fill_conventional.py`'s own `fill_person()` - the real Form B1/B2 key-person-block writer for both SANRAL Technical-Submission template families - never threaded the `ProvenanceLog` `log` parameter either `main()` already accepts (and already passes into `sanral_fill.fill_company_front()`) down into `fill_person()` itself, so a key person's ECSA/SACPCMP registration number or date, when genuinely absent on file, was silently left blank with zero trace in `field_provenance.json` and no flag on `ACTIONS_TO_SIGN.md`

**Area:** `engine/fill_tender.py`'s and `engine/fill_conventional.py`'s `fill_person()` (the Form B1/B2 key-person block writer, called once per key-person slot by each file's own `main()`), plus a new regression test, `engine/test_fill_person_registration_provenance.py`.

**How this was found.** The "confirmed vs written/logged" bug class is exhausted per standing notes, but only for the specific list of filler files that list names (`fill_a_forms.py`, `fill_sbd_docx.py`, `fill_flat_pdf.py`, `build_general_pack.py`, `sanral_fill.py`, `company_documents.py`, `fill_docx_forms.py`, `generate_action_checklist.py`, `generate_cv.py`) - `fill_tender.py`/`fill_conventional.py` are not on that list. `assemble_pack.py`'s own `FILLERS[family].main(...)` call passes a real `ProvenanceLog` (`tech_log`) as each filler's `log` argument, and both files' own `main()` signatures accept `log=None` and pass it straight into `sanral_fill.fill_company_front()` for the company-level front page - but neither file's own `main()` ever passed `log` into its OWN `fill_person()` function (no `log` parameter existed on `fill_person()` at all), even though `fill_person()` writes a key person's full Form B1/B2 block: name, ID number, description, employment type, ECSA/SACPCMP registration, qualifications, years of experience, and every project row. Four of those fields - `ecsa_number`, `ecsa_date`, `sacpcmp_number`, `sacpcmp_date` - are the ONE group conditionally written (`if q.get(...): wb.set_value(...)`, exactly the already-fixed SARS-TCS-PIN/VAT-number shape from Findings 368/371) with no `log` call in either branch, since there was no `log` to call at all.

**Confirmed real and reachable, not theoretical.** `ecsa_number`/`sacpcmp_number` are plain nullable `text` columns on `people`, never validated or made mandatory anywhere in the app (`app/app/people/actions.ts`'s `savePerson()` just forwards whatever the form submits) - a key person can be genuinely ECSA-registered with no number yet on file, SACPCMP-only, or have one body's number but not the other's, and still be validly confirmed for a key position (`set_dropdown_for()`'s own hard refusal only covers `ecsa_level` itself being blank, a separate, already-enforced gate). The repo's own committed real sample pack, `packs/r334-030-2025-1f.yaml` (Klipcorp/Henning Jansen van Rensburg, used for both key positions on this contract), is a live, already-existing instance of exactly this gap: `ecsa_number`/`ecsa_date` are on file but `sacpcmp_number`/`sacpcmp_date` are absent entirely from the pack's own `qualifications` block.

**Why this matters.** `generate_action_checklist.py`'s `ACTIONS_TO_SIGN.md` is built purely by filtering `field_provenance` entries for `status in ("assumed_default", "missing")` - a field with NO entry at all, exactly like `ecsa_number`/`ecsa_date`/`sacpcmp_number`/`sacpcmp_date` before this fix, is just as invisible to the checklist as one wrongly marked `confirmed` (Findings 368/369/371-373's own shape). A company with a key person missing a registration number/date on the real, submitted SANRAL Technical Submission workbook was never told, anywhere, to go get it before signing.

**Fix.** Added `log=None` to both `fill_person()` signatures, passed `log` through from each `main()`'s own call site (`fill_person(wb, base, person, pack.get("projects", {}), a.get("position"), log)`), and - following the exact `_log(log, kind, key, value, reason)` convention `sanral_fill.fill_company_front()` already uses for its own optional fields (imported from `sanral_fill`, not reimplemented) - logged `confirmed` with the real value when each of the four fields is written, `missing` with a reason naming the person and the field when it isn't. The document cells themselves are completely unchanged - still written only when a real value is on file, never guessed.

**Verified red-then-green, myself, real exit codes.** New test `engine/test_fill_person_registration_provenance.py`, driving `fill_conventional.main()` end to end against the real committed sample workbook (`templates/samples/R.334-030-2025.1F_ran.xlsm`) and the real sample pack (`packs/r334-030-2025-1f.yaml` - the same fixture `test_fill_b7_legacy_precedence.py` already drives this file against), with a real `ProvenanceLog` passed in (not `log=None`): 5 checks - `ecsa_number`/`ecsa_date` logged `confirmed` with the real on-file values; `sacpcmp_number`/`sacpcmp_date` (genuinely absent from this real sample) logged `missing` with a reason naming "Henning"; both key-person blocks (PL and DS1, same person per this sample pack) each produce their own `ecsa_number` entry. **RED** (`git stash push -- engine/fill_conventional.py engine/fill_tender.py`, the real pre-fix code, new test kept): `python3 test_fill_person_registration_provenance.py` - **5 failure(s)**, exit **1** - every single check fails, confirming `log.entries` contains no `tend1x.*.ecsa_number`/`ecsa_date`/`sacpcmp_number`/`sacpcmp_date` entry of any kind, for either status. `git stash pop` to restore the fix. **GREEN:** same command - **0 failure(s)**, exit **0**.

**Full regression, counted, not estimated.** Ran every one of this repo's 91 `engine/test_*.py` files individually (`find engine -name "test_*.py" | grep -v __pycache__ | wc -l` = 91, the 90 pre-existing files plus this pass's own new one): **90/91 exit 0**; the one non-zero exit is `engine/discovery/test_download_documents.py` (`ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'playwright'`), the same pre-existing, already-documented sandbox-only gap this series' own standing notes say not to re-report - unaffected by this change. Specifically re-ran, individually: `engine/test_fill_tender.py` (0 failure(s)), `engine/test_fill_b7_legacy_precedence.py` (0 failure(s) - this file's own Form B7 precedence coverage for `fill_conventional.py`, unaffected by the unrelated `fill_person()` change), `engine/test_sanral_fill.py` (0 failure(s)), `engine/test_sanral_b7.py` (ALL PASSED), `engine/test_fill_key_persons_malformed.py` (0 failure(s)), `engine/test_fingerprint.py` (0 failure(s)), `engine/test_form_field_audit.py` (0 failure(s)). `python3 -m py_compile engine/fill_tender.py engine/fill_conventional.py` clean.

### Finding 379 (CONFIRMED, NOT FIXED - the one safe part of this, a false comment, IS fixed and pushed to `main`): `companies.bee_procurement_recognition_pct` is captured, shown and offered for editing exactly like its two true document-writing siblings (`bee_level`, `black_ownership_pct`) - but reaches no document, on either pack engine, and no compliance check anywhere in the codebase

**Area:** `app/lib/companyProfileUpdate.ts` (`PERCENTAGE_FIELDS`'s own header comment, now corrected), `engine/pack_generator/confirm_pack.py`'s `confirm()` (the real drop point), `app/app/tenders/[id]/quick-fix-config.ts`'s `VAULT_DRAWER_CONFIG.bbbee`, `app/app/company/_components/EditForm.tsx`/`BeeCidbSection.tsx`, `app/lib/tenderCompliance.ts`.

**How this was found.** Per this pass's own directive (a genuinely different angle from the already-exhausted "confirmed vs written/logged" sweep and from `experienceEvidence.ts`'s already-twice-checked branches) - swept `engine/pack/process_pack_jobs.py`'s `adapt_company()` field by field against every later consumer, the same sibling-field-comparison method several earlier passes have already used. `adapt_company()` reads `bee_procurement_recognition_pct` straight off the `companies` row (migration `0001`, same column as `bee_level`/`black_ownership_pct`) into the profile dict it writes to `profile.json`. `engine/pack_generator/confirm_pack.py`'s `confirm()` - the one gate everything must pass through before reaching `fill_conventional.py`/`fill_tender.py` (its own docstring) - then builds `pack.yaml`'s `company` dict from a **hardcoded** list of keys (lines 176-194): `name`, `bee_level`, `black_ownership_pct`, `status`, `head_office`, `other_offices`, `ecsa_registered`, `sacpcmp_registered`, `total_employees`, `jv_share_pct`, `bee_proof_type`, `bee_proof_expiry` - `bee_procurement_recognition_pct` is simply absent from that list, so it is silently dropped at exactly this translation step and never reaches `pack.yaml`, `sanral_fill.py`, `field_provenance.json` or `ACTIONS_TO_SIGN.md` at all (not even as a `missing` entry - it never gets that far).

**Confirmed this is a real gap, not a field with no intended destination that just happens to be unwired (the already-accepted shape of `System-Status.md`'s standing item 28, `company_offices.proof_type`/`proof_date`).** Three independent checks, not just "it's absent from one dict":

### Finding 381 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, pushed directly to `main`): `engine/discovery/score_outlook.py`'s `extract_experience_evidence()` merges a restated experience-evidence rule (its own documented SANRAL/Transnet shape) correctly for every field it computes EXCEPT `scored_per_project` - a later restatement that reveals the real points ladder is silently discarded if the first-seen restatement didn't show one

**Area:** `engine/discovery/score_outlook.py`'s `extract_experience_evidence()` (the duplicate-rule merge block, immediately after `_parse_evidence_window()`), plus a new regression test in `engine/discovery/test_score_outlook.py`. Read-only consumers, unaffected by the fix itself but confirming why it matters: `describe_evidence_rule()` (same file), `app/lib/experienceEvidence.ts`'s `describeRule()`/`evaluateEvidence()` (reached via `tenders.evaluation_rules`, migration 0016, written by `engine/seed_tender_evaluation_rules.py`).

**How this was found.** Candidate area from this task's own brief: "`discovery/score_outlook.py`'s other extracted-rule fields, distinct from `disqualification_mentioned`/`practical_completion_excluded`, both already checked" (those two were Finding 378/PR #235 and are themselves already read correctly on the merge path). Read `extract_experience_evidence()`'s own duplicate-restatement merge block end to end against every field `_parse_evidence_window()` returns, the same "field computed but dropped somewhere downstream" method several earlier passes in this series have used (`company_offices.office_kind`, Finding 340; the SANRAL B7 TE fields, Finding 377). The dict `_parse_evidence_window()` returns has 11 real fields. When two windows are found to restate the same rule (the function's own docstring names the exact real-world trigger: "SANRAL repeats B6 in the scoring explanation and on the form; Transnet in the narrative and the scoring table"), the merge block updates 8 of them correctly - `projects_required`/`window_years`/`since_year`/`scope`/`consequence` via `dup[k] = dup[k] or r[k]`, `accepted_evidence` via a set union, and `practical_completion_excluded`/`disqualification_mentioned` via `|=` (OR, so either restatement showing the condition is enough). `requires_appointment_and_completion` is never merged, but doesn't need to be - it's part of the dup-match condition itself (`e[...] == r[...]`), so it's already guaranteed equal between the two. `quote` is deliberately display-only, left as the first occurrence's own text (no information carried there matters downstream). That leaves exactly one field with neither treatment: **`scored_per_project`** - computed independently per window (`bool(ladder)`, `_parse_evidence_window()`) but never read, written, or OR'd anywhere in the merge block, so the merged rule silently keeps whichever restatement was seen FIRST, even when a LATER restatement in the same tender's own text states the real points ladder explicitly.

**Confirmed real and reachable, not theoretical - reproduced live against the real, unmodified `score_outlook.py` on `main`, pre-fix:**
```python
import score_outlook as so
text = (
    "3.2 Experience: Tenderers must have completed at least 3 (three) similar projects of similar "
    "scope in the last 10 (ten) years. Submit reference letters as proof.\n"
    + ("Padding line filler text to separate the two windows beyond the 1200-character merge gap. " * 40)
    + "\nScoring table for company experience (reference letters):\n"
    "1 Completed project 10\n2 Completed projects 20\n3 Completed projects 30\n"
)
so.extract_experience_evidence(text)["rules"]
```
The first window (a plain "at least 3 projects" sentence, no ladder) and the second (a real 1/2/3 -> points table, well past the function's own 1200-character `_evidence_windows()` merge gap) genuinely merge into one rule - same `projects_required` (3), overlapping evidence (`reference_letter`), equal `requires_appointment_and_completion` (both `False`) - exactly the dup-match condition the function's own code checks. **Pre-fix, the merged rule reports `scored_per_project: False`**, even though parsing the second window in isolation (`_parse_evidence_window()` on just that text) genuinely returns `scored_per_project: True` - the real ladder information the tender's own text states is thrown away purely because of which window the parser happened to visit first, an artifact of document layout, not of what the tender actually says.

**Why this matters, bounded correctly.** `scored_per_project` does not change any `have`/`check`/`missing` compliance status anywhere - `evaluateEvidence()`'s own status branches key off `n >= need`/`n < need` and the separate `requires_appointment_and_completion`/`ratingsMatter`/`consequence` fields, none of which this bug touches. What it does change is the wording shown to the company on both the SANRAL compliance report (`compliance-data.ts` -> `submission-pack.tsx`) and the general-family Pack Review screen: `describeRule()` (`app/lib/experienceEvidence.ts`, mirrored by `describe_evidence_rule()` on the Python side) renders `scored_per_project` as `"scored per project, full points at N"` vs. the flat, misleading `"N project(s)"` when false; and `evaluateEvidence()`'s own "missing" shortfall message appends `" Scored per project, so each one added earns points."` only when the field is true - so a company genuinely short of items, under a tender that in fact scores incrementally per project (every extra qualifying item earns more points, not an all-or-nothing threshold), would be shown the flat framing and miss that submitting even one more project still helps its score. Not a crash, not a disqualification-gate miscalculation, not a document-content defect (no filled document reads this field at all) - a real, live-reachable, user-facing wording-accuracy gap in exactly the informational text this whole extraction pipeline exists to produce, the same severity tier as Findings 375/377/378 found elsewhere in this same "extracted rule field dropped somewhere before it reaches the person reading it" class.

**Fix.** Added `scored_per_project` to the merge block's own OR-handling, identically to its two true siblings two lines above it:
```python
dup["practical_completion_excluded"] |= r["practical_completion_excluded"]
dup["disqualification_mentioned"] |= r["disqualification_mentioned"]
dup["scored_per_project"] |= r["scored_per_project"]
```
Either restatement showing a real points ladder is now enough for the merged rule to say so - the same "any one occurrence is sufficient evidence" rule this file already applies to `practical_completion_excluded`/`disqualification_mentioned`. No other field, no other function, and no TypeScript file touched.

**Verified red-then-green, myself, real exit code.** New test, `test_experience_evidence_merge_keeps_scored_per_project_from_either_restatement()`, added to `engine/discovery/test_score_outlook.py`, driving the real `extract_experience_evidence()` end to end with the exact text shape reproduced above (3 checks: the two restatements merge into exactly one rule; `projects_required` is still 3; the merged rule's `scored_per_project` is `True`). **RED** (`git stash push -- engine/discovery/score_outlook.py` to isolate the new test from the fix, run from `engine/discovery/`): `python3 test_score_outlook.py` - exit **1**, **1 failure(s)** (`the merged rule's scored_per_project is True - the ladder restatement must not be lost`, actual value `False`); the other 2 new checks and all 13 pre-existing checks still pass. `git stash pop` to restore the fix. **GREEN:** same command - exit **0**, **0 failure(s)**, all **16** checks across the file's 13 test functions pass.

**Full regression, counted, not estimated, all exit codes captured directly, never through a pipe.** Ran every one of this repo's **91** `engine/test_*.py` files individually (`find engine -name "test_*.py" | grep -v __pycache__ | wc -l` = 91, run from `engine/`, one file at a time, each exit code captured with `echo $?` immediately after that file's own run, never through `tail`/`head`): **89/91 exit 0** on the first pass. The 2 non-zero exits are both pre-existing and already documented, neither a regression from this change: `engine/discovery/test_download_documents.py` (`ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'playwright'`, the known sandbox-only gap this series' own standing notes say not to re-report) and `engine/pack/test_b7_hard_stop.py` (exit `124` under this sweep's own 60s-per-file cap - re-run alone immediately after with a 180s cap: **exit 0, 0 failure(s), real 1m31.955s**, the same pre-existing slow-but-passing test this series' own standing notes already flag, confirmed still passing, not a regression). `python3 -m py_compile engine/discovery/score_outlook.py engine/discovery/test_score_outlook.py` - clean. `ruff check engine/discovery/score_outlook.py engine/discovery/test_score_outlook.py` - **2** findings both BEFORE and AFTER this fix (confirmed via `git stash`/`git stash pop`), the exact same 2 pre-existing rule violations at the exact same lines (an unrelated `f`-string-without-placeholder at line 912, and an unrelated stale `# noqa: E402` at the test file's own existing import line) - no new finding introduced.

**Why pushed directly to `main`, not a PR.** No RLS, no money/payment path, no hard-stop/disqualification gate (`scored_per_project` plays no role in any `have`/`check`/`missing` status computation anywhere, confirmed by reading `evaluateEvidence()`'s own status branches directly - it only ever appears inside descriptive text), no worker-image/deployment-config change, no migration/schema surface - one Python engine file plus its own test file, zero SQL, zero TypeScript. `engine/discovery/score_outlook.py` is not one of the six files this track's own guardrail names as requiring a PR for a correctness fix (`fill_a_forms.py`/`fill_sbd_docx.py`/`fill_flat_pdf.py`/`make_envelope_covers.py`/`process_narrative_jobs.py`/`build_docx.py`). ### Finding 382 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, pushed directly to `main`): `engine/cv/generate_cv.py`'s `build_world_bank()` printed the literal word "None" into a real, client-facing CV document whenever a person had an ECSA registration LEVEL on file but no registration NUMBER yet - `q.get("ecsa_number", "MISSING")`'s own default only substitutes when the dict key is ABSENT, but both real callers always build the dict with every qualification key present (value `None` when the column is null)

**Area:** `engine/cv/generate_cv.py`'s `build_world_bank()` (Section 6, "Membership of Professional Associations" - the ECSA line specifically), plus two new regression tests in `engine/cv/test_generate_cv.py`.

**How this was found.** Candidate area from this task's own brief: `process_pack_jobs.py`'s `adapt_company()`/`adapt_person()` helpers, "beyond the already-known Finding 370 PI-insurance-`period_from` issue - look at their OTHER fields, there may be more 'hardcoded placeholder regardless of real data' issues." Read `adapt_company()` end to end first (lines 256-311) - every other field there either passes `row.get(key)` straight through or uses a correct `or` fallback; the only unconditional, no-fallback literal is `period_from` itself (Finding 370, already documented, not re-flagged). Widened the same question to the sibling function `adapt_person()` (line 314) and its qualifications dict, then followed every one of those 18 fields downstream into `generate_cv.py` (the one real consumer) looking for the SAME underlying bug class this file has already been fixed for multiple times (comments at lines ~263, ~561-566, ~577, ~589-593 all document and fix instances of it): `dict.get(key, default)`'s default only ever substitutes when the key is absent, never when the key is present with value `None` - and this engine's own two real adapters (`process_pack_jobs.py`'s `adapt_person()`, `process_cv_jobs.py`'s `adapt_person_row()`) both build their `qualifications` dict via a comprehension/literal that always includes every key, `None` when the underlying column is null. `grep -rn "\.get([^,]*, *['\"]MISSING['\"])"` over every pack/CV/general engine filler file found exactly one remaining site using the broken pattern instead of the already-fixed `or`-fallback shape: `build_world_bank()`'s own ECSA line.

```python
if q.get("ecsa_level"):
    assoc_lines.append(f"Engineering Council of South Africa (ECSA) - {q['ecsa_level']}, "
                        f"registration {q.get('ecsa_number', 'MISSING')}")
    log.confirmed("cv.wb.professional_associations.ecsa", q["ecsa_level"])
```

`ecsa_level`/`ecsa_number` are two independently-nullable columns (`0001_init_schema.sql`, no check constraint tying them together) - a real person can be registered at a level (e.g. a Candidate Engineer awaiting a registration number) with `ecsa_number` genuinely blank. Confirmed `ecsa_number` is always a present key in the real profile dict, not an absent one, by running both real adapters directly:

```python
>>> import process_cv_jobs as pcj
>>> pcj.adapt_person_row({"name": "Jane Doe", "ecsa_level": "Professional Engineer", "ecsa_number": None}, [])["qualifications"]
{'ecsa_level': 'Professional Engineer', 'ecsa_number': None, ...}  # key present, value None
>>> _["ecsa_number"]  # doctest-style continuation
None
```
so `q.get("ecsa_number", "MISSING")`'s own `"MISSING"` default can never fire for this real shape - it only ever would if the dict genuinely lacked the key, which neither real adapter (`process_pack_jobs.py:adapt_person()` nor `process_cv_jobs.py:adapt_person_row()`) ever produces.

**Live-reproduced directly against the real, unmodified `build_world_bank()` on `main`, pre-fix, not reasoned about:**
```python
log = ProvenanceLog(source="test")
profile = {"company": {"legal_name": "Acme Co"}}
person = {"name": "Jane Doe", "role": "Engineer", "projects": [],
          "qualifications": {"ecsa_level": "Professional Engineer", "ecsa_number": None}}
d = gc.build_world_bank(profile, person, "person_0", "summary", None, None, log)
```
**RED** - the real generated `.docx` paragraph text reads, verbatim: `"Engineering Council of South Africa (ECSA) - Professional Engineer, registration None"`. `log.confirmed("cv.wb.professional_associations.ecsa", "Professional Engineer")` is correct and unaffected (it only ever logs `ecsa_level`, not `ecsa_number`) - the bug is confined to the printed document text itself, the exact "prints the literal word None into a real, client-facing CV" bug class already named and fixed multiple times before in this same file (Findings referenced in the file's own comments: project rows' `position_held`/`contact`/`end`, education's `institution`/`graduated`) - this is a new, previously-unswept instance of that same class, not a repeat of any of those.

**Confirmed reachable from the real pipeline, not just the function in isolation.** `process_cv_jobs.py` (the real bridge between the web app's `generated_cvs` request table and this generator) dispatches `{"world_bank": generate_cv.build_world_bank}[job["format"]]` for any real CV job requesting the World Bank format - a real, selectable, donor-funded-tender CV format, not a CLI-only or test-only path.

**Fix.** Replaced the broken `.get(key, default)` pattern with the same `or`-fallback shape this file already uses correctly everywhere else for this exact situation (e.g. the SACNASP/SAGC loop two lines below, `q.get(f'{key}_category') or 'registered'`):
```python
assoc_lines.append(f"Engineering Council of South Africa (ECSA) - {q['ecsa_level']}, "
                    f"registration {q.get('ecsa_number') or 'MISSING'}")
```
A real `ecsa_number` on file is printed exactly as before (unaffected); a genuinely absent one now reads "registration MISSING" (matching this document's own existing convention for other missing sub-fields, e.g. the referee line's `proj.get('contact') or 'MISSING'` a few lines below) instead of the literal word "None". `log.confirmed()`'s own value (`ecsa_level`) is untouched either way - this fix is scoped to the printed document text only, exactly like the precedent fixes this file's own comments already document for other fields.

**Verified red-then-green, myself, real exit codes.** Two new tests added to `engine/cv/test_generate_cv.py`: `test_world_bank_ecsa_level_with_no_number_does_not_print_the_word_none()` (3 checks: the document text contains no literal "None"; it reads "registration MISSING" instead; the provenance entry is still correctly `confirmed` with the real `ecsa_level` value, unchanged) and `test_world_bank_ecsa_level_with_number_still_prints_it()` (1 check, regression guard: a real `ecsa_number` on file still prints verbatim). **RED** (`git stash push -- engine/cv/generate_cv.py` to isolate the new tests from the fix, run from `engine/cv/`): `python3 test_generate_cv.py` - exit **1**, **2 failure(s)**, exactly the two assertions tied to this bug (`the document text does not contain the literal word 'None'` and `the document text reads 'registration MISSING' instead`, both showing the actual text `"...registration None"`); the regression-guard test and all other pre-existing checks still pass. `git stash pop` to restore the fix. **GREEN:** same command - exit **0**, **0 failure(s)**, **55/55** `check()` assertions pass across all **29** test functions in the file (the pre-existing 27 + these 2 new).

### Finding 383 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, pushed directly to `main`): `fill_conventional.py`'s `main()` never got the "Form B7 closing date vs SETUP's own closing date" mismatch warning `fill_tender.py`'s sibling `main()` already has, even though this file's own docstring states the Form B3/B7 cells "turned out to be IDENTICAL to the RRM template"

**Area:** `engine/fill_conventional.py`'s `main()` (the Conventional Consultant Tender family's real SANRAL Technical Submission filler), new pure function `b7_closing_date_note()`, plus a new regression test file `engine/test_fill_conventional.py` (this file had no dedicated test at all before this pass).

**How this was found.** Per the task brief's own "genuinely different precedent-comparison (two structurally similar code paths treated inconsistently)" angle: `fill_tender.py` (RRM Consultant Tender family) and `fill_conventional.py` (Conventional Consultant Tender family) are explicitly documented twins - `fill_conventional.py`'s own module docstring states "The TEND 1X key-person block layout, date triplets and Form B3/B7 cells turned out to be IDENTICAL to the RRM template." Diffing the two files end to end (`diff engine/fill_tender.py engine/fill_conventional.py`) surfaced one place where they've already drifted apart in the opposite direction from the "confirmed vs written/logged" class this track has repeatedly found before: `fill_tender.py`'s `main()` reads Form B7's own pre-filled closing date (`TEND 1X!F125`) and compares it against the SETUP sheet's own closing date (`SETUP!C3`), appending a warning to `notes` (the list `assemble_pack.py` surfaces into the pack's own manifest warnings) when they disagree - factored into a pure, tested function `tender_check_notes()` after Finding 114 (2026-11-01) found this check used to only `print()`, never reaching a human. `fill_conventional.py`'s `main()` has no such check anywhere - not even a `print()` - despite being otherwise maintained in lockstep with its sibling (both files already got the identical Form B7 legacy-TE-precedence fix, 2026-10-26, and the identical `fill_person()` provenance-logging fix, Finding 376, earlier this same day).

**Confirmed the shared cell genuinely exists in this template family, not assumed from the docstring alone.** Read the real committed Conventional-family sample directly with `openpyxl` (via `sanral_fill.Workbook`):
```python
wb = Workbook('templates/samples/R.334-030-2025.1F_ran.xlsm')
wb.cached('TEND 1X', 'F125')   # 46317 (a real date serial)
wb.cached('TEND 1X', 'E125')   # 'Tender Closing date:'
wb.cached('TEND 1X', 'C125')   # 'B7 Info:'
wb.cached('SETUP', 'C3')       # 46317 - the SAME serial, on this real sample
```
`TEND 1X!F125` is a real, SANRAL-pre-filled "Tender Closing date:" cell inside the Form B7 block on this template family too, labelled identically to the RRM template's own `F125` cell `tender_check_notes()` already reads - confirming the docstring's "IDENTICAL" claim for this specific cell, not just assuming it. Also confirmed the OTHER two checks `tender_check_notes()` makes (bundled `TENDDER` rows, per-contract Form C2.4 figures) genuinely do NOT apply to this template family - rows 17-40 column D on the real sample's own `TEND 1X` sheet are all blank, matching the docstring's own "single C2.4 summary sheet (not six per-contract sheets)" - so only the Form B7 closing-date check was missing, not the whole set.

**Live-reproduced directly, pre-fix, not reasoned about:**
```python
fc.b7_closing_date_note("2026-10-29", "2026-11-05")
```
pre-fix, this function didn't exist at all (`AttributeError`) - `main()` had no equivalent code path, so a Conventional-family pack whose Form B7 closing date disagreed with its SETUP closing date (the exact, real-world risk `fill_tender.py`'s own Finding 114 fix exists to catch) produced no warning, no note, nothing - the identical silent gap Finding 114 already found and fixed once, just never ported to this twin.

**Fix.** Added `b7_closing_date_note(close, b7)` to `fill_conventional.py` - a pure function returning 0 or 1 note, the same shape `fill_tender.py`'s own `tender_check_notes()` uses, with identical wording ("Form B7 closing date ({b7}) differs from the SETUP sheet's own closing date ({close}) - check which is correct before relying on this."). `main()` now reads `b7 = serial(wb.cached(T, "F125"))` alongside the `close` it already computed (previously only inlined into a `print()`, never stored), calls the new function, and extends its own `notes` the same way `fill_tender.py` does - a real `print()` WARNING line is kept too, for parity with the sibling's own console output. The real document cells themselves are completely unchanged - this is a warning-surfacing fix only, identical in shape and risk to Finding 376/the original Finding 114, neither of which changed any written cell value either.

**Verified red-then-green, myself, real exit codes.** New test file `engine/test_fill_conventional.py` (none existed before this pass): the pure function in isolation (mismatched dates -> one note naming both; matching dates -> no note), plus two checks against the real committed Conventional sample (`templates/samples/R.334-030-2025.1F_ran.xlsm`, the same one `test_fill_b7_legacy_precedence.py` already drives end to end) confirming `TEND 1X!F125` really holds a value and really agrees with `SETUP!C3` on today's real template (so the fix produces no spurious warning on real data), and a full end-to-end run of `fill_conventional.main()` against that same real sample confirming no `"Form B7 closing date"` note appears in its real returned `notes`. **RED** (`git stash push -- engine/fill_conventional.py`, the new test file kept): `python3 test_fill_conventional.py` - exit **1** (`AttributeError: module 'fill_conventional' has no attribute 'b7_closing_date_note'`, failing on the very first pure-function check, before any of the other 3 checks could even run). `git stash pop` to restore the fix. **GREEN:** same command - exit **0**, all checks pass (pure-function pair, the real-sample F125 read, and the real end-to-end run).

### Finding 384 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, pushed directly to `main`): `engine/discovery/score_outlook.py`'s `_bbbee_points_by_level()` matched the literal word "Level" case-SENSITIVELY, the one regex in this file that doesn't, so a real tender's B-BBEE specific-goals points table rendered in any other case silently returned no table at all, even though its own sibling regexes (`BBBEE_TABLE_RE`/`BBBEE_ROW_RE`) correctly recognise the SAME table as present

**Area:** `engine/discovery/score_outlook.py`'s `_bbbee_points_by_level()` (the SANRAL-style B-BBEE level/points table parser feeding `_specific_goals()` and, through it, `estimate_score_outlook()`'s own `specific_goals` field), plus a new regression test in `engine/discovery/test_score_outlook.py`. Read-only consumer, unaffected by the fix itself but confirming why it matters: `app/lib/scoreOutlookChips.ts`'s Discovery-page "Specific goals: ..." chip, which only renders at all when `specific_goals.points_estimate` is non-null.

**How this was found.** Per the task brief's own candidate area "`score_outlook.py`'s OTHER extraction functions, distinct from the already-done experience-evidence merge (Finding 381)." `score_outlook.py` is almost entirely built on regexes, and essentially every one of them that matches a real word of running tender text is deliberately case-insensitive - a `grep -n "re.compile\|re.search" score_outlook.py` sweep of the whole file found `re.IGNORECASE` (or `re.I`) on every single regex that matches literal English/table words, with one sole exception: `_bbbee_points_by_level()`'s own `re.search(rf"Level\s*{level}\b([^\n]*)", text)`, line 139 - no flag at all. Two sibling regexes a few lines away, about the exact same real-world table (`BBBEE_TABLE_RE = re.compile(r"B-?BBEE\s+(?:Status\s+)?Level", re.IGNORECASE)` and `BBBEE_ROW_RE = re.compile(r"B-?BBEE\s+status\s+level\s+of\s+contributor\s+\d", re.IGNORECASE)`), both correctly use `re.IGNORECASE` - the exact "two structurally similar code paths treated inconsistently" precedent-comparison angle the task brief names. Confirmed `_bbbee_points_by_level()`/`_specific_goals()` have NO dedicated unit test anywhere in the suite (`grep -n "bbbee\|specific_goals" test_score_outlook.py` - zero hits before this pass), so this inconsistency had never been exercised by a real table at all, in either case.

**Live-reproduced directly against the real, unmodified function on `main`, pre-fix, not reasoned about:**
```python
import score_outlook as so
text = (
    "3.2 SPECIFIC GOALS\n"
    "B-BBEE STATUS LEVEL OF CONTRIBUTOR    POINTS (90/10)    POINTS (80/20)\n"
    "LEVEL 1    10.00    20.00\n"
    "LEVEL 2    9.00    18.00\n"
    "LEVEL 3    6.00    14.00\n"
)
so.BBBEE_TABLE_RE.search(text) is not None   # True - this sibling regex sees the table is there
so._bbbee_points_by_level(text)              # {} - pre-fix: nothing, despite the table being real and readable
so._specific_goals(text, {"bee_level": 1}, "90/10")
# pre-fix: {"basis": "unrecognised", "bases": [], "points_estimate": None,
#           "reason": "A specific-goals section exists but its criteria could not be identified from the text."}
```
An all-caps "LEVEL 1  10.00  20.00" rendering (the same table header style a scanned/typeset Book 1 table commonly emphasises in caps - and a shape the file's own sibling regexes are explicitly written to tolerate) is not a contrived edge case: it is the ordinary range of real-document casing this entire file exists to be robust to, which is exactly why every other word-matching regex here already carries `re.IGNORECASE`.

**Why this matters, bounded correctly.** `specific_goals.points_estimate` is a real, user-facing number - `app/lib/scoreOutlookChips.ts`'s Discovery-page chip (`"Specific goals: ${goals.points_estimate}"`) renders only when this field is non-null, right next to the preference-system and functionality chips. Pre-fix, a tender whose real B-BBEE table happened to render in a different case than exactly `"Level"` silently fell through to `_specific_goals()`'s generic `"unrecognised"`/`"mixed"` fallback path - the chip simply never appears for that tender, with no error, no wrong number, just a real, computable signal quietly withheld from the person deciding whether to bid. Not a crash, not a disqualification-gate miscalculation, not a document-content defect (nothing is written to any filled document from this field) - a real, live-reachable, case-sensitivity gap in a purely-regex extraction pipeline, the same "informational signal silently dropped before it reaches the person reading it" severity tier as Findings 375/377/378/381.

**Fix.** Added `re.IGNORECASE` to the one `re.search()` call inside `_bbbee_points_by_level()`'s per-level loop - identical to its two sibling regexes two lines away:
```python
m = re.search(rf"Level\s*{level}\b([^\n]*)", text, re.IGNORECASE)
```
Purely permissive (matches a strict superset of what matched before); the function's own existing `table.get(1) != (10.0, 20.0): return {}` safety gate is untouched, so a document whose "Level N" lines were something else entirely (its own documented false-positive guard, e.g. a B-BBEE proof-of-status paragraph) is still rejected exactly as before - this only widens which CASE of the real table's own rows get read, nothing else.

**Verified red-then-green, myself, real exit codes.** New test, `test_bbbee_points_by_level_is_case_insensitive_like_its_sibling_regexes()`, added to `engine/discovery/test_score_outlook.py` (4 checks: `BBBEE_TABLE_RE` already recognises the all-caps table as present; the table itself is now parsed, not dropped; level 2's points are read correctly too; `_specific_goals()`'s own real output reports `"10 of 10"` for a level-1 company under 90/10, not the generic "could not be identified" fallback). **RED** (`git stash push -- engine/discovery/score_outlook.py` to isolate the new test from the fix, run from `engine/discovery/`): `python3 test_score_outlook.py` - exit **1**, **3 failure(s)**, exactly the three assertions tied to this bug (the table/level-2 parse and the `_specific_goals()` real-output check); the lone "BBBEE_TABLE_RE already recognises..." control check and every one of the 14 pre-existing checks still pass. `git stash pop` to restore the fix. **GREEN:** same command - exit **0**, **0 failure(s)**, all **17** checks across the file's 15 test functions pass (13 pre-existing + 4 new).

**Full regression, counted, not estimated, every exit code captured directly, never through a pipe.** Ran every one of this repo's **92** `engine/test_*.py` files individually (`find . -maxdepth 2 -name "test_*.py" | grep -v __pycache__ | wc -l` = 92, run from `engine/`, one file at a time, each exit code appended to a results file immediately after that file's own run, never glanced at through `tail`/`head`): **90/92 exit 0**. The 2 non-zero exits are both pre-existing and already documented, neither a regression from this change: `engine/discovery/test_download_documents.py` (`ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'playwright'`, the known sandbox-only gap this series' own standing notes say not to re-report) and `engine/pack/test_b7_hard_stop.py` (exit `124` under this sweep's own 60s-per-file cap - re-run alone immediately after with a 180s cap: **exit 0, 0 failure(s), real 1m29.525s**, the same pre-existing slow-but-passing test this series' own standing notes already flag, confirmed still passing, not a regression). `python3 -m py_compile engine/discovery/score_outlook.py engine/discovery/test_score_outlook.py` - clean. `ruff check engine/discovery/score_outlook.py engine/discovery/test_score_outlook.py` - **2** findings both BEFORE and AFTER this fix (confirmed via `git stash`/`git stash pop`), the exact same 2 pre-existing rule violations at the exact same lines already documented by Finding 381's own entry for this file (an unrelated `f`-string-without-placeholder at line ~912/921, and an unrelated stale `# noqa: E402` at the test file's own existing import line) - no new finding introduced.

**Why pushed directly to `main`, not a PR.** No RLS, no money/payment path, no hard-stop/disqualification gate (`specific_goals.points_estimate` plays no role in any pass/fail/disqualification computation anywhere - confirmed by reading every consumer: `scoreOutlookChips.ts` only ever renders an informational chip from it), no worker-image/deployment-config change, no migration/schema surface - one Python engine file plus its own test file, zero SQL, zero TypeScript. `engine/discovery/score_outlook.py` is not one of the six files this track's own guardrail names as requiring a PR for a correctness fix (`fill_a_forms.py`/`fill_sbd_docx.py`/`fill_flat_pdf.py`/`make_envelope_covers.py`/`process_narrative_jobs.py`/`build_docx.py`). Not a correctness fix to any document a company signs or submits - confirmed no filler reads `specific_goals`/`_bbbee_points_by_level()` or anything from `score_outlook.py`'s B-BBEE extraction at all; this field only ever reaches a TypeScript *display* chip. Not auth-adjacent, and - like Finding 381's own identical reasoning for this same file - not "anything `pack-review.tsx`/`submission-pack.tsx` imports from, even transitively" either: `score_outlook.py` is pure Python read by nothing in `app/` directly, reaching the app only after a separate, already-run Discovery pipeline persists its output, at which point it is `scoreOutlookChips.ts` (a Discovery-page-only file, not imported by `pack-review.tsx`/`submission-pack.tsx`) that actually reads it.

### Finding 385 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, pushed directly to `main`): `score_outlook.py`'s own `FUNCTIONALITY_NA_RE` never actually matched the one live document it was written to recognise - `docs/specs/Tender-Evaluation-Engine-Audit.md`'s own quoted real-world evidence, "DPWI architectural PSP, 'Scoring quality / functionality: N/A'", has a colon between "functionality" and "N/A" that the regex's own character class never allowed for

**Where:** `engine/discovery/score_outlook.py`, `FUNCTIONALITY_NA_RE` (module level, just above `_functionality()`) and `_functionality()`'s own first branch, which is the only caller.

**How this was found.** Continuing this pass's own candidate angle - `score_outlook.py`'s OTHER extraction functions, not yet swept by Findings 381 (`extract_experience_evidence()`'s merge gap) or 384 (`_bbbee_points_by_level()`'s case-sensitivity gap). `_functionality()` has its own dedicated test file, `test_score_outlook_functionality.py` (Manifest v2, 2026-10-29) - read it end to end, then read `_functionality()` and its one `FUNCTIONALITY_NA_RE` regex against the real-world evidence this whole file's own module docstring points to for every rule it implements, `docs/specs/Tender-Evaluation-Engine-Audit.md`'s "Round 2" section (the same document Findings 340/343 already traced other rules back to this pass). Line 80 of that doc is the regex's own origin story, quoted verbatim: "DPWI architectural PSP, 'Scoring quality / functionality: N/A'." Checked the regex against its own justifying quote directly, not just against the function's output - `FUNCTIONALITY_NA_RE.search("Scoring quality / functionality: N/A")` returned `None`.

**The bug, read from the regex itself.** `FUNCTIONALITY_NA_RE = re.compile(r"functionality\s*\n?\s*N/?A\b", re.IGNORECASE)` - between "functionality" and "N/A" it only ever allowed `\s*\n?\s*`: a run of plain whitespace, with at most one literal newline character folded in. The real DPWI phrasing has a colon in that gap ("functionality: N/A"), which is not whitespace and is not matched by `\s`. So the regex this module built specifically to recognise "a buyer explicitly marking functionality as not applicable" has never actually matched the one real sample that motivated its own creation - only a synthetic, newline-separated test string (`test_present_false_and_present_none_branches_carry_the_same_new_keys()`'s own `"Functionality\nN/A - price and specific goals only."`) ever exercised it, so the gap was never caught.

**Confirmed the real consequence, not just the regex miss.** `_functionality()`'s first branch is `if FUNCTIONALITY_NA_RE.search(text) and not THRESHOLD_RE.search(text): return {"present": False, ...}`. With the regex never matching, a document that explicitly states functionality is not applicable instead falls all the way through to `func_match = FUNCTIONALITY_RE.search(text)` - and for a document whose ONLY functionality-related text is that one "quality / functionality: N/A" line (nothing else anywhere mentions "functionality" near an evaluation word), `FUNCTIONALITY_RE` doesn't match either, so the function returns `{"present": None, "reason": "No functionality/quality evaluation mentioned in the available text."}` - the "nothing was ever said about this" state, not the "a buyer explicitly said no functionality stage" state, even though the buyer plainly did say exactly that. Live-reproduced directly against the real, unmodified function (no live Supabase project needed - a pure function, exactly how this file's own test suite already exercises it):

```
>>> so._functionality("Scoring quality / functionality: N/A")
{'present': None, 'threshold': None, 'has_sub_minimum': False, 'sub_minimum_rule': None, 'criteria': [],
 'reason': 'No functionality/quality evaluation mentioned in the available text.'}
```

**Confirmed the real, reachable consumer.** `estimate_score_outlook()`'s summary-building block only appends a functionality line for `func.get("present")` truthy OR `func.get("present") is False` explicitly - `present: None` matches neither `if`, so the Discovery page's own summary list silently says nothing about functionality at all for a tender like this, and `app/lib/scoreOutlookChips.ts`'s own chip logic is the identical shape (`if (func?.present === true) {...} else if (func?.present === false) {...}`, no branch for `null`) - so the one real, already-fetched tender this project has evidence for never got its "No functionality gate" chip (`tone: "success"`), the one chip that would have told the company this tender has no functionality hurdle to clear at all.

**Fix.** Widened the character class between "functionality" and "N/A" from `\s*\n?\s*` (whitespace only) to `\W{0,3}` (up to 3 non-word characters - covers the real colon, and the dash/slash a buyer's own "<label>: N/A"-style formatting could equally use, same short, bounded allowance this file's own other regexes use elsewhere) - still anchored to the literal words "functionality" and "N/A" immediately around it, so it can't drift onto an unrelated sentence. Confirmed this still matches the original synthetic newline-separated test string unchanged, plus the real DPWI quote, a plain colon, and a dash variant.

**Verified red-then-green.** Added `test_the_real_dpwi_na_wording_is_actually_recognised()` to `engine/discovery/test_score_outlook_functionality.py`, checking both the regex directly against the real quoted evidence and `_functionality()`'s own returned `present` value. **RED** (before the fix, real exit code captured directly): `python3 test_score_outlook_functionality.py` -> `2 failure(s)`, exit `1` - both new checks failed exactly as predicted (`FUNCTIONALITY_NA_RE` not matching; `present` reading `None` instead of `False`), every pre-existing check in the file still passing. **GREEN** (after the fix): same command -> `0 failure(s)`, exit `0`, 16/16 (14 pre-existing + 2 new).

**Full regression.** `python3 engine/discovery/test_score_outlook.py` - `0 failure(s)`, all pre-existing checks (including Findings 340/343/381/384's own dedicated cases) unaffected - this fix touches no code either of those tests exercise. `python3 engine/discovery/test_assess_tender.py` and `python3 engine/discovery/test_opportunity_requirements.py` (the two closest siblings that also read `score_outlook`-adjacent text) - both clean. `python3 -m py_compile engine/discovery/score_outlook.py engine/discovery/test_score_outlook_functionality.py` - clean. `ruff check` on both touched files - **2** findings both BEFORE and AFTER this fix (confirmed by re-running against the pre-fix regex): the exact same 2 pre-existing, unrelated violations Finding 381's own write-up for this file already documented (an `f`-string-without-placeholder at `score_outlook.py` line ~932, and a now-genuinely-unused `# noqa: E402` on the test file's own existing import line) - no new rule violation introduced by this change.

**Why pushed directly to `main`, not a PR.** No RLS, no money/payment path, no hard-stop/disqualification gate - `functionality.present`/`threshold` feed only an informational Discovery-page chip and summary sentence (confirmed by reading every consumer: `scoreOutlookChips.ts` and `estimate_score_outlook()`'s own `summary` list), never any pass/fail or disqualification computation. No worker-image/deployment change, no migration/schema surface - one Python engine file plus its own test file, zero SQL, zero TypeScript. `engine/discovery/score_outlook.py` is not one of the six files this track's own guardrail names as requiring a PR for a correctness fix. Not a correctness fix to any document a company signs or submits - no filler anywhere reads `_functionality()`'s output. Not anything `pack-review.tsx`/`submission-pack.tsx` imports from, even transitively - same reasoning Findings 381/384 already established for this exact file: it is pure Python, reached only via a separate, already-run Discovery pipeline, with `scoreOutlookChips.ts` (a Discovery-page-only file) as the real TypeScript-side consumer.

**Mandatory open-PR cross-check, by the exact filenames touched (`engine/discovery/score_outlook.py`, `engine/discovery/test_score_outlook_functionality.py`).** Listed all **61** open PRs (`#164`/`#165`/`#176`-`#213`/`#215`-`#235`, confirmed live via the GitHub MCP tools immediately before starting this pass - the identical set Findings 381/382/383/384 each already confirmed, unchanged since) and checked every title/head-branch for `score_outlook`/`functionality`/`discovery`/`bbbee` - zero hits (same zero-hit result the prior three `score_outlook.py` findings this pass already established for this file). `git fetch origin main` immediately before starting this pass and again immediately before this push both showed `main` unchanged at `5bf645c` (Finding 384's own commit) - no sibling-track commit landed in either gap.

**Backlog status.** No new standing item needed - a self-contained, now-fixed extraction bug, not a judgment call for Sarel. Standing item 23's open-PR count unchanged at 61 (no PR opened).

**Numbering note.** Re-verified live, twice: once before drafting (`main`'s own last real `QA-Edge-Case-Findings.md` entry is **384**; all 61 open PRs re-checked for a claim on 385+, none found) and again immediately before this push (`main` still at `5bf645c`, all 61 open PRs re-checked again, still no claim on 385+) - **385** confirmed next-free both times, no collision.

To verify independently: `cd engine/discovery && python3 test_score_outlook_functionality.py` (expect 16/16 checks pass, exit 0). Run `python3 -c "import score_outlook as so; print(so.FUNCTIONALITY_NA_RE.search('Scoring quality / functionality: N/A'))"` from `engine/discovery/` before and after `git show 5bf645c:engine/discovery/score_outlook.py`'s own prior copy to see the match go from `None` to a real `Match` object. `python3 engine/discovery/test_score_outlook.py` (0 failures, unaffected).

### Finding 387 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, pushed directly to `main`): `lib/trialLifecycle.ts`'s `trialDay7Candidates()` was the one candidate function in the file with no retry safety at all - an EXACT calendar-day match (`daysUntil(trial_ends_at) === 7`), unlike its own two true siblings in the same file, both deliberately RANGE-based for exactly this reason

**Where:** `app/lib/trialLifecycle.ts`, `trialDay7Candidates()` (and its own `TRIAL_DAY_7_AT_DAYS_LEFT` constant); the copy in `app/lib/emailTemplatesTier0.ts`'s `trialDay7MilestoneEmail()` that the fix required updating; the stale comment in `app/scripts/send-onboarding-nudges.ts`'s `lifecycleRecipients()` docstring that named this exact-match shape as a "worst case" without ever fixing it.

**How this was found.** Candidate angle 4 (precedent comparison - two structurally similar code paths treated inconsistently), applied inside a single file rather than across files. `lib/trialLifecycle.ts` holds exactly 3 candidate-selection functions, all for the same `company_subscriptions` row, all consumed by the same sender script (`scripts/send-onboarding-nudges.ts`) through the same one-time idempotency-claim mechanism (`lib/notificationEngine.ts`'s `sendNotification()`, migration 0092/0093's `notification_claims`): `trialDay7Candidates()`, `trialExpiringCandidates()`, `trialExpiredCandidates()`. Reading all three side by side: `trialExpiringCandidates()` matches a 48-hour RANGE (`hoursLeft > 0 && hoursLeft <= 48`) and `trialExpiredCandidates()` matches an open-ended RANGE from expiry onward (`<= now`) - both documented, both self-healing on a missed run, since the one-time claim (not the candidate function) is what actually prevents a double-send. `trialDay7Candidates()` alone used `daysUntilFn(s.trial_ends_at) === TRIAL_DAY_7_AT_DAYS_LEFT` - an exact match, true on exactly one calendar day per company, ever.

**This had already been named in passing, three times, but never itself investigated or fixed.** `docs/specs/System-Status.md` (2026-11-09, Finding 348's own write-up) and `docs/specs/QA-Edge-Case-Findings.md` (Finding 162, 2026-11-07) both already call out this exact-match shape as the "worst case" consequence of two OTHER bugs they were fixing (a PostgREST 1000-row pagination gap; a discarded RPC error with no logging) - each time as a side note about what a company would lose if that other bug's own failure mode hit on exactly the one qualifying day. Neither pass investigated whether the exact-match shape itself could be safely widened, or why it differs from its own two true siblings in the same file. The real, independent risk this pass investigated and confirmed: the whole GitHub Actions cron run for `.github/workflows/onboarding-nudges.yml` simply not firing (or firing late) on the one qualifying day needs no code bug anywhere else at all - scheduled GitHub Actions workflows are documented to occasionally skip or run late under platform load - and this file's own two true siblings are already built to survive exactly that; this one function was not.

**Confirmed the real idempotency mechanism makes this safe to widen with no change to send frequency.** Read `scripts/send-onboarding-nudges.ts`'s `runTrialDay7()`: its idempotency key for this notification is `` `trial-day-7-${sub.company_id}-${userId}` `` - no day, threshold or run-date component at all, exactly the same shape `runTrialExpiring48h()`/`runTrialExpired()` already use for their own, already-range-based candidates. `claim_notification()` (migration 0092) is a one-time-ever claim per key - so widening `trialDay7Candidates()` to a range changes nothing about how many times a company is actually emailed (still exactly once, ever, per the claim), only whether a missed run can catch up on a later one.

**The one real complication, found by reading the consumer, not assumed.** `trialDay7MilestoneEmail()` (`lib/emailTemplatesTier0.ts`) hardcodes the literal day count into its own copy - the pill reads `"TRIAL - DAY 7"`, the subject reads `"You're halfway through your trial..."`, and the plain-text body reads `"...trial, day 7: ..."`. A naive range-widening (match any day `<= 7`) would make this exact same, unchanged copy send on day 6, day 5, day 3, etc. too - correct for catching up a missed run, but now making a factually wrong claim ("DAY 7") on every day of the window except the first. This is why a mechanical "just change `===` to `<=`" fix is not actually safe on its own, and is presumably the reason this was flagged three times but never fixed.

**Fix.** Two parts, both needed together: (1) `trialDay7Candidates()` now matches a bounded range, `left <= TRIAL_DAY_7_AT_DAYS_LEFT && left > TRIAL_DAY_7_FLOOR_DAYS_LEFT` (new constant, `2`) - floored just above `trialExpiringCandidates()`'s own 48-hour window so the two never compete for the same day, the same non-overlapping-windows shape the other two candidates already establish between themselves. (2) `trialDay7MilestoneEmail()`'s copy no longer claims a specific day: the pill is now `"TRIAL CHECK-IN"`, the subject `"Here's what you've built in your trial so far"`, and the text body drops `", day 7"` - still naming the two real facts the email always existed to show (packs built so far, the real trial-end date), just never a specific elapsed-day claim that could be wrong once the function can genuinely fire on more than one day. Also corrected the now-stale comment in `send-onboarding-nudges.ts`'s `lifecycleRecipients()` docstring, which named the old exact-match shape as an open "worst case" - it now says plainly that this particular consequence no longer applies, with a pointer to this fix.

**Verified red-then-green, not asserted from reading alone.** Added 4 new cases to `app/lib/trialLifecycle.spec.ts` (`vitest`) and corrected the one pre-existing case that encoded the old bug as expected behaviour (`"off-threshold day counts yield nothing"` asserted `daysLeft === 6` returns `[]` - that assertion was the bug, re-split into "does not fire before day 7" (`8` -> `[]`, unchanged) and the new retry-safety cases). **RED** (`git stash push -- lib/trialLifecycle.ts` to isolate the pre-fix implementation with the new spec file already in place, `npx vitest run lib/trialLifecycle.spec.ts`): **1 failed, 11 passed** - exactly the predicted new "still fires on any day between the 7-day mark and the 48h handoff" case, `expected [] to deeply equal [{...}]`. **GREEN** (`git stash pop` to restore the fix, same command): **12/12 passed**.

**Full regression.** `npx vitest run` (whole `app/` suite) - **84 files, 688 tests, all passed**, including `scripts/send-onboarding-nudges.spec.ts` (8/8, unaffected - it mocks `trialDay7Candidates()`'s own callers, not this function's internals) and `lib/deadlineReminders.spec.ts`/`lib/complianceExpiryReminders.spec.ts`/`lib/briefingReminders.spec.ts` (the other exact-day-match-by-design reminder families named in this file's own header comments - confirmed unaffected, their own exact-match shapes are a deliberate, separate design this fix does not touch). The `*.test.ts` node loop (`find . -name "*.test.ts" -not -path "*/node_modules/*"`, each run via `node --experimental-strip-types`, real exit codes) - **32 files, 0 failures**, unaffected (this fix touches no `.test.ts` file). `npx tsc --noEmit` (after `npx next build` first, per this track's own standing LayoutProps gotcha) - **0 errors**. `npx eslint .` - **0 errors, the same 3 pre-existing warnings** (`Logo.tsx`'s two `<img>` warnings, `analytics/page.tsx`'s unused `STAGE_META`), confirmed unchanged. `node --experimental-strip-types scripts/render-email-samples.ts` re-run clean, confirming the new copy renders without error (`00-trial-day-7-milestone.html`, subject now `"Here's what you've built in your trial so far"`).
