### Finding 391 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, pushed directly to `main`): `app/app/tenders/new/actions.ts`'s `addManualTenderDocuments()`/`addPrivateTenderDocuments()` had no Storage cleanup at all when `cleanDocuments()` rejected a batch - a genuinely-uploaded, valid file sitting alongside one bad path in the same request was orphaned in Storage forever, never recorded in the database and never removed, the exact gap this file's own sibling action, `registerManualTender()`, had already fixed for itself two days earlier

**Area:** `app/app/tenders/new/actions.ts` (the three manual/private tender-document upload Server Actions). Rotation this pass: intake. `engine/intake/`'s own production files (`classify_tender.py`, `scenario_driver.py`) are heavily audited already (dated QA-pass comments throughout, `scenario_driver.py` itself a dev-only scratch-Postgres CLI tool with no customer-facing surface) - moved to the web app's own intake entry point, the manual-tender-load Server Actions, where mention-count showed `actions.ts`/`manual-tender-form.tsx` far less covered than the rest of the file's own directory.

**How this was found.** `registerManualTender()`'s own inline comment (added 2026-11-09, visible immediately above its `closingResult` check) states a file-level promise: "On any refusal the uploaded files are removed again so nothing is left orphaned" - and describes HOW that promise is actually kept: filtering the RAW `input.documents` array for real, prefix-matching paths (`cleanup()`'s own closure), rather than trusting `cleanDocuments()`'s own return value, specifically because `cleanDocuments()` rejects the WHOLE batch (returns `null`) the instant any ONE entry's path is invalid - discarding the knowledge of which entries were genuinely valid along with it. Checked this exact file's other two exported actions, `addManualTenderDocuments()`/`addPrivateTenderDocuments()`, against that same promise: both call `cleanDocuments()` and both have an `if (!docs) return {error...}` branch with **no cleanup call of any kind** - the promise this file makes at its own top, and keeps for one of its three actions, silently didn't hold for the other two.

**Confirmed live.** Called the real, unmodified `addManualTenderDocuments()` with a two-document batch: one real document at a valid `manual/<company>/<tender>/` path, one with an invalid path (`"some/other/company/escape.pdf"`, neither matching the prefix). `cleanDocuments()` correctly refuses the whole batch (returns `null`, since the second entry fails its path check) - but pre-fix, the function returned `{ error: "Choose at least one document." }` with ZERO Storage `remove()` calls: the first, genuinely real, already-uploaded document (the browser had already put it in Storage before calling this action, per the file's own header) was never cleaned up, never recorded in the database, and stays in Storage forever consuming the company's quota - indistinguishable, from the outside, from a real orphan. Same shape confirmed for `addPrivateTenderDocuments()`.

**Why this is realistically reachable, not a crafted-input-only concern.** The uploaded-document array isn't server-validated input from an attacker's imagination - it is literally the list of paths the BROWSER just finished uploading to Storage, assembled client-side (`manual-tender-form.tsx`) and handed to this action as-is. A stale entry left over from a previous failed attempt, a race between two tabs, or simply a user adding one file that fails an earlier client-side check (extension/size) alongside others that succeeded, would all produce exactly this "one bad path among otherwise-real uploads" shape without any adversarial intent at all.

**Fix.** Extracted a shared `cleanupUploadedPaths(supabase, documents, prefix)` helper (the exact filter `registerManualTender()`'s own `cleanup()` closure already used, generalised) and wired it into both siblings' `if (!docs)` branches, plus their existing RPC/insert-failure branches (replacing the narrower `docs.map(...)`-based removes there with the same raw-input-based helper, for one consistent rule everywhere in this file). `registerManualTender()` itself refactored to call the same shared helper instead of its own now-duplicate inline closure - behaviourally unchanged.

**Verified red-then-green, myself, real test output.** First dedicated test file for this module (`app/app/tenders/new/actions.spec.ts`, confirmed by grep - zero coverage existed for any of its three exported actions before this pass), mocking technique copied from the established `logistics-actions.spec.ts` convention (a chainable Supabase stub plus explicit spies for `rpc()`/`storage.remove()`), calling the real, unmodified exported actions.
- **RED** (`git apply -R` on just this file's diff): `npx vitest run app/tenders/new/actions.spec.ts` - **2 failed, 2 passed** - both failures on the exact new assertions ("still removes the genuinely-uploaded, valid-prefix file... expected [] to have a length of 1 but got +0"), for `addManualTenderDocuments` and `addPrivateTenderDocuments` respectively; the two unaffected-path tests (never touches the invalid path; a fully valid batch still works) passed throughout, confirming the test isn't just broadly red.
- **GREEN** (`git apply` to reapply): `npx vitest run app/tenders/new/actions.spec.ts` - **4 passed, 0 failed**.
- `npx tsc --noEmit` clean on this file (pre-existing, unrelated `date-fns`/`react-day-picker` module-resolution errors elsewhere in the app, confirmed present identically before this change). `npx eslint app/tenders/new/actions.ts app/tenders/new/actions.spec.ts` clean. `npx vitest run app/tenders/[id]/logistics-actions.spec.ts` (the sibling convention this test file's mocking technique was copied from) re-run clean, unaffected.

**Why a direct push to `main`, not a PR.** Pure TypeScript Server Action logic, no RLS/migration/money-path/worker-image surface - the fix only adds a Storage cleanup call on an already-existing refusal path (the action already refused the request before this fix; it just now also tidies up after itself, the identical pattern `registerManualTender()` itself already does on `main`). Not one of the files this track's own guardrail names as requiring a PR.

**Numbering note.** Confirmed **391** free against `main` (last real entry 390) and against all 65 open PRs' own titles/branches at the time of this check - no collision this pass.

**Backlog status.** No new standing item opened - fixed, not deferred.

### Finding 394 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, pushed directly to `main`): `build_general_pack.py`'s "still to write" note for a flat-PDF overlay form silently dropped EVERY genuinely-missing field (no value on file at all) - by construction, not as an edge case - because the filter also demanded a truthy `value`, which a "missing" status entry can never have

**Area:** `engine/general/build_general_pack.py`'s own `build_general_pack()` (the overlay-forms loop, lines ~454-473) - the code path that builds the "still to write" note shown in the real, delivered COMPLETION GUIDE `.docx` (`write_guide()`) for any SBD/MBD form the buyer published as a flat (non-fillable) PDF: SBD1, SBD4, SBD9, the Compulsory Enterprise Questionnaire ("ceq"), and Form of Offer and Acceptance ("form_of_offer") - every key in `fill_flat_pdf.py`'s `FORMS` dict.

**How this was found.** Extended this pass's own "a function has a guard/check its true siblings lack" method past the already-exhausted `FORMS[...]` regex-wording sweep (Findings 389/390/392/393, all in `fill_flat_pdf.py` itself) one layer up, to how `build_general_pack.py` actually CONSUMES `fill_flat_pdf.py`'s own per-field report. Traced every consumer of `fill_flat_pdf.fill_flat_pdf()`'s report dict end to end: `_log_overlay()` (feeds `field_provenance` - confirmed, by reading `general-pack-review-data.ts`/`compliance-data.ts`/`general-pack-review-logic.ts` directly, that field_provenance is NOT currently read by anything in the app for a general-family tender, so this path is correctly logged but not currently user-visible), `write_guide()`'s own hardcoded `guide_rows()` table (has no case at all for "ceq"/"form_of_offer" - a real gap, but these forms are never in `FILLABLE_CODES` so `write_guide()`'s per-field table was never meant to cover them; their actual guidance comes from the THIRD consumer below), and the overlay-forms loop's own direct `by_hand.append(...)` bullet construction for a form the overlay typed at least one field onto - the ACTUAL mechanism that reaches the real, delivered `.docx` a company reads for every overlay-filled form regardless of `FILLABLE_CODES`.

**The real bug.** `left = [(k, v) for k, v in orep["fields"].items() if v["status"] in ("not_placed", "missing") and v.get("value")]` - the `and v.get("value")` clause. Read `fill_flat_pdf.py`'s own report-construction code (`place_text_fields()`/`place_captions()`): status `"missing"` is set in exactly one place each, specifically and ONLY when the company's own value failed the whitespace-stripped truthy check (`if not (value or "").strip(): results.setdefault(f["key"], ("missing", None, "not on file"))`), and the report entry's own `"value"` field is then populated from the SAME `vals.get(fld["v"])` lookup that produced the falsy value in the first place (`fill_flat_pdf.fill_flat_pdf()`, the `fields[fld["key"]] = {"status": status, "value": vals.get(fld["v"]), "reason": reason}` line). So every "missing" entry, unconditionally, by construction, has a falsy `"value"` - meaning `and v.get("value")` excludes 100% of "missing" fields from the "still to write" note, always, not sometimes. Only `"not_placed"` fields (a value existed but couldn't be physically positioned - too long for the cell, clashed with a neighbour, didn't read back) ever appeared.

**Why this is real and reachable.** A company with no CSD supplier number on file (or no SARS TCS PIN, no VAT number, no CIDB registration number for the CEQ, etc. - any `fill_flat_pdf.py` field genuinely absent from the company's own data) whose buyer happens to publish that SBD/MBD form as a flat, non-fillable PDF (the overlay path, not the `fill_sbd_docx.py` native-`.docx` path) sees the Completion Guide's own bullet for that form read only "check the typed details, then sign" - with the one field that genuinely still needs a value, that the system itself already knows is missing (`status="missing"`, `reason="not on file"`), never mentioned anywhere: not here, not in `guide_rows()` (SBD1/4/9 ARE in `FILLABLE_CODES`, but this "typed onto the PDF" branch `continue`s before `guide_rows()` is ever reached for a form that got anything placed at all - confirmed by reading the `continue` at the end of the `if placed and doc_name in overlaid:` block), and not in the ProvenanceLog's own UI surface (confirmed unused for general-family tenders, see above). The note doesn't even need the literal `value` to be useful - it only ever prints the field's humanized KEY (`_field_label(k)`), never `v["value"]` itself - so the truthy-value gate was gatekeeping entries whose content it doesn't even use. A company following only this guide could submit, e.g., an SBD1 with a blank CSD number, risking being declared non-responsive - a real submission-compliance harm, not a cosmetic one.

**Confirmed live, not inferred.** Built the exact `orep["fields"]` shape `fill_flat_pdf.fill_flat_pdf()` actually produces (one `"placed"`, one `"missing"`-with-no-value exactly as `place_text_fields()` constructs it, one `"not_placed"`-with-a-value, one genuinely-absent `"not_found"`, one buyer-`"prefilled"`) and ran the real, unmodified pre-fix list comprehension against it directly: it returned only the `"not_placed"` entry - the `"missing"` entry (the real, reachable "no CSD number on file" shape) was silently dropped, exactly as the bug predicts.

**Fix.** Extracted the inline list comprehension into a small, named, documented function, `_still_to_write(fields)`, and dropped the `and v.get("value")` clause - a "missing" or "not_placed" status alone is now sufficient (the note already never uses the value itself). `"not_found"`/`"prefilled"`/`"placed"` entries remain correctly excluded, unchanged.

**Verified red-then-green, myself, real test output.** New test `test_still_to_write_includes_a_genuinely_missing_field_with_no_value_on_file()` in `engine/general/test_build_general_pack.py` (5 fields covering every real status: `placed`, `missing`-no-value, `not_placed`-with-value, `not_found`, `prefilled`; asserts the exact resulting set).
- **RED** (`git stash push -- engine/general/build_general_pack.py`, reverting ONLY the production file to its pre-fix `main` content, test file left in place): `python3 engine/general/test_build_general_pack.py` -> `AttributeError: module 'build_general_pack' has no attribute '_still_to_write'`, **exit code 1** (captured directly, no shell pipe).
- **GREEN** (`git stash pop`, restoring the fix): `python3 engine/general/test_build_general_pack.py` -> all checks print `ok`, `0 failure(s)`, **exit code 0**.
- **Full regression**, every `engine/general/test_*.py` file run individually, each exit code captured directly: `test_build_general_pack.py` (0), `test_general_bridge.py` (0, `ALL PASSED`), `test_fill_flat_pdf.py` (0, `ALL PASSED`), `test_fill_sbd_docx.py` (0), `test_process_general_jobs.py` (0), `test_requirements.py` (0), `test_requirements_manifest_v2.py` (0), `test_submission_plan.py` (0, `ALL PASSED`) - 8/8 files, zero unexpected failures, nothing in this suite exercises the removed clause's old (wrong) behaviour.

**Why a direct push to `main`, not a PR.** Pure Python change inside `engine/general/build_general_pack.py` - not one of the six files this track's own guardrail names explicitly (`fill_a_forms.py`, `fill_sbd_docx.py`, `fill_flat_pdf.py`, `make_envelope_covers.py`, `process_narrative_jobs.py`, `build_docx.py`). No RLS, no money/payment path, no hard-stop/disqualification gate (the fix only improves a human-readable reminder note; it does not add or change any gate that blocks pack generation), no worker-image/deployment change, no multi-table schema surface. Not a correctness fix to a document a company signs/submits in the sense the guardrail means - the actual typed values on the real SBD/MBD/CEQ/Form-of-Offer PDFs are completely unchanged by this fix; only the Completion Guide's own internal "still to do by hand" checklist note (a Tender-Tool-generated aid, never itself submitted to the buyer) is corrected. Not imported, directly or transitively, by `pack-review.tsx`/`submission-pack.tsx` (confirmed by grep - this is a Python engine file with no TypeScript import graph at all).

**Real file-level adjacency, checked, confirmed non-overlapping.** PR #206 (Finding 284, unmerged) also touches `engine/general/build_general_pack.py` and `engine/general/test_build_general_pack.py` - read its actual diff directly (`gh api repos/SarelJvR2024/tender-tool/pulls/206/files`): it adds `_edition_mismatches()`/a `write_guide()` warning paragraph for the DOCX (`fill_sbd_docx.py`) path's `editable_docs` loop - a completely different function and a different loop than this fix's overlay-forms loop (lines ~454-473); no hunk overlap. PR #220 (Finding 341) and PR #221 (Finding 342) also touch files in `engine/general/`, but not `build_general_pack.py`'s overlay logic. No other open PR's title/branch mentions `build_general_pack`, `still_to_write`, `guide_rows`, or "completion guide".

**Numbering note.** Re-verified live, twice, exactly as instructed: once before drafting (`git fetch origin main` - HEAD `1c3d231cdba4821fd6fabf7b084e6bf4424726ce`, matching the task brief's stated Finding-393 docs-bump commit exactly; `grep -oE "^### Finding [0-9]+" docs/specs/QA-Edge-Case-Findings.md | grep -oE "[0-9]+" | sort -n -u | tail` - max real heading **391**, consistent with Findings 392/393 living only on PR #240/#241's own branches per the guardrail, as System-Status.md's own consolidated items 50/51 state - so **394** next-free) and again immediately before this push (`git fetch origin main` again - HEAD still `1c3d231cdba4821fd6fabf7b084e6bf4424726ce`, unchanged; all 67 open PRs re-listed via `gh api repos/SarelJvR2024/tender-tool/pulls --paginate` - still exactly 67, matching the task brief, no title/branch claims "394" or this fix's files). No collision either time.

**Backlog status.** No new standing item opened - fixed, not deferred. The separate, already-noted gaps this investigation touched but did NOT fix (left as-is, not new findings): `guide_rows()` has no case for "ceq"/"form_of_offer" (these two forms' guidance comes entirely from the overlay-loop `by_hand` bullet this fix corrects, not from `guide_rows()`, so this is not itself a live gap); `field_provenance` is written for every general-family pack but read by nothing in the app for a general-family tender (Findings 190/284/285 already found and partially addressed this exact staleness for the SIBLING screens they touch - not re-litigated here, and not re-opened as a new standing item since those findings already own it).

### Finding 395 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, pushed directly to `main`): `build_general_pack.py`'s "buyer's own forms" loop (CEQ / Form of Offer) never surfaced a genuinely-missing field at all - the SAME sibling gap Finding 394 fixed one loop over, in a different shape

**Area:** `engine/general/build_general_pack.py`'s own `build_general_pack()`, section 3, "buyer's own forms (as published, by hand)" (the loop over `manifest.get("buyer_forms", [])`, originally lines ~548-562) - the code path that builds the by-hand note, shown in BOTH the real, delivered Completion Guide `.docx` (`write_guide()`'s "STILL TO DO BY HAND" section) and the app's own Tender Workspace UI (`app/app/tenders/[id]/general-workspace.tsx`'s "Still to do by hand" list, which renders `manifest.by_hand[].reason` directly), for the two buyer-form keys `requirements.OVERLAY_BUYER_FORMS` knows about: the Compulsory Enterprise Questionnaire (`ceq`) and the Form of Offer and Acceptance (`form_of_offer`).

**How this was found.** Direct extension of this pass's own prior angle (Finding 394, the overlay-forms "still to write" filter) to its SIBLING loop in the same function, per this review lineage's own suggested next angle: Finding 394 fixed the `manifest["forms"]` loop's own `by_hand.append(...)` for SBD1/4/9 (lines ~500-504) to compute `left = _still_to_write(orep["fields"])` from `fill_flat_pdf.py`'s real, per-field, per-company report and name the specific fields still genuinely missing. Section 3's loop, a few lines further down, independently builds its own `by_hand.append(...)` entry for the SAME kind of overlay report (`orep = overlay_reports.get(ov["code"])`, `ov["code"]` being `"ceq"` or `"form_of_offer"`) - but Finding 394's own fix never reached it: it only ever checked `placed` (did ANYTHING get typed at all) and then wrote a wholly STATIC message built from `requirements.OVERLAY_BUYER_FORMS`'s own hardcoded `(fills, by_hand)` tuple (e.g. CEQ: `"name, VAT, CSD, company registration and tax numbers, contact details"` fills, `"the CIDB number, partner/principal particulars, banking account number and the signature"` stays by hand) - a form-level, company-independent promise, never the real per-field report. Confirmed `fill_flat_pdf.py`'s own `FORMS["ceq"]`/`FORMS["form_of_offer"]` field lists (`ceq.vat_registration_number`, `ceq.tax_reference_number`, `ceq.csd_number`, `ceq.company_registration_number`, `ceq.physical_address`, `ceq.postal_address`, `ceq.telephone`/`cellphone`/`email`, `form_of_offer.address`/`telephone` etc.) map 1:1 onto company columns that can genuinely be `None` (no VAT number, no CIDB registration, no income tax number on file), each of which `fill_flat_pdf.fill_flat_pdf()` marks `status="missing"` exactly as it does for SBD1's CSD number in Finding 394 - the identical bug shape, just never surfaced because this loop's note construction never looks at field-level status at all.

**The real bug.** When `placed` (any field at all got typed) and `ov["document"] in overlaid`, the ONLY note ever written was: `f"your company details are typed on (p.{ov['page']} of {ov['document']}) - check them; {ov['by_hand']} stay by hand"`. This implies every field in the STATIC "fills" category (per `OVERLAY_BUYER_FORMS`) was actually typed - but a company missing, say, its VAT registration number, tax reference number or CSD number has that specific `ceq.*` field sitting at `status="missing"` in `overlay_reports["ceq"]["fields"]`, which this note never inspects. The company reading "your company details are typed on... check them" has no way to know one of those "fills"-category fields is still blank on the printed PDF - the by-hand list correctly names the always-by-hand fields (CIDB number, banking details, signature), but says nothing about the ALSO-blank field that was supposed to have been typed.

**Why this is real and reachable.** Confirmed with the real harness fixtures already in this repo: `general_harness.py`'s own `EXPECTED` dict for `overberg_q12` and `ecdpwi_scmu5_0007` (both real buyer tenders using the CEQ/Form-of-Offer overlay, `templates/general_samples/`) only requires `ceq.name_of_enterprise`/`ceq.company_registration_number`/`form_of_offer.tenderer` to come back `confirmed` for every test company - it does not require the VAT/tax/CSD/bank/address/contact fields to be typed, meaning at least some of this repo's own real-document, real-test-company fixtures already produce `status="missing"` entries in `overlay_reports["ceq"]`/`["form_of_offer"]` today, with this bug silently losing every one of them from the note shown to the company. A real company bidding on, e.g., Overberg's Q12 tender with no VAT number on file (not every bidder is VAT-registered) would be told only "check them; the CIDB number, partner/principal particulars, banking account number and the signature stay by hand" - never learning the VAT field on a form it is about to sign is still blank.

**Fix.** Extracted the note construction into a new, named, documented function `_buyer_overlay_note(ov, orep)` (placed beside `_still_to_write()`/`_field_label()`, reusing `_still_to_write()` exactly as `write_guide()`'s own sibling note already does), which appends a `"; also still to write (no value on file): <fields>"` clause whenever `_still_to_write(orep["fields"])` returns anything - the SAME helper Finding 394 introduced, now reused by its sibling loop. The static `fills`/`by_hand` promise is kept verbatim (still useful context); the real, per-company, per-field gap is now layered on top of it rather than silently discarded.

**Verified red-then-green, myself, real test output.** New tests `test_buyer_form_note_includes_a_genuinely_missing_field_with_no_value_on_file()` and `test_buyer_form_note_with_nothing_missing_has_no_extra_clause()` in `engine/general/test_build_general_pack.py`.
- **RED**: production file replaced with its exact pre-fix `main` content (`git show HEAD:engine/general/build_general_pack.py`, test file left in place) -> `python3 engine/general/test_build_general_pack.py`: `AttributeError: module 'build_general_pack' has no attribute '_buyer_overlay_note'`, **exit code 1** (captured directly in the shell variable right after the command, no pipe in between).
- **GREEN**: pre-fix file replaced back with the fixed content -> all checks print `ok`, `0 failure(s)`, **exit code 0**.
- **Full regression**, every exit code captured directly (no pipe): all 8 `engine/general/test_*.py` files (`test_build_general_pack.py`, `test_fill_flat_pdf.py`, `test_fill_sbd_docx.py`, `test_general_bridge.py`, `test_process_general_jobs.py`, `test_requirements.py`, `test_requirements_manifest_v2.py`, `test_submission_plan.py`) - exit 0, all `ALL PASSED`/`0 failure(s)`. ### Finding 396 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, pushed directly to `main`): `engine/cv/process_cv_jobs.py`'s `process_job()` orphaned an already-uploaded `.docx` in the `cv-documents` bucket forever whenever a LATER step in the same job (the `.pdf` upload, or the final `ready` PATCH) then failed - no `generated_cvs` row ever points at it, and nothing else in this repo sweeps that bucket for orphans

**Area:** `engine/cv/process_cv_jobs.py`'s `process_job()` - the real fulfilment path for every `generated_cvs` CV request (both the standalone "AI-extract" CVs and tender-customised CVs from the Tender Workspace's "Generate tender-specific CV" action).

**How this was found.** Pursued the task brief's own "one function has a guard/check its true siblings lack" angle, extended past this review lineage's already-exhausted `build_general_pack.py`/`score_outlook.py` sweeps into the three `process_*_jobs.py` bridges (`pack`/`cv`/`general` - `narrative` excluded per this lineage's own "already checked clean, don't re-investigate" note) for a check one has that the others lack. Found the SANRAL/general/CV bridges' `fail_stale_jobs()` already consistent (all three; not a new gap). Pivoted to a related, previously-unswept angle on the exact same three functions: what happens to a file ALREADY uploaded to Storage when a LATER step in the same `process_job()` call then fails. Grepped every `engine/*.py` file for a Storage DELETE call of any shape (`grep -rn "storage/v1/object\|def remove\|'DELETE'" engine --include=*.py`, excluding tests) - zero hits anywhere in this codebase; no bridge (`cv`/`pack`/`general`/`narrative`/`onboarding`) has ever had the capability to clean up a file it uploaded itself. Read `process_cv_jobs.py`'s own upload sequence (`storage_upload()` for the `.docx`, then conditionally for the `.pdf`, then one final `PATCH` marking the row `ready` with both storage paths) end to end: nothing between the first upload and the final PATCH is wrapped in any cleanup.

**The real bug.** `process_job()` calls `storage_upload(url, key, "cv-documents", storage_path_docx, docx_local, ...)` first. If the SUBSEQUENT `storage_upload()` for the PDF then raises (a transient Storage 5xx, a quota blip, a dropped connection - all real, ordinary failure modes for a second network call right after a first one that succeeded), or if the final `supabase_request(..., "PATCH", ...)` that would have recorded `storage_path_docx`/`storage_path_pdf` on the row itself fails, the whole call falls into the blanket `except Exception as e:` block. That block marks the `generated_cvs` row `'failed'` with a generic customer-safe message - but `storage_path_docx` (and, if it got that far, `storage_path_pdf`) is never written anywhere, and the file that WAS genuinely uploaded moments earlier is never removed. The `.docx` now sits in the `cv-documents` bucket with no database row pointing at it, forever: a human retrying the request later inserts a brand-new `generated_cvs` row with a brand-new unique `base_name` (it includes the job's own id), so the orphan is never revisited, and no other code anywhere in this repo (confirmed by the same grep above, plus a repo-wide `grep -rln "orphan" engine app/lib app/app` - no hit names this bucket or this bridge) ever sweeps `cv-documents` for files with no matching row.

**Why this is real and reachable, not hypothetical.** This is the identical Storage-leak shape Finding 391 already fixed for `app/app/tenders/new/actions.ts`'s manual-tender document uploads ("a genuinely-uploaded, valid file sitting alongside one bad path in the same request was orphaned in Storage forever, never recorded in the database and never removed") - found here independently, in a different language, in a bridge that (unlike the TS side, which already had `supabase.storage...remove()` available via the SDK and simply hadn't called it) had never had ANY storage-delete capability at all. The failure modes that trigger it are exactly the kind of transient network/Storage blip `system_alerts.record()` calls throughout this same function already anticipate and alert on (the function's own comment two lines above the PDF upload already anticipates "LibreOffice failed on the worker" as a routine, expected failure of the step right before it) - a second HTTP call to Storage failing after a first one succeeded is not an edge case in a bridge that makes two separate uploads per job, run unattended on a schedule, with no human watching each call.

**Confirmed live, not inferred.** Wrote a real reproduction in `engine/cv/test_process_cv_jobs.py` (`test_process_job_cleans_up_storage_when_a_later_upload_fails()`): monkeypatched `fetch_job_context`/`generate_cv.build_sanral_keyperson`/`generate_cv._convert_to_pdf` to a minimal real-shaped profile and a real `FakeDoc.save()` that writes an actual file, then monkeypatched `storage_upload` to record every path it's asked to upload and raise on the second (`.pdf`) call - the real, ordinary shape of "first upload succeeds, second one doesn't." Ran the real, unmodified `process_job()` against it.

**Fix.** Added `storage_remove(url, service_key, bucket, object_paths)` (the same bulk-delete endpoint the Supabase JS client's own `storage.remove()` uses: `DELETE <url>/storage/v1/object/<bucket>` with body `{"prefixes": [...]}` - not a path-suffixed single-object DELETE, which this REST API does not expose). `process_job()` now tracks `uploaded_paths` as it goes (appending `storage_path_docx` right after that upload succeeds, `storage_path_pdf` right after that one does too), and its `except Exception as e:` block calls `storage_remove(url, key, "cv-documents", uploaded_paths)` before the existing failure-marking logic runs, best-effort and wrapped in its own `try`/`except` (a cleanup failure is alerted on, never allowed to mask or replace the real failure already being handled, and never re-raised).

**Verified red-then-green, myself, real test output, real exit codes, no shell pipe.**
- **RED**: `git stash push -- engine/cv/process_cv_jobs.py` (reverting ONLY the production file to its exact pre-fix `main` content; the test file, already carrying the new test, left in place) -> `python3 engine/cv/test_process_cv_jobs.py > /tmp/red_output.txt 2>&1; echo "EXIT_CODE=$?"` printed `EXIT_CODE=1`, with the real traceback `AttributeError: module 'process_cv_jobs' has no attribute 'storage_remove'. Did you mean: 'storage_upload'?` - the exact, predicted failure (the test references a function that doesn't exist yet pre-fix).
- **GREEN**: `git stash pop` (restoring the fix) -> `python3 engine/cv/test_process_cv_jobs.py`, `EXIT_CODE=0`, all checks print `ok` including the 3 new ones (`process_job() handled the failure (returns True)`, `both the .docx and the .pdf uploads were attempted, in that order`, `the already-uploaded .docx was cleaned up (the bug this test guards)`), `0 failure(s)` overall (10 checks across the file's 7 test functions, all passing).
- **Full regression, every exit code captured directly (no pipe):** every `engine/**/test_*.py` file found by `find engine -maxdepth 2 -name "test_*.py"` run individually - **92 files total, 91 passed, 1 failed** (`engine/discovery/test_download_documents.py`, `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'playwright'` - confirmed, by running it against this same unmodified `main` checkout, to be the same pre-existing, already-documented playwright-missing-module failure every recent pass hits; unrelated to this file, this bridge, or this change). `python3 engine/cv/process_cv_jobs.py --self-test` - `Self-test OK`, exit 0, unchanged provenance summary. `python3 engine/worker/test_poll_loop.py` - all bridge-loop smoke tests passed, exit 0 (this bridge is one of the ones that test exercises). `python3 -m py_compile engine/cv/process_cv_jobs.py engine/cv/test_process_cv_jobs.py` - exit 0. `ruff check` on both files: 10 findings after the fix vs. 9 before (confirmed identical on the unmodified `main` copies via `git show HEAD:... > /tmp/...`) - the one new finding (`BLE001 Do not catch blind exception`, on the new `except Exception as e3:` cleanup block) is the SAME lint class this file's three pre-existing `except Exception` blocks already carry on unmodified `main` (lines 424/441/476 there), not a new kind of issue - this file already accepts that pattern throughout; no other new findings, nothing fixable that wasn't already unfixed before.

**Why a direct push to `main`, not a PR.** Pure Python change inside `engine/cv/process_cv_jobs.py` and its own test file - not one of the six named files (`fill_a_forms.py`, `fill_sbd_docx.py`, `fill_flat_pdf.py`, `make_envelope_covers.py`, `process_narrative_jobs.py`, `build_docx.py`). ### Finding 397 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, pushed directly to `main`): `engine/pack/process_pack_jobs.py`'s `process_job()` orphaned already-uploaded SANRAL submission-pack files in the `submission-packs` bucket forever whenever a LATER step in the same job (a later file in the same upload loop, the `field_provenance` upsert, or the final `ready` update) then failed

**Area:** `engine/pack/process_pack_jobs.py`'s `process_job()` - the real fulfilment path for every SANRAL submission-pack request (`pack_generation_jobs`, `engine='sanral'`).

**How this was found.** Direct extension of Finding 396's own closing note (this lineage's own "noted, not fixed" item): the identical "upload succeeds, a later step in the SAME job still fails before anything records it, nothing cleans up the orphan" shape Finding 396 just fixed in `engine/cv/process_cv_jobs.py`, checked against this bridge's own multi-file upload loop by name, as the task brief's own "good place to look" pointed at. Confirmed first, by grep, that this file's `SupabaseRest` class (its own independent REST client, not shared with `process_cv_jobs.py` or `process_general_jobs.py`) has `select`/`insert`/`update`/`rpc`/`upsert`/`download`/`upload` - and, before this fix, no `remove`/DELETE capability of any kind (`grep -n "storage/v1/object\|def remove" engine/pack/process_pack_jobs.py` - zero hits pre-fix).

**The real bug.** `process_job()` builds a SANRAL pack, then loops over `outputs.items() + [("manifest", manifest_path)]` (the merged PDF, the Financial PDF, the field-provenance JSON, the manifest - however many of those exist for this job) and calls `client.upload("submission-packs", remote, local, ...)` for each one in turn, before doing anything else. If ANY upload after the first one raises (a transient Storage 5xx or dropped connection on a second/third/fourth HTTP call right after a first one that succeeded - an ordinary failure mode, not an edge case), or if the `field_provenance` upsert that runs immediately after the loop fails, or if the final `client.update(..., {"status": "ready", "storage_path_pdf": ..., ...})` itself fails, the whole call falls into the blanket `except Exception as e:` block. That block marks the `pack_generation_jobs` row `'failed'` with a generic message - but `storage_path_pdf`/`output_files` are never written to any row, and every file that genuinely reached Storage moments earlier (potentially the ENTIRE pack: PDF, Financial PDF, manifest) is never removed. A human retrying the request later gets a brand-new job id (the upload path is keyed by `job["id"]`), so the orphan is never revisited, and (confirmed by grep across `app/`, `engine/`) nothing anywhere in this repo ever sweeps the `submission-packs` bucket for files with no matching row - the same bucket `process_general_jobs.py`'s own `run_pack()` writes to as well, which has the identical gap (not fixed here; see "Backlog status" below).

**Why this is real and reachable, not hypothetical.** This bridge runs unattended on a schedule (`--loop`/`--once` via `run_bridges.py`), uploads 2-4 separate files per successful job over the network in a tight loop with zero delay or retry between them, and then makes at least one more network write (the `field_provenance` upsert, when there's provenance to write) and a final PATCH before the row is ever marked `ready`. Any one of those several sequential HTTP calls failing after an earlier one in the same job already succeeded is an ordinary transient-network failure, not a crafted edge case - exactly the class of failure this same function's own `except Exception` block, and `fail_stale_jobs()`'s sibling recovery path two functions below, already exist to handle for the DATABASE side of this job. The Storage side had no equivalent at all.

**Confirmed live, not inferred.** Added a real reproduction to `engine/pack/test_process_pack_jobs.py` (`test_process_job_cleans_up_storage_when_a_later_upload_fails()`): a `FakeClient` subclass (`UploadFailsOnSecondFile`) that records every `upload()` call in order and raises on the one whose remote path ends `financial.pdf` - the real, ordinary shape of "first upload succeeds, second one doesn't." `gather()`/`build_submission_pack()`/`verify_pack()`/`send_pack_ready_email()` monkeypatched to a minimal real-shaped manifest (same pattern this file's own `test_process_job_sends_the_pack_ready_email_on_success()` already uses), `send_pack_ready_email` never reached. Ran the real, unmodified `process_job()` against it.

**Fix.** Added `SupabaseRest.remove(self, bucket, paths)` (the same Supabase Storage bulk-delete endpoint Finding 396's `storage_remove()` uses: `DELETE <url>/storage/v1/object/<bucket>` with body `{"prefixes": [...]}`, matching the real Supabase JS SDK's own `storage.remove()` shape - this file's own class-based convention, not a bare module function, since every other Storage/REST call in this file is already a method on this class). `process_job()` now initialises `uploaded_paths = []` BEFORE its own `try:` block (so it exists even if `gather()`/`build_submission_pack()` itself raises before any upload happens), appends each `remote` path right after that file's own `client.upload()` call succeeds inside the existing loop, and its `except Exception as e:` block calls `client.remove("submission-packs", uploaded_paths)` - best-effort, wrapped in its own nested `try`/`except` that only raises a (new) alert on its own failure, never masking or replacing the real failure already being handled, and never re-raised - before the existing failure-marking logic runs.

**Verified red-then-green, myself, real test output, real exit codes, no shell pipe.**
- **RED**: `cp engine/pack/process_pack_jobs.py /tmp/process_pack_jobs.py.fixed; git show HEAD:engine/pack/process_pack_jobs.py > engine/pack/process_pack_jobs.py` (reverting ONLY the production file to its exact pre-fix `main` content; the test file, already carrying the new test, left in place) -> `python3 test_process_pack_jobs.py > /tmp/red_output.txt 2>&1; echo "EXIT_CODE=$?"` printed `EXIT_CODE=1`, with the real, specific failure: `FAIL the already-uploaded submission_pack.pdf was cleaned up (the bug this test guards)  ((['co-a/tenders/t-a/job-cleanup/submission_pack.pdf', 'co-a/tenders/t-a/job-cleanup/financial.pdf'], []))` - both files really were uploaded (the pdf AND the financial pdf, confirming the upload loop really does reach the second file before failing), and `removed` is really empty (no cleanup attempted at all, pre-fix) - `1 failure(s)` overall.

### Finding 398 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, pushed directly to `main`): `engine/general/process_general_jobs.py`'s `run_pack()` orphaned already-uploaded general-tender pack files in the shared `submission-packs` bucket forever whenever a LATER step in the same job (a later file in the same upload loop, or the `field_provenance` upsert) then failed

**Area:** `engine/general/process_general_jobs.py`'s `run_pack()` - the real fulfilment path for every general (non-SANRAL) submission-pack request (`pack_generation_jobs`, `engine='general'`).

**How this was found.** Picked up by name, the third and final instance of the identical Storage-orphan shape Finding 396 (`engine/cv/process_cv_jobs.py`) and Finding 397 (`engine/pack/process_pack_jobs.py`) already fixed in this lineage - both of those write-ups explicitly left this file noted as "genuinely real, not yet fixed." Confirmed first, by grep, that this file's own `Supabase` class (its own independent REST/Storage client, `class Supabase` around line 130 - not shared with `process_cv_jobs.py`'s module-level `storage_remove()` or `process_pack_jobs.py`'s `SupabaseRest`) has `select`/`update`/`insert`/`delete`(table rows only)/`upsert`/`rpc`/`download`/`upload` - and, before this fix, no Storage-object-delete capability of any kind (`grep -n "storage/v1/object\|def remove" engine/general/process_general_jobs.py` - zero hits pre-fix, only the existing `upload`/`download` methods).

**The real bug.** `run_pack()` builds a general-tender pack (`bgp.build_general_pack()`), then uploads the merged PDF to `PACK_BUCKET` ("submission-packs"), then loops over `res["outputs"].items()` (the filled forms, completion guide and provenance JSON `build_general_pack()` produced for this job) uploading each in turn, then - if a `field_provenance` row exists for this company's own pack - upserts the pack's field provenance. Before this fix, none of that sat inside any `try`/`except`: if any upload after the first, or the `field_provenance` upsert, then failed (an ordinary transient Storage/network failure on any of several sequential HTTP calls in the same job - the exact same failure mode Findings 396/397 already established as real and ordinary, not a crafted edge case), the exception propagated straight out of `run_pack()` into `process_job()`'s own blanket `except Exception as e:` block, which marks the `pack_generation_jobs` row `'failed'` with a generic message. `storage_path_pdf`/`output_files` are never written to any row, and every file that genuinely reached the shared `submission-packs` bucket moments earlier (confirmed by grep: the same `PACK_BUCKET = "submission-packs"` constant `process_pack_jobs.py` writes to) is never removed - orphaned forever, since a retried request gets a brand-new `job["id"]` and therefore a brand-new upload prefix, and (confirmed by grep across `app/`, `engine/`) nothing anywhere in this repo ever sweeps that bucket for orphans.

**Why this is real and reachable, not hypothetical.** This bridge runs unattended on a schedule (`--loop`/`--once` via `run_bridges.py`) and, on every successful `generate_pack` job, makes a minimum of two and typically four-plus sequential network writes to Storage (the merged PDF, then one `client.upload()` per output file - forms, completion guide, provenance JSON) plus a `field_provenance` upsert, with zero delay or retry between any of them, before `process_job()` ever marks the row `ready`. Any one of those calls failing after an earlier one in the same job already succeeded is the ordinary transient-failure case this track's own guardrail note anticipated, not a contrived scenario.

**Confirmed live, not inferred.** Added a real reproduction to `engine/general/test_process_general_jobs.py` (`test_run_pack_cleans_up_storage_when_a_later_upload_fails()`): a `FakeClient` subclass (`UploadFailsOnSecondFile`) that records every `upload()`/`remove()` call in order and raises on the one whose remote path ends `guide.docx` - the real, ordinary shape of "the PDF upload succeeds, the next output file's upload doesn't." `job_tender()`, `own_pack()`, `download_tender_documents()`, `bgp.local_docs_for()`, `gather_pack_inputs()`, `bgp.build_general_pack()` and `provenance_pack_id()` were monkeypatched to a minimal real-shaped manifest/outputs pair (same monkeypatch-the-heavy-dependencies pattern Finding 397's own test used on `process_pack_jobs.py`'s `gather()`/`build_submission_pack()`), so the real, unmodified `process_job()`/`run_pack()` ran against them end to end.

**Fix.** Added `Supabase.remove(self, bucket, paths)` (the same Supabase Storage bulk-delete endpoint Finding 396's `storage_remove()` and Finding 397's `SupabaseRest.remove()` use: `DELETE <url>/storage/v1/object/<bucket>` with body `{"prefixes": [...]}` - this file's own class-based convention, matching `process_pack_jobs.py`'s shape rather than `process_cv_jobs.py`'s bare module function, since every other Storage/REST call in this file is already a method on this one `Supabase` class). `run_pack()` now initialises `uploaded_paths = []` immediately before its own upload-and-upsert block, appends each remote path right after that file's own `client.upload()` call succeeds, and wraps the whole block (pdf upload, output-files loop, `field_provenance` upsert) in a `try`/`except Exception as e:` that calls `client.remove(PACK_BUCKET, uploaded_paths)` best-effort - wrapped in its own nested `try`/`except` that only raises a (new) `system_alerts` warning on its own failure, never masking or replacing the real error - then re-raises the original exception unchanged, so `process_job()`'s existing failure-marking logic (and the real, specific error message a human sees) is byte-for-byte untouched.

**Verified red-then-green, myself, real test output, real exit codes, no shell pipe.**
- **RED**: `git stash push -- engine/general/process_general_jobs.py` (reverting ONLY the production file to its exact pre-fix `main` content via the stash; the test file, already carrying the new test, left in place) -> `cd engine/general && python3 test_process_general_jobs.py > /tmp/red_output.txt 2>&1; echo "EXIT:$?"` printed `EXIT:1`, with the real, specific failure: `FAIL the already-uploaded submission_pack.pdf was cleaned up (the bug this test guards)  ((['co-a/tenders/t-a/job-cleanup/submission_pack.pdf', 'co-a/tenders/t-a/job-cleanup/guide.docx'], []))` - both files really were uploaded (the pdf AND the guide, confirming the upload loop really does reach the second file before failing), and `removed` is really empty (no cleanup attempted at all, pre-fix) - `1 failure(s)` overall.
- **GREEN**: `git stash pop` (restoring the fix) -> `python3 test_process_general_jobs.py`, `EXIT:0`, every check prints `ok` including the 4 new ones for this test (`process_job() handled the failure (returns True)`, `the job was marked failed, not left 'generating'`, `both the pdf and the guide uploads were attempted, in that order`, `the already-uploaded submission_pack.pdf was cleaned up (the bug this test guards)`), `0 failure(s)` overall across this file's full suite (now 9 test functions).
- **Full regression, every exit code captured directly (no pipe):** every `engine/**/test_*.py` file found by `find engine -name "test_*.py"` (92 files) run individually, each `cd <its dir> && python3 <file>.py`, real exit code captured per file with no shell pipe - **92 files total, 91 passed, 1 failed** (`engine/discovery/test_download_documents.py`, real exit code **1**, `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'playwright'` - the same pre-existing, already-documented playwright-missing-module failure Findings 396 and 397 both hit on an unmodified checkout; unrelated to this file, this bridge, or this change). `engine/general/test_general_bridge.py` (the real end-to-end fake-HTTP-server test of this exact bridge, including a real `generate_pack` job run to a real merged PDF) and `engine/general/test_build_general_pack.py` individually re-confirmed clean (exit 0).

**Why a direct push to `main`, not a PR - assessed explicitly, not assumed, per this task's own caution that this bridge's upload path may sit closer to the real pack-build path than the CV bridge did.** Pure Python change inside `engine/general/process_general_jobs.py` and its own test file - not one of the six named files (`fill_a_forms.py`, `fill_sbd_docx.py`, `fill_flat_pdf.py`, `make_envelope_covers.py`, `process_narrative_jobs.py`, `build_docx.py`). No RLS (no migration, no SQL touched). No money/payment path. No hard-stop/disqualification gate - the fix adds no new gate and changes no `JobRefusal`/`verify_problems` logic; a job that fails still fails exactly the same way, with the same customer-facing error message, just without leaking files. No worker-image/deployment change (no Dockerfile, no dependency, no new network host - the DELETE call targets the exact same Storage host and bucket every upload in this file already talks to). No multi-table schema surface (zero schema change - `field_provenance`'s own upsert shape is unchanged, only wrapped). **Not a correctness fix to a document a company signs/submits**, despite `run_pack()` sitting directly on the real general-tender submission-pack build path (confirmed by reading the full function: `bgp.build_general_pack()` fully builds and writes the merged PDF and every output file to local disk BEFORE any upload is attempted, exactly the same build-then-upload order `process_pack_jobs.py` already has) - the real submitted PDF/forms/completion-guide content a company's pack actually contains on the SUCCESS path (the only path ever delivered to a buyer) is byte-for-byte unchanged by this fix; the `try`/`except` added here wraps only the upload-and-upsert calls, never touches `build_general_pack()` or anything upstream of it, and re-raises the original exception verbatim on failure. Confirmed by grep (`grep -rn "process_general_jobs" app/`) that no TypeScript file imports anything from this file - every hit is a docstring/comment reference in other `app/` files describing what the Python bridge does, never a code import (impossible across the Python/TypeScript boundary in any case); it is a standalone Python worker process, never imported by `pack-review.tsx`/`submission-pack.tsx`/`general-pack-review.tsx`/`general-workspace.tsx` or anything else in `app/`, even transitively. This task's own explicit caution against assuming the same risk profile as Findings 396/397 without checking was taken seriously: `run_pack()`'s own upload/build intertwining was read function-by-function above, specifically to rule out the concern - the build and the upload are two cleanly sequential phases, not interleaved, so a Storage-side cleanup fix on the upload phase cannot touch document-filling correctness.

**Real file-level adjacency, checked, confirmed non-overlapping.** Re-checked the live list of all 67 open PRs (`#164`/`#165`/`#176`-`#213`/`#215`-`#241`) via the GitHub MCP tools: none has a title or `head.ref` branch name mentioning `process_general_jobs`, `general pack`, `run_pack`, `storage_remove`/`.remove(`, or this bridge's own upload loop at all. Two open PRs DO touch this same file for unrelated reasons, both checked directly via their own diffs: PR #221 (Finding 342) changes `gather_pack_inputs()`'s CV-selection filter (around line 737, unrelated function); PR #195 changes `private_documents_for()`'s and `own_path()`'s path-traversal check (around lines 345/607-620, unrelated functions). Neither touches the `Supabase` class or `run_pack()`'s own upload loop (around lines 205/811+) - no hunk overlap with either.

### Finding 401 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, pushed directly to `main`): `app/lib/clarificationWindowReminders.ts`'s `clarificationThresholdFor()` was an EXACT match on 10 or 2 days left - the same no-retry-safety shape Finding 387 (`lib/trialLifecycle.ts`'s `trialDay7Candidates()`) had just been fixed for, found here independently in a different file - a missed/late daily cron run permanently lost that threshold's clarification-window reminder, with no way to ever catch up

**Area:** `app/lib/clarificationWindowReminders.ts` (`clarificationThresholdFor()`, used by `send-operational-alerts.ts`'s `runClarificationWindow()`). Rotation this pass: compliance/reminders, mention-count heuristic.

**How this was found.** `app/lib/complianceExpiryReminders.ts` (lowest mention count in the directory) was checked first - its own `complianceExpiryCandidates()` has the identical exact-match shape (`daysLeft === COMPLIANCE_EXPIRY_THRESHOLD_DAYS`), but tracing its real caller confirmed it is DEAD CODE: `send-operational-alerts.ts`'s own header comment states this stage "was REMOVED 2026-10-27... `lib/complianceExpiryReminders.ts`... now unused by any live sender - left in place (still tested, harmless)". Not a live bug - ruled out before writing anything up. Moved to the next-lowest file, `clarificationWindowReminders.ts`, and found the SAME shape still live: `clarificationThresholdFor()` used `[10, 2].includes(daysLeft)` - an exact match, not a range - exactly the pattern this session's sibling track had just fixed in `trialLifecycle.ts`'s `trialDay7Candidates()` (Finding 387, landed on `main` this same window).

**Confirmed live and reachable.** `send-operational-alerts.ts` runs via `.github/workflows/operational-alerts.yml`'s own cron, `"20 4 * * *"` - once a day, no more. `clarificationWindowCandidates()` (which calls `clarificationThresholdFor()`) is the only gate deciding whether a `tender_tasks` row of `kind='clarification'` gets its 10-day or 2-day reminder; with the pre-fix exact match, a task whose `daysLeft` landed on exactly 10 (or exactly 2) on a day the cron run was skipped, delayed past midnight SAST, or failed outright - no code bug needed, scheduled GitHub Actions workflows are documented to occasionally skip or run late under load - would NEVER get that threshold's reminder again: every subsequent day's `daysLeft` is a different integer, matching neither 10 nor 2. Confirmed via the existing (pre-fix) test suite's own assertion, which encoded exactly this gap as intended behaviour: `clarificationThresholdFor(9)` and `clarificationThresholdFor(5)` both asserted `null`/no-candidate, meaning a task one day short of the window, or squarely in the middle of it, got nothing - there was no "close enough, catch up" path at all.

**Confirmed this is genuinely reachable, not purely theoretical.** `runClarificationWindow()`'s own dedup key, `claim(supabase, "clarification_window", tender.id, task.company_id, String(threshold), opts)`, has no day/date component at all - only the threshold ("10" or "2") - confirming (same as Finding 387's own trial-lifecycle precedent) that widening the match to a range changes nothing about how often the email actually sends: `claim_notification()`'s one-time-ever claim is what prevents a double-send, this function matching only one exact day was never load-bearing for correctness, only an accidental single point of failure for a missed run.

**Fix.** Widened `clarificationThresholdFor()` to two non-overlapping ranges, same shape as `trialDay7Candidates()`: `daysLeft <= 10 && daysLeft > 2` maps to threshold `10`; `daysLeft <= 2 && daysLeft > 0` maps to threshold `2`. Floored the 10-day window just above the 2-day window so the two never compete for the same day; floored the 2-day window at 0 so a task already due today or overdue stays out of scope, matching the original exact match's own scope (it could never match 0 or a negative number either).

**Verified red-then-green, myself, real test output.** Updated `clarificationWindowReminders.spec.ts`'s own tests that had encoded the old exact-match behaviour as intended (the "does not fire when daysLeft is not exactly on a threshold" case, previously asserting `daysLeft: 5` -> no candidates), and added new cases for the catch-up window itself.
- **RED** (`git apply -R` on just this file's diff): `npx vitest run lib/clarificationWindowReminders.spec.ts` - **3 failed, 12 passed** - all three failures on the new catch-up-window assertions (`clarificationThresholdFor(9)`/`(5)`/`(3)` all expected to now resolve to threshold 10, and the `clarificationWindowCandidates` catch-up test), confirming the exact predicted gap.
- **GREEN** (`git apply` to reapply): `npx vitest run lib/clarificationWindowReminders.spec.ts` - **15 passed, 0 failed**.
- `npx tsc --noEmit` clean on this change (pre-existing, unrelated `date-fns`/`react-day-picker` module-resolution gaps elsewhere, confirmed present identically before and after). `npx eslint lib/clarificationWindowReminders.ts lib/clarificationWindowReminders.spec.ts` clean. Full `npx vitest run`: 663 passed / 6 failed, all 6 failures in `lib/payfast.spec.ts`/`lib/properties.spec.ts`/`app/company/properties/actions.spec.ts` - the same pre-existing, unrelated missing-`date-fns`-module sandbox gap this session has already confirmed elsewhere, reproduced identically with this change reverted.

**Why a direct push to `main`, not a PR.** Pure TypeScript threshold logic, no RLS/migration/money-path/worker-image/hard-stop surface - the real send is still gated by `claim_notification()`'s own one-time dedupe, unchanged by this fix. Not one of the files this track's own guardrail names as requiring a PR. Same precedent as Finding 387's own direct push for the structurally identical trial-lifecycle fix.

**Numbering note.** Drafted as 391 at rotation start (last real entry then was 390); by the time this fix was ready, the sibling track had already landed Findings 392-400 and opened PR #243 (also claiming "Finding 400" for an unrelated `compliance-data.ts` CV-match bug, same compliance/reminders area but a different file). Re-verified **401** free against `main` (`e4f6fc3`, last real entry 400) and against all 69 open PR titles/branches before this push - no collision.

**Backlog status.** No new standing item opened - fixed, not deferred.

### Finding 402 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, pushed directly to `main`): `page.tsx`'s own "Key positions" CV-jobs list matched `generated_cvs` by `position_code` alone, with no `person_id` check at all - a third, independently-found site of the exact "stale position reassignment" shape

**Area:** `app/app/tenders/[id]/page.tsx` - the Tender Workspace's own "Key positions" card (the main `/tenders/[id]` route page, not a sub-screen).

**How this was found.** Extended this lineage's own productive method from Finding 400 ("compare a TS-side correctness guard against its Python-side sibling that builds the structurally identical data") past the one site Finding 400 already found. Finding 400's own write-up names `engine/pack/process_pack_jobs.py`'s real CV-gathering loop (`build_submission_pack()`) as the authoritative sibling: `g = next((g for g in gen if g["position_code"] == p["code"] and g["person_id"] == pid ...` - filtering by BOTH `position_code` and `person_id`. Grepped every `app/` site that reads `generated_cvs` filtered or matched by `position_code` (`cv-compare.tsx`, `compliance-data.ts`, `page.tsx`, `activity-log.tsx`) and checked each against that same sibling, rather than assuming Finding 400's own fix covered the whole class.

- `cv-compare.tsx` (`CvCompare()`): already correct - its own query filters by `tender_id` + `position_code` + `person_id` together (`.eq("position_code", positionCode).eq("person_id", personId)`). Not a bug.
- `compliance-data.ts`: this IS Finding 400's own site - fetched PR #243's branch read-only (`git fetch origin pull/243/head:pr243tmp`, then `git diff main pr243tmp`, then deleted the local branch ref immediately after per this track's own guardrail against touching another PR's branch beyond read-only reference) to confirm the scope of that fix - it touches only `compliance-data.ts` (`generatedCvs.find(...)` -> new `matchGeneratedCvForPosition()` helper in `app/lib/tenderCompliance.ts`) and is NOT yet merged (PR #243, open, docs-only commit `e4f6fc3` on `main` records it but the real fix lives only on the branch).
- `activity-log.tsx`: genuine negative, see Confirmed-clean note below.
- `page.tsx`: the real, previously-undocumented bug, below.

**The real bug.** `app/app/tenders/[id]/page.tsx`'s own "Key positions" card computes:
```ts
const positionJobs = generatedCvs.filter((g) => g.position_code === code);
```
even though the exact same query, two lines above it in the same component (`.select("id, position_code, person_id, format, detail, status, storage_path_docx, storage_path_pdf, error_message")`), already fetches `person_id` on every row, and the local `GeneratedCv` type (`person_id: string;`) already declares it. The field is fetched and typed; this one filter simply never reads it.

**Concrete failure scenario, traced end to end, not hypothetical.** Position `PL` is confirmed for Henning; `requestTenderCv()` runs and his tailored CV finishes generating (`generated_cvs.status = 'ready'`, real `storage_path_docx`/`storage_path_pdf`, both with working signed download URLs on this page). `PL` is then reassigned to Jane via `PositionPersonSelect`'s own form (`confirmPositionPerson()` in `actions.ts`) - confirmed by reading `actions.ts` that a reassignment only ever upserts `tender_pack_assignments.confirmed_person_id`; no `generated_cvs` row is ever touched, deleted, or re-pointed by it. The Key Positions card now correctly shows "Confirmed: Jane" on `PL`'s row (`confirmedId` comes from the fresh `tender_pack_assignments` read), but the CV-jobs list directly underneath that same row (`positionJobs.map(...)`) still lists Henning's own "ready" job: its format/detail, its green "Ready" status pill, and working "Word"/"PDF" download links - with nothing on screen distinguishing whose CV it actually is, since the rendered row never prints a person's name at all, only the job's own fields. A reviewer reading "ready" plus live download links directly below Jane's own confirmed name has a real, concrete reason to believe Jane's own tailored CV already exists, and to download and hand-attach the wrong person's CV into the submission pack. If `PL` is reassigned a second time to nobody (unconfirmed), the same stale job list keeps showing with no confirmed person's row even displayed above it, which is more clearly wrong on its face but equally unfixed pre-patch.

The actual submission-PACK build is unaffected either way: `process_pack_jobs.py`'s own CV-gathering loop already re-matches by `person_id`, so the wrong CV is never automatically bundled into a generated pack - this is a human-facing display/review-screen bug (a person could be misled into manually using the wrong file), not a document-content bug. That distinction is what keeps this a direct push rather than a PR - see the guardrail analysis below.

**Confirmed clean (genuine negative): `activity-log.tsx`.** Its own `generated_cvs` read (`select("id, position_code, status, requested_by, requested_at, completed_at, error_message, people:person_id(name)")`) is a chronological activity-log/history view ("a CV was requested for <name> on <date>"), not a "what applies to this position right now" display - each row already carries its own `people:person_id(name)` embed naming exactly who it was requested for at the time, and a past event is correctly unaffected by a later reassignment (there is no "currently confirmed person" concept for history to match against). Not the same shape; not a bug.

**Fix.** Extracted a new pure function, `cvJobsForPosition()`, into a new file `app/app/tenders/[id]/position-cv-jobs-logic.ts` - the same extraction pattern `won-project-sync-logic.ts` already established beside this exact `actions.ts`/`page.tsx` cluster for the structurally identical `projects`-row problem (`staleSyncedProjectRows()`, QA-Edge-Case-Findings.md 2026-10-19). `cvJobsForPosition(generatedCvs, positionCode, confirmedPersonId)` returns `[]` outright when `confirmedPersonId` is falsy (so an unconfirmed position never shows a lingering stale job either), otherwise filters by `position_code === positionCode && person_id === confirmedPersonId`. `page.tsx`'s own `positionJobs` now calls this instead of the bare `.filter()`. Deliberately NOT built on PR #243's own new `matchGeneratedCvForPosition()` helper in `app/lib/tenderCompliance.ts`, despite the conceptual overlap (both are "match a `generated_cvs` row to a position's current person") - that PR is unmerged, and a `main`-track fix must stand on `main` as it actually is today, not depend on another track's own open PR landing first, or landing in its current shape. (`matchGeneratedCvForPosition()` also returns a single `.find()` match, suited to compliance-data.ts's "is there one usable CV" check; `page.tsx` needs the full filtered job HISTORY for a position, a `.filter()`, so even once #243 merges this would stay a distinct, if sibling, function.)

**Verified red-then-green, myself, real test output, real exit codes, no shell pipe.** New test file `app/app/tenders/[id]/position-cv-jobs-logic.test.ts` (7 cases), run the way this repo's own `*.test.ts` convention actually requires - confirmed empirically first: `node --experimental-strip-types --test "<path>"` reports `# tests 0` for ANY file under this directory, because node's own `--test` glob matching mishandles the literal `[id]` path segment (confirmed on the pre-existing `won-project-sync-logic.test.ts` too, not just the new file) - this repo's CI (`.github/workflows/app-ci.yml`, "Run every *.test.ts file directly (not via node --test's glob - see header)") already works around this by invoking each file directly, `node --experimental-strip-types "$f"`, which is what every reproduction below uses.
- **RED**: temporarily overwrote `position-cv-jobs-logic.ts` with its pre-fix shape (a bare `generatedCvs.filter((g) => g.position_code === positionCode)`, no `confirmedPersonId`/`person_id` check at all - the exact shape `page.tsx` itself had) -> `cd app && node --experimental-strip-types 'app/tenders/[id]/position-cv-jobs-logic.test.ts'` -> **exit 1**. `# tests 7` / `# pass 4` / `# fail 3`. The 3 real, specific failures: (1) "the real bug: a position reassigned to a different person..." - expected `[]`, got Henning's stale `job1` row back; (2) "a position with jobs for both the old and new person..." - expected `['job-new']`, got `['job-old','job-new']`; (3) "position currently unconfirmed..." - expected `[]`, got Henning's stale `job1` row back. The 4 cases that don't depend on the missing check (no jobs, matching job for the confirmed person, a different position's job, multiple historical jobs for the same confirmed person) still passed, confirming the failures are specific to the bug, not a broken test file.
- **GREEN**: restored the real fix (file content exactly as committed) -> same command -> **exit 0**, `# tests 7` / `# pass 7` / `# fail 0`.
- **Full regression, every exit code captured directly, no shell pipe:** `cd app && npm run typecheck` - **exit 0**, clean (no `LayoutProps` false-positive hit on this run). `npm run lint` - **exit 0**, 0 errors (2 pre-existing warnings in unrelated files, `app/_components/Logo.tsx`/`app/analytics/page.tsx`, confirmed present before this change too). `npm run build` - **exit 0**, production build succeeds, `/tenders/[id]` route present in the output. `npx vitest run` - **exit 0**, **85 test files / 695 tests, all passing**. Every `*.test.ts` file in the repo, run individually the exact CI way (`find . -name "*.test.ts" -not -path "*/node_modules/*"`, each one's own exit code checked in a `while read` loop, never `$?` after a pipe) - **33 files found, all exit 0**.

**Why a direct push to `main`, not a PR - assessed explicitly, each guardrail risk factor checked, not assumed.** Pure TypeScript change confined to `page.tsx`'s own render (one filter call replaced, plus one new import) and a new, zero-dependency pure-logic file beside it. **No RLS** (no migration, no SQL touched). **No money/payment path**. **No hard-stop/disqualification gate** - the fix adds no new gate and changes no `verify_problems`/disqualification logic; a position with no confirmed person still gets exactly the same "Fix: no key person confirmed - blocks the submission pack" treatment as before, unchanged. **No worker-image/deployment change** (no Dockerfile, no dependency, no Python engine touched at all). **No multi-table schema surface** (zero schema change - the `generated_cvs`/`tender_pack_assignments` queries themselves are byte-for-byte unchanged; ### Finding 403 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, pushed directly to `main`): `app/lib/deadlineReminders.ts`'s `reminderThresholdFor()` was an EXACT match on 3 or 1 days left - the same no-retry-safety shape Findings 387/401 already fixed twice, found here a third time, in a HIGHER-STAKES notification (a tender's real closing deadline, not a trial milestone or a clarification window)

**Area:** `app/lib/deadlineReminders.ts` (`reminderThresholdFor()`, used by `deadlineReminderCandidates()`, the sole gate in `scripts/send-deadline-reminders.ts`'s "closing in 3 days / 24 hours" email); `app/lib/emailTemplates.ts`'s `deadlineReminderEmail()` (the subject line, which this fix also had to make honest once the function can fire on more than one day). Rotation this pass: the task brief's own suggested lead - "notifications/alerts code outside clarification/trial (briefing_date reminders, closing_date reminders, addendum/corrigendum alerts)" - applied to `closing_date` reminders specifically.

**How this was found.** Before touching this, confirmed the two obvious "stale position/person reassignment" leads the task brief named were genuine dead ends, not re-treads to force a finding out of: `engine/discovery/score_outlook.py` (985 lines) has zero references to `position_code`, `person_id`, `confirmed_person_id`, `generated_cvs` or `tender_pack_assignments` anywhere - it extracts experience-evidence/scoring rules from tender text, not position/person data at all, so this shape cannot apply there; "`engine/general/general_bridge.py`" does not exist as a file - the real module the task brief meant is `engine/general/process_general_jobs.py` (its own test file is named `test_general_bridge.py`), which Finding 398 (this same lineage, same day) already read and fixed for an unrelated bug (the Storage-orphan class) and which has no position/person-reassignment surface either (it builds a general-family pack, not SANRAL key-position CVs). Then swept every remaining `app/` site reading `generated_cvs`/`tender_pack_assignments` filtered by `position_code` that Findings 400/402's own write-ups hadn't already individually ruled in or out (`actions.ts`, `pack-inputs-actions.ts`, `position-person-select.tsx`, `submission-plan-data.ts`, `pastSubmissionReuse.ts`, `won-project-sync-logic.ts`) - every one of them already correctly pairs `position_code` with `person_id`/`confirmed_person_id` (traced individually below, under "Confirmed clean"); the "stale reassignment" class is genuinely exhausted across `app/`, not just at the two sites Findings 400/402 already found.

Moved to the task brief's second suggested lead instead: a fresh rotation over the notifications/alerts code outside clarification/trial. `app/lib/deadlineReminders.ts` (84 lines) and `app/lib/briefingReminders.ts` (74 lines) both carry a header comment admitting they share "the same exact-day-match + per-company-fanout shape" with each other - read both, and their own existing spec files, side by side with the two already-fixed siblings (`lib/trialLifecycle.ts`'s `trialDay7Candidates()`, Finding 387; `lib/clarificationWindowReminders.ts`'s `clarificationThresholdFor()`, Finding 401).

**The gap, traced, not guessed.** `reminderThresholdFor()`, pre-fix:
```ts
export function reminderThresholdFor(daysLeft: number): ReminderThresholdDays | null {
  return (REMINDER_THRESHOLD_DAYS as readonly number[]).includes(daysLeft) ? (daysLeft as ReminderThresholdDays) : null;
}
```
`REMINDER_THRESHOLD_DAYS = [3, 1]` - an exact match on exactly 3 or exactly 1, nothing else. Its own pre-fix header comment justified this with "...so each threshold fires once per tender" - the exact same misconception Finding 387 already identified and fixed for `trialDay7Candidates()`: firing-once is actually guaranteed by `record_deadline_reminder_sent()`'s own one-time dedupe claim (migration 0080's unique constraint on `(tender_id, company_id, threshold_days)` - no day/date component at all, confirmed by reading the migration directly), not by the match being exact. The pre-fix test file even encoded this as intended behaviour: `deadlineReminders.spec.ts`'s own `reminderThresholdFor(2)` asserted `toBeNull()` - a tender exactly 2 days from closing got no reminder of either kind.

**Confirmed live and reachable, not purely theoretical.** `scripts/send-deadline-reminders.ts` is run once a day by `.github/workflows/deadline-reminders.yml`'s own cron (`"10 4 * * *"`), no more - the workflow's own header comment explicitly accepts that "if a run is ever delayed or dropped," the feature "degrades to... today's reminder arrives a bit late," written on the assumption that a late run can still catch up. With the pre-fix exact match it could not: a tender whose `daysUntil(closing_date)` landed on exactly 3 (or exactly 1) on a day the cron run was skipped, delayed past SAST midnight, or failed outright - no other code bug needed, scheduled GitHub Actions workflows are documented to occasionally skip or run late under platform load, the same risk Finding 387's own write-up already established for this exact mechanism - would NEVER get that threshold's "closing in 3 days"/"24 hours" warning again: every subsequent day's `daysLeft` is a different integer, matching neither 3 nor 1. Unlike Findings 387/401 (a trial milestone email; a clarification-window nudge), this is the one reminder in this family whose entire purpose is to stop a company from missing its own bid submission deadline - the highest-stakes instance of this shape found in this lineage so far.

**Confirmed this is genuinely safe to widen, the same way Findings 387/401 confirmed it for their own files.** Read `record_deadline_reminder_sent()` (migration 0080) directly: its dedupe key is `(tender_id, company_id, threshold_days)`, with no day/date component - so widening `reminderThresholdFor()` to a range changes nothing about how many times a company is actually emailed for a given threshold (still exactly once, ever, per the claim), only whether a missed/late run can catch up on a later one instead of permanently losing that threshold.

**The one real complication, found by reading the consumer, not assumed - same shape Finding 387 hit for `trialDay7MilestoneEmail()`.** `deadlineReminderEmail()`'s own subject line was hardcoded off a binary `urgent = daysLeft <= 1` split (`"Closing in 24 hours: ..."` vs `"Closing in 3 days: ..."`), independent of the real `daysLeft` - so once the 3-day threshold can genuinely fire a day late (catching up a missed run at `daysLeft === 2`), the pre-fix subject would have read "Closing in 3 days" while only 2 genuinely remained: not a cosmetic slip but an email that materially overstates how much time a company actually has left on its own bid deadline. The body text (`whenText`) was already dynamic (`closes in ${daysLeft} days`) and needed no change - only the subject was stale.

**Confirmed clean (genuine negatives) - every other `generated_cvs`/`tender_pack_assignments` site filtered by `position_code` alone, so the "stale reassignment" class (Findings 400/402's own shape) is not quietly still open elsewhere:**
- `app/app/tenders/[id]/actions.ts` (`requestTenderCv()`, `syncWonProjectToTeam()`): every `generated_cvs`/`tender_pack_assignments`/`projects` read or write pairs `position_code` with `person_id`/`confirmed_person_id` together - the `syncWonProjectToTeam()` function is itself the ORIGINAL, pre-existing instance of this fix class (`won-project-sync-logic.ts`'s `staleSyncedProjectRows()`), already correct.
- `app/app/tenders/[id]/pack-inputs-actions.ts`, `app/app/tenders/[id]/position-person-select.tsx`: both read/write `tender_pack_assignments.confirmed_person_id` directly, scoped by `(tender_pack_id, position_code)` - the assignment row itself, not a derived CV/document lookup; nothing to go stale.
- `app/app/tenders/[id]/submission-plan-data.ts`, `app/app/tenders/[id]/disqualification-guard.tsx`: both select `generated_cvs` filtered by `person_id` (from `person_role_eligibility` role tags) directly, never by `position_code` at all - a different, already-correct matching shape (and the subject of Finding 342/355's own, separate `tender_id`-scoping fix).
- `app/lib/pastSubmissionReuse.ts`'s `planPositionReuse()`: copies a confirmed `(position_code, confirmed_person_id)` pair from a past tender to a new one only when the new tender lists the same position AND the person is still on file - the pair travels together throughout; never reads `position_code` alone.

**Fix.** `reminderThresholdFor()` now matches two bounded, non-overlapping ranges instead of an exact value: `daysLeft <= 3 && daysLeft > 1` -> threshold `3`; `daysLeft <= 1 && daysLeft > 0` -> threshold `1` - the identical shape `trialDay7Candidates()`/`clarificationThresholdFor()` already use, floored at 0 so a tender already closing today or overdue stays out of scope (matching the original exact match's own scope, which never matched 0 or a negative number either). `deadlineReminderEmail()`'s subject now reads the real `daysLeft` directly (`"Closing today"` / `"Closing in 24 hours"` / `"Closing in N days"`), the same "stop claiming a specific day once more than one day can fire" correction Finding 387 made to `trialDay7MilestoneEmail()`'s copy.
