### Finding 404 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, pushed directly to `main`): `app/lib/briefingReminders.ts`'s `briefingThresholdFor()` was an EXACT match on 5 or 1 days left - the exact sibling gap Finding 403 named by hand and left open, now closed the same way, a fourth instance of this no-retry-safety shape (387/401/403/404)

**Area:** `app/lib/briefingReminders.ts` (`briefingThresholdFor()`, the sole gate in `briefingReminderCandidates()`, which `scripts/send-operational-alerts.ts`'s `runBriefingReminders()` calls for the "briefing session in 5 days / 24 hours" email).

**How this was found.** Finding 403's own write-up named this file by hand as the single best remaining lead in this lineage: `briefingReminders.ts`'s own header comment already claims to share "the same exact-day-match + per-company-fanout shape as `lib/deadlineReminders.ts`" - read the real current code rather than trusting that paraphrase, and it checked out exactly:
```ts
export const BRIEFING_REMINDER_THRESHOLD_DAYS = [5, 1] as const; // 1 day = "24 hours"
export function briefingThresholdFor(daysLeft: number): BriefingReminderThresholdDays | null {
  return (BRIEFING_REMINDER_THRESHOLD_DAYS as readonly number[]).includes(daysLeft) ? (daysLeft as BriefingReminderThresholdDays) : null;
}
```
An exact match on exactly 5 or exactly 1, nothing else - identical shape to `trialDay7Candidates()` (387), `clarificationThresholdFor()` (401) and pre-fix `reminderThresholdFor()` (403). The pre-fix spec file encoded the gap as intended behaviour too: `briefingReminders.spec.ts`'s own test named it "matches exactly 5 days and 1 day (24 hours), nothing else" and asserted `briefingThresholdFor(4)` -> `toBeNull()`, and a separate test asserted `briefingReminderCandidates([tender], () => 3)` -> `[]`.

**Confirmed this is genuinely safe to widen, by reading the real dedupe mechanism, not assumed from the other three fixes' precedent alone.** This alert type does NOT use `record_deadline_reminder_sent()`/`notification_claims` at all - it uses a third, separate dedupe table, `sent_operational_alerts` (migration 0092), shared across three operational-alert types (print cutoff, briefing, compliance expiry). Read migration 0092 directly: `record_operational_alert_sent(p_alert_type, p_tender_id, p_company_id, p_threshold_key)`'s unique constraint is `unique nulls not distinct (alert_type, tender_id, company_id, threshold_key)` - no day/date component. Read the real caller, `scripts/send-operational-alerts.ts`'s `runBriefingReminders()`, to confirm `threshold_key` is actually populated with the THRESHOLD, not `daysLeft`: `const firstClaim = await claim(supabase, "briefing", tender.id, companyId, String(threshold), opts);` - `threshold` is `briefingReminderCandidates()`'s own returned `threshold` field (5 or 1), never the raw `daysLeft`. So widening `briefingThresholdFor()` to a range changes nothing about how many times a company is actually emailed for a given threshold (still exactly once, ever, per the claim) - only whether a missed/late cron run can catch up on a later day instead of permanently losing that threshold.

**Confirmed live and reachable, not purely theoretical.** `scripts/send-operational-alerts.ts` is run by `.github/workflows/operational-alerts.yml`'s own cron, once a day, same mechanism Findings 387/401/403 already established is documented to occasionally skip or run late under GitHub Actions platform load. A tender whose `daysUntil(briefing_date)` landed on exactly 5 (or exactly 1) on a day that run was skipped or delayed past the real calendar-day boundary would NEVER get that threshold's briefing-session warning again - every subsequent day's `daysLeft` is a different integer, matching neither 5 nor 1. Arguably higher-stakes than Finding 403's own closing-date reminder in one specific way: a missed closing-date reminder still leaves the tender's real deadline ahead, so a company can still self-notice and submit in time; a missed briefing-session reminder, once the briefing itself has passed, cannot be acted on at all - there is no "catching up" on attending a briefing that already happened. (The fix below still closes the gap for every case where the cron catches up before the briefing date itself, which is the actual realistic failure mode - a skipped run the day after, not days after.)

**The email-subject-line sibling check Finding 403 asked this pass to make - genuine negative, not a second bug.** Finding 403 found `deadlineReminderEmail()`'s subject hardcoded off a binary `urgent = daysLeft <= 1` split, independent of the real `daysLeft`, and fixed it to read the real value. `lib/emailTemplates.ts`'s `briefingReminderEmail()` was read side by side with it: `const whenText = opts.daysLeft <= 1 ? "in 24 hours" : \`in ${opts.daysLeft} days\`;` followed by `operationalSubject(opts.contractLabel, level, \`Briefing session ${whenText}\`)` - this already reads the real `daysLeft` directly into both the subject and body, with no hardcoded day number anywhere in the function. ### Finding 405 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, pushed directly to `main`): `app/lib/printCutoffReminders.ts`'s `printCutoffCandidates()` never checked `dispatch_status` at all - a physical-box pack already printed, bound and handed to a courier kept firing the real "URGENT: print & sign deadline" cron email as if nothing had been dispatched

**Area:** `app/lib/printCutoffReminders.ts` (`printCutoffCandidates()`, the sole candidate-selection gate `scripts/send-operational-alerts.ts`'s `runPrintCutoff()` calls for the real "48-hour print & transit cutoff" operational alert email - the Operational Notification Engine's own highest-stakes physical-logistics warning).

**How this was found.** The task brief's own suggested-angle list named "print-cutoff reminders' OTHER logic beyond the threshold itself" as an unexplored lead - Findings 387/401/403/404 had just closed out every *threshold* (missed-run-safety) shape across the notification engine, and `printCutoffReminders.ts` itself was the one file in that family explicitly confirmed (by Finding 404's own closing note) to be a *genuinely different* shape (`hoursLeft <= 48`, a one-sided bound, not an exact-day match) - so it had never actually been read end to end for its own, separate correctness. Reading `printCutoffCandidates()` in full: it excludes `CLOSED_STAGES` (`submitted`/`briefing_shortlisted`/`won`/`lost`, keyed off `tender_packs.pipeline_stage`) and then goes straight to `hoursUntilPrintSignDeadline()` - it never once reads `pack.dispatch_status`, even though the type it's passed already carries that field. Cross-checked against the one other module that computes the exact same `printSignDeadline()`/`hoursUntilPrintSignDeadline()` math over the same fields, `lib/dispatchTriage.ts`: both of its own real functions, `classifyDispatchBucket()` (`notYetDispatched = !DISPATCHED_STATUSES.includes(input.dispatchStatus)`) and `operationalStatusMessage()` (fixed for its own physical-box branch by Finding 352, 2026-11-10, for this exact reason), treat `dispatch_status` as load-bearing - a pack already `printed_and_bound`/`out_for_delivery`/`submitted_and_receipted` is deliberately excluded from "still needs printing" in both. `printCutoffReminders.ts` is a *third* consumer of the identical fact and had never been given the same guard - a genuinely new site of a known shape (Finding 352's own class), not a re-tread of Finding 352 itself: that Finding fixed the dashboard/workspace UI message text; this is the real cron-driven email send, a completely different file and a completely different code path, never touched or even mentioned by Finding 352's own write-up.

**Confirmed live and reachable, not purely theoretical - traced the real, independent write paths.** `pipeline_stage` and `dispatch_status` are two separate columns on `tender_packs`, written by two separate, unrelated Server Actions with no synchronization between them at all:
- `pipeline_stage` is only ever written by `app/pipeline/actions.ts`'s pipeline-board move (`upsert({ ... pipeline_stage: stage }, { onConflict: "company_id,tender_id" })`) - a manual drag on the Pipeline kanban board.
- `dispatch_status` is only ever written by `app/tenders/[id]/logistics-actions.ts`'s `advanceDispatchStatus()` (`update({ dispatch_status: next }).eq("id", tenderPackId).eq("company_id", companyId)`) - a manual tap-to-advance button in the Pack Compiler tab / dashboard Lane C, with no `pipeline_stage` write anywhere in that same function or file.

So a real, ordinary workflow - a company finishes compiling its physical submission box, taps through "Printed & bound" -> "Out for delivery" -> "Submitted & receipted" in the dispatch tracker, days or hours before closing - leaves `dispatch_status = 'submitted_and_receipted'` while `pipeline_stage` can genuinely still read anything *other* than `submitted`/`briefing_shortlisted`/`won`/`lost` (e.g. `building`, if the company simply hasn't separately gone to the Pipeline board to drag the card over - a second, independent manual step nothing in the dispatch flow prompts or performs). `printCutoffCandidates()`'s own `CLOSED_STAGES` check does nothing to catch this, since `pipeline_stage` is exactly the field that's stale here. The real cron (`.github/workflows/operational-alerts.yml` -> `send-operational-alerts.ts` -> `runPrintCutoff()`) then sends the real, live `printCutoffEmail()` - subject `"URGENT: Physical print & sign deadline in N hours"`, body `"...there isn't enough time left to print, bind and deliver a physical submission before it closes"` - to a company that has already done exactly that, as soon as the raw closing-date math alone drops to 48 hours, regardless of how early the box was actually dispatched. The one-shot `record_operational_alert_sent()` dedupe key (`alert_type, tender_id, company_id, threshold_key` = `"print_cutoff"`/tender/company/`"48h"`) means this fires exactly once per tender - but that one time is a false alarm, not a safety net: the company that did the sensible thing (dispatch early) is the one punished with a scary, factually wrong "you're about to miss your own deadline" email.

**Fix.** Exported `DISPATCHED_STATUSES` from `lib/dispatchTriage.ts` (previously module-private, used internally by `classifyDispatchBucket()`/`operationalStatusMessage()`) rather than re-deriving a second copy of the same three-value list in `printCutoffReminders.ts` that could later drift from it - the identical "never a second number/list that could disagree" rule this codebase already follows for `hoursUntilPrintSignDeadline()` itself (this file's own header). `printCutoffCandidates()` now also skips any pack whose `dispatch_status` is in `DISPATCHED_STATUSES`, alongside its existing `CLOSED_STAGES` check:
```ts
for (const pack of packs) {
  if (CLOSED_STAGES.includes(pack.pipeline_stage)) continue;
  if (DISPATCHED_STATUSES.includes(pack.dispatch_status)) continue;
  ...
}
```
A genuinely-not-yet-dispatched pack (`not_ready`/`compiling`/`print_ready`) inside the 48h window is completely unaffected - confirmed by a dedicated sanity assertion in the same new test (same `hoursLeft`, same everything else, `dispatch_status: "print_ready"` still returns the one real candidate).

### Finding 406 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, pushed directly to `main`): `/pipeline`'s own Kanban board sorted `submitted`/`won`/`lost` most-recent-first but silently never sorted `briefing_shortlisted` - a 4th hand-kept stage list that drifted the moment the stage was added, the exact root cause `OUTCOME_FORM_STAGES` (Finding, 2026-11-06) already named and fixed once for a different pair of lists

**Where this came from.** A fresh least-recently-touched sweep (per this pass's own task brief) over the compliance/notification engine and several `app/lib`/engine/ candidates turned up nothing new - several files were read in full (`company_profiles.py`, `eskom_bulletin.py`, `tenderRoles.ts`, `positionSuggestions.ts`, `opportunityInsights.ts`, `compileReadiness.ts`, `OpportunityRow.tsx`/`OpportunityTable.tsx`, `marketPricing.ts`'s `tenderFrequencyTrend()`) and each held up. The real lead came from a different angle: grepping every hardcoded `pipeline_stage` list in the whole repo (`grep -rn '"won".*"lost"\|DONE_STAGES\|CLOSED_STAGES\|ACTIVE_STAGES' app engine`) to check whether migration `0105`'s `briefing_shortlisted` stage (added after at least one other hand-kept list already drifted - `opportunityInsights.ts`'s `DONE_STAGES`, fixed 2026-10-31, and `lib/pipeline.ts`'s own `OUTCOME_FORM_STAGES`, fixed 2026-11-06 for `OutcomeForm`'s stage gate) had been correctly added to every such list, or only most of them. Every list this grep found DOES include it correctly (`CLOSED_STAGES` x2, `DONE_STAGES` x2, `RETURNABLES_EXCLUDED_STAGES`, `BRIEFING_REMINDER_EXCLUDED_STAGES`, `DEADLINE_REMINDER_EXCLUDED_STAGES`, `ACTIVE_STAGES` x2, `reuse-past-submission.tsx`'s inline check) - except one: `app/app/pipeline/page.tsx`'s own column-sort loop.

**The bug, read directly in the real current code.** `pipeline/page.tsx` groups cards into one array per `PIPELINE_STAGES` column, then re-sorts a subset of them:
```ts
const byStage = Object.fromEntries(PIPELINE_STAGES.map((s) => [s, [] as Card[]])) as Record<PipelineStage, Card[]>;
for (const c of cards) byStage[c.stage].push(c);
// Open work sorts by what closes next; outcomes by most recent first.
for (const s of ["submitted", "won", "lost"] as const) {
  byStage[s].sort((a, b) => (b.stageChangedAt ?? "").localeCompare(a.stageChangedAt ?? ""));
}
```
`cards` itself comes from the page's own Supabase query, ordered `closing_date` ascending (`.order("closing_date", { ascending: true })`) - correct for the "open work" columns (`found`/`assessing`/`building`), which the comment says should "sort by what closes next." The comment's OTHER half - "outcomes by most recent first" - is meant to cover every stage that's no longer open work (`submitted`, `briefing_shortlisted`, `won`, `lost`), but the hand-written array only lists 3 of those 4. `git log -p` on this exact line shows why: it was written in commit `ff98f25`, the SAME commit that added the `briefing_shortlisted` column to the board at all (a 2026-11-06 pass fixing the then-separate bug that `briefing_shortlisted` was unreachable through the UI) - the new column was wired into `PIPELINE_STAGES`/`STAGE_META`/`ACTION_LABEL`/`EMPTY_COPY` everywhere else in that same commit, but this one sort array was simply never widened to include it, because nothing forced the two to stay in sync.

**Real, user-visible effect, not cosmetic.** The `briefing_shortlisted` column is rendered via `PIPELINE_STAGES.map((stage) => { const column = byStage[stage]; ... column.map((c) => <TenderCard ... />) })` - a plain Kanban column, same as every other stage. Each card not in "open work" (`!open` for `briefing_shortlisted`) shows its own `stageChangedAt` as its visible date line (`${STAGE_META[c.stage].label} ${shortDate(card.stageChangedAt)}`, e.g. "Briefing / shortlisted 3 Nov 2026") - so the column's own displayed per-card date and its on-screen order disagree the moment it holds more than one card: cards sit in whatever order the original closing-date-ascending query happened to leave them (an order that has nothing to do with when they reached this stage, since every card in this column has already closed), instead of the "newest activity first" order every sibling non-open-work column (`submitted`/`won`/`lost`) correctly shows. A company tracking several tenders through briefing/shortlisting sees the one column on the whole board whose visible order doesn't match what it's showing.

**Fix.** Pulled the whole group-and-sort block out of `pipeline/page.tsx` into a new, pure, exported `groupCardsByStage()` in `lib/pipeline.ts`, sorting against `OUTCOME_FORM_STAGES` (already `["submitted", "briefing_shortlisted", "won", "lost"]` by construction, derived from `NEXT_STAGES`/`OUTCOME_STAGES` - see that constant's own header comment) instead of a 4th hand-written copy of the same stage set:
```ts
export function groupCardsByStage<T extends { stage: PipelineStage; stageChangedAt: string | null }>(
  cards: readonly T[],
): Record<PipelineStage, T[]> {
  const byStage = Object.fromEntries(PIPELINE_STAGES.map((s) => [s, [] as T[]])) as Record<PipelineStage, T[]>;
  for (const c of cards) byStage[c.stage].push(c);
  for (const s of OUTCOME_FORM_STAGES) {
    byStage[s] = [...byStage[s]].sort((a, b) => (b.stageChangedAt ?? "").localeCompare(a.stageChangedAt ?? ""));
  }
  return byStage;
}
```
`pipeline/page.tsx` now just calls `const byStage = groupCardsByStage(cards);`. Reusing `OUTCOME_FORM_STAGES` (rather than naming the 4th list by hand) means a future stage added to that constant's own derivation automatically gets sorted here too - the exact "two hand-kept stage lists had to stay in sync and didn't" root cause that constant's own 2026-11-06 header comment already names, here found independently a third time (after `opportunityInsights.ts`'s `DONE_STAGES` and `OutcomeForm`'s own stage gate).

**Verified red-then-green, myself, real test output, real exit codes, no shell pipe.** Added 4 new tests to `lib/pipeline.spec.ts`'s new `groupCardsByStage` describe block (recency-sorts `briefing_shortlisted`; recency-sorts `submitted`/`won`/`lost` too, confirming the already-correct siblings are unaffected; leaves "open work" columns in input order; every card lands in its own stage's column with every column present even when empty). ### Finding 408 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, pushed directly to `main`): `engine/discovery/opportunity_requirements.py`'s `classify_release()` reported `route: "general"` for a discovered release whose own documents were never actually classified at all - a storage-fetch hiccup on a genuinely-SANRAL-shaped workbook silently became a false "verified general tender" confidence signal on `/admin/discovered-opportunities`

**Where this came from.** The task brief's own suggested starting point - "has Finding 252/253's pagination-helper bug class really been checked for `process_narrative_jobs.py`'s/`process_pack_jobs.py`'s own separate request helpers?" - was run down fully first and confirmed a genuine dead end, not a re-tread to build on: `process_narrative_jobs.py`'s `fail_stale_jobs()` (line 176) and `poll_once()` (line 386) both already route through its own locally-defined `supabase_request_all()` (added by Finding 253, confirmed by its own header comment at lines 74-83), and `process_pack_jobs.py` has no standalone `supabase_request()` function at all - only `SupabaseRest.select()`, already paginated by Finding 252 itself. Finding 253's own write-up (`docs/specs/QA-Edge-Case-Findings.md`, "This lead is now genuinely exhausted") re-confirmed directly: re-grepped all of `engine/` for `status=eq.`/`&select=\*` outside test files - only the four files Finding 253 already fixed match, nothing new. Abandoned this lead as exhausted, per the brief's own instruction to abandon rather than force a technically-real-but-already-closed angle.

Pivoted to a "lowest real mention count in a directory" rotation (the brief's other suggested angle): counted real references to every `engine/*.py` file across both standing docs and picked `engine/discovery/opportunity_requirements.py` (41 total mentions, genuinely low for a file this consequential - it feeds a real admin-facing confidence score) from the newest-built, least-reviewed area of the whole repo (built and verified in the same session that produced `System-Status.md`'s own final two entries - the `discovered_opportunity_requirements`/`compileReadiness.ts` confidence work and the Market Intelligence page). Explicitly NOT one of the files this track's own "already ruled out" list names (`compileReadiness.ts`, `company_profiles.py`, `eskom_bulletin.py`, `tenderRoles.ts`, `positionSuggestions.ts`, `opportunityInsights.ts`, the `/admin/discovered-opportunities` page/row/table files, `marketPricing.ts`'s `tenderFrequencyTrend()`) - this is a different file one layer upstream of `compileReadiness.ts`, which only ever reads what this file writes and was never itself touched.

**The bug, read directly in the real current code.** `classify_release()` downloads every document on file for a release and, when none of them has a classifiable extension (`.xlsm`/`.xlsx`/`.docx` - the only formats `classify_tender.classify_documents()` can actually open), takes an early return before `classify_documents()` is ever called at all:

```python
if not doc_entries:
    if fetch_errors:
        signal = (f"{len(fetch_errors)} of {len(downloaded)} downloaded document(s) looked like a "
                  "workbook or .docx form, but couldn't be re-fetched from storage just now - see "
                  "unreadable_documents.")
    else:
        signal = (f"{len(downloaded)} document(s) downloaded, none of them a workbook or .docx form "
                  "classify_documents() can look inside (PDFs, mostly) - nothing to route on yet.")
    return {
        "release_key": release_key, "source": source, "buyer": buyer,
        "route": "general", "family": None,
        ...
    }
```

This single `"route": "general"` is returned for TWO epistemically different situations, pre-fix:

1. **`else` branch (no `fetch_errors`): every downloaded document has a non-classifiable extension** - e.g. only PDFs. "General" IS a sound conclusion here: a SANRAL Technical/Financial Submission workbook is always `.xlsm`, so if literally no `.xlsm`/`.xlsx`/`.docx` file exists among what downloaded, there is no possible SANRAL workbook to have missed. (This is the shape the file's own existing test, case 6, correctly covers and asserts.)
2. **`if fetch_errors` branch: at least one downloaded document HAS a classifiable extension - could genuinely BE the SANRAL workbook - but its bytes could not be re-fetched from Storage this run** (object moved/deleted since download, or a transient Storage error). Here "general" is NOT sound: the one file that could have proven this is SANRAL is exactly the file `classify_documents()` never got to open. `classify_release()`'s own sibling branch for the analogous "every download failed outright" case (lines 118-127, when `not downloaded` at all) already gets this right - it correctly returns `"route": None` rather than guessing - but this second, narrower "fetch failed after download succeeded" case silently inherited the WRONG sibling's conclusion instead.

Confirmed live with the file's own real `Fake` Supabase/Storage test harness (`test_opportunity_requirements.py`'s own case 7, which the test file already built specifically to exercise this exact fetch-failure shape, for a DIFFERENT assertion - the `signal` text and `unreadable_documents` list - but never checked what `route` came back as): seeding one `.xlsm`-titled row marked `status='downloaded'` with a `storage_path` that is never actually `put()` into the fake Storage (a real 404 on fetch, exactly like an object deleted after `download_discovered_documents.py` ran) produced `route='general'` pre-fix, even though `classify_documents()` was never invoked for this release at all this run.

**Real, concrete downstream effect - not cosmetic.** `app/app/admin/discovered-opportunities/page.tsx` reads `discovered_opportunity_requirements.requirements_status` as `"extracted"` the moment ANY row exists for a release (line 81: `requirements_status === "extracted" ? { status: "extracted" as const, route: r.requirements_route, ... }`), and `classify_all()` upserts a row for this early-return case exactly like every other classified case - so this release's `requirements_status` reads `"extracted"` and `route` reads `"general"`. `app/lib/compileReadiness.ts`'s `assessCompileConfidence()` (deliberately NOT itself touched by this fix - see "already ruled out" above) then runs its documented `requirements.route === "general"` branch: **+15 points**, with the basis line shown verbatim in the admin UI reading **"+15: requirements extraction ran and classified this as a general (non-SANRAL) tender."** That sentence is false for this release: extraction did not run; the one file that might have resolved it simply couldn't be re-fetched. A transient Storage hiccup on a genuinely SANRAL-shaped release therefore silently manufactured a real, visible "yes, we checked, it's a general tender" confidence boost for Sarel reviewing `/admin/discovered-opportunities` - the exact kind of fabricated-certainty signal this whole confidence mechanism's own header comment (`compileReadiness.ts`, "this function does NOT fake that check... reports one of three HONEST states") was written to prevent.

**Fix.** Split the single shared return into its two real cases, each now setting its own honest `route` before the shared return dict is built:

```python
if not doc_entries:
    if fetch_errors:
        signal = (f"{len(fetch_errors)} of {len(downloaded)} downloaded document(s) looked like a "
                  "workbook or .docx form, but couldn't be re-fetched from storage just now - route "
                  "is unknown, not general - see unreadable_documents.")
        route = None
    else:
        signal = (f"{len(downloaded)} document(s) downloaded, none of them a workbook or .docx form "
                  "classify_documents() can look inside (PDFs, mostly) - nothing to route on yet.")
        route = "general"
    return {
        "release_key": release_key, "source": source, "buyer": buyer,
        "route": route, "family": None,
        ...
    }
```

`route: None` is already a valid, already-supported value for this column (migration `0072`: `route text check (route is null or route in ('sanral', 'general'))`, already used by the sibling "every download failed" branch) - no schema change needed. With `route=None`, `compileReadiness.ts`'s existing `else` fallback branch applies unchanged (`"+0: requirements extraction ran but found nothing to route on"`), the same honest-no-bonus outcome the sibling "all downloads failed" case has always gotten for the identical underlying "we don't actually know" situation - no change needed to that file, confirming this bug lived entirely in `opportunity_requirements.py`, not in the already-ruled-out `compileReadiness.ts`.


The one real, specific failure: `FAIL case 7: route is None (unknown), NOT 'general' ... (general)` - exactly the predicted gap, 23 ok / 1 FAIL out of 24 checks.

### Finding 409 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, pushed directly to `main`): `engine/discovery/tender_enrichment.py`'s `_tender_context()` conflated "this tender genuinely has no discovered documents" with "the discovered_opportunities read itself failed" - a transient Supabase/network hiccup silently, permanently downgraded a tender to heuristic-only scope/tags with nothing logged and no retry

**Where this came from.** Extended the task brief's own newly-discovered Angle 11 shape (Finding 408: "a function that genuinely can't classify something vs. a function that COULD have but hit a transient error, both silently reported as the same confident-sounding answer") by sweeping `engine/discovery/*.py` and `engine/pack/*.py` for other functions with multiple early-return/except branches that might make the identical mistake. Most candidates checked out clean and were confirmed NOT instances of this shape: `discovery_downgrades.py`'s `flag_update()`/`is_downgrade()` (ERROR/closed are deliberately excluded from `FIT_RANK`, by design, not conflated); `assess_tender.py`'s `read_release()` (its `depth` states - `metadata_only`/`no_extractable_text`/`full_document` - are already carefully distinguished, with `fetch_notes` only collapsing to `no_extractable_text` when EVERY attempted document failed, not when one of several succeeds); `process_pack_jobs.py`'s `tender_updates_on_record()`/`directors_on_record()` (both already correctly return `None` on a read failure vs. `[]` for a genuinely empty register - explicit "[] = ...; None = couldn't be read" docstrings, already matching the Finding 408 pattern correctly). `tender_enrichment.py`'s `_tender_context()` was the one real hit: its own `except Exception: return {"documents": [], "buyer": None}` silently merges the two situations under the exact same value, with no log line at all - unlike every other failure path in this same file (`member_labels()` logs a `WARNING`; `_llm_scope_result()`/`_fetch_boq_items()` both log their own degrade reason).

**The bug, read directly in the real current code.** `_tender_context(client, tender)` (pre-fix):
```python
try:
    opps = client.select("discovered_opportunities", {"tender_id": tender["id"]})
except Exception:
    return {"documents": [], "buyer": None}
```
`client.select()` (`company_profiles.RestClient.select()`) raises `RuntimeError` on any PostgREST HTTP error (rate limit, 500, auth hiccup) and lets a plain `urllib.error.URLError`/timeout propagate uncaught from a dead connection - both land in this `except Exception`. Pre-fix, that produced the EXACT SAME return value as a tender that genuinely has no `discovered_opportunities` row at all (never went through Discovery) or has rows with no `document_urls` - the honest, legitimate "nothing to read" case `run()`'s heuristic-only fallback exists for. Nothing distinguished the two, and nothing was logged either way.

**Real, concrete downstream effect - not cosmetic.** `run()` (the batch CLI, `python3 tender_enrichment.py run`) calls `_tender_context()` once per unenriched tender, then unconditionally: (1) runs `enrich()` with `documents=[]`/`document_text=None` - the pure heuristic/`description_text` scope path, `confidence: "heuristic"` - and (2) `PATCH`es that tender's `tags_updated_at = now()`, then (3) upserts a `tender_scope_records` row recording that heuristic result as the tender's answer. Step (2) is the real damage: `run()`'s own tenders query (no `--all`) is `rows = [r for r in rows if not r.get("tags_updated_at")]` - once `tags_updated_at` is set, that tender is PERMANENTLY excluded from every future un-flagged run. A transient Supabase read hiccup on ONE tender, on ONE run, therefore baked in a wrong, never-retried "heuristic, no documents" verdict for that tender forever (until someone manually re-runs with `--all`), with zero operator-visible trace that anything had gone wrong - the file's own documented design intent ("THREE possible sources... each honestly labelled by `scope_source` - never silently upgraded or conflated", "No ML - keyword/rule matching... deliberately industry-agnostic") never anticipated this path being reached by a plain I/O failure rather than a genuine absence of documents.

**Confirmed live, with a real in-memory fake client (no network, no live Supabase - same evidence discipline as the file's own existing pure-function tests), reading the actual pre-fix behaviour before touching anything:**
```
PATCHED: [('tenders?id=eq.ta', {...heuristic tags...}), ('tenders?id=eq.tb', {...heuristic tags...})]
UPSERTED tender_ids: ['ta', 'tb']
LOG: Enriching 2 tender(s) (unenriched only) with document fetch...
LOG: Updated tags on 2 tender(s); wrote 2 tender_scope_records row(s) (0 document_confirmed, 2 heuristic).
```
`tb`'s own `discovered_opportunities` read was made to raise `RuntimeError("GET discovered_opportunities failed: 503 Service Unavailable")` - and it was still silently marked enriched, with a wrongly-heuristic `tender_scope_records` row written, and literally nothing in the log mentions the failure.

**Fix.** `_tender_context()` now takes a `log=print` parameter and returns a third key, `error`: `None` for a genuine empty/no-row read, the exception's own message for a failed read - logged immediately, consistent with every other degrade-path in this file:
```python
def _tender_context(client, tender, log=print):
    try:
        opps = client.select("discovered_opportunities", {"tender_id": tender["id"]})
    except Exception as e:
        log(f"  [{tender.get('slug') or ...}] could not read discovered_opportunities for this tender: {type(e).__name__}: {e}")
        return {"documents": [], "buyer": None, "error": str(e)}
    ...
    return {"documents": docs, "buyer": buyer, "error": None}
```
`run()` now checks `ctx["error"]` and, when set, logs a plain "SKIPPED this run ... will retry next run" line and `continue`s - that tender gets NO `tags_updated_at` write and NO `tender_scope_records` row this run, so a plain re-run (or the normal `--all` re-enrichment pass) will try it again instead of having silently and permanently given up on it.

**Verified red-then-green, myself, real test output, real exit codes, no shell pipe.** Added `test_tender_context_no_documents_is_not_an_error()`, `test_tender_context_read_failure_is_flagged_and_logged()` and `test_run_skips_a_tender_whose_document_lookup_failed()` to `test_tender_enrichment.py` (the last one against a minimal in-memory fake `RestClient`, `select`/`_req`/`upsert` only, monkeypatching `te._client` for the duration of the call - no network, no live Supabase, same discipline the rest of this file states up front).
- **RED** (pre-fix source, same new tests, run from a disposable repo-shaped copy under `/tmp` so relative config paths still resolve): `python3 test_tender_enrichment.py` -> **exit 1**, crashes on the very first new test (`TypeError: _tender_context() got an unexpected keyword argument 'log'`) - the signature itself is part of the fix. Running the 3 new tests individually against the pre-fix module (bypassing that crash to see the real-world shape manifest): the first two raise the same `TypeError`; the third (`test_run_skips_a_tender_whose_document_lookup_failed`, which calls the OLD 2-arg signature internally via `run()`) runs to completion but **4 of its 6 assertions FAIL** - exactly the predicted gap: `tb` IS marked `tags_updated_at`, `tb` DOES get a `tender_scope_records` row, and nothing is logged about the failure.
- **GREEN** (fix applied): `python3 test_tender_enrichment.py` -> **exit 0**, `0 failure(s)`, **88/88** checks pass (counted by wrapping `check()` and tallying every call across the whole file's `main()`, not estimated) - including all **12** checks across the 3 new tests.

**A genuine pre-existing-test regression caught by the full sweep, not glossed over.** The first full-regression run surfaced `engine/discovery/test_tender_enrichment_cli.py` (a SEPARATE, I/O-mocking test file for this same module, deliberately split from the pure-function `test_tender_enrichment.py` - see its own docstring) failing: `test_tender_context_never_raises_when_table_read_fails()` asserted `ctx == {"documents": [], "buyer": None}` on a broken read - i.e. it had encoded the PRE-FIX conflated behaviour as the expected, correct one. ### Finding 410 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, pushed directly to `main`): `watch_tender_updates.py`'s `OcdsDays` cached a transient OCDS-feed read FAILURE for one day the exact same way it cached a genuine "nothing published that day", and that one shared cache poisoned the "release not found" check for every OTHER actively-pursued eTenders tender in the same run, not just the one being checked when the read actually failed

**Baseline re-verified live, twice, exactly as instructed.** First, before drafting: `git fetch origin main` - HEAD `71861f63888b2b630f4cd155a7886ea5f80c5bce` (Finding 409's own commit), matching the task brief exactly; `git status` clean. `grep -oE "^### Finding [0-9]+" docs/specs/QA-Edge-Case-Findings.md | grep -oE "[0-9]+" | sort -n | tail` on `main`'s own current copy of this file - last real entry **409**. `gh api repos/sareljvr2024/tender-tool/pulls --paginate -X GET -f state=open -f per_page=100` - exactly **70** open PRs (`#164`/`#165`/`#176`-`#244`), matching the task brief exactly; grepped every title/branch for "410"/"finding-410" - none. **410** confirmed next-free. Second, immediately before pushing: `git fetch origin main` again - HEAD unchanged at `71861f6`, no sibling-track commit landed in between; same grep against the re-fetched file - still **409** as the last real entry; open-PR count re-confirmed at **70** via the same API call, same number list, none touched.

**Mandatory open-PR cross-check by exact filename (not bug vocabulary), before writing the fix.** Grepped all 70 open PR titles/branches for `watch_tender_updates`/`ocds`/`OcdsDays` - exactly one hit, PR #216 ("fix: Finding 333 - watch_tender_updates.py's own writer was never wired into any scheduled workflow"). Read its real changed-file list (`gh api repos/sareljvr2024/tender-tool/pulls/216/files -q '.[].filename'`): `.github/workflows/corrigendum-alerts.yml`, `.github/workflows/tender-update-watch.yml`, `app/lib/workflowRegistry.ts`/`.spec.ts`, `docs/specs/QA-Edge-Case-Findings.md`, `docs/specs/System-Status.md`, `engine/notify/record_heartbeat.py` - PR #216 does not touch `engine/discovery/watch_tender_updates.py` or its test file at all; its own PR body states so explicitly ("the script itself was not modified, only newly scheduled"). No real collision, confirmed by diff file list, not assumed from the title alone.

**Where this came from.** A fresh read of `engine/discovery/watch_tender_updates.py` end to end (not yet individually read by this lineage as a whole system, only patched twice for narrow, unrelated gaps - the OCDS-vs-SANRAL alerting-symmetry fix and the `briefing_shortlisted` `ACTIVE_STAGES` addition) looking for a genuinely new angle beyond every exhausted one named in this pass's own task brief. `OcdsDays` is this file's own small in-run cache for one-day OCDS windows, built once per `run()` call and shared, via the single `ocds` object `run()` passes to every pursued tender's own `check_tender()` call in its one loop over `active_pursuits()`. Its own docstring (pre-fix) promised only "each fetched at most once per run" - read `releases()` against that promise literally: on a successful fetch it caches the result; on a failed fetch (network/API error) it ALSO caches a value - `[]` - under the exact same key, with no way for anything downstream to tell "this day was read and genuinely had nothing" from "this day's read blew up".

**Why `today` specifically makes this reachable, not a one-in-a-million edge case.** `find()`'s own candidate-day list for ANY pursued eTenders tender always starts with `today` and the two days before it (`RECENT_DAYS = 3`), before any tender-specific `known_day`/`discovered_day` walk-back - so `today` is a candidate day for literally every pursued eTenders tender checked in a given run, every run. This watch's own header states it runs "every couple of hours" against "a handful of one-day OCDS windows and SANRAL pages" - i.e. it is completely ordinary, not rare, for more than one pursued eTenders tender to need `today`'s window in the same run. A single transient OCDS API blip (a timeout, a 5xx, a dropped connection - exactly the class `releases()`'s own `except Exception` is written to survive) hit while checking whichever tender happens to be processed FIRST in that run's loop poisons `today`'s cache entry to `[]` for the rest of that same run. Every subsequent pursued tender whose release might genuinely be sitting in `today`'s window then has `find()` silently reuse that cached `[]` - no second attempt is ever made - and, finding no match in any window, reports "OCDS release {ocid} not found in the windows read": a spurious `system_alerts.record(..., "error", ...)` call (noise Sarel would see on `/admin`) AND a silently skipped update-check for that tender this run (no addendum, no closing-date change, no briefing-date change gets reported to any company pursuing it, even if one genuinely posted). Self-heals on the NEXT run (`run()` builds a fresh `OcdsDays` instance each time, so the poisoned cache does not persist to disk or across runs) - but within the run that hits it, every healthy, unrelated tender sharing that day is wrongly told its own release could not be found, for a reason that has nothing to do with that tender at all.

**Confirmed live, not just reasoned about - real RED repro with the actual pre-fix module.** Added `test_transient_day_fetch_failure_does_not_poison_other_pursued_tenders()` to `engine/discovery/test_watch_tender_updates.py`: two pursued eTenders tenders, t1 and t2 (processed in that order, by `tender_packs` insertion order), each with its own real release sitting on `today` - the only day either can be found on. `fetch_ocds_day` raises on its first call (today's fetch, made while checking t1) and succeeds on every call after. Stashed only the production file (`git stash push -- engine/discovery/watch_tender_updates.py`, keeping the new test) and ran the test file directly against the real, unmodified pre-fix module:
```
$ python3 test_watch_tender_updates.py
...
  OCDS 2026-11-07: fetch failed (transient network blip)
[system-alert] tender_updates error: The OCDS feed could not be read for one day: RuntimeError: transient network blip
[system-alert] tender_updates error: A pursued eTenders tender's OCDS release could not be found in the windows this run checked: OCDS release ocds-test-1 not found in the windows read
[system-alert] tender_updates error: A pursued eTenders tender's OCDS release could not be found in the windows this run checked: OCDS release ocds-test-2 not found in the windows read
  PASS t1 (the tender actually hit by the transient failure) still gets its own 'not found' alert, unchanged ({'t2', 't1'})
  FAIL t2's own release - genuinely findable with a fresh fetch - must not be wrongly reported as 'not found' just because t1's transient failure poisoned today's cache first (tenders reported missing: {'t2', 't1'}) - THIS IS THE FIX THIS TEST EXISTS FOR
  FAIL t2's own watch state shows its release genuinely found this run, not a false 'not found' (...)
  FAIL today's feed was fetched exactly twice - once that failed (checking t1), once that succeeded (checking t2) - a failed fetch must never be cached as a genuine empty day (calls=1)

3 FAILED:
  - t2's own release - genuinely findable with a fresh fetch - must not be wrongly reported as 'not found' ...
  - t2's own watch state shows its release genuinely found this run, not a false 'not found' ...
  - today's feed was fetched exactly twice ... (calls=1)
```
**Exit code: 1** (checked directly, no pipe). t2 - a tender with nothing at all wrong with it - was wrongly reported as having a missing release, purely because t1's unrelated transient failure ran first in the same loop, exactly as predicted: `calls=1` proves `fetch_ocds_day` was never even attempted a second time for `today` while checking t2.

**Fix.** `OcdsDays.releases()`: a failed fetch is still reported exactly as before (same `print()`/`system_alerts.record(..., "error", ...)` call, unchanged severity and message) but is no longer written into `self.cache` - it returns `[]` for that one call only, leaving the day uncached so the NEXT caller that needs it (whether that's the same tender trying a different candidate day, or a different tender later in the same run) gets its own fresh `fetch_day()` attempt rather than silently inheriting someone else's failure. A genuinely successful fetch (including one that legitimately found nothing) is still cached exactly as before - "fetched at most once per run" now actually means "fetched", not "attempted". `find()` itself, `check_tender()`, and every call site's own error-reporting shape are completely untouched - this is a one-function, cache-only fix.

**Verified red-then-green, myself, real test output, real exit codes, no shell pipe.**
- **RED** (pre-fix module, via `git stash push -- engine/discovery/watch_tender_updates.py` keeping only the new test, run from the real `engine/discovery/` directory): `python3 test_watch_tender_updates.py` -> **exit 1**, **3 FAILED** (quoted above) - reproduces the real bug live, not hypothetically.
- **GREEN** (`git stash pop` to restore the fix): `python3 test_watch_tender_updates.py` -> **exit 0**, **ALL PASSED** - all 3 test functions (the two pre-existing OCDS-vs-SANRAL symmetry tests, unchanged and still passing, plus the new one, **12 checks total** across the file, counted from the real `PASS`/`FAIL` lines printed) pass, including `calls=2` (today's feed genuinely refetched once t1's failure is no longer cached) and t2's own `tender_watch_state` row showing `last_error: None`, `last_found_at` set - its release genuinely found.

**Full regression, all 92 `engine/**/test_*.py` files (`find engine -name "test_*.py" | wc -l` - 92, confirmed by direct count, not estimated), each run individually, in its own file's directory, with a 180-second-per-file timeout, each file's own bare exit code checked immediately, never through a pipe:** **91 passed, 1 pre-existing, unrelated failure** - `engine/discovery/test_download_documents.py`, `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'playwright'` (the same missing-optional-dependency sandbox gap Findings 408 and 409 both already hit and noted; confirmed by its own traceback to have nothing to do with this change - it fails identically on an unmodified checkout). `engine/discovery/test_watch_tender_updates.py` itself (the file this fix touches) passed within that same full sweep, run a second time on its own immediately after for the exact RED/GREEN evidence above.

Small, safe fix, no risk factor present -> pushed directly to `main`, per this track's own guardrail.

**Why this is not a re-tread of any exhausted angle.** Not Angle 11 (the early-return/except conflation feeding a status/confidence/retry field, Findings 408/409) - `releases()`'s own bug is a shared, in-memory, within-one-run CACHE being poisoned across tenders, not a function returning the same value for two epistemically different inputs to ONE caller; the two situations here (day genuinely empty vs. day's read failed) are already reported with completely different messages and severities to the SAME caller, as they always were - the bug is that the resulting cache entry is then blindly reused by every OTHER tender's own lookup in the same run, a cross-call-sharing bug this lineage has not named before. ### Finding 411 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, pushed directly to `main`): `scripts/send-operational-alerts.ts`'s print/transit cutoff, compulsory-briefing countdown and clarification-window-expiry stages all used the OPT-IN-gated `operationalRecipients()` instead of `criticalBidRecipients()` - the exact "cannot be disabled for active bidders" alert category migration 0093's own header names - so every company that had never found and toggled the generic "Email notifications" setting on `/company` (the out-of-the-box state for every company, by migration 0073's own default) got NONE of these 3 alerts at all

**Area:** `app/scripts/send-operational-alerts.ts` (the shared `companyRecipients` import, used by all 3 of this script's stages), plus `app/app/company/Notifications.tsx`'s own rendered copy. Rotation this pass: notify. Mention-count heuristic picked `app/lib/notificationRecipients.ts` (17 mentions, lowest in the directory) as the starting point.

**How this was found.** `notificationRecipients.ts`'s own `criticalBidRecipients()` has a detailed docstring explaining why 3 (later 4, Finding 163) alert types bypass `company_members.daily_digest_opt_in` entirely: "gating these... on it would mean a company's own bidding team silently misses an addendum or a closing deadline unless someone found and clicked a toggle described as a generic 'daily digest'." Checked every real caller of both `operationalRecipients()`/`criticalBidRecipients()` (confirmed by grep, not guessed): `send-discovered-tenders.ts` (the actual daily digest - matches `operationalRecipients()`'s own test file describe-block title, "the discovered-tenders digest's own gate") and `send-operational-alerts.ts` are the only two real callers of `operationalRecipients()`. But `send-operational-alerts.ts` is NOT the discovered-tenders digest - its own header describes its 3 stages as "critical operational alerts": a 48-hour physical print/transit cutoff, a 5-day/24-hour compulsory-briefing countdown, and a 10-day/2-day clarification-window-expiry reminder. All 3 are genuinely bid-specific and time-critical, the same category already named in `criticalBidRecipients()`'s own docstring - yet all 3 were resolving recipients through the OPT-IN-gated function instead.

**The decisive, explicit confirmation this is a contract violation, not a judgment call.** Migration `0093_notification_engine.sql`'s own header states outright: "every notification type this migration's own two tables serve is either already covered by an existing, narrower opt-in (`company_members.daily_digest_opt_in`, 0073) **or is an operational/compliance alert the brief itself says 'cannot be disabled for active bidders'**." Sarel's own brief, in Sarel's own words, already classifies this entire category of alert as non-optional. Migration `0073_daily_digest_opt_in.sql`'s own column comment confirms the opt-in default: `daily_digest_opt_in boolean not null default false` - "Sarel's own instruction was an opt-in, not an opt-out, feature." Put together: every company, from the moment it signs up, defaults to receiving NONE of these 3 "cannot be disabled" alerts, unless a member happens to find and toggle a setting labelled generically "Email notifications" (and described on that same page as being about "a once-a-day email when a new tender matching your profile is found" - nothing about print cutoffs or briefings at all).

**Confirmed live and reachable - this is the default state for every company, not an edge case.** Traced `send-operational-alerts.ts`'s own `import { operationalRecipients as companyRecipients }`, used identically by all 3 of `runPrintCutoff()`/`runBriefingReminders()`/`runClarificationWindow()`. `operationalRecipients()` filters on `m.daily_digest_opt_in` being `true`; with the column defaulting to `false` for every member, a company that has never touched this toggle - which 32 of 33 real companies had never done, per `Notifications.tsx`'s own 2026-10-30 history cited in its header comment - gets zero recipients back from every one of these 3 stages, every time, forever. The real-world consequence: a SANRAL bidder could miss the news that their physical submission needs to go to print within 48 hours, or that attendance at a compulsory briefing session is due tomorrow (in SA public procurement, missing a compulsory briefing is typically an absolute, non-waivable disqualifier) - silently, with the product never having sent anything to warn them, despite Sarel's own brief explicitly requiring these alerts to be undisable-able.

**Fix.** One import swap in `send-operational-alerts.ts` (`operationalRecipients as companyRecipients` -> `criticalBidRecipients as companyRecipients`) fixes all 3 call sites at once, since they share the one alias. Updated `Notifications.tsx`'s own rendered copy (already corrected once for Finding 341's compliance-digest omission) to name all 7 now-bypassing categories, so the toggle's own description stays honest about what it does and doesn't control.

**Verified red-then-green, myself, real test output.** Added one new test per stage to `send-operational-alerts.spec.ts` (`daily_digest_opt_in: false`, a real email on file - the realistic default-state shape, not an empty-company edge case) asserting the claim/send is actually attempted, not skipped as "zero recipients."
- **RED** (`git apply -R` on just the production file's diff): `npx vitest run scripts/send-operational-alerts.spec.ts` - **3 failed, 7 passed** - all three failures on the new "still attempts to claim/send for an opted-out member" assertions, the other 7 pre-existing tests (which all use either `daily_digest_opt_in: true` or an empty-recipients case) unaffected, confirming the fix is narrowly targeted.
- **GREEN** (`git apply` to reapply): **10 passed, 0 failed**.
- `npx tsc --noEmit` clean (pre-existing, unrelated `date-fns`/`react-day-picker` module-resolution gaps elsewhere, confirmed identical before/after). `npx eslint` clean on all 3 changed files. Full `npx vitest run`: 683 passed / 6 failed, all 6 the same pre-existing, unrelated missing-`date-fns`-module sandbox gap already confirmed elsewhere this session, reproduced identically with this change reverted.

**Why a direct push to `main`, not a PR.** Pure TypeScript recipient-resolution logic - the same single-line import swap already made, and already pushed directly, for 4 other alert types (corrigenda/addenda, returnables, closing-deadline, compliance-expiry) over the preceding two weeks. No RLS/migration/money-path/worker-image surface; `criticalBidRecipients()` itself is unchanged (already live, already tested, already proven correct by its own 4 existing callers) - this fix only changes which of two already-existing, already-correct functions 3 call sites point at.

### Finding 412 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, pushed directly to `main`): `app/lib/titleCase.ts`'s `displayTenderTitle()` ran its digit-preservation check AFTER its mid-title-lowercase check, so a letter+digit road/section code whose bare letters collide with a stop word (SANRAL's own "Section A1 to A2" shape, or AT2/ON3/OR5) silently lost its digit guarantee and rendered lowercase ("a1"/"a2"/"at2") on every ALL-CAPS tender title shown on `/discovery` and the Tender Workspace header

**Baseline re-verified live, twice, exactly as instructed.** First, before drafting: `git fetch origin main` - HEAD `97b37ecd4c4b71eaf41a617e2377e5e05cf60869` (Finding 411's own commit), matching this pass's own starting state exactly; `git status` clean. `grep -oE "^### Finding [0-9]+" docs/specs/QA-Edge-Case-Findings.md | grep -oE "[0-9]+" | sort -n | tail` on `main`'s own current copy of this file - last real entry **411**. `gh api repos/sareljvr2024/tender-tool/pulls --paginate -X GET -f state=open -f per_page=100` - exactly **70** open PRs (`#164`/`#165`/`#176`-`#244`); grepped every title for "412"/"titlecase" - none. **412** confirmed next-free. Second, immediately before pushing: `git fetch origin main` again - HEAD unchanged at `97b37ec`, no sibling-track commit landed in between; same grep against the re-fetched file - still **411** as the last real entry.

**Mandatory open-PR cross-check by exact filename, before writing the fix.** Pulled every open PR's own changed-file list (`gh api repos/sareljvr2024/tender-tool/pulls/<n>/files -q '.[].filename'` for all 70, one call per PR, 283 files total) and grepped for `titleCase` (case-insensitive) - zero hits across every open PR. `titleCase.ts`/`titleCase.test.ts` are untouched by any in-flight branch.

**Where this came from.** A fresh "lowest real mention count in a directory not yet reviewed" rotation over `app/lib/*.ts`, counting each file's own mentions across `QA-Edge-Case-Findings.md`+`System-Status.md`. `titleCase.ts` (introduced 2026-10-23, "Phase 2 Opportunities triage" brief - "clean title casing, not raw scraped ALL-CAPS" for government portals that publish titles fully in capitals) had never been independently re-audited since the one earlier fix already recorded in its own header comment (the hyphenated-word, "RE-ADVERTISED"/"CO-ORDINATION" fix). Read `titleCaseWord()` end to end against its own stated invariants, one of which is explicitly tested: "a reference code with digits is left exactly as-is."

**The bug.** `titleCaseWord(word, isFirst)` ran two checks in this order: (1) `if (!isFirst && LOWERCASE_MID_WORDS.has(bare.toLowerCase())) return word.toLowerCase();` and only then (2) `if (/\d/.test(word) || KNOWN_ACRONYMS.has(bare)) return word;` - where `bare` is `word` with every non-letter character (digits included) stripped out first. For a word like `"A1"` mid-title, `bare` is `"A"`, and `"a"` is one of `LOWERCASE_MID_WORDS`'s own entries (the article "a") - so check (1) fires FIRST and returns `"a1"`, a full two characters before check (2) - the one that is supposed to protect anything with a digit - ever gets a chance to run. The existing, already-passing test for the digit guarantee ("a reference code with digits is left exactly as-is") only ever exercised a digit-and-punctuation-only code (`"R.396-010-2025/1F"`), whose `bare` (`"F"`) never collides with a stop word, so this gap was never caught by it.

**Why this is real and reachable, not a contrived input.** South African road/civil tenders (this product's own primary SANRAL/NRA domain) routinely name sections, routes and zones with a single letter plus a number - "Section A1", "Section A2", and the module's own `LOWERCASE_MID_WORDS` set (`a, an, and, at, for, in, of, on, or, the, to, with`) has SEVEN single/two-letter entries that collide with this exact shape the moment a digit is appended: `A1/A2/A9`, `AN3`, `AT2`, `IN5`, `ON3`, `OR5`, `TO4`. Every government procurement portal this module's own header names (SANRAL, Rand Water, Eskom, municipal boards) "routinely publishes titles fully in capitals" - the exact precondition (`isAllCaps()`) that triggers this transform at all. A real tender titled e.g. `"UPGRADE OF SECTION A1 TO A2"` (or an Eskom-style notice naming a feeder/substation like `"AT2"`) would have rendered, on both `/discovery` and the Tender Workspace header (`app/app/tenders/[id]/page.tsx`), as `"Upgrade of Section a1 to a2"` - a specific real road section's own name mangled into lowercase on the very pages a bidder reads to confirm which project a tender actually refers to.

**Confirmed live, real RED repro against the actual pre-fix module, not just reasoned about.**
```
$ node --experimental-strip-types -e '
import { displayTenderTitle } from "./lib/titleCase.ts";
console.log(JSON.stringify(displayTenderTitle("UPGRADE OF SECTION A1 TO A2")));
console.log(JSON.stringify(displayTenderTitle("MAINTENANCE OF AT2 PUMP STATION")));
'
"Upgrade of Section a1 to a2"
"Maintenance of at2 Pump Station"
```

**Fix.** Reordered the two checks in `titleCaseWord()` so the digit/`KNOWN_ACRONYMS` guard runs FIRST (returning the word exactly as-is the moment it carries a digit or is a known acronym), and the `LOWERCASE_MID_WORDS` mid-title check runs second, only for a word with no digit. Verified by inspection and by the regression tests below that no existing acronym/stop-word pair overlaps (`KNOWN_ACRONYMS` and `LOWERCASE_MID_WORDS` share no entry), so every previously-correct case ("AND"/"OF"/"WAR"/"ZK"/"SANRAL"/the hyphenated "RE-ADVERTISED" case/the punctuation-only reference code) is completely unaffected by the reorder - confirmed by re-running every one of the file's existing tests unchanged. Deliberately does NOT touch the separate, pre-existing and structurally different ambiguity for a bare stop-word with no digit at all (e.g. "OR" in "OR TAMBO", the real district municipality/airport name, still reads as the conjunction "or" after this fix) - that is the identical kind of accepted limitation this function's own comment already names for "WAR" vs. "ZK" (no dictionary to disambiguate a real short word from a real short name/initialism), not something a reorder of the digit check can or should resolve, and not claimed as fixed here.

**Verified red-then-green, myself, real test output, real exit codes, no shell pipe.** Added two new tests to `app/lib/titleCase.test.ts` (the exact `A1`/`A2` SANRAL-section shape, plus every other `LOWERCASE_MID_WORDS` entry paired with a digit: `AT2`, `ON3`, `OR5`).
- **RED** (`git stash push -- app/lib/titleCase.ts`, keeping only the new tests, run against the real, unmodified pre-fix module from `app/`): `node --experimental-strip-types --test lib/titleCase.test.ts` -> **exit 1**, **9 tests, 7 pass, 2 fail** - both failures exactly the two new assertions (`'Upgrade of Section a1 to a2'` vs. expected `'Upgrade of Section A1 to A2'`; `'Maintenance of at2 Pump Station'` vs. expected `'Maintenance of AT2 Pump Station'`), every pre-existing test still passing.
- **GREEN** (`git stash pop` to restore the fix): `node --experimental-strip-types --test lib/titleCase.test.ts` -> **exit 0**, **9 tests, 9 pass, 0 fail**.

**Full regression.** `npx tsc --noEmit` (whole `app/` tree) -> **exit 0**, clean. `npx eslint lib/titleCase.ts lib/titleCase.test.ts` -> **exit 0**, clean. `npx vitest run` (the full suite; `titleCase.test.ts` itself runs under node's own test runner, not vitest, same convention as this codebase's other `node --experimental-strip-types --test` files, so it is not double-counted here) -> **exit 0**, **86 test files, 715 tests, all passed**. This fix touches no Python engine code (`git diff --stat` shows only the two TypeScript files), so the `engine/**/test_*.py` sweep was not re-run for it - consistent with this track's own precedent for a pure-TypeScript fix (e.g. Finding 411's own write-up).

**Guardrail/risk classification, each factor checked, not assumed.** Pure TypeScript, one pure function in one file (`titleCase.ts`) plus its own test file. **No RLS** - zero SQL/migration touched. **No money/payment path.** **No hard-stop/disqualification gate** - this function never gates pack generation, compliance or disqualification logic anywhere; it is a cosmetic display transform, and its own header states the stored title is never rewritten. **No worker-image/deployment change** - no Dockerfile, no dependency, no workflow YAML touched. **No multi-table schema surface** - zero migration, zero schema change. **Not one of the six named files** (`fill_a_forms.py`/`fill_sbd_docx.py`/`fill_flat_pdf.py`/`make_envelope_covers.py`/`process_narrative_jobs.py`/`build_docx.py`). **Not a correctness fix to a document a company signs/submits** - confirmed by grep: `titleCase.ts`/`displayTenderTitle` is imported only by `app/app/discovery/page.tsx` and `app/app/tenders/[id]/page.tsx` (both read-only display pages), and neither `pack-review.tsx` nor `submission-pack.tsx` imports this file, even transitively (it has zero imports of its own, and its only two consumers are page components, not shared data-loading modules). Small, safe fix, no risk factor present -> pushed directly to `main`, per this track's own guardrail.

**Why this is not a re-tread of any exhausted angle.** Not the naive-UTC class (no date/time code anywhere in this file). Not Angle 12's per-run cache poisoning (no cache, no cross-item shared state - a pure, stateless string transform called once per word). Not the storage-orphan class, the `build_general_pack.py` not_found drop, the `fill_flat_pdf.py` FORMS regex sweep, the TS-side-guard-vs-Python-sibling comparison, the exact-day/threshold-match no-missed-run-safety shape, the stale-position-reassignment shape, the dispatch_status-not-checked shape, the hand-kept-`pipeline_stage`-list-drift shape, or Angle 11's early-return/epistemic-conflation shape - none of those mechanisms exist in a pure, single-word text-casing function. Not a re-tread of this same file's own one prior fix (the hyphenated-word/multi-run `/g`-flag fix) - that fix was about which LETTER RUNS inside one word get title-cased; this fix is about which of two independent CONDITIONS on the whole word gets checked first. Not `tenderRoles.ts`, `positionSuggestions.ts`, `opportunityInsights.ts`, `compileReadiness.ts`, or any other file on this track's own already-ruled-out list.

The adjacent "OR Tambo" ambiguity named above is explicitly NOT a new standing item either - it is the same already-accepted, already-documented "WAR"/"ZK" limitation this file's own header comment already names and declines to chase, just illustrated with a real South African place name rather than an ordinary word.

### Finding 413 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, pushed directly to `main`): `app/lib/analyticsLogic.ts`'s `monthKey()` read the UTC calendar month of a raw `stage_changed_at` timestamp instead of its real South African (SAST) one, silently bucketing a win/loss decision made just after SAST midnight into the Analytics "Win/loss trend" chart's PREVIOUS month

**Baseline re-verified live, twice, exactly as instructed.** First, before drafting: `git fetch origin main` - HEAD `59da4c3e5131a650ef5606026c7886c32f815e81` (Finding 412's own commit), matching this pass's own starting state exactly; `git status` clean except this pass's own two edited files. `grep -oE "^### Finding [0-9]+" docs/specs/QA-Edge-Case-Findings.md | grep -oE "[0-9]+" | sort -n | tail` on `main`'s own current copy of this file - last real entry **412**. `gh api repos/sareljvr2024/tender-tool/pulls -X GET -f state=open -f per_page=100` - exactly **70** open PRs; grepped every title for "413"/"analyticslogic"/"win/loss"/"analytics" - none. **413** confirmed next-free. Second, immediately before pushing (below): `git fetch origin main` again - HEAD unchanged, no sibling-track commit landed in between; same grep against the re-fetched file - still **412** as the last real entry.

**Mandatory open-PR cross-check by exact filename, before writing the fix.** Pulled every one of the 70 open PRs' own changed-file lists (`gh api repos/sareljvr2024/tender-tool/pulls/<n>/files`, one call per PR) and grepped for `analyticsLogic` (case-insensitive) - zero hits on the filename itself. One adjacency hit on `app/app/analytics/page.tsx` (PR #164, "savings-counter-capacity-messaging"): read that PR's own diff hunks for the file directly (`gh api .../pulls/164/files` -> `.patch`) - its two hunks touch only the imports block (adding `fetchCompanySubscription`/`PLAN_MONTHLY_ZAR`) and the savings-summary `Promise.all`/`monthlyPlanPriceZar` block, both well above and unrelated to the win/loss-trend section (`decidedEntries`/`buildWinLossTrend` call) this fix touches - confirmed a real non-collision, not assumed from the filename match alone.

**Where this came from.** A fresh "lowest real mention count in a directory not yet reviewed this lineage" rotation over `app/lib/*.ts`, after an extended search across `app/lib`, `app/app/**`, `engine/**` and `app/scripts/**` for low-mention files that turned up several already-exhausted or too-low-severity leads (a falsy-zero `locMatch.points` display gap in `lib/scoreOutlookChips.ts`'s locality chip, reachable only for a functionality-kind locality row scored literally zero points - judged theoretical, not pursued; the `expandDisciplines()`/`matched_by_group_tag` angle, already fixed by the 2026-11-04 pass scoped to `opportunityDisciplineMatch.ts` alone; several hand-kept `pipeline_stage` lists, all already consistent). `app/lib/analyticsLogic.ts` (42 lines) had one prior mention (`QA-Edge-Case-Findings.md`'s own search-technique write-up, which checked `buildWinLossTrend()`'s `won`/`lost` stage filter against `normalizeStage()` and the `'bidding'` legacy value - a clean negative - but never examined either function's date/timezone handling at all). Re-reading `monthKey()`/`buildWinLossTrend()` end to end against `lib/dates.ts`'s own already-documented Finding 289/290 precedent (a day-level naive-UTC-slice bug, independently present at a second site, `engine/notify/daily_digest.py`'s `submission_due_signals()`) raised the obvious question this file had never been asked: does the exact same bug class exist here, one level up, at MONTH granularity?

**The bug.** `monthKey(dateStr)` was `return dateStr.slice(0, 7);` - a naive slice of the raw ISO string. `decidedAt` (the only caller, `app/app/analytics/page.tsx`) is `tender_packs.stage_changed_at`, a `timestamptz` set by `0021_tender_pipeline_stage.sql`'s own trigger (`new.stage_changed_at := now();`) and read back over PostgREST as a UTC-offset ISO string. For any decision recorded while its UTC time-of-day is 22:00-23:59:59, that string's own first 7 characters read the UTC calendar month, which is the WRONG, EARLIER month once converted to the real South African (SAST, UTC+2, no DST) calendar the tender/bidding world actually runs on: e.g. `"2026-11-30T23:30:00Z"` is `2026-12-01 01:30` in SAST - genuinely December - but `.slice(0, 7)` reads `"2026-11"`. `buildWinLossTrend()`'s own bucket-generation loop had the matching, second half of the same bug: it anchored the "current month" on `now.getFullYear()`/`now.getMonth()` directly - the Node process's own LOCAL time zone, which is UTC on every runtime this app actually deploys to (no `TZ` env var is set anywhere in this repo; confirmed live in this sandbox: `getFullYear()`/`getMonth()` and `getUTCFullYear()`/`getUTCMonth()` return identical values for the same `Date`). So the two sides of this function were internally self-consistent (both naively UTC, so they agreed with EACH OTHER) but both wrong relative to the real SAST month a South African user is actually in - exactly the same "a company's real calendar day/month is SAST, not the database's storage timezone" shape Finding 289 already established for `daysUntil()`, just never ported to this file's own month-level math.

**Why this is real and reachable, not hypothetical.** `stage_changed_at` is written by an ordinary database trigger every time any user moves a tender to `won`/`lost` on the Bids board (`app/app/pipeline/page.tsx`) - an entirely normal, frequent user action with no unusual precondition. Roughly 2 of every 24 hours (SAST 00:00-01:59, i.e. UTC 22:00-23:59 the day before) is in the broken window - about 8% of all possible decision times, every single day, not a rare edge case. The user-visible effect is concrete and silent: a win or loss recorded in that window shows up, on `/analytics`'s own "Win/loss trend" chart, under the PREVIOUS month's bar instead of the real one - understating last month's actual win/loss activity and overstating (or inventing a nonzero bar for) the month before it, with no error, no log line, and no way for Sarel or a customer looking at their own trend chart to know a count is misplaced.

**Confirmed live, real RED repro against the actual pre-fix module, not just reasoned about.**
```
$ node --experimental-strip-types -e '
import { monthKey } from "./lib/analyticsLogic.ts";
console.log(monthKey("2026-11-30T23:30:00Z"));
'
2026-11
```
(the real SAST calendar month for that instant is `2026-12`).

**Fix.** `monthKey()` now shifts the timestamp by a shared `SAST_OFFSET_MS` (`2 * 60 * 60 * 1000`, the same UTC+2/no-DST fact `lib/dates.ts`'s own `closingDayOf()` already relies on) before reading the calendar month: `new Date(new Date(dateStr).getTime() + SAST_OFFSET_MS).toISOString().slice(0, 7)`. `buildWinLossTrend()` now shifts `now` the identical way first, then reads `getUTCFullYear()`/`getUTCMonth()` off the SHIFTED instant (not the unshifted process-local `now.getFullYear()`/`getMonth()`) to anchor its "current month," and generates the preceding months by plain integer year/month arithmetic (`anchorYear * 12 + anchorMonth - i`, floor-divided/modded back into year+month) rather than `new Date(now.getFullYear(), now.getMonth() - i, 1)`, which depended on the same host-local-timezone reading this fix removes. Every existing test (all using mid-day/mid-month timestamps, nowhere near a SAST boundary) is completely unaffected by this reorder-of-basis, since shifting a mid-day timestamp by 2 hours never crosses a calendar-month line.

**Verified red-then-green, myself, real test output, real exit codes, no shell pipe.** Added 4 new assertions to `app/lib/analyticsLogic.spec.ts`: one direct `monthKey()` pair (the `2026-11-30T23:30:00Z` -> `"2026-12"` boundary case, plus a non-boundary control the same number of hours earlier that must still read `"2026-11"`, proving this isn't a blanket "always add a month" fix), and two `buildWinLossTrend()` cases - one with `now` safely inside December (both UTC and SAST) and a `decidedAt` straddling the SAST boundary (isolates the `monthKey()` half of the bug: the entry used to be silently dropped from every bucket, not just miscounted into the wrong one), and one with the real current instant itself straddling the boundary (isolates the bucket-anchoring half: the whole window's own "current month" used to be one month early).
- **RED** (`git stash push -- app/lib/analyticsLogic.ts`, keeping only the new tests, run against the real, unmodified pre-fix module): `npx vitest run lib/analyticsLogic.spec.ts` -> **exit 1**, **1 test file failed, 9 tests total, 3 failed / 6 passed** - all three failures exactly the three new boundary-straddling assertions (the `monthKey()` boundary assertion plus both new `buildWinLossTrend()` cases); the fourth new assertion (the non-boundary control) and every pre-existing test passed unchanged.
- **GREEN** (`git stash pop` to restore the fix): `npx vitest run lib/analyticsLogic.spec.ts` -> **exit 0**, **1 test file passed, 9 tests, 9 passed, 0 failed**.

**Full regression.** `npx tsc --noEmit` (whole `app/` tree) -> **exit 0**, clean. `npx eslint lib/analyticsLogic.ts lib/analyticsLogic.spec.ts` -> **exit 0**, clean; a full `npx eslint .` across the whole `app/` tree also -> **exit 0** (3 pre-existing warnings, 0 errors, none on either changed file: an unrelated `<img>`-vs-`next/image` warning in `Logo.tsx` and an unrelated pre-existing unused-import warning in `analytics/page.tsx` itself, both present identically before this change). `npx vitest run` (the full suite) -> **exit 0**, **86 test files, 718 tests, all passed** (`analyticsLogic.spec.ts` itself grew from 6 tests to 9 - the 3 new assertions above - so this is Finding 412's own last-recorded 715, plus this pass's net +3, reconciling exactly). `node --experimental-strip-types --test lib/*.test.ts` (the separate node:test-runner suite, for files using that convention instead of vitest - unaffected by this change, run anyway for completeness since this fix touches shared TypeScript) -> **exit 0**, **276 tests, 276 pass, 0 fail**. This fix touches no Python engine code (`git diff --stat` shows only the two TypeScript files), so the `engine/**/test_*.py` sweep was not re-run for it.

**Guardrail/risk classification, each factor checked, not assumed.** Pure TypeScript, two pure functions in one file (`analyticsLogic.ts`) plus its own test file, with exactly one real caller (`app/app/analytics/page.tsx`, confirmed by grep - `grep -rn "monthKey\|buildWinLossTrend" app --include="*.ts" --include="*.tsx"` returns only that one page plus the file's own definitions/spec). **No RLS** - zero SQL/migration touched. **No money/payment path** - this is a read-only analytics display, not `dealEconomics.ts`'s pricing math or anything billing-related. **No hard-stop/disqualification gate** - this never gates pack generation, compliance or disqualification logic; it only decides which month-bucket a chart bar's count lands in. **No worker-image/deployment change.** **No multi-table schema surface** - zero migration, zero schema change. **Not one of the six named files** (`fill_a_forms.py`/`fill_sbd_docx.py`/`fill_flat_pdf.py`/`make_envelope_covers.py`/`process_narrative_jobs.py`/`build_docx.py`). **Not a correctness fix to a document a company signs/submits** - confirmed by grep: `analyticsLogic.ts` is never imported by `pack-review.tsx` or `submission-pack.tsx`, directly or transitively (its only consumer, `analytics/page.tsx`, is a standalone read-only reporting page with no pack-generation or submission-content role). Small, safe fix, no risk factor present -> pushed directly to `main`, per this track's own guardrail.

**Why this is not a re-tread of any exhausted angle.** This IS the same underlying naive-UTC-vs-SAST-calendar class Finding 289/290 already named and fixed at the DAY granularity (`daysUntil()`, `submission_due_signals()`) - but those fixes, and the standing EXHAUSTED-ANGLES list's own angle 9/5 framing, are both scoped to `datetime.date.today()`/exact-day-threshold-match reminder candidates; this is a third, independent site of the identical underlying fact-of-the-world ("SAST, not UTC, is the real calendar") at MONTH granularity, in a TypeScript display function neither prior fix's own audit trail mentions touching. Not Angle 12's per-run cache poisoning (no cache, no cross-call shared state). Not the storage-orphan class, the `build_general_pack.py` not_found drop, the `fill_flat_pdf.py` FORMS regex sweep, the stale-position-reassignment shape, the dispatch_status-not-checked shape, the hand-kept-`pipeline_stage`-list-drift shape (this file's own stage filter was already checked and ruled clean, separately, before this pass), or Angle 11's early-return/epistemic-conflation shape - none of those mechanisms exist in this pair of pure date-bucketing functions.
