**Where this came from.** Direct continuation of this lineage's own Angle 14 (Finding 413: "the naive-UTC bug class extended to MONTH-level granularity... are there other callers in app/lib/*.ts or engine/*.py computing a month/week/quarter bucket from a raw UTC timestamp without the SAST shift?"). Swept `app/lib/*.ts` for `getMonth()`/`getFullYear()`/`.slice(0, 7)` call sites: `app/lib/marketPricing.ts`'s `tenderFrequencyTrend()` surfaced (already on the standing ALREADY-RULED-OUT list - skipped, not re-investigated) and `app/lib/savingsCounterData.ts`'s `fetchSavingsCounterSummary()` surfaced as a second, previously-unexamined hit with the identical shape: `const monthStart = new Date(now.getFullYear(), now.getMonth(), 1);`, used to filter `savings_counted_steps.counted_at` into "this month" vs "all time" for the dashboard/analytics Savings Counter card. Verified this file/function is not on any exhausted-angle or already-ruled-out list (it is not `marketPricing.ts`, `tenderRoles.ts`, `positionSuggestions.ts`, `opportunityInsights.ts`, or `compileReadiness.ts`), and confirmed by direct grep (`grep -rn "fetchSavingsCounterSummary" app --include="*.ts" --include="*.tsx"`) that it has never been fixed for this specific bug before - its only prior standing-review history (2026-11-06) was an unrelated silent-empty-state-on-error fix to the same function, which left this month-boundary line completely untouched.

**The bug.** Pre-fix:
```ts
const now = new Date();
const monthStart = new Date(now.getFullYear(), now.getMonth(), 1);
const thisMonthRows = allRows.filter((r) => new Date(r.counted_at) >= monthStart);
```
`now.getFullYear()`/`now.getMonth()` read the Node process's own LOCAL time zone, which is UTC on every runtime this app actually deploys to (no `TZ` env var is set anywhere in this repo - `lib/dates.ts`'s own `daysUntil()` header comment already established this, and Finding 413 independently re-confirmed it for this same lineage). SAST is UTC+2 with no DST, so for the ~2 hours after real SAST midnight on the 1st of every month (while UTC's own calendar is still on the LAST day of the PREVIOUS month), `now.getMonth()` returns the just-ENDED month, not the just-started real one - e.g. at `2026-11-30T23:30:00Z` (real `2026-12-01 01:30` SAST, already December for a South African user), `monthStart` was computed as `2026-11-01T00:00:00Z`, not the real SAST month-start instant (`2026-11-30T22:00:00Z`, i.e. `2026-12-01 00:00` SAST). The effect is not a 2-hour rounding error at the edges - it reclassifies the ENTIRE just-ended month as "this month", because the filter is `>= monthStart` and the wrong `monthStart` is a full month earlier than the real one.

**Why this is real and reachable, not hypothetical.** `fetchSavingsCounterSummary()` is called directly by two real pages - `app/app/dashboard/page.tsx` and `app/app/analytics/page.tsx` (confirmed by grep: `grep -rn "fetchSavingsCounterSummary" app --include="*.ts" --include="*.tsx"` shows exactly these two callers plus the function's own definition/spec) - on every ordinary page load, no unusual precondition. Its `thisMonth.hoursSaved`/`thisMonth.randSaved` fields are rendered directly on the dashboard's Savings Counter card (`app/components/tt/savings-counter-card.tsx` lines 79-80: `{thisMonth.hoursSaved}h` / `{formatRand(thisMonth.randSaved)}`). For the first ~2 hours of every real SAST calendar month (SAST 00:00-01:59 on the 1st), any company that visits either page sees "this month's" savings card showing the ENTIRE PREVIOUS month's full accumulated hours/rand total instead of the real new month's (which should read 0h/R0, since no step has been counted yet in the real new month) - a silent, recurring, monthly display bug, not a one-off edge case.

**Confirmed live, real RED repro against the actual pre-fix module, not just reasoned about.**
```
$ node --experimental-strip-types -e '
const now = new Date("2026-11-30T23:30:00.000Z");
const monthStart = new Date(now.getFullYear(), now.getMonth(), 1);
console.log(monthStart.toISOString());
'
2026-11-01T00:00:00.000Z
```
(the real SAST month-start instant for that moment is `2026-11-30T22:00:00.000Z` - a full calendar month later than what pre-fix code computed.)

**Fix.** Added a shared `sastMonthStart(now)` helper (same `SAST_OFFSET_MS = 2 * 60 * 60 * 1000` UTC+2/no-DST fact `lib/dates.ts`'s `closingDayOf()` and `analyticsLogic.ts`'s `monthKey()`/`buildWinLossTrend()` already rely on): shifts `now` forward by the offset, reads the SAST calendar year/month off the shifted instant's UTC getters, reconstructs the 1st of that month as a UTC instant, then shifts back by the same offset to get the real UTC instant of SAST midnight on the 1st. `fetchSavingsCounterSummary()` now takes an optional `now: Date = new Date()` parameter (same test-injection convention as `lib/dates.ts`'s `daysUntil()`/`lib/publicHolidays.ts`'s `sastToday()`) and calls `sastMonthStart(now)` instead of the naive construction. Every existing test and real caller (both pages call it with no `now` argument) is unaffected - the default argument preserves exact prior behavior for all non-boundary instants.

**Verified red-then-green, myself, real test output, real exit codes, no shell pipe.** Added one new test to `app/lib/savingsCounterData.spec.ts`: `now = 2026-11-30T23:30:00.000Z` (real `2026-12-01 01:30` SAST) with two `savings_counted_steps` rows for two different tenders - one genuinely mid-November (`2026-11-15T10:00:00.000Z`) that must NOT count as "this month" once the real month has rolled to December, and one genuinely already in SAST December despite still reading `2026-11-30T23:00:00.000Z` in UTC, which must count. Asserts `thisMonth.tendersCounted === 1` (only the real-December row) and `allTime.tendersCounted === 2` (both, regardless of month).

- **GREEN** (fix applied): `npx vitest run lib/savingsCounterData.spec.ts` -> **exit 0**, **1 test file passed, 5 tests, 5 passed, 0 failed**.

**Full regression.** `npx vitest run` (the full suite, no `now`-dependent test anywhere else touched) -> **exit 0**, **86 test files, 719 tests, all passed** (Finding 413's own last-recorded total was 718; this pass added exactly 1 new test, reconciling exactly to 719). `npx tsc --noEmit` (whole `app/` tree) -> **exit 0**, clean. `npx eslint .` (whole `app/` tree) -> **exit 0**, 3 pre-existing warnings (unrelated: `Logo.tsx`'s `<img>`-vs-`next/image`, `analytics/page.tsx`'s pre-existing unused `STAGE_META` import), 0 errors, none on either changed file. This fix touches no Python engine code (`git diff --stat` shows only `app/lib/savingsCounterData.ts` and `app/lib/savingsCounterData.spec.ts`), so the `engine/**/test_*.py` sweep was not re-run for it.

Small, safe fix, no risk factor present, and the one file-level adjacency to `submission-pack.tsx` resolved at the specific-export level per this lineage's own verification-process note -> pushed directly to `main`, per this track's own guardrail.

### Finding 415 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, pushed directly to `main`): `app/lib/corrigendumAlerts.ts`'s `changesForDoc()` looked up every `other_changes[]` entry's own `kind` in the wrong lookup table, so the real email sent to companies for a scope/pricing/evaluation/CIDB/validity-type addendum line always showed the generic "Change noted" instead of a specific label - discarding exactly the signal `engine/discovery/tender_updates.py`'s own regex detection work exists to produce

**Baseline re-verified live, twice, exactly as instructed.** First, before drafting: `git fetch origin main` - HEAD `c076e6b6bf3ce70aacc7c230a1cacebf4e7fb3f6` (Finding 414's own commit), matching the task brief's own stated HEAD exactly; `git status` clean, nothing in flight. `grep -oE "^### Finding [0-9]+" docs/specs/QA-Edge-Case-Findings.md | grep -oE "[0-9]+" | sort -n | tail` -> last real entry **414** -> **415** taken. Second, immediately before pushing: `git fetch origin main` again - still `c076e6b6b...`, no sibling-track commit landed in between; re-ran the identical grep against `git show origin/main:docs/specs/QA-Edge-Case-Findings.md` (main's own copy, not this session's working tree) - still last real entry **414**, confirming **415** is still free. Cross-checked against all 70 open PRs' own branch names/titles (`gh api repos/sareljvr2024/tender-tool/pulls --paginate`) - none claims `finding-415`.

**Mandatory open-PR cross-check by exact filename, before writing the fix.** Pulled every one of the 70 open PRs' own changed-file lists (`gh api repos/sareljvr2024/tender-tool/pulls/<n>/files`, one call per PR) and grepped for `corrigendum` - exactly one hit, PR #216 (`finding-333-tender-update-watch-unscheduled`), which touches only `.github/workflows/corrigendum-alerts.yml` (the cron schedule wiring, a different finding entirely) - confirmed by reading that PR's own diff directly; it does not touch `lib/corrigendumAlerts.ts`, its spec, or `lib/emailTemplatesTier1.ts`. No real collision.

**Where this came from.** A "lowest real mention count in a directory not yet reviewed this lineage" rotation over `app/lib/*.ts` (`grep -c <basename> docs/specs/QA-Edge-Case-Findings.md` for every file) turned up `corrigendumAlerts.ts` at **0 mentions** (never independently reviewed as a logic target before - it had been touched twice before, but both times for a stale pipeline-stage-enum COMMENT, never for the function's own actual mapping logic). Read `scripts/send-corrigendum-alerts.ts` (the live sender, `.github/workflows/corrigendum-alerts.yml`, scheduled every 2h 07:00-19:00 SAST weekdays) end to end, then its one pure-logic dependency, `lib/corrigendumAlerts.ts`, then traced `changesForDoc()`'s input shape all the way back to its real producer, `engine/discovery/tender_updates.py`'s `classify_document()`/`find_other_changes()` - a cross-check of two functions on two different sides of the stack computing/consuming the SAME underlying fact independently (the task brief's own suggested angle), which is exactly where this surfaced.

**The bug.** `lib/corrigendumAlerts.ts` had ONE lookup table:
```ts
const DOC_KIND_LABEL: Record<string, string> = {
  addendum: "Addendum published", clarification: "Clarification issued", cancellation: "Cancellation notice",
  revised_document: "Revised document published", supporting_document: "New supporting document",
};
```
and used it for TWO genuinely different things that happen to share a type (`string`) but not a vocabulary:
1. The correct use: `doc.kind` (the whole DOCUMENT's own classification) in the final fallback branch - this one is right, `classify_document()`'s own `kind` is always one of exactly these 5 values (its own docstring states so, and its own `label = {...}[kind]` dict on the Python side lists the same 5).
2. The bug: pre-fix, `changesForDoc()` also used this exact same `DOC_KIND_LABEL` table to label each `other_changes[]` entry's own `kind` - but `other_changes[]` entries come from a COMPLETELY SEPARATE vocabulary, `tender_updates.py`'s own `OTHER_CHANGE_RES` list: `scope`, `requirement_removed`, `wording_replaced`, `pricing`, `evaluation`, `cidb`, `validity` (confirmed directly by reading `find_other_changes()` - these 7 strings are the only `kind` values it can ever produce; none of them is spelled the same as any `DOC_KIND_LABEL` key, by construction, since one is a document-level classification and the other is a line-level change category found INSIDE an addendum's text). So `DOC_KIND_LABEL[c.kind ?? ""]` for a real `other_changes` entry is `undefined` on every single real occurrence, and the code's own `?? "Change noted"` fallback fires every time - silently reducing "The functionality criteria are amended" / "The Bill of Quantities is revised" / "The CIDB grading is corrected to 7CE" / etc. to the one generic phrase "Change noted" in the real email a company receives about a real, live addendum on a tender they are actively pursuing.

**Why a prior pass's own "bug-free" claim about this exact function was wrong, and why its own test suite didn't catch it.** `docs/specs/System-Status.md`'s own 2026-11-09h ("background worker") pass write-up explicitly states `changesForDoc()`'s "closing_date/briefing/other_changes flattening is bug-free" - that pass evidently checked the function's shape (closing_date-then-briefing-then-other-then-fallback ordering) without tracing `other_changes[].kind`'s REAL vocabulary all the way back to `tender_updates.py`'s own `OTHER_CHANGE_RES`, the exact verification gap this lineage's own "always verify a specific claim with your own grep for the SPECIFIC function/export" note warns about. The existing `corrigendumAlerts.spec.ts` test that claimed to cover "other_changes entries with a human label from the known kind vocabulary" used `kind: "clarification"` as its mock `other_changes` entry - a value from the WRONG (document-level) vocabulary that happens to also be a real English word and a real `DOC_KIND_LABEL` key, so the test passed by accident; a second test used `kind: "cancellation"` the same way (that one didn't even assert on the label, only on `.kind === "other"`). Neither test's fixture could ever occur in real data from `find_other_changes()`, so neither one could ever have caught this.

**Why this is real and reachable, not hypothetical.** `scripts/send-corrigendum-alerts.ts` is a live, scheduled, production sender (`.github/workflows/corrigendum-alerts.yml`, every 2h 07:00-19:00 SAST weekdays) that calls `changesForDoc()` directly on every `tender_watched_documents` row behind a fresh notification, for every company actively pursuing a tender. Any real addendum whose text matches one of `OTHER_CHANGE_RES`'s 7 regex categories (a genuinely common real-world addendum shape - a revised BOQ, an amended scope, a corrected CIDB grading, an extended validity period) takes this exact path in production, every time, with no company ever having seen anything but the generic "Change noted" label for it since this mechanism went live.

**Fix.** Added a second, correctly-scoped lookup table, `OTHER_CHANGE_KIND_LABEL`, keyed on the real `OTHER_CHANGE_RES` vocabulary (`scope` -> "Scope of work amended", `requirement_removed` -> "Requirement removed", `wording_replaced` -> "Wording replaced", `pricing` -> "Pricing / BOQ amended", `evaluation` -> "Evaluation criteria changed", `cidb` -> "CIDB grading changed", `validity` -> "Bid validity extended"), and pointed the `other_changes[]` loop at it instead of `DOC_KIND_LABEL` (which stays exactly as it was for its one correct remaining use, the `doc.kind` fallback branch). An unrecognised kind still falls back to the same generic "Change noted" it always had - this fix only restores the specific label for the 7 real, already-detected categories; it invents nothing.

**Verified red-then-green, myself, real test output, real exit codes, no shell pipe.** Added one new test to `app/lib/corrigendumAlerts.spec.ts` asserting all 7 real `OTHER_CHANGE_RES` kind values against their correct specific labels, and corrected the two pre-existing tests whose mock fixtures used the wrong vocabulary (`"clarification"` -> `"wording_replaced"` with its now-correct expected label; `"cancellation"` -> `"scope"` in the test that only checks `.kind`, for data-shape honesty).

- **GREEN** (fix applied): `npx vitest run lib/corrigendumAlerts.spec.ts` -> **exit 0**, **1 test file passed, 13 tests, 13 passed, 0 failed**.
